documents.title: resume.jnap.me — editorial dossier
documents.body:
# resume.jnap.me — editorial dossier

Astro single-page resume that reframes the `resume-site/` content into an editorial dossier for creative firms. Typography leans on Fraunces + Space Grotesk, with a controlled grid and two intentional "weird" interruptions (rotated systems note + section code overlays) to nod to Wolff Olins' Lloyd's project without copying it.

## Stack
- [Astro 5](https://astro.build) static output (Vercel friendly)
- TypeScript + module aliasing for cleaner imports
- PDF rendered from the canonical public web resume
- Single CSS system in `src/styles/global.css` with embedded print + motion rules
- Systems section has layout + view toggles (grid vs. column stack for highlights; accordion/table/badges/tabs/timeline for the catalog).

## Getting started
```bash
npm install        # or make install
npm run dev        # start Astro locally on http://localhost:4321
npm run build      # production build into ./dist
npm run preview    # serve the build (used for PDF export)
npm run skill:graph -- --clusters=6   # generate skill clusters via OpenAI embeddings
```

`make` wrappers are included for parity (`make dev`, `make build`, `make pdf`, etc.).

## Content + configuration
- All resume facts live in `src/data/resume.json` (copied directly from the provided `resume-site/`). Do not edit them inline in the markup.
- Hero/section copy lives in `src/data/copy.json` so the prose can be tuned without touching templates.
- CTA + site metadata live in `src/config.ts`. Update `bookCallUrl` there if the scheduling link changes.
- The hero "Download PDF" button serves `public/resume.pdf`. Regenerate it whenever the site changes (see below) so Vercel ships the current print.

## Generating the PDF
```bash
make pdf
```
This runs `npm run pdf`: build the canonical JSON-backed page, then print its actual public DOM through `scripts/export-pdf.mjs` to `public/resume.pdf`. This preserves the web contact privacy rules and current career facts. `npm run pdf:html` exports an already-built page. Do not replace this artifact with the separate LaTeX/pit resume: its facts and phone policy differ. The old fetch script is retained for historical reference and is not the default export path.

## Deploying to Vercel
1. Push to GitHub and import the repo in Vercel.
2. Framework preset: **Astro**.
3. Build command: `npm run build`; Output directory: `dist`.
4. Ensure `public/resume.pdf` is committed so the CTA stays live.

## Typographic + layout system
- Fraunces headlines use optical-size variations layered over Space Grotesk body copy to echo editorial dossiers.
- 12-column-inspired grid with alternating spans for Experience vs. detail rails.
- Section codes offset in the margin and the rotated hero systems-note are the two intentional "weird" moves.
- Skill meters visualize years of experience (normalized across the full catalog) instead of raw numerals only.
- Print styles strip shadows/backgrounds, remove CTA buttons, reveal URLs, add a masthead, and include page numbers.

## Verification checklist
- ✅ Book-a-call CTA hits `https://cal.com/justin-napolitano-gvu3p3/intro`.
- ✅ Download PDF points to `/resume.pdf` (regenerate via `make pdf`).
- ✅ Experience, projects, skills, education, and publication match `resume-site/` content.
- ✅ Layout responds across mobile/desktop + print.

## Skill graph pipeline
Set `OPENAI_API_KEY` (the script calls OpenAI's embeddings API) and run:

```bash
npm run skill:graph -- --clusters=6
```

The script reads `src/data/resume.json`, filters to the displayed skills, generates embeddings via `text-embedding-3-small`, clusters them with a lightweight k-means implementation, and writes `public/skill-graph.json` with cluster labels, membership, and 2D PCA coordinates. Pass `--hidden=true` to include suppressed skills, `--model=text-embedding-3-large` for higher fidelity vectors, or `--output=some/path.json` to change the destination. After generating the file, visit `/skill-graph` (static map) or `/skill-graph-test` (interactive canvas playground) in the local dev server.

# Unified brand implementation — issue #32

Authority: [approved contract](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/littlelink/blob/ae3e9062d8e06a1158af74a29cbd8b549d82b3e2/docs/branding/2026-10-22/brand-contract.md). Inter and Source Serif 4 are served locally from public/fonts with included OFL licenses; system fallbacks remain available. No font service or runtime dependency added. Removed old Google Fonts import; existing analytics consent behavior and routes remain intact.

Canonical JSON and all career facts unchanged. Older PDF guidance conflicts with this repo's newer explicit content-authority manifest. Deployed PDF is raw data-strategist-resume/pit/resume.pdf; the separate merge-with-website draft is not deployed and has different facts. Do not claim copy sync or silently reconcile facts in a visual change. Preserve public/resume.pdf until its paired PDF is reviewed.

Validation: npm run check (0 errors, 6 existing hints), npm run build, npm run resume.format.validate-source, npm run resume.format.validate-export -- --profile=web_resume all pass. Validator export gates check policy/source existence, not rendered browser or PDF fidelity. Rendered browser QA remains a release gate. No new dependency, network integration, authentication or infrastructure changes. Existing privacy rules (phone not public web) preserved.

Rollback: revert focused presentation commit. Existing Vercel Astro build uses npm run build with dist output. Do not merge/deploy until coordinator resolves governance registration and paired visual QA.

documents.title: Career Content Authority
documents.body:
# Career Content Authority

`src/data/resume.json` is the first canonical store for shared career-suite facts. The content authority manifest at `src/data/content-authority.json` defines which fields are public, which fields are private, which downstream targets consume projections, and which repo-local JSON commands are stable enough for Codex Platform or MCP wrappers to call.

This repo owns the resume content model, PDF generation, and resume/CV export behavior. The platform repo owns orchestration contracts only.

`src/data/resume-format.json` is the target-local projection of the platform resume format contract. It lists the output profiles this repo can validate for agents: ATS PDF, human PDF, web resume, targeted job application packets, and the planned ATS DOCX fallback.

## JSON Command Surface

The first API surface is a repo-local command:

```bash
node scripts/career-content-api.mjs status
```

Every command emits a JSON envelope with:

- `ok`
- `status`
- `repo_id`
- `command`
- `blockers`
- `artifacts`
- `next_actions`

Supported commands:

- `status`: validates the content authority and returns counts, public identity, and sync targets
- `profile`: returns the public profile and high-level resume inventory
- `sync-preview --target=all`: previews deterministic downstream payloads for `resume`, `docs`, `hire`, and `link`
- `tailor-preview --job-text="..."`: ranks existing skills, experience, and projects against a job posting without generating a PDF or inventing facts
- `job-normalize --job-text="..."`: normalizes a posting into deterministic job fields, keywords, and detected requirement terms
- `fit-report --job-text="..."`: scores job overlap against canonical resume facts and exposes gaps
- `selection-plan --job-text="..."`: creates a source-backed section plan for `targeted_job_application`
- `review-packet --job-text="..."`: bundles normalized job data, fit report, selection plan, claim audit, and risk flags
- `format-status`: returns output profiles, source-fact counts, and format contract pointers
- `format-validate-source`: validates canonical resume content and source fact IDs
- `format-validate-export --profile=web_resume`: validates one output profile against current source and artifacts
- `format-claim-audit --targeted-packet-json='{"source_fact_ids":["identity.name"]}'`: checks selected fact IDs in a targeted packet

## Publish Workflow

The current publish path remains:

1. update `src/data/resume.json`
2. run `npm run career:status`
3. run `npm run career:sync-preview -- --target=all`
4. run `npm run resume.format.status`
5. run `npm run resume.format.validate-source`
6. run `npm run resume.format.validate-export -- --profile=web_resume`
7. run `npm run career:review-packet -- --job-text="..."` before any targeted application use
8. run `npm run check`
9. run `npm run build`
10. run `npm run pdf` when a refreshed PDF is needed

Tailored resume PDF generation should consume a reviewed `review-packet` after the selection plan and claim audit pass.

## Application Automation Boundary

Job polling, job-fit scoring, application packet generation, and application submission are separate later workers. This slice only prepares the content and selection substrate. Automatic submission must remain deferred until there is explicit policy for identity use, claim review, destination allowlists, and human approval.

documents.title: Resume Format Command Surface
documents.body:
# Resume Format Command Surface

This repo implements the target-side API expected by the platform resume-format contract. The commands are side-effect free and emit JSON envelopes for Codex Platform, MCP wrappers, or future web control panes.

## Commands

```bash
npm run resume.format.status
npm run resume.format.validate-source
npm run resume.format.validate-export -- --profile=web_resume
npm run resume.format.claim-audit -- --targeted-packet-json='{"source_fact_ids":["identity.name"]}'
```

The command IDs match the platform contract:

- `resume.format.status`
- `resume.format.validate-source`
- `resume.format.validate-export`
- `resume.format.claim-audit`

## Source Facts

The command surface derives stable `source_fact_id` values from `src/data/resume.json`.

Examples:

- `identity.name`
- `skill.data-science-platforms.sql`
- `experience.data-engineer-adventhealth.bullet.1`
- `project.heart-failure-quality-metrics-dashboard.bullet.1`

Tailored resume previews now return these IDs with ranked skills, experience, and projects. Any future worker that generates a targeted packet must preserve the IDs so `resume.format.claim-audit` can reject unsupported or private claims before a human review.

## Output Profiles

Profiles live in `src/data/resume-format.json`.

- `web_resume`: public site profile, available now
- `ats_pdf`: parser-friendly PDF profile, backed by `public/resume.pdf`
- `human_pdf`: recruiter/referral PDF profile, backed by `public/resume.pdf`
- `targeted_job_application`: JSON selection packet profile, available now
- `ats_docx`: planned fallback profile, not exported yet

`ats_docx` intentionally reports as planned instead of blocked. The profile is part of the contract so agents know it exists, but this slice does not create a DOCX renderer.

documents.title: Resume Job Application Workflow
documents.body:
# Resume Job Application Workflow

This workflow defines how agents can turn a job posting into a reviewed resume packet without inventing facts or submitting applications.

The machine-readable contract is `src/data/job-application-workflow.json`. The current command surface is repo-local JSON:

```bash
npm run career:job-workflow
npm run career:job-normalize -- --job-text="..."
npm run career:fit-report -- --job-text="..."
npm run career:selection-plan -- --job-text="..."
npm run career:review-packet -- --job-text="..."
```

## Operating Boundary

This repo can provide canonical resume facts, role-fit previews, selection plans, review packets, and eventually reviewed PDF exports.

This repo must not submit applications automatically in this slice. Submission requires a later policy for identity use, destination allowlists, claim review, and explicit human approval.

## Workflow Nodes

1. `job_intake`
   Normalize a job posting into source-backed fields: source URL, company, title, location, employment type, description text, and capture timestamp.
   Available through `npm run career:job-normalize`.

2. `fit_scoring`
   Compare the posting to canonical skills, projects, and experience. Missing requirements become gaps, not invented claims.
   Available through `npm run career:fit-report`.

3. `resume_selection`
   Produce an ordered selection plan from existing content references. The worker can rank and exclude content, but it cannot create new facts.
   Available through `npm run career:selection-plan`.

4. `review_packet`
   Prepare a human-reviewable packet with the fit report, selected content, exclusions, and risk flags.
   Available through `npm run career:review-packet`.

5. `pdf_export`
   Generate a tailored PDF only after review approval.

6. `application_submission`
   Deferred. This remains blocked until a separate application submission governance slice exists.

## Agent Contract

Agents should call:

- `npm run career:status`
- `npm run career:profile`
- `npm run career:job-workflow`
- `npm run career:tailor-preview -- --job-text="..."`
- `npm run career:job-normalize -- --job-text="..."`
- `npm run career:fit-report -- --job-text="..."`
- `npm run career:selection-plan -- --job-text="..."`
- `npm run career:review-packet -- --job-text="..."`
- `npm run resume.format.validate-source`
- `npm run resume.format.claim-audit -- --targeted-packet-json='{"source_fact_ids":["identity.name"]}'`

All commands return JSON envelopes and are side-effect free. The review packet is a handoff artifact for humans and later export workers; it is not approval to generate a tailored PDF or submit an application.

Tailored packets must carry `source_fact_ids` from the ranked content returned by `tailor-preview`. Missing IDs, unknown IDs, or private IDs are claim-audit blockers.

## Future ExecPlan Sequence

The next implementation slices should be:

1. `future:resume-pdf-export-worker`
   Produce tailored PDFs from approved selection plans.

2. `future:application-submission-governance`
   Define policy before any application submission worker exists.

3. `future:resume-fit-scoring-v2`
   Replace simple keyword scoring with a richer scorer once the review-packet contract is stable.

documents.title: Resume Job Targeting Command Surface
documents.body:
# Resume Job Targeting Command Surface

This repo now exposes a side-effect-free JSON workflow for turning a job posting into a source-backed resume selection plan.

The workflow is intentionally conservative: it does not create new claims, generate a PDF, or submit an application. It only normalizes the posting, scores overlap against `src/data/resume.json`, selects existing source facts, and emits a human-review packet.

## Commands

```bash
npm run career:job-normalize -- --job-text="..." --company="..." --title="..."
npm run career:fit-report -- --job-text="..."
npm run career:selection-plan -- --job-text="..."
npm run career:review-packet -- --job-text="..."
```

Every command emits the standard envelope:

- `ok`
- `status`
- `repo_id`
- `command`
- `blockers`
- `warnings`
- `artifacts`
- `next_actions`

## Workflow

1. `job-normalize`
   Accepts `--job-text`, `--job-file`, or `--job-json` and returns a normalized posting with deterministic `source_id`, keywords, and detected requirement terms.

2. `fit-report`
   Scores the normalized posting against canonical summary, skill, experience, and project facts. Missing terms become explicit gaps.

3. `selection-plan`
   Produces a section-by-section plan for `targeted_job_application`. Every selected item carries `source_fact_ids`.

4. `review-packet`
   Runs the selection through the same source-fact boundary as `resume.format.claim-audit`, then returns risk flags and the review policy.

## Input Modes

Text input:

```bash
npm run career:review-packet -- --job-text="Senior analytics engineer role requiring SQL and BI"
```

Structured input:

```bash
npm run career:review-packet -- --job-json='{"company":"Example Co","title":"Analytics Engineer","source_url":"https://example.com/job","description_text":"SQL, BI, data modeling"}'
```

File input:

```bash
npm run career:review-packet -- --job-file=fixtures/job-posting.json
```

The structured fields are:

- `source_url`
- `source_id`
- `company`
- `title`
- `location`
- `employment_type`
- `description_text`
- `captured_at`

`description_text` is required. Missing source URL, company, title, or capture timestamp are warnings so a quick exploratory fit report can still run.

## Agent Boundary

Agents may call these commands to inspect fit and prepare a packet. They must not treat a packet as approved.

Allowed:

- compare a posting to canonical facts
- show evidence-backed matches and gaps
- select existing fact IDs
- prepare a review packet for a human

Blocked:

- inventing claims
- exporting private fields
- generating a tailored PDF without approval
- submitting applications

The next durable step is a reviewed export worker that consumes `review-packet` output after approval.

documents.title: hire-me
documents.body:
# hire-me

An irreverent-but-useful hiring one-pager built with Astro + Tailwind for recruiters, hiring managers, and collaborators who want the receipts fast.

## Getting started

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open http://localhost:4321/ to preview the site.

## Customize

- Update contact + case-study links, metrics, and references in `src/config/profile.ts`.
- Swap icons or add new CTAs in `public/icons/`.
- Adjust colors/typography in `src/styles/global.css` if you want a different palette.

## Deploy

Same as any Astro project—Vercel, Netlify, etc. Ship the dist folder or hook it straight to a platform.

## Reuse in other Astro projects

- Import the shared theme tokens via `@import './src/styles/design-system.css';` (or add it to your layout) to get the light/dark palette + surface styles.
- Components are prop-driven and exported through `src/components/index.ts`, so you can cherry-pick like `import { HeroSection } from '../components';` and pass your own data.
- All prop types live in `src/config/profile.ts` and are re-exported alongside the components for type-safe configs.
- Theme/debug controls stay in `PageLayout`, but you can also import `design-system.css` directly if you prefer your own layout wrapper.

documents.title: Jayburd Bookkeeping
documents.body:
# Jayburd Bookkeeping

A planned bookkeeping system for separate LLC and personal books, with a Go
backend, PostgreSQL ledger, Next.js interface, and GCP delivery.

## Current stage

The first synthetic PostgreSQL posting slice is implemented: balanced manual
journals, spot conversion, exact reversals, scoped reads and trial balance, with
atomic audit/receipt/outbox records. Go supplies transaction and HTTP adapters.
An identity adapter requires managed TOTP sign-in and checks revocation; controlled
setup creates synthetic entity/book/account bundles atomically. See the
[identity/setup evidence](docs/runbooks/identity-setup.md).
The first application adds a bounded Go server, managed sign-in/TOTP screens,
book setup, split journal review/posting and trial balance. Default server mode
exposes health only; the UI remains unconfigured until the owner supplies public
identity configuration. See [application evidence](docs/runbooks/first-app.md).
Reviewed setup and posting requests now survive a lost response or browser restart:
prepare, execute, recover the saved result, then explicitly acknowledge it.
See [command recovery evidence](docs/runbooks/command-recovery.md).
There is no live identity configuration, bank connection, cloud deployment or
approval to use these books as a system of record.

## Start here

1. Read [project context](docs/index.md) and [product scope](docs/product.md).
2. Read the [architecture decision](docs/decisions/0001-architecture.md).
3. Follow the [delivery workflow](docs/delivery.md).
4. Review [Infisical setup](docs/infisical.md).
5. Resume from the [recovery proof and remaining gates](docs/runbooks/command-recovery.md).

For source material and reading priorities, use the
[annotated bibliography](docs/research/bibliography.md).

## Local commands

For an interactive review with fictional generated data, run `make demo` and open
[the synthetic demo](http://localhost:39083). It seeds two fictional LLCs into
disposable PostgreSQL and serves the real bookkeeping components and Go API.
Stop with Ctrl+C; restart `make demo` to reset. See the
[demo runbook](docs/runbooks/synthetic-demo.md) for prerequisites and data limits.
Use **Watch a few transactions** for step-by-step request/commit/replay evidence,
or **Run thousands** for 1,000/5,000/10,000 real postings with a final balance check.

Requires Go 1.26.10 and Git. These commands need no cloud account or credentials.

```sh
make check
make test
make build
make backlog
make packet ID=JB-001
make issue-drafts
```

For the browser package, use Node 24.18.0 and `npm --prefix web ci`, then
`make web-check web-test web-build`. Install the pinned test browser with
`cd web && npx --no-install playwright install chromium`, then run
`make web-browser` from the repository root. Browser tests use synthetic adapters;
they never connect to a managed identity project.

`bin/api` starts loopback health-only mode. See the [server contract](docs/contracts/server.md)
for explicit managed composition and the [browser contract](docs/contracts/browser-auth.md)
for the separate provider configuration and recovery gates.

Database work is SQL-first, using `golang-migrate` and pgx, without an ORM. Start with the [database contract](docs/contracts/database.md) and
[migration commands](db/migrations/README.md). `make migration-test` separately
requires Docker and tests disposable PostgreSQL migrations. `make ledger-test`
runs the synthetic accounting, permission, concurrency and recovery proof on an
internal Docker network with no published database ports.
`make app-integration` requires those tools plus the installed browser and tests
the real Next rewrite, Go HTTP service and PostgreSQL together. It drops a response
after commit and proves recovery without a duplicate journal. Identity is synthetic;
this does not test the managed sign-in provider. Ports 39081–39083 must be free.

The backlog is a one-time issue seed, not a mirror of GitHub status. After
publication, GitHub Issues own execution state and native dependency links.
Markdown in this repository owns design and evidence. No separate vault,
vector database, or autonomous agent scheduler is required.

## Repository map

| Location | Authority |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/` | Product, decisions, contracts, research, and evidence |
| `planning/backlog.json` | Reviewed initial issue proposals and stable IDs |
| `planning/issues.json` | Published issue identities, never execution status |
| `cmd/project/` | Credential-free validation, packets, and issue drafts |
| `cmd/api/`, `internal/server/` | Bounded HTTP lifecycle and explicit managed composition |
| `web/` | Next.js application, memory-only sign-in and synthetic browser proof |
| `internal/identity/` | Managed authentication adapter; offline boundary tests |
| `internal/ledger/` | Go transaction and HTTP adapters; unit/integration tests |
| `db/migrations/` | Restricted SQL accounting authority and immutable migration history |
| `tests/corpus/` | Original synthetic fixtures and independent expected balances |
| `.github/` | Issue forms, PR template, CI and dependency update configuration |

The future application layout is documented in the architecture decision;
empty application and infrastructure directories are intentionally not seeded.

documents.title: Accounting scenarios and policy decisions
documents.body:
# Accounting scenarios and policy decisions

## Status and assumptions

Draft for JB-001/JB-002. Synthetic examples are proposed acceptance oracles, not
approved policies for actual LLCs. The development accrual/USD profile is selected in
[ADR 0005](../decisions/0005-development-accounting-policy.md); real-entity policy remains open. Examples involving
receivables use an illustrative accrual book with USD functional currency;
January/February 2026 dates and UTC accounting timezone are fixture assumptions.
Entity A and Entity B have separate books even under one owner. No tax is inferred.
[S01/S02](../research/database-sources.md) support double-entry and reconciliation;
[contract sources](../research/contract-sources.md) distinguish FX authority limits.

## Proposed chart and sign interpretation

Asset/expense accounts normally have debit balances; liability/equity/revenue
accounts normally have credit balances. Contra accounts reverse the presentation
convention. Account type/normal side do not prohibit opposite-side movements.
For each line store a positive magnitude and explicit debit/credit side; reports
calculate debit minus credit before applying their presentation convention.
Control accounts require source/subledger linkage once a subledger is enabled.

## Worked cases

Amounts below are USD unless marked EUR. Each row names a future test case.

| ID | Trigger and expected postings | Required observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-01 | Approved opening balances: Dr bank 1,000; Cr owner capital 1,000 | Opening evidence explains both sides; never invent equity to hide an unexplained difference. |
| AC-02 | Service earned and paid: Dr bank 200; Cr service revenue 200 | One journal despite repeated import. |
| AC-03 | Supplies consumed: Dr supplies expense 30; Cr bank 30 | Account classification is reviewed, not inferred from debit direction. |
| AC-04 | Card purchase: Dr expense 40; Cr card payable 40. Payment: Dr card payable 40; Cr bank 40 | Payment is not a second expense. |
| AC-05 | Split purchase: Dr expense A 20; Dr expense B 10; Cr bank 30 | Three lines, one balanced journal. |
| AC-06 | Refund of AC-03: Dr bank 30; Cr supplies expense 30 | Linked refund; actual tax/revenue treatment depends on source facts. |
| AC-07 | Bank transfer: Dr savings 100; Cr checking 100 | Both feed observations link to one transfer; no income/expense. |
| AC-08 | Contribution: Dr bank 100; Cr capital 100. Draw: Dr distributions 25; Cr bank 25 | Equity classification assumes owner activity, not payroll or a loan. |
| AC-09 | Reclassify AC-05: exact reversal, then Dr expense A 15 / Dr expense B 15 / Cr bank 30 | Original unchanged; correction/reversal links retained. |
| AC-10 | Accrual: Dr expense 60; Cr payable 60. Settlement: Dr payable 60; Cr bank 60 | Expense recognized once; cash-basis alternative requires its own policy. |
| AC-11 | A lends B 50: A Dr due-from-B 50 / Cr bank 50; B Dr bank 50 / Cr due-to-A 50 | Two separately authorized journals; common transfer reference, no cross-entity lines. |
| AC-12 | Book bank 950; statement 970; outstanding payment 20 | Adjusted statement 950 matches books; timing item needs no new journal. A missing bank fee requires an explicit draft adjustment. |
| AC-13 | Closing races a posting into January | Exactly one serialization order; a close that wins prevents a new January posting. |
| FX-01 | EUR receivable 100 at 1.10 USD/EUR: Dr receivable 110; Cr revenue 110 | Retain EUR 100 and the rate provenance. |
| FX-02 | Same exposure at January close, 1.20 USD/EUR: Dr receivable 10; Cr FX gain 10 | EUR quantity unchanged; carrying value becomes USD 120. |
| FX-03 | February settlement of FX-02 at 1.15: Dr USD bank 115; Dr FX loss 5; Cr receivable 120 | Exposure becomes zero; cumulative FX gain is 5, not 15. |
| FX-04 | Alternative to FX-03: settle EUR 50 at 1.15: Dr USD bank 57.50; Dr FX loss 2.50; Cr receivable 60 | Remaining EUR 50 has USD carrying value 60; do not execute both alternatives in one fixture. |
| FX-05 | Historical-cost asset acquired for EUR 100 at 1.10 | Preserve USD cost 110 on FX-only period review; other valuation/depreciation policies are separate. |
| FX-06 | Exchange EUR cash 100 carried at USD 110 for USD 115, fee USD 2 | Dr USD bank 113; Dr fees 2; Cr EUR cash 110; Cr FX gain 5. Original currency buckets need not individually balance. |

AC-01 through AC-10, sequentially, give bank 1,145 (checking 1,045, savings 100),
capital 1,100, distributions debit 25, expenses 130 and revenue 200. AC-09 is a
net-zero reclassification. Net income 70; assets 1,145 equal equity 1,145 after
including income and distributions. Trial-balance debits and credits each total
1,300. AC-11 onward are independent branches, not additions to this oracle.
A balanced trial balance alone does not prove completeness or proper classification.

## Policy decision register

| Question | Draft position | Acceptance owner / blocking scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reporting framework and accounting basis | Development accrual selected; US GAAP research target, not conformance | Owner/accountant, JB-001; recognition/FX rules |
| Functional currency and accounting timezone per book | Explicit, effective-dated approved policy; development profile selects USD/UTC | Owner/accountant; book activation |
| Rounding and precision | See money contract; development half-even selected; no automatic residual lines | Owner/accountant; money DDL/posting |
| Opening source and cutover | Reviewed complete opening trial balance, evidence and reconciliation | Owner/accountant; opening/live use |
| Permissions | Reader, preparer, poster, closer; trusted service actor distinct | Owner/schema reviewer; runtime grants |
| Close/reopen and errors in prior periods | Locked periods; correction in approved open period; no reopen endpoint in first slice | Owner/accountant; close policy |
| Rate source, dates, staleness, exceptions | Same-day synthetic spot profile selected; live provider policy pending | Owner/accountant; automated FX |

## Coverage and sequencing

Core mechanics cover double-entry, corrections, entity separation and provenance.
Accruals, deferrals, depreciation, revenue recognition, impairment, inventory,
leases, payroll, taxes and consolidation need topic-specific policy/contracts
before automation. A manual journal is not permission to claim those rules are
implemented. Unsupported automated treatments return a typed error or review state.
Presentation-currency translation and consolidation require separate statements,
OCI/elimination rules and contracts; aggregation must not be labelled consolidation.

First implementation target: ADR 0005 and the posting boundary narrow the
synthetic slice without closing the broader JB-001 policy work. Review
AC-01–AC-10 and FX-01–FX-06, then implement named tests from the SQL contract.
AC-01–10 now run through the synthetic PostgreSQL posting implementation and
fixed original-unit/balance checks. FX-01 is exercised as manual spot posting;
full FX position/reconciliation/close workflows remain future work. See the
[posting proof](../runbooks/posting-proof.md).

documents.title: Accounting correctness contract
documents.body:
# Accounting correctness contract

## Status

Target contract; no ledger implementation exists. JB-001 resolves accounting
policy before JB-004 implements posting. Requirements below need named tests.
Multicurrency is required; review the proposed [money contract](multicurrency.md)
and [accounting scenarios](accounting-scenarios.md). Policy and automated FX
implementation remain gated. Apply the [standards contract](standards.md) to
messages and practices.

## Durable posting boundary

Within one PostgreSQL transaction: authenticate/authorize the trusted actor for
the entity, coordinate with period closing, validate accounts and currency,
balance the full entry, write journal and lines, audit the operation, persist
the idempotency receipt, and append required outbox intent. Commit or roll back
everything. Database grants must prevent alternate unchecked write paths.

## Invariants and acceptance evidence

| Invariant | Required test/evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Debits equal credits in the book's functional currency; original currency amounts retain their units | Reject unbalanced, empty and invalid-account entries; accept supported FX entries with explicit valuation provenance; never balance by adding unlike currency units |
| Exact finite amounts and explicit rounding | Decimal parsing, precision/scale bounds; no float, NaN or infinity |
| Entity isolation, including references | Allowed, denied, mixed-entity, revoked and deleted-principal tests |
| Atomicity | Inject failure after header/line/audit/outbox writes; no partial commit |
| Replay safety | Same key+payload returns same result; changed payload conflicts; concurrent duplicate yields one entry |
| Posted history is immutable | Direct mutation denied; reversal links to original; correction preserves provenance |
| Closing and posting are serialized | Race tests prove no posting into a period that closed first |
| Provider facts differ from bookkeeping | Pending/posted, removed and corrected source records never silently change posted journals |
| Transfers do not double-count expense | Bank/card payment matching and intercompany reconciliation fixtures |
| Reports agree with ledger | Golden trial balance, P&L, balance sheet and general-ledger fixtures |
| Reconciliation is explicit | Statement opening/closing balances, outstanding items, unmatched/duplicate rows |
| Source evidence is traceable and protected | Access-scoped attachments, audit events and redacted diagnostics |

## Operational boundary

Imports and classifications produce drafts until a reviewed policy authorizes
posting. Model-generated suggestions, if introduced later, grant no authority.
Use synthetic fixtures locally and in CI. Restore drills and accountant-reviewed
exports precede a separate live cutover decision.

documents.title: Acquisition dispatch runtime
documents.body:
# Acquisition dispatch runtime

## Reviewed scope

Issue #7 extends the SQL-owned demand and delivery sidecars with a bounded Go
publisher and consumer. The coordinator approved the function wire with migration
15's sole SQL author before implementation. SQL remains the source of truth for
current authority, stable acquisition claim identity, fences, completion receipts,
retry timing and the eight-failure OR 24-hour budget. Queue acceptance is not
acquisition completion. Importing source observations never posts journals.

`NewPublisher(db, bindingUUID, observer.Transport)` implements `observer.Ticker`.
`NewConsumer(db, Runner)` implements `observer.WakeupHandler`. The injected Runner
has the existing acquisition `Run(ctx, Scope, claimUUID)` signature. Production
composition must supply distinct publisher and sync logins. No default credentials,
provider calls, HTTP mount, scheduler or deployment are enabled by these constructors.

## Protocol and authority

The existing strict `work-wakeup-v1` parser accepts only operation UUID, string
positive dispatch generation and numeric schema version 1. The task target version
is 2 and its name is lowercase SHA256(operation UUID + `|` + generation + `|2`).
This separates acquisition task identity from observer target 1. Root-owned explicit
acquisition HTTP/Cloud Tasks constructors pin the route, workload identity, target
version and deadline; callers cannot choose a URL or financial payload.

Publisher Tick runs at most 60 seconds and 25 candidates: discover and commit,
read candidates, recover, dispatch claim and commit, enqueue outside SQL, then
record the transport outcome in a new committed transaction. Transport has ten
seconds per call. Partial counts describe local progress, not backlog completion.
ALREADY_EXISTS is enqueue evidence only. Unknown claim COMMIT suppresses enqueue.
Contradictory transport result plus error is rejected without guessing evidence.

Consumer validates bytes before SQL, commits the delivery claim, validates its
scope/version/lease and calls Runner with the SQL-owned stable acquisition UUID.
It reserves five seconds for settlement and caps its own request at 75 seconds
inside the separate HTTP 80-second budget. Runner independently caps acquisition
at 60 seconds. Parent cancellation propagates; an arbitrary injected dependency
must honor context, and no promise of forcible termination is made.

Settlement receives only completed/retryable/permanent/unknown and a rounded-up
retry delay. SQL independently checks original and deterministic mutation-restart
completion receipts and actual acquisition leases before acknowledging or replacing
business claims. A completed Go return alone does not authorize success. Unknown
COMMIT, cancellation and unrecognized errors are unknown hints, never a new UUID.
Retry-After through 24 hours is not shortened. `retry_deferred` and a longer delay
quarantine rather than automatically retry sooner. When a crash loses a known
provider delay before settlement, SQL must quarantine the ambiguous abandoned
attempt rather than manufacture a shorter wait.

Only a committed done/quarantined result or committed recoverable retry_wait
handoff returns nil. Busy/not_due/stale and unknown settlement COMMIT remain
errors. SQL owns redispatch after acknowledged retry_wait; no in-memory timers
or background goroutines carry durable work. Outer lease expiry cannot permit
concurrent use of a still-live original or derived acquisition set.

## Transaction and failure policy

Each function uses SERIALIZABLE with four seconds active, three-second statement
and one-second lock timeouts, and an independent one-second rollback cleanup.
Only confirmed 40001/40P01 whole-transaction rollback retries, at most three times.
Other unknown COMMIT errors, including 08007 and 40003, expose no prepared result.
Role validation rejects SET ROLE impersonation, opposite worker/API/owner and
privileged memberships, as well as direct application-table grants. SQL additionally
validates enrolled login and current mandate. Metadata and external errors expose
only closed adapter-owned classifications, never provider text or credentials.

## Evidence and standards

The [background work](background-work.md) STD-01 internal-message assessment
applies: this is an internal wakeup, not an ISO 20022 financial exchange. Existing
source acquisition retains its pinned proprietary profile and ISO currency mapping.
Reviewed the existing [observer runtime](observer-runtime.md) OR01 PostgreSQL
SQLSTATE discussion, [observer transport](observer-transport.md) OT01–OT06 selected
Cloud Tasks deduplication/authentication sections, and [acquisition runner](acquisition-runner.md)
PI01/PI02/PI08 complete-update/pagination evidence. Reusing these mechanisms avoids
a second queue client or a second acquisition implementation. Delivery sidecars,
local budgets and conservative quarantine are project policy, not vendor guarantees.

Unit tests exercise unknown claim/settlement, bounded rollback retry, external calls
outside transactions, exact target identity, safe error classifications, Retry-After
rounding and cancellation. Actual PostgreSQL composition evidence is tracked in the
[stage runbook](../runbooks/acquisition-dispatch-runtime.md); synthetic proof does not
qualify hosted OIDC, Cloud Tasks delivery or live financial use.

documents.title: Acquisition dispatch SQL
documents.body:
# Acquisition dispatch SQL

## Reviewed decision and sources

Migration 15 proposes a narrow delivery bridge for #7. Existing requested/completed
sync generations and sync sets remain acquisition authority; no cursor or source
checkpoint is copied. Discovery includes initial generation 1 even without a wakeup
row. Queue identity, business claim identity and acquisition fence are distinct.

Reviewed official Google Cloud Tasks [overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/dual-overview)
(at-least-once delivery, task-name deduplication and task lifecycle), [HTTP task creation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/creating-http-target-tasks)
(explicit target/OIDC configuration) and [create API](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.queues.tasks/create)
on 2026-10-14. Facts: duplicate delivery is possible and named-task deduplication can
outlive a deleted task. Inference: durable SQL completion, not enqueue acknowledgement
or ALREADY_EXISTS, proves work; replacing a lost task needs a new dispatch generation
while retaining unresolved acquisition identity. Review covers those selected public
sections, not a cloud deployment or provider qualification.

Reuse [worker SQL](worker-sql.md), [background work](background-work.md),
[acquisition runner](acquisition-runner.md), [sync SQL](provider-sync-sql.md) and
[connection operations](connection-operations-sql.md). Internal work-wakeup-v1 with
fixed acquisition target profile 2 has no ISO 20022 business-message designation.
ISO currency/date source semantics and accounting policy are unchanged.

## Frozen interfaces

All functions belong to integration; UUID parameters name server-owned identities.
Publisher role is existing bookkeeping_publisher; consumer role is bookkeeping_sync,
with exact owner-enrolled actual login/scope checks. No new role or journal-observer
handler is introduced. All calls are short Serializable transactions; network and
acquisition.Run occur only after committed claims.

- `enroll_sync_delivery(actor,e,b,key,raw)` owner-only. JSON is
  `{publisher_login,worker_login,service_principal_id,enabled}`; immutable identity
  must match existing connection_worker, response `{binding_id,binding_revision}`.
- `sync_delivery_discover(binding,maximum)` returns `{created_count}` (maximum 25).
- `sync_delivery_candidates(binding,maximum)` returns `{operation_ids:[uuid]}`.
- `sync_delivery_recover(operation)` returns status no_change/retry_wait/
  redispatched/done/quarantined.
- `sync_delivery_dispatch_claim(operation,holder)` returns status
  claimed/not_due/done/quarantined, operation_id/entity_id/book_id,
  dispatch_generation string, target_version 2, task_name_hex, dispatch_fence
  string|null and lease_until timestamp|null.
- `sync_delivery_dispatch_result(operation,generation,holder,fence,result)` takes
  accepted/already_exists/timeout/transient/rejected and returns `{recorded:boolean}`.
- `sync_delivery_claim(operation,dispatch_generation,holder)` returns status
  claimed/done/busy/not_due/quarantined, operation_id/entity_id/book_id/stream_id,
  claim_id uuid|null, fence string|null, lease_until timestamp|null,
  deadline_at timestamp|null, target_version 2.
- `sync_delivery_settle(operation,holder,fence,outcome,retry_after_seconds)` accepts
  completed/retryable/permanent/unknown and returns done/retry_wait/quarantined/stale.

The task name is lowercase SHA-256(operation UUID + `|` + decimal dispatch generation
+ `|2`). Only IDs/version belong in the wakeup. Neither queue headers nor payload
select a principal, provider account, credentials, handler or SQL scope.

## State, authority and recovery

Migration 24 adds [explicit known-failure recovery](plaid-acquisition-recovery.md).
Terminal operations and receipts remain immutable. A separate recovery receipt
releases only a proven failed slot after an authorized manual request; automatic
discovery still leaves unresolved quarantine alone. Stream status exposes the
durable disposition and a fixed decoder diagnostic instead of equating queued
demand with running work.

The binding links one actual publisher login and the configured acquisition worker
login/service principal to one book. Disabling either binding or connection worker
mandate stops dispatch and consumption. Every replay rechecks role separation,
active principals/entity/book, service read/import membership and current source,
consent and Item authority. This does not revoke the worker's independent acquisition
SQL capability; revoke that source/service authority to stop all direct acquisition.

One operation captures demanded generation per stream. A partial unique index
retains quarantined operations in that stream slot. Success releases the slot;
demand arriving during acquisition therefore becomes a successor operation. Immutable
wakeup rows are intent evidence, not a second mutable checkpoint or consumed cursor.
Discovery and recovery are bounded to 25 candidates. Future retry waits, healthy
leases and accepted tasks awaiting their queue-loss interval cannot occupy the
candidate page ahead of due work.

Enqueue leases last 30 seconds; consumer leases last 120 seconds. The original and
deterministic pagination-restart sync claims, plus the stream's current inner lease,
are inspected before takeover. An expired outer lease never overrides a live inner
lease. A committed sync completion receipt independently proves success, including
when Runner or settlement acknowledgement was lost. Uncertain enqueue uses the same
task name; queue loss after 15 minutes advances dispatch identity, not business
identity. A committed retry handoff creates its next dispatch immediately and sets
its not-before time atomically, so it does not wait for queue-loss recovery.

Only known expired/failed acquisition state permits a new business claim. An
expired staging set is abandoned and fenced before replacement. A known retryable
settlement retains at least Retry-After (maximum 86,400 seconds; minimum scheduling
backoff 5 seconds). Eight failed claims or 24 hours from first execution quarantine
the operation. No new webhook resets these budgets. A lost provider-failure
classification cannot reconstruct Retry-After from an abandoned set: recovery
quarantines `outcome_unknown`, requiring future explicit operator recovery. No
automatic repair or administrative reset is included in this slice.

Permanent quarantine fences this operation's original/derived staging set so a late
worker cannot publish after termination. Immutable enqueue and run receipts preserve
exact replay results after current authorization. Queue acknowledgement never posts a
journal and never substitutes for a source completion receipt. Fixed SQL errors
P2900–P2905 denote malformed, denied, conflict, stale, state and bounds; no credential
or raw provider payload belongs in delivery tables or responses.

The 24-hour limit prohibits new claims and redispatch; it is also the cooperative
Runner deadline. Completion receipts have no immutable completion timestamp, so SQL
does not prove publication occurred before that cutoff. A real durable receipt
still wins when discovered later: elapsed delivery age cannot erase published
source evidence or falsely report it as failed.

documents.title: Bounded synthetic acquisition runner
documents.body:
# Bounded synthetic acquisition runner

## Reviewed decision

Coordinator approved this #102 profile before implementation. Go composes the
existing exact Plaid decoder and SQL complete-set publication. No network or storage
call holds a database transaction; acquisition never posts journals. SQL owns current
consent, service/account authority, generation, fencing and atomic cursor publication.
This slice uses injected synthetic credentials/providers and private local evidence;
it does not activate Plaid, Sandbox, cloud storage, scheduled delivery or live books.
The proprietary `jayburd-plaid-transactions/1`, API `2020-09-14`, ISO currency/date
mapping and STD-01 assessment remain as in [sync SQL](provider-sync-sql.md).

## Callable composition

`New(Beginner, Provider, CredentialResolver, EvidenceStore)` returns a Runner.
`Run(ctx, Scope{EntityID,BookID,StreamID}, claimUUID)` runs one bounded acquisition.
The caller persists/reuses the same canonical claim UUID until its outcome is known;
a new UUID is an explicit fresh attempt, never an automatic unknown-commit retry.
`SQLRepository` supplies compiled, parameterized calls through a restricted sync
pool. No connection string, caller actor, destination URL or secret comes from a
wakeup. Outcome contains only status and counts; errors expose fixed classifications.

`CredentialResolver.Resolve(ctx, CredentialReference{ReferenceID,Version,ItemID,
Environment})` returns memory-only access/client credentials. The resolver validates
stored reference/version/Item/environment binding. It must honor cancellation and
must not log tokens. No resolver discovers files/environment/ADC in this package.
`NewPlaidHTTP(http.RoundTripper)` pins HTTPS sandbox.plaid.com/transactions/sync,
Plaid-Version, account filter, count500 and original-description inclusion.
Credentials are injected on each call; redirects and automatic provider retries are
forbidden. Full response bytes are capped at2MiB and parsed without float conversion.

## SQL and recovery protocol

Each SQL call has4s active budget plus independent1s rollback,3s statement/1s lock
limits and at most3 confirmed40001/40P01 retries. Unknown COMMIT exposes no prepared
result and stops acquisition. Role checks reject SET ROLE and mixed privileged,
API, owner, observer, publisher and identity capabilities. SQL remains authority.

`sync_resume(e,b,stream,claimUUID)` reauthorizes before returning absent, staging,
completed, abandoned or quarantined; it includes set/fence/reason and an optional
committed receipt. Completed replay returns that receipt without provider access.
`sync_context(e,b,stream,set,fence)` reauthorizes a live attempt and returns only
approved account/currency metadata, opaque credential reference/version, Item pins,
cursor/page/counts, lease and exact limits. No token crosses SQL.

Issue #225 adds bounded `currency_versions` for the bound monetary identity.
Resolve each source date against its installed version; retain singleton `currency`
for compatibility. [History contract](plaid-history-currency.md) defines source
evidence, migration ordering and unchanged bookkeeping-date gates.

Order: resume/claim COMMIT → context → existing evidence lookup. For a missing page:
context → credential read → fresh context → provider request → exact decode → fresh
context → durable private evidence. Then stage COMMIT; after the final page, complete
COMMIT. Revocation after an external request may leave in-flight bytes in memory;
no stage/publication can bypass current SQL authorization. Context cancellation never
means a blocked arbitrary dependency was forcibly terminated.

A stage COMMIT with lost reply is recovered by the same claim UUID and SQL page
position; if it did not commit, replay the same retained raw bytes/normalized page,
not a new provider response. Unknown completion resolves through sync_resume.
Unknown claim cannot authorize any credential or provider call until recovered.

A pagination mutation abandons the entire set and restarts from committed C0 once,
using a deterministic second claim UUID. Its reason is durable for process replay.
Other ambiguous provider/transient failures abandon and return retryable status;
new acquisition begins C0 with a new explicitly chosen claim. No partial page retry
or partial cursor publication. Failed cleanup prevents internal restart.

## Bounds and evidence

Run budget60s; provider call10s; credential read5s. SQL permits10pages,500changes/page,
1000changes and2MiB normalized complete set with90s lease. This runner additionally
caps total retained raw bytes at2MiB, a stricter project bound, not a Plaid limit.
One mutation restart at most; no invented durable retry scheduler or50k-row claim.

`LocalEvidence` composes the existing synthetic-only [staging store](import-staging.md).
Generated stable UUIDs bind entity/book/stream/set/page and chunk identity; no caller
path. Up to two1MiB immutable chunks precede an immutable manifest. Read validates
scope, cursor, lengths and digests, then Put replay compares complete bytes. Manifest
publication occurs last. Chunk/manifest fsync/no-replace/0700root/0600file and symlink
rules come from staging. Delete tombstones the manifest before both chunks, preventing
late resurrection; lifecycle metadata remains. Partial writes are private orphans,
not SQL-published evidence. Retention and encrypted hosted storage remain future work.

## Primary sources and alternatives

Reviewed2026-10-13 from PI01/PI02/PI08 in the [source register](../research/plaid-ingestion-sources.md):

- [Plaid Transactions API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/),
  sync pagination, options.account_id, count and response fields. Each filtered
  account has its own cursor. Original source bytes and signed amount lexemes are
  retained; SDK float conversion is deliberately avoided.
- [Sync migration guide](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/sync-migration/),
  complete update application and pagination mutation restart from original C0.
  Our private staging/SQL publication and bounded restart are project inferences.
- Existing pinned pgx retry/commit evidence in [observer runtime](observer-runtime.md)
  and [import service](import-service.md), and filesystem mechanisms in staging.

Alternative: adopt partially staged provider pages across expired leases. Rejected
for this slice because the merged SQL contract intentionally starts a new set at C0.
Cloud object storage and an SDK may replace injected implementations only after
preserving exact bytes, bounded cancellation and unknown-outcome semantics.

## Provider retry instruction

Retry-After seconds or HTTP-date values are preserved up to24hours. Longer values
produce retry_deferred, never a shortened automatic retry. Invalid or past values
use five seconds. Outcome is a proposed caller instruction only: this slice has no
scheduler and performs no delayed retry. Injected dependency errors are reduced to
a closed public classification; whole credential objects reject JSON and redact
formatted representations. Individual credential fields are deliberately available
only for the provider request builder and must not be logged.

documents.title: Acquisition transport and host
documents.body:
# Acquisition transport and host

## Decision and sources

Reuse owned observer transport mechanisms through explicit acquisition constructors;
keep journal observation and acquisition separate fixed profiles. No caller chooses
a handler, scope, provider URL or credential. This is the #7 synthetic implementation
slice; it creates no Cloud Run service, task, identity or provider connection.

Refreshed BW02/BW03: Google Cloud [issues and limitations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/common-pitfalls),
duplicate delivery/order and throttling; [HTTP tasks](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/creating-http-target-tasks),
OIDC service-account authentication; [Task REST v2](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.queues.tasks),
dispatch deadline. These facts require durable deduplication and authorization;
they do not promise process cancellation or business completion. Deadline and pool
budgets below are project policy, not Cloud Tasks recommendations.

Alternative: a generic request-selected handler factory. Rejected because a valid
journal wakeup must never select provider acquisition. Duplicating authentication
and queue clients would also create two implementations of the same security rules.

## Fixed profiles

| Profile | HTTP paths | Target version / task digest | Budgets |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Existing journal observer | `/internal/observer/publish`, `/internal/observer/consume` | 1; existing SHA-256 of operation UUID, dispatch generation and 1 separated by pipes | Existing 60-second HTTP / 65-second task unchanged. |
| Acquisition | `/internal/acquisition/publish`, `/internal/acquisition/consume` | 2; SHA-256 of operation UUID, dispatch generation and 2 separated by pipes | 80-second HTTP / 85-second task / 90-second server write. |

Both use the exact identifier-only `work-wakeup-v1` envelope. Acquisition SQL loads
only its own operation table under current enrolled publisher/worker authority.
A structurally valid foreign operation ID fails; authentication never grants scope.
Constructors pin HTTPS Cloud Run destination, audience, invocation email and subject;
task metadata and arbitrary headers are not credentials. No browser route is added.

Acquisition reserves time around its 60-second runner for verified identity, request
read, claim and settle. A 120-second delivery lease is not acquisition authority:
takeover must additionally wait for any original or pagination-restart set lease.
Unknown commits preserve stable claims. Only confirmed durable outcomes/handoffs
can acknowledge delivery. Queue creation/409 is never completion.

## Host and acceptance

An injected lifecycle host sets read-header/read limits, bounded header bytes,
idle/write timeouts and shutdown budget. It does not discover credentials or choose
SQL/provider dependencies. Explicit composition remains necessary for deployment.
Internal scheduling messages have no selected ISO 20022 financial designation;
STD-01 and existing currency/accounting boundaries remain unchanged.

Named acceptance: acquisition profile isolation, OIDC-before-body rejection,
deadline/overload/cancellation, exact queue identity and no cross-profile enqueue;
actual SQL/runner tests prove replay, recovery and source publication separately.
Executed evidence belongs in the [delivery runbook](../runbooks/acquisition-dispatch.md).

documents.title: Ledger HTTP API contract
documents.body:
# Ledger HTTP API contract

## Status and authority

OpenAPI 3.1.1 implementation-review contract: [machine-readable definition](../../api/openapi.json).
An HTTP adapter and [bounded server composition](server.md) are implemented;
default health-only mode mounts no bookkeeping routes. No deployed verifier or
public service is provided. A managed identity adapter
and atomic `POST /v1/setup` are specified by the
[identity/setup contract](identity-setup.md). The specification describes the first posting/read/reversal/
close/report interface; transport validation is not accounting approval. Every
operation also follows [SQL invariants](ledger-sql.md) and [money semantics](multicurrency.md).
The [posting boundary](posting-boundary.md) specifies the first executable slice.
Close is explicitly deferred pending reviewed close-evidence storage/workflows;
its documented route must not be mounted by the first server.

## Operations and permissions

Ledger routes start `/v1/entities/{entity_id}/books/{book_id}`; the separate
`POST /v1/setup` route creates a new scope. `GET /v1/workspace` returns bounded,
currently readable configuration under the [workspace contract](server.md#workspace-contract).
The UI uses the [durable command contract](command-recovery.md): register with
`POST /v1/commands`, discover via `GET /v1/commands/pending`, and explicitly
execute, cancel or acknowledge via `POST /v1/commands/{command_id}/{action}`.
These transitions use the command ID and empty object body; only registration
requires an `Idempotency-Key`. Current read/post authority applies on recovery.
Legacy direct endpoints below retain their independent replay obligations.
Authentication is
bearer-token transport; issuer/audience binding, MFA and revocation follow the identity/setup contract;
the actual GCP project remains a deployment decision. No actor ID is accepted from request JSON.

| Method and suffix | Permission | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POST `/journals` | post | 201 committed manual identity/spot journal |
| GET `/journals/{journal_id}` | read | 200 immutable journal with valuation provenance |
| POST `/journals/{journal_id}/reversals` | post | 201 exact linked reversal; no client-generated replacement lines |
| POST `/periods/{period_id}/close` | close | 200 closed period; fails without valid reviewed evidence |
| GET `/trial-balance?through_date=YYYY-MM-DD` | read | 200 cumulative debit/credit balances through date, policy currency and snapshot revision |

These are local bookkeeping operations, not registered ISO 20022 messages.
Applicability review: currency codes use ISO 4217 metadata; banking/payment
exchange definitions are not assigned to these internal operations. ISO audit-data
mappings remain required for future exports; the trial-balance HTTP response is
not asserted to be an ISO audit export. Any later financial interchange adapter
must select its exact definition/profile under the [standards contract](standards.md).

## Request and replay rules

Amounts are decimal strings, revisions are unsigned decimal strings within the
SQL bigint range, and IDs are UUID strings. Business dates have no timezone;
operational timestamps use RFC 3339 UTC. Reject unknown/duplicate JSON fields.
The selected request limit is 1 MiB and 1,000 journal lines; these are engineering
bounds for the first implementation. Unknown account/currency/rate references,
invalid dates and overflow fail before any durable journal writes.

Ledger mutation requests require `Idempotency-Key` and `expected_revision`.
Setup requires the key but creates its initial revision in SQL. The SQL
contract defines scope/canonicalization/actor binding. The expected revision is
optimistic concurrency, not authorization. Successful retries return original
status and body with `Idempotent-Replay: true`, even if the period later closes,
provided the actor is still authorized. A stale revision on new work conflicts;
a known successful receipt is resolved first. After timeout or 503, resend the
same key and body. If a receipt may exist, do not change the expected revision
under the same key. Changes after a confirmed conflict use a new key.

## Errors and response safety

Use RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with stable type URI, title, status,
project `code`, and request ID. Detail contains a safe actionable explanation,
never SQL, tokens, provider payloads or another entity's identifiers. Public
problem-document URLs require a reviewed deployment base. Until deployment,
the review convention is `https://bookkeeping.example.invalid/problems/{code}`;
this is a non-routable example, not a deployed documentation URL. Select the real
base before publishing `/v1` and keep each problem type stable thereafter.

| Status | Code examples / handling |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | invalid_request: malformed JSON, duplicate fields, missing headers |
| 401 | unauthenticated: missing/invalid bearer token; WWW-Authenticate: Bearer |
| 403 | permission_denied: known accessible scope, insufficient operation permission |
| 404 | not_found: absent resource or inaccessible entity/book; indistinguishable |
| 409 | revision_conflict, idempotency_conflict, pending_command, invalid_command_state, period_closed, already_reversed, close_evidence_stale |
| 413 | request_too_large: body limit exceeded |
| 422 | invalid_journal, invalid_amount, unsupported_policy, result_out_of_range, close_evidence_required |
| 500 | internal_error: unexpected failure, generic detail and request ID only |
| 503 | temporarily_unavailable: exhausted retry/deadline, Retry-After; replay same key |

All financial responses use `Cache-Control: no-store`. Journal responses preserve
original currency amounts, functional currency, policy and selected rate IDs.
No partial response claims posting succeeded. No POST is acknowledged with 202
for a journal whose transaction has not committed.

## Acceptance and evolution

OpenAPI documents shape, not cross-line sums, database reference validity or
permission enforcement. `TestAPIContract` must cover valid requests, extra fields,
malformed money, absent credentials, denied scope, redacted problems, replay after
close/revocation and revision conflicts. SQL test names remain in the SQL contract.
Keep changes backward-compatible within `/v1`; new required request fields or
semantic reinterpretations require an explicit version/migration decision.

Further entity/book/account management, draft approvals, journal lists/pagination, statement
import, reconciliation, settlement, revaluation and exports are separate next
slices. Their durable obligations are recorded in the SQL contract; they have no
invented placeholder HTTP endpoints here. First implementable slice is manual
identity/spot posting and reads under ADR 0005 and the posting boundary, then exact reversal.
An internal synthetic identity adapter may exercise SQL tests, but cannot stand
in for a production bearer-token verifier.

documents.title: Public sign-in configuration availability
documents.body:
# Public sign-in configuration availability

## Decision and applicability

#289, 2026-10-24. This presentation/composition slice keeps the existing
[browser authentication](browser-auth.md) authority and public configuration
allowlist intact. Bootstrap availability is separate from verified session state.
It is not a financial exchange or an ISO20022 message; financial/currency payloads
and standards mappings are unchanged. No API/SQL/schema, persistence or new identity
mechanism. Reviewed existing browser-auth and identity-setup contracts and their
canonical browser-auth-sources reference selections; no new external API claim.

## States and recovery

Initial mount, source change and explicit retry render loading, without login
inputs or the missing-installation warning. Runtime configuration fetch retains
no-store/omit credentials/no redirect and a five-second timeout. Network,
timeout, non-success HTTP and incomplete JSON transport failures show generic
temporary unavailability with one explicit retry control. No automatic retries,
raw diagnostics, secrets or session resurrection.
The pre-hydration server shell also renders loading; it cannot classify the
browser's runtime configuration before that request. The exact-image smoke
requires this shell without password inputs, while separately requiring absent
runtime configuration to return503/no-store and finance/demo routes to deny.

Successful HTTP/supplied configuration must pass the existing exact public-field
validation. Invalid configuration, unavailable SDK adapter or conflicting SDK
installation remains operator-only invalid configuration with no fallback source.
Only a valid initialized controller enters ready. Existing verified email/TOTP,
memory-only persistence, fresh token/revocation and API permission rules stand.

An exact configuration-source identity and attempt revision fence snapshots.
Source/retry changes immediately mask the previous controller before effect
cleanup; abort/unmount fences late fetch/JSON responses even if transport ignores
abort. Cleanup signs out any initialized old controller, invalidating pending
SDK results through existing epochs. Retry is offered only for unavailable
bootstrap, never to reset an active verified session. No browser persistence.

## Alternatives and evidence

Keeping unconfigured for every failure conflates installation with loading and
offers no recovery. Automatic retries add repeated requests and hide the user
action; choose bounded fetch plus explicit retry. Replacing controller auth phases
would mix availability with verified identity and expand the trust boundary;
choose separate bootstrap state and preserve controller/Firebase code.

Acceptance: delayed valid config never displays invalid installation; HTTP503,
network and timeout retry restores inputs; invalid/supplied-conflicting settings
stay denied; unmounted/stale requests cannot initialize SDK or resurrect a session;
source changes sign out and mask the prior controller. Component and browser
fixtures remain credential-free. Required core/web/full-stack gates and a marked
runbook; actual managed-browser sign-in evidence remains separate. Sensitive
authentication composition needs review before release, without relaxing identity.

documents.title: Automatic ledger accounts for provider binding
documents.body:
# Automatic ledger accounts for provider binding

## Decision record

**Question and scope.** When a verified new Plaid Item contains several selected
depository accounts, how can a creator bind all of them without first editing the
chart of accounts? This contract covers new depository bindings only. Credit and
loan policy is deferred to #210; investments and unknown types remain unbound.

**Status and owner.** Accepted for #209 by owner direction on 2026-10-19.

**Sources.** The existing [connection SQL contract](connection-sql.md) establishes
one provider account, source account and ledger account per binding. The
[accounting contract](accounting.md) establishes asset/debit/monetary semantics.
Plaid's [Accounts API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/) account `type`,
`subtype`, `account_id` and currency fields were reviewed on 2026-10-19. The
[Sandbox guide](https://plaid.com/docs/sandbox/) was reviewed for fictional
multi-account behavior and default test credentials. PostgreSQL 17 documentation
for [transaction isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/transaction-iso.html)
and [function security](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/perm-functions.html)
remains registered as S08/S12 in the database source register.

**Review depth and evidence.** Only the named Plaid field definitions and Sandbox
credential/multi-account sections were reviewed. Plaid establishes provider
metadata, not ledger classification. PostgreSQL establishes transaction and
privilege mechanisms; Jayburd owns the atomic command and retry policy.
The detailed source record and product-profile interpretation are in
[automatic account binding sources](../research/automatic-account-binding-sources.md).

## Provider support profile

Plaid's current account-type schema recognizes six top-level types:
`depository`, `credit`, `loan`, `investment`, `other` and `payroll`. Plaid also
publishes type/subtype combinations and a product support matrix. Those describe
provider data availability; they do not authorize a Jayburd ledger category.

Issue #209 permits automatic creation only when the verified manifest contains:

- `type: depository`;
- `subtype` equal to `checking`, `savings`, `money market` or
  `cash management`;
- exactly one ISO 4217 currency identifier that resolves to an installed currency
  version on the binding date.

Plaid depository subtypes `cd`, `ebt`, `hsa`, `limited purpose checking`,
`paypal` and `prepaid` remain visible and unbound in this slice because their
ownership, restriction or presentation semantics require an explicit policy.
Missing and unrecognized subtypes also remain unbound. `credit` and `loan` are
deferred to #210. `investment`, `other` and `payroll` require separate contracts.
The allowlist is versioned Jayburd policy and must not expand merely because Plaid
adds or renames a type or subtype.

**Interpretation.** Each selected depository account needs a separate monetary
asset ledger account so its balance, observations and reconciliation remain
separate. The creator must review the proposed code, name, currency and active
date. Provider type/subtype may seed a neutral label but never authorizes an
accounting policy or opening balance.

**Alternatives.** Requiring pre-created accounts preserves the existing API but
breaks the ordinary Plaid journey. A separate create-accounts command exposes a
partial state and a second retry boundary. Creating accounts in the existing
binding command preserves explicit review and makes account creation, source
binding, permissions, stream activation and receipt one atomic operation.

**Uncertainty.** Provider subtype can be absent or change. Code suggestions can
race another chart edit. Unknown types, missing currency and conflicting codes
must fail closed or remain unbound. The first slice does not create credit, loan,
investment or opening-balance entries.

## Request and invariants

`ConnectionBindingRequest.bindings[]` retains `ledger_account_id`. It adds an
optional `new_ledger_account` object with exactly:

- `account_id`, equal to `ledger_account_id`, generated before submission;
- owner-reviewed `code` and `name`;
- fixed `category: asset`, `normal_side: debit`, `monetary: true`;
- `active_from`, equal to the reviewed binding date.

An existing-account binding omits `new_ledger_account`. A new-account binding
includes it. The same ledger account ID, code or provider account cannot appear
twice in one command. Codes and names use the existing ledger bounds. Every new
account's provider manifest entry must satisfy the exact provider support profile
above and have a supported ISO 4217 currency version valid on the binding date.
The server validates both `type` and `subtype`; browser eligibility is
presentation only and cannot broaden the server allowlist.

The browser proposes one new account per eligible provider account. Suggested
codes are derived from the current reviewed book snapshot in stable increments;
the creator can edit them. Suggested names use bounded provider subtype plus a
stable ordinal, never a provider account ID or balance. A conflicting or stale
proposal returns for review; neither SQL nor Go silently renumbers it.

## Atomicity and recovery

`integration.bind_connection` remains the single serializable command. Under the
current authority and attempt locks it checks the immutable manifest and complete
request, creates all requested ledger accounts, creates source accounts and
streams, grants capabilities, activates the Item/attempt and writes the existing
receipt. Any error rolls back the whole transaction.

The existing actor/scope/operation/idempotency-key receipt owns retry. A repeat
with the exact normalized body returns the recorded result. A different body for
the same key conflicts. Fixed client-generated ledger account IDs plus the receipt
make a lost acknowledgement recoverable without duplicate accounts. Binding makes
no Plaid call, creates no journal and records no opening balance.

## Standards applicability

This is an internal chart-setup command, not an ISO 20022 message. Currency
selection uses the installed ISO 4217 identifier/version and minor-unit record.
ISO 21378/21926 export mappings are unaffected. Provider JSON remains a documented
proprietary adapter; no ISO conformance is claimed.

## Acceptance

- `TestConnectionAutoAccountBinding`: three verified depository accounts create
  three distinct monetary asset ledger/source accounts and active streams.
- `TestConnectionAutoAccountAtomicity`: conflict and injected failure leave no
  partial ledger accounts, sources, grants, streams or activation.
- `TestConnectionAutoAccountReplay`: exact same-key replay returns the same account
  and stream identifiers; changed body and concurrent code collisions reject.
- Go and HTTP tests reject malformed account semantics, missing or unsupported
  provider type/subtype combinations, invalid currency/date and ledger-account ID
  mismatch before mutation.
- Browser tests default all eligible accounts to distinct proposals, permit
  existing-account selection and opt-out, and keep unsupported accounts visible.
- The full synthetic browser/API/PostgreSQL journey reaches review with zero
  automatically posted journals.

Follow-up #210 owns reviewed liability support. #88 owns the fresh hosted Sandbox
proof after deployment; #90 continues to gate live institutions.

documents.title: Available-to-use planning contract (proposal)
documents.body:
# Available-to-use planning contract (proposal)

## Decision record

**Status:** proposed for #251, 2026-10-21. Owner/accountant acceptance pending.
**Question:** How can one book show a dated estimate of cash left after named
commitments without presenting a balance, forecast or authorization as fact?
**Scope:** read-only Plan tool for one authorized entity/book, one original
currency bucket at a time. No cross-entity pooling, payment, reservation,
posting, provider write, or service grant. #248 must define Position and #1
must settle real policy before a live result is accepted. #56 must define any
future service role. [Source review](../research/available-to-use-sources.md)
separates sourced accounting facts from these product choices.

### Alternatives and provisional selection

| Model | Benefit | Failure mode / disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cash less one reserve number | Easy to explain and enter | Hides dates, double counts bills already paid, and implies a single universal spending limit. Retain as a clearly named *owner reserve* input, not the entire model. |
| Dated cash-flow scenario with explicit obligations and reserves | Answers “for what and by when?” and exposes timing/uncertainty | Needs reviewed due-date, source status and overlap rules. **Proposed** model, subject to owner/accountant review and fixed-case validation. |

### Proposed meaning and arithmetic

The displayed heading is **“Scenario headroom through DATE”**, never “cash
balance”, “spendable cash” or “approved to spend”. A context line identifies
book, scenario, as-of accounting date, generated time, horizon, currency and
source freshness. The posted cash figure is a ledger-derived input, not the
result. Exclude unposted provider observations from that figure.

For one selected cash account set and **one currency** `C`, define `B_C` as
the posted cash position at book revision `R` and accounting date `D`, subject
to #248's account membership/sign rules. Each future cash movement has signed
exact amount `m_i`, effective date `t_i`, source identity and status. For every
day `d` in `[D,H]`, the proposed curve is:

`P_C(d) = B_C + sum(m_i where D < t_i <= d) - F_C(d)`

where `F_C(d)` is the owner-entered minimum cash floor valid on `d`. The
proposed headroom is `min(P_C(d) for D <= d <= H)`, with the date of the minimum
shown. A one-day horizon is permitted. Treat due-date uncertainty as a range of
separate scenarios, never silently choose the optimistic date. Missing amounts,
ambiguous overlaps, unreviewed policy, unsupported FX, stale/unavailable Position
or authorization failure return **unknown/unavailable** with reasons rather
than zero. A negative result is shown signed and labeled **shortfall in this
scenario**; it never clamps to zero.

Only cash effects belong in `m_i`. A posted payable and its later planned cash
settlement may both be visible, but the payable itself is not subtracted from
cash until its anticipated payment date. A posted payment already reflected in
`B_C` must be excluded from future movements. Proposed stable movement keys and
explicit supersedes/settles links prevent overlapping import, owner assumption,
and later service forecasts from silently counting twice. If the overlap cannot
be decided, block the estimate. This is a design rule, not an implemented match.

No implicit exchange or functional-currency roll-up. Each original currency
quantity keeps its ISO 4217 version and units. Functional booked amounts and
valuation provenance can be displayed beside posted evidence, but a future
foreign-currency obligation requires an explicit dated rate *scenario* and
separate policy review before any combined functional estimate. Never reuse a
posted historic rate as a future forecast or add unlike units.

### Inputs, provenance and uncertainty

| Input | Origin | Required trace and freshness | Treatment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `B_C` posted position | Authorized ledger/reporting read under #248 | entity/book, cash account IDs, accounting date, book revision, policy/currency versions, journal trace, generated time | Exact posted amount for that revision; completeness of source acquisition is separate. |
| Observed source item | Bank/provider or statement staging | source ID/version, observed/effective timestamps, status, account binding and ingestion state | Context only until posted or explicitly promoted to a reviewed scenario movement; never alters posted cash. |
| Obligation or expected inflow | Owner entry, posted payable schedule, or future scoped service | origin ID, amount/currency, due date or range, creation/review timestamps, owner, confidence and source link | Scenario assumption. Posted liability is evidence, not an automatic cash deduction. |
