| Reserve floor | Owner entry | purpose, amount/currency, active dates, reviewer, version | Scenario constraint, not a ledger entry or held funds. |
| Adjustment | Owner entry | signed amount, reason, date, source/reviewer and expiry | Explicit scenario only; cannot correct ledger state. |

Confidence is displayed as **posted evidence / observed / owner assumption /
service proposal**, plus separate **confirmed / estimated / disputed / unknown**
review status. These labels do not express a statistical probability. A newer
source observation does not make an old book revision current. A refreshed book
revision invalidates a pinned scenario result until it is recalculated with
current read permission. Staleness threshold and escalation language require
owner review; v1 should show timestamps and a conservative unavailable state
rather than invent a universal threshold. Source errors and denied reads must
not reveal financial values or existence across books.

### Synthetic, independently worked illustrations

These decimal examples are fixed design expectations, not produced by code and
not approved live policy. Assume a fictional USD book, `D=2026-01-01`,
`H=2026-01-31`, exact opening posted cash `1000.00`, no other movements unless
specified, and a constant `100.00` reserve floor.

| Case | Inputs beyond base | Expected minimum and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sufficient | None | `1000.00 - 100.00 = 900.00` on D; scenario headroom `900.00`. |
| Committed obligation | `-600.00` due Jan 15, linked to a posted payable; payable itself has no second cash effect | Jan 15 projection `1000.00 - 600.00 - 100.00 = 300.00`; headroom `300.00`. |
| Uncertain item | Another `-250.00` with unknown amount or due date | `unknown`, with uncertain obligation ID; do not publish `300.00` as complete headroom. A separate explicitly incomplete scenario may still show the known `300.00` subtotal. |
| Multiple currencies | USD base above and distinct EUR `200.00` posted cash, EUR `50.00` floor | USD `900.00` and EUR `150.00` shown separately; no `1050.00` mixed-unit figure. |
| Stale/unavailable Position | Posted snapshot cannot be refreshed or authorized for selected revision | `unavailable`; previously cached `900.00` is not shown as a current result. |
| Negative | `-1100.00` due Jan 15 | Jan 15 `1000.00 - 1100.00 - 100.00 = -200.00`; display `-200.00` shortfall. |
| Timing | `-800.00` Jan 10; `+900.00` Jan 20 | Jan 10 `100.00`, Jan 20 `1000.00`; headroom `100.00`, not end-date `1000.00`. |

The first case's cash and reserve are synthetic assumptions. It does not prove
the book is reconciled, funds are legally available, or the plan is executable.

### Future service boundary (proposal only)

Later services may receive a separately approved, revocable **purpose, entity,
book, currency, account and amount/time bounded** capability. A service may
first submit a proposal that the owner reviews; reading a Plan estimate grants
no write capability. A future execution contract must define trusted workload
identity, enrollment, current permission check at execution, explicit approval,
idempotency, outbox/worker recovery, revocation and audit evidence. It must not
derive authority from a scenario ID, browser state, provider token or caller
actor ID. Revocation must prevent queued work from executing a new effect.
No capability schema or API is approved here.

### Standards applicability and acceptance gates

The Plan calculation and prospective internal JSON are local analytical
semantics: **ISO 20022 not applicable as a registered message** because there is
no financial institution exchange or selected registered business message.
Any later payment initiation must choose its actual ISO 20022 message version,
namespace and counterpart usage profile. Currency identifiers and minor-unit
metadata: **ISO 4217 applicable**, pin the release and validity interval via
the existing reference contract. **ISO 21378:2019 and ISO 21926:2026:** relevant
to eventual audit export/semantic mapping, unresolved at field level because
only public abstracts/preview were reviewed; no audit-conformance claim. An
internal Plan export, if proposed, needs a separate applicability and loss review.
No ISO designation is invented for this calculation. See the source register
for edition, review depth and gaps. The accounting framework and jurisdiction
remain governed by #1, not by ISO naming.

Before implementation, owner/accountant must approve eligible cash accounts,
whether available means general or purpose-limited funds, obligations and
reserve categories, timing horizon, uncertainty policy, stale thresholds,
entity restrictions, and treatment of foreign cash. #248 must settle Position
semantics; #56 must settle service authorization. Follow-on work must name
`TestPlanExactTimeline`, `TestPlanOverlapAndPaidExclusion`,
`TestPlanUnknownAndStale`, `TestPlanCurrencyIsolation`,
`TestPlanRevisionAndRevocation`, and fixed corpus cases above. Tests need a
separate oracle and synthetic fixtures. No endpoint, SQL object, UI component or
service permission exists because of this document.

### Open owner decisions

1. Which obligations count: posted payables with expected payment dates,
   manually entered commitments, debt minimums, tax estimates, or another
   reviewed set? How are paid/duplicated items resolved?
2. Are reserves hard purpose restrictions, owner planning floors, or both, and
   who may change each reserve?
3. What horizon and date convention answers the owner's first planning question,
   and what uncertainty or source age makes the estimate unavailable?
4. Is the view per book, per eligible cash account, or per restricted purpose?
   Which funds can never be pooled, even within one book?

These decisions gate Plan acceptance only. Position and Ledger may proceed under
their own approved contracts without waiting for this proposed metric.

documents.title: Background work contract
documents.body:
# Background work contract

## Decision and implementation boundary

**Proposed #63 design, 2026-10-13; implementation belongs to #7 under #57.**
Use PostgreSQL transactions for accounting and durable work state, Cloud Tasks
for directed HTTP wakeups, and bounded Go handlers. Pub/Sub remains deferred
until independent subscribers justify it. Sources BW01–BW05 and alternatives are
recorded in [background-work sources](../research/background-work-sources.md).
Provider acquisition details belong to #70; this document owns generic delivery,
identity, fencing and recovery requirements. No worker is implemented here.
The first #7 consumer is strictly `journal.observe` version1: reload one committed
journal/event pair and record durable consumption, with **no new posting**. This
is not a generic workflow engine; SQL allows only explicitly reviewed handler
versions, with provider acquisition a separately gated #70 extension.

Current migrations implement immutable `integration.outbox_message` rows:
`entity_id, book_id, message_id, event_type='journal.posted', event_version=1,
target_id, book_revision, created_at`; unique target per book, inserted in the
same transaction as journal, posting receipt and audit. No publisher, delivery
status, consumer receipt or lease exists. Do not UPDATE these rows or broaden
their event-type check to simulate jobs. `integration.operation_receipt` only
covers immutable post/reverse receipts. `ledger.interactive_command` covers
user setup/post recovery and one unacknowledged command per principal; neither
is a generic job table. New objects/functions require a reviewed forward migration.

## Facts, commands and applicability

`journal.posted` version 1 is a fact that journal `target_id` committed at
`book_revision` in its scope. Reversal journals also emit it; consumers reload
the immutable journal to learn its kind/reversal link. It contains no permission,
posting instruction, amount or source document. Reordering is allowed. The ledger
revision also advances for setup; consumers cannot assume contiguous event revisions
or wait for a missing event for every revision integer.

A directed command requests a named, versioned handler to perform work. Proposed
transport JSON `work-wakeup-v1` has exactly:
`{"schema_version":1,"operation_id":"<uuid>","dispatch_generation":"<positive integer>"}`.
Maximum 1024 UTF-8 bytes; reject unknown/duplicate keys, null, wrong versions and
noncanonical UUID/integer strings. It contains no amount, actor, entity, provider
token, cursor, account identifier, URL or arbitrary handler name. Load those
references from authorized durable records. Queue metadata is never business
identity. Command UUID is immutable across automatic retries and redispatch;
queue task IDs change only with persisted dispatch generation. A handler/version
and canonical request digest are fixed on the durable command at creation.

| Message/practice | Standards assessment and mapping |
| --- | --- |
| Internal `journal.posted` v1 | ISO 20022 external message encoding not selected/applicable for this internal committed-ledger notification: no bank counterparty or registered profile claimed. Preserve scoped journal UUID, book revision, event version and timestamp; do not call it a camt statement. BW05 reviews FAQ/methodology, not every message definition. This is a proposed bounded applicability interpretation requiring STD-01 review. |
| `work-wakeup-v1` | Internal scheduling envelope, not a payment/report instruction. No financial ISO message identifier/namespace invented. Validate exact version/IDs; money/currency mapping occurs only in the owned financial operation, never this envelope. |
| Financial effects or provider messages | Existing accounting, multicurrency and standards contracts remain authority. ISO 4217 versioned currencies and applicable ISO 20022 profile mappings are required in those operation contracts. Generic retries do not approve missing mappings or automated posting. |
| Worker/audit receipts | Internal execution evidence. ISO 21378:2019 / ISO 21926:2026 audit exchange mapping unresolved; no audit-export conformance claim. Preserve stable provenance for future mapping without inventing normative fields. |

STD-01 review of the above scope and named version/replay tests are implementation
gates. Normative accounting/ISO export gaps block the corresponding financial
adapter, not safe internal contract review.

## Proposed durable records and uniqueness

These are logical SQL contracts, **not approved physical DDL**. All scope keys
must participate in foreign keys/uniqueness; UUIDs alone never authorize access.

| Proposed record | Required meaning and key |
| --- | --- |
| `integration.work_operation` | UUID, handler/version, canonical request digest, authority reference, scoped resource/connection reference, creation time, state, business attempt count, next eligible time, deadline, current worker/fence/lease and terminal outcome reference. Financial request bodies stay in their owned protected store. Unique semantic key prevents duplicate operation creation. |
| `integration.outbox_delivery` | Sidecar linking event UUID + consumer/version to exactly one work operation; uniqueness on that tuple. A configured consumer is mandatory before fanout. Unconsumed historical events remain intact; do not mark all old rows delivered implicitly. |
| `integration.work_dispatch` | Operation UUID + dispatch generation; queue/target configuration version, deterministic task-name digest, pending/publishing/enqueued/uncertain/retired state, enqueue attempts, last attempt/result time, publisher fence/lease. No completion semantics. |
| `integration.work_receipt` | Immutable outcome per `(operation_id, execution_generation)` with request digest, handler/version, fence, scoped result references, fixed outcome code, timestamps and authorization evidence version. Successful terminal effect has a unique operation completion guard, regardless of queue generation. |
| `integration.work_attempt` | Append-only bounded metadata: operation, attempt UUID, fence, start/end, classified outcome, duration, no raw exception/provider body/credential/cursor. |

A stable semantic key for event work is `(scope,message_id,consumer_id,handler_version)`;
for connection work it is `(connection_id,connection_generation,target_generation,handler_version)`.
Same key/different digest rejects conflict. Existing receipts are never overwritten.
New handler versions do not automatically replay historical financial effects:
consumer rollout/backfill needs an explicit reviewed replay scope and effect key.

Work state transitions:
`ready -> running -> succeeded | retry_wait | blocked | cancelled | quarantined`;
`retry_wait -> running` when eligible; expired `running` may be reclaimed only
under a new fence. `succeeded` and `cancelled` are terminal. `blocked` requires a
specific corrective action (for example renewed consent), not timer-only retry.
`quarantined` requires explicit authorized retry/replacement with reason and audit.
Do not delete terminal receipts or reset counters to conceal failures.

## Identity and authority

Separate publisher identity (read/claim/ack dispatch and enqueue configured queue),
Cloud Tasks invocation identity (invoke exact handler/audience), and consumer
identity (owned claim/commit functions and required provider access). No worker
inherits database owner/migrator, unrestricted ledger tables or arbitrary URL
invocation. Runtime IAM/SQL grants remain a reviewed #7/#26 deployment gate.
OIDC verification pins issuer, audience and permitted service principal; Cloud Run
invoker IAM plus application binding to the configured handler protects invocation.
Task headers/name alone are not authentication. Invalid caller/envelope gets
401/403/400 and no business claim; bounded telemetry alerts on repeated rejects.

A service token authenticates workload, not authority over an LLC. Reload current
entity/book enablement and the operation's authority before claim, before each
external call and in the commit transaction. User-delegated operations require
current principal/membership; scheduled connection work uses a separately approved,
revocable connection mandate and permitted account scope. An event's original
poster is provenance, not perpetual delegated authority. Do not invent membership
from an OIDC subject or allow the service to post merely because it can fetch data.
The first consumer needs an explicitly provisioned service principal with scoped
read authority, separate from the original poster; provisioning/grants remain
implementation gates. No authorized mandate means no dispatch for that work type.

Revocation updates the same authority/resource rows locked by claim/commit and
increments connection generation/fence where applicable. A call authorized before
revocation may already be in flight; cancellation is best effort. Recheck after
return and discard/stage-clean according to #70 policy, never publish protected
results under revoked scope. A commit authorized/locked first may finish before
revocation commits; later work fails. Existing completed receipts may suppress
reexecution after revocation but return only a fixed empty task acknowledgement,
never old financial output to the caller. Terminal receipt lookup itself is scoped
to the authenticated configured consumer.

## Publisher and fast-consumer race

1. A business producer commits owned state and work intent together. Journal
   consumers derive unique sidecars/operations from immutable outbox facts in a
   bounded repeatable scan; absent sidecar is discoverable after a crash.
2. Claim due dispatch rows ordered by eligible time/UUID using short transactions
   and `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. Increment publisher fence, set database-clock
   lease, commit. Never keep the transaction open during enqueue.
3. Create task with a deterministic hash of operation UUID + dispatch generation
   + configured target version. Resolve target from allowlisted config, never data.
4. On enqueue acknowledgement, compare-and-set the matching publisher fence and
   dispatch generation only. **Never set work state to running/succeeded or back
   to ready here.** A fast consumer may finish before the publisher records enqueue.
   Its durable receipt wins; a delayed publisher acknowledgement cannot undo it.
5. Enqueue timeout is uncertain, not proof of absence. Retry the same task identity
   first. `ALREADY_EXISTS` may describe an active or recently deleted task: it is
   deduplication evidence, not business success or proof a future delivery exists.
   Record that distinction. If work remains due, recovery can issue a new persisted
   dispatch generation under its lock; old/new deliveries still deduplicate by
   operation/effect identity.

Publisher leases/fences protect dispatch metadata only. They are distinct from
consumer fences and must never authorize business completion. Lease expiry is
eligibility for takeover, not proof the old network request stopped.

## Consumer fencing and receipts

Claim by operation UUID under current authorization. A successful **terminal**
receipt returns 204 without effect; terminal denial returns 204 only after durable
outcome recording. A successful intermediate-step receipt is not operation
completion: its durable continuation must remain eligible/discoverable, and replay
must neither repeat that step nor suppress the remaining work.
An active unexpired claim returns 503/Retry-After without consuming a business
attempt. An eligible claim increments the resource fence and business attempt,
sets `running`, increments the work `execution_generation` (starts at0, first
claim1; monotonic for every accepted claim), and sets the database-clock lease,
then commits. One immutable receipt per execution generation records a bounded
step/terminal outcome; the separate unique successful-operation guard prevents
two generations from completing the same effect. Resource-level serialization
is required for connection work: two
operations on one connection cannot each hold an effective fence.

Database time is authority; use a fresh server time when checking lease, not a
worker clock or the transaction-start timestamp after a long wait. Heartbeat
requires matching holder, fence, generation and unexpired lease; expired holders
cannot revive themselves. After a failed heartbeat or request cancellation, stop
new external calls. Commit always validates the fence even if cancellation was lost.

For a local effect, one transaction locks authority/resource/work rows in a
consistent reviewed order, checks holder/fence/unexpired lease/current generation,
request digest and eligibility, applies the **owned** operation, writes its receipt
and marks completion. Any failed predicate rolls back all domain state/checkpoints.
When an effect uses ledger posting, it must invoke its owned SQL operation and
idempotency contract with explicitly approved authorization; never duplicate
posting rules in Go. No automated financial mutation consumer is approved by this task.
For `journal.observe` v1, verify event scope, target UUID, type/version and book
revision equal the immutable journal header, then insert the unique consumption
receipt in the same authorized transaction. A mismatch quarantines without any
ledger write. Its only effect is the receipt; no additional outbox or posting.

External side effects cannot become atomic with SQL by writing a receipt afterward.
Require provider idempotency key based on stable operation identity, or a durable
`uncertain` attempt and status reconciliation before retry. When neither exists,
quarantine; never blindly repeat an irreversible call. Initial #70 acquisition is
read-only and cannot initiate payments or change provider accounts.

204 acknowledgement follows committed completion, durable terminal outcome, or a
committed continuation handoff. A committed continuation means the bounded step
ended but the operation may remain incomplete; work status must say so. If receipt
commit fails after a response was prepared, return non-2xx. If commit result is
uncertain, reread receipt under fresh authorization before reexecuting. Crashes
between effect/receipt/ack are named fault-test boundaries, not exactly-once claims.

## Per-connection catch-up interface with #70

In #70 a connection is one approved provider account stream (an Item/account
binding), not automatically an entire provider Item. Shared credential grouping
does not widen authority. One effective writer/fence per connection stream.
Distinct counters: `connection_generation` changes on reconnect/revocation/scope
reset; `fence_token` changes on worker takeover; `requested_generation` increments
for accepted wakeups/catch-up requests; `target_generation` is captured by a run;
`completed_generation` advances only after complete accepted acquisition. None is
`ledger.book.revision`. Provider `source_revision` advances only on published
source changes and is not a bookkeeping revision or posting approval.

Webhook/scheduler commits `requested_generation += 1` and ensures durable eligible
work in one transaction. Coalescing reduces queue tasks, not this durable demand.
A run captures the target then follows #70's staging/cursor contract. A partial
page can persist a protected staging continuation plus next-step work atomically;
it does not advance committed provider cursor or completed generation.

The complete-update commit validates connection generation/fence/lease, current
mandate/scope, expected committed checkpoint and batch completeness; publishes
normalized changes, checkpoint, source revision, operation receipt and completed
generation atomically. While holding the connection lock, if requested generation
exceeds completed generation, create/ensure the next eligible operation. A wakeup
arriving afterward takes the same lock and creates work itself. Thus neither race
can silently erase a wakeup. Duplicate external notifications may cause an empty
catch-up, never duplicate accounting effects. Provider-specific changed/removed
records, cursor invalidation and mutation-during-pagination belong to #70.

## Bounds, retry, queue loss and operator recovery

Proposed initial settings require synthetic measurement and pool-budget review:
publisher batch <=25, at most one enqueue call at a time, 30-second publisher
lease; handler work budget 60 seconds/<=10 provider pages, each provider call <=20
seconds (also bounded by remaining handler budget); consumer lease 90 seconds,
heartbeat <=30 seconds; Cloud Tasks deadline 90 seconds. SQL transactions use
5-second statement and 1-second lock timeout. Enqueue RPC <=10 seconds. No lease
renewal permits exceeding the handler budget. Durable continuation splits longer
acquisition; #70 owns complete-update size/age caps. Consumer pool max1 per instance,
max1 instance, queue concurrency1 preserve the accepted #7 baseline and must fit the existing
shared database budget including overlapping revisions. No deployment tuning claim.

Accepted claims increment `attempt_count`; failed attempts separately increment
`failed_attempt_count` exactly once when ending retryably/permanently or when
an expired running attempt is atomically abandoned during takeover. Delivery
duplicates, authorization rejects and active-lease contention increment neither.
Successful continuations increment attempts but not failures. Append-only attempt
identity prevents two recovery scanners counting the same crash twice.

Application retry is durable: jittered exponential delay starting 5 seconds,
cap15 minutes, honor longer provider Retry-After, maximum8 failed business attempts
or24 hours elapsed since first claim, **whichever comes first**, then quarantine.
Successful bounded continuation does not count as a failed attempt; provider batch
limits still prevent endless work. Distinguish transient timeout/429/5xx from
permanent malformed/version/semantic errors and blocked consent. Administrative
retry records reason and an explicit additional attempt/age budget, rechecks
authority and allocates a new execution generation on the next claim. Cumulative
counters/history and semantic effect key remain unchanged; completed operations
are never retried as new work. A reviewed budget grant, not a counter reset,
allows an operator to resume quarantined work.

Cloud Tasks retry is delivery assistance, not this attempt budget. Google currently
documents attempt/duration stopping conditions jointly; do not assume an OR cutoff
from queue configuration. Hard application limits are checked in SQL even if the
queue keeps delivering. Use bounded backoff settings reviewed with the runtime;
no reliance on unlimited task lifetime or task-name deduplication retention.

A scheduled bounded recovery scan checks durable due/retry/expired-running work,
missing sidecars, and enqueued work lacking a terminal receipt/active lease. It
can atomically retire a stale dispatch generation and create a new one, retaining
the same operation. Initial stale-dispatch threshold15 minutes; sweep cadence1
minute is a proposal to measure against #12 costs, not a latency guarantee. Queue
purge, retention expiry, max retries, missed scheduler ticks and publisher downtime
cannot delete durable business intent. Duplicate old task deliveries remain safe.
The accepted #7 activation is every-minute Scheduler to a bounded HTTP publisher,
maximum one publisher instance, with private OIDC consumer; use this baseline
until measured evidence supports a reviewed change. Alert on oldest eligible work
age, recovery redispatches, lost heartbeats, poison
counts and attempt saturation; queue depth alone is not completion evidence.

Quarantine stores fixed reason code, safe attempt metadata and authorized resource
references, not raw provider payload/exception. Operator actions pause, cancel,
retry or replace only through scoped reviewed commands with audit/reason. Cancelling
increments/invalidate fences atomically; it does not undo posted journals. An
irreversible uncertain external effect must be reconciled before cancellation is
reported settled. Deleting queue tasks is optional cleanup, never cancellation
authority. Retention/deletion periods and redacted operator UI are unresolved #7
release gates; retain synthetic evidence only until approved lifecycle is specified.

## Planned acceptance matrix

All names below are **planned**. Existing ledger tests prove posting/outbox
atomicity for their fixtures, not these worker state machines.

| Test/evidence | Required outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `TestWorkIntentAtomicity` | Producer rollback leaves no intent; commit then crash still discoverable; sidecar scan repeats without duplicate operation; source outbox remains immutable. |
| `TestWorkEnvelopeBoundary` | Strict version/UUID/generation/size, unknown fields, spoofed headers/issuer/audience/caller denied; source event is never executed as a posting command. |
| `TestPublisherUncertainEnqueue` | Enqueue success + receipt failure, RPC timeout, dedup tombstone, expired publisher lease and delayed acknowledgement retain correct dispatch history; fast completed consumer cannot be regressed. |
| `TestConsumerDedupOrder` | Duplicate/reordered/old-generation messages produce one authorized effect; setup gaps in book revisions do not deadlock; wrong request digest conflicts. |
| `TestWorkFenceTakeover` | Overlapping claims, expired holder, clock skew, late heartbeat, old process surviving request deadline and cancellation cannot commit; new holder succeeds once. |
| `TestWorkReceiptAtomicity` | Crash before effect, before receipt, before commit and after commit/before ack; domain state/checkpoint/receipt atomic; commit ambiguity rereads instead of repeating. |
| `TestWorkAuthorizationRace` | Disabled/revoked principal/entity/connection, mixed scope, service-only caller, scope change during provider wait; no unauthorized call after check or commit after revocation wins. Calls already in flight are not falsely claimed prevented. |
| `TestConnectionWakeupRace` | Wakeup before/during/after complete commit preserves requested demand; partial stages never move committed cursor; stale connection generation fails despite matching operation UUID. |
| `TestWorkRetryQuarantine` | Transient/backoff/Retry-After, permanent poison, consent block,8-attempt OR24h guard, bounded continuation and authorized retry/cancel retain audit and effect identity. |
| `TestWorkRecoveryWithoutQueue` | Purge/expiry/task tombstone/scheduler outage/missed ack recovered from SQL; redispatch does not duplicate effects or replace a healthy active lease. |
| `TestExternalEffectUncertainty` | Idempotent provider replay reconciles once; unknown non-idempotent effect quarantined and cannot be blindly retried. |
| `TestWorkResourceBoundary` | Concurrency/pool/SQL/HTTP/page/body caps, cancellation, contention, crash and backlog; no network wait holding SQL transaction; redacted logs and bounded metadata. |
| `TestJournalObservationReceipt` | Scoped event/journal header correspondence and unique receipt, no second posting/outbox; bad target/type/version/revision quarantined. |
| `ReviewWorkerStandardScopeV1` | STD-01 internal message assessment, version mappings and deferred financial/audit adapters reviewed; no ISO/production claim. |

## Implementation handoff and alternatives

Preserve #7 acceptance aliases: `outbox-contract-review` maps this document plus
standards review; `fault-matrix` maps the failure tests above; `completion-proof`
maps `TestJournalObservationReceipt` and receipt atomicity; `durable-failure` maps
quarantine/recovery; `transport-auth` maps envelope/authentication and revocation.
Remote acceptance remains dependent on #5/#26/#11; a canceled predecessor is
never treated as completed evidence.

Before #7 runtime work, approve concrete DDL/functions/constraints/role grants,
the fixed journal-observer handler, mandate/consent model with #70,
retention/recovery operations, queue configuration and pool-budget evidence. New
DDL must expose the CAS predicates and unique effect guard to integration tests.
Use fake clock/provider/queue failures plus disposable PostgreSQL; no live sources
or cloud calls in default CI. No OpenAPI operation is advertised by this prose.

A database-only polling worker avoids queue ambiguity and is viable; Cloud Tasks
is retained for managed dispatch/backoff, with SQL retaining recovery authority.
CDC/logical replication can relay outbox changes but adds connector/slot lifecycle
and still needs idempotent consumers. Pub/Sub fanout is deferred; per-consumer
sidecar identity leaves room for it without changing immutable facts. Scheduled
bounded scans trade latency for idle cost; continuous polling requires measured
justification. These are design choices, not guarantees supplied by an outbox
pattern or a queue product.

documents.title: Encrypted bank credentials
documents.body:
# Encrypted bank credentials

## Decision and sources

Owner selected encrypted PostgreSQL writes on 2026-10-15 (#162–#164) to replace
per-account Infisical keys, finite slots and source-to-runtime delivery. Static
Plaid client credentials retain the existing Infisical/Secret Manager path.

Reviewed selected official sections on 2026-10-15:
[Plaid persistent tokens](https://plaid.com/docs/identity/add-to-app/#get-a-persistent-access_token)
requires secure server-side persistence, not Infisical specifically;
[Cloud KMS envelope encryption](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/envelope-encryption)
describes local data encryption keys protected by a remotely held wrapping key;
[KMS integrity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/data-integrity-guidelines)
describes request/response CRC32C and verification flags. These sources support the
mechanisms, not certification or hosted qualification. Our scoped SQL boundary,
immutable version policy and retry rules are application design decisions.

## Persistence and authority

### Canonical KMS project identifier correction (#194)

Reviewed 2026-10-19: Cloud KMS [resource hierarchy](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/resource-hierarchy)
and [symmetric encryption](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/encrypt-decrypt)
use `projects/PROJECT_ID/.../cryptoKeys/KEY_NAME` for a key resource. Review covers
the resource-name table and encrypt/decrypt request examples, not all API behavior.
An operator-controlled probe encrypted only a fixed synthetic marker: the numeric
project resource returned permission denied, while the project-ID form succeeded
with the same principal and fixed key. The attempted API-account impersonation
was denied; this probe does not independently qualify the runtime identity.

Decision: compose API and acquisition KMS resources from their validated project
ID. Secret Manager references continue using their separately validated numeric
project number. Go checks the exact configured key and numeric immutable version;
it does not rewrite a returned resource name because that name participates in AAD.
Forward migration 20 permits canonical project IDs in both ciphertext-write
functions while preserving existing numeric metadata for compatibility. Runtime
key equality still rejects foreign projects/keys. No ciphertext or AAD is rewritten.
The down migration refuses when canonical-ID envelopes exist, before restoring
numeric-only write validation. This avoids claiming a compatible rollback after
new envelopes have been written.

Owned repair compatibility (#326):32's new reconnect handoff branch inadvertently
copied19's numeric-only resource grammar.33 restores exactly20's reviewed numeric
or canonical project-ID grammar for that branch, retaining its current scope,
proof, consent, expiry, closed AEAD envelope, immutable winner and API-only ACL.
No envelope/AAD/key resource is rewritten; runtime key equality still applies.
The nonrepair fallback remains20. Disposable/quiesced33 down refuses before
function replacement if canonical reconnect handoff history exists; it neither
deletes ciphertext nor treats abandoned history as safe to erase. Canonical new
enrollment history remains compatible with32's20 fallback. No managed rollback
or migration application is approved by this source correction. Independent
SQL profile/forward/down evidence: [handoff compatibility](../runbooks/hosted-handoff-kms.md).

Acceptance: canonical-ID KMS request/CRC/readback tests, numeric-key configuration
rejection, SQL canonical and malformed-name cases, migration forward/down guards,
and synthetic connection/binding/acquisition. A fresh Hosted Sandbox run remains
required after migration and runtime promotion. Official Plaid SDK adoption is
tracked separately in #195 and does not repair a KMS resource-name failure.

Migration 18 adds integration.bank_credential, owned by bookkeeping_owner. Store
only AES-256-GCM ciphertext, a random 96-bit nonce, KMS-wrapped random 256-bit data
key, format version and wrapping-key-version resource. No token, unwrapped data
key, or plaintext envelope crosses SQL. PostgreSQL encryption at rest alone is
not this protection. KMS permissions and SQL permissions are independently required.

Canonical UTF-8 JSON array AAD binds profile, entity, book, credential reference,
logical version, provider Item and environment. Both local AEAD and KMS wrapping
use that binding; local AEAD additionally authenticates the returned wrapping-key
version. Reject foreign scope/reference/version/Item/environment, altered
ciphertext/nonce/wrapped key/key resource, malformed metadata and invalid CRCs.

API SQL wrappers recheck current connection authority and the initiating actor's
matching claimed attempt before write/read. Writes require a recorded manifest
and exact SQL-assigned reference/version. A worker reads only through current
sync_context lease/fence authority; the function obtains the credential reference
from SQL, never a caller-chosen lookup. No application gets direct table access.
No key or token belongs in API responses, receipts, logs, migrations or Terraform.

### Existing credential for an owned repair (#319)

The optional internal `RepairCredentialReader` reads only through32's
`get_repair_bank_credential(actor,entity,book,attempt)`; SQL derives the existing
reference/version/Item, never a caller-selected credential lookup. The Go scoped
adapter validates the returned closed addressed metadata against the service's
expected tuple **before** any unwrap. SQL must commit successfully first; current
scope/proof/consent denial or an unknown reply cannot reach KMS. The existing
AEAD/KMS AAD profile and wrapping-key equality remain unchanged. Unscoped reads
are unavailable. No generic lookup fallback, Seal/Put, new randomness or version
publication is part of this read.

Before Link creation, SQL permits the exact fresh `link_pending` repair under
original live consent. In `link_ready`, pending completion cannot read a bank
credential, even if a successful receipt exists but no claim has committed.
After explicit proof-pinned claim, read-only recovery of that same attempt may
repeat after the unclaimed Link deadline while original source consent/current
scope remain live. Revocation, terminal cancellation or expired consent still
denies. This is not a new execution grant, a fresh Link or consent renewal. See
[the owned repair protocol](hosted-reconnect.md) for the authoritative scope and
uncertainty rules. Generic new/rotate reads and encrypted handoff APIs are unchanged.

This phase supplies the credential adapter only; concrete service use and Hosted
reconnect remain disabled until the rest of319/320 is implemented and qualified.
Named SQL/AEAD/signature evidence and limits are in
[the purpose-read stages](../runbooks/hosted-repair-vault.md). The existing
operational/nonfinancial standards applicability below is unchanged; no financial
exchange, ISO designation, currency or accounting mapping is introduced.

Rows are immutable per scope/reference/version. Put first reads an existing row
and verifies its decrypted token equals the supplied memory-only token. Concurrent
writers return the existing winner; decrypt/compare rejects a different token.
Confirmed same-version retries and lost commit recovery do not require identical
new randomness, and never repeat Plaid exchange. New logical versions append rows.
No plaintext fallback or automatic legacy-secret import. Legacy resources remain
untouched; an encrypted runtime rejects missing rows instead of guessing storage.

## Failure and deployment

The exchange claim still commits before Plaid mutation. The encrypted store checks SQL function permissions and performs a fresh
KMS wrap/unwrap preflight before consuming a public token; SQL write/readback and
credential confirmation precede binding review. Exchange and DB are not one atomic
transaction: a crash after exchange but before durable ciphertext may lose the
token. Such an attempt cannot be repaired by repeating a consumed public token.
Existing #160 has no observed source token; preserve its audit trail and use an
explicit abandonment/new-enrollment path after classification, not manual reset.

Provision the fixed development KMS key in workers infrastructure; API encrypts
and decrypts, acquisition only decrypts. No publisher decrypt permission. Forward
migration must precede matching API/worker rollout. The tables are additive, but the new abandoned state requires updated UI/API
clients. Old binaries must not handle abandoned attempts. Old/new credential formats
are not silently interchangeable; complete the coordinated application rollout
before using the abandonment action.

## Standards and acceptance

This internal credential-storage protocol is not an ISO 20022 financial message.
It does not change currency/accounting contracts or imply ISO cryptographic
certification. Named evidence must cover fresh/replay migrations, restricted API
and worker SQL, current revocation/lease checks, immutable conflict/lost commit,
tamper/wrong AAD/KMS key/integrity denial, redaction and synthetic end-to-end
connection/binding/acquisition. Hosted Sandbox acceptance remains separate.


## Explicit lost-token abandonment

POST `connection-attempts/{attempt}/abandon` requires
`{"confirm_unrecoverable":true}`. Current initiating-actor connection authority is
rechecked. An unclaimed new setup, or a new unpublished credential-recovery
attempt with no stored DB ciphertext, can move to immutable `abandoned`. Preserve nonce/hash/claim/manifest
and append an audit event; do not delete or recycle anything. Discovery excludes
this terminal state from unfinished_count. It never removes the provider Item;
known orphaned Sandbox Item cleanup remains explicit. **Try connecting again** is
the user's affirmative request to resolve and restart a failed new enrollment.
For claimed credential recovery the UI first reconciles the exact attempt; only a confirmed recovery conflict
followed by an exact read of the still-unresolved attempt can invoke abandon.
The server checks that no ciphertext or credential publication exists before
accepting the command. An uncertain response or another unfinished attempt
stops the restart. The old provider exchange is never repeated.
This route is an internal operational command, not an ISO 20022 message.

Unclaimed new-setup cancellation additionally follows [#200](hosted-link-enrollment.md#explicit-cancellation-and-retry-200); it cannot discard a claimed exchange or published credential.

documents.title: Binding review recovery contract
documents.body:
# Binding review recovery contract

## Scope

This contract covers a new Plaid Item after public-token exchange and encrypted
credential publication, while its attempt is still `binding_review`. Completion
remains the normal path: the owner reviews distinct ledger-account proposals and
submits one atomic binding command. Cancellation is an explicit fallback that
removes the provider Item before another enrollment becomes available.

Issue #215 owns this slice. Automatic supported-account creation remains defined
by [automatic account binding](automatic-account-binding.md); credit and loan
policy remains #210.

## Binding readiness

The browser derives proposals only from the verified attempt manifest, current
book snapshot, installed ISO 4217 currency versions, and selected binding date.
It must name each unmet requirement beside the disabled confirmation: binding
date, at least one complete selection, matching ledger/currency fields, unique
ledger accounts, reviewed new-account code/name, or owner acknowledgement.
Unsupported provider accounts remain visible and unbound.

## Cancel state machine

Only an authorized, new-mode `binding_review` attempt with its exact paused Item,
published encrypted credential, and zero streams may begin cancellation. The
database locks the attempt and Item, changes both to `disconnect_pending`, and
increments the Item generation before provider I/O. This serializes against the
binding command: whichever transition commits first wins.

The service reauthorizes the exact attempt, reads only its addressed encrypted
credential, and calls Plaid `/item/remove`. A confirmed response, or Plaid
`ITEM_NOT_FOUND` on a retry, permits finalization. Finalization rechecks the
claim, Item, generation, credential publication, and absence of streams; it then
marks the Item `disconnected` and attempt immutable `abandoned`. The encrypted
credential and audit events remain under the existing retention contract, but
the removed access token is no longer usable.

A timeout, malformed response, provider failure, lost prepare response, or lost
final response never releases the enrollment gate by inference. The attempt
stays `disconnect_pending`; repeating the same cancel action resumes removal for
that exact Item. No path recreates Link or repeats public-token exchange.

Cancellation creates no ledger account, source account, namespace, stream,
grant, balance, transaction, or journal. It is a Plaid lifecycle operation and
not an ISO 20022 financial message. Existing ISO 4217 mapping and accounting
policy are unchanged.

## Evidence

Synthetic SQL tests must prove prepare/finalize guards, bind-versus-cancel
serialization, replay, current authority, zero streams, and zero journals.
Service tests must prove exact credential addressing, `/item/remove`,
already-removed recovery, provider failure, and lost-response resumption.
Browser tests must prove named readiness blockers, explicit confirmation, and
fresh enrollment only after server-confirmed abandonment.

documents.title: Browser authentication
documents.body:
# Browser authentication

## Decision and boundary

Implementation contract for the first app, 2026-10-11. Use modular Firebase Web SDK
with memory-only persistence and operator-provisioned, verified email/password
accounts. Source review and alternatives: [browser sources](../research/browser-auth-sources.md).
No signup, anonymous mode, emulator, demo authentication, cookies or persistent token
storage. Public runtime identifiers are `JAYBURD_FIREBASE_API_KEY`,
`JAYBURD_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN`, `JAYBURD_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`, delivered through
`/api/auth-config`; missing/invalid configuration leaves sign-in unavailable and
does not initialize the SDK. See the [runtime/bridge contract](private-api-bridge.md).
These public identifiers are not server credentials.

## Session flow

Verified password-only success enters enrollment, never bookkeeping; unverified
users follow the email-verification flow below. Generate and display a
manual authenticator key only after explicit action; clear it on enrollment completion,
cancellation, logout or unmount. Enrollment always ends in signout. A new password
sign-in must complete the managed TOTP challenge. Only one existing TOTP factor is
supported; multiple factors or non-TOTP factors fail closed pending operator recovery.
No provider error text, password, token, setup key or OTP enters logs or application
storage. Inputs clear on submission/phase change. The SDK necessarily retains its
refresh token in memory; browser compromise remains outside this guarantee.

`AuthProvider`, `LoginPanel`, and `useAuth()` expose `phase`, `getToken()`,
`signOut()`, `rejectSession()` and `sessionKey`. Consumers call `getToken()` per API
request, call `rejectSession()` on backend 401, and discard financial state whenever
`sessionKey` changes or phase leaves `signed-in`. SDK token expiry/refresh errors
invalidate the session. A token returned after logout is discarded; cancelled SDK
operations cannot restore UI state and finish with another SDK signout. Browser
claim inspection is a UX gate only: Go validates signature, audience, issuer,
revocation, TOTP claim and enrolled principal on every protected API request.

## Acceptance and release gaps

Named Vitest suites `AuthController` and `FirebaseAdapter boundary` cover the above
with credential-free fixtures. Identity Platform configuration is applied (see
the identity runbook); verified user provisioning, enrollment/recovery, hosted
origin/TLS and end-to-end MFA remain release
gates. Identity flows have no applicable ISO 20022 financial message; no ISO
conformance is claimed. Financial requests follow existing API/currency contracts.

## Email verification before enrollment

Owner-directed implementation, 2026-10-12; sources BA03. An unverified successful
password login enters `verifying-email`, never enrollment or `signed-in`.
Only explicit **Send verification email** calls the SDK for its current user.
There is no recipient argument, automatic send, signup or admin verification flag.
Success means the SDK accepted the request, not proven inbox delivery. Provider
errors are replaced with a generic message; an in-memory 60-second interval
between attempts reduces accidental resends, including failures. This is UX
throttling, not an abuse-control guarantee; Google quotas still apply.

Use Google's default hosted action handler without custom continuation URLs.
Jayburd never receives/parses/stores verification links or action codes. After
opening the email, the user returns and clicks **I have verified my email**.
Reload provider user data: false stays verification-only; true signs out and
requires fresh credentials before TOTP enrollment. Failed reload signs out.
Cancellation invalidates late completions; no verification operation grants
bookkeeping access or invokes ledger APIs. Refresh loses the memory-only session.

Acceptance: `FirebaseAdapter boundary` tests send/reload and absent/unverified
user denial; `AuthController` tests phase isolation, resend throttling, pending
and verified refresh, failure and cancellation; `LoginPanel` tests explicit send,
status and fresh-login transitions. Existing browser and Go verification gates
remain required. This internal identity flow has no ISO 20022 message mapping.
Alternative custom email handlers/mail infrastructure add action-code handling
and delivery responsibilities without benefit to this slice, so are deferred.
Real inbox delivery, link expiry/reuse, sender configuration and TOTP enrollment
require owner evidence; synthetic tests do not establish them.

The [local identity rehearsal](identity-rehearsal.md) reuses this component through
validated public configuration without mounting the financial application. It is
an explicit operator tool, not an application route or a substitute for Go/SQL
identity acceptance. Its browser-only success screen never grants ledger access.

documents.title: Development Cloud Run rollout
documents.body:
# Development Cloud Run rollout

## Decision

Implement the owner-requested #27 deployment slice, 2026-10-12. Terraform owns
services and the migration job; GitHub only invokes the configured job. A separate
runtime state bucket holds `runtime` and `migration` prefixes. Existing
`application` state remains owner-operated Cloud SQL. This avoids giving the
workflow database administrator rights or using partial `-target` applies.
Sources G19–G23 in the [GCP register](../research/gcp-sources.md) establish the
mechanisms, not successful cloud acceptance. Alternative: one state with targeted
migration applies; rejected because it conflates database/runtime authority and
makes staged plans harder to reason about.

## Authority and runtime

Foundation adds a separate `jayburd-dev-deploy` federation pool, disabled by default,
with exact owner/repository IDs, main, workflow_dispatch and deploy-dev workflow.
A separate pool prevents the existing repository-only builder principal binding
from accepting deployment tokens, or vice versa. Owner dispatch and an exact
release-file hash are the promotion boundary; an unprotected GitHub environment
name is not approval. The triggering actor must also be the owner.

Deployer gets Cloud Run admin, repository image reader, runtime bucket object
admin and ActAs on only API/frontend/migrator. The former application-state grant
moves to runtime state. No database-state, foundation-state, project IAM-admin,
image-writer or secret-reader grant is added. Cloud Run admin is project-scoped:
it can change service IAM and launch code as those three identities, including
migrator SQL privileges. It is a privileged release identity, not a sandbox.
Only owner-reviewed source may receive it. No runtime Token Creator role is needed.
API gets a custom `firebaseauth.users.get` role for revocation lookup.

API ingress is network-reachable but IAM-restricted to frontend Invoker; this is
not an internal-only VPC service. Cloud Run-to-internal ingress requires additional
network routing, deferred to avoid VPC/NAT cost and complexity. Frontend exposes
sign-in publicly; finance still requires the managed Go authentication boundary.
Deterministic service origins remove circular frontend/API configuration. The
API explicitly accepts its deterministic origin as a custom ID-token audience.

Both services use request billing, min zero/max two at service and revision levels,
1 CPU/512 MiB. API concurrency 16 and a five-connection pool; web concurrency 32.
Old/new API revisions can use 20 connections, bounded again by the SQL login cap.
Cloud Run instance maxima are scaling controls, not hard spending guarantees.
API startup probes `/readyz`, web probes `/api/auth-config`; only a ready revision
receives latest traffic. API liveness uses `/healthz`, avoiding database-triggered
restart loops. Migration has one task, zero retries, dedicated identity and a
660-second task bound around its existing ten-minute process deadline.

## Release and rollback

The workflow requires reviewed `deploy/dev-release.json` and its exact SHA256
provided by the owner at manual dispatch. There is deliberately no enabled/sample
release file. [Release instructions](../../deploy/README.md) define fields.
Runtime manifests now use schemaVersion2 with mandatory explicit connection state;
[connection release policy](connection-release.md) defines propagation and
configuration-bound rollback. Migration/verify manifests remain schemaVersion1.
Missing, expired, foreign-project, mutable-image, mixed-build and incomplete
metadata fail before cloud authentication. Unsigned candidate receipts alone
cannot approve release. Successful owner/main build metadata and all three
same-run/attempt receipts must match the manifest. Recheck #23/#24 merged and verify their merge commits are ancestors of the release; require
#6/#11/#26 closed; owner evidence links supplement, not replace, these checks.

Exception for gathering database evidence: [migration-only release](migration-release.md)
uses `operation: migrate`, foundation #5 and ancestral bootstrap #44 instead of
full application closure gates. The same hash/owner/build/expiry rules apply;
it exits after verified migration execution and cannot apply runtime services.

Forward order: migration-root plan/apply, execute-and-wait with exact execution readback, runtime-root plan/apply,
anonymous transport probes, minimal receipt. One GitHub concurrency group and
GCS locking serialize workflow deployments; the SQL advisory lock protects other
migration runners. Do not run owner applies concurrently. A migration failure
leaves both service configurations untouched. Failure after API update can leave
mixed API/web versions: this is not an atomic two-service rollout. Require
backward-compatible contracts, investigate and dispatch explicit rollback.

Rollback requires a successful earlier deploy run, matching retained API/web
receipt and reviewed compatibility with the current schema. It skips both job
configuration and migration execution, redeploying known digests via Terraform.
Never down-migrate automatically. Expired build/deployment artifacts block this
workflow; preserve approved evidence and review a durable retention path before
long-term operation. No arbitrary image override bypass is offered.

Provider logs and saved plans stay runner-private and are never artifact uploads.
After all offline gates, WIF produces one masked, one-hour deployer access token
passed through step-scoped environment settings to Terraform and gcloud. No
credential file is created; the job timeout is 50 minutes. Tokens are not renewed
or logged. Receipts contain public image/release identity and ready revision IDs. No real token acquisition,
state/plan inspection or cloud operation occurs in default tests.

## Acceptance and limits

`make release-test`: immutable/hash/expiry/build/rollback rejection, anonymous
transport denial and actual shell orchestration under fake executables, including
migration failure and rollback-without-SQL. `make infra-test`: pinned-provider
validation with synthetic mocks for IAM, state separation, service capacity,
managed configuration and job bounds. Existing Go checks remain required; no SQL,
API financial semantics or new ISO 20022 message changes.

Real deployment still requires owner foundation update, reviewed Cloud SQL apply
and role bootstrap, Identity Platform/MFA/domain setup, principal enrollment and
Infisical evidence. The first runtime uses IAM DB login and public Firebase
identifiers, so it has no application secret to invent or sync. Infisical remains
the selected authority when secrets are needed. Transport smoke proves only API
anonymous denial, web unauthenticated denial and available shell/config. Real MFA,
revocation, cross-entity denial, synthetic posting/recovery, load, restore and cost
remain separate #27/#12 acceptance; passing deployment must not close those issues.

## Limited Sandbox qualification

The separately reviewed [Sandbox release contract](sandbox-release.md) adds explicit
`sandbox-promote`/`sandbox-rollback` operations for the fixed development project.
Full promote/rollback gates above remain unchanged. Sandbox releases require the
bounded database proof (#130), and connection-enabled/worker releases also require
delivery implementation (#131). Hosted activation is separately tracked in #133.
Scheduling remains paused; no production or full-readiness claim follows.

documents.title: Cloud SQL connection and migration contract
documents.body:
# Cloud SQL connection and migration contract

## Decision

Implement #26 without changing merged SQL. Terraform owns a PostgreSQL 17 Enterprise
single-zone instance and API/migrator IAM users. Owner bootstrap creates reviewed
NOLOGIN roles and a `deployment` schema; a distinct migration binary applies embedded,
checksummed SQL. Runtime startup never migrates. Sources and limits are in the
[GCP source register](../research/gcp-sources.md).

This is infrastructure/internal configuration, not an ISO 20022 financial message.
ISO currency and accounting contracts remain unchanged. `deployment` holds only
migration-control metadata, never journal or provider payloads.

## Configuration and authority

API selects `-database-mode=cloudsql -cloud-sql-instance=PROJECT:us-central1:INSTANCE`
alongside existing managed-mode flags. Project must equal the identity project;
JAYBURD_DATABASE_URL presence is rejected in connector mode. URL mode remains
compatible. Health mode does not construct clients or read a database URL.

Connector 1.25.3 uses metadata-only API and IAM-login token sources, lazy refresh,
public-IP TLS tunnel and automatic IAM authentication. No ADC discovery, key file,
password, private network or host override is accepted. pgx TLS is disabled only
inside this authenticated encrypted tunnel; no fallback to direct TCP exists.

API identity is derived as `jayburd-dev-api@PROJECT.iam`, database `bookkeeping`.
Pool cap is 5, minimum 0; connections age out at 30 minutes plus up to five minutes
jitter and idle out at five minutes. Dial/refresh bounds are 15 seconds; startup
is bounded to 20 seconds. Existing shorter request/transaction deadlines still
apply; cold connection failure returns unavailable rather than extending posting.
Migrator derives its separate login, uses at most two connections and permits
60-second SQL statements with a 10-second SQL lock timeout.

Terraform enables IAM authentication, encrypted connector enforcement, no authorized
networks, max_connections 50, initial 10 GiB SSD with growth capped at 20 GiB,
daily backups with seven retained copies and seven-day PITR. SQL statement/error
statement logging is suppressed; redacted application metrics remain separate.
No SLA is claimed for shared-core capacity. Cloud IAM client/login roles are
project-scoped for two accounts; SQL role grants restrict authority within the
selected instance. Broader inherited project grants require deployment review.

## Bootstrap and migration

Migration 8 requires the owner-operated bootstrap to precreate the safe NOLOGIN
`bookkeeping_publisher` and `bookkeeping_observer` capability roles. Rerun the
reviewed bootstrap before applying migration 8 to an existing hosted database;
the restricted migrator still has no CREATEROLE privilege. This does not provision
worker IAM logins, observer bindings or service permissions. Those remain a
separate hosted-worker enrollment gate. API readiness rejects worker-role membership.

Migration 12 additionally requires safe NOLOGIN `bookkeeping_sync`. The reviewed
bootstrap now precreates it without enrolling any worker or granting API membership.
Rerun that bootstrap through the existing owner-operated procedure before a hosted
migration12 rollout; this delivery does not perform that rollout or retrieve secrets.

Owner uses [bootstrap SQL](../../db/bootstrap/cloud-sql.sql) with existing API and
migrator IAM role identifiers. Administrator must own the database/schema and have
CREATEROLE plus sufficient authority to alter the two logins; this authority is
not granted to the migrator. Bootstrap rejects unsafe attributes/inherited roles,
grants only CONNECT to API, grants migrator database CREATE and explicit SET ROLE
bookkeeping_owner, and gives migrator access to deployment. API has no DDL/table
or enrollment grant. Connection limits are 20 API and 2 migrator across revisions.
Actual Cloud SQL administrator compatibility remains a live gate.

An explicit `bootstrap_operator_email` application-root input may provision one
human IAM SQL operator with `cloudsqlsuperuser` membership and Cloud SQL
client/login IAM bindings; default null creates none. API/migrator resources
remain unchanged. This operator is a development administration identity, never
a runtime identity. The owner authorized evaluating this G24 path after #42.
Membership does not prove CREATEROLE, ownership or authority to alter other IAM
logins; verify those before bootstrap. Password administration is the alternative,
with owner-only credential injection if required.

For this owner-operated check only, the pinned Cloud SQL Auth Proxy v2.26.0 may
consume existing ADC internally with automatic IAM authentication. Use a private
Unix-socket directory (0700), not a network listener; psql ignores startup files
and never prompts for a password. Do not expose tokens, credential files or raw
provider errors. The application connector remains metadata-only. Stop the proxy
after the check. Failed checks must not leave an unnecessary administrator: remove
the optional operator through Terraform after confirming it owns no objects.
After successful bootstrap, role/schema ownership must be transferred or retained
explicitly before removing the login; never silently abandon a privileged user.
`database_roles` is write-only: zero drift is not proof of SQL membership. Verify
SQL privileges separately, and retain the explicit input on later applies while
the operator is needed. See [IAM bootstrap evidence](../runbooks/iam-bootstrap.md).

`cmd/migrate` defaults to offline `-action=verify`. Explicit `-action=up -instance=...`
uses IAM transport and golang-migrate 4.20.1; no down/force/target command exists.
It rejects invalid artifacts before network access and unsafe migrator privileges,
serializes runners with a database advisory lock, checks stored artifact hashes,
registers attempted files before execution and uses golang-migrate's separate
version/dirty-state lock. `deployment.migration_artifact` stores filename, SHA256
and registration time; it is not a claim that every registered version succeeded.
The library owns `deployment.schema_migrations` as the applied/dirty authority.

`cmd/migrate -action=status -instance=...` uses the same restricted IAM connector
but only a read-only repeatable-read transaction to check current clean version
and exact registered hashes. It does not create metadata or run migrations. The
[status release contract](migration-status.md) defines its distinct reviewed
`verify` operation and receipt; the human operator receives no additional access.

Resealed registered SQL is rejected. Crash after artifact registration is replayable
with the identical package; dirty SQL execution blocks retry until owner-reviewed
repair. Migration SQL remains immutable. A signal requests stop between migrations;
a running statement is bounded by its timeout. Errors are fixed/redacted, never
raw provider errors or SQL text. Digest promotion and migration Job invocation
belong to #27; this slice does not invoke GCP.

## Acceptance and recovery

`TestConnectorConfiguration`, `TestConnectorRejectsAmbiguity` and
`TestCloudSQLSelection` prove transport selection and bounds without credentials.
`TestArtifactIntegrity`, `TestRestrictedMigration` and `TestMigrationContention`
cover local artifacts, non-superuser migration/replay, runtime denial, durable
checksum drift and overlapping execution. Terraform's application tests assert
recovery/capacity/transport configuration. Existing migration and ledger suites
remain required. Passing these tests does not establish IAM token/TLS acceptance.

Denial evidence must match the expected SQLSTATE, not merely any failure:
`42501` for forbidden DDL/table reads/owner role, and `P2101` for an unknown
principal at the workspace entrypoint under its required repeatable-read isolation.
Connection failures, missing objects and the `P2100` isolation precondition do
not demonstrate authorization. Direct-table probes use zero-row reads.

Maximum planned demand including overlapping API/publisher/consumer revisions is
28 runtime connections, plus two migrator and five administrative = 35 below the
configured 50. The [hosted platform](hosted-platform.md) now composes two-connection acquisition
worker pools and separately reviewed login bootstrap; deployed acceptance remains #7. Live shared-core login
latency, actual pool recovery, backup restore/PITR, exact restored journal totals
and replay remain #26/#12 cloud evidence. Restore into a separate temporary instance;
never replace/delete the original automatically. Record recovery time/data-loss
window and retire only the drill instance after review. No backup artifact or
Terraform plan/state enters agent context.

documents.title: Recoverable bookkeeping commands
documents.body:
# Recoverable bookkeeping commands

## Decision and scope

Implementation decision for #9, owner project maintainer, 2026-10-11. Store one
immutable reviewed setup/post/import command before execution. One unacknowledged command
per principal prevents a lost result from silently becoming a new interactive
request. This deliberately serializes one user's interactive workflow across tabs;
it does not limit entity/account counts. No queue, worker or automatic execution.
Sources and alternatives: [recovery research](../research/recovery-sources.md).

## State and authority

A command is `prepared`, `committed` or `cancelled`. Registration persists exact
validated JSON and its principal, operation and target; it never posts a journal.
Execution invokes owned SQL setup/post/import functions and marks the command committed
in the same serializable transaction. The existing receipt, audit and outbox
invariants remain authoritative. Failed execution rolls back, leaving prepared.
Only explicit user confirmation executes; discovery never executes or acknowledges.

All transitions lock the active principal first, then follow existing scope/book
lock order and command locking consistently. Execution/cancellation serialize;
cancellation cannot report success after posting committed. Acknowledgement is
explicit and terminal-only; it releases the one-unacknowledged-command gate but
never deletes immutable request/result history. Runtime has restricted functions,
no table access. Same registration key with changed content conflicts.

Discovery/results reauthorize the current principal and current operation-specific scope. Setup/post retain read/post
authority; import requires entity read+import and source read+import.
Another principal cannot discover, execute, cancel or acknowledge a command.
Revoked scopes fail closed without returning request/result financial data. The
owning principal may explicitly clear an inaccessible command through the bounded
payload-free recovery action: prepared work is cancelled and acknowledged, while
terminal work is acknowledged. The action refuses currently authorized commands,
never executes or reverses accounting work, and preserves immutable history.
Command storage has the existing 1MiB request bound; it is not a general draft API.
The gate applies to this interactive workflow. Existing direct setup/post API
clients retain their original idempotency obligations; this is not semantic
duplicate detection across independently submitted business transactions.

## HTTP contract

- `POST /v1/commands`, required `Idempotency-Key`: register
  `{operation: setup|post|import, entity_id: uuid|null, book_id: uuid|null, body: object}`.
  Setup requires null targets; post/import require both. Return 201 `Command`.
- `GET /v1/commands/pending`: return `{command: Command|null}`; no query/body.
- `POST /v1/commands/pending/clear`: exact body `{}`; return `{cleared:boolean}`.
  It reveals no command fields and qualifies only after current scope authorization
  returns not-found or permission-denied for the owning principal.
- `POST /v1/commands/{command_id}/execute`, `/cancel`, `/acknowledge`: body `{}`,
  return 200 `Command`. Command identity supplies retry identity; no extra key
  authorizes a changed operation. Execution returns the stored result on replay.

`Command` fields: `command_id`, `operation`, nullable `entity_id`/`book_id`,
`state`, immutable `body`, nullable `result`, `created_at` (RFC3339),
`acknowledged` (boolean). `result` is SetupResult, Journal or ImportCommandResult. Import pins batch/preview
IDs, preview/binding/source revisions and the synthetic CSV profile; counts and
revisions are decimal strings. See [import SQL](import-sql.md).
All responses are no-store. Existing RFC9457/auth/body rules apply. New409 codes
may distinguish a pending command or invalid state; no sensitive raw error detail.
Registration input rejects duplicate/unknown JSON fields, including nested input.
Internal recovery is not an ISO20022 exchange; unchanged financial payloads retain
ISO4217 version references. No new accounting or standards-conformance claim.

## Import boundary

Import registers reviewed intent on the same principal gate. Only explicit
execution creates immutable observations, provenance and review items; it creates
no journals or journal outbox effects. Imported replay returns the saved result
under current permissions without requiring the source still be active. Initial
execution requires current active source and pinned preview/binding/source state.
New import functions do not make the general API an upload or arbitrary-row API.

The current workspace can discover, cancel and acknowledge import commands. It
disables import execution because it cannot yet display the source-row preview;
confirmation requires an importing client that presents that reviewed evidence.
No browser-persisted file, request or financial payload is introduced.

Cancelling an import command cancels the batch only if its pinned preview remains
current. If a refresh has already replaced that preview, cancellation terminalizes
only the old command; acknowledge it before registering and confirming the newer
preview. Cancelling the current preview first prevents a later refresh. Both
orders serialize under the owned SQL locks; no cancellation executes an import.

## Browser and acceptance

Load pending state before enabling new work. Review registers a durable command;
confirmation executes it. Session/tab loss clears local state but leaves server
recovery. Ambiguous responses trigger discovery/retry of the same command; no new
key/body or acknowledgement is synthesized. A committed result remains visible
until the user acknowledges it. Cancelling a prepared command requires server
confirmation, followed by acknowledgement before new work.

Named proofs: `TestCommandLifecycle`, `TestCommandAuthorization`,
`TestInaccessibleCommandClear`, `TestCommandConcurrency`,
`TestCommandLostAcknowledgement`; synthetic browser
setup/post/report, dropped real response followed by remount/recovery, and denied
scope. Full Go/PostgreSQL regression and existing browser unit/component gates
remain required. Live Firebase and deployed GCP verification remain separate.

## Source-linked posting extension

Migration11 adds `source_post` to the same principal recovery gate. Its body pins
review/draft/source/binding/book revisions and contains the immutable full
`posting_body`; SQL requires exact equality to the saved draft. The recovery UI
shows those lines after refresh. Execute commits the journal, source link, review
state and receipt together. Cancel does not post; acknowledge does not reverse.
Current permissions are rechecked even for committed replay. See the
[source review SQL contract](source-review-sql.md) and
[delivery evidence](../runbooks/populated-demo.md).

documents.title: Connection HTTP operations
documents.body:
# Connection HTTP operations

## Decision

Expose the reviewed connection service through an optional explicitly injected
`server.Dependencies.Connections`. Normal `Managed` startup leaves it absent;
there is no environment switch that silently activates Plaid or secret writes.
The same authenticated principal, exact origin boundary and 12-second request
budget as the accounting API apply. SQL rechecks current connection authority.

This implements #101's owned HTTP boundary. It does not add the #104 Link UI or
configure the hosted provider/Infisical writer. Proprietary Plaid JSON and internal
connection commands are not ISO 20022 messages. Currency/date semantics follow the
existing standards profile. See [service](connection-service.md) and
[SQL](connection-sql.md) contracts for state, authority and credential recovery.

## Routes

Issue #155 adds [creator onboarding](self-service-connections.md) in the explicitly
configured managed connection runtime. GET discovery remains read-only and can
return empty lists for eligible unconfigured creators. Begin(new) prepares the
book and persists the attempt atomically before Link work. Existing configured
or delegated books retain current grants; revoked grants are never recreated.
No request can supply worker logins or service principals.

Prefix `/v1/entities/{entity}/books/{book}`; IDs are canonical UUID strings.

| Method / suffix | Service operation |
| --- | --- |
| POST `/connection-attempts` | Begin with mode and explicit affected-stream approval. |
| GET `/connection-attempts` | Actor-scoped attempt discovery; optional limit 1–100 and before UUID. |
| GET `/connections/streams/{stream}/status` | Safe current publication/status pins; unknown provider update stays null. |
| POST `/connections/streams/{stream}/operations` | Explicit pause/resume/request with Item, binding and stream revision pins. |
| GET `/connection-attempts/{attempt}` | Safe current attempt projection. |
| POST `/connection-attempts/{attempt}/execute` | Memory-only nonce/Link handoff; omit public token for Hosted Link completion. One-shot provider mutation. |
| POST `/connection-attempts/{attempt}/complete` | Empty object; server retrieves the attempt-scoped encrypted Hosted Link token and checks Plaid completion before the one-shot claim. |
| POST `/connection-attempts/{attempt}/reconcile` | Empty object; resolve known credential state without repeating exchange. |
| POST `/connection-attempts/{attempt}/bindings` | Explicit verified account/source/ledger/currency selection. |
| GET `/connections` | Bounded current connection list. |
| POST `/connections/streams/{stream}/disconnect` | Expected binding revision; account-only local fencing. |

Begin, bindings, stream operations and disconnect require one `Idempotency-Key`, 1–128 characters in
`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`. Every POST requires exactly `application/json`, no content encoding,
one UTF-8 object at most 32 KiB, no duplicate or unknown fields and nesting at most
16. Only attempt discovery accepts the named limit/before query parameters; duplicate, unknown or malformed values are rejected. Encoded alternative paths and GET bodies are rejected. HEAD
cannot invoke reads. Authentication precedes body parsing or service access.

Success is JSON with status 200 and `Cache-Control: no-store`. Begin alone returns
an ephemeral nonce/Link token; browser consumers must keep these only in memory.
Status/list never return credential references, token hashes, operation claims or
provider diagnostics. No request body, underlying error or token is logged here.
Fixed error codes map invalid input to 400, denied/not-found to 403/404, conflict,
stale or credential recovery to 409, limits/unsupported modes to 422, and uncertain commits/temporary
failures to 503. Unknown failures become generic 500. No response acknowledges an
uncertain remote exchange or local commit as success.

## Evidence and limits

`TestConnectionHTTPBoundary` and `TestConnectionHTTPFailures` cover routing,
identity, origin, malformed requests and redaction. These injected tests prove
transport only. Named service/SQL proofs establish lifecycle behavior; the
[delivery runbook](../runbooks/provider-acquisition.md) records actual results.
A canceled request cannot undo remote exchange; durable recovery state must outlive
its connection. No automatic posting, hosted availability or provider qualification.

## Recovery and stream controls

Migration 14 adds actor-scoped attempt discovery, an authoritative unfinished count,
and a fresh-new-attempt guard while preserving exact-key replay. Expired unclaimed
attempts remain inspectable without authority to execute their old handoff.
Account-stream pause/resume has an independent revision so stale browser controls
cannot undo a later lifecycle transition. Manual request queues durable intent; it
does not call a provider or report completed acquisition. The exact returned
status may be a replayed receipt; refresh status before issuing a new operation.
See [SQL operations](connection-operations-sql.md) for current-grant checks.

Hosted Sandbox Begin also returns a validated memory-only URL; execute may return
unchanged link_ready while session completion is pending. See the
[Hosted Link contract](hosted-link-enrollment.md) for completion and recovery.

documents.title: Connection operations SQL
documents.body:
# Connection operations SQL

## Decision and reviewed sources

Proposed migration 14 extends existing generation-fenced acquisition. Human operations,
verified notification intake and worker catch-up create durable generation requests;
none fetches provider data or posts a journal. The coordinator reviews interfaces
before DDL. Migrations 1–13 remain immutable.

Reviewed 2026-10-14: [Plaid verification](https://plaid.com/docs/api/webhooks/webhook-verification/)
algorithm/key/signature, issued-at and exact-body SHA-256 sections; [Transactions API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/)
SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE and synchronization readiness; PostgreSQL 17
[transaction isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/transaction-iso.html)
Serializable retry requirements. Review covers these public sections only, not live
provider qualification or normative ISO certification. PI02/PI04/PI08 in the
[annotated source register](../research/plaid-ingestion-sources.md) remain applicable.

Facts: verification authenticates exact bytes and a signed issue time; sync notifications
indicate available work, not locally published history. Inference: deduplicate the
canonical ES256 signed-delivery identity, not body alone (a later identical body may signal new
work); commit the receipt with generation increment and outbox intent. Alternative
of a separate queue state machine is rejected: the existing requested/completed
generations and fenced sets already own durable acquisition progress.

Plaid JSON remains proprietary, API 2020-09-14. Internal operations have no applicable
ISO 20022 business-message designation. Existing ISO 4217/RFC3339 source semantics
are unchanged; no new money conversion, accounting policy or conformance claim.

## Interactive recovery and status
