All public functions use actual API role, authenticated actor, entity/book UUIDs and
current read/connect/import plus source read/import/bind where a source exists.
`list_connection_attempts(actor,e,b,maximum,after_id)` limits 1–100, ascending UUID
keyset, returning `{items:[ConnectionAttempt + expired_unclaimed:boolean + binding_expired:boolean],
next_cursor:uuid|null,unfinished_count:string}`. Only the same actor's attempts are
visible. Private nonce, fingerprints, claim and credential references never appear.
The unfinished count covers all actor attempts, independently of pagination. Active
and disconnected are terminal; an expired attempt without a provider claim is not
unfinished. Expired binding_review is a known published credential outcome and is
also excluded, with binding_expired=true; its old paused Item and reference remain
retained, and binding still rejects expiry. This permits fresh enrollment without
repeating exchange or silently removing provider access. Claimed ambiguity in other
states stays unfinished even after handoff expiry.

A forward `begin_connection` wrapper authorizes and locks the book, preserves exact
existing-key replay, and rejects a fresh new enrollment while any unfinished attempt
exists for this actor/book. Concurrent fresh requests serialize under the canonical
book lock; whole Serializable retries remain required. Expiry never grants permission
to repeat a claimed provider operation. Existing known-attempt reconciliation is
unchanged. There is no new cancellation or remote-operation recovery bypass.

`connection_stream_status(actor,e,b,stream)` returns:

```text
{stream_id,source_account_id,sync_item_id,state:active|paused|disconnected,
 stream_revision:string,item_state,item_generation:string,binding_revision:string,
 requested_generation:string,completed_generation:string,queued:boolean,
 lease_active:boolean,last_completed_at:timestamp|null,readiness,last_error,
 provider_updated_at:null}
```

Readiness is exactly TRANSACTIONS_UPDATE_STATUS_UNKNOWN, NOT_READY,
INITIAL_UPDATE_COMPLETE or HISTORICAL_UPDATE_COMPLETE from complete publication.
Queued means requested generation exceeds completed generation, not worker dispatch
or current authority to run. Lease_active reflects an unexpired local lease only.
Last complete timestamp comes from SQL publication; no provider-updated timestamp is
available. Last error is only the latest set's known abandonment reason, or null:
pagination_mutation, provider_failure, decoder_rejected, cancelled, item_changed,
lease_expired, account_disconnected, account_paused. Never echo upstream diagnostics.

`mutate_connection_stream(actor,e,b,stream,key,raw)` requires exact JSON:
`{action:pause|resume|request,expected_item_generation:string,
expected_binding_revision:string,expected_stream_revision:string}`. Keys use the
existing 1–128 ASCII idempotency profile. It returns an immutable status snapshot;
clients refresh current status after receipt recovery. Current caller authorization
precedes exact receipt replay; changed input under the same actor/book/key conflicts.
First execution verifies all three pins.

Pause affects only this stream: abandon held set, clear lease, increase fence and
stream_revision; preserve cursor, source binding and sibling acquisition. Resume
requires current consent, namespace, service/source grants and active Item; atomically
changes stream state/revision and requests a generation. Request requires the same
active acquisition authority. Paused/disconnected cannot acquire; disconnected is
terminal. Stream revision starts at 1 and advances only pause/resume; source approval
pins and financial drafts are not changed by these operations.

## Durable signal and verified ingress

Existing `request_sync(e,b,stream,key)` keeps its wire and actual enrolled worker
identity checks, now commits signal plus `integration.sync_wakeup` generation fact.
The new immutable outbox has entity/book/stream/requested_generation primary key,
globally unique message UUID, closed reason and database creation time. Reasons are
worker/manual/resume/webhook/catchup. Existing sync_signal gives stable-key replay.
The journal outbox cannot safely host this event: its target FK and uniqueness are
specific to journal entries. No observer queue tables, lease engine or dispatcher are
repurposed. Current requested/completed generations remain the work authority.

`bookkeeping_webhook` is a new NOLOGIN role with exactly one runtime function. Its
actual login may not inherit API/owner/sync/observer/publisher/identity/migrator or
privileged roles. Owner-only `set_webhook_ingress(login name,environment,key,enabled)`
binds the actual session login to sandbox. The operator receipt records session_user,
exact input and resulting revision. Disabling this configuration stops new ingress;
it does not revoke already authorized account workers. Mixed-role guards extend
sync login, ledger authorization and observer binding authorization forward.

`accept_verified_webhook(environment,receipt_key,raw)` is callable only by this
configured ingress login, in Serializable transactions. Trusted verifier JSON is:

```json
{"item_id":"provider-case-sensitive-id","body_sha256":"64-lowercase-hex",
 "issued_at":1791936000,"webhook_type":"TRANSACTIONS",
 "webhook_code":"SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE"}
```

Receipt key is SHA-256 of the verified header/payload plus canonical ES256 signature
R || min(S, N-S), encoded as the signing profile specifies. This prevents equivalent
ECDSA signature representations from creating another signal. Go must verify signature, trusted
key, exact raw body, age and bounds before SQL; storing a hash does not prove ownership
or replace cryptographic verification. SQL stores only bounded validated metadata,
not body/JWT/token. Initial SQL acceptance checks age at most 300s and future skew
at most 60s. Receipt replay still requires current ingress/Item/source/consent/service
authority; original age does not defeat database commit recovery. HTTP verification
continues to enforce its own current-age policy on each delivery.

SQL resolves the provider/environment/Item tuple; the caller supplies no actor or
entity/book. Up to 25 currently eligible bound streams receive one signal each,
with the receipt and outbox facts in the same transaction. Unknown/disabled/noeligible
Item uniformly denies without a receipt. Paused or revoked sibling bindings do not
receive work. Replay rechecks every originally accepted stream before duplicate
acknowledgement; a different valid later JWT with the same body remains a new signal.
Response `{state:accepted|duplicate,receipt_id:uuid,stream_count:integer}` is private
service metadata; public HTTP acknowledgement need not disclose it.

## Catch-up and limits

`catchup_sync(e,b,tick uuid,maximum integer,after_id uuid|null)` is sync-role-only.
It scans up to 100 current eligible streams owned by the actual worker login within
trusted injected scope, returns `{items:[{stream_id,requested_generation:string}],
next_cursor:uuid|null}` and requests through the same signal/outbox helper. Ineligible
streams are skipped; no caller actor or credential reference is returned. Stable tick
plus stream identity is one durable increment across retries and page-size changes.
Newly inserted streams before a page cursor are picked up by a subsequent tick; this
is bounded discovery, not a frozen full-scope snapshot or scheduler implementation.

All affected principals are locked in UUID order before entity/book/source/Item/
stream locks. Signal/completion share those locks: completion publishes only its
captured target, preserving later requested generations. No financial row is touched
by any operation in this migration. Errors are fixed connection_operation_rejected:
P2800 malformed/isolation, P2801 authority, P2802 conflicting replay, P2803 stale
revision/time, P2804 unfinished/invalid state, P2805 bound. Existing P270x/P260x
current-authorization failures retain their classifications. Retry serialization and
deadlock as whole transactions; unknown commits must resolve by the same key.

Physical receipt/outbox tables are owner-owned, runtime DML is absent and immutable
triggers retain receipts. Raw provider evidence retention, delivery transport,
webhook deployment, scheduled execution and account-specific retry/backoff policy
remain separately qualified. A durable signal is not a dispatched task or a claim
that account balances are current.

documents.title: Explicit connection configuration in releases
documents.body:
# Explicit connection configuration in releases

## Decision

Runtime releases use schemaVersion2 and require `connections`: null explicitly
disables enrollment; a complete metadata object enables the existing Sandbox-only
composition. Omission and legacy runtime schemaVersion1 are rejected before cloud
authentication. Migration/verification releases retain schemaVersion1 and cannot
carry connection settings. This closes the silent-default reset from PR110.

The object uses the existing Terraform names: infisical_origin, infisical_project,
infisical_identity, link_events_qualified, client_id_version, client_secret_version,
consent_expires_at. `link_events_qualified` remains a required boolean, but may
be false for the [Hosted Link profile](hosted-link-enrollment.md). It describes
ordinary-SDK account enablement, not overall Sandbox qualification. No credentials, destination overrides or extra fields. Validate
exact approved origins/nonzero UUIDs, canonical same-project numeric resources and
positive int64 project/version IDs. Absolute consent expiry must remain future, at most30
days away, and later than release authorization expiry. Owner review binds the
exact file hash; existing closure/build/migration gates remain unchanged.

The CLI passes this object unchanged to runtime.tfvars.json. The transport receipt
records a canonical digest of the approved configuration, not evidence of provider
readiness or observed runtime settings. Rollback requires the prior successful
receipt's same configuration digest, including expiry; changed or expired connection
policy needs a separately reviewed forward promotion. Legacy receipts without that
digest cannot establish configuration-preserving rollback.

## Evidence and alternatives

### Explicit owned Hosted repair (#328)

Engineering profile for the source-only328 delivery; actual activation remains
separately reviewed. Optional boolean `hosted_repair` defaults absent/false.
Existing absent-field configuration/digests and webhook-only behavior remain
unchanged. True requires the fixed Sandbox project/receiver, a live finite local
approval, the encrypted store and source32/33 plus the owned service/receiver.
It cannot select a provider environment, URL, product or account scope.
It propagates only as `-plaid-hosted-repair=true` through reviewed runtime metadata.

True is eligible only for `sandbox-promote`/`sandbox-rollback`. Release gates must
require merged repair SQL/receiver/store/service/runtime source ancestral to both
workflow and selected same-build images, accepted302/303 readiness and current
owner compatibility review of schema33, API/receiver images and SQL bootstrap.
The runtime PR gate must use this delivery's actual published PR identity before
ready review; a guessed/unbound self-gate is not acceptable. Tests do not authorize
activation or turn issue closure/prose into automated live-receiver evidence.

The selected migrator's existing read-only status/hash check runs before runtime
rollout, requiring its exact clean embedded schema (at least33 by source ancestry).
No direct API schema-table grant or startup SQL/KMS probe is added. For the new
repair-enabled Sandbox rollback only, run the same selected-image **status** job
before API rollback; never `up`, force or down. Legacy rollback remains job/DB-inert.
This explicit exception prevents an old-schema repair rollback from starting bank
work. Same approved connection digest/prior Sandbox receipt rules still apply.

Alternatives rejected: enabling repair from the existing webhook URL silently
expands prior approval; skipping status for repair rollback leaves a schema gap;
running up during rollback mutates data; broadening API SQL grants or runtime key
matching weakens authority. Keep provider/SourceItem consent unchanged; changed or
expired approval always requires fresh exact-byte review. Cold expired optional
enrollment still starts SQL-only bookkeeping recovery without dependency I/O.

This is internal operational authorization/release metadata under STD-01, not an
ISO20022 financial exchange. Existing crypto, API2020-09-14, currency, original
units and accounting mappings are unchanged. Named runtime/CLI/release/infra/
status-before-rollout and expired-recovery evidence is recorded in
[the runtime stages](../runbooks/hosted-repair-runtime.md). Human security review
and actual303/275/320 qualification remain independent release requirements.

### Explicit Sandbox webhook enrollment (#271)

Optional `webhook_url` adds only the fixed reviewed dedicated Sandbox receiver:
`https://jayburd-dev-webhook-9088794002.us-central1.run.app/webhooks/plaid`.
Both fixed development project identifiers are required. Empty/null/arbitrary
values in release metadata are rejected; omit the field for the legacy profile.
Its presence changes the approved configuration digest and therefore cannot be
silently introduced by rollback. Terraform threads the explicit flag to the API;
runtime validates it before I/O. No request can choose a notification destination.
This changes new enrollment only; existing Item updates remain a separately
authorized proposal in [webhook enrollment](webhook-enrollment.md). Provider ACK
does not establish Transactions delivery. Dedicated public host release and source
consent must be qualified independently before enabling the field in a release.

### Existing release source review

Reviewed selected HashiCorp input-variable assignment/default/precedence sections
and Google Cloud Run revision management on2026-10-14:
[Terraform variables](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/values/variables),
[Cloud Run revisions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/managing/revisions).
Variables omitted from the generated file fall back to configuration defaults;
Cloud Run revisions capture configuration changes. Requiring an explicit state is
our release-policy inference, not a vendor accounting or security guarantee.

An optional field would retain the omission hazard. Reading live configuration to
silently preserve it would weaken exact-hash review and introduce another authority.
We choose an explicit versioned manifest. Infrastructure/internal configuration is
not an ISO20022 financial message; existing transaction/currency mappings stand.

## Acceptance and limits

Named release tests cover enabled/null propagation, omission/legacy rejection,
partial/cross-project/alias/overflow metadata, expiry, unchanged migration isolation,
configuration-bound rollback and deterministic receipt digest. Default tests use
fictional metadata and no provider/cloud calls. This does not create a release,
provision Infisical, implement Link/reconnect, deploy workers or qualify Sandbox.
#27/#11 retain delivery/configuration acceptance; #88 retains provider qualification.

## First Sandbox writer configuration

The first hosted qualification selects project
`ec11c550-d143-4902-be67-e33266753539` and writer identity
`56d2a541-a48d-4bcc-ae0c-11f48c945ba2`, origin `https://app.infisical.com`.
The [isolated role exception](provider-vault.md#approved-isolated-sandbox-role-exception)
is owner-approved; the manifest evidence must link the configuration confirmation.
Use the existing Hosted Link profile (`link_events_qualified=false`); do not infer
ordinary-SDK qualification from saved identity settings. A complete reviewed
manifest still requires the public Firebase browser identifier, exact build/image
receipts and numeric static GSM pins. No placeholder identifier may be deployed.


## Encrypted bank-token runtime transition (#162–#164)

The new API/consumer image pair selects encrypted PostgreSQL storage, with fixed
KMS resource `projects/{projectNumber}/locations/us-central1/keyRings/jayburd-dev/cryptoKeys/bank-credentials`.
This name is frozen in source and matches workers Terraform; it is not chosen by
an HTTP request, ambient environment or mutable alias. Existing schemaVersion2
Infisical/mapping identifiers remain validated compatibility metadata, but the new
dynamic-token runtime never reads them. Static client versions remain authoritative.

Apply workers KMS resources/grants, forward migration 18, and matching API/consumer
images before owner enrollment. Keep scheduling paused. After encrypted credentials
are activated, legacy-image rollback is incompatible; use a compatible encrypted
image or reviewed forward repair. Deployment acceptance must enforce this build
compatibility, not rely on the unchanged configuration digest. Hosted KMS/IAM and
owner acceptance remain #164; synthetic tests do not close that gate.

Runtime promotion/rollback gates now require closed #162/#163 and merged #165
ancestral to the selected build and workflow. The existing deploy workflows check
that ancestry before cloud authentication. Worker gates carry the same barrier.
This prevents selecting pre-encryption images even with an unchanged legacy
connection-policy digest. Migration/verification-only gates remain unchanged.

documents.title: Connection service boundary
documents.body:
# Connection service boundary

Approved synthetic implementation design for #101, 2026-10-13. SQL migration13
owns current connect permission, attempts, one-shot claims, explicit bindings and
shared Item fencing. This package supplies injected provider and immutable secret
storage boundaries. No real provider, Infisical, cloud or credential access occurs.

`Begin`, `Execute`, `Reconcile`, `Attempt`, `List`, `Bind`, and `Disconnect` accept
verified actor/entity/book scope. Begin modes are new/reconnect/rotate/remove.
Existing Item operations require the reviewed generation and complete approved
stream IDs. Tokens returned to the browser remain memory-only. The browser returns
the original Link token and nonce; SQL receives hashes only, while the provider
verifies the completed session association before exchange. Client metadata never
authorizes account ownership. Missing provider association fails closed.

SQL commits each external-operation claim before I/O. Only the first confirmed
claim may exchange/rotate/remove. A lost SQL acknowledgement performs no provider
operation. A lost provider acknowledgement remains credential recovery and is never
blindly retried. Successful exchange verifies Item/accounts, durably records that
manifest with a preallocated credential reference, then writes the secret version.
Exact reference/version/Item and token readback precede reference publication.
Recovery only reads a deterministic version and revalidates its manifest; it never
repeats exchange or rotation. An absent secret remains unresolved.

Reconnect verifies the same Item and account scope; changed Item identity requires
a new connection and explicit overlap review. Rotation fences every sibling before
external mutation. Single-account disconnect never calls Item removal. Full Item
removal requires all affected bindings, fences locally first, and confirms remotely
before reporting removal complete. Posted journals and source history are retained.

Selected depository accounts map explicitly to ledger/source/currency/evidence.
SQL permits a first provider namespace without an overlap hold only where it proves
there is no prior namespace/evidence; existing sources retain overlap review.
Unsupported accounts are metadata only. No balances, journals or transactions are
invented by connection management.

## Sources and limits

Reviewed selected official sections on 2026-10-13, extending PI05–PI08:

- [Plaid Link API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/): token creation/expiration and
  token-get session results. Complete non-Hosted session events require provider
  enablement. The injected strict session verifier is a Hosted-Link-compatible
  qualification profile, not a claim that arbitrary callbacks prove association.
- [Plaid Items API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/items/): exchange identifies an Item;
  rotation replaces its credential; removal invalidates Item access. Remote
  operations are not assumed transactional with local SQL.
- [Plaid Accounts API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/): server account metadata,
  case-sensitive identities and account-type/currency mapping. Names/masks are not
  ownership proof; balance data is not used by this service.

These are selected public documentation sections, not Sandbox qualification.
Proprietary Plaid JSON retains the existing STD-01 assessment; ISO4217 currency
references and date rules apply. No ISO20022 or legal-consent conformance is claimed.
The concrete HTTP adapter uses injected transport and fixed sandbox endpoints;
Infisical production adapter and hosted Link/event availability remain #88 gates.

## Concrete adapter and recovery limits

`NewHTTPProvider` performs no I/O and requires explicit credentials, transport and
a fixed future `ConsentExpiresAt`. This is a local authorization upper bound, not
a fabricated provider-reported consent date. The effective expiry is the earlier
of this bound and a provider expiry when present. A null provider expiry leaves
the fixed local bound intact; reconciliation never rolls it forward.

Requests use sandbox.plaid.com, Plaid-Version2020-09-14, Transactions only, US and
English for this bounded qualification profile. No caller chooses the destination.
The client permits one attempt, three seconds per call, no redirects, and at most
256KiB response bytes. Duplicate keys, trailing JSON and nesting beyond32 reject;
material tokens/identifiers must be bounded printable ASCII. Metadata balances
are ignored without conversion to money. Unsupported account types remain visible
as metadata and cannot be bound by SQL.

New-Link association requires a matching returned Link token and exactly one
completed `results.item_add_results` entry matching the public token. Deprecated
`on_success` is not a fallback. The concrete adapter **rejects reconnect before
creating or claiming an attempt** because the ordinary update-mode session proof
has not been qualified. Injected-provider reconnect tests prove our lifecycle,
not a working hosted reauthentication flow. The existing access token or a
successful accounts lookup alone never proves user reauthentication.

Normal service calls have a ten-second aggregate budget inside the existing
server twelve-second request budget. SQL calls use bounded SERIALIZABLE retries
only for confirmed rollback, and return `commit_unknown` for ambiguous COMMIT.
Denial deliberately maps to `not_found` to avoid exposing unauthorized scope.
`exchange_claimed` and `disconnect_pending` are unresolved states, never connected
or permission to repeat a provider mutation. A Link token lost before browser
delivery is not recreated through the same idempotency key.

Immediate storage readback compares exact token bytes and the complete addressed
reference/version/Item. After process loss, the original bytes are intentionally
unavailable: reconciliation trusts the immutable secret-store version contract
and revalidates the complete provider manifest. It cannot repair a lost exchange
response, absent version, changed manifest or uncertain Item removal automatically.
An orphan private secret version may remain after revocation; it is not an active
database reference and requires separately authorized retention cleanup.

Existing [Infisical policy](../infisical.md) uses one-way synchronization into GCP
Secret Manager with runtime read-only access. Dynamic enrollment writes require a
separately reviewed writer identity, paths, propagation acknowledgement and exact
version visibility. This implementation supplies only injected store semantics;
it adds no Infisical writer or alternate direct-read path. `Secret.WithValue`
intentionally exposes plaintext to a trusted adapter callback only; formatting and
JSON serialization remain redacted/rejected. Go strings are not claimed zeroizable.

## Validation requirements

Synthetic lifecycle tests must prove denial before I/O, wrong scope/session, current
revocation, duplicate claims, unknown provider/secret/SQL acknowledgement, exact
secret readback, same-Item reconnect, sibling rotation fencing, explicit binding,
account disconnect versus Item removal, and no credential serialization. Actual SQL
tests must compose the service with migration13 and verify no financial mutations.

documents.title: Connection lifecycle SQL
documents.body:
# Connection lifecycle SQL

## Approved decision

Coordinator-approved #101/#102 foundation, 2026-10-13. Migration 13 adds durable
connection attempts and opaque credential-reference publication to migration 12.
Tokens never enter SQL. Go's trusted connection service verifies Link association,
provider Item/account metadata and secret-store acknowledgement through injected
interfaces. SQL authorizes scope and controls publication; it cannot make a remote
exchange transactional or certify live account ownership. Synthetic provider/secret
adapters are proof tools, not a hosted connection integration.

Provider Link/Items JSON is proprietary, not ISO 20022. Existing PI05–PI08, ISO 4217
and date rules apply. Refreshed official [Items API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/items/)
sections public-token exchange, access-token invalidation and Item removal, and
[Link update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode/), 2026-10-13. These establish
separate remote operations and same-Item update behavior; they do not guarantee
idempotent recovery after lost responses. Our inference is a one-shot durable claim,
verified manifest, deterministic secret reference and explicit uncertain state.
Blind remote retries and storing tokens in the database are rejected alternatives.
Only selected relevant sections were reviewed; no Sandbox/production qualification.

## Authority and identity

Existing `bookkeeping_api` is the trusted backend SQL boundary, as for decoder
publication. Connection functions take the server-resolved actor, never identity
from Link metadata. New explicit entity `connect` membership is owner-provisioned;
current read/connect/import is required for mutations and replay. Existing-source
binding additionally requires source read/import/bind. Worker principal/login is
owner-configured per book and cannot be selected by a runtime request. Provider-first
creation explicitly consents to bounded actor/service read+import and actor bind
source grants; no administrative permission, grant option or arbitrary grantee.
The service's entity read/import grants must already exist. Worker configuration
disable/replacement governs connection enrollment/management, not revocation of
previously enrolled sync streams; revoke their current principal/source permissions
or pause/disconnect the Item to stop existing acquisition. No implicit credential
retrieval/write permission follows from this configuration.

One Item belongs to one entity/book, at most 25 account streams. Existing source
mapping remains immutable; new namespaces on an existing source hold overlap.
Only a new provider-first source with no namespace/evidence starts without that
hold. Currency/depository/ledger mapping is explicit; provider account name/mask
never establish ownership. Mismatched reconnect Item cannot inherit old cursors.

## Frozen SQL interfaces

Scope/actor/attempt/claim/nonce/Item/stream identifiers are UUIDs; keys are bounded
text. All calls use SERIALIZABLE and fixed diagnostics. No new public raw-manifest
HTTP route is implied by these trusted-backend SQL functions.

- `begin_connection(actor,e,b,key,raw)` takes mode new/reconnect/rotate/remove,
  sync_item_id nullable UUID, expected_generation nullable decimal string,
  approved_stream_ids UUID array. New requires null/null/empty; other modes require
  exact current affected set and generation. Returns private context; execute_link
  true only for first new/reconnect insertion. Attempt/nonce/expiry are durable.
- `record_link_session(actor,e,b,attempt,nonce,raw)` takes link_token_sha256 and
  expires_at. Hash pins association, not ownership. Link/public tokens remain outside SQL.
- `claim_connection(actor,e,b,attempt,nonce,raw)` takes nullable link_token_sha256
  and public_token_sha256. New requires both; reconnect Link only; rotate/remove
  neither. Returns execute_provider true only for first claim. Replays are false;
  uncertain claim commit cannot authorize a repeated provider side effect.
- `record_connection_manifest(actor,e,b,attempt,claim,raw)` takes verified item_id,
  accounts [{account_id,type,iso_currency_code nullable}], consent_expires_at;
  persists credential_pending before secret write. Types are depository/credit/
  loan/investment/other; unsupported accounts remain unbound. No token fields accepted.
- `confirm_connection_credential(actor,e,b,attempt,claim)` follows confirmed secret
  write/readback. New enters binding_review; reconnect/rotate require same Item and
  all bound accounts still valid before reactivation. Remote exchange is never repeated.
- `connection_failure(actor,e,b,attempt,claim,reason)` records fixed uncertainty,
  preserving recovery and local fences instead of claiming success.
- `connection_context(actor,e,b,attempt)` is the trusted service projection below.
  `get_connection_attempt(actor,e,b,attempt)` is its safe browser projection.
- `bind_connection(actor,e,b,attempt,key,raw)` takes consent_grants:true and bindings
  [{account_id,ledger_account_id,currency_version_id,source_account_id nullable,
  expected_binding_revision nullable,binding_date,binding_evidence_ref}]. Only
  verified accounts are selectable. Scope/currency/date/deposit and current grants
  are checked before atomic source/namespace/stream publication.
- `list_connections(actor,e,b)` returns {items:[{sync_item_id,item_id,state,
  item_generation,accounts:[{stream_id,account_id,source_account_id,state,
  binding_revision}]}]}; bounded at 100 Items/25 accounts with explicit overflow.
- `disconnect_stream(actor,e,b,stream,key,expected_binding_revision bigint)` fences
  only that account; returns {stream_id,state:"disconnected"}. It never removes Item.
- `confirm_item_removed(actor,e,b,attempt,claim)` records confirmed remote removal.
  Whole-Item approval/fences precede provider I/O; unknown reply stays unresolved.

Private context fields: attempt_id,entity_id,book_id,mode,state,nonce,expires_at,
sync_item_id nullable,item_generation nullable string,expected_item_id nullable,
claim_id nullable,credential_ref nullable,credential_version nullable string,
previous_credential_ref nullable,previous_credential_version nullable string,
link_token_sha256 nullable,public_token_sha256 nullable,manifest nullable,
execute_link boolean,execute_provider boolean. Get/replay execution booleans are false.
Public attempt: attempt_id,entity_id,book_id,mode,state,expires_at,sync_item_id,manifest.
No hashes, nonce, secret refs or claim are exposed by status. Bind also returns streams
[{stream_id,source_account_id,namespace_id,binding_revision,overlap_review_required}].

States are link_pending, link_ready, exchange_claimed, credential_pending,
binding_review, active, credential_recovery_required, disconnect_pending and
disconnected. An exchange_claimed attempt after a crash is unresolved recovery work,
never authority to repeat the remote call. Attempt history may say active while the
current Item listing shows a later lifecycle state. Attempt handoff expires after
15 minutes, clamped to earlier Link expiry; expiry blocks a first claim and new
binding, while already reserved credential recovery still requires current grants
and unexpired verified consent. There is no automatic secret cleanup.

Owner-only SECURITY INVOKER provisioning functions are
`set_connect_permission(actor,e,b,subject,key,enabled)`,
`set_connection_worker(actor,e,b,key,raw)` with
{service_principal_id,worker_login,enabled}, and
`set_source_bind_permission(actor,e,b,source,key,raw)` with
{expected_binding_revision,principal_id,enabled}. Receipts record operator login and
attesting actor. These functions are not exposed to the API role.

Fixed `connection_rejected` diagnostics: P2700 malformed/isolation; P2701 current
authority; P2702 identity/replay conflict; P2703 stale/expired pins; P2704 wrong stage
or invalid verified selection; P2705 bounded overflow. PostgreSQL transaction retry
codes remain visible to the Go transaction owner. Keys accept 1–128 ASCII identifier
characters; raw envelopes reject unknown/duplicate keys and are bounded before casts.

## Credential and lifecycle invariants

SQL allocates immutable target reference/version before external effects. Verified
manifest commits before secret write. Confirmed write/readback precedes activation.
Lost exchange response remains credential_recovery_required; no claim reacquisition.
Lost secret acknowledgement can resolve only the SQL-pinned reference and verified
manifest; no replayed exchange/rotation. Reconnect uses existing reference and
verifies same Item/filter. Rotation fences all siblings before provider invocation;
replacement reference publication is atomic and leaves source identities/cursors.
Removal fences all approved streams first; local disconnect does not imply remote
removal. Revocation/expiry checks apply even to replay; journals/evidence are retained.

## Acquisition additions

`integration.sync_context(e,b,stream,set,fence)` is sync-role-only, rechecks current
session/permissions and live attempt, then returns stream_id,set_id,fence string,
provider,environment,item_id,account_id,item_generation string,credential_ref,
credential_version string,binding_revision string,starting_cursor,request_cursor,
next_page_index,page_count,byte_count,change_count,final_page,lease_until,
currency {code,version_id,minor_unit,valid_from,valid_to nullable}, and limits
{max_pages:10,max_changes:1000,max_bytes:2097152,max_page_changes:500}.

`integration.sync_resume(e,b,stream,claim_uuid)` reauthorizes before returning
{state:absent|staging|completed|abandoned|quarantined,set_id nullable,fence nullable
string,reason nullable string,completion nullable receipt}. Absent is an explicit
object, not JSON null. This enables resolution after an unknown commit without
unnecessarily repeating provider calls. Expired staging cannot gain a new fence;
new attempts restart C0 under the existing rules.

## Acceptance and limits

Planned actual PostgreSQL proof covers scoped role/grant revocation, one-shot claims,
unknown-commit replay, manifest/credential sequencing, provider-first vs overlap,
exact account/currency bindings, same-Item reconnect, sibling rotation fencing,
single-account disconnect, Item removal uncertainty and private context access.
Named executed evidence belongs in the [runbook](../runbooks/connection-sql.md).
No test names here imply PASS. Hosted adapters, secret policy and Sandbox/live
qualification remain explicit external gates.

Private context revalidates Item generation and the approved sibling set for every
nonterminal attempt before exposing credential references. Unclaimed attempts also
require unexpired handoff authority; public status remains readable with current
permissions after these pins become stale.

New and first-claimed reconnect/rotation/removal operations require Item state
active, paused or reauthorization_required. A claimed operation first moves the
Item into credential_recovery_required or disconnect_pending, excluding overlapping
remote mutations even when two attempts were prepared beforehand. Only that pinned
attempt may reconcile its recorded manifest/reference. Unknown operations without
a persisted manifest have no automatic recovery path; a new attempt cannot bypass
the unresolved remote outcome. Generation fencing alone cannot cancel an in-flight
provider request.

documents.title: Connection recovery and acquisition status UI
documents.body:
# Connection recovery and acquisition status UI

## Review and decision

Coordinator-approved design for #104 after merged #107. Reviewed the existing connection
workspace, HTTP/service/SQL lifecycle contracts and provider-sync SQL sections
on Item state, request generations, leases and complete publication. These reuse
the recorded PI05–PI08 provider sources; this is presentation and scoped control,
not a new provider wire or ISO 20022 claim. Currency/date handling retains the
existing standards profile.

The previous UI's memory-only enrollment latch cannot recover an attempt after
reload. Authenticated durable discovery must complete before new enrollment is
offered; unavailable, partial or malformed discovery fails closed. Browser storage
is not an alternative. An expired unclaimed attempt must be distinguished by the
server from unresolved claimed work; expiry never authorizes another exchange.

## Proposed presentation

A recovery section lists scoped durable attempts with clear state and permitted
inspection/reconciliation and expired-unclaimed presentation. No nonce, Link/public token, provider claim,
credential reference or raw provider error is displayed or persisted. Unfinished
provider exchanges stay unresolved; reconciliation never blindly retries exchange.

Each source stream shows current readiness, requested/completed generations,
last complete publication and a separately labeled unknown provider update time.
Publication is local atomic source visibility; it is not a provider update timestamp,
a posted balance, or proof that all history exists. Initializing, paused, pending,
lease-expired and credential recovery states remain visibly incomplete.

Pause/resume applies to one account stream. The explicit confirmation names that
account and states that sibling acquisition and posted journals are unchanged.
A manual sync request only records requested work; its receipt cannot claim an
executed provider pull or a changed posted balance. Both use current server pins,
explicit confirmation and the exact original idempotency key on uncertain replies.

## Frozen wire

GET `connection-attempts?limit=100&before=UUID` (before optional) returns
`{items:[ConnectionAttempt + expired_unclaimed:boolean + binding_expired:boolean],next_cursor:UUID|null,
unfinished_count:string}`. SQL calculates unfinished_count across all pages;
zero permits a new Begin after successful discovery, and SQL also blocks a fresh
Begin if unfinished work exists. Each page is bounded at100 and current permissions
apply on every read. Expired unclaimed rows are inspected without replay; claimed
uncertain work is never treated as expired authorization for another exchange.
Known `binding_review` publication whose handoff expired has binding_expired:true;
it is excluded from unfinished_count, keeps credential history and its paused Item,
and cannot be bound through the expired attempt. The UI labels it distinctly and
hides binding controls. Inspection rechecks discovery before clearing any local
enrollment latch; a concurrent unknown attempt still blocks a fresh Begin.

GET `connections/streams/{stream}/status` returns stream/source/Item identifiers,
stream state/revision, Item state/generation, binding revision, requested/completed generations,
queued and lease_active booleans, readiness, last_completed_at, fixed last_error
and provider_updated_at:null. Revision/generation values stay decimal strings.
The UI loads one selected stream on explicit request, avoiding an unbounded fanout
across every account. It checks all three selected identities before display.

POST `connections/streams/{stream}/operations` takes `{action:pause|resume|request,
expected_item_generation:string,expected_binding_revision:string,
expected_stream_revision:string}` and one
Idempotency-Key. It returns status. An uncertain reply retains its exact body/key
in component memory. Stream revision independently fences pause/resume without
changing source binding/review authority. After confirmation, the UI reads fresh status so an old replay
receipt cannot masquerade as current state. Rejection does not authorize a new
provider exchange. Tokens and request bodies remain outside browser persistence.

The last_error allowlist is pagination_mutation, provider_failure, decoder_rejected,
cancelled, item_changed, lease_expired, account_disconnected, account_paused or null.
These fixed outcomes are shown as text; no raw provider diagnostic is accepted.
Existing concrete reconnect stays unavailable pending qualification. No provider
SDK or cloud integration is enabled by this UI.

## Acceptance

Named tests will cover reload discovery before Begin, expired-unclaimed versus
claimed recovery, malformed/incomplete discovery, revoked and stale scope,
late mutation responses, Item-wide confirmation, exact same-key unknown-result
recovery, honest timestamps and no browser persistence. Existing explicit review
and posting continue through source review and durable command recovery.

## Fresh link-ready inspection gap (#186)

The owner observed a new `link_ready` attempt after the 2026-10-18 Sandbox retry,
then **Review attempt** produced the generic unconfirmed-operation banner. The
screen still showed no connected Item. The screenshot does not establish the
GET status, a malformed response or a provider outcome. Inspection is a
read-only exact-attempt GET; it cannot finish Link or recover the memory-only
handoff. The current UI catches most non-403/404 failures as the same generic
message, so diagnosis must distinguish transport, API and response-validation
failures using only a fixed status/problem code and redacted request metadata.

Proposed UI acceptance: a fresh Begin followed by discovery and exact-attempt
GET displays `link_ready` without an error; if the detail read fails, preserve
independently valid discovery and show a safe action matched to the failure.
For an active handoff, completion controls remain visible and named as the path
forward. For a lost handoff, offer server-side completion status recovery first;
show a guarded restart only when the conditions in
[Hosted Link enrollment](hosted-link-enrollment.md) are proven. Technical
attempt IDs belong in secondary details rather than the
primary bank setup action. A successful GET alone must not mark an Item
connected, authorize another exchange or close hosted acceptance.

documents.title: Bounded connection workspace
documents.body:
# Bounded connection workspace

## Decision and sources

Issue #104's first UI slice uses the frozen [HTTP](connection-http.md),
[service](connection-service.md) and [SQL](connection-sql.md) contracts. Selected
sections reviewed: routes, authority, one-shot claims, verified manifest binding,
credential recovery and concrete adapter limitations. These reuse PI05–PI08's
recorded source review; this UI adds no provider behavior or ISO message claim.
Internal connection commands follow the existing standards applicability profile;
currency versions and dates remain explicit. No live qualification is implied.
The [Hosted Link completion contract](hosted-link-enrollment.md) extends the
original adapter flow with an explicit new-tab handoff and completion check.

## Component contract

`Connections` accepts api, entity, book, currencies, locked, denied, onReview and an
optional injected `link` adapter. `link.open({linkToken,signal})` returns a
memory-only `{publicToken}` or null for cancellation. Root owns composition; an
absent adapter means new bank setup is unavailable, while list reads remain usable.
New scope, lock and unmount discard sensitive state and abort the Link adapter.
Late results cannot execute an exchange, update another scope or start binding.

Supported operations are list, new connection, explicit first-provider binding,
known attempt inspection and reconciliation, and account-only disconnect.
Connection attempts are a separate durable lifecycle from posting commands.
Unknown exchange outcomes are inspected, never automatically exchanged again.
Binding/disconnect retries preserve the exact request and idempotency key in
memory; page loss requires reading durable status before any new action.

Each selected verified depository account maps to an explicitly chosen active
monetary debit asset account, matching currency version and binding date. No
account is preselected and no permission is inferred from the workspace import
flag. A generated binding evidence UUID identifies the explicit local confirmation,
not a fabricated bank document. SQL remains authoritative for grants and mappings.

## Presentation and limits

Current Item status and historical attempt status are labeled separately. Active
means enrolled, not complete acquisition or a balance. Unavailable reads never
render as empty connections. Pending/changed/removed source items use the existing
review/posting workflow; `onReview(sourceID)` opens its explicit source selector.
No automatic posting or financial totals originate here.

No public attempt discovery, pause, acquisition retry or timestamp projection exists.
Known attempt inspection needs its UUID; reload cannot rediscover a lost Begin
response. The local unfinished-enrollment latch also disappears on scope/lock/remount;
it is not durable cross-session prevention of a second enrollment. Reconnect is unavailable in the concrete provider profile. Item rotation,
Item removal, existing-source overlap binding and real Link hosting are deferred.
These limits keep full #104 acceptance open. Required evidence: component scope,
revocation, interrupted flow and single-flight tests, injected enrollment/binding;
root owns keyboard/mobile and browser→Go→PostgreSQL journey evidence.

documents.title: Database design contract
documents.body:
# Database design contract

## Decision and status

Design before product DDL. This is a proposed logical model and review standard,
not an approved physical schema. JB-001 resolves accounting policy; JB-002 owns
the first schema review. [Accounting invariants](accounting.md) remain authoritative.

## Current review package

| Contract | Purpose and status |
| --- | --- |
| [Schema ownership ADR](../decisions/0004-schema-ownership.md) | Owner-accepted namespace and naming direction; grants proposed |
| [Accounting scenarios and policy](accounting-scenarios.md) | Worked examples and unresolved owner/accountant decisions |
| [Money and multicurrency](multicurrency.md) | Proposed amounts, rate provenance and FX lifecycle |
| [SQL contract](ledger-sql.md) | First-slice column dictionary, roles, transaction ordering and named acceptance tests |
| [HTTP contract](api.md) | Operation semantics and draft OpenAPI 3.1.1 document |
| [Additional source review](../research/contract-sources.md) | Exact source scope, interpretations and limitations |

This index states the review requirements; the SQL contract owns the detailed
first-slice model. No SQL migration or runtime endpoint implements these drafts.

## Logical relationships

An entity owns separate books. A bank/provider account is a source of observations;
a ledger account is an accounting classification. Never collapse those concepts.
Journal lines reference accounts in the same entity AND book as their journal.

```mermaid
erDiagram
    ENTITY ||--o{ MEMBERSHIP : authorizes
    PRINCIPAL ||--o{ MEMBERSHIP : receives
    ENTITY ||--o{ BOOK : owns
    BOOK ||--o{ LEDGER_ACCOUNT : classifies
    BOOK ||--o{ ACCOUNTING_PERIOD : closes
    BOOK ||--o{ JOURNAL : records
    JOURNAL ||--|{ JOURNAL_LINE : contains
    LEDGER_ACCOUNT ||--o{ JOURNAL_LINE : classifies
    ENTITY ||--o{ SOURCE_ACCOUNT : connects
    SOURCE_ACCOUNT ||--o{ SOURCE_OBSERVATION : supplies
    SOURCE_OBSERVATION ||--o{ SOURCE_LINK : traces
    JOURNAL ||--o{ SOURCE_LINK : explains
```

This omits proposed audit/idempotency/outbox tables and reconciliation details;
cardinality alone does not enforce balanced entries or authorization.

## Required physical specification per table

Document purpose/owner, row grain, primary/business keys, every column's SQL type,
nullability, default, meaning and allowed values. Specify entity-scoped foreign
keys, unique/check constraints, lifecycle/deletion, sensitive fields, access roles,
retention, indexes justified by named queries and expected cardinality. Use
`snake_case`; distinguish accounting `date` from operational `timestamptz`.
Decide exact money representation, currency rules and rounding before columns
are approved. Do not use float or assume a fixed two-decimal world.

## Required operation specification

For posting, reversal, reconciliation and close, record:

1. Trusted caller, entity permission and operation inputs.
2. Preconditions and state transitions, including revoked access and closed periods.
3. Transaction isolation, lock order, retryable SQLSTATEs and bounded retry policy.
4. All writes and their atomic boundary, idempotency scope and payload comparison.
5. Result/error semantics, audit/source evidence and allowed subsequent operations.

Posting must not expose an intermediate unbalanced journal. Ordinary row CHECKs
cannot enforce cross-row balancing. JB-002 must choose and prove the owned write
boundary, privileges and any deferred constraint triggers. Cross-entity references
must fail in PostgreSQL, not merely in UI validation. Intercompany movements
require linked entries in separate books, never a mixed-entity journal.

## Review and acceptance matrix

| Contract evidence | Named future test |
| --- | --- |
| Entity keys, references and grants | `TestEntityReferencesAndPrivileges` |
| Exact money and balanced atomic posting | `TestPostingInvariants` |
| Concurrent idempotent requests | `TestPostingReplayConcurrency` |
| Posted immutability and linked correction | `TestJournalCorrectionHistory` |
| Posting versus close lock protocol | `TestPostingCloseRace` |
| Golden-month reports and reconciliation | `TestGoldenMonth` |
| Old/new application compatibility | `TestSchemaCompatibility` |

These are requirements, not implemented tests. SQL must be reviewed with example
queries and `EXPLAIN` evidence when data volumes make plans meaningful. An ERD or
successful migration is not acceptance evidence for accounting behavior.

## Done when and blockers

JB-002 is ready when reviewed column dictionaries, operation contracts, role
matrix, invariants and named test cases cover the first slice. Blockers: accounting
basis, functional currencies, opening balances, timezone, permission model and
acceptance of the proposed posting enforcement mechanism. Then create product
migrations and their tests for the approved slice.

documents.title: Development canary delivery job
documents.body:
# Development canary delivery job

## Decision

Owner requested job/identity wiring on 2026-10-14 while PR #113 is reviewed.
Compose its adapter as a one-shot Cloud Run Job, initially restricted to the
root key `JAYBURD_DELIVERY_CANARY` and destination `jayburd-dev-bank-sync-canary`.
The command cannot select Plaid keys, custom URLs or credential values. This
canary must pass before widening job scope to the adapter's existing mappings.
It is not a financial message; ISO 20022 is not applicable.

`cmd/deliver` shares the existing digest-pinned worker image, with `/deliver` as
an explicit entrypoint override. The source is the owner-selected isolated canary project, keeping Viewer scope
away from Plaid. Missing configuration rejects before authentication;
`-check` validates metadata offline. `-lookup` authenticates for an exact-key,
exact-version request with `viewSecretValue=false`, imports and expansion disabled;
it prints only validated ID/version fields and makes no registry/destination calls.
Only `-execute` permits delivery and requires an explicitly supplied source ID.
SIGTERM cancels the bounded operation. Logs contain fixed status text only. An
acknowledgement is not independent payload verification or current authorization.

The isolated `infra/gcp/delivery` root owns the delivery service account, a canary
container, private receipt bucket, optional job and separate invocation identity.
It owns no Plaid container or workers state. Registry IAM is create/get only within
`delivery-v1/`; destination IAM is versions.add only on the canary. The task has
no SQL, source write, destination read, metadata list or secret administration role.
One task, parallelism one, retry count zero and a 60-second platform timeout bound
execution. Concurrent executions still rely on the adapter's durable intent fence.

The Infisical identity uses GCP ID Token Auth with the exact delivery service-account
email, Viewer access only to the isolated canary project, and token TTL/max TTL at most 900 seconds.
It is separate from both the native App Connection and the application writer.
No static keys, personal token or GitHub secret retrieval is needed.

## Controlled invocation

Default `canary=null` creates no executable job. A configured job defaults to lookup
mode with no destination write grant; execute mode adds only the canary version-adder
grant after an explicit metadata review. GitHub federation is disabled by
default and cannot be enabled without reviewed canary metadata. The manual workflow
is bound to repository/owner/actor IDs, main and its exact workflow_ref. Its separate
runner can get/run only the canary job; it has no overrides, job update, actAs,
secret or registry access. There is no scheduler. Workflow success means submission
only; the owner checks Cloud Run execution and redacted receipt evidence separately.

Owner-operated Terraform bootstrap requires an isolated durable backend and reviewed
image receipt. This slice adds invocation through GitHub, not an IAM-capable GitHub
bootstrap deployer. Existing application/worker release workflows remain separate.

## Sources, alternatives and evidence

Reviewed relevant official sections on 2026-10-14:

- [Google provider v8.6.0 job reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google/v8.6.0/website/docs/r/cloud_run_v2_job.html.markdown):
  task template, service account, command, task count, retries and timeout fields.
  These define configuration, not measured runtime behavior.
- [Infisical GCP ID Token Auth guide](https://infisical.com/docs/documentation/platform/identities/gcp-auth):
  machine identity creation, removal of default Universal Auth, exact allowed
  service-account emails and project membership. GCE project/zone restrictions
  do not establish Cloud Run identity scope.
- Existing [delivery source review](scoped-delivery.md#sources-and-alternatives)
  governs exact source versions and unknown acknowledgements.

An always-on service or scheduled poller adds unnecessary lifecycle/retry surface
for the first canary. Reusing API identity would combine source-write and delivery
capabilities. Neither is selected. Runtime IAM propagation and Infisical plan scope
remain uncertain until actual qualification.

Acceptance: `TestExecutionGate`, `TestExecuteRedaction`, providersecrets canary tests,
eight mocked `delivery.tftest.hcl` runs, and candidate container rejection checks.
See the [living runbook](../runbooks/delivery-job.md) for executed evidence and limits.

Metadata source review (2026-10-14): [Infisical Retrieve query parameters](https://infisical.com/docs/api-reference/endpoints/secrets/read)
document `viewSecretValue=false`, exact `version`, disabled reference expansion and
imports. Reviewed those sections, not a hosted response. Unknown response fields
are discarded and never printed; this does not claim the provider cannot return
unexpected fields. Lookup success establishes metadata/auth access only.

## Authorized Sandbox extension

The [hosted Sandbox probe](hosted-sandbox-probe.md) extends the delivery command
allowlist to the two original root Plaid keys. Explicit `key` selects the only
destination granted write access; lookup stays value-disabled. A separate optional
probe identity gets read-only access to the two destination containers. The manual
workflow selects one of two fixed jobs, without overrides or broader invocation IAM.
This supersedes the initial canary-only command restriction above.

## Fixed dynamic-slot extension (#131)

Owner authorized completion of the hosted Sandbox journey on 2026-10-15. The same
explicit command now also accepts exactly `slot-00` through `slot-07`; adapter
mapping fixes their folder to `/bank-sync` and destinations to
`jayburd-dev-bank-sync-slot-00` through `slot-07`. No folder flag, arbitrary key,
credential argument or source discovery/listing is added. `LookupSelected` reads
only metadata for an explicit key/version with values, imports and expansion
disabled; `LookupRoot` retains its root-only compatibility boundary.

Terraform retains the existing `canary` input/job name for compatibility and adds
one selected slot's `secretVersionAdder` grant in execute mode only. Workers own
slot containers; the delivery root does not create/adopt them. Lookup mode removes
all delivery destination-write grants. The job stays one task, zero retries and
60 seconds, with the distinct delivery identity and existing immutable registry.
The adapter rejects returned wrong folder metadata when present; the request
always selects the fixed folder even when the provider omits that response field.

Use a dedicated API-writer Infisical identity and an approved development project
with `/bank-sync`. Writer create/read permission and delivery read permission are
separate from static Plaid source access. On plans without folder/custom-role
support, project isolation alone does not prove create/read-only permissions;
review the actual grant before activation. Do not reuse the delivery identity for
API writes or silently widen it to Admin.

Evidence: `TestSelectedSlots`, `TestSlotMetadataLookup`, `TestDynamicSlots`, existing
unknown-acknowledgement/slot-reuse tests and twelve new mocked Terraform runs.
These are synthetic implementation evidence; actual token propagation, readback
and SQL activation remain a separate hosted acceptance. The prior Infisical and
Google source review above and [adapter sources](scoped-delivery.md#sources-and-alternatives)
apply unchanged. This internal credential protocol has no ISO 20022 mapping.

documents.title: One-click synthetic acquisition
documents.body:
# One-click synthetic acquisition

## Boundary and decision

Issue #97 supplies a **test-only** loader in integration-tagged server test files.
The ordinary application binary has no demo endpoints or synthetic identity.
The coordinator approved three fictional LLCs, one bank account each, 3,000 source
transactions, and bounded explicit request-driven progress. No bank connection,
real upload, automatic journal, cloud workload or background runner is introduced.

The fixture administrator separately provisions source read/import/review grants
through their owner-only functions, plus entity prepare membership. Existing setup
grants only read/post. Prepare fixture insertion does not restore an existing
revoked membership; no runtime self-grant or SQL authorization relaxation exists. Book setup, batch registration, staging,
decoding, preview and explicit import use the existing restricted runtime pool.
The runtime loader never retains the administrator connection. The root composition
owns a private staging Store and keeps its directory for the disposable database's
lifetime. Rebuilding the handler against that database reconstructs identities from
setup/source/registration receipts; deleting the object directory while retaining
its database is unsupported and must not be called successful recovery.

## Hook and HTTP protocol

`bootstrapDemoAcquisition(ctx, admin, pool, store)` returns an `http.Handler`.
Bootstrap creates three idempotent fictional books/sources and registers empty
batches. It does not decode/import transactions or create journals. Composition
mounts it only in the disposable demo integration binary, under the existing
BrowserBoundary for the local demo origin. The handler independently requires the
exact fictional demo bearer identity before returning status or touching SQL.

- `GET /v1/demo/acquisition`: return durable progress; no query parameters.
- `POST /v1/demo/acquisition/step`, body exactly `{}`: perform at most one stage,
  then return freshly read progress. No scope, file, row, amount or URL is accepted.
- Both return `{profile:"synthetic-acquisition-v1",total_count:"3000",
  imported_count:string,complete:boolean,blocked:boolean,
  pending_command_id:string|null,batches:[{name,entity_id,book_id,
  source_account_id,batch_id,state,imported_count:string}]}`.
- Errors are `{error:{code}}`: unauthorized (401), invalid_request (400),
  demo_busy/demo_blocked (409), or demo_retry_required (503). Internal details
  never appear. Responses are no-store. A 503 is not proof of rollback; read status
  and resume the same durable identities.

One explicit Load/Resume action authorizes the synthetic import sequence. The UI
makes successive bounded POSTs only while the user keeps that action active.
Pause stops new requests; no hidden goroutine continues processing. Each request
has a 20-second overall context. A local TryLock rejects overlapping step calls;
SQL receipts, source/statement uniqueness and the existing recovery gate provide
durability and retry safety, not this process lock.

A stage is one of: upload+strict preview, register reviewed import command, execute
that command, or acknowledge its committed result. Existing pending commands must
match the exact demo batch, scope and pinned latest preview before execution or
acknowledgement. Unrelated, cancelled or changed approval blocks progress; it is
never silently discarded. A lost response resumes via Batch and Recovery.pending.
Only imported batches count toward imported_count; completion waits for the last
demo command acknowledgement. This is synthetic import confirmation, not approval
to create financial journals. Journal posting remains a separate review action.

## Dataset and independent oracle

Each LLC has 1,000 deterministic CRLF CSV rows, within the strict decoder's maximum:
500 inflows of USD 100.01 and 500 outflows of USD 25.02, alternated over January 2026.
Names explicitly say Fictional. Descriptions identify customer payments and
operating expenses; there are no real names, bank identifiers or credentials.
Entry IDs are stable within the registered fictional namespace. Integer cents
produce exact decimal strings; no float, rounding or balance plugs are used.

Independent expected values are 1,000 observations/review items/provenance links
per LLC, 3,000 overall, USD 50,005.00 inflows and USD 12,510.00 outflows per LLC,
and USD 37,495.00 net each / USD 112,485.00 overall. Import creates zero journals,
zero ledger outbox messages and changes no book revision. Imported observations
are real database records; they are not prefilled chart values or generator-only
validation. Account setup is outside the before/after import revision assertion.

## Sources and standards

This is a project-authored deterministic fixture, not a bank export or a licensed
external dataset. The [statement decoder](statement-decoder.md),
[private staging](import-staging.md), [import orchestration](import-service.md),
[SQL import](import-sql.md) and [command recovery](command-recovery.md) remain the
reviewed authorities. Their SI/ST/DI/OR source sections establish existing syntax,
exact-value, transaction and ownership mechanisms; no new external source or
normative text was consulted for this fixture. The synthetic CSV exception applies;
ISO4217 USD metadata is retained, and no ISO20022 exchange/conformance claim is made.
USD-only demo acquisition is not a product-scope reduction: broader multicurrency
requirements and existing EUR/JPY/KWD proofs remain unchanged.

documents.title: Durable source import and review contract
documents.body:
# Durable source import and review contract

## Decision and implementation boundary

Implemented subset: [migration10 SQL authority](import-sql.md) and
[Go storage/decoder orchestration](import-service.md), with
[delivery evidence](../runbooks/durable-import-delivery.md). These own the exact
initial function/projection shapes and refinements. The full HTTP, paginated
review, decisions/drafts and source-post workflow below remains proposed;
no upload UI or hosted storage is supplied by the foundation.

**Proposed physical/API contract for review**, 2026-10-13, owner project maintainer;
[#8](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/8), with
[#61](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/61) and
[#70](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/70).
No DDL, endpoints, upload storage, review queue or source posting is implemented
by this document. First implementation remains synthetic deposit-account CSV.
The implemented [decoder](statement-decoder.md) owns byte/field semantics;
this contract owns proposed durable identity, transactions and review boundaries.
The [provider contract](provider-ingestion.md) owns future acquisition, consent,
fences and complete-set publication. It must not call the CSV upload endpoints.

Store immutable evidence separately from mutable review projections and posted
journals. Import confirmation creates uncategorized review items, not journals.
Explicit draft review and explicit posting are separate operations. This refines
the earlier phrase “import drafts”: an uncategorized review item is not yet a
valid ledger posting request. Standards, permission, retention and physical-design
review below must be accepted before the corresponding implementation.

## Identity and scope

Stable source account is a server-issued UUID for one real-world deposit account
within an entity, bound to exactly one book/account in this first profile. No
rebinding or namespace reset endpoint. A second adapter for the same account
must select that UUID and undergo overlap review; creating another UUID to avoid
duplicate detection is prohibited. Ownership cannot be proved by name/mask/hash.
Binding approval records the actor and synthetic evidence reference; real source
ownership and duplicate-account detection remain provider qualification gates.

An adapter namespace is a registered immutable identity tuple, not caller text:
CSV `(profile, synthetic_dataset_id, source_account_ref)`; later Plaid
`(provider, environment, item_id, provider_account_id)`. Its UUID is only a handle;
the full tuple has a unique constraint and case-sensitive equality. A new Item
creates a different namespace and requires overlap review; token/run/lease/parser
versions never change transaction identity. Retired datasets/namespaces cannot
be reactivated or reused.

Observation business key is `(entity_id, source_account_id, namespace_id,
external_entry_id)`, extending the earlier CSV three-part proposal explicitly.
CSV IDs obey its 64-character grammar; future provider IDs retain their adapter
grammar. Repeated byte uploads and repeated observations are different cases:

| Input | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| Same statement reference, metadata and exact bytes | Return the existing authorized batch; no new evidence or review item. |
| Same statement reference, changed bytes/metadata | `statement_identity_conflict`; no replacement. |
| New statement reference, same IDs and canonical fields | New file provenance links to existing observation revisions; no new review items. |
| Same ID, changed material fields | Whole CSV batch held as `rejected` with `source_correction_required`; existing observation unchanged. Future explicit correction intake can append a revision. |
| Different IDs, identical date/amount/description | Two observations and two review items. Never deduplicate by similarity. |
| CSV and Plaid IDs for a suspected shared purchase | Preserve both observations; require explicit overlap decision before the newly overlapping evidence can produce a journal. |

Canonical equality compares all decoded fields, canonical exact amount, currency
version and booked date. Original amount lexemes remain evidence, so `0012.500`
and `12.50` can compare equal without erasing original input. SHA-256 identifies
exact bytes and assists integrity checks; it is neither row identity nor a
substitute for full canonical equality. Duplicate IDs inside one file still
reject the entire file under the decoder contract.

## Proposed SQL dictionary

Schema/naming follow [ADR 0004](../decisions/0004-schema-ownership.md). Below,
`scope` means `entity_id uuid, book_id uuid`, present in every book-owned PK/FK;
IDs are server-generated UUIDs, `rev` is nonnegative bigint serialized as a
canonical decimal string over HTTP, and `instant` is timestamptz. Columns are
NOT NULL unless `?`; dates use the decoder's Gregorian bounds. All referenced
history uses RESTRICT/NO ACTION, never cascading deletion. Text is bounded by
the selected profile; metadata JSON cannot hide financially material fields.

| Table / grain | Columns beyond scope and scoped primary key | Constraints / lifecycle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `banking.source_account` / stable account | `source_account_id`, `ledger_account_id uuid`, `currency_version_id uuid`, `binding_revision rev`, `source_revision rev`, `state text`, `created_by uuid`, `created_at instant`, `binding_evidence_ref uuid` | Entity/source UUID unique independently of book; same-scope ledger-account FK; positive binding revision; state active/paused/retired. Binding accepts only active monetary asset deposit mapping. Currency/version/date and account category checked under locks, not cross-table CHECK. |
| `banking.source_namespace` / registered adapter identity | `namespace_id`, `source_account_id uuid`, `adapter text`, `identity jsonb`, `state text`, `created_by uuid`, `created_at instant` | Exact allowlisted identity keys/types; unique entity/adapter/identity with full tuple equality. Composite FK to source account; immutable identity/account; active/retired; CSV profile only initially. |
| `banking.import_batch` / statement occurrence | `batch_id`, `source_account_id uuid`, `namespace_id uuid`, `statement_ref text`, `binding_revision rev`, `profile text`, `parser_version text`, `starts_on date`, `ends_before date`, `object_id uuid`, `byte_sha256 bytea?`, `byte_count integer?`, `state text`, `created_by uuid`, `created_at instant`, `expires_at instant`, `raw_deleted_at instant?` | Unique namespace/statement_ref within scope; namespace/source composite FK; 32-byte digest and 1..1048576 bytes required after publication. Immutable identity/metadata; starts<end; lifecycle below. Object ID generated before upload, never URL/path from caller. |
| `banking.import_preview` / immutable validation result | `preview_id`, `batch_id uuid`, `preview_revision rev`, `source_revision rev`, `binding_revision rev`, `rows jsonb`, `diagnostics jsonb`, `error_count integer`, `truncated boolean`, `created_at instant`, `expires_at instant` | Unique batch/preview_revision; 1..1000 decoded rows on success, zero usable rows on rejection; rows retain decoder values/ordinals and new/existing classification plus referenced observation/revision. At most100 redacted diagnostics. Max 2 MiB serialized preview, no arbitrary JSON keys. |
| `banking.source_observation` / adapter transaction identity | `observation_id`, `source_account_id uuid`, `namespace_id uuid`, `external_entry_id text`, `current_revision rev`, `created_at instant` | Unique scoped source/namespace/external ID, and entity/source/namespace/external ID. Composite FK enforces namespace belongs to source; current revision references an existing scoped observation revision via deferred FK. Identity never changes or frees for reuse. |
| `banking.observation_revision` / immutable source version | `observation_id, revision rev`, `source_state text`, `booked_date date?`, `currency_version_id uuid?`, `direction text?`, `amount_lexeme text?`, `amount numeric(38,9)?`, `description text?`, `previous_revision rev?`, `recorded_at instant` | Composite PK scope/observation/revision; previous revision same observation. CSV requires booked/date/currency/direction/positive amount/description. source_state booked for CSV; direction inflow/outflow. Finite exact lexical validation precedes typmod; no rounding. Reserved future pending/removed revisions require separately reviewed profile; removed rows retain prior evidence and cannot invent missing values. |
| `banking.import_row` / provenance occurrence | `batch_id, record_ordinal integer`, `observation_id uuid`, `observation_revision rev`, `original_fields jsonb` | PK scope/batch/ordinal; ordinal 2..1001; seven exact decoded CSV fields plus amount lexeme only; immutable scoped FK to revision. Every imported row links, including duplicates from another file. |
| `banking.review_item` / bookkeeping event group | `review_id`, `source_account_id uuid`, `review_revision rev`, `state text`, `retired_into uuid?`, `created_at instant`, `updated_at instant` | Same-scope FK retired_into; only unposted groups can retire; retired groups cannot draft/post. State needs_review/overlap_hold/correction_hold/draft_ready/posted/ignored. One group can retain multiple adapter observations; status is not source state. Unresolved pending/removed evidence cannot produce a draft. |
| `banking.review_evidence` / historical group observation membership | `decision_id, observation_id`, `review_id uuid`, `linked_revision rev` | Immutable scoped PK decision/observation; FKs decision/group/revision; old memberships remain history. |
| `banking.review_assignment` / current observation group | `observation_id`, `review_id uuid`, `decision_id uuid` | PK scope/observation gives one current group. Scoped FK to review_evidence decision/observation and group; controlled reassignment only with a new matching decision. Source-account equality checked under locks. |
| `banking.review_decision` / immutable action | `decision_id`, `review_id uuid`, `expected_review_revision rev`, `kind text`, `actor_id uuid`, `reason text`, `body jsonb`, `created_at instant` | kind initialize/match/distinct/ignore/draft; exact versioned body, <=64 KiB; reason1..500 except generated initialize reason. Contains pinned observation/review revisions and evidence IDs; no credentials or raw object content. |
| `banking.review_draft` / immutable proposed posting | `draft_id`, `review_id uuid`, `review_revision rev`, `binding_revision rev`, `source_revision rev`, `book_revision rev`, `posting_body jsonb`, `created_by uuid`, `created_at instant` | Complete existing posting schema <=1 MiB; source deposit leg is exact, remaining lines explicitly chosen; unique review/review_revision. No journal exists at creation. Revisions make old drafts stale without rewriting them. |
| `banking.review_posting` / immutable posted linkage | `review_id`, `draft_id uuid`, `command_id uuid`, `journal_id uuid`, `posted_at instant` | Unique scoped review/draft/command/journal as appropriate: one initial journal per event group. All same-scope FKs. Corrections link separately reviewed reversals/adjustments; initial link cannot be overwritten. |

Initialization decisions and normalized observations are written only on confirmed
import, not preview. A repeated-row import leaves the existing group/state alone.
Existing generic audit and operation receipts are used only after a reviewed
operation-code/shape extension; do not assume their current allowlists accept
imports. No speculative event is added to `journal.posted`.

## Permissions and owned functions

Propose new entity permission `import`, plus source-account-specific grants
`banking.source_permission(scope,source_account_id,principal_id,capability,
revoked_at?)`, PK including capability. Capabilities bind/import/review/read;
bind permission is assigned by a separately reviewed operator function, never
self-granted by uploading. Existing setup does not grant these permissions.
Import requires current entity read+import and source import; retrieval requires
entity read and source read; decisions/drafts require read+prepare and source
review; source posting additionally requires post. Binding requires entity
read+import plus source bind. Namespace registration is controlled binding work,
not a free-form request parameter. Owner/operator provisioning is an open gate.

`bookkeeping_api` receives EXECUTE on narrow `banking` functions only, no table
DML/DDL. Objects/functions are owned by existing NOLOGIN `bookkeeping_owner`;
the deployment/migration login is not the runtime owner. Preserve the reviewed
migration role path and keep API identities outside owner membership. Revoke
PUBLIC and fix trusted search_path.
Proposed function family `(actor uuid, entity uuid, book uuid, raw_request text)`:
`create_import_batch`, `get_import_batch`, `publish_import_preview`,
`prepare_import`, `execute_import`, `cancel_import`, `acknowledge_import`,
`list_review`, `get_review`, `decide_review`, `create_review_draft` and
`prepare_source_post`. Internal upload publication additionally receives a trusted
object receipt, never a caller-supplied path. SQL revalidates strict unique-key
JSON and scoped identities; Go owns authenticated identity, bounded object I/O
and decoder invocation. Provider workers receive no CSV/API impersonation grant;
their later publication function needs its own fenced service authorization.

All mutations use SERIALIZABLE and existing principal/entity/membership/book lock
order, then source-account locks sorted by UUID, operation/batch/review locks,
and observation locks sorted by UUID. Source-grant changes take compatible locks.
Recheck current auth before receipt replay or returning evidence. Lock source
accounts even for disjoint namespaces to serialize dedup/overlap decisions.
Source changes increment source_revision; review changes increment review_revision.
Neither increments ledger book revision unless a journal actually posts. This is
the provider contract's explicit refinement of the older blanket book-revision
rule; future close/reconciliation evidence must pin both revision domains.

## Upload, import and recovery transactions

1. Register immutable batch metadata and generated object ID with actor-scoped
   idempotency receipt. State `received`; current auth applies on replay. PUT raw
   bytes to the owned API; it streams at most 1 MiB + sentinel to private staging with
   a 15 s deadline, outside SQL. No URL fetch, public upload URL or DB transaction
   spans object I/O. A 20 s total request deadline bounds this synchronous slice.
2. Server verifies stored bytes/digest and decodes against pinned binding/currency
   metadata. Short SQL publication rechecks auth/binding and object receipt,
   records `validating → preview_ready|rejected` with immutable preview. Publication
   failure leaves no visible preview; same PUT can retry/reconcile the same object
   and bytes. Different bytes conflict; compare retained bytes on ambiguous hash equality rather
   than trusting a caller digest. Orphans are private and swept. Expiry or
   cancellation winning publication prevents a late successful preview.
3. Explicit confirmation registers an `import` recoverable operation containing
   batch, preview/revision, binding/source revision and profile. Extend the existing
   one-unacknowledged-command gate across setup/post/import/source_post; discovery
   never executes. Preparation, execution, cancellation and acknowledgement use
   the same principal-scoped recovery semantics and must be reviewed together.
