4. Execution reauthorizes, resolves an existing receipt before mutable checks,
   then verifies exact pinned revisions and every row identity. One transaction
   writes all new observations/revisions, all row links, new review groups and
   initialization decisions, source revision, audit and receipt; batch becomes
   `imported`. Any changed preview/dedup state returns 409 and requires refreshed
   preview plus explicit confirmation, not silent skipping or partial import.
5. Lost commit response is 503 with recovery of the same command. Cancel-before-
   commit creates no observations; commit-before-cancel returns committed. Explicit
   terminal acknowledgement releases the gate, never deletes history. Retry whole
   transactions at most 3 times within 5 s for serialization/deadlock only; do not
   retry object side effects inside the transaction. Unknown commit never means
   “create another key.” Expired/cancelled/rejected batches cannot first execute.

Batch state progression is received → validating → preview_ready|rejected;
preview_ready → imported|cancelled|expired. Received/validating may also expire or
cancel. `rejected` is terminal. A new statement_ref does not permit changed content under
an existing observation ID: it still rejects as source_correction_required. Only
a future separately reviewed correction-intake operation may admit that revision.
Refresh of an unexpired preview creates a new immutable preview_revision and
invalidates prepared stale work. Raw-object lifecycle is separate from batch
state; deletion never changes imported to expired.

## Proposed HTTP boundary

Prefix `P=/v1/entities/{entity}/books/{book}`. Authenticated bearer/private bridge,
strict duplicate/unknown-field rejection, no-store and safe RFC9457 errors follow
existing API contracts. Server owns all actors/IDs/counts/digests. Dates/UUIDs and
money retain existing string profiles. No routes are mounted by this proposal. These signatures are review boundaries,
not generated OpenAPI or an executable exhaustive validator; implementation must
add strict schemas and contract fixtures without silently broadening the profile.

| Request | Exact new body / response boundary |
| --- | --- |
| `POST P/import-batches`, Idempotency-Key | `{source_account_id,namespace_id,binding_revision,statement_ref,profile,starts_on,ends_before}` →201  Batch. Profile fixed to decoder profile; revisions strings; statement_ref follows CSV ID grammar. |
| `PUT P/import-batches/{batch}/content` | Raw bounded CSV, fixed content type; no multipart or query. →200  Batch after validation publication, including rejected outcome. Retry identical bytes only. |
| `GET P/import-batches/{batch}` | No body/query →200  Batch; no raw object URL or bytes. |
| `POST P/import-batches/{batch}/preview`, Idempotency-Key | `{expected_preview_revision}` →200  Batch with refreshed immutable preview; only unexpired preview_ready batches. |
| `POST /v1/commands`, Idempotency-Key | Proposed operation `import`, scoped body `{batch_id,preview_id,preview_revision,binding_revision,source_revision,profile}` →existing Command envelope; execute/cancel/acknowledge remain existing recovery routes after extension. Import result `{batch_id,created_count,existing_count,source_revision}`; paged rows expose stable IDs. |
| `GET P/import-batches/{batch}/rows` | Query `preview_revision`, optional `cursor`, `limit` 1..100 (default 50); →`{profile,batch_id,preview_revision,source_revision,rows,next_cursor}`. Rows `{record_ordinal,disposition,observation_id,observation_revision,review_id,fields}`; new IDs nullable before import; disposition new/existing. Fields exactly the decoder's original/canonical values. |
| `GET P/review-items` | Required source_account_id; optional state, limit 1..100 (default 50), cursor; →`{profile,source_revision,items,next_cursor}`. First slice requires source_account_id; no mixed-source global revision invented. |
| `GET P/review-items/{review}` | No body/query →Review with provenance and current pinned revisions, never raw credentials/object URL. |
| `POST P/review-items/{review}/decisions`, Idempotency-Key | `{expected_review_revision,source_revision,kind,reason,other_review_id,other_review_revision}`; kind match/distinct/ignore, other fields null for ignore. →Review. Match requires two same-source groups and both revisions. Distinct may name another group or use both other fields null for an explicit new-event attestation after overlap review. |
| `POST P/review-items/{review}/drafts`, Idempotency-Key | `{expected_review_revision,source_revision,binding_revision,expected_book_revision,posting_body}` →201  `{draft_id,review_id,review_revision,source_revision,binding_revision,book_revision,posting_body}`. This is draft creation only. |
| `POST /v1/commands`, Idempotency-Key | Proposed operation `source_post`, body `{review_id,draft_id,review_revision,source_revision,binding_revision,expected_book_revision}` →existing Command envelope. Execution atomically revalidates the stored draft/source and invokes owned posting logic, writes review_posting and marks posted with the journal/audit/receipt/outbox commit. Never call existing HTTP post followed by a separate link write. |

Batch is `{profile:"durable-import-v1",batch_id,source_account_id,namespace_id,
state,binding_revision,source_revision,preview_id,preview_revision,created_count,
existing_count,diagnostics,error_count,truncated,raw_available,created_at,expires_at}`;
unavailable preview/count fields are null, not guessed zero. Diagnostics retain
decoder's code/record/field only. Review is `{profile:"source-review-v1",review_id,
source_account_id,state,review_revision,source_revision,binding_revision,
evidence,draft_id,journal_id,blockers,created_at,updated_at}`. Evidence entries are
`{observation_id,observation_revision,namespace_id,adapter,external_entry_id,
source_state,booked_date,currency_version_id,direction,amount,description,
raw_available}`; values follow the source profile, no float. Max 100 evidence
entries/group; additional matches fail with review_limit rather than truncate.
List items omit evidence and contain summary currency/direction/amount only when
unambiguous; mixed/conflicting groups return null summaries and blockers.

Page cursors bind scope, complete filters, source/preview revision and last UUID
(batch rows use ordinal), <=2048 bytes with canonical opaque encoding. Changed
revision returns 409 `source_snapshot_changed`, no partially fresh list. Response
limit 2 MiB; diagnostics at most 100. All mutation JSON except full drafts <=64 KiB;
draft/request posting limit 1 MiB and existing 1000-line cap. SQL/request row limits
must reject before partial effects. No raw download endpoint in first slice.
Errors: 400 shape ; 401 identity ; 403 current permission ; 404 nonexistent/inaccessible
object uniformly ; 409 identity/revision/state/replay conflict ; 413 bytes ; 422 profile/
review limit ; 503 retryable/unknown commit. Never include source values or raw SQL.

## Overlap, corrections and approval

Registering an additional namespace puts newly acquired rows into overlap_hold
until explicit distinct/match decisions; similarity may rank candidates only.
Match is allowed only within one source account and compatible currency/direction/
amount/date evidence. It creates an immutable decision, moves unposted evidence
into the retained group under both group locks and retires the redundant projection
without deleting its history. A group with an existing journal is retained; two
already-posted groups cannot be merged through this endpoint and require correction
review. A distinct decision preserves two legitimate events. Contradictory evidence
stays correction_hold. No silent auto-match across adapters or new Items.

Merge appends review_decision and review_evidence rows, changes review_assignment
under both group locks, and sets the unposted donor's retired_into to the retained
group in the same transaction. All existing unposted drafts on either group become stale; review revisions
increment. When the retained group is already posted, preserve its posted state,
journal_id, original draft and immutable review_posting; only the donor draft
becomes stale. The new evidence/review revision grants no second posting authority. Retired groups remain readable with their original
history but cannot receive new assignments or commands. Match cannot target a
retired group or create a cycle; resolve and explicitly review its current group.
Distinct with no candidate is an explicit new-event attestation, not a conclusion
from a failed similarity search. Incorrect matching reversal remains a separate
reviewed compensating operation, never deletion.

Draft creation requires needs_review with no unresolved blockers. It checks exact
source deposit leg, explicit offset lines, accounting date and valuation, and
sets draft_ready. Foreign transaction currency requires explicit supported FX
references; never replace source units with functional currency or guess a rate.
Posting rechecks pinned source/review/binding/book revisions and permissions,
including prior match decisions, then atomically creates the initial journal/link.
Ignoring requires a reason and preserves source evidence. Reconsidering ignored
items needs a separately reviewed decision; deleting/reimporting cannot reset it.

Future provider modifications append revisions; source removal appends a tombstone.
Unposted draft approval becomes stale and correction_hold; an already-posted
group retains journal_id and exposes correction_hold with an exception. Existing
journals never change; explicit reversal/adjustment is separate accounting work.
The first CSV profile rejects source corrections instead of inventing provider
precedence. A manual journal made outside this workflow is not automatically
recognized as duplicate; manual-to-source linkage is a separate acceptance gate.

## Evidence storage and retention

Apply the [statement proposal's synthetic retention](statement-import.md#security-provenance-and-retention):
24 h rejected/orphan bytes, seven days unconfirmed evidence, 30 days imported raw.
Normalized revisions, receipts, retired identities and posting provenance persist
for dataset lifetime. Raw deletion records raw_deleted_at and keeps digest/metadata;
raw_available means confirmed retained object, not proof of current retrievability.
Private generated object identifiers, encrypted storage, authorization and no
logs/browser persistence remain mandatory. No raw public URL, third-party scan,
remote fetch or analytical payload. Metadata publication never precedes complete
object publication. Idempotent cleanup rechecks retention/hold before deleting,
records unavailable after confirmed deletion, and reconciles uncertain deletion;
it cannot delete a newly imported object's evidence using a stale preview expiry.
No cleanup runner or cloud bucket is introduced here. Live retention/legal holds,
backup erasure, source ownership and accountant cutover remain explicit gates.

## Standards, sources and alternatives

Internal durable-import-v1/source-review-v1 are not bank exchange messages; no ISO
20022 identifier/namespace is invented. The selected synthetic CSV exception is
already recorded for decoder scope; durable acquisition and later Plaid each need
their reviewed usage decision. ISO 4217 currency-version references apply;
RFC 3339 full dates/UTC timestamps profile ISO 8601 semantics. SI01–SI06 and the
[standards contract](standards.md) retain source versions/access limits. No IBAN,
BIC or LEI interpretation is added. ISO 21378:2019/21926:2026 audit mapping and camt
version/usage profile under #17 remain unresolved, not supplied by these APIs.

Primary sections reviewed 2026-10-13; references establish mechanisms, not approval:

| ID / exact source sections | Finding and project interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| DI01 — PostgreSQL17 [§5.5.1–5 keys/constraints](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/ddl-constraints.html) and [§13.2.3 serializable](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/transaction-iso.html) | Composite keys/FKs enforce referential scope; cross-table CHECK is unsuitable; serializable transactions can require complete retry. Inference: serialize import publication and use immutable revisions plus scoped uniqueness, not application-only dedup. |
| DI02 — OWASP [File Upload Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html), File Storage Location, User Permissions, Upload and Download Limits | Storage segregation, authorization and bounded uploads are layered controls. Inference: private staging plus separate SQL publication and explicit orphan cleanup. Numerical caps/retention are project proposals, not OWASP requirements. |
| DI03 — Plaid [Transactions API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/), transaction_id, pending and pending_transaction_id fields | IDs are case-sensitive; pending details can change; pending linkage is conditional. Inference: stable adapter identity and immutable revisions, no amount/name identity or assumed pending lineage. Mutable API docs reviewed only these fields; provider version/mapping remains the separate provider contract. |

These sections were read directly; no full ISO normative text or real provider
payload was accessed. Alternative hash-only dedup conflates identity and evidence;
similarity dedup loses identical purchases. Direct import-to-post removes explicit
accounting review. Storing files in PostgreSQL would simplify atomic bytes/metadata
but grows ledger backups and broadens runtime access; private object staging is
chosen provisionally, subject to tested publication/cleanup. Entire provider event
sourcing is unnecessary: append-only source revisions and current projections
preserve corrections without replacing the transactional ledger.

## Acceptance and implementation sequence

All tests below are **planned**, not executed evidence. Independent fixed fixtures
must inspect journal/line/book-revision/outbox counts after every import operation.

| Required named evidence | Fixed expected outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `TestDurableImportScope` | Wrong/revoked/disabled/mixed entity/source denies retrieval, replay and publication; runtime table DML and namespace self-registration fail. |
| `TestDurableImportIdentity` | Two USD 12.50 rows with different IDs create 2 items; repeated file creates 0; new-file overlap links 2; changed 12.51 under same ID rejects whole batch; forced equal hash cannot bypass full-field comparison. |
| `TestDurableImportAtomicity` | Inject each observation/link/review/audit/receipt failure:0 partial rows and0 journals; concurrent equal imports produce one observation per identity. |
| `TestDurableImportRecovery` | Lost commit returns same IDs/counts; cancel/execute and revoke/execute races follow serialization; stale preview requires explicit refresh/reconfirmation. |
| `TestDurableImportObjects` | Upload/publish/deletion crash boundaries, byte/record/deadline limits + 1, orphan/expiry races and redaction; raw expiry retains identities, receipts and normalized evidence. |
| `TestSourceReviewOverlap` | CSV/Plaid overlap requires explicit match; already-posted group retains one journal; two distinct identical purchases remain 2; contradictory/mixed-scope match denied. |
| `TestSourceDraftPosting` | Import and draft create0 journals; explicit source_post creates 1 linked journal atomically; replay adds 0; source/book/binding/review changes reject stale approval; lost commit recovers same linked result. |
| `TestSourceCorrectionHistory` | Pending/removed not eligible; modified posted evidence leaves original journal unchanged and raises hold; foreign amounts retain EUR/JPY/KWD units and explicit FX gates. |
| `TestSourceReviewPagination` | Exact scoped cursor, limits, stale revisions and denied actor return no mixed snapshot or leaked evidence. |

First review these physical/API choices, permission provisioning and object-store
ownership. Then implement binding + private
batch/preview + atomic import with synthetic tests; then review decisions/drafts
and recoverable source_post; then Plaid complete-set publication and qualification.
The journal-observer worker does not satisfy provider acquisition/cleanup gates.
Issue #8 remains open through its actual end-to-end acceptance. This contract does
not authorize live imports, cloud resources, automatic posting or accounting policy.

documents.title: Optional enrollment expiry and bookkeeping availability
documents.body:
# Optional enrollment expiry and bookkeeping availability

## Decision and boundary

Implementation proposal for #281, 2026-10-24. Keep structurally valid expired
Sandbox enrollment configuration as a disabled provider capability rather than
an invalid bookkeeping server configuration. Partial/unsafe metadata and future
expiry beyond the existing thirty-day maximum still reject before I/O. Release
authorization remains strict/future under connection-release; this change does
not make an expired release eligible for promotion or renew source consent.

Runtime checks an injected clock (production uses time.Now) at construction and
each provider-dependent service entry. At the exact deadline authorization has
expired. Cold startup after expiry returns the real SQL-authorized connection
service with no provider/credential adapters and performs no managed token,
secret, KMS or provider call. Expiry during static credential initialization
falls back to that same service. A live approved runtime gates every outgoing
dependency HTTP request at the deadline as well; no retry or grace is added.

## Authority matrix

| Operation | Expired optional enrollment policy |
| --- | --- |
| Identity, ledger, workspace and durable setup/post/import recovery | Unchanged verified identity/current SQL authority; no dependency on enrollment |
| List connections, list/get attempts, stream status | SQL-authorized metadata reads remain available; no provider credential required |
| Stream disconnect, pause/resume/request | Existing local SQL authority and per-source consent/revision fences remain authoritative; no source fetch in API |
| Begin, execute, complete Hosted Link, reconcile credentials, bind, abandon Item | Fail existing temporarily_unavailable/HTTP503 before SQL claim/secret/provider work; metadata discovery remains available |
| Existing workers | Unchanged independent source consent/generation/permission fences; optional new-enrollment policy does not renew or revoke an Item |

Explicit Item-wide provider removal/abandonment is not a local stream disconnect;
it remains unavailable without current provider authority. Preserve unknown
results and exact attempts; never replace a recovery action with new enrollment.
Request-time permission validation and immutable journal/outbox rules are unchanged.
No financial data enters browser persistence or operational logs.

## Sources, applicability and alternatives

Reviewed selected official sections on 2026-10-24:
[Go Time.After](https://pkg.go.dev/time#Time.After) (displayed go1.27.3 public
reference; strict ordering semantics; pinned1.26.10 page inaccessible, local
Go1.26.5 tests and canonical pinned CI are separate implementation evidence)
and [Cloud Run container lifecycle/startup](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/container-contract#lifecycle)
(instances must start a listener within the startup bound; failed startup cannot
serve requests). Public sections only; these sources establish mechanisms, not
permission to make bank calls. The existing #281 incident and
[app recovery evidence](../runbooks/app-recovery31.md) establish the project failure.

Separating configuration validity from optional capability authority is our
inference. Rejected alternatives: extending the deadline silently changes owner
approval; disabling all connection routes loses SQL-only status/disconnect;
continuing to load credentials after cold expiry adds unnecessary dependency
failure and secret access. Keeping the entire API down is fail-closed but blocks
unrelated authorized command recovery. This design denies provider operations
while preserving their durable status and independent bookkeeping authority.

Standards applicability: this internal lifecycle/authorization rule is not a
financial exchange and has no ISO20022 message mapping. Existing financial
payload, ISO4217 dated currency/original-unit mappings and accounting policy
are unchanged. No new data schema, migration, message version or conformance
claim. Follow standards.md and the annotated bibliography for those mappings.
Security review applies to authorization/secret boundary changes before release;
synthetic proof is not AppSec, hosted, or live-bookkeeping approval.

## Acceptance

Deterministic runtime tests cover before/at/after deadline, cold restart, expiry
during static reads, malformed expired metadata, zero expired dependency I/O,
and outgoing-request fences. Service tests cover every provider entry denied
without SQL/secret/provider effects and current SQL-only reads/controls including
permission denial. The actual synthetic browser/Next/Go/PostgreSQL setup and
lost-commit recovery journey runs with a real expired enrollment composition;
bank begin returns unavailable and dependency transports are tripwires.
Core and web/app-integration gates remain required. Actual hosted revision and
saved-command recovery evidence remains open until a separately scoped release.

documents.title: Financial reporting contract
documents.body:
# Financial reporting contract

## Decision and status

**Proposed for #51; design only, 2026-10-13.** Go serves scoped reports from the
existing PostgreSQL ledger. No reporting ledger, new service or client-side
accounting engine. Owner review of this contract precedes SQL/OpenAPI work in
#53. [Issue #50](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/50)
owns the application; #1 owns live accounting policy, #10 close/export acceptance,
and #59 advanced FX/consolidation. [Sources](../research/financial-reporting-sources.md)
FR01–FR05 distinguish evidence from project choices.

The existing `reporting.trial_balance(actor,e,b,through_date)` in migration 2
returns cumulative net debit/credit balances, authorized book revision and
functional currency. It includes originals and reversals and limits totals below
10^29. This contract adds proposed report behavior; it does not reinterpret that
endpoint or claim the new routes/functions/tests exist. All merged SQL stays
immutable; implementation requires a new migration and reviewed OpenAPI types.

## Scope, dates and policy

Every request names exactly one entity and book. No arrays, implicit all-LLC sum,
caller-supplied principal or mixed-scope partial success. Verified identity maps
to the existing principal; each report requires current `read` membership.
The first profile is `dev-accrual-usd-v1`: synthetic accrual, UTC accounting
calendar. Show basis, timezone, policy IDs and currency on every report.
Cash-basis conversion, tax statements, consolidated statements, presentation
translation and GAAP/IFRS compliance are not implied.

Inputs are real Gregorian `YYYY-MM-DD` dates, years 0001–9999. Range reports use
`[starts_on, ends_before)`; point reports use inclusive `through_date`. Compare
accounting dates, never browser timezone or `posted_at`. No default date from a
client locale. Point reports compare `<= through_date` directly, avoiding
9999-12-31 overflow. Reject inverted/empty ranges. Future dates are allowed for
review and do not manufacture future activity. Period state is informational;
closed does not mean audited. Unposted drafts never contribute. Original postings
continue contributing after reversal; a reversal offsets them on its own
accounting date. Opening values come from actual earlier postings, never a
balancing plug or inferred starting cash.

Select one supported basis/functional currency across all relevant policy
revisions, including the opening history. Missing policy coverage or a basis,
functional currency version/scale change without an approved transition mapping
returns `unsupported_policy`. Inactive accounts with history remain visible.
Multicurrency original units and immutable rate IDs remain in drill-down;
functional amounts are the booked amounts, never retranslated at today's rate.
Aggregate original units only within the same currency version; no cross-currency
unit total. Current SQL permits only positive original/functional amounts and
identity/spot valuation. Zero-unit revaluation, settlement and presentation FX
remain blocked by their own contracts.

## Amounts, signs and statement definitions

Use exact PostgreSQL numeric aggregates without coercing intermediate sums into
`numeric(38,9)`. Serialize amounts as canonical decimal **strings**, no exponent,
group separators, plus sign or negative zero. At most 29 integer and 9 fractional
digits; signed net fields may start with `-`; debit/credit fields are nonnegative.
Normalize zero to `"0"`, remove insignificant trailing zeros, reject overflow
with `result_out_of_range` before response. UUIDs and revisions are strings;
revision is a canonical nonnegative decimal integer string in the existing SQL
bigint range (including `"0"`), never a JavaScript number. Display pads
from currency metadata without discarding nonzero precision. All totals,
comparisons and running balances are checked against the same bounds.

For an account let `N(S)` be sum(debit functional amount minus credit functional
amount) for eligible lines in set S. Account normal side describes presentation;
it never changes posting arithmetic. Contra balances stay negative in statement
sections; do not take absolute values or suppress unexpected signs.

| Report | Exact required meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Trial balance | For each account through the inclusive date: `debit_balance=max(N,0)`, `credit_balance=max(-N,0)`. Include zero accounts existing in the accepted revision. Sum columns independently and require equal totals. These are **net balance** totals, not gross journal turnover. |
| General ledger | One required account filter; opening `N(date < starts_on)`, period debit/credit turnover, closing `opening + period_debits - period_credits`. Each row includes signed running balance in ascending `(accounting_date, journal_id, line_number)` order. A page's first running balance includes all prior eligible rows, not only that page. |
| P&L | Over the exact range, revenue is `-sum(N(revenue))`, expense is `sum(N(expense))`, net income is revenue minus expense. Owner capital, distributions, loan proceeds and transfers are excluded by account category. No tax/recognition adjustments inferred from labels. |
| Balance sheet | Through date: assets `sum(N(asset))`, liabilities `-sum(N(liability))`, direct equity `-sum(N(equity))`, unclosed earnings `-sum(N(revenue)+N(expense))` over **all** prior eligible history. Total equity = direct equity + unclosed earnings; assets = liabilities + total equity. Distributions reduce direct equity. The derived earnings line never creates a journal. |

The initial balance sheet is explicitly **unclassified**: the five account
categories do not establish current/noncurrent, cash-flow or tax classifications.
The derived line is called `unclosed_earnings`, not current-year profit. When
closing transfers revenue/expense to equity, residual revenue/expense naturally
falls to zero; do not add lifetime P&L again to transferred retained earnings.
Automated annual close, comparative pre/post-close earnings and fiscal-year
classification require #10's closing-journal policy before support. Unsupported
closing semantics fail rather than silently misstate P&L.

Report line identity is `account:<UUID>` for account rows and fixed versioned
section IDs (`assets`, `liabilities`, `direct_equity`, `unclosed_earnings`,
`revenue`, `expense`, `net_income`, `total_equity`). Labels are not identifiers.
First layout `basic-unclassified-v1` sorts accounts by code under bytewise `C`
collation then UUID; GL sorts by the tuple above. No caller SQL/order expression.
Every subtotal carries a server-generated selector: scope, same revision,
relevant dates, category/account IDs and sign multiplier. Account selectors lead
to GL; category/derived selectors first list contributing accounts, then GL.
Journal references resolve through the existing authorized journal read; the UI
never guesses membership or derives inclusion from a label. Original amount,
currency version, rate ID, policy ID, journal kind and reversal link accompany
line detail. Source documents remain references only when separately authorized;
missing source evidence is explicit, never fabricated.
The future report drill-through wrapper must validate the pinned revision and
call the authorized journal reader in the same transaction; the current standalone
journal endpoint has no report-revision parameter and alone cannot prove this tie.

## SQL, authorization and snapshot contract

Proposed restricted entry point:
`reporting.financial_report(actor uuid, e uuid, b uuid, request jsonb) returns jsonb`.
A strict tagged request selects TB/GL/BS/P&L, validated dates, account selector,
optional comparison and expected revision. Go validates transport and injects
trusted identity; SQL owns scope, membership, arithmetic and selection. No arbitrary
SQL or dynamic identifiers. Use the existing restricted owner/function pattern,
fixed safe search path, revoke PUBLIC execution, grant only reviewed reporting
wrappers to `bookkeeping_api`; no direct table SELECT/DML/DDL grants.

Each request runs in one short **repeatable-read** transaction, calls
`ledger.authorize(...,'read',false)` before aggregation or account lookup, then
uses the authorized book revision. This function uses `FOR SHARE`: a PostgreSQL
`READ ONLY` transaction is incompatible. Use ordinary repeatable-read with the
restricted role and query-only wrapper; do not remove authorization locks to gain
a read-only label. It must not mutate ledger, receipt or outbox state. Bound retries
of the whole transaction on serialization failure; no partial rows on failure.
Authorization locks serialize against revocation/disable: revocation committed
before authorization denies; if a report holds the lock first, it may complete
before revocation commits. No promise of retracting already delivered bytes.
Every page/export rechecks membership even when book revision is unchanged:
permission revocation need not increment the book revision to invalidate access.

For cross-request continuity choose **revision validation**, not a retained MVCC
snapshot: initial response returns `snapshot_revision=R`; subsequent pages,
comparisons, exports and drill-down require R. After fresh authorization, if current
book revision differs, return 409 `report_snapshot_changed`, no financial body.
Never silently continue at a new revision. New backdated entries and setup edits
therefore invalidate navigation too. Existing account semantics are mostly
immutable but account additions/deletions/active-to changes are not historically
versioned; filtering journals by revision alone cannot reconstruct the whole report.
No historical report request is promised. The UI offers an explicit refresh,
discards the old page set and starts again. Frequent writes may cause restarts;
measured demand can justify a separately reviewed snapshot/export mechanism later.
Do not hold database transactions open between browser requests.

First-page results and their totals/comparisons are one snapshot. Subsequent pages
use a versioned base64url cursor containing last sort tuple, revision, report kind,
layout and canonical filter digest, max 2048 bytes. Treat it as untrusted input,
validate all fields and require exact filter equality; it is **not** an access
token or authorization proof. Changing a cursor cannot access another scope or
avoid current permissions. Keyset pagination only, no offsets. Order ties include
UUID and GL line number so retries yield neither duplicates nor missing rows.
HTTP buffers the bounded response before commit and emits success only after
transaction success. Set `Cache-Control: no-store`; no tokens/rows in logs,
URLs copied to analytics, browser persistence or shared caches.

## Proposed HTTP surface and bounded execution

Proposed additive GET paths under `/v1/entities/{entity_id}/books/{book_id}/reports/`:
`trial-balance`, `general-ledger`, `balance-sheet`, `profit-and-loss`. Existing
trial-balance route remains backward compatible. Point routes accept `through_date`;
range routes accept `starts_on`, `ends_before`; GL additionally requires `account_id`.
Common optional `snapshot_revision`, `cursor`, `limit` (default 100, maximum 500).
Reject unknown/duplicate query fields, malformed UUID/date/decimal revision and
incompatible filters with 400 `invalid_request`.

Comparison is one explicit `compare_through_date` for point reports or paired
`compare_starts_on`/`compare_ends_before` for P&L; GL comparisons are unsupported.
All comparisons use the same authorized revision and currency/basis/layout, align
by account/section ID, and zero-fill an absent balance. Return current, prior,
and signed `difference=current-prior` as strings. Omit percentages in v1 to avoid
undefined denominators and misleading sign changes. Reject unsupported policies;
never perform implicit currency translation to make comparison work.

Envelope: `contract_version="financial-reporting-v1"`, report/layout IDs,
entity/book IDs, functional currency code/version/minor units, basis/timezone,
policy IDs, normalized date/comparison filters, `snapshot_revision`, UTC RFC3339
`generated_at`, `next_cursor` or null, exact totals and `rows`. Each account row
includes identity/code/name/category/normal side, amount fields appropriate to
report and selector. GL rows include the provenance listed above. `generated_at`
is generation time, not an accounting cutoff or a claim of currentness after commit.
Default first-page requests capture current revision; pinned requests never auto-refresh.

Reuse API problem semantics: 401 invalid credentials; 404 absent/inaccessible
scope/account; 403 known membership lacking read; 409 changed snapshot; 422
unsupported policy or result bound; 503 deadline/retry exhaustion. Error bodies
contain request ID and fixed problem code only, no financial values or existence
hints. Scope authorization precedes snapshot mismatch disclosure. Timeouts never
produce a zero/partial report. Request cancellation cancels SQL work.

Initial engineering limits: one book, one comparison, range <=366 days, one GL
account, <=500 rows/page, 5-second database statement timeout, 1-second lock timeout,
10-second request deadline, at most 2 whole-transaction attempts within deadline,
2 MiB encoded JSON response. Point/opening history is not truncated to 366 days.
These are proposed limits, not measured capacity. Existing indexes `journal_date`
and `account_history` are candidates; implementation must EXPLAIN synthetic
1,000- and 100,000-journal scopes, prove entity/book predicates early, measure
opening/running sums and shared-core contention. Pagination does not itself bound
aggregate scan cost. Add only measured composite indexes in a new migration;
if limits fail, return explicit unavailable and revise the query design, not totals.

## CSV review export

Proposed `GET .../reports/{kind}/export.csv` uses the same scope, filters, explicit
revision and authorization; ignores no unsupported filters. Export contains all
selected rows, never just the visible page, with max 10,000 data rows, 10 MiB UTF-8
bytes and the same 10-second deadline. Detect excess before emitting headers/body;
return 422 `report_export_limit`, never a truncated success. Buffer in bounded
memory; no background job, bucket, share link or browser persistence in this slice.
A repeated download repeats authorization and may fail after revocation.

The implementation contract must pin a stable header order and RFC4180 quoting/CRLF;
the proposed `financial-reporting-csv-v1` profile
repeats provenance columns (report/layout/scope/revision/currency/date filters and
generation time) on data rows. Empty exports contain header plus one explicit
`row_kind=summary` row with actual opening/closing totals and provenance (all zero
only for empty inception). Define row kinds account,
posting, subtotal, summary so totals cannot be accidentally counted as postings.
Machine reconciliation uses exact decimal fields and UUIDs, not display labels.

To avoid relying on fragile spreadsheet escaping, v1 export omits arbitrary
account codes/names/descriptions/reasons/source text; UUIDs plus fixed enum labels
provide drill-through. Magnitudes are unsigned canonical decimal; each measure
has a separate `<measure>_sign=positive|negative|zero` and `<measure>_magnitude`
pair. Posting debit/credit side remains a separate field. Dates,
UUIDs and enums follow strict generated grammars. Quote all fields, double embedded
quotes, reject control characters and any value outside its field grammar before
serialization. The approved header must be fixed. Thus no cell is user-controlled formula text;
a validator error rejects the entire file. Rich descriptive CSV requires a later
reviewed transformation and spreadsheet compatibility test; CSV is not promised
safe after arbitrary downstream editing, or exact numeric import by spreadsheets.
JSON remains the lossless contract. This is an internal **review export**, not an
approved accountant/audit exchange. ISO audit mappings below block that promotion.

**Remaining wire-schema gate:** before CSV implementation, specify and review the
ordered header, row-kind field/nullability matrix, provenance/comparison columns,
and the amount/sign pairs for opening, turnover, closing, current, prior and
difference. The profile name is reserved for this proposal, not an implemented
or fully specified wire schema. JSON report implementation and CSV delivery need
separate acceptance; scope and safety requirements above do not settle the missing
column mapping.

## Standards applicability and open policy

| Practice/message | Assessment, mapping and acceptance |
| --- | --- |
| Internal JSON/SQL reports and selectors | ISO 20022 message encoding: not applicable to this application-owned report/query exchange (FR04); no bank/network counterparty or message profile selected. Scope is a project interpretation for review, not proof no financial-reporting message could ever apply. No ISO namespace/version is invented. Internal schema is `financial-reporting-v1`; validate exact money, side, currency/date and reversal semantics in tests below. |
| Currency identifiers | ISO 4217 applicable: reuse immutable `reference.currency` code/version/minor units and recorded source release; no live unpinned code list. FR04/public overview does not approve FX policy. `TestReportCurrencyBoundary` rejects mismatches/unmapped versions. |
| Audit/accountant CSV | ISO 21378:2019 applicable research target; ISO 21926:2026 semantic mappings unresolved (bibliography R04/R05). Abstract/preview access does not settle normative fields. Preserve ledger IDs, dates, sides, currencies and provenance in internal review CSV; no claim of mapped ISO export. Required normative mapping/profile approval blocks accountant/audit export implementation, not review of this proposal. |
| Dates and identifiers | Use existing ISO-style Gregorian full dates/RFC3339 timestamps and UUID contracts; no new ISO identifier assigned. FR05 reviews RFC3339 §5.6/§5.7 and RFC4180 §2 for transport; these IETF formats are not accounting recognition rules. |
| Financial statements | FR01 supports introductory mechanics; actual framework/jurisdiction, fiscal year, taxonomy, live opening balances and annual close need owner/accountant decisions (#1/#10). ASC/IAS review remains pending; do not relabel synthetic statements compliant. |

Any unresolved required standards mapping blocks the corresponding implementation
slice under [standards.md](standards.md). Before a release, review this table,
record exact supported versions/profile and STD-01–05 evidence for the applicable
scope. Basic review reports and accountant-ready exchange are separate gates.

## Independent expected results and planned acceptance

Use fixed [golden-month.json](../../tests/corpus/golden-month.json) values, not
expectations recomputed by report SQL, generator or a shared aggregation helper.
For fictional A in January: checking 1045, savings 100, capital credit 1100,
services credit 200, general expense 100, category A/B expense 15 each,
distributions debit 25; supplies/card/payable zero. Trial-balance totals are
**1300 debit = 1300 credit**; P&L revenue 200, expense 130, profit 70; balance
sheet assets 1145, liabilities 0, direct equity 1075, unclosed earnings 70,
total equity 1145. Fictional B stays checking 70/capital credit 70. Hand-review
these constants separately from fixture-loading account classifications.

Checking GL `[2026-01-02,2026-01-03)` has opening 1000, debit turnover 200,
credit turnover 0, closing 1200. Empty February keeps January closing values,
zero activity/P&L and checking opening/closing 1045. Empty inception has all-zero
statements. A reversal dated in February leaves January as posted; February P&L
includes its offset exactly once. For cent/scale tests add independently reviewed
USD 0.01 + 0.02 = 0.03, JPY 1 + 2 = 3 and KWD 0.001 + 0.002 = 0.003 in
separate supported-policy books; non-USD policy setup is planned, not current
posting-profile support. EUR 10 booked at USD 11 retains EUR 10 and USD 11;
a later 1.20 rate never changes that report. Max amount plus 0.01 overflow must
fail as a whole report. Do not aggregate these books/currencies together.

All following names are **planned**, not claims of current coverage:

| Named evidence | Acceptance |
| --- | --- |
| `TestFinancialReportsGoldenMonth` | Exact constants above; TB = GL closings, BS balances, P&L ties to earnings; independent B isolation; all financial outputs strings. |
| `TestReportDateBoundaries` | Opening/empty periods/inception, inclusive point vs exclusive range, UTC/date input, leap/invalid/max dates; drafts absent. |
| `TestReportCorrectionHistory` | Original plus linked reversal and replacement, different period, exact original FX; no rewritten history/double counting. |
| `TestReportCurrencyBoundary` | Original-unit buckets, functional policy transitions denied, 0/2/3-decimal fixtures, overflow, no floating/exponent serialization. |
| `TestReportStatementSigns` | Contra asset/revenue, distributions and unexpected credit expense preserve sign; unclassified labels; planned closing transfer does not double-count equity. |
| `TestReportSnapshotPagination` | Equal-date ties, page concatenation equals fixed full results/running sums, tampered cursor denied, backdated post/setup invalidates R, comparisons/drill-through share R. |
| `TestReportAuthorizationRace` | Anonymous/unknown/disabled/revoked/prepare-only/post-only denial, mixed scopes and foreign account IDs; concurrent revocation linearization and later-page denial; no leaked totals. |
| `TestReportNoMutation` | API direct SQL/DML/DDL denial, exact SQLSTATE; report success/failure leaves ledger/receipts/outbox unchanged; lock serialization retries bounded. |
| `TestReportCSVReviewExport` | Full selection vs page, header/provenance/empty shape, decimal-sign round trip, malicious label omitted, malformed field rejected, row/byte limits all-or-nothing, revoked repeat denied. |
| `TestReportResourceBounds` | Synthetic query plans/timing, full-history opening, cancellation/deadlock/timeout, limits and redacted failures; measurements recorded without a cloud-capacity claim. |
| `ReviewFinancialReportingStandardsV1` | Owner reviews applicability/profile, source limits and deferred normative audit mapping; no blanket ISO/GAAP claim. |

## Alternatives and implementation order

FR02 explains transaction snapshots; our inference is that short revision-validated
requests fit the current mutable metadata and small pool. Keeping exported MVCC
snapshots alive avoids refresh but consumes connections/locks; durable materialized
reports add retention, revocation and storage obligations. Neither is justified
before measured failures. Client aggregation cannot be the accounting authority;
a warehouse/read replica introduces lag and a second authorization surface.

First approve the contract/standards interpretation and fixed constants; then add
restricted SQL, invariant tests and measured indexes, then reviewed OpenAPI plus
Go API/CSV tests, generated clients and browser integration. No generated OpenAPI
change in this design-only task: proposed paths are deliberately not advertised
as runtime operations. Owner/accountant policy and audit-export mappings remain
explicit gates; cloud acceptance is independent of these design tests.

documents.title: First bookkeeping interface
documents.body:
# First bookkeeping interface

## Decision and scope

Implement #9's manual slice: authorized entity/book selection, controlled setup,
manual split journals, explicit review and posting, and trial balances. The browser
uses generated OpenAPI types and same-origin bearer requests; tokens and financial
state remain in memory. [Source review](../research/frontend-sources.md) records
framework decisions. Statement import, general persisted drafts, journal browsing,
reversal UI and bank synchronization remain later work.

## Durable commands and session boundary

The [command recovery contract](command-recovery.md) owns prepare, execute, cancel
and acknowledgement semantics. Load pending commands before enabling new work.
Review registers one immutable command; only explicit confirmation executes it.
Committed or cancelled outcomes remain visible until explicit acknowledgement.
New work is blocked while discovery fails or any command remains unacknowledged.

Uncertain registration retains the same key/body for retry. Uncertain execution,
cancellation or acknowledgement discovers server state; it never automatically
executes, cancels or acknowledges. A prepared command recovered after sign-in
still requires confirmation. A commit winning a cancellation race displays its
committed result. Another tab's acknowledgement may release the server-owned gate.
Current authorization applies to every discovery and transition; inaccessible
pending work blocks new work until authorized operator restoration.

Session changes clear browser financial views. Tokens and request bodies are never
persisted in browser storage. Server discovery recovers registered work after
session/tab loss; unregistered form edits are not durable. The application does not
substitute a fake success or silently create a new request after uncertainty.

The server-only `BOOKKEEPING_API_ORIGIN` chooses a trusted HTTPS backend or explicit
loopback HTTP endpoint. Browser input cannot choose that target. Authentication
follows [browser auth](browser-auth.md); cookies provide no authority.

## Accounting and standards

Amounts and revisions remain strings. No browser sums, currency conversions or
rounding determine posting acceptance. Setup explicitly uses the reviewed
accrual/UTC/USD development policy with installed currency metadata. Manual spot
journals preserve original currency and require a reviewed rate ID. These internal
operations are not ISO 20022 financial messages; ISO 4217 semantics follow the API
and standards contracts.

## Acceptance

Named Playwright journeys cover setup registration/confirmation/acknowledgement,
split review, identical uncertain registration retry, lost execute/ack responses,
prepared recovery after remount, commit/cancel race presentation and denied scope.
A separate real PostgreSQL→Go→Next→browser harness verifies durable response-loss
recovery. Unit tests cover safe transport and session invalidation. TypeScript,
generated-contract drift and production builds complement database proofs; live
Firebase/GCP and live-use policy remain separate gates. Results belong to the
[command recovery runbook](../runbooks/command-recovery.md).

documents.title: Optional hosted connection composition
documents.body:
# Optional hosted connection composition

## Approved bounded composition

The API keeps connection enrollment disabled unless explicit complete metadata
configuration is supplied. `plaid-link-events-qualified` remains ordinary-SDK
account metadata; false is supported by the Sandbox Hosted Link profile.
Enabled composition requires managed mode and the existing Cloud SQL IAM API pool;
no second pool, alternate DSN, provider credential argument or environment lookup
is introduced. Disabled composition reads no metadata token or secret and mounts
no optional connection routes. Partial or contradictory settings fail startup.

Configuration identifies GCP project ID plus its explicitly configured canonical numeric project number, approved Infisical origin/project UUID/dev
namespace/identity UUID, GCS metadata registry bucket/prefix, two distinct exact
numeric Secret Manager versions in projects/{number} resources for static Plaid client credentials, and a fixed
absolute local consent expiry. Live Sandbox approval is at most30days from startup
using an explicitly supplied instant, with no renewal default. Well-formed expired
optional enrollment starts SQL-only bookkeeping/attempt inspection without any
dependency access; malformed or unsafe configuration still rejects. This is the
accepted281 availability boundary, not a consent extension.

Current encrypted composition validates identifiers before I/O, constructs the
fixed canonical-project-ID KMS wrapper and PostgreSQL bank store, then reads only
the two exact static credential versions with a bounded startup deadline. Registry/
Infisical identifiers remain validated compatibility metadata; the API no longer
uses finite per-account secret slots, registry discovery or a dynamic secret writer.
Acquisition uses its separately scoped encrypted read-only resolver. Values stay
inside memory/Secret wrappers. The existing
Plaid HTTP provider and connection service reuse SQL current permission, one-shot
claims, manifest verification, immutable credential readback and recovery semantics.
No startup Plaid calls, Infisical writes, Link session or account binding occur.
The command uses direct managed metadata transport without proxy/ADC discovery.

## Link and operational limits

The [Hosted Link enrollment profile](hosted-link-enrollment.md) creates a
Plaid-hosted session and resolves server completion before exchange. It does not
require ordinary-SDK Link-events enablement. Retained LinkEventsQualified metadata
cannot establish that Plaid enabled it. Owned Hosted repair requires the separate
default-false `HostedRepair` capability and exact fixed Sandbox receiver, schema33
and compatible binary/bootstrap. Existing webhook-only configuration stays repair-
disabled. Operator flag `-plaid-hosted-repair=true` is private deployment metadata,
never an HTTP/browser-selected permission. Current SQL still owns actor, Item,
source, consent, proof and claim authority. See the [owned repair protocol](hosted-reconnect.md)
and [exact release profile](connection-release.md). Actual interactive session/
secret/SQL/webhook qualification remains open; a configured flag is not acceptance.

Existing12s API budget is unchanged. Unknown exchange/write/propagation outcomes
follow durable service recovery; a slow propagation cannot authorize a new exchange
or blind secret mutation. Existing health/readiness is DB/auth readiness, not a
claim that Plaid, Infisical delivery or all qualification steps passed.

## Sources and standards

This composition adds no financial message and retains existing proprietary Plaid
2020-09-14 and ISO mappings in connection/provider contracts. Reviewed official
[Infisical GCP Auth](https://infisical.com/docs/documentation/platform/identities/gcp-auth)
GCP ID Token Auth, sample identity request and login sections: audience is the
Infisical identity UUID, not an invented HTTPS URI. Configure the writer identity's
short token TTL to satisfy the providersecrets adapter's bounded policy. Metadata
UUID audience support is owned by worker runtime; the retained legacy writer
source review does not imply current encrypted API writer use. Composition must not
silently substitute a different audience. Source review does not qualify deployed
IAM or secret propagation. The coordinator links the annotated source in shared
bibliography; dependency secret and worker contracts own their wire details.

## Callable boundary and command metadata

`connectionruntime.New(ctx, Config, connections.Beginner, http.RoundTripper, Tokens)`
returns the existing connection Service or a fixed error. It returns nil/nil when
fully disabled. `Config.Validate` and `ManagedScope` reject partial metadata,
non-managed/API-URL mode, unmatched hosting project, mutable version aliases and
cross-number credential resources before startup secret access. Construction has a
15s total static-read budget; source adapters retain their stricter request bounds.
Project ID-to-number association is explicitly operator/Terraform configured, not
inferred or proven by string validation. Exact canonical numeric response names and
CRC32C are checked by GCPReader; no ID/number alias equality is assumed.

Command flags (identifiers and policy only): `-connections-enabled`,
`-plaid-link-events-qualified`, `-provider-project-number`, `-infisical-origin`,
`-infisical-project`, `-infisical-environment`, `-infisical-identity`,
`-provider-registry-bucket`, `-provider-registry-prefix`, `-plaid-client-id-version`,
`-plaid-client-secret-version`, `-plaid-consent-expires-at`, optional fixed
`-plaid-webhook-url` and separate default-false `-plaid-hosted-repair`. Existing `-project`,
`-mode managed`, and `-database-mode cloudsql` remain mandatory for enabled hosting.
No secrets are accepted by these flags. Existing URL-database behavior is unchanged
when optional connections are disabled; this composition introduces no new discovery.

Hosting metadata is fixed to the Terraform namespace: project IDs have6–30characters;
registry bucket is `{project-id}-jayburd-dev-credential-registry`, prefix
`provider-credentials-v1`; static containers are `jayburd-dev-bank-sync-client-id`
and `jayburd-dev-bank-sync-client-secret`. Swapped, foreign or arbitrary containers
fail before secret access even if other IAM grants accidentally exist. Cold restart
after well-formed optional approval expiry preserves SQL-only bookkeeping/attempt
inspection and performs no dependency I/O. Provider entries stay unavailable before
SQL/secret/KMS/provider work; warm outgoing transport also rechecks the same exact
deadline. Any new provider approval is separately explicit; there is no grace or
startup renewal. Disabled composition remains entirely inert.

documents.title: Sandbox Hosted Link enrollment
documents.body:
# Sandbox Hosted Link enrollment

## Decision and sources

Issue #125 implements the owner's requested next Sandbox application slice
(2026-10-14). New enrollments in the Sandbox HTTP adapter request Hosted Link;
existing synthetic SDK fixtures remain supported. No live-bank activation.

Reviewed relevant creation/completion sections of Plaid's
[Hosted Link guide](https://plaid.com/docs/link/hosted-link/) and
[Link API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/) on 2026-10-14, API version 2020-09-14.
Hosted Link exposes completed session results without account-specific enablement.
Ordinary SDK session results require Link-events enablement from Plaid support.
Plaid recommends the SDK for owned frontends. Our temporary qualification choice
avoids that external prerequisite; retain the SDK as the product alternative and
revisit after enablement. This does not qualify institution-specific behavior.

## Contract

Begin includes an optional ephemeral `hosted_link_url`, limited to HTTPS
secure.plaid.com/hl/ with an opaque alphanumeric/hyphen/underscore path segment,
no query, fragment, userinfo or port. Both server and UI validate it. No
SMS/email, redirects or webhook integration is added. The URL and Link token
are transient browser handoff material; the server also stores an encrypted,
attempt-scoped Link token for completion after reload. SQL retains the hash.
A new-tab link uses noreferrer/noopener.

Explicit completion posts `{}` through the new complete route. Before claiming
exchange, SQL context must match the retained token hash, unexpired new attempt
and current authority. The server reads one
bounded /link/token/get result. Zero completed public tokens returns the unchanged
link_ready projection; the user can check again. Multiple tokens, malformed,
stale or cross-session responses fail closed. Exactly one completed result provides
the public token in server memory, then the existing one-shot claim, session
verification, exchange, manifest and immutable credential publication run.
No automatic polling/retry of exchange. An uncertain reply requires existing
attempt inspection/reconciliation. Scope changes clear browser handoff material;
the server retains its encrypted attempt-scoped copy for authorized recovery.

## Source-backed recovery implementation (#187)

[Plaid's Hosted Link guide](https://plaid.com/docs/link/hosted-link/)
recommends retaining the Link token associated with the application's user,
strongly recommends a completion webhook, and documents `/link/token/get` as a
way to obtain completed-session results for up to six hours after the session
ends. A redirect or Plaid success screen alone does not prove local exchange,
storage or binding. The reviewed sections and limits are recorded as PI12 in
[the Plaid source register](../research/plaid-ingestion-sources.md).

Migration 19 stores an immutable encrypted Link handoff bound by AEAD/KMS AAD
to the exact actor/entity/book/attempt. Only scoped SQL functions can read its
ciphertext, after current grants and worker revision checks. The authenticated
`POST /connection-attempts/{id}/complete` accepts only `{}`; the server decrypts
and verifies the original Link-token hash, queries `/link/token/get`, then uses
the existing one-shot claim, exchange and encrypted credential publication.
The browser never receives a recovered token. The attempt remains claimable
until the earlier of seven hours after Begin or six hours after Plaid's Hosted
URL expiry; the URL itself still expires at the provider time. Provider results
older than six hours are rejected. Encrypted handoff rows remain immutable
audit history after expiry and are never used to start a new Plaid session.
Revoked actor/book authority blocks reads and completion. This bounded **use**
window is not a deletion policy; physical ciphertext retention needs a
separately reviewed lifecycle.

Evaluate verified `SESSION_FINISHED` webhook delivery as the recommended
provider path with `/link/token/get` as a bounded recovery/read path. This work
depends on the separate webhook authenticity and durable processing gates in
#103 and #87; an unverified webhook must not authorize exchange. Until that
design is accepted, continue explicit user-driven completion for an intact
same-tab handoff, showing **Open Plaid Sandbox** and **Check bank setup
completion** prominently.

## Explicit cancellation and retry (#200)

Owner direction now permits discarding an unfinished **new** setup even if the
user completed Plaid. This supersedes the earlier absence-of-completion restart
proposal. The application does not claim that no provider session exists.
The existing one-shot exchange claim is the authoritative local boundary:
`abandon` locks the same attempt as `claim_connection`, rechecks initiating
actor authority, and permits `link_pending`/`link_ready` only without a claim,
sync Item, stored credential or publication. A winning cancellation makes the
attempt immutable `abandoned`; a winning exchange claim rejects cancellation.
No provider calls occur during cancellation, and no credential or audit history
is deleted. This can leave an unused provider session; it is not bank-access
revocation or Plaid Item removal. Existing claimed lost-credential abandonment
keeps its original guards.

The UI offers **Try again** and **Cancel setup** beside the blocking setup after
reload. Both use authenticated POST `/abandon` with the existing explicit
confirmation body. Retry creates a new session only after confirmed abandoned
state and refreshed zero unfinished count. A lost reply reads that exact attempt;
failed reads or a competing claim never authorize a new enrollment. Cancel does
not create a replacement. Terminal attempts remain audit history.

Issue #215 extends this boundary after a credential has been published. A
`binding_review` attempt cannot be abandoned by a local state update alone: the
application follows the provider-backed prepare/remove/finalize contract in
[binding review recovery](binding-review-recovery.md). The earlier unclaimed and
unrecoverable-credential paths remain unchanged.

This is an internal operational state change, not an ISO 20022 financial
message. Existing currency and ledger contracts are unchanged. Migration 21
updates the function through release tooling; no operator record edits occur.
Sources: existing PI12 review and local claim/publication contracts. An attempted
2026-10-19 refresh of Plaid's tokens page was unavailable; no new provider
behavior is assumed. Acceptance is synthetic SQL/service and browser evidence,
not a claim of fresh hosted enrollment success.

Acceptance: synthetic browser/API/PostgreSQL fixtures cover same-tab completion,
reload, completed session after reload, no completed result, duplicate results,
concurrent claim, transport uncertainty, denied scope and repeated clicks.
One old attempt can yield at most one exchange and one stored credential. A
fresh Hosted Sandbox test must reach binding review; #160 and #164 remain open
for separate hosted credential and worker evidence.

Explicit account binding and existing acquisition/review remain separate. This
change cannot post a journal. Migration 19 adds encrypted Link handoffs and
extends the unclaimed completion window. Internal operational commands and
Plaid proprietary JSON are not ISO 20022 messages; existing ISO 4217 mapping applies.

## Fresh-enrollment recovery correction (#187, wave 2)

Coordinator reviewed 2026-10-22; existing migration 19 supplies encrypted
actor/entity/book/attempt retention and current authority. No new migration or
API field is required for this correction. This does not enable ordinary
reconnect, SDK OAuth return or LINK webhook acceptance.

The first server-side `CompletedPublicToken` lookup checks the exact retained
Link token against the provider response, one completed modern Item-add result,
bounded token shape, completion freshness and no ambiguity. `VerifySession`
currently repeats those same checks for new enrollment and also rejects an
expected existing Item. Repeating that lookup after the one-shot SQL claim can
strand a valid setup on a second-read outage without ever exchanging its token.

For a server-resolved new enrollment only, `Execute` retains an unexported local
typed proof of both token hashes. Before exchange, the SQL claim must still
match the exact new mode, nonce, Link hash, public hash and absence of an expected
existing Item. The proof comes only from the trusted lookup, never browser input,
request/context metadata or an exported verified flag. Caller-supplied public
tokens continue through `VerifySession`. SQL claim/expiry/current scope checks
and immutable credential publication remain authoritative. No provider exchange
is retried on uncertain SQL/provider acknowledgement; replay inspects state.

`CompleteHosted` uses one ten-second aggregate context and bounds the retained
ciphertext/KMS read by the earlier recovery expiry. Expired, canceled or denied
attempts do not start a provider lookup. `Execute` obtains fresh SQL context after
the retained-token read; revocation during that read therefore blocks completion.
The encrypted row is not deleted: immutable historical ciphertext retention and
physical deletion policy remain unresolved. These use bounds are not a TTL.

The UI distinguishes the short Hosted URL lifetime from the durable setup
recovery deadline. URL expiry removes navigation but preserves explicit checking
of an already completed session. A completion conflict refreshes authorized
discovery and updates expired-unclaimed state; an expired recovery window hides
stale completion/cancel guidance. It does not create another attempt automatically.

Final validation exposed an existing default-date initialization race: the form
could accept a user's binding date before the passive initializer replaced it
with today. The existing synchronous date/proposal initializer now runs before
paint through a client layout effect, retaining its `!date` guard. This changes
initialization timing, not the default date, subsequent user edits, proposal rules
or keyed scope reset. `TestConnectionsEnrollmentBinding` asserts the chosen
2026-01-02 date reaches the submitted binding request. LR06 records the React
mechanism; a retry/timeout increase is not used to hide the observed failure.

Alternatives: keep the redundant post-claim lookup (rejected because transient
read failure strands a verified session), trust browser success (rejected), or
exchange before SQL claim (rejected duplicate-effect risk). Signed
`SESSION_FINISHED` is a separate future profile, not a shortcut in this change.
STD-01 proprietary Plaid bootstrap applicability and existing currency/accounting
mapping are unchanged; no ISO 20022 message or conformance claim is invented.

Acceptance: `TestHostedRecoverySingleAssociation` uses the actual HTTP adapter
and fails any second lookup while completing exactly once; caller-token mismatch,
pending/ambiguous/outage/lost-claim and replay tests retain the original safety
boundaries. Deadline and revocation fixtures cover retained-token access. UI
expiry tests preserve completion after URL expiry and stop the discovered 409
expiry loop. Full-stack journeys remain synthetic provider/identity evidence.

Reviewed current official sections and limits: LR05 in
[the recovery source register](../research/plaid-link-recovery-sources.md).

## Acceptance and limits

[Qualification recovery](plaid-link-recovery-qualification.md) adds fixed guidance
for a unique fresh modern finished exit before claiming exchange. Legacy,
unfinished and ambiguous exits do not authorize completion. Explicit cancellation
still uses the existing SQL race guards; no provider-absence assertion is made.

`TestHostedLinkNavigation` and `TestHostedLinkCompletion` reject unsafe URLs,
ambiguous and stale results. `TestHostedCompletionClaimBoundary` proves pending
and invalid authority never consume a claim and exchange occurs once. UI tests
“Hosted completion stays pending, then exposes verified binding review” and
“Hosted handoff clears on …” cover completion, uncertainty, cancel and scope changes.
`TestSyncReviewPostJourney` checks explicit binding, acquisition, exact cents and
zero automatic journals through PostgreSQL.
Actual interactive Hosted Link, deployed acquisition, historical completion and
signed webhook qualification remain open in #88 until observed separately.

## Release compatibility

The pinned Sandbox adapter now always creates Hosted Link. Retain the existing
schemaVersion2 `link_events_qualified` boolean as ordinary-SDK account metadata,
but accept false: Hosted Link does not depend on that enablement. Terraform must
pass its actual value, never force true. The field remains required and included
in release/rollback digests; this does not silently enable connections=null.
Older binaries still reject false and are not eligible for this profile. Build
and promotion must pin this implementation. New Go/release/Terraform tests prove
false propagates without weakening credential, expiry, identity or disabled gates.

documents.title: Hosted Sandbox platform composition
documents.body:
# Hosted Sandbox platform composition

## Decision and boundary

This slice composes the existing acquisition protocol with real dependency adapters.
Cloud SQL remains authority; private Cloud Run publisher/sync services use Scheduler
and Cloud Tasks. [Worker configuration](hosted-workers.md), [evidence storage](hosted-evidence.md),
[provider vault](provider-vault.md) and [API composition](hosted-connections.md) own
their interfaces. No new accounting message or migration is introduced. Existing
ISO mappings remain unchanged; infrastructure identifiers are not financial messages.

The [controlled release contract](worker-release.md) separates owner-operated
workers bootstrap from the two-service worker-runtime root. Dedicated worker
federation and state prevent routine CI from administering bootstrap IAM or secrets.
Scheduler remains paused and owner-controlled. Build publication produces a tested
candidate; exact-byte owner approval and existing closure gates govern deployment.
Follow the contract's owner migration procedure before adopting existing services.

## SQL setup and activation order

Existing migrations through15 and safe capability roles must be present. Owner
provisions the two IAM logins through Terraform, then runs
[worker-logins.sql](../../db/bootstrap/worker-logins.sql) through the established
private Cloud SQL operator procedure with identifier-only `publisher_user` and
`sync_user` variables. Expected usernames are `jayburd-dev-publisher@PROJECT.iam`
and `jayburd-dev-sync@PROJECT.iam`. The script validates both before mutation,
rejects privileged/cross-capability membership, grants inherited execution without
SET ROLE or role administration, sets search_path to pg_catalog and caps each
login at four connections across overlapping revisions. It grants no table access,
DDL, ledger ownership or business enrollment. No password or runtime migration.

Owner separately enrolls the current service principal/import membership,
`integration.set_connection_worker`, then `integration.enroll_sync_delivery`
using the reviewed actor/entity/book and idempotency contracts. Never insert directly
into their tables. Keep Scheduler paused until exact binding, private OIDC callers,
Infisical propagation and Sandbox execution readiness have been verified. One runtime
publisher binding serves one selected book in this first release; multi-book fan-out
and linear scalability remain #89 work.

Pools: API five per instance, worker two each. With overlapping configured API
revisions (20), two overlapping worker revisions each (8), migrator (2) and five
operator connections, modeled demand is35 against max_connections50. This is a
configuration budget, not a measured capacity claim.

## Acceptance and missing evidence

`test-worker-bootstrap.sh` uses PostgreSQL17 and a non-superuser administrator to
prove replay, inherited capability, SET/DDL denial and unsafe membership rejection.
Mocked Terraform tests check exact IAM destinations, paused scheduling,
digest-pinned configuration and state separation. These do not prove
Cloud SQL's administrator behavior, caller JWTs, Cloud Tasks delivery or secret sync.

The [Sandbox diagnostic](plaid-sandbox-qualification.md) is opt-in and partial.
Actual Link UI/association, dynamic pending-to-posted, webhook delivery, persisted
cursor-to-review consistency and zero automatic journals still require hosted
qualification. Application release configuration follows [explicit connection policy](connection-release.md).
[Browser Link loading](plaid-link-browser.md) and paused worker promotion are
implemented for synthetic review. Reconnect support and real hosted qualification
remain open; no production institution or official-book approval follows.

documents.title: Owned Hosted Link repair — #275
documents.body:
# Owned Hosted Link repair — #275

## Decision and scope

Proposed2026-10-24 by the coordinator, for implementation review. No reconnect
capability or hosted clearance is delivered by this document. Retain the current
Hosted frontend for one bounded Sandbox repair; the SDK transition remains a
separate direction. Production requires #308 and its environment-isolation work.
This phase allocates no migration number and changes no SQL, runtime or consent.

Problem: current `HTTPProvider.SupportsMode` rejects reconnect, migration19's
encrypted handoff is new-only, and ordinary update completion is not represented
by the pinned SDK's Item-add result. A healthy account lookup, browser redirect,
deprecated callback or foreign `LOGIN_REPAIRED` notification cannot prove that our
owned attempt repaired the selected Item.

LR07 in [the source register](../research/plaid-link-recovery-sources.md) records
the reviewed modern signed notification and update-mode sections. The event
identifies a Link token/session and outcome; it has no Item identity or completion
timestamp. Our inference is to join that proof to the **server-created** Link
hash and preselected SQL Item context. JWT issuance time establishes notification
freshness only. Actual ordinary Sandbox update delivery/shape remains unproved.

| Alternative | Decision / cost |
| --- | --- |
| Owned Hosted session plus signed completion receipt | Proposed bounded extension; requires receiver, SQL proof and ACL work before enabling repair |
| Move all enrollment to Web SDK | Better vendor-recommended owned frontend; adds lifecycle/OAuth/account-event qualification before it solves server authority |
| Accept Item health, redirect or deprecated success | Rejected: none identifies our completed update session |
| Exchange another public token | Rejected: repair reuses the existing access credential; risks creating a different Item |

Revisit if the actual update session lacks the documented signed event or the
retained-token association is ambiguous. Keep repair disabled and obtain provider
clarification rather than falling back to callback/account-health evidence.

## Authority and fixed protocol

1. The verified owner explicitly selects the existing Item and complete approved
   stream set. SQL rechecks current principal/entity/book authority, live source
   consent, Item generation and all sibling streams. Never trust browser Item,
   account, credential reference, generation or user identifiers as authority.
2. The backend reads the SQL-selected existing credential through the current
   vault/AAD boundary. It creates an **explicit Hosted** update Link using that
   credential, existing redirect/webhook configuration and no extra products,
   account-selection widening or user-based multi-Item update. New enrollment
   remains unchanged. Set an explicit **proposed** reconnect deadline of15minutes
   from attempt creation, capped by provider expiry. This requires new SQL: merged
   migration19 globally changed the attempt default to seven hours and its
   `record_link_session` adds six hours for both new and reconnect. Do not claim
   that reconnect is already short-lived. Replace that behavior for reconnect
   without shortening new enrollment recovery, changing old immutable receipts or
   extending source consent. Existing unclaimed reconnect attempts need an
   explicit migration disposition: cap eligibility at the immutable original
   `connection_event` begin receipt's `recorded_at` plus15minutes in the new
   claim/proof gate; require exactly one such event, otherwise deny. Attempts
   have no `created_at` column; do not invent one or rewrite their history.
   A longer vendor URL lifetime grants no local authority.
3. Before returning the URL, atomically persist nonce, Link hash, deadline and
   encrypted handoff under current actor/entity/book/attempt authority. Extend
   migration19's put/get only for the intended reconnect states. Concurrent
   handoff writes must still yield the existing single encrypted winner. Browser
   memory may hold transient URL/initialization material; no browser persistence.
4. The dedicated receiver verifies the bounded raw request's existing ES256,
   JWK and exact body digest before interpreting or submitting an event. Preserve
   the verifier's five-minute maximum age and sixty-second future tolerance.
   Reject duplicate JSON fields, malformed identifiers/hashes, unknown outcomes,
   wrong environment and invalid key/time/signature without SQL business work.
5. Parse only `LINK/SESSION_FINISHED` with `status=success|exited`, bounded
   `link_token`, `link_session_id`, and Sandbox environment. Hash Link/session
   identifiers before SQL. Validate bounded optional public-token fields and
   discard them; do not assume an update event has an empty array, log tokens,
   or exchange any of them. `user_id` supplies no ownership. Do not fabricate
   `item_id`, `finished_at` or ordinary Item-update API results.
6. A restricted SQL receipt function resolves exactly one current reconnect
   attempt by retained Link hash, then locks and rechecks it. Zero matches is
   ignored; multiple matches is denied without choosing one. Recheck ingress
   login/revision/environment, current principal/book authority, live consent,
   Item generation, sibling stream set and deadline before retaining proof.
   Require signed `iat >= original begin receipt time - 60seconds`; later notification
   delivery does not extend the deadline. Preserve prior immutable receipts.
7. Store only closed normalized hashes, outcome, signed issuance time, receipt
   time and the exact scoped attempt/Item-generation association. Never retain
   raw webhook/JWT, Link/public/access tokens or provider financial payloads.
   This receipt **does not** claim, resume, publish, create a demand or read bank
   secrets. The public receiver has no vault/KMS/Item API authority.
8. An explicit owner completion/recovery request reauthorizes SQL, reads the
   retained handoff and verifies its hash. Pending proof returns the unchanged
   attempt with fixed waiting guidance; no claim, bank credential read or provider
   request. One distinct successful session is eligible. Exited proof remains
   blocked. More than one distinct session, or conflicting outcomes for one
   session, is ambiguous and remains blocked before claim. Offer only explicit
   unclaimed local cancellation followed by a separately confirmed fresh attempt.
9. SQL claim itself requires and pins the exact eligible proof; an API-role
   caller cannot bypass it by directly invoking the older claim interface. Use
   the existing atomic Item fence/claim and full stream checks. Once claimed,
   later receipts cannot replace the selected proof or authorize another repair.
10. After claim, reuse the existing credential reference/version and read the
    current manifest. Require the expected Item and every approved bound account
    with compatible type/currency. Missing/de-selected accounts leave the Item
    paused; newly discovered accounts remain unbound. Do not silently revise the
    consent scope, binding identities or local consent deadline. Replace the
    reconnect branch of existing confirmation, which otherwise copies the
    manifest expiry: enforce no later than the old live Item approval, also
    honoring any earlier provider expiration. Never revive an expired approval.
    Confirmation
    checks the proof, claim, current generation/scope and publishes one
    repair-caused demand per still-active approved stream using existing
    `signal_sync` with reason `resume` and stable key `repair:<attempt UUID>`.
    Acquire current stream authority/locks in stable order; do not unpause an
    owner-paused stream. This is new explicit confirmation wiring, not an existing
    implicit callback. Replay of that same cause cannot add another generation;
