    independent manual/webhook/scheduler signals retain their own semantics.
    Source/account/history and posted journals remain
    unchanged. No new Item, exchange, token rotation or automatic posting.

## SQL interface and locking review

Implementation profile32 (#318): two immutable grains `link_session_receipt`
(one delivery, primary key environment/receipt hash, scoped attempt FK, Link /
session / raw-body hashes, closed outcome, integer signed iat and receipt time)
and `link_repair_claim` (one attempt, exact successful receipt FK, claim UUID,
original credential reference/version and live consent ceiling). No direct runtime
table grants. Private reconnect projection adds `item_consent_expires_at` for319;
confirmation independently rejects a later manifest expiry. Existing mutable
unclaimed reconnect expiry is capped with a new immutable policy-change event;
no original event or terminal effect is rewritten. Missing/ambiguous begin evidence
denies eligibility. This is the explicit legacy disposition required above.
Actual synthetic stages and limits are in [the SQL delivery runbook](../runbooks/hosted-repair-sql.md).

Compatibility correction33 (#326): the32 reconnect handoff copied19's numeric-only
KMS resource check and rejected the canonical project-ID key used by the runtime.
Restore20's exact numeric-or-canonical grammar without changing any repair gate,
ACL, ciphertext or AAD. This is not a new key-selection policy: the existing
runtime still checks its configured key/version during unwrap. The held319
concrete SQL/AEAD service test exposed this gap; numeric-only profile fixtures
did not prove canonical compatibility.33 down is disposable/quiesced-only and
refuses retained canonical reconnect envelopes before replacing the function.
No managed apply or source qualification follows from this correction alone.

The mutable attempt also gains an immutable-once `repair_scope_sha256`, pinned
only by a fresh server-authorized begin. Canonical input includes source-binding
and stream revisions/states, namespace/source identities and consent/worker scope;
ordinary cursors/demands and display labels are excluded. Legacy missing scope
cannot be inferred from current rows: deny and require explicit local cancellation
and a separately reviewed fresh attempt. This profile requires the initiating
actor to be the existing Item consent principal; delegated repair needs separate
review. Neither a grant reset nor a changed binding silently reauthorizes old work.

The dedicated webhook session remains barred from `ledger.authorize` and all API
entrypoints. Its private receipt locker rechecks the SQL-selected initiating actor,
current read/connect/import memberships and existing source/worker capabilities
under canonical locks. It does not weaken that global cross-role guard, accept an
actor from the event, SET ROLE or acquire any API/table grant. Actual restricted
login tests must prove both receipt acceptance and continued API/ledger denial.

Lock the union of actor, configured worker, original consent principal and all
stream service principals in UUID order **before** the existing book/source/Item
chain. The existing connection helper alone locks only actor/configured worker;
do not acquire other principal locks later under the Item. Exact normalized
receipt fields are `link_token_sha256`, `link_session_sha256`, `body_sha256`,
`status` and integer `issued_at`; raw argument is this closed object, not a payload.
Require globally unambiguous retained token association across all modes before
unclaimed proof/claim; a new-mode token must not be reinterpreted as repair. Use
a nonunique lookup index and deny collisions, not an unreviewed global unique
constraint over existing history. Human security review is still pending before
managed release, and no actual ordinary update event is qualified.

Allocate a forward migration only under a fresh sole-writer lease after checking
main/#65. Merged13/14/19 and later definitions are immutable. Review current
[database foundations](../research/database-foundations.md) before DDL.

Proposed restricted interfaces (parameter names below are descriptive):

- `integration.accept_verified_link_session(environment text, receipt_key text,
  raw text)`: only `bookkeeping_webhook`. `raw` is a **closed normalized** JSON
  object containing Link/session/body SHA256, status and integer signed `iat`,
  not the provider body. Enforce exact keys/types/bounds in SQL. Return only
  accepted/duplicate/ignored and bounded counts; never disclose an attempt to
  the public caller. Receipt key/body mismatch fails atomically.
- `integration.connection_link_proof(actor uuid,e uuid,b uuid,id uuid)`: only
  `bookkeeping_api`, current owned scope. Return pending/success/exited/ambiguous
  and private receipt hashes needed for completion; no browser token or cross-
  scope discovery. Recheck authority/deadline at claim, not just this read.
- `integration.get_repair_bank_credential(actor uuid,e uuid,b uuid,id uuid)`:
  only API, derives the old reference/version/Item from the exact current repair
  and returns its existing AEAD envelope plus closed addressed metadata. Permit
  current unclaimed `link_pending` creation, or the exact proof-pinned nonterminal claim;
  `link_ready` completion cannot read the bank credential before proof/claim.
  no ciphertext publication/write.319 must use this purpose-specific read rather
  than18's generic lookup, which chooses a matching attempt by expiry and can
  select an older active enrollment after reconnect changes the Item generation.
  Confirmed/abandoned/expired/revoked repairs cannot read through this interface.
  Go must verify the addressed envelope/AAD and reuse the credential, without
  creating another encrypted version. Original generic APIs remain unchanged.
- Extend `claim_connection` to require/pin proof for reconnect and retain all
  existing new/rotate/remove restrictions. Extend handoff put/get only as above;
  `abandon_connection` may cancel **unclaimed** reconnect locally. Cancellation
  does not call Item removal or reactivate the old credential. Claimed attempts
  require exact recovery, never automatic abandonment/replacement.

Use integration-owned immutable receipt/proof rows and no direct runtime table
grants or PUBLIC EXECUTE. A hash lookup identifies a candidate only. Follow the
existing principal/entity/book authority locks, source accounts ordered by
source_account_id, Item, then attempt order; never take an attempt lock and then
acquire a source or Item lock. Recheck the complete sibling stream set under that
order, then lock/write proof and receipt rows. Pin proof under the same locks
as claim, so concurrent event, cancellation, permission revocation and repair
cannot slip through a previously read eligibility result. Design exact constraints
and receipts with the single SQL implementation, not a parallel schema draft.

Dedicated-login bootstrap currently permits only
the two receipt functions after32:
`accept_verified_webhook(text,text,text)` and
`accept_verified_link_session(text,text,text)`. Its closed allowlist retains owner/API/sync/table/vault/KMS denial,
ingress disable/replay and failed-bootstrap atomicity. Independently assess the
actual Cloud SQL IAM marker compatibility; verifier31 is not an automatic webhook
role exception. Migration, binary and bootstrap must be compatible before release.

## Signed receiver implementation profile — #319 phase1

After raw ES256/JWK/body/time verification, the dedicated Go receiver classifies
the event and checks its entire closed schema. `LINK/SESSION_FINISHED` requires
Sandbox, success/exited, visible-ASCII Link token1–4096bytes and session1–256bytes.
Optional deprecated public token and each public-token array member are bounded
to1–4096bytes; at most25members. Optional user ID is1–256visible-ASCII bytes.
Absent optionals and empty arrays are allowed; explicit null, wrong types,
duplicates, unknown fields and empty identifiers are rejected. These are local
fail-closed bounds, not vendor guarantees or a claim of Multi-Item support.
Actual update shape remains a qualification gate; revisit this profile with
reviewed metadata if the provider delivers a different representation.

LR07's modern properties were rechecked2026-10-24 against the official Link API
SESSION_FINISHED section in full. It defines success/exited and token/session/
environment fields, optional public-token/user metadata, and Hosted default
enablement. It does not establish our SQL ownership association or actual delivery.
The existing STD-01 operational/nonfinancial assessment above remains unchanged;
no financial mapping, currency policy, API version or SDK upgrade is introduced.

Only private hashed Link/session/outcome metadata survives parsing; the SQL call
uses exactly the normalized five-key object above and a fixed purpose function.
No raw tokens, user identity or request-selected SQL function cross the boundary.
The committed private acknowledgement is accepted/duplicate count1 or ignored
count0. It must match the verified event kind before HTTP204; old Transactions
acknowledgements cannot stand in for Link proof, or vice versa. Invalid/mixed
outputs fail closed. Current authority/expiry denial maps to fixed HTTP403 with
no SQL diagnostics; unknown commit remains503, never an automatic bank operation.

Named evidence and limits: [signed receiver stages](../runbooks/hosted-link-receipts.md).
This phase adds no credential reader, concrete reconnect capability, API/UI
completion wiring or hosted acceptance; subsequent319/320 and303 remain required.

## Service integration profile — #319

The concrete adapter requires a separate explicit `HTTPConfig.HostedRepair`
capability, default false, **and** the existing exact fixed Sandbox receiver.
Constructor validation rejects repair without that receiver before I/O. An
existing Transactions webhook opt-in alone stays repair-disabled. Alternative
reuse of that old URL setting as implicit repair permission was rejected: it
would silently expand an already reviewed configuration. No new endpoint, key,
product, account selection or Production environment is selected by a request.
328 propagates the default-false flag through private CLI/runtime/release metadata;
actual activation still needs separate exact finite approval and compatible
schema33/API/receiver images/restricted bootstrap. Source ancestry and302/303
readiness gates precede cloud authentication; selected-image status precedes
runtime rollout, including the explicitly enabled repair rollback profile.
No source merge or existing webhook setting alone enables repair.

Enabled qualification composition requests explicit Hosted update using the
SQL-selected existing credential,900second URL lifetime, US/English, fixed
receiver and server actor identifier. Products/additional consent/update-account
selection/user-based multi-Item options are omitted. Local SQL's15minute cap and
earlier original source consent stay authoritative regardless of URL lifetime.
Encrypted handoff must commit and verify before the service returns the URL;
concurrent/replayed begin cannot create another provider Link.

Owner completion reads current SQL context and owned proof before even the Link
handoff/KMS read. Pending returns the same attempt; exited/ambiguous block.
Direct execute rejects a public token or changed nonce/Link hash; SQL still pins
proof atomically with claim. Repair never calls new-mode `VerifySession`, token
get, exchange, rotation, generic secret read, wrapping preflight or credential Put.
All bank reads use the optional exact-attempt purpose reader with addressed
existing reference/version/Item checks. A missing reader fails closed.

Only an explicit committed-claim completion/reconcile may repeat the read-only
manifest and SQL confirmation, even when no manifest was saved after a lost
claim reply. Preserve the existing credential version and full approved account
manifest; SQL owns sibling/type/currency/current scope checks. Cap provider
manifest expiry at the original SQL-projected approval and any earlier already
known manifest deadline. Immutable manifest replay must match; a changed account
set or narrower expiry remains blocked for review rather than overwriting evidence.
No later response renews consent. Current SQL rejects expired/revoked scope before
key work, and confirmation rechecks it before one stable repair-caused demand per
active approved stream. Owner-paused streams and unapproved new accounts stay so.

Local unclaimed repair cancellation inspects the public scoped attempt then calls
only SQL abandonment, so an expired Link does not prevent it or trigger Item
removal/restart. The existing independent global provider-enrollment approval gate
still precedes this entrypoint and every provider entry; no grace/renewal was added.
New/rotate/remove uncertainty rules and the new-enrollment Hosted resolver remain
unchanged. This operational proprietary protocol retains the STD-01 assessment
and existing crypto/ISO currency/accounting profiles; no ISO conformance claim.

Delivery stages and limits: [service integration](../runbooks/hosted-repair-service.md).
Actual ordinary update notification, managed identities, browser reload and
independent acquisition equality still require303/320/275 qualification.

## Replay, recovery and operational limits

Exact body/receipt replay has no new effect; re-signed same session/outcome may
add an immutable receipt but never another eligible session or repair-caused wakeup. Conflicting
outcomes and distinct sessions block unclaimed completion. Late events after claim
cannot mutate pinned proof, reactivate a revoked/stale Item or undo confirmation.
Other-mode/new-enrollment events are ignored by this reconnect boundary. Existing
new enrollment keeps its modern token-get verification and one-shot exchange.

Unknown claim reply is inspected by exact attempt. For reconnect only, the same
current-authorized claim/proof/credential can repeat the read-only manifest and
confirmation after a lost response, including failure before the first manifest.
There is no fresh Link, exchange, rotation, different proof or automatic retry
loop. Keep new/rotate one-shot uncertainty rules unchanged. Revocation, source
consent expiry, generation or stream drift denies recovery without publishing. Terminal success
replay returns its existing receipt; journals are never produced by this path.

The15minute deadline governs **unclaimed** Link/proof/claim eligibility. An already
committed proof-pinned claim may be explicitly reconciled after its Link window
ends, under the same current permissions, generation/scope and original live
source-consent ceiling. Never reopen its Link or mint another execution grant.
This follows the existing13 context distinction between unclaimed expiry and
durable claimed recovery; it is our engineering policy, not new Plaid consent.
Alternative hard-expiring claimed recovery would strand a paused Item after a
lost reply despite valid durable proof. Reject that alternative: repeat only
read-only manifest/confirmation, and deny when source authority actually expires.
`TestHostedRepairSQLClaimedExpiryRecovery` must prove same claim/credential, one
repair cause, no duplicate effect and no secret access after source revocation.

An ingress outage yields pending recovery and keeps acquisition paused. Owner
can explicitly cancel an unclaimed attempt; no client callback bypass. Disabling
ingress, release rollback or local cancellation is not provider consent removal.
Use the existing scoped disconnect/remove contract when that action is intended.

This changes authorization/session state: human security review is required
before managed release. Do not weaken signature checks, reuse API identity for the
public receiver or grant it secret access to simplify delivery. Exact image/schema,
bootstrap/ingress receipt and separately authorized finite reset_login mandate
precede hosted testing. #271/#303 own actual signed delivery. No cloud call,
provider call, consent renewal or Production activation is authorized here.

## Standards and acceptance

Under STD-01 this is proprietary Plaid authorization and internal operational
receipt state, API2020-09-14/Go SDK49.0.0. No ISO20022 financial exchange or audit
data export is introduced; no applicable financial-message designation is invented.
Existing dated ISO4217 currency identifiers, decimal money, original currency and
accounting policy are unchanged. No ISO conformance claim. Applicable crypto and
least-privilege controls retain the existing webhook/vault profiles.

These named acceptance cases are **proposed, not implemented evidence**:

| Case | Independent expected observation |
| --- | --- |
| `TestHostedRepairSignature` | Invalid signature/body/key/age/future/duplicate JSON never reaches business SQL |
| `TestHostedRepairForeignScope` | Unknown, multiply matched, new-mode, foreign actor/book/Item/generation/hash denied or ignored; no mutation |
| `TestHostedRepairReplay` | Repeated/re-signed same session produces one claim and one repair-caused wakeup per active approved stream; raw secrets absent from receipts/logs |
| `TestHostedRepairAmbiguous` | Exited/conflicting/two-session preclaim proofs cannot be selected; explicit unclaimed cancellation only |
| `TestHostedRepairNoSecretAccess` | Pending receiver/completion has zero bank-token/vault/KMS/exchange/manifest calls; receiver role cannot acquire those rights |
| `TestHostedRepairRevoked` / `Expired` / `ReducedScope` | Current SQL denies late receipt/claim/confirm/recovery, preserves paused acquisition, never widens scope |
| `TestHostedRepairUnknownClaim` | Lost claim response recovers the same existing claim, including no stored manifest; no second exchange or credential |
| `TestHostedRepairRecovery` | Actual API/SQL/browser reload, lost confirmation and repeated click keep the exact attempt and one terminal receipt |
| `TestHostedRepairPublication` | Fixed source/account/history/credential-version IDs and journal totals unchanged; exactly one repair-caused wakeup per active approved stream after confirmed same-Item manifest, paused streams unchanged |

Implementation gates: `make check test build migration-test ledger-test
connection-state-test connection-service-test connection-ops-test webhook-test
webhook-bootstrap-test web-check web-test web-build web-browser app-integration`.
Fixtures must assert fixed outcomes independently of generated expected values.
Add actual restricted-role direct-call bypass, ingress-disable, lock-race and
shared-Item sibling tests. Browser fixtures use no real identity or financial data.

Hosted evidence separately records image/schema/bootstrap, fixture name, platform,
bounded mandate and times, induced login-required, owned update event receipt,
same Item/credential/stream continuity, one resumed demand and independent repeat
equality with absolute zero journals and `integration.outbox_message` rows of
event_type `journal.posted` in the fresh book. Other acquisition wakeup/outbox
intent is expected; do not mislabel it a posting or require every outbox empty.
Then exercise expiry,
revoked/reduced scope, cancellation and unknown response with exact receipts.
Injected events do not clear #88 O04/I01 or production qualification.

documents.title: Hosted Sandbox probe
documents.body:
# Hosted Sandbox probe

## Decision

Owner explicitly authorized the actual Sandbox test and its missing wiring on
2026-10-14. The probe creates one disposable fictional Item through Plaid's Sandbox
API, exchanges its token, selects a USD account, runs the existing exact-decoding
sync diagnostic, and attempts Item removal. This bypasses Link deliberately; it
cannot qualify interactive Link, application persistence, webhooks or live books.

The job reads only two pinned numeric GCP versions using managed identity. It has
no source-manager access or secret writes. Credential delivery separately uses the
existing immutable intent/receipt adapter for fixed root keys PLAID_CLIENT_ID and
PLAID_SECRET. Lookup remains value-disabled; each delivery requires reviewed ID and
source version. Infisical project access must be supplied by the owner.

## Execution boundary

Explicit opt-in is required; no default networking. Only sandbox.plaid.com is used,
redirects are disabled, responses are bounded, errors are fixed codes, and tokens
and provider payloads remain in runtime memory. No database, journal, file output,
webhook or production URL. At most one Item creation/exchange per execution; no
retry after unknown acknowledgement. Cleanup gets its own bounded context after
an access token is obtained. A failed exchange may leave an orphaned Sandbox Item;
report that ambiguity without retrying creation. Cloud Run retries are zero.

## Sources and acceptance

Reviewed Plaid [Sandbox API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/sandbox/) public_token/create
and [Items API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/items/) public_token/exchange and item/remove
on 2026-10-14. API-created Items bypass interactive Link. Inference: this provides a
credential/provider smoke test without claiming application association proof.
Existing [qualification contract](plaid-sandbox-qualification.md) governs sync limits
and partial-only receipts. No financial interchange added; ISO 20022 does not apply.

Tests must demonstrate fixed Sandbox host, redacted output, cleanup after sync
failure, no retry after exchange ambiguity, no calls without opt-in, and exact
numeric credential pinning. Hosted evidence remains separate from injected tests.

documents.title: Hosted Sandbox verifier execution
documents.body:
# Hosted Sandbox verifier execution

## Scope and decision evidence

Issue272, owner request2026-10-23 to provision the restricted verifier and execute
a fresh independently authored Sandbox proof. Engineering profile for review;
new sensitive runtime/IAM source requires human review before release. No new
product migration, public endpoint, provider secret access or posting permission.
The existing [comparison contract](sandbox-verification.md) remains authoritative.

Use one private Cloud Run job with the trusted worker image containing the inert
`/sandbox-verify` binary. Its separate IAM identity gets only Cloud SQL connector/
IAM-login roles and read access to a dedicated synthetic-input bucket. Owner SQL
bootstrap grants only the preexisting NOLOGIN capability; membership has INHERIT
true and ADMIN/SET false. No credential key or service-account impersonation is
created. One task, parallelism1, retries0, timeout120s; comparator budgets remain
the existing15s transport/4s transaction/3s statement/1s lock. No scheduler.

Only a reviewed run ID directory is mounted read-only at `/verification`. Inputs
are exactly manifest.json, fixture.json and identity-map.json. Existing CLI hashes
both financial fixture and identity-map bytes against a finite owner mandate
before connecting. Bucket is private, uniform-access, no versioning or soft-delete,
with one-day fallback lifecycle. Operator uploads each object create-only and
deletes the three exact generation-pinned objects immediately after comparison;
lifecycle is not a claim of prompt deletion. No secrets or raw provider responses
may enter this bucket, Terraform variables/state, logs or public evidence. Bucket
viewer permits reading other directories in that dedicated synthetic-only bucket;
`only-dir` is a filesystem view, not an IAM boundary. Remove inputs promptly and
grant no access to application evidence/token buckets. Disable runtime when idle.

## Acceptance sequence and boundaries

Current hosted application configuration expired2026-10-22. The concrete release
candidate uses trusted build39898191502 attempt1/source edb778e, release expiry
2026-10-23T18:00Z and new-session Sandbox consent deadline2026-10-23T20:00Z.
This is an explicitly proposed fresh-run interval, not permission to extend an
existing Item. Application configuration supplies new enrollment metadata; only
the new synthetic source is enrolled. Its persisted Item consent remains SQL
authority. Existing sources keep their prior consent and no live connection is
authorized. Exact-hash owner dispatch under deploy/README.md remains required.

1. Validate safe platform identity/SQL capability without a business mandate.
2. Author a complete small fixture before provider injection; pin exact dates and
   original lexemes independently. Start with one new synthetic checking source.
   Equal-valued purchases retain distinct logical identities. USD is this case's
   test unit, not a reduction of required multicurrency scope.
3. Use a new bounded Sandbox source consent; expired prior consent is not renewed
   implicitly. Use real managed browser identity and reviewed app book setup.
4. Obtain a separate identity-only map using the reviewed projection below;
   do not derive expected financial fields from adapter/observations/provider output.
5. Complete actual acquisition and idle stream; owner-enroll exact current source/
   binding/Item/generation plus both digests under a fresh <=60-minute mandate.
6. Upload exact bounded files outside Terraform; run one explicit job. Validate
   execution identity/image/command/volume/action and bounded result. Preserve
   both equality and absolute-zero journal/outbox evidence; no test posting.
7. Revoke the mandate, delete exact input generations and disable runtime. Retain
   only redacted outcomes and metadata receipts. Unknown commit or mismatch is
   not PASS; no automatic retry, source mutation or scope widening.

## Reviewed sources and standards

### Identity readback correction, engineering profile for review

The [Sandbox create response](https://plaid.com/docs/api/sandbox/#sandboxtransactionscreate)
documents only request_id, not transaction IDs (selected request/response sections
reviewed2026-10-23). The earlier comparison contract's assumption that injection
response metadata supplies the map cannot implement this endpoint's actual wire
shape. This correction permits a separate bounded readback solely for identity.

For the first fresh posted-only proof, independently author all financial fixture
rows before creating/injecting any provider data. Give each logical row a unique
synthetic description tag, including purchases with equal amounts. Owner-private
transport pipes one complete initial account-filtered sync page to the offline
identity projector. It requires HISTORICAL_UPDATE_COMPLETE, no further pages and
no modified/removed records, exact expected row count and account, unique matching
tags and unique provider IDs. Larger/dynamic histories require a separately
reviewed pagination/history protocol; this helper cannot certify them.

Projection copies transaction_id only. It consults name only to match pre-authored
identity tags; it never reads amounts/dates/currencies/states into the expectation
or compares them to decide which identity matches. Those fields are tested later
by SQL against the unchanged authored fixture. Wrong/missing/duplicate tags and
unexpected identities reject the map rather than adapting expectations. Original
financial fixture bytes remain hash-pinned; modifying provider financial fields
cannot change the projected ID map. Raw readback stays ephemeral/unlogged in the
owner-private pipe; only the map is written create-only to the private run directory.
The agent sees fixed outcomes/counts, not raw readback. No token/DSN/network flag
or credential discovery belongs in the projector.

The local operator command is `bin/sandbox-identity-map -action=project
-fixture=<absolute reviewed directory>/fixture.json -fixture-sha256=<approved hash>
-account-id=<exact synthetic account ID> -input-fd=3`. The owner supplies only the
complete account-filtered response through a private pipe on descriptor3. Saved
payload files/stdin/stderr are rejected. It writes the fixed sibling identity-map.json
create-only/0600 and emits only a readiness Boolean/count. This is an offline
identity association tool, not a provider transport, acquisition or evidence of
financial equality. No raw response is sent to the agent or retained in artifacts.

For this first case, directly configure the custom user with the independently
authored transactions before Link; no transaction-create endpoint call is needed.
Use a separate complete initial provider readback for identity association. If the
owner cannot supply the authorized private pipe, leave the hosted proof blocked;
do not substitute observed SQL rows, browser UI counts or a general data dump.
The separate [owner-private transport](sandbox-identity-transport.md) prepares a
bounded single-request producer for this gap. It requires independently reviewed
owner injection and source scope; it adds no application credential export or
automatic provider authority. Actual injection/transport remains unproved.

Alternative matching by amount/date or regenerating expectations from observed
rows would destroy oracle independence. Trusting creation-array order is not
documented and cannot identify returned IDs anyway. A tagged identity-only
projection narrows the correction to provider identity association. Named tests
must prove financial-field changes leave the map identical and incorrect identity,
account, incomplete/duplicate/modified input cannot produce a map. Hosted proof
still requires actual acquisition and complete comparison, not projector success.

Reviewed2026-10-23 selected official sections, not full product manuals:

- [Cloud Run job storage mounts](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/jobs/cloud-storage-volume-mounts),
  Required roles, Terraform, Limitations and mount-specific-directory sections:
  storage viewer supplies reads, read-only GCS mounts expose files without image
  changes; FUSE lacks full POSIX/concurrent-write semantics. Our create-only inputs,
  digest checks and dedicated bucket are design controls, not FUSE guarantees.
- [Plaid custom users](https://plaid.com/docs/sandbox/user-custom/), configuration,
  transactions and date handling: custom account overrides support explicit data;
  default fields may generate data and date rolling changes expected dates. Use
  explicit history and roll_dates_forward=false for exact dated fixtures.
- Existing PostgreSQL17 role/function/locking sources in the comparison contract
  govern SQL authority; no new financial comparison algorithm or DDL is introduced.

Alternative: general operator SQL or reused sync identity broadens financial and
credential authority. Baking dynamic inputs into an image retains them in build
artifacts; secret volumes misuse credential storage for ephemeral test inputs.
The isolated bucket adds a narrow private input channel while preserving the
existing CLI and image. Actual FUSE compatibility and IAM denial require hosted
evidence, not a mocked Terraform PASS.

ISO20022 registered messages do not apply to this proprietary operational
execution/input transport. ISO4217 dated identity and original units remain
required by the unchanged comparison profile; ISO21378:2019 audit relevance has
only the previously reviewed abstract, with no export/conformance claim.

Named gates: verifier bootstrap replay/unsafe-role/ACL rejection against real
disposable PostgreSQL30; mocked infrastructure deny-by-default/exact job/image/
identity/read-only bucket/no secret access; existing independent comparison tests;
core/migration/ledger gates as applicable. Actual hosted receipt/cleanup remain
separate acceptance. Follow-up272/88; no production qualification.

## Focused threat review

| STRIDE boundary / risk | Control and named evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Spoofed scope/login or elevated SQL access (high) | Derived verifier login, canonical SQL effective-ACL predicate, finite mandate pins; real bootstrap and existing verifier authorization tests |
| Changed expectations or substituted identity input (high) | Fixture authored before provider action, owner-private identity-only projection, exact fixture/map hashes and complete comparison; financial-independence and ambiguous-identity negatives |
| Unauthorized disclosure via storage/output (high) | Dedicated private bucket, read-only runtime, no provider-secret rights, private create-only map, fixed CLI outcomes; mocked IAM and CLI redaction/file-mode tests; actual hosted IAM still pending |
| Replay/unknown commit falsely recorded as PASS (high) | Existing one-attempt comparator drops uncertain results; zero job retries, validated execution plus bounded result; existing unknown-commit tests and operator receipt review |
| Unbounded job/input or lingering data (medium) | One task/pool1/120s job, bounded files/pipe/transaction, exact generation cleanup and idle job removal; limit tests and actual cleanup readback required |

This is a bounded engineering threat review; it is not independent AppSec signoff.

documents.title: Hosted acquisition worker composition
documents.body:
# Hosted acquisition worker composition

## Reviewed boundary

The coordinator approved separate publisher and sync service identities, Cloud SQL
IAM authentication and a maximum of two pooled connections per process. One worker
mode exposes one fixed private acquisition route. The existing dispatch SQL remains
authority for enrolled logins, current consent, leases, retry budgets and completion.
No provider data is fetched at startup; no migration or enrollment runs in a worker.

`Config` contains identifiers only: mode, instance connection name, explicit TCP
listen address, pinned caller audience/email/subject, and publisher-only binding
and queue identifiers. Publisher binds `/internal/acquisition/publish`; consumer
binds `/internal/acquisition/consume`. Existing Google signature verification and
exact workload policy run before body or SQL access. Cloud Run IAM is an additional
boundary, not a substitute for the application verification. Hosted header/OIDC
behavior must be qualified before activation.

`New(config, Dependencies)` composes injected SQL, verifier, queue or Runner through
the existing authenticated HTTP adapters and bounded worker host. `Managed` builds
actual Cloud SQL, Google-key verification, Cloud Tasks REST and Sandbox acquisition
clients. Consumer construction requires an explicit credential resolver and durable
evidence store. No local temporary evidence fallback, environment token, credential
file or ADC discovery is allowed. Missing adapters prevent construction.

## Managed identity and lifecycle

Cloud SQL login names are fixed `jayburd-dev-publisher@PROJECT.iam` and
`jayburd-dev-sync@PROJECT.iam`; database name remains bookkeeping and region
us-central1. Publisher and sync use the existing IAM connector, lazy refresh and
explicit metadata token sources. Pool maximum is two, minimum zero; no raw TCP
fallback, owner/API role substitution or worker-provided DSN is accepted. The
coordinator owns IAM SQL user creation and restricted SQL role/binding provisioning.

Metadata OAuth and ID-token access use a fixed Google metadata endpoint, required
Google metadata header, five-second request limit, bounded body and no redirects.
Tokens remain in memory and never appear in error text. Explicit injected transports
support synthetic tests. Production HTTP transport disables ambient proxies and
bounds connections per host at two. This is direct metadata credential access, not
ADC discovery. Constructors themselves retrieve no tokens.

The existing worker host sets header/read/write/idle bounds, private route admission
and graceful shutdown. Managed startup has a bounded database connection check;
it does not assert a book mandate is enrolled or a provider qualified. Dependency
cleanup is idempotent and follows request drain. Cancellation remains cooperative.
No hosted activation, account connection or real provider request is part of tests.

## Source review and decisions

Reviewed selected official sections on 2026-10-14, starting with OT01–OT06 and the
GCP source register already indexed in the bibliography:

- **HW01:** Google Cloud [service identity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/securing/service-identity),
  service/deployer identities, metadata access-token request and token types.
  Metadata returns the configured service identity; ID tokens and OAuth access
  tokens have different purposes. Google advises against setting a credential-file
  environment variable for Cloud Run service identity. Our fixed endpoint, bounds
  and rejection of ambient overrides are local application policy.
- **HW02:** Cloud SQL [IAM login](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/iam-logins)
  and [IAM users](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/add-manage-iam-users),
  automatic connector authentication and service-account SQL username suffix.
  Authentication does not create SQL privileges; separate owner bootstrap remains
  necessary. The two-connection cap is the project's bounded initial profile.
- **HW03:** Cloud Run [container contract](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/container-contract),
  listener binding, metadata server and shutdown sections. The container uses an
  explicit public bind argument; standalone configuration defaults to loopback.
  Local host tests prove shutdown mechanics, not Cloud Run delivery behavior.

Pinned local `golang.org/x/oauth2/google` ComputeTokenSource and Cloud SQL connector
remain the existing metadata-only transport implementation. Reusing these and the
reviewed worker host avoids a second SQL connector or invented OIDC verifier.

This configuration is an internal control-plane contract, not a financial ISO 20022
message. Existing standards applicability and source-data currency profiles remain
unchanged. Hosted qualification, secret-version mappings and durable raw evidence
acceptance are explicit additional gates, recorded in the delivery runbook.

## Executable deployment profile

`cmd/worker` accepts only explicit publisher/consumer mode. Both require the Cloud
SQL instance and caller audience/email/numeric subject. Production CLI pins queue
`jayburd-dev-acquisition` in us-central1, publisher caller `jayburd-dev-scheduler`,
consumer caller/task invoker `jayburd-dev-task-invoker`, all in the instance project.
Consumer additionally requires `-project-number` and exact numeric GSM resources
for `jayburd-dev-bank-sync-client-id` and `jayburd-dev-bank-sync-client-secret`.
The project number is separately supplied by reviewed deployment configuration;
no ID/number alias fallback is performed. Registry bucket is PROJECT-jayburd-dev-credential-registry,
prefix provider-credentials-v1; evidence bucket is PROJECT-jayburd-dev-acquisition-evidence.
These constructors compose the concrete providersecrets resolver and cloudevidence
store. No plaintext secret flag or environment read exists.

Metadata IdentityToken also accepts canonical nonzero Infisical machine identity
UUIDs. **HW04:** [Infisical GCP auth](https://infisical.com/docs/documentation/platform/identities/gcp-auth),
ID-token guide/sample metadata request reviewed 2026-10-14: audience is the machine
identity ID, not an HTTPS service URL. Tests reject malformed UUIDs/newlines before
network access. This correction preserves the fixed Google metadata destination.

documents.title: Local managed identity rehearsal
documents.body:
# Local managed identity rehearsal

## Decision and boundary

Owner-authorized #39, 2026-10-12. A separate static browser entry reuses the
production AuthProvider, Firebase adapter, controller and LoginPanel. It contains
no Bookkeeping import, bridge, database connection or token display. The existing
Next.js application and deployment workflow do not gain a rehearsal route/mode.

The owner opens `http://127.0.0.1:39091` and supplies only the public Firebase web
API key. Project and auth domain are fixed to `jayburd-bookkeeping-dev` and its
firebaseapp.com domain. Configuration lives in browser memory. No environment
files or credentials are loaded; a missing/invalid key cannot initialize auth.
The shared provider accepts validated public configuration as an optional prop;
production continues fetching its existing runtime endpoint.

A Node static server binds only IPv4 loopback, validates Host and serves only
root HTML and compiled JS/CSS assets. It exposes no config mutation endpoint,
proxy, CORS, directory listing, source map or API routes. CSP limits browser
connections to the two Google identity endpoints; no remote scripts or frames.
Vite builds the separate entry with environment-file loading/public directory
copying disabled. Default tests use synthetic values and block external requests.
Alternative full local application would unnecessarily expose finance routes;
a custom auth implementation would drift from the production login flow.

## Owner proof and limits

The owner privately requests verification mail, opens Google's hosted link,
returns to check verification, signs in again, enrolls TOTP and completes a fresh
password/TOTP challenge. Record only redacted outcomes. Reload/signout clear memory;
provider errors stay generic. API-key HTTP-referrer restrictions must permit the
exact loopback origin if enabled; do not weaken API restrictions globally. This
email/password flow uses no OAuth redirect or custom continue URL; do not add
localhost to hosted redirect configuration without evidence it is needed.

This proves browser/provider behavior only. Revoked/deleted identity denial by
the Go verifier, SQL principal mapping, entity authorization, hosted TLS/Invoker,
link expiry/reuse and recovery require separate reviewed evidence before #6/#27
acceptance. Do not label the browser's MFA state as server authorization.
No ISO financial-message mapping applies; ledger contracts and SQL are unchanged.

## Acceptance

Named server tests cover loopback binding, Host/method/path denial and CSP.
Browser rehearsal tests block external traffic and prove missing/invalid settings,
production verification UI using synthetic provider responses, no finance request
and no persistent credentials. Existing web and Go suites remain required.
Sources BA04 in the browser source register; evidence belongs in the rehearsal
runbook. Actual email/TOTP outcomes are owner-only, not inferred from tests.

documents.title: Identity and controlled setup
documents.body:
# Identity and controlled setup

## Decision and scope

Implementation-review contract for #6, 2026-10-11. Use Google Identity Platform
and Firebase Admin Go SDK for managed end-user authentication. The SDK verifies
ID tokens with revocation checking on every request. Require TOTP MFA; bind exact
issuer and subject to an explicitly enrolled ledger principal, never email,
request actor IDs, tenant claims or custom permission claims. No automatic signup.
Application tests remain synthetic. Provider configuration is owned by the
[isolated identity root](../../infra/gcp/identity/README.md); actual setup and
remaining live proof belong in the [runbook](../runbooks/identity-setup.md).

Sources and alternatives are recorded in [identity sources](../research/identity-sources.md).
Self-managed passwords would add recovery and credential-storage responsibility;
a generic JWT verifier would still need provider revocation and lifecycle work.
The official SDK is selected despite its larger dependency graph.

## Authentication boundary

Only bearer ID tokens are accepted. The adapter requires an explicitly supplied
Admin client and project ID; it never loads credentials. The caller must construct that client without emulator mode; the SDK retains
its initialization mode. The adapter also rejects emulator environment presence
at construction and on each request.
Check SDK verification, issuer, audience, subject, expiry, issued/authentication
times, non-tenant scope and `firebase.sign_in_second_factor=totp` before mapping.
Verification/mapping has a five-second deadline and fails closed without logging
tokens or SDK errors. Provider revocation is checked at request time, not atomically
with database commit. Database principal/membership disabling still serializes
with posting. Queued work must reauthorize at execution; no worker is implemented.

Browser composition uses an explicit HTTPS origin. Reject foreign/opaque/duplicate
Origin headers and cross-site Fetch Metadata. Cookies confer no authority; no
cookie/session endpoint or permissive CORS is added. Future cookie-based UI sessions
require a separately reviewed CSRF/session contract. A bearer-token client must
not persist tokens in localStorage. TLS, redacted access logs, rate limits, SDK
workload identity/IAM and MFA enrollment/recovery require deployment evidence.

## Enrollment and setup SQL

Forward migration 000003 adds a distinct NOLOGIN `bookkeeping_identity_operator`
role. It may enroll an issuer/subject through `ledger.enroll_principal`, but may
not perform table DML or accounting operations. Runtime cannot enroll users.
Enrollment records the database session identity and is retry-safe for the same
issuer/subject; disabled identities cannot be silently reactivated.

`ledger.resolve_principal(issuer,subject)` exposes only an active mapped UUID.
The trusted Go adapter alone supplies these verified values. The runtime database
identity is a trusted service boundary, not a credential issued to end users.

`POST /v1/setup` creates one entity, book, policy, open period and 2–100 accounts
in a single serializable transaction for an enrolled user. It grants that creator
read/post permissions only. Existing entities cannot be claimed or modified here.
Body fields: `entity_name`, `entity_kind` (legal/personal), `book_name`,
`starts_on`, `ends_before`, `functional_currency_version_id`, `accounts`.
Each account has `code`, `name`, `category`, `normal_side`, `monetary`.
IDs are server-generated; no actor, membership, initial balance or journal input.
Development policy remains ADR 0005: accrual, UTC, USD/2, half-even, synthetic spot.
This restriction concerns functional policy; existing foreign transaction currency
support remains. Reference currencies are installed separately by the operator.

Require Idempotency-Key; scope is principal + setup operation. Strict unique-key
JSON, bounded text and arrays; array order remains meaningful. Canonical equality
uses validated jsonb with normalized currency UUID. Successful replay returns the
original 201 response only while principal/entity/read/post grants remain active.
Atomic immutable setup receipt/audit includes creator, request ID and result IDs;
setup has no asynchronous consumer and emits no speculative outbox event.
Unknown commit returns 503; retry the identical key/body. Invalid input is 400,
unsupported policy 422, conflicting key 409, disabled/inaccessible scope 404.

## Standards applicability and acceptance

These identity/setup operations are internal application controls, not ISO 20022
financial exchanges. Currency metadata references ISO 4217 under the existing
[standards contract](standards.md); no ISO designation or audit export is claimed.

`TestIdentityBoundary` covers MFA, issuer/audience/time/scope, provider rejection,
missing/deleted/disabled mappings and safe failures. `TestBrowserBoundary` covers
origin/cookie behavior. `TestControlledSetup` covers real-role enrollment limits,
atomic creation, posting from returned IDs, replay/conflict, invalid bundles,
revocation and rollback. `TestSetupConcurrentReplay`, `TestSetupCommitAcknowledgementLoss` and
`TestSetupRevocationRace` exercise real transaction failures/locks.
Existing ledger authorization/concurrency tests remain
required. Live provider verification and browser login are release gates, not
replaced by SDK-boundary test doubles.

documents.title: Development image delivery
documents.body:
# Development image delivery

## Decision and scope

Issue #27 first implementation slice, 2026-10-11: owner-triggered, main-only
publication of tested API, migrator, worker and standalone Next.js images. No deployment
is coupled to publication. Sources G14–G16 in the [register](../research/gcp-sources.md)
support the packaging, metadata and authentication choices; live federation is unverified.

The build workflow reuses Seed validation before building linux/amd64 candidates.
Each image is built once, tested by its local content ID, scanned with pinned Trivy
for HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerabilities including unfixed findings, inventoried as
CycloneDX, then pushed without rebuilding. Buildx metadata records build provenance.
The receipt links commit, run/attempt, tested local content ID (configuration or manifest/index, depending on Docker store) and registry
manifest digest. Tests reject missing build evidence and mismatched identities.

Metadata is unsigned evidence, **not a signed attestation or SLSA conformance**.
Docker's load exporter does not retain image attestations. Keeping unsigned
build metadata is an explicit first-slice limitation; registry-first attested
publication would require a separately controlled quarantine/promotion path.
Do not use these receipts as an automated deployment authorization.

## Identity and ownership

The workflow accepts no arbitrary ref or shell input. Both its guard and existing
foundation WIF require owner actor ID 55423093, repository ID 1414515318, main and
workflow_dispatch; provider additionally pins owner ID and workflow path.
`GCP_PROJECT_ID` and `GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER` are public repository variables. Foundation
WIF stays disabled until owner review and explicit apply; this change does not
enable it. Registry writer is the builder's only cloud resource role.

Cloud authentication occurs after build/test/scan. The action creates no credential
file; a short-lived masked access token passes directly to Docker login. Docker
configuration is runner-temporary and excluded from all image contexts/artifacts.
No Terraform state, secret-manager access or runtime impersonation is involved.
Credential-free PR CI only builds/tests locally. Default commands never publish.

Tags include commit, run and attempt, compatible with immutable registry tags.
A failed matrix can leave a partial set of images; require the complete four-component build to succeed. The existing application
release validator still consumes its three API/migrator/web receipts; the worker
receipt is a separate candidate and does not authorize worker deployment. Failed publication
never grants rollout authority. Artifacts expire after 30 days; retain an approved
release receipt separately before this expiry. Old tagged candidates require a
reviewed retention policy; current cleanup only deletes old untagged images.

## Frontend boundary and next slice

Failed HIGH/CRITICAL scans retain only `receipts/vulnerabilities.json` in a
separate `rejected-scan-*` artifact for seven days. This vulnerability-only report
is diagnostic evidence, never a candidate receipt or release authorization. Later
authentication/publication steps stay skipped after scan failure. Missing reports
(for example scanner download failure) warn without changing the failed outcome.

The non-root/read-only standalone image includes traced runtime files and static
assets. The [runtime identity/private API bridge](private-api-bridge.md) now reads
operator-supplied public identifiers at request time and separates the frontend
service token from the user's bearer. An unconfigured image remains unavailable.
No identity identifiers or backend destination are baked into its build.
Runtime excludes npm/Yarn and requires patched OpenSSL packages; the builder
retains npm for locked installation. APK patch resolution may advance, so release
authority binds the final tested/scanned digest. See [source G28](../research/gcp-sources.md#g28--node-runtime-image-contents--2026-10-12).

The next deployment slice must wire runtime settings and the API Invoker grant,
then prove real IAM/MFA behavior. Candidate receipts remain non-deployable until
migration/rollout and cloud acceptance are reviewed; a passing bridge test does
not approve publication or establish real authentication.

No financial message or SQL contract changes; existing ISO assessments remain
applicable. Acceptance: receipt integrity tests and isolated runtime proofs run
in CI. Actual registry publication, IAM denial, real MFA, Infisical acceptance,
serialized migration/rollout and compatible rollback remain #27 release gates.

## Acquisition worker candidate

`Dockerfile.worker` has an explicit allowlisted build context and a non-root scratch
runtime. Its isolated container proof checks fail-closed startup without any cloud
network. Real managed startup still needs reviewed metadata, Cloud SQL role grants,
private callers and exact provider-store versions. The owner-operated workers root
owns initial infrastructure; the application deployment identity receives no new
bootstrap/secret authority. Automated worker promotion is not implemented here.

documents.title: Synthetic import service orchestration
documents.body:
# Synthetic import service orchestration

## Boundary

Issue #93 under #8. Coordinator reviewed the Service/SQLRepository separation
before implementation. This local adapter connects the existing private staging
and strict decoder to the durable SQL import boundary. It creates no journals,
executes no import command automatically, and introduces no HTTP endpoint, cloud
object store or provider acquisition. Explicit import confirmation uses the existing
interactive command recovery gate; the service does not provide a bypass.

## API and SQL boundary

`New(Beginner, Storage)` composes caller-owned dependencies. `Register(ctx, Scope,
key, Registration)` registers profile/source/namespace/binding/date identity;
`Batch(ctx, Scope, batchID)` and `Review(ctx, Scope, reviewID)` read public scoped
wrappers. `Upload(ctx, Scope, batchID, staging.Source)` transfers source ownership,
stages and previews; `Preview(ctx, Scope, batchID)` reconciles existing retained
bytes. Upload/Preview use a 20-second overall context budget. No method accepts a
filesystem path, URL, caller digest or decoded row list.

The private repository calls exactly `banking.register_import_batch`,
`banking.import_context`, `banking.publish_import_preview`,
`banking.get_import_batch` and `banking.get_review_item`. All arguments use
parameter binding. Context contains SQL-generated object identity and approved
currency/date expectations; the service validates canonical UUIDs, bigint-string
revisions and decoder expectations before I/O. Registration returns private
service metadata, so it must not be exposed unchanged through a future public
HTTP route. Public Batch uses the separate SQL wrapper without object details.

Publication contains profile, server SHA256 and byte count, plus either complete
rows preserving amount/canonical_amount/currency_version_id or decoder diagnostics,
total and truncated. SQL independently checks the full shape and semantics.
An unknown publication result returns no preview. `Preview` explicitly retries
from retained exact bytes; successful SQL replay owns the stable preview identity.
Scope.Actor must come from verified identity in future composition, never a body.

SQL P2400/P2401/P2402/P2403/P2404 map to fixed invalid_request/not_found/
import_conflict/stale_preview/import_limit. Infrastructure/source errors retain no
cause text. Actual storage object_conflict maps to statement_identity_conflict;
missing/deleted evidence maps to evidence_unavailable. Durable decoder rejection
returns a successful rejected batch with bounded diagnostics, not an exception
containing rejected values.

## Ownership and transactions

The authenticated composition supplies a verified principal and entity/book scope.
These values are not credentials or evidence of permission: SQL checks current
membership and source grants on every call. SQL commits authorization and returns
server-owned batch/object/decoder metadata before any storage access. Input source
ownership transfers at Upload entry; denied/invalid requests still close it with
an independent one-second cleanup context. Once passed to staging.Put, staging
owns exactly one close. Sources must honor context in Read and Close; an arbitrary
blocked io.Reader is not made cancellable by an adapter or goroutine.

No SQL transaction spans storage, reading, or decoding. Private staging provides
immutable exact-byte equality on replay, including full-byte comparison rather
than hash-only identity. Only SQL-returned scoped UUIDs select an object; user
paths, URLs and user-supplied digests are never accepted. Bounded staged bytes are
decoded using SQL-returned expectations, then SQL independently reauthorizes and
publishes the complete preview or bounded diagnostics atomically. Decoding failure
has no usable partial rows. Preview alone creates no source observations/review
items or journal; explicit import is separate.

Each SQL call has a four-second active budget, three-second statement timeout,
one-second lock timeout and four-second idle-transaction timeout. The independent
one-second cleanup budget preserves the five-second transaction bound. Only 40001/40P01 confirmed
rollback outcomes retry the complete transaction, at most three attempts with
bounded jitter. Cleanup always uses an independent one-second context. Response
JSON is capped at 2 MiB. Unknown COMMIT suppresses result and automatic replay;
return `commit_unknown`, then reconcile using the same batch/statement identity.
SQLSTATE 08007/40003 are explicitly ambiguous. Storage publication can similarly
be uncertain: no compensating delete is attempted because published evidence
may already be referenced by a committed or uncertain preview.

## Sources and applicability

This continues the reviewed mechanisms and alternatives in
[durable import](durable-import.md) (DI01–DI02),
[private staging](import-staging.md) (ST01–ST03),
[strict decoding](statement-decoder.md) (SI01–SI06), and
[observer runtime](observer-runtime.md) (OR01: PostgreSQL17 error-code table).
The review covers the cited selected sections and existing implementations, not
additional normative standards text. Internal synthetic CSV remains the recorded
standards exception; ISO4217 reference currency IDs retain their meaning. This
service is not an ISO20022 financial message or a conformance implementation.

## Validation status

Implementation and fault evidence are recorded in the
[living runbook](../runbooks/import-service.md). Hosted encryption, retention
cleanup, real ownership/provider qualification and HTTP upload composition remain
separate acceptance gates.

documents.title: Synthetic durable import SQL
documents.body:
# Synthetic durable import SQL

## Decision and boundary

Migration 10 implements the reviewed SQL subset of [durable import](durable-import.md)
for #92 under #8/#84/#85. Registration and preview create no observations. An explicit
`import` interactive command atomically creates immutable source evidence and
uncategorized review items. It creates no journal, line, posting receipt, outbox
message, valuation, reconciliation or book revision change. Go owns verified actor
identity, private byte storage, strict CSV decoding and transaction retries.

Coordinator reviewed signatures and publication trust before implementation. The
API database login is a trusted backend boundary: it already supplies verified
actor IDs. Its narrow publication function accepts server-produced decoded rows;
there is **no public HTTP row-publication endpoint**. SQL independently validates
all row keys/types, ordinal/ID uniqueness, source/currency/date equality, original
amount grammar and exact canonical scale. SQL cannot prove bytes it cannot read:
Go must read back the immutable private object, compare exact bytes on retry and
invoke the strict decoder. A digest or caller-supplied row array is not that proof.

Only synthetic `jayburd-synthetic-statement-csv/1` is accepted. The public projection
profile is `durable-import-v1`. No provider worker, bank connection, automatic
posting or live-account authority is introduced.

## Physical contract and privileges

All new book-owned tables have `(entity_id,book_id,...)` primary/foreign keys,
NO ACTION history references and owner `bookkeeping_owner` (NOLOGIN). Migration1–9
remain unchanged. `banking.source_namespace` gains a composite source/namespace
unique key. Source revision becomes nonnegative; binding edits increment only
binding revision, confirmed imports increment only source revision. Existing
immutable mapping and terminal retirement remain enforced.

| Object | Grain and invariant |
| --- | --- |
| `banking.import_batch` | Unique scoped namespace/statement reference; immutable source, binding revision, interval, profile/parser, server object UUID, actor and expiry. Original complete publication JSON, digest and byte count cannot be replaced. State received/preview_ready/rejected/imported/cancelled; imported body and result persist together. |
| `integration.import_registration` | Immutable actor/scope/idempotency-key receipt naming exact metadata and batch. An independently keyed request for the same statement reuses the batch only when metadata agrees. |
| `banking.import_preview` | Immutable scoped batch/revision result with pinned source/binding revisions, validated rows or bounded rejection diagnostics, counts and timestamp. Latest revision is selected by descending revision. |
| `banking.source_observation` | Immutable scoped source/namespace/external-entry identity; unique also across entity/source/namespace/entry. Current revision is fixed at 1 in this profile and has a deferred FK to its immutable revision. |
| `banking.observation_revision` | Booked evidence: date, currency version, direction, positive exact `numeric(38,9)`, original amount lexeme, description and full canonical equality object. No pending, modified or removed profile yet. |
| `banking.import_row` | Immutable scoped batch/physical-record occurrence linked to observation revision, retaining original decoded fields and money lexeme even when an earlier file already supplied the observation. |
| `banking.review_item`, `review_decision`, `review_evidence`, `review_assignment` | Immutable first-profile projection and initialization decision. One assignment per observation. First namespace initializes needs_review; later overlapping namespaces initialize overlap_hold. No matching/drafting/posting transition is implemented. |

Runtime API receives EXECUTE only on the five new functions below and existing
`get_source`. Owner helpers, operator grants and every table remain inaccessible
to API/observer/publisher roles. Functions use a fixed trusted search path. Existing
setup/post command permissions and worker boundaries are preserved.

`ledger.membership` explicitly permits new `import` authority. Operator-only
`banking.set_source_import_permission(actor,e,b,source,key,raw)` accepts exactly
`{expected_binding_revision,principal_id,enabled,entity_import_enabled}`. Revisions
are canonical decimal strings; booleans independently attest source and entity
import grants. Existing entity/source read grants are not created implicitly.
The function requires explicit owner role, current active approving principal and
entity read, active grantee/read membership for any grant, and a matching binding
revision. Pure revocation can remove dormant grants for disabled/revoked readers.
Receipt records authenticated `session_user` separately from attested `approved_by`.
No self-grant through an API function or initial book setup exists. Changing entity
import authority affects all sources in that entity; source grants remain separate.

Import mutations require SERIALIZABLE and current entity **read+import** and source
**read+import**, including replay, pending discovery, cancel and acknowledgement.
Public history reads require current entity/source read under REPEATABLE READ or
SERIALIZABLE. Authorization serializes with principal/entity/membership/book/source
grant changes; command operations take the strongest principal lock first. The book
lock serializes writes without changing its financial revision. Source locks serialize
namespaces and deduplication. All I/O occurs outside SQL transactions.

## Exact service functions

Every function returns `jsonb`; IDs are UUIDs, money/revisions/counts strings.
`actor,e,b` are UUID arguments supplied by trusted server identity and route scope.

| Function | Exact boundary |
| --- | --- |
| `banking.register_import_batch(actor,e,b,key text,raw text)` | Body `{source_account_id,namespace_id,binding_revision,statement_ref,starts_on,ends_before,profile}`; returns service context. Metadata/key <=8 KiB/128 ASCII characters. Existing receipt reauthorized before replay. |
| `banking.import_context(actor,e,b,batch uuid)` | Requires import authority. Returns public batch fields plus decoder profile, opaque object_id, source_account_ref, starts_on, ends_before, and currency `{code,version_id,minor_unit,valid_from,valid_to}`; absent currency upper bound is empty string. Cancelled/expired/unavailable unimported data is denied before storage I/O. Received/preview_ready additionally require active source/namespace and unchanged binding. Imported exact replay retains current authorization but does not require current active/pinned state. |
| `banking.publish_import_preview(actor,e,b,batch uuid,raw text)` | Trusted service only. Success input `{profile,sha256,byte_count,rows}`; rejection input `{profile,sha256,byte_count,diagnostics,total,truncated}`. Returns public batch. SQL-owned source metadata rechecked; complete publication equality checked on retry, even if hashes agree. |
| `banking.get_import_batch(actor,e,b,batch uuid)` | Read-authorized public projection, no private object reference or bytes. |
| `banking.get_review_item(actor,e,b,review uuid)` | Read-authorized first-profile review and immutable evidence projection. No write authority. |

Success rows are exactly `{record,source_account_ref,entry_id,booked_on,currency,
direction,amount,description,canonical_amount,currency_version_id}`. `record` and
`byte_count` are bounded JSON integers; `amount` retains the decoder lexeme and
`canonical_amount` is its exact decimal normalization, never float or rounded.
Records are 2..1001 in order, IDs follow the decoder ASCII grammar, descriptions
are 1..500 printable ASCII characters. Dates must be real Gregorian full dates
inside both batch interval and pinned currency validity. Significant fractional
scale cannot exceed pinned minor units; JPY zero and KWD three are supported.
At most 1000 rows, 1 MiB stored bytes and 2 MiB publication JSON; row-limit failure
is atomic. Rejection diagnostics are exactly `{code,record,field}`, using fixed
decoder codes, at most 100 retained entries and 10000 counted detections. SQL adds
`source_correction_required` when an existing observation differs materially.

Public batch contains profile, batch/source/namespace IDs, state, binding/source
revision, preview_id/revision, created_count/existing_count (null before preview),
diagnostics/error_count/truncated, raw_available, created_at/expires_at, and nested
`preview` (null or `{preview_id,preview_revision,binding_revision,source_revision,
created_count,existing_count}`). Top-level source_revision is current; **confirm
using the nested preview's pinned revisions**, not a newly observed top-level value.
`raw_available` means metadata published and no recorded deletion, not proof that
an object is physically retrievable. No raw URL/path is returned.

The bounded review projection contains profile, review/source IDs, state,
review/source/binding revisions, created_at, null draft_id/journal_id, blockers and
evidence. Each evidence entry contains observation/revision/namespace IDs,
external_entry_id, source_state, booked_date, currency_version_id, direction,
canonical amount and description. The broader parent contract's updated_at,
adapter/raw availability fields, pagination and mutable review operations remain
unimplemented; this SQL projection is not the final public review API.

Fixed SQL errors: P2400 malformed input; P2401 uniformly denied/inaccessible scope;
P2402 identity/state conflict; P2403 stale binding/preview/source; P2404 bound or
revision exhaustion. No source field appears in error messages. Invalid decoder
files and source correction conflicts publish a successful rejected batch with
safe diagnostics rather than partially importing rows.

## Confirmation, replay and stale work

Existing `ledger.register_command` accepts operation `import`, non-null entity/book,
and body exactly `{batch_id,preview_id,preview_revision,binding_revision,
source_revision,profile}`. Existing execute/cancel/acknowledge calls still take `{}`.
The one-unacknowledged-principal gate covers setup/post/import together. Its
immutable command body, terminal result and action audit supply operation receipt
and recovery: no separate immediate-import function is granted to runtime.

First execution checks current active source/namespace, latest preview, exact pins,
expiry and all canonical existing-row values. One transaction creates every new
observation/revision, every provenance link, every initialization decision/group,
one source revision increment, imported batch result and committed command/audit.
Even a provenance-only batch increments source revision because durable evidence
changed. Result is `{entity_id,book_id,batch_id,created_count,existing_count,
source_revision}` with counts/revision strings. An existing committed command
returns its exact result after current authorization and before mutable checks.
A new command targeting an already imported batch requires the original exact body
and returns that result without additional effects.

Same statement/metadata returns the same object reference; private storage compares
actual bytes. New files with canonical-equal source IDs create provenance only.
Canonical equality excludes only physical record position and original amount
lexeme; all remaining decoded fields, exact amount and currency version compare.
Different IDs with identical purchases remain different observations. A changed
existing ID rejects the **whole batch**, including otherwise valid new rows; changing
statement_ref does not authorize correction. A new namespace preserves both source
identities and places new evidence into overlap_hold, never similarity auto-match.

Source revision changes require publishing the same immutable decoded evidence
again to create a new preview revision, then explicit new confirmation. Binding
revision belongs to immutable registration metadata: grant, namespace or state
changes require a newly registered statement/batch with current binding, not silent
repinning of an old batch. Authenticated read history remains available.

Reviewed cancellation refinement: a prepared command always becomes terminal
cancelled; it cancels its batch only if its pinned preview UUID is still latest.
If refresh won first, cancelling/acknowledging the obsolete command preserves the
new preview for explicitly registered confirmation. If cancellation of the current
preview won first, the batch is terminal and later publication fails. Executing any
cancelled command fails. A committed batch cannot be cancelled. Source/book locks
and SERIALIZABLE retries establish these orderings without crossing object I/O.

Unknown commit must recover the same command; retry only whole transactions for
serialization/deadlock within the caller's bounded retry budget. Do not recreate
keys or repeat object side effects inside a SQL retry.

## Sources, alternatives and open gates

Standards applicability follows [STD-01](standards.md), [decoder](statement-decoder.md)
and [SI01–SI06](../research/statement-import-sources.md). This internal synthetic
profile is not an ISO 20022 financial exchange. Currency identifiers/versioned
minor units use the reviewed ISO 4217 mapping; Gregorian dates follow the existing
ISO 8601/RFC 3339 usage profile. No ISO conformance or accounting-framework approval
is claimed. Source units are preserved without inventing FX or posting policy.

Reviewed 2026-10-13: PostgreSQL17 [§5.5 keys/foreign keys](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/ddl-constraints.html),
[§13.2.2–3 isolation and full transaction retry](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/transaction-iso.html),
and [CREATE FUNCTION, SECURITY DEFINER/search_path/privileges](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-createfunction.html).
These primary sections corroborate scoped declarative constraints, snapshot/locking
behavior and restricted owned functions (existing DI01/database source records).
Inference: immutable evidence plus source revision pins is sufficient here; a
second event store is unnecessary. Hash-only identity, similarity deduplication
and immediate import-to-journal were rejected because they lose evidence or bypass
review. Exact SQL money validation complements the existing Go decimal-string
normalizer; SQL does not duplicate the CSV byte parser. Source documents were read
in selected sections only; no additional normative ISO text was acquired.

Evidence and exact commands are in the [living runbook](../runbooks/import-sql.md).
Retention metadata persists but no cleanup/tombstone reconciler is implemented.
Seven-day unconfirmed expiry is an execution gate, not deletion. Hosted encrypted
storage, raw retention/holds, provider acquisition/corrections, review decisions,
source-to-draft/post, reconciliation and live approval remain separate gates.

documents.title: Private synthetic import staging
documents.body:
# Private synthetic import staging

## Decision and API

Implemented root-reviewed local foundation for #82 under #8/#55. This adapter stores synthetic
exact bytes only; no decoder, SQL publication, authorization, upload endpoint or
UI is added. Durable-import/statement-decoder contracts remain authority for
future integration. STD-01 synthetic internal CSV assessment is unchanged; no
financial exchange or ISO-conformance claim.

`Open(existingRoot)` requires an owner-created private 0700 directory on local
Linux/macOS storage. `NewReference(Scope{EntityID,BookID})` generates a random
object UUID; all three IDs must be canonical lowercase nonzero UUIDs. Only this
server reference reaches `Put(ctx,Ref,Source)`, `Read(ctx,Ref)` and `Delete(ctx,Ref)`.
Identifiers are not authorization: the future authenticated caller must check
current scope before every operation. There are no caller filenames or URLs.
Receipts contain the reference, byte count and server-computed SHA-256. Read
returns a bounded copy and receipt; it never exposes a path or long-lived handle.

Source owns `Read(context.Context, []byte)` and `Close(context.Context)`. Put
accepts ownership and closes it exactly once, including invalid/cancelled input.
Source implementations must honor the read context and bounded close context.
The adapter cannot cancel an arbitrary blocking io.Reader or uncooperative source;
it does not hide a blocked read in a goroutine. Operations use a 15s deadline,
1MiB plus one sentinel, zero-byte rejection and bounded cleanup. Regular local
filesystem calls/fsync themselves are not context-interruptible; deadline checks
bound admission/progression, not a hung kernel/filesystem call.

## Publication, replay and deletion

Flat names contain only validated scope/object IDs or generated temporary IDs.
os.Root confines operations; nofollow opens, regular-file/owner/mode checks and
0700/0600 permissions reject unsafe entries. Per-object nonblocking flock serializes
cooperating Store instances/processes with context-aware waiting. Uploaded temporary
bytes are private and not a published object. Fsync file then close, acquire lock,
check tombstone and existing exact bytes, hard-link without replacement, then fsync
directory. Existing bytes must compare in full even if digests match. Failed/unknown
publication never returns a receipt; retry reconciles the same reference.

Delete publishes and fsyncs a permanent zero-byte tombstone before removing raw
bytes and syncing the directory. It also tombstones missing references, preventing
late publication after cancellation. Repeated deletion converges; Put cannot reuse
a deleted identity. Reads under the same lock honor the tombstone. Already returned
byte copies cannot be revoked. Tombstones/lock metadata persist; this is not secure
erasure or hosted retention approval. Crashed temp files remain private orphans;
retention sweeps and encrypted Cloud Storage remain separate work.

A cancellation observed before publication leaves no visible object. Once link or
tombstone publication begins, later failure/cancellation is `storage_unknown`:
retry/reconcile, never assume nothing happened. All errors are fixed codes and
contain no paths, payload values, reader errors or raw filesystem diagnostics.

## Sources, alternatives and limits

Reviewed selected mechanisms on 2026-10-13:

- **ST01 — Go Authors, Go1.26.9 `src/os/root.go` and File.Sync implementation**:
  local pinned toolchain source, Root/OpenRoot/OpenFile/Link/Lstat and Sync comments.
  [Public os reference](https://pkg.go.dev/os#Root) corroborates confinement and
  warns Root follows in-root symlinks and does not block mounts/devices. The public
  page served a newer version; pinned local source owns implementation assumptions.
  We add nofollow/type checks and exclude hostile same-UID/admin mutation, mounts,
  network filesystems and unsupported platforms from this local adapter's boundary.
- **ST02 — Linux man-pages6.19**, [link(2), DESCRIPTION/ERRORS/BUGS](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/link.2.html),
  [fsync(2), DESCRIPTION](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/fsync.2.html):
  hard links do not replace existing names; syncing file data alone does not
  guarantee directory-entry persistence. Inference: same-directory no-replace
  publication plus directory sync, explicit uncertainty on failure. These calls
  are not tested hardware/power-loss guarantees; network filesystems are excluded.
- **ST03 — Linux man-pages6.19**, [flock(2), DESCRIPTION/NOTES](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/flock.2.html):
  advisory locks and nonblocking contention support cooperating-process exclusion.
  Inference: immutable lock files, never unlink locks while the store exists;
  unsafe writers/admins are not contained by advisory locking.

Rename can replace existing evidence; a check-then-rename race is unacceptable.
A database blob would simplify metadata atomicity but changes the reviewed storage
boundary. Hash-only replay cannot prove exact equality. A cross-platform unsafe
fallback would weaken pathname/locking guarantees, so unsupported systems fail
closed. Synthetic concurrency, process-exit/fault retry, cancellation, bounds, redaction
and tombstone evidence is recorded in the [living runbook](../runbooks/import-staging.md).

documents.title: Investigate: owned status and handoff proposal
documents.body:
# Investigate: owned status and handoff proposal

## Decision record

**Question and scope:** Issue #255 asks for one focused place to resume unresolved
bookkeeping work. This document proposes a read and handoff boundary, not a new
queue, posting authority, navigation position or aggregate status API. **Status:**
proposed for owner/coordinator review, 2026-10-21. The existing [command recovery](command-recovery.md),
[source review](source-review-sql.md), [connection status](connection-status-ui.md)
and [reporting HTTP](reporting-http.md) contracts own their respective facts.
The selected entity/book must come from verified, currently authorized scope.

The alternative is a single cross-source `attention_count` assembled in the
browser. Reject it for the first slice: source review requires a source selector
