and pagination, command recovery is principal-wide, connection status is read
per stream, and report failures are transient. Adding those values would silently
change their scopes and would make a missing source look like zero. A future
server-owned index needs a separate reviewed API/SQL contract and proof that each
source is complete, current and authorized.

## Source inventory

| Work kind | Authoritative read and scope | Action owner and resolved state | First-slice treatment / gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Source review | `GET /v1/entities/{e}/books/{b}/sources`, then `GET .../review-items?source_account_id=...&state=...&limit=...&cursor=...`. Source and review permissions are checked on each read. A review page pins `source_revision`; `needs_review`, `overlap_hold`, `draft_ready`, `correction_hold` and `posted` are distinct. | Existing review detail/category/draft and recoverable `source_post` flow. Only explicit reviewed command execution posts; `posted` has immutable journal evidence. Holds are not category-ready work. | Show a chosen, authorized source's unresolved rows, with its own filter/revision and pagination. Source-list overflow, a failed page, or unread sources prevent any book-wide empty claim. `correction_hold` requires the current source-review implementation contract and must not be mapped to an ordinary draft action. |
| Unacknowledged command | `GET /v1/commands/pending` is principal-wide and reauthorizes operation-specific scope. `null` means no command on that principal gate; a returned command may target another book. | Existing execute/cancel/acknowledge; terminal `committed` or `cancelled` remains pending until explicit acknowledgement. Inaccessible work uses payload-free `/pending/clear` only under its contract. | Show only a command whose returned target matches the selected book and whose current payload is authorized. A command for another book is not this book’s item; its principal-wide gate may still block new work. Do not expose its body through a cross-book summary. |
| Enrollment attempt | `GET .../connection-attempts?limit=100&before=...` is actor/book-scoped and gives server-owned `unfinished_count` for attempts. Exact attempt detail rechecks authority. Expired unclaimed, claimed uncertainty and expired binding review differ. | Connections owns completion, inspection, reconciliation, binding and guarded abandonment. Active/disconnected/abandoned or server-qualified expiry changes the attempt state; a UI read cannot infer a provider result. | Display its own status and count only if the optional connection service is composed and discovery completes. Do not call `unfinished_count` an Investigate total. A link-ready attempt is not a connected account. |
| Stream acquisition | `GET .../connections` selects an authorized stream; `GET .../connections/streams/{stream}/status` reads one exact stream. Requested/completed generations, readiness, local publication time, queue/lease and fixed `last_error` are distinct. `provider_updated_at` can be null. | Connections owns pause/resume/request, with current pins, confirmation and exact-key uncertain-result recovery. A request only queues intent; complete publication is not a posted balance. | A selected stream can be investigated. No book-wide health count or generic retry is derivable from one-stream reads. `last_error` null does not mean complete history. |
| Report/read failure | The corresponding scoped report or pinned journal GET owns revision, authorization and error. No durable report-error list is defined. | Retry the same scoped read after a 503, refresh/reselect after 409, or leave the view on denial. Reports and Ledger retain their own direct tool access. | Contextual handoff only while the failed operation is in memory. Do not manufacture a persistent issue, count or resolved record. |
| All Transactions | Issue #242 remains open and blocked by #238/#239 plus a scoped API contract. | No owner taxonomy or cross-book queue action is approved here. | No cross-book or unassigned history in the first Investigate slice. |

The current UI does not receive a reliable book-wide status snapshot. In
particular, `No known items` is truthful only for a named, fully read scope (for
example, the selected source and filter after its page chain reaches the end).
It is not a default screen heading or a synonym for successful Position loading.

## Handoff and presentation boundary

Position or Ledger may pass an **in-memory intent**: canonical selected entity and
book IDs, observation date, optional book/report revision, optional account ID or
source ID, and the originating tool. A display label, monetary amount or badge
from the caller is never status authority. Investigate validates identifiers and
reads its owning source after entry; it may discard an unsupported hint. A stale
pin triggers a fresh scoped read and an explicit `Changed since you opened it`
message, never an action against the old pin. Returning to the origin restores its
selected book/date/selection where still authorized, then that tool refreshes its
own evidence. No financial request, token or intent enters URL, browser storage
or telemetry.

Investigate uses one source and one task at a time. The user chooses **Review
source**, **Recover command**, or **Check connection**; contextual report errors
stay with the originating tool. These are candidate tasks, not a required top
navigation arrangement. Ledger and Reports remain directly available as focused
tools. The selected book/date/currency and source freshness remain visible while
working; amounts stay exact decimal strings with source currency and no client FX.

Each read surface has four separate outcomes: `Still loading` before an answer;
`No known items` only after a complete authorized read for that named scope;
`Status unavailable` for absent optional service, transport failure, truncated
or malformed/incomplete data; and `Permission denied` when current authorization
fails. A stale 409 is `Changed since you opened it` and requires refresh before
action. A 404 that can hide another principal's resource never reveals whether
that resource exists. Late responses from an old book/source selection are
discarded. An item without a currently supported action remains inspectable
with its owner and reason; it gets no speculative button.

## Standards, sources and limits

This is an internal status/navigation contract, not a bank financial exchange or
an ISO 20022 message. Existing Plaid exchange mappings and ISO 4217 currency
version/source-date validation stay with their owners. No new monetary field,
audit export, ISO message version or accounting policy is selected. ISO 21378:2019
and ISO 21926:2026 are relevant when audit export/semantic mapping is designed;
their public abstracts/previews do not establish this screen's field-level
conformance. See [standards](standards.md) and the [source review](../research/investigate-sources.md).

Facts above are from the reviewed local contracts and route implementation.
Inference: composition must preserve those scopes and cannot derive a global
empty/ready conclusion. Remaining decisions: whether a server-owned index is
worth adding, its completeness/freshness contract, and owner review of the exact
task vocabulary. #104 owns connection behavior; #242 owns cross-book transaction
taxonomy; #248 owns Position snapshot semantics. None is completed by this design.

## Acceptance evidence for an implementation issue

Use fixed synthetic examples in the [runbook](../runbooks/investigate-contract.md).
Named browser cases should prove one actionable source item, empty selected
source, unavailable connection runtime, denied book, stale source/pin, cross-book
command and handoff/back navigation at 390px and keyboard width. API/SQL tests
must prove current permissions, pagination/completeness and no leaked payload.
For any changed browser/API boundary run `make web-check web-test web-build
web-browser app-integration` plus `make check test build`; for migrations or
ledger mutations add their required database gates. This proposal itself does
not satisfy those implementation tests.

documents.title: First ledger SQL contract
documents.body:
# First ledger SQL contract

## Decision and scope

JB-002 physical/transaction specification. Migrations 000001/000002 now implement
the synthetic manual posting subset; see [evidence](../runbooks/posting-proof.md). The first manual
posting target is finalized for implementation review in [posting boundary](posting-boundary.md)
and [ADR 0005](../decisions/0005-development-accounting-policy.md); their narrowed
scope and decisions supersede earlier proposals below. Broader close/FX workflows
remain gated. Accepted namespace direction is [ADR 0004](../decisions/0004-schema-ownership.md).
The first proof uses controlled synthetic book/account setup and supports manual
identity/spot journal posting, exact reversal and authorized reads. Period close
remains a later workflow; closed-state rejection is required immediately. Position accounting,
provider import and reconciliation are logical contracts below, not complete
physical schemas. [Money rules](multicurrency.md) and [scenarios](accounting-scenarios.md)
are prerequisites. An API cannot bypass these requirements.

Select a narrow database function boundary over granting API roles table DML.
Go validates transport/identity and orchestrates one transaction; owned database
functions enforce durable invariants. Alternatives: Go with deferred triggers
requires broader write privileges and a proven complete mutation protocol; raw
row CHECKs cannot enforce full-journal balance. Evidence: S07/S08/S11/S12 in the
[source register](../research/database-sources.md). The selected design still requires privilege and concurrency tests before
claiming implemented enforcement.

## Model and scope keys

An entity has memberships and books; each book has policy revisions, accounts,
periods and posted journals; each journal has at least two lines. A line references
an account and journal in the same entity/book. Books support separate reporting
bases but this slice does not automatically maintain parallel books.
Currency/rate reference data is shared; source observations never become ledger
entries without an authorized posting operation.

For every book-owned row, use `(entity_id, book_id, <row_id>)` as the primary key
and preserve those columns in every foreign key. Book key is `(entity_id, book_id)`;
entity key is `entity_id`. Globally generated UUIDs do not replace scope constraints.
Unique business keys include entity/book. No cross-entity journal or implicit
cross-book line. All foreign keys use RESTRICT/NO ACTION, never deletion cascades
into financial history. Use ordinary exact text codes with CHECKs initially,
not PostgreSQL enums that complicate later vocabulary changes.

## Column dictionary

All columns below are NOT NULL with no default unless marked `?` (nullable) or
`= value` (default). IDs are `uuid`, minted server-side. `instant` means
`timestamptz`; `money` means the proposed validated `numeric(38,9)` domain;
`rate` means validated `numeric(38,18)`. Codes are `text` with explicit checks;
no float types. Exact request inputs must be checked before typmod coercion.
The first migrations implement amount/rate domains; input text is validated
before typmod coercion. Tables for future adjacent workflows remain contracts.

| Table / row grain | Columns beyond the scope key | Keys, checks and lifecycle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ledger.entity` / legal or personal accounting owner | `entity_id uuid`, `name text`, `kind text`, `created_at instant`, `disabled_at instant?` | kind legal/personal; archive, no deletion of referenced owners |
| `ledger.principal` / trusted authenticated identity | `principal_id uuid`, `issuer text`, `subject text`, `disabled_at instant?`, `created_at instant` | Unique issuer/subject; subject is not an email lookup; never store bearer credentials |
| `ledger.membership` / entity permission for principal | `entity_id uuid`, `principal_id uuid`, `permission text`, `revoked_at instant?` | PK entity/principal/permission; permissions read/prepare/post/close; FKs entity/principal; regrant is audited |
| `ledger.book` / accounting book | scope key, `name text`, `revision bigint = 0`, `created_at instant`, `disabled_at instant?` | Unique entity/name; revision >= 0; explicit book row is serialization lock |
| `ledger.book_policy` / immutable approved policy revision | scope plus `policy_id uuid`, `effective_from date`, `effective_to date?`, `functional_currency_version_id uuid`, `basis text`, `timezone text`, `posting_scale smallint`, `rounding_mode text`, `rate_policy_code text`, `approved_by uuid`, `approved_at instant` | Unique book/effective_from; disjoint half-open intervals under book lock; approved complete policies only; timezone recognized; scale 0–9; basis/rounding/rate codes from reviewed policy; FK currency/principal |
| `ledger.account` / classification within book | scope plus `account_id uuid`, `code text`, `name text`, `category text`, `normal_side text`, `monetary boolean`, `active_from date`, `active_to date?` | Unique book/code; categories asset/liability/equity/revenue/expense; side debit/credit; dates half-open; semantic changes after use require new account or explicit migration contract |
| `ledger.period` / non-overlapping posting interval | scope plus `period_id uuid`, `starts_on date`, `ends_before date`, `state text = open`, `closed_at instant?`, `closed_by uuid?`, `close_revision bigint?` | starts < end; no overlap within book under setup/book lock; state open/closed; closed metadata all present iff closed; FK principal; never reopen by direct update |
| `ledger.journal_entry` / one committed journal | scope plus `journal_id uuid`, `period_id uuid`, `policy_id uuid`, `accounting_date date`, `kind text`, `description text`, `posted_at instant`, `posted_by uuid`, `book_revision bigint`, `reverses_journal_id uuid?`, `reason text?` | Kinds manual/reversal in first slice; FK same-book period/policy/reversed journal; reversal needs original+reason; unique book/reversed-journal for nonnull original; only posted rows, no mutable status; description 1–500 characters |
| `ledger.journal_line` / one side/amount/account | scope plus `journal_id uuid`, `line_number integer`, `account_id uuid`, `side text`, `transaction_currency_version_id uuid`, `transaction_amount money`, `functional_amount money`, `valuation_basis text`, `rate_observation_id uuid?` | PK scope/journal/line_number; FK same-book journal/account; line_number 1–1000; side debit/credit; positive amounts in first slice; basis identity/spot or carrying/functional_adjustment reserved for future operations; cross-field money checks per contract |
| `reference.currency` / one currency definition version | `currency_version_id uuid`, `alphabetic_code text`, `numeric_code text?`, `minor_unit smallint?`, `valid_from date`, `valid_to date?`, `source_release text` | Code `[A-Z]{3}`, numeric code three digits if assigned; unique code/valid_from; disjoint validity intervals; no assumed minor unit when absent; referenced versions immutable |
| `reference.rate_observation` / one immutable sourced quote | `rate_observation_id uuid`, `base_currency_version_id uuid`, `quote_currency_version_id uuid`, `quote_per_base rate`, `effective_at instant`, `observed_at instant`, `source text`, `source_reference text`, `purpose text`, `policy_code text`, `supersedes_id uuid?` | Currency/self FKs; positive finite rate; purpose spot/closing/valuation; provenance retained; ingestion identity unique source/source_reference; conflicting redelivery is reviewed, never overwritten |
| `integration.operation_receipt` / one successful command | scope plus `operation text`, `idempotency_key text`, `principal_id uuid`, `request_hash bytea`, `normalized_request jsonb`, `canonical_version smallint`, `result jsonb`, `http_status smallint`, `created_at instant` | PK scope/operation/key; key 1–128 safe ASCII; hash exactly 32 bytes; full normalized request equality is authoritative per posting boundary; result schema versioned; retain for book lifetime pending retention policy; no unsafe TTL that enables a duplicate financial effect |
| `audit.action` / one committed actor action | scope plus `action_id uuid`, `principal_id uuid`, `operation text`, `target_id uuid`, `book_revision bigint`, `request_id uuid`, `recorded_at instant`, `reason text?` | Append-only; no raw financial payloads/tokens in diagnostics; target checked by operation; external audit durability requires separate design |
| `integration.outbox_message` / durable committed notification intent | scope plus `message_id uuid`, `event_type text`, `event_version integer`, `target_id uuid`, `book_revision bigint`, `created_at instant` | Append-only financial intent with identifiers only; event type journal.posted/period.closed; future dispatch state is separate; creation alone does not implement delivery |

Journal reversal keeps original policy and valuations to preserve exact historical
amounts, but its accounting date belongs to a currently open period. If functional
currency changed, reject pending a currency-transition contract. The first slice
rejects reversal of a reversal and reversal of position-affecting entries until
their correction semantics are specified.

## Roles, grants and trusted identity

| Role | Allowed | Explicitly denied |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bookkeeping_owner` (NOLOGIN) | Own schemas, functions and tables | Runtime login/use by application |
| Migration identity | Controlled SET ROLE to owner during reviewed migrations | Application use or default CI access to live database |
| `bookkeeping_api` | Schema USAGE and EXECUTE on explicitly granted ledger/read operations | Schema CREATE, ownership, direct base-table SELECT/DML, role escalation |
| Future worker role | Only individually reviewed operation grants | Implicit API privileges or arbitrary actor impersonation |
| Human reporting identity | Reviewed entity-authorized reporting interface | Unrestricted shared reporting views/base tables |

Revoke PUBLIC CREATE on public and PUBLIC function execution where applicable;
set default privileges for the actual owner before function creation. Runtime
roles receive no inherited owner membership, superuser or BYPASSRLS. Use qualified
objects and trusted `search_path = pg_catalog, ledger, reference, integration,
audit, pg_temp` on privileged functions; none of these schemas is runtime-writable.
Revoke function EXECUTE from PUBLIC in the same migration transaction as creation.
See PostgreSQL function security S12; grant tests must include malicious temporary
objects and altered session search_path. Extensions need an explicit separate review.

The Go service is a trusted identity boundary: validate issuer, audience, expiry
and subject, map to principal, and pass trusted identity separately from JSON input.
A shared SQL role cannot prove which human is calling; these functions protect
against unchecked DML, not a fully compromised trusted service forging principals.
Every operation reloads current principal/membership state; no caller-set entity
session variable or RLS claim substitutes for identity. RLS is deferred pending
its own reviewed role policy; scoped read functions and composite keys are required.

## Transaction and lock protocol

All mutations use SERIALIZABLE. Lock in this order: principal FOR SHARE;
entity FOR SHARE; relevant membership FOR SHARE; book FOR UPDATE; existing receipt; period; affected
accounts in UUID order; original journal if needed. Revocation/archive updates the same
principal/entity/membership rows; book setup, account edits, posting and closing all take
the same book lock. Every change affecting posting/report interpretation or close
evidence (including configuration, reconciliation and valuation revisions) also
increments book revision; approval evidence records the revision it reviewed.
Thus revocation that wins blocks later work; work already
serialized before revocation may commit. Different books can progress independently.
No multi-book transaction is exposed in this slice. Close/post contention is a
measurable tradeoff: benchmark before replacing the simple lock protocol.

Retry SQLSTATE 40001/40P01 by rolling back and rerunning the entire transaction,
including current authorization, with bounded jitter: proposed maximum 3 attempts
within a 5-second request budget. Exhaustion returns a retryable 503; client reuses
its key. No external network work or irreversible side effects inside a transaction.
Timeout/disconnect after commit is resolved by the receipt, not a guessed failure.

### Post journal

1. Validate trusted actor, size/shape, decimal inputs and required idempotency key.
2. Begin transaction and take authorization/book locks. Reject disabled scope.
3. Resolve receipt before mutable period/account checks. Same actor, command and
   normalized request returns original status/body; different payload/actor conflicts.
   Recheck current permissions even on replay; do not leak old results after revocation.
4. For new work, validate expected book revision, one open period containing the
   accounting date, effective approved policy, account activity and currency/rate
   provenance. Book must have no unresolved configuration. Check full journal
   has 2–1000 lines and exact equality of functional debit/credit totals.
5. Increment book revision once; insert journal/lines, audit action, receipt and
   outbox intent. All succeed or all roll back. Return 201 only after COMMIT.

Payload normalization and receipt equality follow [canonical replay version 1](posting-boundary.md#canonical-replay-version-1).
SQL owns normalization, stored normalized-request comparison and diagnostic hash;
Go supplies original body text, never a trusted hash. Reject duplicate/unknown
JSON keys before jsonb conversion. Failed validation leaves no receipt; successful
keys never become reusable.

### Reverse journal

Same protocol and `expected_revision` semantics. Authorize post; copy original
lines with sides swapped and identical amounts/rate references; set original link
and supplied reason/date. Require open target period and active permitted accounts;
if an account is archived, use a separately reviewed correction instead of bypassing
activity checks. Unique reversal link prevents two full reversals with different
keys. Return new journal 201; original remains untouched. No generic DELETE/PATCH.

### Close period

Authorize close; same locks/receipt/revision protocol. The request identifies an
immutable reviewed close-evidence record covering reconciliation, outstanding
items, required adjustments, FX completion and report review. Close validates that
record belongs to this book/period and exact expected book revision. Caller boolean
`reconciled=true` is never evidence. Increment revision, mark closed and append
audit/receipt/outbox in one transaction; return 200 with period/revision. No new
posting into a closed period. Earlier open periods must be resolved before close.
A replay of a successful close returns its receipt; another key on a closed period
conflicts. A close-evidence physical contract is outstanding: endpoint remains
non-implementable until that dependency is accepted.

Period locking differs from fiscal-year closing entries for temporary accounts.
Annual closing/retained-earnings rules and reopening are separate pending contracts.

### Read/report

Authorize each request; use one repeatable-read transaction for a
multi-query response, so its lines/totals share one snapshot. Read principal/entity/membership
and book with FOR SHARE under the posting boundary's revocation ordering. This requires a READ WRITE
transaction even though the operation performs no business writes; PostgreSQL
READ ONLY does not permit these row locks. Apply the bounded retry policy. Journal reads return complete immutable data;
trial balance derives functional totals from posted lines, filters by book/date
and includes snapshot book revision and functional currency. Reversed originals
and reversals both contribute; do not filter originals away. Never convert report
currency opportunistically. Pagination uses deterministic accounting_date/journal_id
order and a cursor bound to scope/filter/snapshot; pagination contract is pending,
so a list endpoint is deliberately absent from this first interface.

## Adjacent workflow contracts and remaining physical work

| Operation | Required durable semantics before its own implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Import | Source account belongs to entity; immutable versioned observations, provider identity/checkpoint deduplication and provenance; corrected source cannot edit posted books |
| Reconcile | Statement identity, currency, balances and covered dates; scoped line allocations, unmatched items and explicit reviewed difference; match is not an automatic journal |
| FX remeasure | Versioned valuation batch, currency exposure positions, carrying-value deltas and unique operation identity; serialize against settlement/close |
| Settle | Position/allocation references, remaining quantity/carrying amount, fees and FX journal in one transaction; no over-allocation |
| Intercompany | Separate authorized journals linked by transfer identity; unmatched side visible; never claim atomic cross-book completion without a dedicated protocol |
| Export | Authorized immutable report snapshot and mapping/version manifest; apply ISO 21378/21926 assessment; no raw base-table dump |

These need complete dictionaries and API definitions next; reserving schema names
is not completion. Preserve [background delivery contract](background-work.md);
this slice only specifies atomic outbox intent, not a publisher/worker lifecycle.
ISO applicability for these identifier-only internal notifications: they describe
local journal/period commits, not banking interchange; no registered financial
message definition is claimed. Version the local event contract. If an adapter
later creates a bank-facing message, assess and validate its ISO profile separately.

## Queries, indexes, recovery and acceptance

Proposed indexes: journal `(entity_id, book_id, accounting_date, journal_id)` for
dated reads; line `(entity_id, book_id, account_id, journal_id)` for account history;
PKs/unique business keys cover scoped lookups and receipts; rate pair/effective time
supports rate selection. Record expected row counts and EXPLAIN on synthetic data
before optimizing. No benchmark or cardinality target has yet been approved.
Migrations use reviewed golang-migrate files; no live automatic down migrations.
Before cutover, prove backup/restore retains journals, reference versions, receipts
and outbox intent together, and replay cannot duplicate restored financial effects.

| Named future evidence | Acceptance |
| --- | --- |
| `TestSchemaPrivileges`, `TestEntityReferencesAndPrivileges` | Runtime DDL/DML, cross-entity/book references, forged request scope, revoked/disabled actors, search-path attacks denied |
| `TestPostingInvariants`, `TestMoneyInputBounds` | Empty/unbalanced/invalid amounts fail; identity/spot rules hold; failure at each write leaves no partial state |
| `TestPostingReplayConcurrency` | Concurrent same keys yield one entry; changed payload conflicts; reordered object keys replay; reordered lines conflict |
| `TestJournalCorrectionHistory` | Exact reversal, duplicate reversal conflict, original immutable and reports count both |
| `TestPostingCloseRace`, `TestRevocationRace` | Documented serialization orders hold; close evidence stale after any relevant change |
| `TestGoldenMonth`, `TestFXLifecycle` | Scenario arithmetic and reconciliations agree; no unsupported automated FX claim |
| `TestSchemaCompatibility`, `TestLedgerRestoreReplay` | Forward migration compatibility and restored idempotency/history proven |

Execution status is recorded in the posting proof runbook; full FX lifecycle
and live recovery/cutover remain future gates. ADR 0005 and the posting boundary select the synthetic development policy,
precision and enforcement target. A synthetic actor adapter does not approve a
production identity provider or real-LLC setup. Close, settlement,
reconciliation and full FX automation have additional explicitly stated gates.

documents.title: Migration-only development release
documents.body:
# Migration-only development release

## Decision

Add `operation: migrate` to the existing exact-hash deployment workflow. It applies
only the migration Terraform root, executes the dedicated job, validates its
immutable execution metadata and exits before runtime service changes. Owner
reviews the manifest and dispatch hash. The existing deployer identity and
concurrency group remain; no new federation trust or runtime privilege is added.

This resolves the ordering dependency: #26 needs migration evidence before full
application promotion can require #26 closed. Alternative owner-terminal migration
apply is possible, but would duplicate release validation and execution tracking.
This is infrastructure configuration, not a new ISO financial message or SQL policy.

For inspection without forward execution, use the separately defined
[read-only status release](migration-status.md); it preserves these release gates
but requires a status-capable image and a distinct operation/receipt.

## Contract

The migration manifest contains exactly schemaVersion, project, projectNumber,
operation, build, images, evidence and expiresAt. Keep all three same-build image
receipts; only images.migrate can execute. Evidence has bootstrap and compatibility
issue-comment links; no browser configuration or rollback field is accepted.
Hash, expiry, owner/main successful build and exact image checks remain unchanged.

Require foundation #5 closed and bootstrap PR #44 merged and ancestral to both
the workflow source and image source. Owner bootstrap evidence approves the SQL
preconditions. #26 remains open; #6/#11 are unrelated to this IAM-only job and
remain mandatory for promote/rollback. A migration-only manifest cannot reach
either service root or anonymous application smoke.

## Evidence and recovery

Selected execution metadata must match the approved digest, migrator account,
exact forward-only arguments, one task, zero retries and timeout. Require completed
success, one successful task, no failed/cancelled/running/retried tasks. Record only
execution identity, approved build/image and completion time. No environment, logs
or state is uploaded. A missing/mismatched receipt blocks acceptance even if SQL
may already have committed; investigate before rerunning. Never force or down.

Use explicit `[]` projections for container and condition array fields. TaskSpec
serializes its int64 timeout as a decimal string; accept exactly `"660"` or numeric
`660`, with no general coercion. Source G29 and the first real execution exposed
this distinction; [recovery evidence](../runbooks/migration-execution.md) records
read-only verification after a successful job and failed hosted receipt parsing.

Sources G19 and G27 establish job execution and immutable metadata; synthetic
release/orchestration tests prove rejection/order only. Actual job and SQL version,
checksums and replay remain live #26 evidence. Operator ownership cleanup remains
required before runtime release.

documents.title: Read-only migration status release
documents.body:
# Read-only migration status release

## Decision

Add `operation: verify` to the existing exact-hash release workflow. It configures
the existing migration job with `-action=status`, under the existing migrator IAM
identity. No new identity, grant, job, database or financial message is introduced.
This is internal deployment metadata; existing ISO financial assessments stand.

The retained human operator cannot read deployment tables or SET ROLE to the
migrator. Granting it broader access would undermine the current separation.
Running another `up` to discover status would mix inspection with mutation. Use
the workload's existing authority for a read-only transaction instead.

## Contract

Keep the migration-only manifest fields, all three successful same-build receipts,
owner/main/hash/expiry checks and bootstrap gates. Verification needs a new image
implementing status; the earlier approved migration image does not support it.
Terraform accepts only `up` or `status`; no arbitrary job argument is accepted.
Verification may update job configuration, but never runs application rollout.

Status verifies embedded source checksums and restricted migrator privileges, then
opens a read-only transaction. Require exactly one clean schema-version row at the
highest embedded up migration and an exact filename/hash match for every registered
artifact, with no missing/extra entries. No grants, DDL, registration, force, down,
application reads or financial payloads. Errors emit the existing fixed failure.

An exact successful `status` execution emits `migration-verification-passed`,
distinct from `migration-execution-passed`; neither qualifies for app rollback.
Missing tables, dirty/wrong versions, artifact drift and unsafe identities fail.

## Owned Hosted repair rollback verification (#328)

The separate repair-enabled Sandbox profile adds the same exact selected-image
read-only status/hash check before `sandbox-rollback` runtime rollout. It may
update/execute the existing job with `-action=status`, never up/down, using the
existing workload identity. The same-build source ancestry includes33 and the
repair runtime; the actual database must match the selected image's highest
embedded version and complete hash set. This adds no direct API table grant or
startup probe. Legacy rollback without the explicit capability stays job/DB-inert.

This operation can emit a bounded `migration-verification-passed` receipt for its
own read-only step; it is not a substitute prior application rollback receipt.
The prior successful Sandbox transport receipt and identical approved connection
digest remain required. A failed/foreign/up/retried/mismatched status execution
stops before runtime changes. Source and mocked orchestration tests establish
these mechanics only; actual job/SQL authority still needs scoped hosted evidence.

## Evidence and next action

The SQL authority is the existing migration library's version and artifact tables;
the execution contract and serialization sources are G27/G29. Existing local
restricted-role tests establish the synthetic baseline. Add status mismatch and
read-only checks, release isolation/argument tests and mocked Terraform action
tests before review. Actual cloud status requires a fresh build and separately
reviewed `verify` manifest. Only a clean status permits the planned replay stage.

documents.title: Money and multicurrency contract
documents.body:
# Money and multicurrency contract

## Status and source boundary

Representation and operation requirements for JB-002. The selected synthetic
development profile is [ADR 0005](../decisions/0005-development-accounting-policy.md),
with exact rounding and replay details in [posting boundary](posting-boundary.md). ISO 4217 identifies
currencies; it does not select the accounting framework. See
[contract sources](../research/contract-sources.md) C04 and bibliography R03/R06/R07.
The FX examples are conditional accounting illustrations; US GAAP paragraph-level
review remains outstanding. This contract does not assert GAAP/IFRS compliance.

## Representations

Keep transaction currency, book functional currency and presentation currency
separate. Functional currency belongs to an approved book policy revision. Changing
it requires a dedicated transition contract; never reinterpret historical journals.

Selected storage bounds for the first posting slice: finite `numeric(38,9)`, maximum 29 integer digits; rates:
finite positive `numeric(38,18)`, maximum 20 integer digits. Validate lexical scale
and range BEFORE casting to these types, since PostgreSQL can round on coercion.
These bounds are engineering choices, not currency-standard requirements.
HTTP money/rates are unsigned plain-decimal strings, no exponent or grouping.
Reject negative values, NaN, infinity and excess precision. Side conveys sign.

Currency versions record ISO code, numeric code when assigned, minor-unit metadata,
validity interval and source release. Non-currency assets need a separate future
unit contract. Currency validity and posting precision are distinct policies;
never assume all currencies use two decimals. Proposed functional posting scale
is the selected currency's minor unit, bounded by storage precision, with half-even
rounding. ADR 0005 selects this for the synthetic profile; real-entity exceptions still
require explicit policy.

UI display uses versioned currency minor-unit metadata and decimal-string
padding/trimming only. USD `125.5` displays as `125.50`; nonzero digits beyond the
minor unit stay visible instead of being rounded away. Missing or ambiguous
metadata preserves the original string. Display does not change saved requests,
ledger amounts or valuation. `amount.test.ts` covers zero/two/three decimal
currencies, storage-scale zeros and large values beyond JavaScript safe integers.

## Line semantics

`transaction_amount` is the original currency magnitude; `functional_amount` is
its booked magnitude. Ordinary lines require both positive. A valuation line may
have zero transaction amount and positive functional amount, keeping the original
foreign exposure currency. Small real exposures whose valuation rounds to zero
require a reviewed precision exception; do not silently drop them in this slice.

Every line has a valuation basis: `spot`, `carrying`, `functional_adjustment` or
`identity`. Identity requires matching currencies and amounts. Spot requires an
immutable rate observation and recomputation at approved rounding. Carrying needs
a source position/allocation, never an arbitrary client exchange rate. Adjustments
require a reviewed valuation/correction reference and privileged operation kind.
All journal functional debits equal functional credits exactly. Raw currency
buckets are never summed together to test balance. Ordinary API posting initially
accepts only identity/spot lines; specialized operations own carrying/adjustment
lines, and those operations remain blocked until their full contracts are accepted.

Rate observations record base/quote currencies, quote-units per base-unit, rate,
effective time, observation time, provider/reference, purpose and policy revision.
For a transaction-to-functional conversion, base is transaction currency and quote
is functional currency. No guessed inversion, fallback to 1 or replacement of
historical observations. Missing/stale/nonexchangeable rates block automatic posting
and require an explicit reviewed valuation method. Store selected provenance on
posted lines; later provider corrections create new observations.

## Measurement and settlement requirements

Under the illustrative IAS-21-derived policy, monetary exposure uses period-end
rates; historical-cost nonmonetary items retain transaction-date valuation; fair
value items use the relevant valuation-date rate. Ordinary monetary exchange
differences affect earnings, with exceptions requiring separate policy. See C04.

Project operations must retain foreign quantity and functional carrying amount
per identified position. Revaluation posts only the difference from current
carrying value, not repeatedly from initial cost. Settlement allocations remove
foreign quantity and its associated carrying value; consideration and fees are
separate, with the balancing FX difference explicit. Partial allocation rounds
under one policy; the final allocation consumes the exact residual. A rerun of a
valuation/settlement operation cannot duplicate its effect. Concurrent allocations
must not exceed the open position. See [FX-01–FX-06](accounting-scenarios.md).

Reversing a posted journal swaps sides while preserving original amounts/rates;
it is a correction, not a new conversion at today's rate. Position-affecting
reversals also need inverse allocation effects and are outside the first manual
posting slice. FX profit/loss and presentation-translation reserves remain distinct.
Explicit rounding lines use an approved account and bounded tolerance; never
silently alter a user line or manufacture a balancing amount for arbitrary errors.

## Acceptance and remaining gates

`TestMoneyInputBounds` covers zero/2/3-decimal policies, half-way rounding, overflow,
scale, nonfinite input and identity rules. `TestFXLifecycle` covers FX-01–FX-06,
rate direction/staleness, period changes and reruns. `TestSettlementAllocationRace`
covers concurrent partial settlements and final residuals. Manual bounds/spot tests now execute against PostgreSQL; full FX lifecycle
and settlement allocation tests remain future work. See the
[posting proof](../runbooks/posting-proof.md).

Before automated settlement/revaluation, specify position/allocation physical
columns, operation permissions, valuation batches and reversal semantics. For the first manual posting implementation, use only ADR 0005
and its same-day synthetic rate policy; live rate-provider policy remains open. This deliberate boundary prevents generic journal creation from
pretending to implement receivable subledgers or the full currency lifecycle.

documents.title: Local observer runtime adapter
documents.body:
# Local observer runtime adapter

## Decision and scope

Implemented the receipt-only Go adapter for the nine functions in
[worker SQL](worker-sql.md), issue #7. SQL remains the sole authority for
membership, journal/event identity, retries, fences, leases and receipts. No HTTP,
OIDC, Cloud Tasks SDK, credential access, deployment or financial mutation is
included. The [background-work](background-work.md) STD-01 internal-wakeup
assessment applies unchanged; no ISO financial or audit exchange conformance.

## Owned interfaces and budgets

`Beginner.BeginTx(ctx, pgx.TxOptions)` supplies a configured database connection.
Separate `Publisher` and `Consumer` constructors receive different role-bound
beginners. A publisher also receives one explicit binding UUID and an injected
`Transport.Enqueue(ctx, Task)`. A task contains only deterministic hexadecimal
name, target version 1 and a `work-wakeup-v1` envelope. Target URLs and identity
configuration belong to the future transport adapter, not database data.

Publisher exposes Discover, Candidates, DispatchClaim, DispatchResult, Recover
and Tick; Consumer exposes Claim, Heartbeat, Finish, Fail and Handle. Every SQL
call uses SERIALIZABLE, transaction-local 5s statement/1s lock timeout, an overall
6s call deadline, immediate COMMIT and at most three full retries for 40001/40P01.
Cleanup has its own bounded 1s context; idle transaction timeout is set to 6s. Validate session/current-role equality,
exact capability and absence of owner/API/migrator/other-worker capability and
privileged role flags inside each transaction; direct application-table privileges are rejected. SQL validates enrolled session login
and current scoped authority. No caller-supplied principal is accepted.

Tick has a 60s overall deadline, discovers at most 25 facts, enumerates at most 25
operation UUIDs and processes them sequentially: Recover → DispatchClaim → COMMIT
→ Enqueue (at most 10s) → DispatchResult → COMMIT. No transport call holds a SQL
transaction. Queue result codes are accepted/already_exists/timeout/transient/
rejected. Errors map to fixed codes; arbitrary transport/SQL text is never returned.

Handle uses the same 60s bound and validates the exact three-key wakeup before SQL:
schema_version numeric 1, canonical lowercase operation UUID and positive signed-
bigint-range dispatch_generation string, maximum 1024 bytes, no duplicates,
unknown fields, nulls or trailing JSON. It commits Claim before invoking Finish.
SQL done/observed becomes completion only after successful COMMIT; busy/not_due
remain retryable. Heartbeat/Fail are explicit primitives; receipt-only Handle has
no external business step or fabricated failure receipt.

## Unknown commits and metadata

An unclassified COMMIT error is `commit_unknown`, never automatic transaction
replay, completion, or permission to enqueue. A subsequent Tick/Handle consults
SQL again: completed work returns done; an uncertain claim remains busy until
SQL recovery accounts for abandonment. Explicit server 40001/40P01 may retry.
Neither queue acknowledgement nor a prepared SQL result proves observation.
Validate every returned status, nonnull/null metadata shape, positive generation/
fence, bounded candidates and fixed target version. Before enqueue independently
recompute SHA-256(operation UUID|dispatch generation|1); reject digest mismatch.

## Evidence and sources

Existing BW02–BW04 and WS01–WS03 source sections cover duplicate delivery, task
identity, transactional locks and current-time leases. P05 in
[posting sources](../research/posting-sources.md) reviews pinned pgx transactions;
this adapter uses the repository's pgx/v5 v5.11.0. Unit fault tests and disposable
PostgreSQL adapter/fake-queue integration cover role separation, rollback,
whole-transaction retries, commit-loss suppression, no queue call before commit,
duplicate/reordered delivery, revocation, expiry and context cancellation.
Actual Cloud Tasks/OIDC/network-response-loss proof remains a separate gate.

**OR01**, PostgreSQL Global Development Group, PostgreSQL 17
[Appendix A, Error Codes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/errcodes-appendix.html),
classes 08, 23, 25 and 40 reviewed 2026-10-13. Codes 08007 and 40003 explicitly
name unresolved transaction/statement completion; the presence of a `PgError`
alone does not establish rollback. Our conservative policy treats unclassified
COMMIT errors as unknown. Only explicit serialization/deadlock rollback,
constraint/owned-trigger rejection, failed-transaction state and pgx's explicit
commit-rollback sentinel count as confirmed failure. Only serialization/deadlock
is retried. Unit tests assert no enqueue, replay or exposed claim metadata for
both ambiguous SQLSTATEs. This code table is mechanism evidence, not a network
failure simulation or an exactly-once transport guarantee.

documents.title: Private observer transport
documents.body:
# Private observer transport

## Scope and decision

Implemented foundation for #7: wrap the existing [runtime adapter](observer-runtime.md) in
separate publisher/consumer HTTP handlers and a Cloud Tasks REST v2 transport.
SQL remains authoritative for scope, leases, fencing, recovery and receipts.
There is no financial payload or posting operation. The STD-01 internal-wakeup
assessment in [background work](background-work.md) applies unchanged; this is
not an ISO 20022 financial exchange or a conformance claim.

## Implemented boundaries

`NewPublisherHTTP(Ticker, TokenVerifier, CallerPolicy)` and
`NewConsumerHTTP(WakeupHandler, TokenVerifier, CallerPolicy)` return independent
`http.Handler` instances. Separate constructors receive an already configured Publisher or Consumer, an
injected Google ID-token verifier, and an exact audience/email/subject policy.
POST `/internal/observer/publish` accepts only `{}`; POST
`/internal/observer/consume` accepts the existing 1024-byte `work-wakeup-v1`.
Identity is verified before reading a body or invoking SQL. Caller headers never
supply an actor, book, binding, queue, URL or credential. One request per handler
can be active, with a 60-second overall budget and five-second verification.
A consumer acknowledges only successful committed Handle; unknown/busy outcomes
return 503. Protocol failures return 400/404/405; identity failure returns 401.
Publisher 200 exposes discovered/candidates/enqueue_calls/recorded/skipped only;
those counts describe this tick, never backlog completion. Consumer success is
204 only after Handle succeeds. No error response contains runtime diagnostics.

The queue adapter fixes project/location/queue, consumer URL, audience and
invocation service account at construction. It receives context-aware access
credentials and an injected HTTP RoundTripper; construction discovers no secrets.
One ten-second create attempt sends a deterministic task name and the unchanged
identifier envelope, with an OIDC token and 65-second dispatch deadline. It
never follows redirects or retries a create call. Queue acknowledgement is not
observation completion; uncertain responses retain durable SQL recovery.

`NewCloudTasksTransport(QueueConfig, AccessTokenProvider, http.RoundTripper)`
implements the existing Transport. AccessToken(ctx) must return a context-bound
short-lived OAuth access token with Cloud Tasks scope. Target URL must be the
fixed consumer path on HTTPS *.run.app; audience is the same origin, optional
root slash. No ports, userinfo, query, fragment or encoded path. The invocation
service account belongs to the queue project. Each enqueue validates the exact
existing envelope and recomputes its deterministic SHA-256 task identity before
credentials. Only 200/201 plus matching full task name yields accepted; 409 is
already_exists, 408/504 timeout, 429/5xx transient, other 4xx rejected. Redirects,
malformed/oversized responses and network failure are transient uncertainty.
No response body or token is logged. Successful create bodies are capped at
16 KiB; token strings at 8 KiB. No application-level create retry.

`NewGoogleTokenVerifier(http.RoundTripper)` uses the already pinned Google
validator with public Google JWKS only, five-second HTTP timeout, no redirects,
and a strict 64 KiB key-response limit checked using one sentinel byte. Only RS256 is accepted; the handler
requires exact issuer, audience, subject, email, boolean verified-email and
current issue/expiry timestamps with at most one-hour lifetime. One Authorization
Bearer value is required; X-Serverless-Authorization is rejected. Cloud Tasks
headers carry no authority.

Composition must supply separate restricted database logins and workload
identities, plus a worker http.Server with ReadHeaderTimeout5s, ReadTimeout5s,
WriteTimeout70s, IdleTimeout30s and MaxHeaderBytes16KiB. The normal API server
15-second budget is incompatible and is not reused. A five-second request-body
read deadline supplements server timeouts. Injected verifiers, credential
providers and transports must honor context; no claim is made that context
can interrupt arbitrary blocked io.Reader implementations. Constructors do not
load ADC or start a listener. No worker executable is delivered in this slice.

## Source review and alternatives

Reviewed 2026-10-13, starting with bibliography BW02/BW03. These are implementation
mechanisms, not hosted acceptance evidence.

- **OT01:** Google Cloud [service-to-service authentication](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/authenticating/service-to-service),
  service-account setup, acquiring/configuring ID tokens, and receiving requests.
  Cloud Run Invoker is separate from application caller authorization. Audience
  identifies the receiving service. X-Serverless-Authorization removes the
  signature before delivery to the container; this adapter requires verifiable
  Authorization and rejects alternate-header ambiguity. Actual hosted header
  behavior must pass before activation.
- **OT02:** Google Cloud REST v2 [tasks.create](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.queues.tasks/create),
  request body, deduplication, response view, OAuth scopes. Named-task conflicts
  can refer to recently removed tasks; full-name acknowledgement is never a
  receipt. The adapter requests BASIC view and never fetches financial content.
- **OT03:** Google Cloud REST v2 [Task and HttpRequest](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.queues.tasks),
  task identity, base64 body, OIDC authorization and dispatchDeadline. Cancellation
  does not guarantee stopped processing. The chosen 65-second queue deadline
  allows a small margin over the 60-second handler budget; SQL fences remain
  necessary. Queue-level overrides require a separate hosted configuration check.
- **OT04:** Pinned `google.golang.org/api/idtoken` v0.298.0, local `validate.go`
  constructor/Validate/RS256 implementation reviewed. It verifies signature,
  audience and expiry; application checks must additionally authorize issuer,
  service-account subject and verified email. No custom cryptographic verifier.

- **OT05:** Google Cloud [Token types, service account ID tokens](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/token-types#service_account_id_tokens),
  RS256 example and issuer/subject/lifetime fields reviewed. Pin exact issuer
  `https://accounts.google.com` and immutable numeric subject, not email alone.
  ID tokens cannot be individually revoked; current SQL authorization remains
  required. Email inclusion and IAM behavior still need hosted qualification.

- **OT06:** Google Cloud REST v2 [OidcToken](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/reference/rest/v2/OidcToken),
  serviceAccountEmail and audience reviewed. The service account must share the
  queue project; enqueue needs actAs authority and an explicit audience avoids
  the target-path default. No IAM permission was provisioned by this work.

Inference: retain REST plus the existing verifier dependency rather than add a
Cloud Tasks SDK for one bounded create operation. An injected SDK could be a
future replacement if it preserves no automatic retry and context ownership.
Polling-only and Pub/Sub alternatives remain as reviewed in background work.

## Acceptance evidence

- `TestWorkerHTTPAuthentication`: missing/multiple/spoofed auth, wrong issuer,
  audience, subject/email, unverified email, expiry/future issue time and verifier
  failure invoke no body read or SQL; fixed errors contain no input/token text.
- `TestWorkerHTTPProtocol`: exact routes/method/query/content-type/body bounds,
  duplicate/unknown wakeup fields and publisher input; only committed success
  acknowledges; unknown/busy/configuration failures remain non-2xx.
- `TestWorkerHTTPAdmission`: one concurrent request, context cancellation and
  deadline propagation; no queue-generated header is trusted as identity.
- `TestGoogleVerifierSyntheticKeys`: real RS256 verification against synthetic
  injected JWKs, signature tamper, unknown keys/algorithm and safe failure.
- `TestCloudTasksWire`: fixed destination, deterministic name, exact base64
  envelope, explicit OIDC audience/account/deadline, no redirects/retries.
- `TestCloudTasksUncertainty`: duplicate acknowledgement, denial, throttling,
  server/transport timeout, malformed/oversized/lost response, wrong returned
  name and redaction. Each attempt obtains at most one token and makes at most
  one request. No outcome asserts durable work completion.

- `TestObserverHTTPComposition`: disposable PostgreSQL plus both HTTP handlers
  and fake REST transport; actual receipt COMMIT acknowledgement loss yields503,
  duplicate delivery yields204, then lost create acknowledgement retains one
  receipt/attempt and unchanged journal/outbox/book revision. No TCP loss or
  actual Google token service was exercised.
- `TestObserverHTTPMixedSyncRole`: added sync membership makes publisher HTTP
  return503 before discovering an operation. The adapter role guard now includes
  bookkeeping_sync alongside owner/API/other-worker capabilities.

Hosted Cloud Run IAM, actual Scheduler/Cloud Tasks identity/header behavior,
queue overrides, invocation account permissions, key rotation, deployment/pool
budgets, costs and latency remain separate acceptance gates.

documents.title: Plaid acquisition recovery
documents.body:
# Plaid acquisition recovery

Issue #220; accepted owner scope, 2026-10-20: repair existing development Sandbox
acquisition without another enrollment. Parent #88 remains open for hosted proof.

## Evidence and decision

Observed: four delivery operations quarantined with `permanent_failure`; three
sets abandoned with `decoder_rejected`, one with `dispatch_quarantined`. HTTP
204 acknowledges a durable disposition, not complete publication. No original
provider response has been read; the precise rejected field is unproved.

Reviewed selected official [Transactions sync response and account-filter
sections](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#transactionssync),
2026-10-20, API request pin 2020-09-14. Account-filtered streams retain separate
cursors. Transactions can precede enrollment (default history request 90 days).
ISO currency validity must still cover the source date. A successful response is
not evidence that our bounded schema/date profile accepts it.

Confirmed compatibility defect: SQL staging rejects an empty first/final account
page with INITIAL_UPDATE_COMPLETE or HISTORICAL_UPDATE_COMPLETE even though the
reviewed Go decoder accepts it. The Item status and filtered account's cursor are
independent (decoder contract's 2026-10-14 correction). Migration 24 accepts these
two known statuses only for the existing strictly empty initial page; it never
permits an empty cursor after a nonempty page or when has_more is true. Named
regression: TestSyncEmptyAccountItemReadiness, all four known Item statuses.
This reproduces a valid-response mismatch, not proof of the actual private page.

Keep strict material validation; do not guess the rejected field or relax money,
currency dates, source ownership, duplicate keys or account filtering. Persist a
closed decoder classification atomically with abandonment; expose only the safe
code and delivery disposition through authenticated stream status. Provider
values and unknown field names never enter diagnostics.

Alternative: blanket retry or reset quarantined rows. Rejected because it destroys
terminal evidence and can restart unknown effects. Explicit Request sync now may
instead release a known permanent failure only when SQL proves abandonment, no
completion and no live acquisition. Append an immutable recovery receipt; retain
the original operation, claim and attempts. Publisher creates a fresh operation
from the existing committed cursor. Unknown outcomes remain blocked.

The current actor/import/source/worker permissions and generation checks remain
mandatory. Existing idempotency receipts prevent a lost response or concurrent
retry from releasing another attempt. Old queue deliveries only acknowledge the
old terminal operation. No journal is posted by acquisition or recovery.

## Standards and storage

Reuse the mappings and limits in [Plaid decoder](plaid-decoder.md),
[dispatch SQL](acquisition-dispatch-sql.md) and [standards](standards.md).
ISO 4217 identifiers, minor units and source-date validity remain mandatory.
These local error/retry messages have no applicable ISO 20022 message definition;
they carry operational classifications, not a financial exchange. No audit export
or ISO conformance claim is introduced. Public vendor sections reviewed; paid ISO
normative text and real provider payloads were not accessed.

New integration-owned diagnostic/recovery sidecars use scoped keys and foreign
keys, immutable receipts, no raw payloads or credentials, and no direct runtime
table grants. Entry functions use current authorization and existing canonical
locks in serializable transactions. Migration 24 is additive; rollback must refuse
to erase recovery evidence. Terminal operation identities remain immutable.

Acceptance: safe decoder-code/atomic-abandon tests; manual recovery authorization,
same-key replay, unknown/live/completed refusal and fresh-claim SQL tests;
frontend quarantine versus queue state tests; complete browser/API/PostgreSQL
journey. Hosted acceptance requires completed generation, publication and reviewed
transactions, never deployment/HTTP acknowledgement alone. Exact compatibility
fix is contingent on the newly classified failure.

documents.title: Bounded Plaid page decoding
documents.body:
# Bounded Plaid page decoding

## Decision and boundary

Issue #102, coordinator approved interface and material-field policy before code,
2026-10-13. Implements only decoding of synthetic `/transactions/sync` responses
for the proposed `jayburd-plaid-transactions/1`, API pin `2020-09-14`. No HTTP client,
SDK, token, provider call, staging, complete-set publication or accounting authority.
The [provider proposal](provider-ingestion.md) remains authoritative for future
acquisition/fencing, whole-set lineage and live qualification.

`DecodePage(raw []byte, Expected) (Page,error)` accepts an approved account ID and
installed ISO currency references (code, UUID, minor unit, inclusive ValidFrom,
exclusive ValidTo; empty end means open). It never derives ownership from payload.
On any error return the zero Page: no partial rows, raw bytes, cursor or account ID.
Errors carry fixed codes only. Input slices are copied on success; callers own
private retention. Returned public structs are ordinary mutable Go values, not
signed attestations or SQL authorization credentials.

## Material mapping

Page JSON fields are `next_cursor,has_more,transactions_update_status,request_id,
sha256,added,modified,removed`. Raw exact page bytes are separately retained and
excluded from JSON. SHA256 identifies evidence but never substitutes for byte or
normalized-field equality. Arrays retain order. The decoder does not invent Item,
environment, stream, fence, page index or request cursor; trusted acquisition must
attach these separately. A complete-set assembler, not this decoder, owns cross-
page identity/lineage and cursor commit. `HasMore=false` is not history readiness.

Each added/modified transaction outputs `account_id,transaction_id,pending,
pending_transaction_id,date,authorized_date,datetime,authorized_datetime,
iso_currency_code,currency_version_id,amount_lexeme,amount,direction,
eligible_for_review,name,merchant_name,original_description`. Nullable fields use
null; omitted optional dates/names normalize to null with exact omission retained
in raw evidence. Pending link is required but nullable. Raw exact transaction
object is separately retained and excluded from JSON. Removed entries expose only
account/transaction IDs, with separately retained raw object.

Positive signed source numbers map to outflow, negative to inflow. Zero, including
negative/exponent zero, retains its original lexeme, unsigned amount `0`, direction
`zero` and readiness false. Pending remains pending, with readiness false. Ordinary
nonzero, nonpending rows are source-ready even with no pending link: readiness
**never** grants journal posting or accounting approval. A pending row cannot
claim a predecessor; self-links reject. Link target existence/removal/state cannot
be established from a single page and stays a complete-set responsibility.

Source date and authorized date are separate full dates; timestamps retain their
original offsets/text with no timezone conversion. Description remains inert source
text. None becomes an approved journal date, category, FX rate or ledger account.
Only exactly one installed currency version valid on source date may resolve;
unofficial/missing ISO and ambiguous or unavailable versions reject the whole page.

## Parser profile and bounds

Issue #258's subsequent [source precision decision](plaid-source-precision.md)
supersedes the currency-minor-unit rejection below: retain exact bounded source
amounts but mark them ineligible and hold their review rows. Magnitude and
nine-decimal storage bounds still reject. Historical diagnostics remain readable.

Issue #258 refines diagnostics without changing the accepted quantity set.
`amount_magnitude_exceeded` means more than 38 significant or 29 integer digits;
`amount_scale_exceeded` means normalized scale above nine;
`currency_precision_exceeded` means a quantity within storage limits that is
not an integral minor unit of the dated ISO 4217 currency. These fixed codes
replace new emissions of the ambiguous `amount_out_of_range`; old receipts
remain readable. No source amount, identifier or payload fragment enters a
diagnostic. SQL retains its exact numeric/lexeme equality and minor-unit checks.
Alternative rounding would lose evidence and is rejected; accepting arbitrary
extra precision would change reviewed storage/accounting contracts. Named proof:
`TestPlaidMoneyDiagnostics`, existing independent-rational fuzz oracle and
`TestDeliveryManualRecovery` for durable classified quarantine/recovery. This is
a diagnostic improvement, not a confirmed repair of the hosted checking cause.

Engineering bounds, not claims about all legal provider payloads:

- 2 MiB exact response, 500 total added+modified+removed changes, nesting depth 32.
- Required arrays are arrays, not null. Accounts contains at most the approved
  account; added/modified require its metadata and type depository. Account mismatch
  in metadata, transactions or tombstones rejects all data.
- IDs are case-sensitive graphic ASCII 1–256 bytes. No URL interpretation or trim.
  Next cursor uses a bounded base64/base64url alphabet, max 256 bytes. Empty cursor
  only for empty no-more initialization, independently of Item update status.
- Required boolean/pending fields cannot be null. Unknown update/payment-channel/
  transaction-type/account-type enums fail closed. Known UNKNOWN update status
  remains explicitly unknown and does not imply completion.
- Strict duplicate decoded keys at every depth, trailing JSON/data, malformed JSON,
  invalid UTF8, lone UTF16 surrogate and decoded NUL are rejected.
- All JSON number tokens, including inert metadata, max 128 bytes and explicit
  exponent in [-100,100]. Amounts remain number lexemes; strings are not accepted.
  Decimal-position arithmetic normalizes zeros without floats, then requires at
  most 38 significant digits, 29 integer digits and 9 fractional digits, plus exact
  installed currency minor precision. Long insignificant zero representations
  within 128 bytes are accepted when normalized quantity fits; never round.
- Name required 1–500 Unicode codepoints; optional merchant/original text max 500.
  Full dates 0001–9999 use strict Gregorian calendar. Timestamps require seconds,
  optional 1–9 fractional digits and explicit offset/Z; leap seconds unsupported.
- Repeated transaction identity within or across added/modified/removed on one
  page rejects. Distinct IDs with identical amount/date/name remain distinct.

Root/account/transaction/removed unknown fields reject. Root allows only the
listed response fields plus accounts. Transaction inert allowlist: account_owner,
check_number, location, payment_meta, personal_finance_category,
personal_finance_category_icon_url, merchant_entity_id, merchant_category_code,
logo_url, website, counterparties, category, category_id; payment_channel and
transaction_type additionally validate known enums. Account inert allowlist:
subtype, balances, mask, name, official_name, verification_status,
verification_name, verification_insights, persistent_account_id, apy,
holder_category. Inert values preserve arbitrary bounded nested JSON (including
unknown nested fields) but contribute no mapped meaning; global duplicate-key,
depth and numeric checks still apply. Account balances are not ledger balances.
`running_balance` accepts null or a JSON number retained only in raw evidence;
its exact lexeme is never converted to float or treated as a ledger balance. This narrower profile may quarantine valid new provider fields.

## Standards and refreshed primary sources

Plaid JSON remains the explicit proprietary-adapter exception described in the
[standards contract](standards.md), not ISO 20022/camt. Installed ISO 4217 currency
versions and RFC 3339 full-date/time syntax retain the existing reference scope.
No new ISO normative text, bank data or provider environment was accessed.

Selected official sections refreshed 2026-10-13:

| Source | Reviewed sections and factual evidence | Project interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Plaid Transactions API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/) | Sync account filter/count/pagination; response accounts, amount/currency, date/timestamps, pending/link, transaction ID, removed, cursor, update status. Amount direction is provider-defined; pending links may be absent; cursors are account-specific; all pages matter. | Exact lexemes, separate dates/state, explicit same-account check; no pending-to-journal shortcut. |
| [Plaid API versioning](https://plaid.com/docs/api/versioning/) | Nonbreaking changes, explicit version header, 2020-09-14. Additive fields/enums and identifier changes can occur without a version change. | Fixed reviewed allowlists may intentionally quarantine additions; pinning alone is insufficient. |

This refresh supplements PI01/PI03/PI08 in the
[source register](../research/plaid-ingestion-sources.md). Reviewed selected sections,
not every field or provider guarantee. Alternative float SDK decoding loses original
number tokens; unrestricted unknown-field acceptance conceals material changes;
rejecting all inert nested additions is stricter but unnecessarily broad for fields
with no financial interpretation. Tests prove this local parser profile only.

## Transaction classification compatibility — 2026-10-14

Issue #118: accept optional `transaction_code` as null or a string of at most
256 Unicode codepoints (our bound). Retain it only in private raw evidence;
never derive direction, ledger category or posting authority from it. Unknown
classification strings remain inert, like other unmapped metadata. Wrong JSON
types reject. Unknown field names and all money/account checks still reject.
The proprietary adapter/ISO applicability above is unchanged.

PI01 documents this nullable classification even where no institution code is
available. Synthetic reproduction proved our previous allowlist rejected its
null form. This is a confirmed compatibility defect, not proof of the cause of
the earlier hosted rejection. Rejecting the documented field prevents valid
pages; accepting every unknown field would remove the material-schema boundary.
`TestPlaidTransactionCode` verifies the narrow alternative, exact cents, raw
retention, omitted normalized mapping, invalid types and account isolation.

## Cursor diagnostic refinement — 2026-10-14

Hosted retest after #120 returned decoder_invalid_cursor. PI01's request cursor
section still documents an upper bound of 256 base64 characters; its response
next_cursor section permits empty text when transactions are not yet available.
Update status describes the Item. We cannot infer from the old error whether
encoding or our empty-progress rule rejected this response. Keep both rules
unchanged and classify them as invalid_cursor_encoding or invalid_cursor_progress.
TestProbeFailuresStayPartialOrBlocked exercises both through the probe. No raw
cursor, length or provider status is added to the receipt.

## Account readiness correction — 2026-10-14

PI01 describes transactions_update_status at Item scope, next_cursor as empty
when transactions are unavailable, and account_id as a separate filtered stream.
Therefore Item completion cannot by itself require a filtered account cursor.
Accept empty cursor only with no changes and has_more=false for any known Item
status. The diagnostic still reports provider_not_ready and never passes sync
without a usable cursor. Unknown status, invalid cursor encoding, changes or
has_more with an empty cursor still reject. This narrow interpretation avoids
both declaring history complete and loosening cursor encoding constraints.
TestPlaidEmptyAccountReadiness covers all four known statuses and rejects all
three change groups/has_more without a cursor; TestHostedScopeAndCleanup covers
one initial wait followed by sync, repeat delta and single Item cleanup.
The hosted progress code identifies the branch but does not expose which
predicate fired; this documented contract correction still requires hosted proof.

## Public schema compatibility review — 2026-10-14

PI11 reviewed every direct field in TransactionsSyncResponse, AccountBase,
Transaction (including TransactionBase through allOf) and RemovedTransaction at
public schema commit 325e2e192bcb422df708029bafe9d950c94df2fd. Root, account and
removed allowlists cover their declared fields. Three remaining transaction fields
needed explicit disposition: business_finance_category and client_customization
are optional null/object enrichment retained only as private raw evidence;
running_balance accepts null or a JSON number. Owner explicitly approved retaining
all reviewed fields on 2026-10-14. Global numeric lexical/depth/byte bounds remain;
balance strings, objects, arrays and booleans reject. Exact source number bytes
remain private evidence, with no currency conversion, rounding or ledger mapping. This does not infer ledger
categories, identities or balances from enrichment. Unknown new field names still
reject, as do scalar/array enrichment values. Existing nested JSON bounds apply.

TestPlaidReviewedEnrichment covers both enrichment forms, exact cents, account
isolation, no normalized metadata leakage, exact balance lexemes beyond float
precision, malformed balance types and unknown fields.
TestPlaidFullPublicSchemaFixture uses fictional values for all declared direct
fields: 8 response, 13 account, 33 transaction, 2 removal fields.
Public schema compatibility does not prove which field a private hosted page
contained; a successful hosted sync remains required. Proprietary API and ISO
applicability are unchanged; no financial message or accounting policy is added.

documents.title: Plaid history and dated currencies
documents.body:
# Plaid history and dated currencies

## Decision and source evidence

Issue #225; owner authorized all available existing-connection history on
2026-10-20. Implementation claim: fix/plaid-currency-history. Product/capacity
follow-up #226 is separate. This is source acquisition, not accounting recognition.

Reviewed selected official sections on 2026-10-20:

| Source | Fact | Application and limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Plaid Transactions API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/), sync cursor, days_requested, account_id, has_more | Initial history defaults to 90 days, maximum 730; initialized Items ignore changed lookback. Initial null cursor reads available updates; all pagination must be consumed. Each account filter has its own cursor. | Preserve existing enrollments/cursors and all returned updates. Do not use cursor now or switch endpoints to discard older history. No guarantee of complete bank history. |
| [Plaid Transactions overview](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/), history availability | History accumulates while connected and may exceed the initial window. | Lookback is not a permanent rolling retention cutoff. Larger history capacity remains #226; current complete-set bounds fail closed without partial publication. |
| [ISO 4217 MA amendment 115](https://www.six-group.com/dam/download/financial-information/data-center/iso-currrency/amendments/dl_currency_iso_amendment_115.pdf), page 1, dated 2002-05-13 | USD/840/2 recorded for El Salvador effective 2001-01-01. | Historical corroboration, not USD's inception or a complete audit of every subsequent amendment. |
| [SIX List One](https://www.six-group.com/dam/download/financial-information/data-center/iso-currrency/lists/list-one.xml), USD record, existing pinned 2026-09-17 release | Current USD/840/2 was reviewed in sandbox-book-bootstrap.md with publication/hash provenance. | A publication date is not the currency's inception. For this bounded profile install an additional local coverage interval [2001-01-01,2026-09-17), corroborated by both source records. It is local supported coverage, not a claim of universal historical ISO conformance. |

No paid ISO normative text, private provider page or bank record was read. The
owner's safe diagnostics prove three currency rejections, not their exact input
field. A synthetic pre-window USD fixture establishes the defect repaired here.

Alternative: change the original immutable USD interval, discard older transactions,
or re-enroll with shorter history. Rejected: these respectively rewrite provenance,
lose source changes, or change enrollment without fixing currency semantics.
Another alternative is to ignore reference dates; rejected because actual currency
changes and minor-unit policies must retain dated metadata.

## SQL and runtime contract

The source binding pins monetary identity. For provider acquisition, resolve each
transaction date against installed currency rows sharing the binding's alphabetic
and numeric codes, with a non-null minor unit. Different code/numeric identity is
never inferred as an FX conversion. Return at most 32 ordered, nonoverlapping
versions in sync_context.currency_versions, retaining legacy currency metadata.
The decoder stores each row's exact selected version/minor-unit interpretation.
SQL independently verifies the selected version, identity, date and exact amount.
Missing coverage, duplicate intervals, unofficial currency or excess precision
reject the whole set; no date rewrite, skipping or automatic reference installation.
The existing singleton context remains an accepted compatibility fallback.

Migration 25 appends a fixed historical USD reference only when the exact reviewed
bootstrap reference is installed; it never changes existing references, bindings,
observations, journals or cursors. The owner-only installer is replay/conflict safe
and is also called by future owner bootstrap. Other currency histories are installed
through separately reviewed reference operations, not hardcoded into the worker.
No runtime DML or new runtime execute grant. Down refuses to delete installed
historical reference evidence. Pause dispatch before migration/runtime promotion;
old workers reject the new context shape, so deploy matching workers before retry.

## Acquisition versus posting

Acquisition publishes all supported source history, independently of source binding
date and book start. Acquisition readiness is not permission to post. Existing
source review and posting still require a book policy, active accounts, valid dated
currencies, an open period, current permissions and an explicit reviewed command.
No opening balance, date substitution or automatic journal is inferred. Historical
version identity remains on observations; no change to journal currency resolution.
Out-of-policy review explanations and initial lookback settings remain #226.

## Standards and acceptance

ISO 4217 applies to code/numeric/minor-unit/date mapping; reuse the project standard
source limits above. Plaid API 2020-09-14 JSON stays the documented proprietary
adapter mapping, not an ISO 20022 message. ISO 21378 export conformance is outside
this source-acquisition change. Multicurrency remains supported through installed
dated references; no rates, FX policy or jurisdictional accounting approval added.

Named evidence: TestHistoricalCurrencyAcquisition, TestCurrencyVersionContext,
TestSandboxUSDHistory, TestSyncHistoricalCurrencyValidation, existing currency/FX
ledger tests and source-review dates. Verify two versions in one set, interval
boundaries/gaps, identity/precision denials, zero journals, replay, out-of-policy
post denial and usable in-policy review. Run migration, ledger, acquisition,
sync-state and repository gates; run app integration before handoff. Hosted owner
retry/publication/review remains required after matching promotion; HTTP 204 alone
does not complete #225 or #88.

documents.title: Reviewed Plaid liability bindings
documents.body:
# Reviewed Plaid liability bindings

## Decision and scope
