Issue #210 extends the atomic binding command from #209 in the synthetic
development book. The owner requested separate ledger accounts for selected
credit and loan accounts. This decision permits `credit / credit card`,
`loan / student`, and `loan / mortgage` from a verified Plaid Transactions
manifest. Each creates or selects one distinct monetary `liability / credit`
ledger account, source account and sync stream after explicit owner review.
All other credit/loan subtypes remain visible and unbound. The book owner must
review the proposed category, normal side, code, name, ISO 4217 currency and
binding date; Plaid metadata alone is not accounting authority.

## Additional registration profile — #258, 2026-10-22

Owner requested `loan / auto`, `loan / consumer`, and `loan / line of credit`
registration in the fictional Sandbox. Extend the existing distinct
`liability / credit / monetary` mapping to those three verified subtypes.
The Accounts API defines them under loan; its product matrix only promises
Transactions for some loan subtypes. Therefore registration permits attempted
acquisition, never inferred history, balances or product coverage. Unknown
subtypes remain unbound; the existing liability posting guard remains mandatory.
Alternative: keep these visible but unbound, which prevents the requested
registration even where Sandbox supplies transactions. Enabling every loan type
would exceed the reviewed scope. Acceptance: mixed seven-account SQL binding,
exact replay, unsupported-type rollback, trusted type/subtype decoder pins and
browser binding tests; hosted registration remains separate #88 evidence.

This extends the existing proprietary Plaid API `2020-09-14` mapping, not a new
ISO 20022 exchange. ISO 4217 dated identifiers/minor units remain enforced;
ISO 21378 audit-export mapping is unchanged and outside this acquisition slice.
No normative ISO conformance is claimed. Refreshed sources are PL04 in the
source register, selected public sections only.

The [Plaid Accounts type and product matrix](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/)
and [Transactions API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/) were
reviewed on 2026-10-20. Transactions coverage for loans is narrower than the
Accounts schema. This profile does not enable the separate Liabilities product.
Provider coverage varies by institution; the manifest and sync response remain
subject to strict account identity checks. See the
[source record](../research/plaid-liability-sources.md).

## Invariants

- `new_ledger_account` has the existing reviewed shape and fixed
  `liability / credit / monetary` semantics for this profile. Server and SQL
  both validate the type/subtype and category pairing. Existing-account
  bindings require the same category and normal side.
- The owner selects an installed, dated ISO 4217 currency version and binding
  date. Every provider account maps to a distinct ledger and source account.
- The current serializable binding command owns account, source, permission,
  stream and receipt creation. Exact idempotent replay returns the same result;
  conflicts and partial failures roll back. No opening balance or journal is
  inferred from Plaid balances or transactions.
- Sync compares the returned account type with the trusted manifest for the
  bound stream. Unknown or changed types fail closed.
- Liability observations may be acquired, but the current source-review
  posting formula is approved only for asset/debit sources. Liability source
  drafts remain blocked until a separately reviewed transaction-direction,
  principal/interest/fee and offset-account policy is implemented. This also
  prevents a credit-card payment or loan payment from being posted as a simple
  expense from the wrong side.

## Standards, alternatives and evidence

This is an internal setup command and proprietary Plaid JSON adapter, not an
ISO 20022 financial message. ISO 4217 code, version, valid interval and minor
unit validation remain mandatory. ISO 21378/21926 export semantics are not
changed. No ISO conformance is claimed.

Treating all Plaid `credit` or `loan` subtypes as supported would exceed the
Transactions product matrix and infer accounting policy from a label. Requiring
manual account pre-creation would restore the broken multi-account journey.
The narrow reviewed allowlist preserves one atomic enrollment and makes the
coverage limit explicit. Provider documentation does not prove institution
coverage or source sign semantics. Fresh Sandbox acceptance must verify the
actual selected accounts and zero automatic journals.

Acceptance: synthetic SQL, Go and browser tests cover one credit card, one
student or mortgage loan, unsupported subtype, distinct accounts, exact replay,
conflict/rollback, manifest type mismatch, and blocked liability draft; the
browser/API/PostgreSQL gate must pass. Hosted qualification belongs to #88.

documents.title: Plaid Link browser boundary
documents.body:
# Plaid Link browser boundary

The managed page supplies an inert `ConnectionLink` adapter. Only the explicit
connect flow calls `open`, after SQL-backed Begin returns a Link token. Demo and
synthetic entry points continue to inject fictional adapters; they do not load
Plaid or inherit the managed adapter. Default server-disabled enrollment remains
unavailable; browser code does not bypass Link Events qualification or server
verification of Link/public-token association.

Reviewed [Plaid Web Link SDK](https://plaid.com/docs/link/web/) on 2026-10-14:
Plaid requires its script to load directly from its CDN and says that the Web SDK
is not versioned. `create` provides lifecycle callbacks and a handler with open,
exit and destroy. Success may contain a null public token for other products;
this Item enrollment profile rejects it. These are vendor mechanisms, not evidence
that a particular account has the required server Link Events capability.

The adapter loads only
`https://cdn.plaid.com/link/v2/stable/link-initialize.js`, with no bundled SDK,
arbitrary script location or fabricated integrity/version pin. SDK load and
initialization share a ten-second bound; an opened session has a five-minute bound.
Only one session per adapter may run. Exit/cancellation returns no token; errors
are fixed text and discard provider metadata/diagnostics. Completion, timeout and
abort destroy the handler. Abort also attempts forced exit, with terminal fencing
set before cleanup can invoke callbacks.

Link/public tokens remain in memory only. No URL, storage, analytics, console or
provider metadata retention is introduced. Scope/session/lock changes abort the
existing Connections lifetime; late callbacks cannot trigger its execute request.
Loading a third-party script cannot promise to undo downloaded JavaScript or erase
vendor memory; cleanup removes our handlers and the SDK iframe, not the browser's
entire execution history. A canceled attempt stays inspectable; it is not silently
replaced or retried. No OAuth redirect-resume storage or reconnect support is added.

This is a proprietary provider bootstrap protocol, not an ISO20022 financial
message. Source/currency/accounting standards are unchanged. Focused fake-SDK unit
tests and intercepted-CDN browser tests validate local lifecycle behavior; they do
not qualify real institutions, provider consent or a live Plaid environment.

## Official Go SDK adapter (#195)

Reviewed 2026-10-19: official [plaid-go v49.0.0 source](https://github.com/plaid/plaid-go/tree/v49.0.0),
commit `0d83b050ea325adda35c6d88bdf24b46fe2f7044`, specifically Link/Item/Accounts
clients, request options, retry caller, and response models. The tagged README
still shows older generated API names; implementation follows the pinned source.
The generated client supports Hosted Link results, explicit credentials and HTTP
transport injection, and retry disabling. Its account balance model uses floats.

Use generated request/response types for connection operations, explicitly select
Sandbox, inject credentials/version, disable all retries, and bound HTTP latency
and response size. Keep duplicate-key/UTF8/JSON rejection at the transport boundary
and replace provider errors with existing static errors. Account responses are
projected to identity/currency metadata before SDK decoding; balance amounts never
enter float models or bookkeeping. Transaction ingestion retains its exact-decimal
decoder. This is transport replacement, not a new financial message or ISO claim.

Compared with retaining handwritten payloads, generated types reduce drift while
our SQL authority, one-shot exchange, encrypted persistence and recovery semantics
remain application-owned. Acceptance: existing wire/denial/session/consent tests,
explicit 429/500/transport-error no-retry cases, poisoned environment overrides,
and the synthetic browser/API/SQL enrollment/acquisition/posting journey. Hosted
provider acceptance remains a separate deployed test.

documents.title: Link recovery qualification and SDK transition
documents.body:
# Link recovery qualification and SDK transition

The bounded #275 [owned Hosted repair protocol](hosted-reconnect.md) proposes the
signed-session association for ordinary update mode. It does not enable repair or
supersede the eventual SDK direction. It supplies a separate protocol before code;
the historical requirements below must not be read as implemented guarantees.

## Decision record — #104 / #187, 2026-10-22

Status: proposed transition; current runtime remains Hosted Link. The owner
authorized completing the qualification plan. This record makes the remaining
security and recovery design reviewable; it does not enable SDK/update mode.

Recommended product direction: official Web SDK for the owned frontend, after
server association and OAuth return recovery are qualified. Retain the deployed
Hosted profile until that replacement passes. The current HTTP provider rejects
reconnect before attempt creation or exchange claim; preserve that guard.

Reviewed official sources and exact sections are recorded as LR01–LR04 in
[the source register](../research/plaid-link-recovery-sources.md). Hosted Link
supports update mode, but that capability alone does not establish which modern
server result proves successful ordinary Item update in this integration.

| Alternative | Benefit | Remaining cost / risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Official Web SDK | Vendor recommendation for owned frontend; direct lifecycle callbacks and OAuth support | Requires qualified server association, redirect resume and device evidence |
| Retain Hosted Link | Existing bounded encrypted handoff and observed non-OAuth enrollment | Extra tab; explicit completion; ordinary update association still unqualified |
| Accept callback or successful accounts lookup | Small implementation | Rejected: client metadata/current credentials do not prove this session's repair |

This is proprietary bootstrap/authorization behavior under the existing STD-01
assessment, not an ISO 20022 exchange. Currency/date/accounting mappings remain
unchanged. No new financial record or accounting policy is introduced.

## Minimal transition requirements for coordinator review

1. **Versioned profile:** explicitly select Hosted or SDK in reviewed release
   metadata. Do not infer SDK enablement from callback success. Qualify actual
   Link Events availability; no fabricated `link_events_qualified=true`.
2. **Server association:** define the exact current modern server response/event
   proving success for new and update sessions. Match retained Link-token hash,
   current actor/entity/book/attempt, unique session, completion time and expiry.
   For repair also match the preselected Item and approved streams. Deprecated
   `on_success`, browser account IDs and a healthy `/accounts/get` alone remain
   insufficient. Obtain provider clarification if ordinary update proof is absent.
3. **SQL:** migration 19 handoff write requires new/link_ready/unclaimed/unexpired;
   its read rechecks current authority, new mode and the recorded token hash.
   The completion service additionally requires link_ready and a live recovery
   window before using that read. Read alone does not impose state/expiry guards.
   A new reviewed migration must extend precisely the intended mode and current
   authority checks before reload recovery for reconnect. Never edit merged SQL.
   Preserve shared-Item generation/stream fences and one-shot claim. Repair must
   reuse the existing access credential and Item: no public-token exchange.
4. **OAuth return:** an authenticated same-origin resume route resolves a scoped
   unclaimed attempt and decrypts its retained Link token server-side; returns
   transient initialization material only after renewed authority. Browser
   persistence may hold no Link/public/access tokens or financial requests.
   If an opaque correlation handle is needed, bind it server-side to current
   actor/scope and expiry; a URL handle alone grants no authority. Treat OAuth
   return parameters as transient vendor input, suppress logs/analytics, and
   remove them from the displayed URL after initialization. Review exact SDK
   `receivedRedirectUri` requirements before implementation.
5. **UI:** show repair only when supported and authorized. Reconnect begins with
   explicit Item/generation/full approved stream confirmation; no new-product
   or new-account consent is implied. Account-selection changes require their
   own scope review. Cancellation never silently reconnects or creates a new Item.
6. **Duplicate prevention:** institution/mask/name are warnings, not ownership
   keys. Compare provider-confirmed selection before exchange where supported;
   distinguish same credentials from legitimate distinct logins and partial
   selections. SQL still prevents duplicate Item/account bindings after exchange.
   Resolve pre-exchange provider metadata and cross-book privacy rules first.
7. **Transport:** signed `SESSION_FINISHED` is notification, not authority to
   exchange blindly. Durable event receipt and user-driven completion share one
   claim. Do not execute completion from public webhook handler without a scoped
   durable operation and explicit reviewed execution contract.

## Synthetic evidence versus hosted execution

### Implemented bounded exit recovery

One matching token response with exactly one finished, fresh session, a bounded
session identifier, a modern `exit` object and no `results` object yields internal
`link_session_exited`. Both a null error (cancellation) and a non-null error
(failed exit) receive the same fixed recovery guidance; no vendor code/message
is exposed. Unfinished, multiple, missing-identifier or legacy-only exits stay
unresolved. Valid completed Item-add results retain their existing precedence.
This classification does not assert that a provider Item is absent.

Before any SQL claim, service maps that classification to existing HTTP 409
`connection_operation_blocked`. Both intact-tab and discovered-attempt UI paths
inspect the exact attempt and refresh authorized discovery before offering the
existing explicit **Cancel setup** / **Try again** actions. A competing completion
instead displays its actual durable state. No automatic abandon, replacement,
exchange, terminal state or API schema change is introduced. Read failures and
revoked scope keep existing fail-closed handling.

Acceptance: `TestHostedExitPreservesClaim`, modern exit/error/unfinished/legacy/
multiple cases in `TestHostedLinkCompletion`, and “offers explicit recovery after
a completion conflict” for same-tab and reload flows. These prove no claim,
exchange, secret publication or automatic cancellation/restart.

`TestHostedLinkCompletion` rejects unfinished/legacy-only/null/ambiguous/stale/
future completion evidence. `plaidLink.test.ts` enumerates 17 applicable Link
error codes and proves fixed diagnostic text, late-callback fencing, no browser
persistence, no automatic reopen and fresh explicit-session recovery. These are
synthetic protocol/privacy proofs; none clears the actual provider error rows.

Use [the #88 matrix](../plans/plaid-88-test-matrix.md) for clearance authority.
For every hosted case record source SHA, deployed revisions/profile, matrix ID,
public fixture name, browser/OS/device, timestamp, action, redacted terminal
status, expected/actual result, evidence location and defect/retest link. Do not
retain provider payloads, tokens, institution account identifiers or screenshots
containing financial records. Failed/blocked cases stay open.

| Rows | Fixture/action and acceptance |
| --- | --- |
| L02–L04 | Complete, cancel, close/reload and expire separate attempts; each resolves its exact durable attempt, at most one exchange/credential, no automatic replacement. Distinguish URL expiry from six-hour result recovery. |
| L05 | Same login twice, distinct login at same institution, overlapping and disjoint selected accounts; no silent duplicate imports and no institution-only blanket rejection. |
| L06 | Public simple-user savings/depository fixture; explicit account binding, first publication and unchanged repeat; reconcile expected scope. |
| O01 | Desktop OAuth happy path, cancel, missing return/expired session and wrong signed-in scope; return to original attempt without persistent tokens or duplicate exchange. |
| O02–O03 | Real supported iOS/Android browsers, institution app installed/absent; record versions and separate each outcome. Keep mobile unqualified until observed. |
| O04 / I01 | On an explicitly authorized fictional Item induce `reset_login`, observe actionable login-required state, repair in update mode and verify same Item/credential/account continuity and resumed sync. Blocked until server association implementation above. |
| O05 / I02–I03 | Revoke/reduce consent, expiration and new-account notices; no acquisition outside explicit current grants and no automatic widening or local expiry extension. |
| I04 | Account disconnect versus full Item removal; explicit confirmation, ambiguous reply inspection, stale-worker fencing and retained approved immutable history. |
| E01 | Each public OTP/questions/selections/multiple-round fixture: success, wrong response and cancel; no exchange before verified completion; inspect/recover exact attempt. |
| E02 | Owner-operated reCAPTCHA success/failure; agent stops at challenge; safe cancellation/retry. |
| E03–E04 | Each of the 17 named matrix codes separately at a supported non-OAuth test institution; verify fixed/redacted application message, retained attempt and explicit recovery; a fake SDK exit is insufficient. |
| E05 | OAuth insufficient-credentials/access-denied selector, missing institution/account and cancel; no scope widening, duplicate Item or automatic replacement. |

Native/webview and UK/EU variants remain excluded only by the current explicit
US web profile. Product/platform expansion reopens their applicability.

documents.title: Closed Plaid provider transport profile — #308/#312
documents.body:
# Closed Plaid provider transport profile — #308/#312

## Source decision

Engineering baseline reviewed by coordinator2026-10-25 before implementation.
Owner authorizes source work toward real-account registration with bank-read-only
access and ledger bookkeeping; this does not accept deployment targets or secrets.
Source acceptance closes #308 only after this baseline is merged/checked. #337
retains the actual unresolved resource/isolation/retention/pilot decision; #316
depends on it. Splitting this gate does not count an absent predecessor as done.

[PP01/PP04/PP06](../research/production-pilot-sources.md) record reviewed official
host, request/version, sync/state and privacy sections and limits. Two closed
profiles: sandbox -> https://sandbox.plaid.com; production ->
https://production.plaid.com. API2020-09-14, pinned SDK49.0.0 unchanged. No arbitrary
URL, ambient discovery, case folding, whitespace normalization, redirect, fallback
or moving an Item between environments. Standard root TLS remains intact.

## Construction and request boundary

Use one small shared immutable profile value with private state. Unknown/empty
explicit profile and zero value reject before I/O. Existing public constructors
remain legacy Sandbox wrappers with identical behavior; new explicit constructors
require a valid profile. No new CLI/runtime/API/browser field or default enables
Production. #313 later wires approved managed composition after #311 SQL authority.

Connection allowlist retains only POST link/token/create, link/token/get,
item/public_token/exchange, item/get, accounts/get, item/access_token/invalidate
and item/remove. These support enrollment, readback and separately authorized
credential/Item lifecycle; none is money movement. Reject test/refresh/payment/
transfer/other paths, userinfo/query/fragment/opaque/encoded-path substitutions.
Use the exact profile host and API header, current bounded SDK transport, no
retries/redirect and existing pre-float account projection. Products stay US
Transactions only. Source312 Production rejects the Sandbox webhook URL and
HostedRepair capability; reviewed Production receiver configuration and repair
qualification belong to #314/#313/#275. Empty Production webhook permits isolated
construction tests; it is not a release-ready notification configuration.

Acquisition permits only fixed POST transactions/sync for the configured profile.
Keep account filtering/count500/cursor, raw bounded bytes, exact original-currency
lexemes, response/error budgets, pagination-mutation and Retry-After behavior.
Add explicit trusted environment metadata to FetchRequest and propagate the SQL
execution context in the runner. Production requires exact production; Sandbox
accepts exact sandbox; omitted metadata is accepted only by the legacy constructor,
not the new explicit Sandbox constructor.
Mixed/unknown context/profile denies before transport. Existing SQL validContext
continues to reject Production until #311; source312 must not weaken SQL checks.
Credentials are opaque: this layer cannot prove their origin from a token prefix.
Addressed credential/AAD/current SQL binding is #313, and must be qualified before
activation. Profile matching is not a substitute secret-origin or consent proof.

## Standards and unchanged semantics

Environment/host selection is operational authorization, not a registered ISO20022
message. Existing proprietary Plaid2020-09-14 financial mapping and ISO4217 dated
currency identities/original units remain unchanged; no float, FX fallback, new
recognition rule or ISO21378 export/conformance claim. SQL true data-origin/profile
version compatibility must be reviewed in #311 before DDL; source312 does not
relabel evidence, add a namespace or authorize real-account posting policy.

## Alternatives, risks and evidence

Changing credentials or one global URL was rejected: it does not carry scope/AAD/
webhook/SQL authority and risks mixing environments. Duplicating all clients was
rejected because financial decode/error rules would drift. Shared closed routing
keeps existing Go/PostgreSQL/Next components; no new DB/service or cloud spend.

STRIDE: spoofed profile/destination (high) -> private immutable closed value,
exact request allowlists and mismatch negatives; secret/evidence substitution
(high) -> current source limitation explicit, #311/#313 binding required; response
tampering/disclosure (high) -> unchanged bounded exact decoder/redacted failures;
unintended capability (high) -> no runtime/API selector, no payment/test/refresh
path and Production repair/notification guard. Human security review before
sensitive code merge/activation remains required. This is engineering review,
not AppSec or actual provider qualification.

Named independent tests: TestClosedPlaidProfiles rejects unknown/zero/malformed
and arbitrary host/path; TestProductionConnectionProfile checks exact injected
request/version/Transactions body and no Sandbox receiver/repair; existing Sandbox
request/SDK/decimal/recovery fixtures unchanged; TestProductionSyncProfile checks
matching/mixed/absent metadata and literal original numeric bytes, pagination and
retry/redaction/redirect negatives. All injected transports: no real provider,
secret reads or cloud I/O from default tests. Core/race/build and appropriate
existing integration regressions before handoff; no migration in #312.

documents.title: Plaid Sandbox qualification and bounded diagnostics
documents.body:
# Plaid Sandbox qualification and bounded diagnostics

## Current acceptance navigation — 2026-10-22

Use the [#88 test matrix](../plans/plaid-88-test-matrix.md) for current coverage,
the [source register](../research/plaid-88-test-sources.md) for reviewed sections
and the [migration29 rollout](../runbooks/plaid-258-rollout.md) for seven-account
hosted evidence. Historical blockers below describe earlier stages; the original
full acceptance obligations remain. This audit changes no executable contract.

## Approved first executable slice

Issue #88 remains an open qualification gate. Coordinator approved a read-only
Sandbox sync diagnostic, not enrollment or a completed application qualification.
The default `sandbox-qualify -mode offline` reads no credential input and makes no
network calls. Explicit `-mode sandbox-sync -allow-sandbox -input-fd N` requires
an owner-injected pipe descriptor N >= 3, never stdin, a TTY or a regular file.
No environment/ADC/credential discovery, URL option or command-line secret exists.
Agents must not execute the provider mode or inspect its input without separately
reviewed execution readiness. Owner supplies an already linked Sandbox access token.
The harness does not create/exchange tokens or impersonate Link association proof.

Input is one bounded JSON object (16KiB, unknown/duplicate keys rejected):
`environment` exactly `sandbox`, `client_id`, `secret`, `access_token` with Sandbox
prefix, selected `account_id`, `currencies` (installed ISO metadata using decoder
Currency fields Code/VersionID/MinorUnit/ValidFrom/ValidTo), and nullable `cursor`.
The cursor may be omitted for an initial snapshot. Inputs are memory-only and
never included in receipts, errors or debug formatting. Metadata selects a probe;
it does not prove SQL scope authorization. Owner must use only fictional accounts.

The harness uses production `acquisition.PlaidHTTP` and `plaid.DecodePage`, with
fixed Sandbox HTTPS host and API version 2020-09-14. Each of two sequential sync
rounds is bounded to ten pages, 1,000 changes and 2MiB aggregate raw bytes. Total
execution deadline is 60s; no automatic retry or pagination restart. First round
checks exact decoding and cursor progression; second starts from the final cursor
and records whether an empty repeat delta was observed. Concurrent provider changes
make that observation unavailable, not proof of an application defect. Historical
readiness is separate from has_more=false. Raw pages are discarded after counting;
no payload, transaction identifier, amount, name, cursor, credential or request ID
is persisted/output. Go memory disposal is not guaranteed physical zeroization.

Receipt profile `plaid-sandbox-diagnostic-v1` exposes only mode, overall status,
fixed named checks/reasons and bounded integer page/change counts. Overall status
is `blocked` before successful first-round evidence, otherwise `partial`; this
executable cannot issue overall `pass`. Individual checks can pass. Counts describe
provider changes seen by the probe, never booked transactions or accounting totals.
The repeat check is not SQL idempotency evidence. The executable opens no database,
so it cannot assert application journal counts or provider-to-review consistency.

## Full #88 acceptance still required

1. Real interactive Link session, verified server session association, one-shot
   exchange and current manifest, explicit binding and credential publication.
2. Actual application runner imports an initial snapshot and an incremental update;
   compare fixture-known exact amounts, identities/currencies and cursor publication
   against source-review SQL. Replay must preserve revision/observation counts and
   assert no journals/outbox posting effects in that same application database.
3. Dynamic Sandbox pending-to-posted update, including removed pending identity and
   added posted identity across pages, complete-set publication, source lineage and
   unchanged already-posted accounting history.
4. Real signed Sandbox webhook through the deployed verifier and SQL receipt into
   acquisition demand. A fire-webhook response alone does not prove delivery,
   signature acceptance, replay protection, dispatch or eventual review publication.
5. Owner reviews a redacted receipt tied to deployed revision and all test stages;
   failures/unfinished stages remain explicit. Sandbox never approves live books.

## Real Link readiness blocker

The [Sandbox Hosted Link profile](hosted-link-enrollment.md) requests a hosted
session and exposes its validated URL. Explicit completion resolves a unique
server session result before claiming exchange. Ordinary SDK use still requires
account-specific Link-events enablement to verify association. Synthetic tests do
not establish either actual interactive completion or account-specific enablement.
`/sandbox/public_token/create` bypasses Link and cannot qualify it. Reconnect and
full deployed acquisition/webhook acceptance remain unqualified.

## Annotated primary sources and review depth

Selected public sections reviewed 2026-10-14; no real API calls or dashboard access:

- SQ01 [Link API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/): `/link/token/create` hosted_link,
  hosted_link_url; `/link/token/get` availability and session results. Supports the
  readiness blocker above; no account-specific enablement was verified.
- SQ02 [Hosted Link](https://plaid.com/docs/link/hosted-link/): creation/completion
  workflow and Sandbox delivery limits. Sandbox does not send Hosted Link email/SMS.
- SQ03 [Transaction states](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/transactions-data/):
  pending lineage and Testing pending and posted transactions. Dynamic test user
  `user_transactions_dynamic` can use non-OAuth `ins_109508`; refresh advances states
  and emits transaction webhooks. Removed/added replacements may span pages, and
  their amounts/names may differ. These are provider records, not posted journals.
- SQ04 [Sandbox API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/sandbox/): public_token/create bypass,
  transactions/create and item/fire_webhook. Custom creation supports up to ten
  transactions per call; explicitly pin account and ISO currency instead of defaults.
  SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE firing is distinct from downstream processing evidence.
- SQ05 [Sandbox overview](https://plaid.com/docs/sandbox/): Differences between
  Sandbox and Production. Institution-specific history limits, pending behavior and
  OAuth flows are not faithfully simulated; do not derive production capacity,
  balance correctness, historical completeness or consent behavior from this probe.

Shared bibliography/index links are coordinator-owned. ISO 4217/date and exact
amount mapping follow the existing [decoder contract](plaid-decoder.md) and
[standards applicability](standards.md). Plaid API is proprietary, not an ISO 20022
message; this operational receipt is not a financial interchange or conformance
certificate. No new accounting policy, SQL schema or dependency is introduced.

## Separate API smoke runner

Owner authorized a [hosted probe](hosted-sandbox-probe.md) that creates a disposable
Sandbox Item via API. It reuses the diagnostic core but does not alter the pipe-fed
command or count that API bypass as real Link qualification. No already-linked
access token is required for this separate smoke runner.

## Redacted decoder classifications — 2026-10-14

Issue #118 preserves the receipt profile and blocked status, but refines decoder
failure reasons to `decoder_` plus these closed codes: limit_exceeded,
invalid_expectation, invalid_json, duplicate_key, invalid_number, invalid_cursor,
invalid_cursor_encoding, invalid_cursor_progress,
invalid_field, unknown_enum, account_mismatch, unsupported_account,
duplicate_identity, invalid_identity, invalid_lineage, invalid_date,
unsupported_currency, amount_out_of_range, amount_magnitude_exceeded,
amount_scale_exceeded, currency_precision_exceeded, unknown_field. Anything else remains
`decoder_rejected`. Never include error text, field names, values or raw pages.
Rejected pages do not increment counts. `TestDecoderReasonRedaction` verifies
wrapped classifications, arbitrary error suppression and receipt redaction;
`TestProbeFailuresStayPartialOrBlocked` verifies actual decoder propagation.

The cursor subcodes distinguish unsupported cursor encoding from empty-cursor
progress/readiness inconsistency. They contain no cursor characters or lengths.
The legacy invalid_cursor classification stays recognized for compatibility.
No acceptance rule is relaxed by this diagnostic refinement.

documents.title: Source precision hold — issue #258
documents.body:
# Source precision hold — issue #258

## Evidence and decision (2026-10-22)

Hosted Sandbox generation 2 failed with the fixed code
`currency_precision_exceeded`, before any checking publication. No amount or raw
provider payload was inspected. This establishes the validation branch, not the
institution's intended value or a floating point artifact. The owner requested a
shared repair across account types.

The [Transactions API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/), selected
`/transactions/sync` transaction amount/currency sections, describes a numeric
settled amount and ISO currency identifier; its `double` transport description
does not authorize rounding imported evidence. Selected public sections reviewed
on 2026-10-22; no complete schema or bank guarantee is claimed. PI01 in the
[source register](../research/plaid-ingestion-sources.md) is the canonical source.

Decision: retain exact source amounts within existing numeric(38,9) bounds even
when they exceed the dated currency's minor-unit precision. Such rows have
`eligible_for_review=false`, enter `correction_hold` and expose
`source_precision_review_required`. Other rows publish in the same atomic set.
Original signed number lexemes and exact unsigned values remain unchanged.
Pending and zero remain held. Over-nine-decimal or magnitude overflow still
quarantine the complete page; this slice does not claim arbitrary precision.

Alternatives: whole-page rejection blocks unrelated transactions (current
defect); rounding loses evidence; dropping the row loses completeness; arbitrary
precision requires a separate storage contract. No account-specific exception.

## Applicability and mapping

This changes proprietary Plaid JSON to internal observation/review semantics,
profile `jayburd-plaid-transactions/1`, API pin `2020-09-14`. ISO 20022 is not a
counterparty exchange here; the existing documented adapter exception applies.
ISO 4217 identifiers, historical versions and minor-unit metadata remain
applicable. Minor units govern posting eligibility, not lossy evidence storage.
ISO 21378:2019 remains relevant to future audit exports; no export or conformance
claim is added and full normative text has not been reviewed. See
[standards](standards.md) for authoritative sources/access limits.

Amount/direction/date/currency/identity mappings are unchanged. SQL independently
checks exact lexeme equality, dated currency and eligibility; it derives the hold
from exact quantity and currency precision. No new transport field, nullable
money, float, new currency reference or ledger rounding policy. No auto-posting.

## Acceptance and compatibility

Named evidence: seven-account, three-currency decoder matrix; independent
rational fuzz oracle; SQL mixed valid/held publication, exact replay, forged
eligibility rejection, draft refusal and zero journal assertions; review browser
test showing all digits and disabled drafting for the held row. Migration 29
precedes the new worker. Old worker inputs remain valid. Down migration refuses
retained sub-minor-unit provider evidence; no deletion or rounding. Existing
posted journals and ledger valuation constraints remain unchanged.

documents.title: Position read model — proposed for #248
documents.body:
# Position read model — proposed for #248

## Decision boundary

**Status:** first-screen scope and visual direction approved by the owner on
2026-10-22; orchestration and acceptance proposal for #248/#249. Position opens
with **All books**, grouped by entity, and supports entity or individual-book
scope. Each row is an independently authorized, explicit-date report. This does
not approve live-entity policy, change SQL/HTTP, classify an account as cash, or calculate
spendable funds. The existing [financial reporting](financial-reporting.md),
[reporting SQL](reporting-sql.md), [HTTP](reporting-http.md), and
[pinned journal](report-drill.md) contracts remain authoritative for implemented
report arithmetic and access. [Evidence](../research/position-sources.md) records
review depth, inference and alternatives.

The approved first screen shows entity/book, functional currency, **Assets**,
**Liabilities**, **Book equity**, and signed **Equity change** against an explicit
earlier date. **Position · Ledger · Reports** remain directly available at the top.
Clean sans-serif text, aligned amounts and alternating faint-gray/unshaded book
rows provide structure; no column tint. Equity increases/decreases may use
restrained green/red with explicit signs, never a claim of spendability,
reconciliation, or favorable/adverse movement in every account category.
Direct equity and unclosed earnings remain report detail. Cash classification,
spendability and attention status are deferred extensions, not first-screen fields.

## All-books orchestration and independent snapshots

Use the current authorized workspace membership list for visible entity/book rows.
Apply all-books, entity or individual-book selection to that list; do not obtain
scope from cached financial responses or caller-provided actor identity. Every
balance-sheet request still authenticates and authorizes its exact entity/book.
The membership list is discovery, never a durable grant. If access changes, clear
that row's prior amounts before rendering its denied/unavailable state. A global
identity failure stops scheduling further reads and clears financial results.

The browser orchestrates existing per-book balance-sheet comparison requests with
**at most four in flight**. Four is an initial UI concurrency bound, not a measured
capacity claim. No new SQL, API route, bulk response, arithmetic or aggregation is
authorized. Queue books beyond the bound and show their pending state honestly;
do not silently truncate the selected scope. Scope/date changes cancel obsolete
work where supported and generation-guard every result so a late old response
cannot overwrite the current selection. Reuse no rows across scope refreshes.

One response provides current/prior totals and their exact signed change for one
book revision. Each row retains its own accounting/comparison dates,
`snapshot_revision`, `generated_at`, currency code/version/minor units and status.
Expose those details accessibly for that row. A shared date control expresses the
requested cutoff, not a shared transaction. Books read before/after concurrent
postings can have different revisions and generation times: label the overview
**Independent book snapshots** and never assign a common report revision.

Successful rows remain visible when another book fails; pending, valid zero, denied,
stale and unsupported rows are distinct. An unavailable row contains no current,
prior or change substitute zero and no retained stale amounts. Each row is either
a complete accepted comparison response or unavailable; do not splice totals
from separate responses. Explicit refresh rereads the selected scope and replaces
row snapshots. Reading one book successfully does not imply all books were read.

Entity headings organize rows only. No entity subtotal, portfolio grand total,
cross-book sum, FX conversion, eliminations or claim of consolidation is permitted,
even when two rows use USD. Books can represent overlapping economic activity.
#59 owns any future consolidated/presentation-currency model. Unsupported book
policies, including functional currencies beyond today's synthetic USD profile,
remain unavailable rather than fabricated multi-currency support. Original
transaction currencies remain accessible in the ledger under existing authority.

Top navigation preserves explicit selected scope and date intent. Ledger/Reports
may require choosing a book within that scope before using their single-book
endpoints; they must not silently choose one or imply a cross-book report.
Evidence for a Position row carries that row's entity/book/date/revision.

## Selection, exact arithmetic and trace

Request exactly one verified, currently readable entity/book, an inclusive
`through_date`, and an explicit earlier comparison `through_date` if movement is
shown. Dates are accounting dates in the book's supported UTC policy, independent
of browser time and journal `posted_at`. A Position line is a point balance,
not a period flow. `Change since` is **current point balance minus earlier point
balance**, preserving a signed result. It does not claim cash flow, profitability,
or the cause of change. The balance-sheet comparison uses one authorized book
revision for both dates. Do not fill a failed or missing comparison with zero.

For eligible posted lines through the selected date, `N(account)=Σ(functional
debit−functional credit)` as an exact decimal. Preserve unexpected signs and
contra balances. The existing unclassified balance-sheet categories define:

| Position line | Exact functional-currency expression | Existing evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Assets | `Σ N(asset)` | Balance-sheet `totals.assets`, account rows and selectors |
| Liabilities | `−Σ N(liability)` | `totals.liabilities` |
| Direct equity | `−Σ N(equity)` | `totals.direct_equity` |
| Unclosed earnings | `−Σ [N(revenue)+N(expense)]` over eligible history | `totals.unclosed_earnings`; derived, never a journal |
| Book equity | Direct equity + unclosed earnings | `totals.total_equity`; comparison change is server-supplied |
| Cash | `Σ N(a)` for a reviewed, versioned set of asset account IDs `C` | **Extension required**; no existing cash classification |
| Other assets | Total assets − Cash | **Extension required** after `C` is approved |

`Total assets = Liabilities + Total equity` is an invariant, not an adjustment.
Never take absolute values to force a pleasant presentation. Account code/name,
provider type and source account links cannot substitute for reviewed cash
membership. A credit-balance cash account stays negative. Inactive historical
accounts remain in totals. Empty valid books return exact zero statement totals;
this is not an unavailable read. Zero totals or an empty report selection cannot
prove that no journals were posted: offsetting entries can have the same result.
The existing balance-sheet API has no authoritative journal-count flag. Display
exact zero without a `No posted entries` claim. Such a status requires separately
owned authoritative metadata before it can be shown.

## Deferred cash and evidence extensions

The server must own cash membership and calculation, not browser-selected rows or
client-side arithmetic. A proposed `position-v1` read extension can return a
versioned `cash_account_ids` policy reference, `cash`, `other_assets`, and their
comparisons, computed with the existing balance-sheet authority and same
revision/transaction. It should reject missing, foreign, non-asset, ambiguous or
unsupported classifications and never silently omit an account. Its eventual
policy storage and update workflow require a reviewed decision before DDL.
Until then, Position omits Cash; a future dedicated cash view must show `Not
configured` without reviewed membership, never relabel total assets as cash.
Initial Position can show current and prior point totals from the existing comparison response; a single
server response is required for consistent movement.

All amounts remain canonical signed decimal **strings**, at most 29 integer and
9 fractional digits; zero is `"0"`. No float or JavaScript financial arithmetic.
Functional currency ISO 4217 code, pinned version ID and minor units accompany
each total. UI padding is display only. A book's original amounts/currency versions
and immutable rate IDs survive in the supporting GL and journal; original units
are never summed across currencies. No cross-book/entity consolidation or
aggregation in this overview. A policy or functional-currency transition without approved mapping returns
`unsupported_policy`, never a converted total. The first implemented report
profile is synthetic accrual/UTC/USD functional currency; future functional
currencies require their own approved policy and tests.

Each account/derived line uses its server-generated selector to show contributing
accounts. A selected account opens scoped GL with the same `snapshot_revision`,
date bounds and exact amounts; a selected GL row opens the existing pinned
journal endpoint in the same revision. The current journal endpoint proves one
selected GL-line inclusion, **not** arbitrary subtotal-to-journal membership.
For subtotal evidence, the UI must expose the contributing account list and then
GL; a direct subtotal journal list needs a bounded server contract and tests.
For point balances, GL must cover opening history through `through_date`, not
only a convenient recent window. An empty account selection shows an explicit
zero and no journals. Original and reversal journals remain immutable on their
own accounting dates; the view never erases the original when corrected.

## Truthful state and attention

Position has three independent clocks: (1) the **accounting cutoff**
`through_date`, (2) the **book snapshot** `snapshot_revision` and
`generated_at`, and (3) **source freshness** from separately authorized
acquisition/status reads. A source being current does not prove its observations
were reviewed or posted. A posted balance does not prove reconciliation,
completeness or availability to spend. `generated_at` is computation time,
not a posting cutoff. Pending/failed commands may need attention but are not
included in balances until posted.

A future `Needs attention` tool requires a separate, typed, server-supported feed of
actionable items with scope, source/status ID, observed timestamp, state and
direct task target. Candidate kinds: unreviewed source observations, failed or
stale acquisition, and a pending/failed command requiring terminal
acknowledgement. Each kind needs its owning contract, authorization and a
reviewed freshness threshold. Until such a feed exists, render `Attention
status unavailable` or omit the list, not `All clear`. Do not infer a reconciled
state from an empty list. Source-only observations and drafts never enter the
posted Position. The attention feed may fail independently; its failure must not
change a valid posted balance into zero or imply a complete review.

| Condition | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| No readable books / valid authorized book returning zero totals | Empty workspace state / exact-zero row; no inference about posted-entry count |
| Unknown or inaccessible scope | 404 with no totals or existence hint |
| Missing credentials / read grant denied | 401 / 403 with no financial body |
| Revision changed between views | 409 `report_snapshot_changed`; discard old evidence and offer explicit refresh |
| Unsupported policy, overflow or timeout | 422 / 503, no partial totals or substitute zero |
| Stale source status | Keep posted Position labelled by revision/date; show separately sourced freshness warning only |

Every report request reauthorizes current read permission before revision
comparison. Responses are `no-store`; no financial rows, tokens or requests in
browser persistence, analytics URLs or shared caches. A later page or drill must
not silently switch revisions. The existing report bounds (4,096 selected rows,
2 MiB response, bounded execution) may make Position unavailable for a larger
book; scale work needs measured evidence, not client truncation.

## Standards and decisions

This is an internal book-query response, not a selected bank-to-bank exchange.
ISO 20022 FAQ and message catalogue R01–R02 were reviewed at public overview
depth; no applicable registered message/version or counterparty usage profile
has been identified for this internal read. The extension therefore uses a
versioned local contract without an ISO designation. Reassess for an actual
financial exchange. ISO 4217 R03 applies to currency identity and versioned
metadata, not FX valuation or account classification. The existing reporting
currency mapping is retained. ISO 21378:2019 R04 and ISO 21926:2026 R05 are
relevant to future audit extraction/semantics; public abstract/preview only was
reviewed, so no field-level mapping or conformance is claimed. The proposed
Position response is not an audit export. No purchased normative text, external
usage profile or live accounting framework was reviewed for this slice.

| Open decision | Owner and condition |
| --- | --- |
| Cash account membership and change control, including restricted cash and cash equivalents | Owner/accountant under #1; approve policy/version and tests before a Cash total ships |
| Real entity basis, opening balances, FX/close semantics | Owner/accountant #1/#10/#59 before live use |
| Attention sources, thresholds and priority | Owning acquisition/command contracts plus owner workflow review |
| Position labels, scope and first-screen order | Owner approved the all-books overview and gray zebra rows on 2026-10-22; browser evidence remains required for #249 |

**Alternative considered:** derive Cash from account codes or linked bank
accounts. It is easy to display but misclassifies noncash or restricted balances
and is not stable under renamed accounts. **Alternative:** aggregate all account
rows in the browser. It duplicates SQL sign/currency/policy rules and can mix
pages or revisions. The proposed server-owned classified subset preserves the
existing ledger/report boundary, at the cost of a policy workflow and extension.

## Named acceptance evidence

The fixed independent values in [Position sources](../research/position-sources.md)
are review fixtures, not generated expectations. First-slice acceptance in #249
must name tests for: exact server-string totals and comparison mapping
(`PositionOverview` fixed values); max-four scheduling and queued completeness;
current membership and per-request denied/global identity results; independent
book revision/date/currency metadata; partial failure without zero substitution;
valid zero versus unsupported policy, without inferring no posted entries;
stale/scope-change late-response rejection;
no cross-book total or client financial arithmetic; and direct top navigation
with explicit scope/date handoff. Browser screenshots at desktop and 390px must
show approved type, row bands, keyboard labels and readable signed changes.
These are required acceptance cases, not claims of existing test coverage.

Deferred extension tests are `TestPositionCashPolicy` (membership/version and
classification), `TestPositionSourceExclusion` (unposted observations/commands),
and `TestPositionBounds` (policy, precision and response caps). Existing reporting
SQL/HTTP tests remain the authority for exact totals, single-book comparison,
revision checks and current authorization. Owner visual approval does not approve
cash policy, real-book accounting, FX, consolidation, or live use; #1/#59 remain
separate dependencies for those operations.

documents.title: First posting operation boundary
documents.body:
# First posting operation boundary

## Decision and implementation scope

This is the implementation target for the next synthetic PostgreSQL posting PR,
read with the [SQL dictionary](ledger-sql.md) and
[development policy](../decisions/0005-development-accounting-policy.md).
It resolves the earlier enforcement alternatives: restricted database functions
own accounting invariants; Go owns trusted identity, HTTP and whole-transaction
retry. A synthetic implementation and named test evidence now exist in the
[posting proof](../runbooks/posting-proof.md); this is not a production release. Evidence/alternatives are in
[posting source notes](../research/posting-sources.md).

Deliver manual identity/spot posting, journal retrieval, exact reversal and a
trial balance. Controlled test setup creates books, policies, accounts, periods,
principals, memberships and synthetic rates. No runtime setup grant, public
identity provider, production bootstrap, period-close endpoint or worker is part
of this proof. Keep #1/#2's broader gates open; this bounded target does not
resolve their real-entity, close-evidence or export requirements.

## SQL call contract

These signatures are implemented in migration 000002. All names are schema
qualified; routines run as `bookkeeping_owner` with the SQL contract's trusted
search path and explicit grants. No overloads or defaulted identity arguments.

| Function | Parameters, in order | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ledger.post_journal` | actor UUID, entity UUID, book UUID, key text, request UUID, body text | One row: `http_status smallint`, `body jsonb`, `replayed boolean` |
| `ledger.reverse_journal` | actor UUID, entity UUID, book UUID, original journal UUID, key text, request UUID, body text | Same receipt result |
| `reporting.get_journal` | actor UUID, entity UUID, book UUID, journal UUID | `jsonb` matching OpenAPI Journal |
| `reporting.trial_balance` | actor UUID, entity UUID, book UUID, through-date text | `jsonb` matching OpenAPI TrialBalance |

Actor and request UUID come from trusted Go context, never user JSON. No request
hash, actor claim, precomputed total or client-selected SQL function is accepted.
Go binds parameters. Mutation body is the original UTF-8 JSON text so the database
can reject duplicate keys with `IS JSON OBJECT WITH UNIQUE KEYS` before
converting to jsonb. This also protects direct
SQL callers of the granted operation. SQL rejects SQL NULL arguments, unknown or
missing fields, JSON null, wrong types and unsupported operation shapes.

For reads, SQL validates the date just as for writes. Business dates use strictly
`YYYY-MM-DD`, real Gregorian dates in years 0001–9999; no infinity or flexible SQL
date coercion. UUID text inside JSON uses standard hyphenated form, case-insensitive,
then normalizes to lowercase. Reject invalid UTF-8/U+0000 and dates/amounts that
cannot round-trip. Go returns no success until its COMMIT succeeds.

## One authority per rule

| Rule | Authority and check |
| --- | --- |
| Network body bound and token verification | Go: 1 MiB bytes, issuer/audience/expiry/subject; no database connection for invalid token |
| Durable input shape/bounds | SQL: same byte bound, 2–1000 lines, duplicate/unknown keys rejected, required nonnull strings, positive exact amounts; Go may reject earlier but never authorize a bypass |
| Principal, entity and permission | SQL reloads current rows; trusted Go principal mapping is the documented trust boundary |
| Policy, account dates and period | SQL resolves exactly one effective policy/period and scoped active accounts |
| Currency and conversion | SQL resolves immutable currency versions by accounting date; identity prohibits a rate ID; spot recomputes exact rounded amount from an eligible stored rate |
| Balance, immutability, reversal | SQL validates full journal; no API role table DML; reversal copies historical values, bypassing fresh-rate selection only |
| Replay, audit and outbox intent | SQL inserts them atomically with the journal; no separately committed receipt |
| Retry and response | Go rolls back/retries the entire transaction on 40001/40P01; emits safe mapped errors only |

A replay checks input syntax and current permission before looking up its receipt;
it does not revalidate rates, account activity, policy/period or expected revision
against today's mutable state. An original historical reversal preserves valuation
but still checks the target period and active accounts. Direct owner/superuser
access is outside runtime guarantees and remains controlled migration authority.

## Exact rounding and amount checks

SQL accepts original decimal **strings**, validates lexical bounds before any
numeric typmod cast, then performs exact unrestricted-numeric multiplication.
Round positive product `x` at scale `s`: let `u = x * 10^s`, `n = floor(u)` and
`f = u - n`; use `n` when `f < 0.5`, `n+1` when `f > 0.5`; at equality choose the
even integer. Divide that integer by `10^s`. Check range/positive result and exact
agreement with the client assertion before storing. Do not substitute PostgreSQL
`round(numeric, s)`, which uses another tie rule [P02]. No float intermediary.

Trailing zeroes up to the lexical storage bound are accepted: `1.000` satisfies
USD two-decimal value precision; `1.001` does not. Decimal syntax with more than
nine fractional digits fails before normalization even if extra digits are zero.
Currency minor units constrain transaction amounts; functional policy scale
constrains functional amounts. Missing metadata or an unsupported scale fails.
The engine must reject unsupported policies rather than applying a USD default.

## Canonical replay version 1

SQL creates and stores `normalized_request jsonb` from validated input, including
operation, path scope, reversal target when applicable, and every accepted body
field. Normalize UUID case and insignificant fractional zeroes; preserve line
order and description/reason Unicode content (no trimming or Unicode normalization).
Revision stays a canonical unsigned decimal string, capped at 9223372036854775807.
Optional absent rate stays absent; explicit null fails. Unknown fields cannot be
silently omitted. The idempotency key is scoped by entity/book/operation, bound to
actor, and excluded from payload; transport request UUID is also excluded.

Compare the full normalized jsonb for equality under `canonical_version = 1`.
Object order is immaterial, array order is material. `request_hash` is computed in
SQL as SHA-256 over UTF-8 `normalized_request::text`; it is an integrity/diagnostic
field, **not** the equality authority. No pgcrypto extension is needed for core
`sha256(bytea)`. Never accept a caller hash. Persist the normalized request and
version for the book lifetime with the receipt, under financial-data access and
retention rules; never log the payload. Preserve version-1 interpretation for old
receipts across upgrades; a new serializer/hash cannot authorize a new effect.

Alternatives: hashing raw HTTP bytes spuriously conflicts on formatting;
Go-only canonicalization trusts a bypassable SQL parameter. Exact stored semantic
comparison costs up to one bounded request per successful command but avoids
using digest equality as the sole financial replay decision.

Same key/actor/normalized payload returns original status/body without writes;
same key with changed body, operation target or actor conflicts. Different
operation names have separate keys by design. New key plus stale expected revision
conflicts; a failed transaction stores no receipt. No TTL, arbitrary replay reset
or retry with a silently changed expected revision.

## Locking and failure protocol

Mutation starts SERIALIZABLE. Lock principal FOR SHARE, entity FOR SHARE,
membership FOR SHARE, then book FOR UPDATE; subsequent order follows the SQL
contract (receipt, period, accounts in UUID order, original journal). Entity
archive, principal disable and membership revoke update the corresponding locked
row. Book disable/setup/account changes use the book lock. This closes the entity
archive race without serializing all posting across an owner's different books.
Missing membership is denied; a concurrent grant may require a fresh request.

The database routines reject an incorrect transaction isolation level; they do
not begin/commit transactions. Each successful mutation increments revision once
and writes one journal, its lines, audit action, receipt and outbox intent. Revision
exhaustion fails before writes; never wrap. No external side effects occur inside
the transaction. At most three attempts within a five-second total request budget;
transaction-local timeouts respect the remaining budget. An uncertain COMMIT is
resolved only by retrying the same operation/key/body in a fresh transaction.

Read functions require REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE, with a READ WRITE
transaction to permit authorization row locks. They take principal, entity and
membership FOR SHARE, then book FOR SHARE, so disable/revoke operations use the
same ordering; short report transactions can temporarily block that book's writes.
Reports include inactive accounts
with history and zero-balance configured accounts, sort by account code then UUID,
and count both originals and reversals. Return a safe `result_out_of_range` 422
if aggregate amounts exceed the documented response bounds; do not truncate.

SQL business errors use fixed SQLSTATEs P2100–P2110 with no financial identifiers
in message/detail: invalid_request/400, not_found/404, permission_denied/403,
revision_conflict/409, idempotency_conflict/409, period_closed/409,
already_reversed/409, invalid_amount/422, invalid_journal/422,
unsupported_policy/422, result_out_of_range/422, respectively. P2111 maps oversized SQL body to request_too_large/413; Go
usually rejects it first. Rate/currency
failures in this slice map to invalid_journal; malformed amount to invalid_amount.
Go never exposes raw database errors. Unexpected failures return generic 500;
serialization/deadlock exhaustion or uncertain commit returns retryable 503.

## PostgreSQL acceptance matrix

| Named test / evidence | Required observation |
| --- | --- |
| `TestSchemaPrivileges` | Actual API role cannot CREATE, SET ROLE owner, read/DML base tables or call ungranted routines; temporary-object/search-path attacks fail |
| `TestPostingInvariants` | Reject empty/unbalanced/mixed-book input; fail after each durable write and at COMMIT; journal/lines/audit/receipt/outbox/revision all roll back |
| `TestMoneyInputBounds` | Half-even vectors above, zero/2/3 minor units, overflow, nonfinite, excess scale, wrong rate direction/date/source, false functional assertion; exact zero balance |
| `TestPostingReplayConcurrency` | Concurrent same key: one effect, one increment; equivalent decimal/object/UUID spelling replays; changed line order/body/actor conflicts; old receipt survives later close/archival |
| `TestEntityReferencesAndPrivileges` / `TestRevocationRace` | Cross-scope references denied; current read/post permission checked; principal/entity/membership revocation ordering proven with barriers, not sleeps |
| `TestJournalCorrectionHistory` | Exact original values/rates reversed; original unchanged; duplicate/full-second reversal rejected; archived target account fails new correction |
| `TestPostingCloseRace` | Controlled test-only closer acquires the production book lock; closing first rejects posting; posting first invalidates stale close revision; no claim of implemented close evidence |
| `TestGoldenMonth` | Load AC-01–10 into actual PostgreSQL, assert fixed balances, original-unit totals and one audit/receipt/outbox per journal; second book isolated |
| `TestManualSpotPosting` | EUR 100 at USD/EUR 1.10 posts USD 110 with preserved rate/currency provenance; full FX lifecycle remains a later gate |
| `TestAPIContract` | Strict shape, denial/redaction, replay headers, COMMIT-before-201, unknown-commit 503; no auth claim from a synthetic actor adapter |
| `TestSchemaCompatibility` / `TestLedgerRestoreReplay` | Fresh/forward migrations and backup restore retain journals, policy/reference versions, receipts and intent; restored retry cannot duplicate |

Use deterministic goroutine/database barriers and capture ordered outcomes. Fake
SQL or fixture arithmetic alone cannot satisfy this matrix. Migration tests use
only disposable PostgreSQL with synthetic seed identities; no live DSN. Current executed evidence and remaining gates live in the posting proof runbook.

documents.title: Runtime identity and private API bridge
documents.body:
# Runtime identity and private API bridge

## Decision

Issue #27 application slice, 2026-10-12. One standalone frontend image reads public
identity configuration at request time and forwards a narrow set of bookkeeping
requests to an operator-selected API. Go remains the authority for signature,
revocation, MFA, principal enrollment and current entity permissions.
Sources G16/G18 in the [GCP register](../research/gcp-sources.md) support the
separate-token and runtime-configuration mechanisms. Synthetic transport tests do
not prove actual Cloud Run IAM or Identity Platform configuration.

## Runtime configuration

`GET /api/auth-config` returns only `apiKey`, `authDomain`, `projectId` from
`JAYBURD_FIREBASE_API_KEY`, `JAYBURD_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN`,
`JAYBURD_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`. These are public identifiers, not credentials.
Only the selected project's `<project>.firebaseapp.com` domain is supported in
this slice; custom domains require explicit review. Partial/invalid settings return
503 and leave sign-in unavailable. No environment dump or provider call occurs.
Responses use `Cache-Control: no-store`; the browser fetches once per provider
mount, omits cookies and abandons late results after unmount. Existing in-memory
MFA/session behavior remains. Remove old NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_* build settings;
they no longer configure this application. A changed configuration requires a new
page load; an existing Firebase app with different identifiers fails closed.

## Transport and authority

Set `BOOKKEEPING_API_MODE=cloud-run`, `BOOKKEEPING_API_ORIGIN` to the exact HTTPS
Cloud Run service origin and `BOOKKEEPING_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` to the exact HTTPS browser
origin. No custom API domains, URL credentials, path/query/fragment or same-target
self proxy are accepted. The backend origin must end in `.run.app`; its value is
also the ID-token audience. No trust is inferred from incoming Host/Forwarded.

The bridge preserves the end-user `Authorization` bearer and fetches a separate
service ID token from Google's fixed metadata endpoint. It sends that token in
`X-Serverless-Authorization`. Incoming service-token, actor, Cookie and forwarding
headers are discarded. Only method, reviewed path/query, user bearer, configured
origin, JSON content type and idempotency key reach the API. Redirects are never
followed. Ambient credential-file, emulator or metadata-host override presence
fails closed; no ADC or service-account key discovery is used.

Cloud Run must separately grant the frontend identity Invoker on only the private
API. The API must validate the end-user token and entity rights on every operation.
The bridge's JWT-shape check is not authentication. No token exchange, identity
claim fabrication, financial cache, write retry or new accounting logic is added.
Frontend concurrency does not replace deployment abuse/rate controls.

Explicit local use requires `BOOKKEEPING_API_MODE=loopback` and distinct HTTP
localhost/127.0.0.1 API/public origins. This still forwards a bearer to the same
Go authorization boundary; it provides no fake identity. Loopback mode is rejected
when Cloud Run's K_SERVICE is present. Missing mode is unavailable, never fallback.

## Bounds and responses

Only workspace, setup, journal posting/read/reversal, dated trial balance and
reviewed durable-command registration/pending/execute/cancel/acknowledge routes are
forwarded. Registration requires an idempotency key; command transitions use their
durable command ID as specified by the existing recovery contract. Close/admin/unknown routes, extra queries and foreign browser origins
are rejected before metadata access. Limits: 32 requests per frontend process,
1 MiB request/response, 16 KiB bearer/metadata token, 4 KiB path/query, 12-second
combined deadline and 3-second metadata deadline. Caller disconnect cancels work.
Buffers are byte-bounded even for streams of tiny chunks. No tokens are cached.

Successful bounded JSON response bytes retain exact decimal strings and receipts.
Error responses retain supported status semantics but replace provider body and
headers with a fixed problem response; cookies and credentials never return to the
browser. Uncertain/lost posting responses remain 5xx, allowing the existing UI to
retry the unchanged request key only after review. No server-side write retry occurs.
All bridge responses are no-store. No request/provider logging is introduced.

## Evidence and next gate

`private API bridge` tests cover separate tokens, header allowlist, route/origin
and configuration denials, lost responses, metadata failures, concurrency,
cancellation and bounded bodies. Public configuration and AuthProvider tests cover
allowlist, unavailable settings and late-result disposal. The container proof
restarts one image with synthetic runtime identifiers and verifies both states.
Existing Go/ledger suites remain the entity/revocation authority, not mocked 401s.

Terraform Invoker grants, runtime environment wiring, real MFA, cross-entity and
revoked-user cloud proof, frontend request logging review, load and rollout/rollback
remain #27 deployment gates. This slice performs no cloud apply or live identity
request. No financial message semantics change; existing ISO 4217/accounting
contracts apply. Runtime authentication/configuration has no applicable ISO 20022
business message and makes no new ISO conformance claim.

documents.title: Independent Production journey — #315

# Independent Production journey — #315

Engineering test decision2026-10-26, source3a2365c. This issue adds synthetic
acceptance only: no product routes, migrations, cloud resources, provider access,
secrets or real records. Existing Sandbox expectations remain independent.

Exercise real Next bridge, Go service, Production HTTP adapters, encrypted bank
and Link stores, restricted SQL sessions, acquisition and reviewed posting. Inject
fictional identity only in the integration executable/component, fake KMS and a
transport that refuses anything except the exact Production request destination.
The Docker network has no external route and no caller DSN or Production reset.
This does not qualify actual identity/MFA, institution support or hosted IAM/KMS.
The controlled pilot prepares owner/worker permissions before enrollment. Production's explicit service constructor deliberately uses operator-configured
books; this test does not claim unprepared-book self-service (#237).

Keep existing literal 0.10/0.20 USD fixture inputs and independently written
expected 0.1/0.2 source amounts, 0.10 debit/credit report change after one reviewed
posting, and zero acquisition journals. Initial empty and multi-page history need
separate explicit runs; exact completed-claim replay must make no provider call.
One selected checking binding is the bounded Production journey, while current
Sandbox three-account binding tests remain unchanged. Simulated provider origin
must be production:false in SQL; all input data is fictional regardless of origin.

Named acceptance: TestProductionProfileJourney (browser complete/reload/lost-result,
selected binding, initial empty/history/pagination/replay, pause/resume, explicit
post/replay/report); existing TestProductionOwnedSessionSQL (owned signed proof,
same addressed encrypted credential); TestProductionProfileCrossEnvironmentDeny,
TestProductionScopePrivileges, TestProductionCredentialEnvironmentBinding,
TestProductionWebhookCurrentScope and TestProductionPostingAuthorityAndReplay.
The matrix in the stage runbook distinguishes one composed journey from component
negatives and actual outstanding hosted gates. Disconnect/revoke must deny fresh
acquisition after the reviewed final posting, preserving existing journals.

Sources: reviewed PP01–09 in production-pilot-sources.md, current literal browser
fixtures and exact SQL/credential/posting contracts from311–314. No new vendor
mechanism/version or financial mapping. Preserve API2020-09-14, ISO4217 original
units, STD-01 applicability and existing ISO21378 review limits; no ISO20022 or
normative conformance claim. Test operational controls have no forced ISO message.

Rejected adapter-only mocks: they cannot prove cross-layer composition. Rejected
calling Production for tests: real authentication/data belong to separately scoped
pilot. Reuse the test fixture infrastructure with explicit closed test mode rather
than introducing application-route auth or another runtime/service/database.
Acceptance does not waive303/320/276, #337 decisions or #316 release review.

documents.title: Production source profile and bank-read-only bookkeeping pilot
documents.body:
# Production source profile and bank-read-only bookkeeping pilot

## Status and purpose

#308 under #90, revised2026-10-25. Owner accepted bank-read-only access with
ledger bookkeeping and linked corrections. The [closed transport baseline](plaid-provider-profile.md)
is an engineering source decision; deployment/isolation/retention and actual pilot
authorization remain pending #337. No activation, spend or security approval.
Owner goal: complete prerequisites, prove Sandbox/recovery, then connect one
personal account and reconcile imported transactions. The approved broader
connect-first redesign is outside this pilot's critical path. Current book-first
setup can be used after its applicable gates pass. No live account is connected
by this document, and no closed issue/deployment is live-bookkeeping approval.

[PP01–06 source review](../research/production-pilot-sources.md) separates vendor
facts from the engineering proposals below. Current adapters, encrypted-token
identity, source/Item SQL and signed webhook scope intentionally require Sandbox.
A Production secret alone cannot enable real accounts. PP01 also rules out moving
an existing test Item to Production: a new owned enrollment is required.

## Proposed pilot boundary

One verified owner, one explicitly named supported source account, one personal
entity/book, one US Transactions Item and desktop browser as the proposed first
client. Exact type/institution, statement currency/interval, deployment targets,
source consent lifetime, retention/deletion, incident contact, cost ceiling and
owner review must be recorded before actual activation. The current pending
account-type question is not an approval. No loan/card accounting policy is
inferred if the selected type changes; unsupported account types stay unbound.
Enforce one reviewed active source binding under the pilot grant. Other accounts
may be discovered within the owner's provider-approved inventory, but remain
unbound; their transactions are not acquired. Reject a second active binding or
foreign-account page atomically rather than treating “one account” as a UI hint.

Bank access is read-only: no payment/money-movement product, Investments,
Liabilities or Transactions Refresh add-on is enabled by default. Intended initial
lookback is90 days, with supplied coverage explicitly recorded. Preserve exact
decimal strings and original currencies; no unrelated-currency totals. A history
hold/overflow/partial response is not complete acquisition and cannot advance a
cursor over discarded data. Posted book balances are not bank balances.

The agent-proposed blanket manual/automatic ledger prohibition is superseded by
the owner's2026-10-25 direction. Jayburd may write balanced journals under current
prepare/post authority and reviewed book policy. Deterministic automation requires
an explicitly enabled versioned rule; pending/unmapped/ambiguous cases go to review.
Bank source consent does not grant ledger posting authority, and a provider/model
category alone does not approve accounting. Acquisition still only publishes
source evidence; a separately authorized posting workflow creates accounting.

Keep source revisions and journal provenance. Posted changes are resolved through
linked exact reversal/replacement or another separately reviewed correction
operation, preserving immutable originals. Reuse existing manual posting/reversal
while #332–#336 deliver reviewed rules, correction resolution/UI and end-to-end
proof. Do not make completion of the entire automatic rule engine a prerequisite
for initial registration. Unimplemented automatic/correction actions remain honestly
unavailable; the present provider-exception queue is not completed correction code.
No live basis, recognition, valuation or loan/card policy is inferred from the
synthetic development profile. Required #1/#10/#90 mandates remain scoped.

Current-authorized committed-receipt readback remains recovery; replay cannot
create another journal. Preserve the command-recovery boundary and current
permissions. The [delivery plan](../plans/source-driven-bookkeeping.md) separates
registration, existing manual bookkeeping and the new automation/correction lane.

This is source-to-statement reconciliation, not an official close or accountant
approval. Relevant #1/#10 criteria and policy implications must be explicitly
dispositioned under #90; this proposal neither closes those issues nor silently
waives their existing gates. Full official-books/cutover remains #13/#58.

## Deployment alternatives and pending choice

Recommended proposal: isolated Production deployment using the existing Go/
PostgreSQL/Next and restricted-worker architecture, with separate workload/SQL
identities, credential/evidence resources, runtime approval and operator receipts.
Separate project/database provisioning and costs require reviewed acceptance;
this is not authority to add a database, service or Terraform root now.

Alternative: explicitly reviewed isolation inside existing infrastructure. It
must demonstrate equivalent source/credential/log/evidence/backup/role and
cleanup boundaries, address real-data classification and retain development
synthetic-only guarantees. Reusing the dev release with a changed secret/URL is
rejected. No architecture decision is accepted by this recommendation alone.

Do not rename or mutate existing Sandbox Items, ciphertext, environment values,
synthetic flags or financial evidence. In particular, never label real records as
synthetic to satisfy existing SQL. Real-data retention and deletion cannot inherit
test reset/cleanup assumptions. No Sandbox diagnostic/verifier can reach Production.

## Authority and integration matrix

| Operation / boundary | Required Production authority and denial |
| --- | --- |
| Runtime composition | Explicit reviewed environment enum/profile and exact deployment target; no ambient discovery, arbitrary endpoint or cross-environment fallback. One provider environment per runtime |
| User setup/Link | Existing verified issuer/subject/MFA/current principal and book authority; explicit finite source consent. Browser cannot select environment, provider endpoint, secret version, service identity or target callback |
| SQL enrollment/source/binding | Operator-approved runtime/provider scope plus existing owner/read/review grants. Immutable environment included in namespace/Item identity; current functions must deny a caller outside their environment capability. No direct table grants |
