| Token storage | Infisical-owned static secret injection with reviewed numeric destination pins; encrypted per-Item tokens with correct environment in AAD and current SQL scope. Cross-environment unwrap/reference/read/write fails before returning plaintext |
| API/provider transport | Closed host/path allowlist and fixed reviewed API-Version; authorized credentials must match runtime environment. No redirect, Sandbox test endpoint or surprise optional product in Production |
| Worker acquisition | Current scoped source consent, generation/binding/lease/cursor checks and exact-money decoder; execution context, credential and runtime environments must agree. Acquisition commits no journal |
| Ledger posting/replay | Current scoped prepare/post authority and reviewed policy/rule; exact source revision and currency provenance. Replay returns the same receipt; corrections append linked effects. No posting from acquisition or categorization alone |
| Signed webhook | Environment-matched key service, cryptographic verification and durable SQL receipt; no unverified body/environment can select a credential or tenant. Owned Item/session repair remains #275; no generic login timestamp as proof |
| Status/disconnect/revoke | Current SQL-authorized reads and local pause/disconnect remain distinct from explicit Item-wide provider removal. Revoke fences queued/inflight authority, retains immutable provenance and records cleanup truthfully |
| Release/rollback | Exact source/images/config/approval/targets and accepted schema floor; separate finite activation, deny expired/mixed/fallback configurations. Old Sandbox image cannot be a compatible Production rollback merely because it starts |
| Comparison/statement | Owner supplies/reviews private records outside agent-visible output. Complete interval, opening/closing balance and exact transaction set under independent expectations; only redacted counts/outcomes retained. Pending/timing differences separately explained |

Each SQL/transport signature, role capability and field propagation must be
reviewed in its bounded child before implementation. Do not solve this with a
global boolean that weakens every Sandbox check. Preserve financial profile
version/provenance; explicitly decide whether the current usage profile is
compatible or needs a new version before DDL. Same semantic money fields do not
by themselves approve changed data provenance or authority.

## Standards applicability

Production remains a proprietary Plaid JSON financial exchange, not ISO20022.
Retain API-Version2020-09-14, exact amount/sign/date/state/identity mapping and
dated ISO4217 references from provider-ingestion, acquisition and liability
contracts. Required multicurrency scope is unchanged; a single-account fixture
is not a one-currency ledger. No new bank message or currency-reference version
is selected here. Profile compatibility/data-origin changes require the reviewed
mapping/version decision in the SQL/transport children. Internal release/IAM/AAD
routing is an operational authority boundary without a forced ISO message.
Audit/export ISO21378 applicability retains its existing review limits; no
normative conformance or accountant approval is claimed.

## Threat review and named acceptance

This bounded STRIDE review is engineering evidence, not independent security
signoff. Auth/secrets/restricted-data/exposure/runtime changes require human
security review before release.

| Threat | Control / proposed acceptance case |
| --- | --- |
| Environment or tenant spoofing (high) | Explicit runtime/SQL capability/current owner scope; TestProductionProfileCrossEnvironmentDeny and TestProductionProfilePrincipalDeny |
| Ciphertext/reference substitution (high) | Environment-bound AAD and addressed SQL authority; TestProductionCredentialEnvironmentBinding, no plaintext/secret in failure output |
| Tampered/replayed Item or event (high) | Signed matched-environment event, owned session proof, durable dedup/revision fences; TestProductionWebhookEnvironmentDeny and existing exact replay/repair cases |
| Financial disclosure or synthetic cleanup of real data (high) | Private Production resources/retention/least privilege, immutable origin, no fixture reset route; TestProductionRecordsNotSynthetic and reviewed backup/deletion receipts |
| Duplicate exchange/journal or false readiness (high) | One durable attempt, source/rule/revision pins, uncertain-result recovery and independent complete-set comparison; TestProductionProfileJourney and TestReviewedRulePostsOnce |
| Unauthorized or stale accounting (high) | Current SQL post permission/policy/rule checks, balanced posting boundary and linked corrections; TestProductionPostingAuthorityAndReplay, TestSourceJournalCorrection50To55. Holds affect uncertain work, not every legitimate journal |
| Outage/overload/cost amplification (medium/high) | Accepted bounded workload/cost/consent limits, no automatic refresh add-on, pause/revoke/restore/kill switch; #64/#89/#58 exact fault evidence |

Proposed names are acceptance obligations, not existing tests. Synthetic fixtures
must drive both profiles with injected transports and real restricted PostgreSQL,
prove foreign credentials/cursors/Items/events/evidence never cross environments,
and retain current Sandbox regression expectations independently of the new code.
Run applicable migration/ledger/core/web/full-stack gates. No default CI makes
Production calls or injects real data. Hosted activation requires a separate
owner-reviewed exact manifest after applicable #88/#274/#275/#276 evidence.

`TestProductionPilotPostingDenied` is a superseded proposal, not a completed test.
Replacement acceptance proves acquisition alone has zero ledger effects, legitimate
authorized posting changes reports exactly once, and unauthorized/stale/revoked
posting denies at actual restricted SQL/API/runtime boundaries. Rule/correction
cases have independently fixed expected journals and original units. Source50 ->
original50 -> bank revision55 -> reversal50/replacement55 must retain original
history and net55, including lost commit/replay. #300's separate unposted Sandbox
oracle retains absolute-zero requirements; do not weaken it or fake zero after
legitimate accounting. #336 owns complete corrective/report proof.

## Decisions still needed before implementation/activation

Owner/security reviewer under #337: accept deployment/data isolation; exact permitted
profile and role/retention threat controls. SQL/transport review: signatures,
capabilities and financial usage-profile compatibility. Qualification coordinator:
all applicable matrix rows and existing #90 policy/reconciliation/scale gates
have explicit evidence/disposition, never suite-name inference. Owner pilot:
account/type/institution/platform, private credentials, complete statement
interval, cost/duration/retention and final approval of the concrete activation.

The implementation children cover SQL authority, profile/transport, credential
and runtime composition, signed webhook/environment isolation, release preparation
and independent synthetic integration. Their IDs and current blockers live in
#308; claim no migration version or writer until the relevant decisions are accepted.

| Issue | Bounded delivery | Hard source prerequisites |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#311](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/311) | SQL environment/data-origin/current authority and restricted functions; retain legitimate scoped posting | Accepted #308 source baseline, exact reviewed SQL contract; sole SQL writer |
| [#312](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/312) | Closed provider profile, enrollment and sync transports | Accepted #308 |
| [#313](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/313) | Credential AAD/addressed storage and managed API/worker composition | #311/#312 |
| [#314](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/314) | Matched-environment key/event/receipt/wakeup | #311/#312; coordinate #271/#275 interfaces and exclusive files |
| [#315](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/315) | Independent offline Production-profile journey, cross-environment and scoped posting/replay authority | #311/#312/#313/#314 |
| [#316](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/316) | Exact finite release/rollback/isolation package | #308/#311–#315 and accepted #337; actual activation stays separately scoped in #90 |

These are native children/blockers of #90, not competing epics. All remain
unclaimed/blocked for implementation until their reviewed prerequisites hold.
SQL and Go profile work can be separate future leases after contract acceptance;
one SQL writer and coordinator ownership of shared profile/CLI remain required.

documents.title: Production credential/runtime composition — #313
documents.body:
# Production credential/runtime composition — #313

Coordinator source decision, 2026-10-26, before implementation. Builds on merged
#311/#312; no deployment/resource/pilot decision is made for #337. No SQL, browser
or financial message changes. Proprietary Plaid2020-09-14 and existing ISO4217
money semantics remain unchanged; operational key/AAD/config metadata has no
applicable registered ISO20022 message. ISO21378 access limits remain unchanged.

## Closed metadata and authority

Legacy constructors/omitted environment remain Sandbox-only. Explicit Production
managed configuration uses `provider-environment=production`, numeric exact
static GSM versions named jayburd-prod-bank-sync-client-id/client-secret, prod
Infisical namespace and dedicated registry/evidence names. Infisical remains the
secret owner; this task neither reads nor delivers the reported
`plaid_production_secret`. Its source version/destination mapping and least-privilege
delivery must be owner-reviewed in #316. Secret contents cannot prove their own
environment; exact approved references and delivery evidence are required.

Production requires explicit bank/link KMS cryptoKey resource names in the runtime
project (us-central1); no dev keyring, mutable version alias or arbitrary URL.
API/worker Cloud SQL IAM logins use dedicated jayburd-prod-api/sync/publisher names;
existing development identities stay unchanged. These are source naming profiles,
not provisioned or approved resources. Production mode rejects development instance,
registry/evidence/key/static references before dependency I/O. Explicit finite
approval fences every outbound dependency request. Cold expired API startup retains
SQL-only status/pause/disconnect/receipt recovery with zero secret/KMS/provider I/O.

Before begin and every provider operation, current SQL
connection_provider_context authorizes actor/entity/book and must agree with the
immutable runtime environment, data origin and both exact configured key resources.
No context caching or browser-selected environment. Production uses existing
configured-book enrollment, not creator onboarding that could manufacture an
unconfigured Production scope. SQL owns current permissions, consent and revision
fences; comparison is runtime anti-confusion, not duplicated permission logic.
Each private attempt must match the runtime profile before provider/credential use.

Bank AAD retains existing fixed tuple/profile and now accepts the two closed
environments. Sandbox ciphertext/AAD stays byte-compatible; Production tuples differ
by environment. Production Link AAD appends the explicit environment to the existing
actor/entity/book/attempt tuple; Sandbox tuple stays unchanged. Bank and Link use
separate configured wrapping capabilities and exact numeric key-version checks.
Addressed storage and current SQL authority precede unwrap; worker expected
environment/Item/reference/version must match before KMS/static credentials.
No relabeling of existing envelopes, new cipher, plaintext SQL or credential logging.

Production notification/reconnect remains rejected here until #314's separate
matched receiver/key/receipt capability is implemented and qualified. No arbitrary
callback option, Sandbox receiver or hosted-repair opt-in in Production. Empty
receiver permits source construction testing only and is not release-ready.

## Evidence and alternatives

PP08 in production-pilot-sources records selected Google KMS AAD and Secret Manager
version-access sections and refreshed Plaid host/storage sections. Vendor facts:
different AAD cannot decrypt; version aliases exist; Items cannot move environments.
Our exact version pins, separate names, per-request preflight and immutable profile
are engineering controls, not vendor policy or security signoff. A secret/URL swap
was rejected because it leaves SQL/key/evidence identities mixed. A duplicate
credential implementation was rejected to preserve current exact recovery behavior.

STRIDE: profile/key/reference substitution (high) -> current SQL preflight, closed
runtime, exact immutable versions and AAD; unauthorized unwrap (high) -> current
addressed SQL scope and worker lease; disclosure (high) -> memory-only secrets,
fixed errors and no raw diagnostics; expired authority (high) -> outbound deadline,
cold inert startup; source mixing (high) -> dedicated IAM/evidence naming and
explicit transport environment. Residual actual IAM/delivery/retention/restore and
pilot acceptance remains #337/#316/#90. Human sensitive-source review before merge.

Acceptance: TestProductionCredentialEnvironmentBinding; Production API/worker
configuration mismatch/expiry/static-only startup tests; private-context-before-begin
and wrong-origin/key tests; actual restricted PostgreSQL Production credential
roundtrip/current-denial tests; unchanged Sandbox credential/recovery regressions.
Synthetic-only default tests, core/race/build, migration/ledger regression and
app-integration before handoff. No new dependencies or migration.

documents.title: Production source SQL authority — #311
documents.body:
# Production source SQL authority — #311

## Decision and boundary

Coordinator engineering review2026-10-25, before forward DDL. Owner assigns311
to this branch and313 separately. Accepted308/312 and current mainc843315 are
the baseline. This contract specifies source authority, not resource provisioning,
an approved real accounting policy, credential injection or live activation.
Only synthetic records are used in tests, including fictional Production-profile
rows; Production environment is a routing/provenance value, not a test-data claim.

Retain `jayburd-plaid-transactions/1`: its exact amounts/original lexemes,
ISO4217 currency-version/date/sign/state mapping and API2020-09-14 do not change.
Environment and Item already participate in namespace identity. Extend supported
environment values, not money semantics or an old row's origin. Existing Sandbox
records stay Sandbox/synthetic; newly enrolled Production Items have synthetic=false.
Data origin is derived from the immutable environment, never supplied by browser
JSON. No Production data is marked synthetic to pass a development constraint.

## Physical specification and administration

One new bookkeeping_owner-owned table `integration.provider_scope`, one row per
entity/book, FK to ledger.book, composite PK(entity_id,book_id): environment text
NOT NULL IN(sandbox,production); api_login/worker_login name NOT NULL;
bank_key/link_key text nullable only for Sandbox; enabled boolean NOT NULL;
revision bigint NOT NULL positive. Key resources are bounded canonical Cloud KMS
cryptoKey names, not secret values or mutable secret aliases. Production compares
envelope key resource exactly to the approved scope key before accepting ciphertext.
No new KMS key is created by configuration. Exact resources remain an owner313/337
decision; fixtures use fictional names. Separate new SQL logins are required for
Production; neither may also belong to an existing Sandbox scope. API login must
be a safe LOGIN with bookkeeping_api and no owner/sync/webhook/operator privileges;
worker must satisfy existing strict sync_login checks. No direct table grants.

Owner-only `integration.configure_provider_scope(actor uuid,e uuid,b uuid,k text,
raw text) RETURNS jsonb`, SECURITY INVOKER, requires current_user=bookkeeping_owner,
SERIALIZABLE and existing source_operator_authorize. Closed raw keys:
environment,api_login,worker_login,bank_key,link_key,enabled. This is an operator
function, never granted to API/worker or mounted as a browser endpoint. Initial
configuration requires no connection attempts, Items, source namespaces or journals
in that book: it cannot promote/relabel an existing Sandbox book. Environment,
logins and key resources are immutable after creation; subsequent calls may only
toggle enabled and increment revision. Same-key/body receipt replay is exact;
changed-body replay conflicts. No automatic role grants, retention/delete policy
or source consent is created. Lock principals/entity/book first, then scope row;
existing connection receipts retain operator audit facts. Revocation uses the same
book lock as ongoing work, so it cannot commit through an authorized transaction.

Internal `integration.provider_environment(e uuid,b uuid) RETURNS text` obtains
the current scope FOR SHARE and verifies session_user against its allowed API or
worker login, current role safety and enabled state. No `SET`/caller actor or JSON
can select a profile. An unconfigured book retains the legacy Sandbox behavior
only for logins not explicitly registered for Production elsewhere. A configured
Production book has no fallback: missing/wrong/revoked scope/login failsP2701.
Both connection_authorize and sync_authorize retain their existing current
principal/membership/book/source/consent/generation/lease checks and additionally
require this environment match. The configured connection worker must match the
approved scope worker. Production API cannot use an unconfigured Sandbox book.

API-only `integration.connection_provider_context(actor uuid,e uuid,b uuid)
RETURNS jsonb`, SECURITY DEFINER, reuses connection_authorize and returns only
environment, data_origin(test/provider), scope_revision as decimal string,
bank_key/link_key. #313 must compare this preflight to its explicit immutable
runtime profile and configured key resources BEFORE begin/provider I/O. It may not
reinterpret a missing scope as Production. No secret, token or envelope is returned.

## Persistence and existing function inventory

Add connection_attempt.environment NOT NULL, backfill ONLY existing rows to their
already-known sandbox origin, and preserve it in its immutable guard. New attempts
derive environment from authorized scope at INSERT; clients cannot write a value.
Private render_connection adds environment/data_origin; public projection unchanged.
sync_item keeps its existing synthetic boolean with the new two-way CHECK:
sandbox AND synthetic=true OR production AND synthetic=false. Extend
source_namespace provider profile check and bank_credential environment check to
the same closed enum. No update of old Item, namespace, receipt, ciphertext or journal.
Insertion guards require each Item/namespace/credential environment to match its
book scope and retain immutable identity on update. Scope cannot subsequently be
reassigned. Cross-table validation uses owned functions/triggers, not a CHECK that
reads other tables. Unique(provider,environment,Item[,account]) remains unchanged.

Latest implementations reviewed:13 connection_authorize/lock/item_pin and
sync_authorize;32 owned repair wrappers and renamed pre32 functions;28 bind_connection
and sync_context;20 put_bank_credential;33 put_link_handoff and its pre32 delegate;
18 bank_credential_authorize/get/worker reads;12 operator enroll and observation
provenance;25 installed currency history/validation;29 exact precision. Patch only
the actual current implementation or active pre32 delegate, preserving wrappers,
ACLs, exact replay/body equality and existing lock/receipt semantics.

confirm_connection_credential's pre32 delegate creates a new Item using a.environment
and synthetic=(environment=sandbox); bind28 uses i.environment for namespace
creation. connection_lock/item_pin reject mismatched attempt/Item scope. Credential
authorization additionally matches env to the exact attempt. put credential and
new-Link handoff use the approved Production key; Sandbox keeps the existing
canonical dev-key grammar. Worker reads derive env/ref from sync_context as before.
Production owned reconnect remains unavailable until314's matched signed receiver
and313's repair runtime exist; do not broaden32's Sandbox-only proof functions.
Webhook ingress, Sandbox diagnostics/verifier and operator enroll remain Sandbox.

Pilot-bound source review refinement before DDL change: Production bind permits
exactly one selected account, and rejects another Item while a non-disconnected
stream already exists in the book (paused counts as bound). Reuse the existing
book lock; no additional lock or race-prone counter. Known committed bind receipt
replay is handled before this new-work limit. Sandbox retains its existing
multi-account behavior. TestProductionSingleAccountPilotLimit names both the
multi-selection and second-Item rejection with unchanged source counts.
An outer begin_connection wrapper rejects a fresh new attempt when any existing
Production Item is not disconnected, before Link/provider work. Existing-key
recovery remains allowed; the owned32 wrapper/delegate is preserved underneath.

No Go credential/runtime/CLI changes belong here. Acquisition's internal SQL
context validator may accept the two closed environments only after the new SQL
scope/worker checks are tested; no default Production constructor is activated.
The runner already propagates trusted environment from312. #313 owns crypto AAD
and composition matching; it must not use this SQL change as credential-origin proof.

## Posting, migration and acceptance

No new posting grant or blanket posting ban. Acquisition alone has zero journal
and journal.posted effects; current legitimate prepare/post/reversal/replay remains
subject to existing book policy and authorization. Synthetic USD/EUR tests do not
approve dev-accrual-usd-v1 for a real book. Corrections remain333 and closed-period/
policy restrictions remain unchanged. No automatic category/model posting.

Forward migration34 only after fresh sole-writer register check. Down refuses if
any Production scope/attempt/Item/namespace/credential exists, including disabled
scope: deleting/rewriting retained provenance is not rollback. On empty/Sandbox-only
state restore exact prior definitions/constraints and remove additive objects;
roundtrip and existing installed-migration checks must pass. SQL files1–33 immutable.

Named tests on actual restricted login sessions and disposable PG17:
TestProductionRecordsNotSynthetic; TestProductionProfileCrossEnvironmentDeny;
TestProductionScopeRevocationAndReplay; TestProductionCredentialSQLBinding;
TestProductionPostingAuthorityAndReplay; TestProductionScopePrivileges. Include
missing/foreign login/book/key/env, attempted JSON profile injection, revoked
current permissions/consent, duplicate commands, existing Sandbox regressions,
independent zero-journal acquisition and exact single authorized post/replay.
Tests must not infer success from administrator calls or mocked PostgreSQL.
Run migration-test, ledger-test, connection-state/credential/acquisition regressions
and core check/test/build. Proposed names are obligations until actually executed.

## Sources, alternatives and threat review

PP01/04/06 and new PP07 in the annotated source register record review depth.
PostgreSQL17 CREATE FUNCTION SECURITY DEFINER section266–292 establishes safe
search_path and atomic PUBLIC revoke/selective grants; Constraints5.5.1 paragraphs
on NULL/cross-table CHECK establish why typed NOT NULL and insertion guards are
needed. These sources establish mechanisms, not this authorization design.
Plaid API host/storage sections establish separate nontransferable Items and
sensitive tokens. Full paid ISO/GAAP texts remain unreviewed; no conformance claim.
This operational authority/AAD protocol has no applicable registered ISO20022
message; proprietary financial mapping and ISO4217 versioned currencies unchanged.
ISO21378 audit relevance retains existing abstract-only access limits.

Rejected alternatives: a global production boolean weakens Sandbox boundaries;
caller-selected environment permits confused deputy use; rewriting rows/ciphertext
destroys origin/AAD; a new DB/service without337 approval expands infrastructure.
Book-scoped explicit authority preserves existing components and legacy Sandbox
while requiring a separately configured new Production book/runtime identity.
Tradeoff: reassignment of Production logins/keys is deliberately unavailable in
this initial scope and needs a separately reviewed rotation/recovery operation.

STRIDE: spoofed runtime/tenant (high) -> session_user + scoped role/login match;
source relabel/tamper (high) -> immutable env/two-way origin/namespace uniqueness;
replay/escalation (high) -> existing current grants and immutable receipts; key
substitution/disclosure (high) -> exact configured key and no plaintext SQL/logs;
revocation races (high) -> SERIALIZABLE/current book locks and whole retry;
unintended egress (high) -> no provider calls/default activation in this change.
Human source/security review remains required before merge; operator resource and
live policy approval are separate. This is coordinator design, not independent signoff.

documents.title: Production signed webhook isolation — #314
documents.body:
# Production signed webhook isolation — #314

Coordinator engineering decision2026-10-26, before implementation. Source baseline
merged313/d0b141b; no deployment/resources, public exposure, credentials, provider
calls or activation. Human sensitive-source review required before merge. Actual
Sandbox signed/reconnect qualification remains303/320/275;315 independently tests
the integrated Production profile,337/316 approve resources and finite release.

## Profile and transport

Legacy constructors/omitted runtime metadata remain Sandbox. Explicit profile
constructors require a valid private plaidprofile value. Key HTTP client, verifier,
SQL adapter and managed receiver must agree before construction. Interface values
used for tests are injected capabilities; no caller body can choose a key URL or
environment. Production key fetch uses only production.plaid.com at fixed POST
/webhook_verification_key/get with API2020-09-14, bounded three-second/no-redirect/
no-retry transport and existing key-ID limits. Credentials resolve lazily through
two exact numeric jayburd-prod-bank-sync-client-* versions, not request paths.

Each verifier owns its profile-local cache; equal key IDs in different environments
share no state. ES256/P-256, canonical header/claims/signature, five-minute age,
future skew, key metadata, raw-body SHA256, duplicate JSON and size/concurrency/
rate budgets remain unchanged. Classify Transactions or modern LINK/SESSION_FINISHED
only after authentication; then require event.environment equals the runtime.
Unverified Item/Link/session identifiers never select tenant, credential or profile.

Managed Production receiver uses the separate jayburd-prod-webhook IAM SQL identity,
nondevelopment instance/project, exact Production static references and finite
approval. Invalid/mixed/expired config rejects before dependency construction.
Each outbound identity/secret/key request rechecks the same deadline; cached-key
events also deny after expiry. No bank-token/KMS/sync/post capability is added to
the receiver. Same fixed route/body/header/time limits; no infrastructure exposure.

Production Link notification configuration is optional for source construction,
but release requires a reviewed receiver. A nonempty URL must be exactly
https://jayburd-prod-webhook-PROJECT_NUMBER.us-central1.run.app/webhooks/plaid,
derived from explicit canonical nondevelopment project-number metadata. No arbitrary
HTTPS URL or browser selector. Hosted repair is a separate false-by-default opt-in
requiring this matching destination. Empty receiver is never release readiness.

## Migration35 SQL design

Keep one PostgreSQL authority and existing restricted bookkeeping_webhook role.
Extend webhook_ingress/webhook_receipt/link_session_receipt closed environment
constraints to sandbox/production. Add immutable webhook_login_profile(login_name
name PRIMARY KEY,environment text NOT NULL in that enum), backfilled from existing
ingress and immutable operator receipts, including retired pre35 Sandbox logins.
No runtime table grants. Operator-only existing set_webhook_ingress
signature binds a safe login permanently to one environment; serialize with the
existing advisory lock, preserve exact operator replay, deny reuse across profiles
even after disabling/replacing ingress. No automatic new ingress row or grant.
The active ingress row still selects one separately provisioned login per profile.

Existing verified receipt signatures and roles remain. Both accept functions must
check login safety, immutable profile and currently enabled ingress before mapping
anything. Transactions resolve Item only within verified environment, retain current
consent/source/principal/worker/namespace checks and bounded atomic wakeups. Production
additionally requires current enabled provider_scope with matching environment and
worker login, under the existing principal/book lock order. Receipt/demand commits
atomically; replay still reauthorizes, cannot duplicate demand or post a journal.
Login safety denies verifier/predefined-role membership and direct application-table
privileges in SQL as well as the Go adapter; role drift is not hidden by a prior
successful bootstrap. Disabling a known unsafe ingress remains possible.

Session lookup counts only exact stored Link hash AND environment. No match,
ambiguity, new-mode, claimed or terminal session is ignored without creating authority.
Only an owned reconnect uses existing receipt-lock/principal/book/worker/sibling/
source/consent checks. Require current provider_scope for Production. Authenticate
the attempt's exact environment throughout scope/claim/credential/handoff; derive
Item from the existing attempt, never a callback or generic login timestamp.
Production owned repair reuses the existing protocol, replacing Sandbox literals
only where reviewed: owned_repair_scope, proof-pinned claim environment, addressed
repair read and reconnect handoff key validation. Bank/Link AEAD uses313's explicit
Production profile/key preflight; no credential exchange/rotation/new version.
All existing ambiguity/expiry/revocation/paused-sibling/replay controls remain.

Owned scope internals stay private; API gets no receipt-ingress/table authority,
webhook gets no credential/claim/confirm/catchup/post authority. SECURITY DEFINER
search_path and PUBLIC revoke/selective grant remain in one transaction. Merged
SQL1–34 immutable.35 down refuses when Production ingress/login-profile/receipt or
repair-claim history exists; it preserves provenance and never deletes to downgrade.
Empty/Sandbox-only disposable down restores exact prior functions/constraints/ACLs.

## Sources, standards, alternatives and evidence

PP09 selected Plaid verification/header/key/age/raw-body and modern session fields,
plus PG17 safe-definer sections266–292 reviewed2026-10-26. Vendor facts establish
signature/session mechanisms, not our tenant/role policy or hosted qualification.
API2020-09-14/SDK49 unchanged. Operational proprietary receipt/AAD/routing has no
registered ISO20022 financial message; no money/currency/recognition mapping changes.
ISO4217 and ISO21378 applicability/access limits remain as reviewed. No conformance.

Rejected global environment fallback or body-selected key service: confused deputy
and profile mixing. Rejected a new SQL role hierarchy that would require duplicating
all role-safety checks; immutable environment-bound existing dedicated logins retain
the reviewed role. Rejected global cross-environment Link-hash lookup; it could
associate one environment's event with the other's attempt. No added database/service.

STRIDE: spoofing/tampering(high) -> exact signature/profile/raw bytes and matched
key transport; cross-tenant escalation(high) -> current SQL scope, owned hash and
dedicated immutable login profile; replay(high) -> atomic receipt/demand and immutable
claim; disclosure(high) -> projection-only SQL, no raw secrets/body logs; outage/cost
(medium/high) -> bounded cache/request/expiry, unknown commit retry semantics unchanged.
Residual actual delivery/IAM/isolation/retention remains unproved until hosted gates.

Acceptance: TestProductionWebhookEnvironmentDeny; explicit-key-host/cache mismatch
tests; real restricted SQL signed Transactions duplicate/reordered/current-consent/
unknown-Item/revoked-scope cases; owned Production Link proof/claim/credential and
wrong-profile/session replay; API/worker/receiver cross-role denial;35 fresh/replay/
down/forward and existing Sandbox regressions. Core, migration, ledger, webhook,
bootstrap, connection/credential/recovery, locked web and app-integration gates.

documents.title: Provider ingestion and Plaid adapter
documents.body:
# Provider ingestion and Plaid adapter

## Decision and scope

**Proposed contract**, owner project maintainer, 2026-10-13, [#70](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/70).
The [runtime implementation boundaries](provider-runtime-boundaries.md) reconcile
this proposal with merged migrations9–11 and define the current synthetic build.
Proposal capabilities below must not be read as implemented provider behavior.
Plan Plaid server-to-server Transactions alongside [CSV](statement-import.md),
feeding a shared source-observation/review layer. CSV is one fixture adapter, not
the architecture. No provider runtime, source tables, general draft API or automated
posting exists by virtue of this document. [PI01–PI08](../research/plaid-ingestion-sources.md)
record official source review. #8 owns importer implementation; #13 owns provider
qualification/cutover; #63/#7 own generic work delivery. No live calls authorized.

Propose profile `jayburd-plaid-transactions/1`, explicit `Plaid-Version: 2020-09-14`,
Transactions-only product access, initially depository accounts bound to monetary
asset accounts. Countries, institution coverage, fees/consent and selected SDK are
unresolved implementation gates. Credit/loan/investment support needs distinct
account mapping; do not silently treat it as deposits. Native bank CSV, camt and
Plaid remain distinct protocols with shared internal semantics.

## Standards applicability

Plaid JSON is a proprietary financial exchange, not ISO 20022/camt. The mapping
below is the proposed non-ISO-adapter decision required by [standards](standards.md);
owner review is required before implementation. ISO 4217 applies to currency-code/
validity references; ISO 8601 date semantics use the existing RFC3339 full-date
profile. Preserve ISO currency metadata versions; do not call unofficial assets
ISO currencies. Audit exports under ISO 21378/21926 remain separate unresolved
mapping work. No IBAN/BIC/LEI interpretation is introduced. #17's official schema/
usage-profile gap remains open; SDK/schema acceptance alone is not conformance.

## Connection lifecycle and authorization

A connection is one account-specific acquisition stream owning provider environment,
Item, provider account, entity and book. Multiple streams may share an Item credential
reference; that reference grants no bookkeeping authority. Each approved
provider account maps explicitly to one stable internal source-account ID and ledger
account, with binding revision and consent provenance. Never infer ownership from
mask, name, institution or public-token contents. One Item cannot fan out into
multiple LLCs/books in this first profile. A separate reviewed Link/connection is
required for another ownership scope; detect suspected duplicate Items and require
an explicit overlap decision before activation, not silent coalescing.

An authenticated authorized user begins a durable Link attempt naming the intended
scope. Server creates the restricted Link token; browser holds temporary Link/public
tokens in memory only. Bind the return to the initiating principal, attempt, scope,
expiry and anti-replay nonce; reauthorize before server token exchange and activation.
Backend validates actual Item/account metadata and the approved binding manifest;
client Link metadata is not ownership evidence. Unmapped/unsupported accounts remain outside acquisition; they cannot activate a
stream until separately bound under an accepted profile. Account metadata may be
used for owner selection, but its transaction payload is not collected.

Application DB stores only opaque credential references/version, never access tokens.
Infisical owns provider client credentials and per-connection token material; workload
identity gets least-privilege access to the needed references. No token enters URLs,
queue bodies, logs, browser storage, fixtures or issues. Provisioning and atomic
reference-publication need a separate secret-store consistency design. A failed
exchange/rotation acknowledgement leaves `credential_recovery_required`; do not
blindly repeat a potentially non-idempotent provider operation or claim connected.

Proposed states: `link_pending`, `binding_review`, `active`, `reauthorization_required`,
`paused`, `credential_recovery_required`, `disconnect_pending`, `disconnected`. Update mode repairs the existing Item
where possible; verify identity/account manifest before resuming its checkpoint.
New Item means a new acquisition generation and overlap review, never assumed ID
continuity. Item credentials have a shared lifecycle distinct from account streams:
rotation atomically pauses/fences **all sibling streams**, writes the replacement
securely, then publishes one consistent credential reference/version to the group.
Resume each authorized stream only after replacement verification. A credential-only
change preserves provider observation identities; checkpoint adoption requires
verified same Item/account/filter, never token identity alone. An uncertain rotation
keeps all siblings in credential recovery.

Disconnecting one account disables/fences only its stream and does not call
`/item/remove`. Removing the entire Item requires explicit approval covering all
affected bindings, atomically disables/fences every sibling locally, and separately
tracks provider removal until confirmed. Lost removal responses stay unresolved,
not falsely deleted. There is no cross-account surprise revocation from disconnect.
Removing provider access never deletes posted journals or their evidence links.

Current SQL grants are read/prepare/post/close; connect/import/sync capabilities
are **proposed**, not implemented permissions. Separate grants/consent are required
for connection management and source acquisition. Each call and publication rechecks
its account-specific connection, consent, entity/book/source-account grant and
stream generation. Revoking one binding pauses/fences that stream; revoking Item
consent or its controlling principal pauses all associated streams. Other authorized
account streams need not stop for a single-account binding revocation.

New accounts remain unbound and are not automatically synced. A filtered response
containing any different/unapproved account fails closed: discard that payload and
staging, do not advance cursor, expose only a safe remediation code. The worker
cannot accept a different account filter from a queue payload or caller parameter.

## Acquisition, staging and complete-update publication

Use `/transactions/sync` with fixed `options.account_id` for each approved stream.
Choose this over Item-wide sync because permission revocation and cursor publication
can stay within one account. Cost: more requests/checkpoints for multiple accounts;
measure during qualification. PI01 documents separate filtered cursors. Stream
identity includes provider, environment, Item, exact account filter, connection
ID and generation. Never implicitly reuse a cursor across changed identity or
configuration. Credential-only rotation may explicitly adopt the existing checkpoint
after same Item/account/filter verification under a new fence; switching between
Item-wide and filtered modes or changing Item/account starts a new generation with
a null cursor and explicit overlap review. The selected implementation supports filtered mode only.

Start historical sync without a cursor; no migration-only `now` shortcut. Proposed
requested history is 90 days at Item initialization, recorded once; availability
still depends on product/institution. Empty initialization remains `initializing`,
not “zero transactions” or “all history complete.” Track initial/historical readiness
and provider last-successful-update separately from our per-stream publication time.

Align with [background work](background-work.md): a durable operation captures
`connection_id`, `connection_generation`, `target_generation` and current checkpoint.
`requested_generation` increments for verified webhook, scheduled or manual wakeups;
`completed_generation` advances only with complete acquisition publication. The
connection `fence_token` is separate from publisher `dispatch_generation`. Queue
messages contain operation/delivery IDs only; scope, cursors and credential references
are loaded internally. These are **new proposed work records**, not an extension of
`ledger.interactive_command`'s setup/post gate or immutable `journal.posted` payloads.

1. Claim connection lease/fence in a short transaction. Capture committed starting
   cursor `C0`, binding manifest and reference versions; create a private staging set.
2. Call sync outside SQL transactions. Preserve raw number tokens and page order,
   protected response provenance/digest, next cursor and `has_more`. Stage each valid
   page durably under current fence; staging is invisible to review/accounting APIs.
3. A successful bounded run may checkpoint **staging continuation**, not publish it.
   A new lease may adopt a valid incomplete set after rechecking generation/C0 and
   acquire a new fence; old worker cannot stage or commit. On page failure, including
   pagination mutation or ambiguous page delivery, abandon that attempt and restart
   the complete update from C0. Never restart only the failed page or mix attempts.
4. Only after `has_more=false`, validate the whole update, including cross-page
   pending lineage and the exact approved account. In one SQL transaction, compare-and-
   swap C0/generation/fence/lease and current authorization; publish immutable source
   revisions/tombstones and review exceptions, final cursor, completion receipt and
   `completed_generation=target_generation`. Update `source_revision`, **not** the
   ledger book revision. Incomplete/invalid sets advance neither public data nor cursor.
5. If requested_generation exceeds completed_generation, persist another bounded
   continuation/wakeup intent atomically. Repeated delivery resolves the receipt;
   commit-ack loss must not replay source effects. New notification during commit
   cannot be erased by an unqualified “sync done” flag.

Proposed engineering bounds (not provider guarantees): sync page size `count=500`; response
2 MiB; call 20s; run 60s/at most 10 pages; lease 90s renewed at 30s; at most 100 pages,
50,000 changes and 50 MiB per complete set; staging lifetime 24h. The #63 handler owns
its tighter transaction/deadline limits. Cap/expiry produces durable `limit_exceeded`
or `staging_expired`, no partial publication; authorized operator review is required
to change bounds. A huge history cannot be “solved” by advancing an incomplete cursor.
Unknown enum/schema or financially material unmapped field holds the set for adapter
review. Additive ignorable metadata must be explicitly allowlisted by parser version.
Do not interpret arbitrary provider URLs or fetch merchant images/websites.

## Observation identity, values and source changes

Durable provider identity is case-sensitive `(provider, environment, item_id,
account_id, transaction_id)`, linked to the stable source-account binding. It excludes
lease, run, filter, credential and connection generation: rotating credentials or
reacquiring history must not manufacture new purchases. A new Item retains distinct
provider identity and needs explicit overlap/continuity review. An
observation revision also names acquisition set/position, parser/API versions and
original value provenance. Same completed acquisition replay is idempotent; same
provider transaction later modified creates a new revision, not a conflicting second
purchase. Preserve all material changes. Ambiguous repeated IDs/change combinations
within a complete set require review rather than invented precedence.

| Provider value | Proposed internal meaning |
| --- | --- |
| JSON `amount` | Decode the original numeric token losslessly before any SDK float conversion. Positive = outflow, negative = inflow; store unsigned exact magnitude and original signed lexeme. Decimal/exponent notation converts by exact coefficient/scale arithmetic, never floating point. Reject >128-byte numeric tokens and exponent outside[-100,100] before expansion; then enforce numeric(38,9) bounds and currency scale. Zero/negative zero retained as review-only observations, not ordinary positive journal lines. |
| `iso_currency_code` / unofficial code | Bind valid ISO code/date to installed currency version. Missing/unsupported/unofficial currency prevents this profile's complete-set publication and records a safe exception; never default USD or sum currencies. |
| `date`, `authorized_date`, optional datetimes | Preserve source posted/pending date separately from authorization date and any supplied timestamp. No local-midnight conversion or substitution of authorized date for accounting date. User later chooses accounting date under book policy. |
| `pending`, `pending_transaction_id` | Source state and explicit lineage only. Pending is ineligible for posting; posted replacement is a distinct ID and must be reviewed at its final amount. A null link on an ordinary directly posted transaction is valid and remains review-eligible. Only suspected but unresolved replacement creates a lineage exception; never guess linkage from equal amounts/names. |
| added / modified / removed | Append new source revision or tombstone, maintain current-source projection and invalidate stale unposted review suggestions. Existing journal and source-to-journal linkage remain immutable; changed/removed evidence on a posted journal creates an exception for explicit correction/reversal review. |
| description/category/enrichment | Inert source text and suggestions, never authority to choose expense/account or execute code. No automatic classification-to-post action. |

Fictional fixed expectations: `12.50` USD → outflow magnitude`12.50`;
`-1.255e2` USD → inflow`125.5` (display125.50); JPY`125` and KWD`1.005` preserve
units. USD`0.001` is unsupported precision, never rounded to a cent. A pending
P 10.00 removed on page 1 and posted Q 12.00 linked to P on page 2 becomes one pending
history plus one eligible posted source, not two purchases. If Q later changes in the same USD currency to
13.00 after a 12.00 USD journal, retain the 12.00 journal and open a 1.00 discrepancy for
review; this does not authorize an automatic 1.00 adjusting entry.

## CSV overlap and accounting boundary

CSV and Plaid observations keep distinct adapter identities even for the same
stable source account. The shared-core key is proposed as
`(entity_id, stable_source_account_id, adapter_namespace, external_entry_id)`; this is a required reviewed
extension of CSV's existing three-part proposal, not a silent change to its file
format. CSV maps to its fixed profile/source namespace and original entry ID;
Plaid maps to provider/environment/Item/account identity and transaction ID, excluding
run/filter/credential generations.
Changing namespaces cannot bypass overlap review or reset dedup tombstones. Record explicit match decisions with actor/time, evidence,
source revisions and one bookkeeping-event group. Amount/date/description equality
is only a candidate, never a dedup key. Two identical coffee purchases with distinct
provider IDs stay two events. A CSV row C and Plaid row P proven to represent one
purchase link to one group without discarding either provenance chain. If C already
has a journal, matching P links evidence to that event and creates no second journal.
Contradictions or uncertain matching block automatic event linkage; separate real
purchases remain separate. Reconnection IDs get the same explicit overlap treatment.

The proposed core owns source revisions, matching decisions, durable drafts and
accounting links; adapters own acquisition and mapping. Source imports never invoke
posting. Draft approval executes reviewed ledger commands later with current ledger
revision/permissions; source revision changes invalidate stale source-based approval.
API/SQL contracts for that boundary are a prerequisite, not implied implemented behavior.

## Verified ingress, retries and privacy

Propose a separately deployed public webhook ingress with signature verification
and only durable wakeup/lifecycle-write authority. The [private API bridge](private-api-bridge.md)
and application Cloud Run API remain private; do not expose the full API to receive
Plaid callbacks. No webhook endpoint or public ingress is created in this slice.
Use a dedicated Plaid webhook verifier, distinct from end-user auth. Require a
single bounded Plaid-Verification JWT, ES256, trusted Plaid-fetched kid/JWK and
valid signature; validate iat age<=5min, proposed future skew<=60s, key metadata and
exact raw-body SHA256 in constant time. Do not deserialize/reserialize before hashing.
Fetch keys only from fixed provider endpoint, never JWT-supplied URLs; bound/cache
keys by kid/environment, reject expired keys, and rate-limit cache misses.
Proposed ingress bounds: 64 KiB body / 8 KiB JWT, strict JSON and approved event schemas.

After verification, resolve environment/Item to its approved active account streams
and persist a scoped delivery receipt plus requested-generation increments/outbox
intents for those streams before 2xx. No unbound account is activated by notification. Use a verified signed-delivery fingerprint for identical replay; different
valid notifications may coalesce into the same outstanding work without losing the
generation signal. No assumption of a provider event-ID field. Unknown/disabled scope
fails with a uniform denial (including an Item with no eligible stream); bad signature/body/age never schedules work. Persistence
failure returns 503. A webhook means “check source,” never a journal or guaranteed
real-time balance. Ignore legacy transaction notifications for sync business logic;
verified lifecycle notifications may mark reauthorization without granting access.

Proposed missed-notification catch-up every 6h and user retry both request the same
worker; neither forces paid refresh. Provider 429/transient failures use bounded
exponential backoff/jitter, Retry-After where supplied, and #63 attempt ceilings.
Consent/login errors pause for user action; unsupported data/limits quarantine for
operator review. Do not hammer a failed connection. UI separately shows last provider
update, last complete publication, initializing, stale (>24h proposed), retrying,
reauthorization-required, disconnected and review exceptions; never “live/synced”
solely because a webhook/task was acknowledged.

Raw authorized staging is private encrypted storage, no public URL/log/body telemetry;
retain no unauthorized account payload. Proposed expiry 24h for abandoned staging,
30 days published raw evidence; normalized revisions, dedup receipts and journal
provenance persist for the approved dataset lifetime. Raw deletion is explicit and
does not free identities for reimport. Provider disconnect, token deletion, source
retention and ledger retention are different actions. Live owner/audience/retention,
legal holds, backup erasure, residency and incident policy remain approval gates;
synthetic proposals are not statutory accounting-retention advice.

## Planned evidence and implementation handoff

All test names are **future requirements**, not executed PASS claims.

| Proposed evidence | Required outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `TestPlaidConnectionLifecycle` | Wrong actor/scope, expired/replayed Link return, mixed ownership and unsupported account reject; reconnect/rotation uncertainty pauses; local disconnect fences calls before provider removal completes. |
| `TestPlaidExactMoney` | Fixed examples above preserve cents, exponent lexemes and 0/2/3 decimals; SDK float path prohibited; overflow/unofficial currency/unknown material field blocks whole set. |
| `TestPlaidCompleteUpdate` | Two-page pending replacement publishes once; mutation or failed page restarts C0; staging pause/crash resumes safely; each cap+1 and expiry leave public checkpoint unchanged. |
| `TestPlaidPublicationAtomicity` | Failure after each source/tombstone/receipt/cursor write rolls back; lost commit acknowledgement resolves same set; source revision advances but ledger book revision/journal count do not. |
| `TestPlaidStreamAndCredentials` | Separate filtered cursors never cross accounts; mode/Item changes start null; credential rotation preserves observation identity and fences every sibling; single-account disconnect never removes the shared Item; Item removal requires all-affected approval. |
| `TestPlaidFenceAndWakeup` | Lease expiry, old connection generation and account revocation reject old calls/commits; webhook during completion causes another requested generation; no stranded catch-up. |
| `TestPlaidWebhook` | Valid signature/body passes; tampered body, wrong algorithm/kid, stale/future token, expired key, size overflow and unknown Item deny without work; only dedicated webhook ingress is public, app API remains private; duplicate/reordered/missed notifications converge via worker/catch-up. |
| `TestPlaidSourceLifecycle` | Ordinary posted row with null pending link remains review-eligible; unlinked pending hold removal creates no journal; modification/removal after posting creates exception, preserves journal; identical separate purchases stay separate. |
| `TestCrossAdapterOverlap` | CSV/Plaid and reconnect overlap need explicit scoped match; existing posted event never gets a duplicate journal; contradictory evidence remains unresolved. |
| `TestProviderPrivacyRetention` | No tokens/payloads in queue/log/error; denied scope returns no evidence; raw deletion retains dedup/link history; disconnect is not history deletion. |

Default future tests use original synthetic responses and locally generated test
signatures, no provider credentials. Separately authorized Plaid Sandbox qualification
may test provider behavior but is neither default CI nor a live-bank proof. Acceptance
requires owner profile/standards/consent/retention decisions; #63/#7 work records,
lease/outbox and handler implementation; #56/#62 credential/identity interfaces;
#8 source/draft/matching SQL/API; #50/#52 connection/review UI; #13 provider/cutover
approval. No DDL or adapter should begin by assuming these proposed interfaces exist.

## Implemented follow-on contracts

The proposal above is historical design context. Migrations 12–14 and owned
adapters implement bounded subsets; current authority lives in
[sync SQL](provider-sync-sql.md), [connection SQL](connection-sql.md),
[operations SQL](connection-operations-sql.md), [acquisition](acquisition-runner.md)
and [verified webhooks](provider-webhooks.md). Use their named executed evidence,
not this proposal's future-test table, to assess readiness. The #103 verifier
normalizes equivalent ECDSA signatures for receipt identity after standard
signature verification; exact original body bytes still determine its digest.
Transport dispatch, timed scheduling and actual Sandbox/live acceptance remain
separate gates. No posted journal follows from a notification or sync request.

documents.title: Provider runtime implementation boundaries
documents.body:
# Provider runtime implementation boundaries

## Decision

Coordinator-reviewed synthetic implementation profile, 2026-10-13, #70/#100/#102.
Extend the [provider proposal](provider-ingestion.md) through separate SQL,
decoder and transport contracts. This record resolves the boundary with merged
migrations 9–11; it does not approve provider access or credential enrollment.

## Existing authority and required extensions

Migration 9 owns scoped source bindings and synthetic CSV namespaces. Migration 10
owns immutable booked observations with revision 1, strictly positive amounts and
recoverable CSV imports. Migration 11 adds category drafts and atomic source-linked
posting. None of those contracts implies provider pending/removal/revision support.
Only a new forward migration may introduce it; existing migration files stay intact.

Provider changes require immutable observation revisions plus a controlled current
projection. A posted journal and its original source evidence remain immutable;
later changes create explicit exceptions. Pending, removed and zero-valued source
items cannot enter the positive journal-line workflow. Original signed numeric
lexemes remain separate from unsigned exact magnitude and accounting direction.
Changes invalidate stale drafts; old prepared commands cannot bypass new state.

One account-filtered acquisition stream owns its cursor. The database checks
current binding, consent, service identity and generation at every mutation. A
dedicated restricted sync role receives narrow functions, not API posting authority.
Owner-only synthetic stream enrollment is a fixture boundary, not Link, consent
verification or a production provider connection. #101 owns those later operations.

## Implementation profile and alternatives

The first SQL complete-set boundary is at most 10 pages, 1,000 changes and 2 MiB of
normalized data. These are project limits, not Plaid guarantees or scalability
results. Exceeding a bound rejects the whole set without advancing the published
cursor. The broader proposal's 50,000-change target remains unproved. A short atomic
publication is preferred to partial page publication, which exposes incomplete
pending replacement and correction state. Larger workloads require measured limits
and a reviewed continuation design, not silently skipping source history.

Decode exact numbers before any SDK float conversion. Decoder output is untrusted
input to SQL authority; successful parsing grants no connection, review or posting
permission. Decode failures return fixed codes without retained unauthorized data.
The decoder does not claim a finished update set from a single page.

The existing journal observer remains receipt-only. Its HTTP/queue transport proves
private invocation and durable acknowledgement semantics independently; it is not
the provider acquisition runner. #102 must compose acquisition with its own state
and complete-set publication before claiming working server-to-server sync.

## Credential lifecycle gate

No current lane reads or writes real credentials. Later #101 must bind exchange
attempts to authorized scope, securely store a new version, then publish its opaque
reference. Uncertain provider exchange or secret-store acknowledgement stays in
credential recovery. Local reference publication cannot make a remote exchange
transactional. Rotation fences every sibling stream before replacing a shared Item
reference; single-account disconnect cannot implicitly remove the Item. Test these
failure points through injected interfaces before any separately authorized Sandbox
qualification under #88.

## Sources, standards and acceptance

Refreshed selected official sections on 2026-10-13: Plaid
[Transactions API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/), account-filtered
cursors, pagination restart, amount fields and initialization; PostgreSQL 17
[transaction isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/transaction-iso.html),
serializable retries; and [function privileges](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-createfunction.html),
security-definer search path and default execution privileges. These explain
mechanisms; the limits, role split and immutable exception model are project choices.
Full source register and earlier lifecycle review: [PI01–PI08](../research/plaid-ingestion-sources.md).

ISO currency/version and date rules follow [standards](standards.md). Provider JSON
and internal work requests are not labeled ISO 20022 messages. Applicable official
message mapping and accounting policy gates remain unchanged.

Named proof and remaining limits belong in the SQL, decoder and transport lane
runbooks and the [combined delivery record](../runbooks/sync-foundations.md).
#85/#87 own independent fault/security acceptance; #89 owns measured scaling.

documents.title: Provider synchronization SQL
documents.body:
# Provider synchronization SQL

Migration 25 [dated-currency history](plaid-history-currency.md) replaces singleton
source-version equality with bound monetary identity plus exact source-date version
validation. Complete-set atomicity and all posting gates remain unchanged.

Migration 13 extends this merged foundation through the
[connection lifecycle contract](connection-sql.md): provider-first binding,
credential references, individual account disconnect, and scoped worker context
and receipt recovery. Read that extension with this record; the original migration
12 enrollment remains an owner-only synthetic fixture boundary.

## Decision and applicability

Migration 12 implements the approved **synthetic acquisition foundation** for
#70/#100. A complete account-filtered change set publishes source evidence and its
cursor atomically. Acquisition never posts a journal. Dedicated `bookkeeping_sync`
logins cannot call interactive, publisher or observer operations. No provider calls,
credential retrieval, Link, webhook ingress, hosted dispatch or cloud deployment is
implemented here. This does not complete the provider epic or approve live books.

Reviewed against migrations 9–11 and official Plaid sections on 2026-10-13.
`jayburd-plaid-transactions/1`, API version `2020-09-14`, is proprietary provider JSON,
not an ISO 20022 message. PI01–PI08/STD-01 and existing ISO 4217 currency references
apply; dates/timestamps retain the [decoder](plaid-decoder.md) ISO 8601/RFC3339 profile.
No normative ISO conformance, ownership proof or new accounting policy is claimed.
The coordinator approved these interfaces before DDL. Existing migrations remain
unchanged; downgrade intentionally fails because evidence is forward-only.

## Identity and authority

`integration.sync_item` has a globally unique case-sensitive
(provider, environment, Item) tuple bound to one entity/book. It retains an opaque
credential-reference UUID/version, explicit consent principal/evidence/expiry,
generation and active/paused/disconnected state. References contain no token and
grant no secret access. This slice permits only plaid/sandbox/synthetic enrollment.
Credential exchange/rotation and real enrollment remain #101.

`integration.sync_stream` binds one Item/account filter to an existing approved
source and a typed provider namespace, a service principal and an actual worker
login. Namespace identity includes provider/environment/Item/account, never a
lease, credential version or connection UUID. Mapping and enrolled identities are
immutable, including through ordinary owner DML. No cursor adoption across filters.
Each claim captures the current source binding revision; every stage/publication
revalidates it. Later permission edits therefore invalidate old claims without
permanently stranding the stream.

Enrollment is **existing-source-only**. Its new namespace always carries
`overlap_review_required=true`; booked positive additions enter `overlap_hold`.
There is no overlap-release implementation here. Provider-first registration and
reviewed overlap release are separate work; this is not end-to-end provider posting.
The posted-correction test uses an explicitly documented synthetic owner fixture to
represent already-approved provider evidence, then invokes the real posting boundary.

Worker functions have no actor argument. SECURITY DEFINER entrypoints require
SERIALIZABLE, `session_user` equal to the enrolled login, current membership in the
NOLOGIN sync role and no direct/inherited privileged or API/owner/observer/publisher/
identity/migrator role. Each operation, including receipt replay, rechecks active
service and consenting principals, current entity/source read+import, active
source/namespace/Item and unexpired consent. SQL cannot retrieve credential refs
through the worker API. No table DML or private helper EXECUTE is granted.

Authority locks precede financial scope locks: UUID-sorted principals, entity and
memberships, book, source, Item, stream, set. Item pause/disconnect uses current owner
approval and the common book lock, so it can revoke even disabled consent/service
subjects without a reverse principal lock. Existing API/observer authorization also
rejects mixed sync membership. SERIALIZABLE failures retry the complete transaction.

## Operator contracts

Both functions below are SECURITY INVOKER, executable only by `bookkeeping_owner`.
The approving principal is an explicit attestation, distinct from authenticated
`session_user`; immutable operator receipts record both, body and result. Current
authority is checked before idempotent replay. Keys are 1–128 characters in
`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`; JSON rejects duplicate/unknown/null required fields before casts.

`integration.enroll_sync_stream(actor uuid,e uuid,b uuid,key text,raw text)` takes:

```json
{
  "source_account_id": "uuid", "expected_binding_revision": "1",
  "provider": "plaid", "environment": "sandbox", "synthetic": true,
  "item_id": "opaque", "account_id": "opaque",
  "credential_ref": "uuid", "credential_version": "1",
  "consent_principal_id": "uuid", "consent_evidence_ref": "uuid",
  "consent_expires_at": "2099-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "service_principal_id": "uuid", "worker_login": "synthetic_sync"
}
```

Existing source mapping/currency and explicit grants remain authoritative; this
function grants no permissions. It increments binding revision for the new namespace,
with at most 25 namespaces. Same Item reuse requires exact scope/consent/reference
agreement; duplicate account enrollment under a new key conflicts. Response:
`{stream_id,sync_item_id,namespace_id,source_account_id,binding_revision,item_generation}`.
UUIDs are strings; revisions are canonical decimal strings.

`integration.set_sync_item_state(actor,e,b,item uuid,key text,raw text)` takes
`{expected_generation:string,state:active|paused|disconnected}`. It increments Item
generation, abandons staged sibling attempts, clears their leases and retains the
committed cursors/evidence. Disconnected is terminal in this profile. Response:
`{sync_item_id,item_generation,state}`. Reactivation does not bypass current consent.

## Worker functions and transactions

All scope/stream/set arguments below are UUIDs; fences are bigint; keys are text
except the UUID claim key. Each call is one short transaction; network/decoder work
runs outside it. Worker EXECUTE is limited to these five functions:

| Function | Mutation and replay |
| --- | --- |
| `integration.request_sync(e,b,stream,key)` | Idempotently increments requested generation. Returns `{stream_id,requested_generation}`; same key returns its original generation. |
| `integration.claim_sync(e,b,stream,claim_key uuid)` | Captures C0, current Item/binding revisions and requested target; allocates monotonic fence and 90-second lease. Returns `{stream_id,set_id,fence,starting_cursor,next_page_index,request_cursor,target_generation,binding_revision,lease_until}`. Same live key revalidates all pins; expired keys reject. A new claim abandons an expired attempt and restarts C0. |
| `integration.stage_sync_page(e,b,stream,set,fence,raw)` | Requires contiguous page index and exact cursor chain; persists private immutable normalized page. Exact full-page replay succeeds; changed replay conflicts. Returns `{set_id,page_count,change_count,final_page}`. |
| `integration.complete_sync(e,b,stream,set,fence)` | Reauthorizes before stored-receipt replay; otherwise requires live pins, final page and full-set validation. Atomically publishes evidence/reviews/cursor/receipt. Returns `{stream_id,set_id,cursor,completed_generation,source_revision,changed_count,readiness}`; count/revision fields are strings. |
| `integration.abandon_sync(e,b,stream,set,fence,reason)` | Requires current live pins. Reason is pagination_mutation/provider_failure/decoder_rejected/cancelled. Clears attempt lease without advancing cursor; returns `{set_id,state:"abandoned"}`. |

Sets are staging/completed/abandoned (quarantined is reserved). Pages, completion,
signal and operator receipts are immutable. A signal racing completion increments
requested generation under the same lock; completion records only its captured
target. `requested_generation > completed_generation` remains durable pending work.
This is a future dispatcher input, not an implemented task transport/outbox handler.
There is no partial-set adoption, lease extension or autonomous retry scheduler.

Unknown commit response requires reconnecting and replaying the exact operation;
never assume rollback. A completion receipt is returned after current authorization
before checking expired/replaced leases or changed pins. Different/stale set/fence
cannot publish. No partial evidence survives an exception or transaction rollback.

## Page, money and bounded publication

The page JSON is exactly the [decoder Page](plaid-decoder.md) plus zero-based integer
`page_index` and nullable `request_cursor`. Fields are next_cursor,has_more,
transactions_update_status,request_id,sha256,added,modified,removed. Transaction rows
are exactly account_id,transaction_id,pending,pending_transaction_id,date,
authorized_date,datetime,authorized_datetime,iso_currency_code,currency_version_id,
amount_lexeme,amount,direction,eligible_for_review,name,merchant_name,
original_description. The decoder's nullable fields remain JSON null; removed rows
contain only account_id and transaction_id. There is no public HTTP row-ingestion API.

SQL revalidates account, installed source currency/version/date/minor units, exact
signed numeric lexeme and canonical unsigned magnitude without float or rounding.
Lexemes are at most 128 bytes, at most 38 significant coefficient digits and exponent
[-100,100]; magnitude fits numeric(38,9). Positive provider amounts mean outflow,
negative inflow, zero direction zero and ineligible. Original signed lexeme is stored
in `provider_amount_lexeme`; existing unsigned `amount_lexeme` semantics remain intact.
Optional text preserves empty strings; descriptions are inert text, not executable
content. Timestamps are validated and preserved without timezone conversion.

Engineering bounds: **10 pages, 1000 changes, 2 MiB normalized complete set;
500 changes/page, 90-second lease, 24-hour staged expiry**. Exceeding a bound rejects
without cursor advancement. Page index 10 is malformed, whole-set/page size overflow
is bounded overflow. These are project bounds, not provider guarantees or a claimed
50,000-change proof. Empty initialization is exactly one empty first/final page with
any known Item update status; it retains C0=null. Item readiness does not establish
account-specific history completeness. Migration 24 aligns this with the reviewed
[decoder correction](plaid-decoder.md#account-readiness-correction--2026-10-14).
An empty initialization response cannot terminate an earlier nonempty page sequence.

Private normalized pages retain raw SHA256 and request ID. Exact raw page bytes are
retained by the pure decoder in memory only; SQL has not seen or persisted those
bytes. Durable raw object storage, access, retention/purge and composition with the
future provider adapter remain separate work. Neither a digest nor normalized JSON
is claimed to reconstruct original evidence or satisfy a live retention policy.

## History, corrections and read projection

Duplicate transaction IDs across all arrays/pages reject the complete set. Existing
added IDs require full normalized-row equality; changed added IDs conflict. Unknown
modified/removed IDs reject. Unchanged modified/repeated removed facts are no-ops;
different IDs with identical money remain different observations. No value-based
CSV/Plaid matching or deduplication occurs; typed namespace identity plus overlap
holds protects against silent duplicate posting.

Immutable provider revisions reference their predecessor and set/page/operation.
Only the source observation's monotonic current pointer changes. Removal retains
previous money/date as historical context and explicitly sets removed state. Pending
replacement uses explicit same-namespace pending_transaction_id, resolved after all
pages; unknown/nonpending/self/reused lineage rejects atomically. IDs stay distinct.

Pending, zero and changed/removed unposted evidence are `correction_hold`; no draft
can be created. Source snapshot increments once when a set changes evidence, making
old drafts/approval pins stale. Book revision, journal, lines, posting receipts and
ledger outbox are never mutated by acquisition.

Posted changes retain posted state and the immutable journal/link. The first change
writes a direct immutable observation-revision/journal anchor; every later read keeps
that original posted evidence even after successive changes/removals. Exceptions
are separate references, not automatically corrected journals or substituted amounts.
Review detail optionally includes:

```text
provider_exceptions: {
  total_count: string, truncated: boolean,
  items: [{exception_id,kind:modified|removed,previous_revision:string,
           current_revision:string,observation_id,created_at}]
}
```

Items are latest 100 by current_revision descending then exception_id. Total count
and truncation are explicit. Full inspection of changed amounts/dates and correction
resolution are deferred; this projection exposes references only. List filters accept
correction_hold; zero source money remains a decimal string and cannot post.

`banking.get_source` retains its exact CSV namespace branch. Provider namespaces are
`{namespace_id,profile,provider,environment,item_id,provider_account_id,state,
overlap_review_required}`; no fabricated null CSV identifiers or credential refs.
This existing SQL read has no new HTTP route in this slice.

## Errors, sources and evidence

Fixed message `sync_rejected`: P2600 malformed input/isolation; P2601 current authority;
P2602 identity/replay conflict; P2603 stale attempt/pin; P2604 invalid/incomplete set;
P2605 bounded overflow. PostgreSQL serialization/deadlock/lock timeout is retried by
transaction owners; SQL does not swallow it or report an uncommitted receipt.

Reviewed primary [Plaid Transactions API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/)
sections transactions/sync, account filtering, amount/pending fields and cursor bounds;
[sync migration guide](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/sync-migration/) complete-loop
restarts, 2026-10-13. Fact: filtered streams need separate cursors and failed pagination
restarts from the original cursor. Inference: private fenced staging plus atomic
publication is safer than partial cursor advancement or inferred source matching.
Existing PostgreSQL 17 DI01/function/locking references and the [database research](../research/database-foundations.md)
support scoped keys, immutable history and complete SERIALIZABLE retry. Review covers
selected sections, not provider qualification or normative ISO certification.

Actual tests and limits are recorded in the [delivery runbook](../runbooks/provider-sync-sql.md).

documents.title: Provider credential storage and propagation
documents.body:
# Provider credential storage and propagation

## Superseded dynamic-token path

Owner selected [encrypted PostgreSQL bank tokens](bank-token-vault.md) on
2026-10-15 (#162–#164). New runtime images do not use the eight-slot writer or
mapping resolver below. Static client-secret delivery remains in use. Keep these
resources and records for history; no automatic migration or deletion is implied.

## Historical reviewed decision

Keep Infisical as source and GCP Secret Manager as the sole acquisition runtime
reader. The coordinator approved a separately scoped connection writer and an
**eight-slot, never-reused pool**, preserving Terraform ownership of destination
containers. Source keys slot-00 through slot-07 in /bank-sync map to precreated
jayburd-dev-bank-sync-slot-00 through slot-07 containers. Only environment dev
and provider sandbox are accepted. Static client-id/client-secret use separate
precreated containers and explicitly configured numeric version resources.

SQL credential_version is logical, not a source or Google ordinal. The private GCS
registry bucket is `${project}-jayburd-dev-credential-registry`, prefix
`provider-credentials-v1`. Conditional creation (`ifGenerationMatch=0`) records
immutable slot intent before source POST; intent binds logical reference/version,
Item/environment, configured namespace and envelope SHA-256. Registry objects
contain no token values. The writer has object create/read, never update/delete;
read-only acquisition gets only object read. Slot capacity is explicit and bounded;
this is not an unlimited enrollment or scale claim.

A committed fresh intent permits one source create only after the precreated Google
container is confirmed empty. Existing or uncertain intent never authorizes another
POST, including when source GET returns 404. Slots may remain unusable after an
interrupted attempt; recovery never recycles them or guesses that an external
operation failed. A separate reviewed pool expansion/recovery contract is required.

The writer can recover a source acknowledgement through exact-key GET with imports
and reference expansion disabled. It verifies namespace and original envelope
digest before considering propagation. This source lookup is control-plane evidence,
not an acquisition direct-read fallback. Up to 16 numeric Google versions are
listed and independently accessed; all must match the expected envelope and CRC32C.
Only an observed numeric resource is pinned, selecting the lowest matching numeric
version deterministically. Source version, Google version and SQL logical version
are independent. Any nonmatching/unavailable version or larger history fails closed.

The immutable mapping records reference, source ID/version, exact Google resource
and envelope digest. Its conditional publication acknowledges an existing identical
mapping after a lost response, but never replaces a conflict. SQL remains
credential_pending until Store.Read verifies the Google payload. Acquisition reads
only the mapping and pinned Google/static versions, with no latest alias or source
fallback. Missing propagation is PARTIAL, not permission to repeat exchange/rotation.

## Approved isolated Sandbox role exception

Owner approval on 2026-10-15 permits built-in **Member** for API writer identity
`56d2a541-a48d-4bcc-ae0c-11f48c945ba2` only in isolated Infisical project
`ec11c550-d143-4902-be67-e33266753539`. See the
