[approval](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/133#issuecomment-6196883808)
and [configuration confirmation](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/133#issuecomment-6197028300).
This supersedes the exact create/read-only Infisical grant below for this bounded
Sandbox journey. Member is broader; no granular or least-privilege claim follows.
Do not grant Admin or add this writer to static Plaid credential/canary projects.

Owner confirms GCP ID Token Auth restricted to
`jayburd-dev-api@jayburd-bookkeeping-dev.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, access and maximum
TTL 900 seconds, and Development `/bank-sync`. These are owner attestations;
hosted authentication/write/delivery remain #133 acceptance. Fixed eight-slot,
create-once behavior, immutable registry, separate delivery identity and numeric
GSM-version validation are unchanged. No production or real-bank approval.

## Concrete interfaces and bounds

`NewGCSRegistry(GCSConfig{Bucket,Prefix,Tokens,Transport})`,
`NewGCPReader(GCPConfig{ProjectID,Tokens,Transport})`, and
`NewResolver(reader,registry,ResolverConfig{ClientIDVersion,ClientSecretVersion})`
provide acquisition's CredentialResolver. `NewStore(StoreConfig,registry,reader)`
provides connections.SecretStore and includes fixed Infisical origin/project/identity,
IdentityTokenSource, transport and the eight Slot definitions. Constructors perform
no I/O or environment/ADC discovery. Managed identity dependencies supply OAuth and
audience-bound ID tokens explicitly.

Only the three selected Infisical Cloud origins and Google's fixed HTTPS hosts are
permitted. Calls have three-second limits, one application attempt, no redirects and
128 KiB response limits; Store operations have eight-second aggregate budgets.
JSON rejects duplicate/case-alias keys, excessive nesting and trailing values.
Google payloads require exact response name and CRC32C. Secrets exist in memory only
outside approved stores; Go strings are not claimed zeroizable. Errors and Preflight
contain fixed codes only, never vendor diagnostics. PASS means one exact runtime
reference was read, not provider functionality, IAM qualification or bookkeeping
approval. Preflight performs no source mutation or provider request.

API service identity may perform this writer capability only through SQL-authorized
connection operations. Its Infisical identity is exact-service-account scoped,
create/read-only for the selected dev folder/keys, TTL at most 900 seconds. It has
no Google secret write permission. The separate delivery identity may add
versions only to precreated destinations; deletion is disabled, key schema is fixed,
and delivery IAM must be qualified without project-wide secret administrator permission.
The [owned delivery adapter](scoped-delivery.md) supersedes the native-sync assumption;
its hosted composition and canary qualification remain pending.
Direct Infisical acquisition reads and dynamic destination creation are not selected.

## Primary source review

Reviewed selected public sections on 2026-10-14; no account configuration was read.

- [Infisical create secret API](https://infisical.com/docs/api-reference/endpoints/secrets/create):
  v4 create returns a secret ID and version. Project, environment and folder are
  explicit request fields. This is not evidence that our account grants create-only
  permissions or that an unknown request did not succeed.
- [Infisical retrieve API](https://infisical.com/docs/api-reference/endpoints/secrets/read):
  exact source version can be requested; imports and reference expansion are
  independently switchable. Source versions do not identify Google versions.
- [Infisical GCP authentication](https://infisical.com/docs/documentation/platform/identities/gcp-auth):
  ID-token login supports Cloud Run with exact allowed service-account emails. The
  documented metadata token audience is the Infisical identity ID. GCE project/zone
  restrictions are not a substitute for a Cloud Run service-account restriction.
  Remove default Universal Auth and bound token TTL under the reviewed deployment.
- [Infisical GCP sync](https://infisical.com/docs/integrations/secret-syncs/gcp-secret-manager):
  scoped key schema, optional automatic sync and deletion disabling are documented.
  Selected documentation does not promise a source-version/destination-version
  bijection or atomic read-after-write propagation. Sync-job success alone is
  insufficient credential publication proof.
- [Google access secret version](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.secrets.versions/access)
  and [integrity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/data-integrity):
  read an explicitly addressed resource; check response identity and CRC32C before
  parsing payload. Transport success alone does not prove reference/Item ownership.

These vendor facts support an explicit private version map rather than an ordinal
assumption. Direct Infisical acquisition reads would change the existing availability
and IAM model and are not selected. Dynamic container creation also needs a reviewed
exception to Terraform-owned containers; this document does not grant that exception.

## Applicability and limits

The storage envelope is an internal security protocol, not an ISO 20022 financial
message. It carries no balances, transaction money or accounting dates. Existing
ISO4217 and accounting requirements remain on provider transaction publication.
No deployed IAM, Infisical plan capabilities, synchronization freshness or Sandbox
credentials have been verified. Preflight reports PASS/PARTIAL/BLOCKED with fixed
reason codes only; values, authorization headers and vendor error bodies are never
report output.

## Proposed acceptance evidence

Implemented synthetic tests cover exact numeric resource addressing, mismatched
response name, CRC32C corruption, cross-project mapping, logical/physical version
inequality, wrong Item/environment, missing mapping, duplicate JSON keys, oversized
or redirect responses, unknown write acknowledgement, immutable mapping conflict,
static provider credentials by resource name, and redacted errors/preflight output.
The runbook records executed evidence; these tests do not establish hosted access.

Google configuration accepts an exact project ID or numeric project number. Because
live responses may use a canonical project representation, deployment must select
and qualify that representation (Terraform can supply the project number). The
reader does not infer alias equivalence or relax exact response-name checking.

documents.title: Verified provider webhook ingress
documents.body:
# Verified provider webhook ingress

## Reviewed scope

Issue #103 implements a separately injected handler for POST `/webhooks/plaid`.
It is not mounted on the bookkeeping API and does not deploy public ingress.
Only Sandbox `TRANSACTIONS` / `SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE` is accepted. This proprietary
notification is not an ISO20022 business message; it carries no accounting amount.
Existing currency/accounting contracts remain unchanged.

## Verification and durability

Require one Plaid-Verification JWT <=8KiB and exact JSON body <=64KiB. Verify only
ES256 using the pinned maintained golang-jwt implementation, strict duplicate-free
JSON, canonical base64url framing, integer issued-at no older than300seconds and
no more than60seconds in the future, and constant-time comparison of the signed
SHA256 with original bytes. Token header URLs/embedded keys are unsupported.

Keys come from an injected provider fixed to Sandbox webhook_verification_key/get,
with no redirects/retries and3second/16KiB limits. Metadata must identify the exact
kid, EC/P-256/ES256/signing use, valid curve coordinates, and creation/expiry times.
Cached expiry is checked on every verification. Local policy: four keys,60second
TTL, four cache misses per minute and one lookup at a time; no stale fallback.
These caps are project choices, not provider guarantees. Unknown or rotated keys
can temporarily receive503 until the bounded lookup budget resets.

After signature/hash verification, strictly validate the approved body fields.
Initial/historical booleans describe the notification, not local sync completion.
The receiver commits a durable receipt keyed by SHA256 of the canonical signed delivery
plus currently authorized requested-generation/wakeup intents atomically before204.
Unknown/disabled/unbound Items receive a uniform denial. Invalid signatures never
reach SQL. COMMIT uncertainty returns503; retrying the same verified delivery
resolves its receipt without repeating generation increments. After normal library
verification, replay identity retains exact header/payload segments and R, but uses
S=min(S,N-S) in the signature segment. This local identity normalization prevents
ECDSA high/low-S equivalents creating separate receipts; it is not new signature
verification. A new signed delivery
with identical body is not permanently suppressed by body-hash deduplication.

Ingress has16 concurrent requests and10second context budget. Hosting must set
bounded socket read/write timeouts; arbitrary injected blocked readers cannot be
made context-cancelable by this package. No token/body/request/provider error logging,
credentials in SQL, transaction acquisition, posting or financial readiness claims.

## Catch-up and SQL ownership

Separate restricted webhook and sync pools are injected. Short serializable
transactions retry at most three confirmed40001/40P01 rollbacks within4seconds;
cleanup gets an independent second. Unknown COMMIT exposes no result and triggers
no blind retry. Catch-up accepts trusted entity/book scope, stable tick UUID,
maximum1–100 and optional canonical stream cursor. SQL reauthorizes each enrolled
stream and commits the same wakeup intent. No scheduler or provider call is started.

## Source evidence

Reviewed official [Plaid webhook verification](https://plaid.com/docs/api/webhooks/webhook-verification/)
key metadata, ES256 procedure, issued-at age and exact-body digest sections (PI04).
Reviewed [Transactions webhooks](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/#sync_updates_available)
SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE fields, optional user identifier and Sandbox environment
(PI01). Pinned golang-jwt/v4.5.2 `ecdsa.go` and `parser.go` were read locally:
SigningMethodES256.Verify uses standard-library ECDSA with JWS R/S framing.
Strict parsing and explicit project clock policy surround that maintained verifier.
Alternative public full-API ingress or JWT-selected key URLs is rejected because
neither is required for this narrow notification authority.

The [JWA ES256 signature representation](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7518#section-3.4)
(section3.4) defines fixed-width R/S encoding. Replay identity normalization is our
local inference for ECDSA's equivalent S values, not an RFC-mandated rejection rule.
Original high-S and low-S signatures remain accepted after library verification.

## Bounded listener composition — #103, 2026-10-22

Status: implementation candidate for coordinator/security review; no public
exposure or deployment is authorized by this package. `internal/webhookhost`
composes only the existing verified handler. `New(keys, receiver, close)` is inert;
`NewSQL(keys, db, close)` supplies the reviewed SQL receiver and requires a separate
restricted webhook pool. `Serve(ctx, listener)` takes ownership of one explicitly
provided listener, drains on cancellation and closes dependencies once. It does
not register bookkeeping, health, catch-up, OAuth or Item-lifecycle routes, discover
credentials, select a database principal or change scheduling. Even `OPTIONS *`
is sent through exact-route denial rather than the Go server's general response.

Local profile: header read2s, full request read5s, handler context8s, response write8s,
idle connection15s, header16KiB and shutdown drain2s. These are project resource
bounds, not a guarantee of a successful response or hosted end-to-end latency.
The existing handler's16-request admission,64KiB body, key bounds and SQL4s budget
remain active. A timeout never converts uncertain durability into success. Only
cooperative injected dependencies can be cancelled; socket close cannot stop
arbitrary blocked Go code. Response security headers contain fixed values, no
CORS capability, and no reflected request/error information. TLS and HTTPS-only
public forwarding require separate deployment review; HSTS alone does not supply
TLS. Server diagnostics are discarded to prevent raw request/panic disclosure;
redacted operational outcomes/metrics remain an explicit hosted follow-up.

### Evidence and alternatives

P88-14 (official [Webhooks API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/webhooks/), configuration,
retry and best-practices sections) and P88-15 (official
[verification procedure](https://plaid.com/docs/api/webhooks/webhook-verification/),
ES256, key metadata, exact-body SHA256 and JWT age) were re-read2026-10-22. Review
was limited to relevant public sections; no personalized Launch Center, provider
payload or credential was accessed. P88-14 requires a response within ten seconds;
local deadlines leave hosted timing as a separate acceptance measurement. Existing
proprietary-notification/ISO applicability above is unchanged; no financial
message, amount or accounting policy is added.

Go's official [`http.Server`](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http#Server) ReadTimeout,
ReadHeaderTimeout, WriteTimeout, BaseContext, DisableGeneralOptionsHandler and
Shutdown descriptions were read in full for these fields2026-10-22; matching
fields were checked in the installed Go1.26.5 standard library. The online page
is mutable (thenGo1.27.3), not the repository's pinned1.26.10 execution proof.
ReadTimeout bounds body reads, while WriteTimeout limits response writes; neither
alone supplies a cancellable durable receiver context. Our explicit context and
socket bounds are the inferred composition. Reusing `workerhost` was considered,
but its90s write budget is for private acquisition work and would weaken this
notification boundary. A fresh API mux was rejected because it risks exposing
private routes. Existing verification and SQL adapters remain the single business
implementation. `TestSignedSocketDelivery`, `TestSocketIsolation`,
`TestStalledBodyRead`, `TestShutdownCancelsReceipt` and
`TestHostConfigurationAndBounds` name the synthetic acceptance evidence.

### Threat review (STRIDE)

| Threat / local risk | Controls and required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Spoofing, high | Existing ES256/kid/key-age/body digest verification; invalid socket requests never reach receiver; real provider delivery remains open. |
| Tampering/replay, high | Original bytes verified before existing atomic SQL receipt/generation wakeup; unknown durability503 and retry; SQL replay/concurrency integration remains separate evidence. |
| Repudiation, medium | Durable receipt is authoritative; no raw request logs; redacted hosted metrics and operator traceability need release review. |
| Disclosure, high | No API routes, request reflection, CORS or diagnostic logs; fixed errors/headers; TLS/secret/IAM provisioning remains unimplemented here. |
| Denial of service, high | Socket/body/header/context/admission/key limits; real stalled socket and cancellation tests; edge/network rate controls and load qualification remain open. |
| Elevation of privilege, high | NewSQL requires separately provisioned pool and existing actual-session restricted-role checks; never reuse API/sync principal. Hosted principal/role proof remains open. |

The applied Citizen Developer security skill requires human/security review before
release for public exposure, restricted data and generated security-sensitive
code. Repository GCP/Infisical authority overrides enterprise Azure product defaults;
no policy exception or production readiness is claimed. The root coordinator owns
the concrete managed-principal configuration review before executable composition.

documents.title: Pinned report journal drill
documents.body:
# Pinned report journal drill

## Decision and scope

Coordinator reviewed and approved 2026-10-13 before migration 7. Refines #53's
[financial reporting contract](financial-reporting.md) without changing accounting
policy. One selected GL line proves journal inclusion in a scoped, revision-pinned
account/date selection. No historical snapshot storage or claim that a selector
was previously issued by the server. Category/subtotal navigation remains deferred.

## SQL and wire contract

`reporting.report_journal(actor uuid,e uuid,b uuid,raw text) returns jsonb` accepts
at most 8,192 UTF-8 bytes, a JSON object with unique keys and exactly these required
fields: `snapshot_revision` (canonical nonnegative bigint string), `account_id` and
`journal_id` (hyphenated UUID strings), `starts_on`, `ends_before` (Gregorian full
dates, half-open range of 1–366 days), `line_number` (JSON integer 1–1000). Nulls,
unknown fields, coercions, invalid Unicode and duplicate keys fail `P2100` /400
`invalid_request`. HTTP: GET `/v1/entities/{entity}/books/{book}/reports/general-ledger/journals/{journal}`;
all other SQL fields are required query parameters. Coordinator owns HTTP/types.

Authorize `read` first using the existing locked principal/entity/membership/book
boundary. Then validate input and compare revision; mismatch fails `P2114` /409
`report_snapshot_changed`. Find the exact scoped account/journal/line with journal
accounting date in the range; absent membership fails `P2101` /404 `not_found`.
Call existing `reporting.get_journal` in this same transaction. Response:
`{contract_version:"report-journal-v1",entity_id,book_id,snapshot_revision,
selector:{account_id,starts_on,ends_before,journal_id,line_number},journal:Journal}`.
`Journal` is the existing immutable journal shape, including original units and
reversal/rate provenance. Its `book_revision` is the posting revision; the outer
`snapshot_revision` is the report observation revision. Maximum response 2 MiB,
otherwise `P2110` /422 `result_out_of_range`. No writes or new table grants.

`Service.ReportJournal` uses repeatable-read, total deadline 9 seconds, statement
5 seconds, lock 1 second, at most two whole-transaction attempts, bounded rollback
cleanup. Return data only after commit acknowledgement; uncertain commit emits
503 with no body. Migration 7 is forward-only, SECURITY DEFINER with fixed safe
search path, PUBLIC execution revoked, wrapper-only grant to bookkeeping_api.

## Sources and alternatives

Reviewed 2026-10-13: PostgreSQL 17 [§13.2.2 Repeatable Read](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/transaction-iso.html#XACT-REPEATABLE-READ)
and [CREATE FUNCTION, Writing SECURITY DEFINER Functions Safely](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-createfunction.html#SQL-CREATEFUNCTION-SECURITY).
Relevant sections read in full; first-party implementation documentation, not
accounting standards. Stable transaction snapshots require complete retries after
serialization failures. Definer functions require trusted search paths and narrow
execution privileges. Our inference is to reuse the existing locked authority
function and reader in one transaction. A standalone journal read plus client-side
revision check permits a race and cannot prove selection. Persisted report tokens
would prove issuance but add storage/lifecycle obligations unnecessary for this
bounded inclusion proof. Revisit for archived reports or signed exports.

Standards applicability inherits FR04/FR05: this internal query is not an ISO 20022
bank exchange and receives no invented ISO message designation; ISO 4217 currency
code/version and existing date/UUID contracts are preserved unchanged. No new
recognition, FX, close or live accounting-policy approval.

## Acceptance

`TestReportJournalPinned` proves real GL membership, exact original journal,
unchanged durable state and stale revision rejection. `TestReportJournalBoundary`
proves malformed/duplicate input, unrelated line/range, wrong scope, revoked read
and restricted grants. `TestReportJournalReversal` preserves correction links and
original amounts. `TestReportJournalAdapter` proves isolation, retries and no data
after lost commit acknowledgement. Runbook distinguishes planned from observed.

documents.title: Internal report review CSV
documents.body:
# Internal report review CSV

## Decision and approval gate

Implemented bounded `financial-reporting-csv-v1` wire profile for #51/#53.
Coordinator reviewed and approved this exact long measure schema on 2026-10-13
before implementation. This is an internal review download,
not an ISO 21378/21926 audit exchange or accountant-approved export. Reuse the
[financial reporting applicability assessment](financial-reporting.md#standards-applicability-and-open-policy)
and [SQL semantics](reporting-sql.md). No SQL migrations or new accounting rules.

## Ordered wire schema

Every cell is quoted, embedded quotes doubled, records end CRLF including the last.
Header has the same fixed field count as every row. UTF-8 without BOM. Columns:

1. `profile,report,layout,entity_id,book_id,snapshot_revision,functional_currency,functional_currency_version_id,minor_units,basis,timezone,generated_at,policy_ids,through_date,starts_on,ends_before,compare_through_date,compare_starts_on,compare_ends_before,selected_account_id`
2. `row_kind,row_id,account_id,category,normal_side,journal_id,line_number,accounting_date,posted_at,journal_kind,reverses_journal_id,policy_id,side,transaction_currency,transaction_currency_version_id,valuation_basis,rate_observation_id`
3. `measure,current_sign,current_magnitude,prior_sign,prior_magnitude,difference_sign,difference_magnitude`.

Each logical SQL row emits one physical CSV record per applicable measure, ordered
by this fixed enum: `net,debit_balance,credit_balance,balance,debit,credit,running_balance,transaction_amount,functional_amount,total_debits,total_credits,opening,period_debits,period_credits,closing,revenue,expense,net_income,assets,liabilities,direct_equity,unclosed_earnings,total_equity`.

These three groups concatenate to the complete ordered header. Inapplicable cells are empty quoted
strings, never zero substitutes. A present zero has `zero,0`; nonzero values use
`positive|negative` and unsigned canonical magnitude. At most 29 integer and nine
fractional digits; no leading integer zeros or trailing fractional zeros (0.01 is valid), exponent or float coercion.

## Row and provenance matrix

All rows repeat profile, report, layout (`account-v1` for TB/P&L, `posting-v1` for GL, `basic-unclassified-v1` for BS), exact scope,
revision, functional currency/version/scale, accrual/UTC, first-page generation
time, semicolon-separated policy UUIDs and applicable normalized date/account filters.
Policy order and all shared provenance must agree across pages (generation time
may differ; only the first is exported). Comparison fields are present only when
requested and supported by SQL; GL comparisons are rejected.

| Kind | Required row fields | Current measures | Prior/difference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| account | row_id,account_id,category,normal_side | SQL row amounts: TB net/debit_balance/credit_balance; BS/P&L balance | SQL comparison amounts/difference when requested |
| posting | row_id,account_id,journal_id,line_number,accounting_date,posted_at,journal_kind,policy_id,side,transaction_currency/version,valuation_basis | SQL debit/credit/running_balance plus original transaction_amount/functional_amount | Empty |
| subtotal | row_id=`unclosed_earnings` only | SQL derived balance | SQL comparison amounts/difference when requested |
| summary | row_id=`summary` only | Complete report totals | Complete comparison totals/difference when requested |

Row IDs are `account:<UUID>`, `line:<journal UUID>:<line number>`, or the fixed
`unclosed_earnings`/`summary` labels. Journal kind is `manual|reversal`, side and
normal side are `debit|credit`, category is `asset|liability|equity|revenue|expense`,
and valuation basis is `identity|spot`. Line number is an integer from 1 through
1,000. Policy IDs use UUIDs separated by literal semicolons; dates use valid
YYYY-MM-DD and timestamps use database UTC microsecond spelling.

All other row fields are empty. Posting reverses_journal_id and rate_observation_id
are nullable according to original SQL provenance. Exactly one logical summary (one record per total measure) follows all
selected data rows, including an empty selection; its opening/closing may be nonzero.
No account code/name, description, reason or arbitrary source text is serialized.
UUIDs, calendar dates, UTC timestamps, numeric strings and closed enums are validated
before serialization; malformed generated fields abort the entire download.

## Execution and bounds

`Service.FinancialReportCSV(ctx,Command)` returns status 200 and CSV bytes only when
complete. Caller supplies trusted actor/scope and explicit snapshot_revision.
Client cursor/limit are rejected. All SQL pages use the same filters/revision with
an initial default 100-row page followed by 500-row pages and a shared ten-second deadline. Every page repeats SQL authorization;
a final fresh report read rechecks authority/revision before release. Revocation or
revision change discards the buffer. No point-in-time authorization promise extends
beyond the last authorized database transaction.

Maximum 10,000 physical data records including summary measures and 10 MiB serialized bytes including
header. This counts measures, not journals: 2,000 GL lines produce 10,004
records including four summary measures and therefore exceed the cap. Comparisons
occupy additional columns, not additional records. Excess returns 422 `report_export_limit`; invalid request returns existing
400 invalid_request; SQL stale/revoked/unsupported errors remain unchanged. Malformed
server output returns safe internal_error. Context timeout/cancellation returns
503 temporarily_unavailable. Existing SQL 4,096 account/GL materialization caps and
2 MiB page cap remain stricter independent limits. No partial output, spool, storage,
background runner or publication. No implementation of arbitrary functional FX.

## Sources and alternatives

Reused FR03/FR05 in [financial-reporting sources](../research/financial-reporting-sources.md).
Re-reviewed 2026-10-13: [RFC4180 §2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4180), complete
record/header/quoting clauses; [OWASP CSV Injection](https://community.owasp.org/attacks/CSV_Injection),
hazard characters and escaping/reopen limitations. These support CSV structure and
why quoting alone is insufficient. Our inference is strict generated grammars plus
omission of arbitrary labels. Alternative descriptive CSV requires separate target
spreadsheet tests; JSON remains the lossless rich-text contract. Neither source
settles accounting policy, ISO audit mappings or spreadsheet numeric precision.

documents.title: Financial reporting HTTP
documents.body:
# Financial reporting HTTP

## Decision and reviewed scope

Coordinator approved this JSON-only refinement of [financial reporting](financial-reporting.md)
on 2026-10-13 before implementation. SQL and monetary semantics remain owned by
[reporting SQL](reporting-sql.md). No SQL migration, CSV, provider, new accounting
policy or live-use approval. OpenAPI is the typed transport authority.

## Wire contract

Four additive GET routes below `/v1/entities/{entity}/books/{book}/reports/`:
trial-balance, general-ledger, balance-sheet and profit-and-loss. The old
trial-balance route remains unchanged. Verified bearer identity supplies the actor;
no caller actor field. Every request authenticates before parsing/report access.
SQL authorizes current scope before checking snapshot revisions or aggregating.

Query names and required date/account combinations follow the SQL contract.
Unknown/duplicate/empty fields, malformed URL escapes, request bodies, HEAD and
noncanonical integer limits reject with 400 invalid_request. The complete request URI caps at 4,096 bytes, matching the existing server and
bridge. The transformed SQL request additionally caps at 8,192 bytes. SQL validates dates, UUIDs, revisions, allowed
combinations, policies and cursor membership. Limit defaults 100 and caps 500.

Response preserves the SQL envelope and exact string amounts, with
contract_version financial-reporting-v1 and layout: account-v1 for TB/P&L,
posting-v1 for GL, basic-unclassified-v1 for BS. Layout is fixed, never caller
selected. Existing SQL provenance, totals, comparisons and selectors are unchanged.
Responses buffer entirely, including encoding, before headers; maximum 2 MiB,
Cache-Control:no-store. Service returns only after successful transaction commit.

Cursor is unpadded canonical base64url of JSON containing exactly version, report,
layout, revision, filter_hash and last_key. Version is financial-reporting-v1;
report/layout must match route; revision must match explicit snapshot_revision.
Maximum 2,048 encoded bytes. Duplicate/unknown/missing keys, alternate encodings,
CRLF, padding, invalid UTF-8, unpaired UTF-16 surrogate escapes and
trailing JSON reject. Generated cursors retain valid Unicode as UTF-8 directly. Decode only transports revision/hash/key
into SQL, which binds entity/book/normalized filters and validates key membership.
No signature or access grant is inferred. Every page reauthorizes.

Errors reuse safe problem responses: 400 syntax, 401 identity, 403 insufficient read,
404 inaccessible scope/account, 409 report_snapshot_changed, 422 unsupported policy
or result_out_of_range, 503 deadline/retry failure, 500 unexpected fault. No rows,
SQL, cursor or token in errors/logs. Existing 9-second service budget includes at most
two attempts, with 5-second statement/1-second lock timeouts. No partial success.

## Sources and applicability

Existing FR01–05 and financial-reporting.md standards assessment apply unchanged:
internal application reporting JSON is not a selected ISO 20022 network message;
ISO 4217 reference identity stays preserved; normative audit mappings remain deferred.
No blanket ISO/GAAP claim. RH01: [RFC 4648](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4648),
October 2006, sections 3.2/3.3/3.5/5 reviewed 2026-10-13: padding may be excluded by
an explicit referring profile; reject nonalphabet bytes and noncanonical pad bits.
RH02: [Go encoding/base64](https://pkg.go.dev/encoding/base64), RawURLEncoding,
Strict and DecodeString reviewed 2026-10-13. Strict still ignores CR/LF; exact
re-encoding equality closes that gap. These sources specify transport, not accounting.
Opaque server-held cursors would add durable state; plain query JSON permits awkward
escaping. Bounded base64url with SQL revalidation fits the current revision model.

## Evidence and remaining work

TestReportingHTTPContract covers transport bounds/redaction/auth/cursor mapping;
TestReportingHTTPPostgres covers actual scoped reports/pagination/revision/revocation
through the handler. Existing SQL tests own golden balances and 1,024 posting proof.
See [living evidence](../runbooks/reporting-http.md). Foundation materialization
caps, supported synthetic USD functional policy, absent CSV/full FX and hosted
performance gates remain unchanged. JSON route delivery does not complete #51/#53.

documents.title: Reporting SQL foundation (#72)
documents.body:
# Reporting SQL foundation (#72)

## Scope and review

Implementation contract refining [financial reporting](financial-reporting.md),
using its FR01–FR05 sources and standards assessment. No HTTP/OpenAPI/browser/CSV
surface in this slice. Existing trial-balance function is unchanged. New migration6
adds only restricted reporting functions. Coordinator review is required before DDL.

## Request and response

`reporting.financial_report(actor uuid,e uuid,b uuid,raw text) returns jsonb` accepts
strict JSON (duplicate keys rejected before jsonb conversion), at most 8,192 bytes.
Required `report` is trial-balance/general-ledger/balance-sheet/profit-and-loss.
Point reports require `through_date`; range reports require `starts_on,ends_before`
(at most 366 days); GL also requires `account_id`. Optional `snapshot_revision` is canonical
nonnegative bigint text; `limit` is JSON integer 1..500 (default 100). Optional comparison
is `compare_through_date` or paired `compare_starts_on,compare_ends_before` for P&L.
GL comparisons reject. Unknown/null/wrong-type/incompatible fields reject P2100.

Foundation cursor is a **JSON object**, not the future HTTP base64url encoding:
`{revision:string,filter_hash:string,last_key:array of strings}`. It must match explicit
snapshot_revision and SHA256 of normalized request filters excluding limit/cursor/
snapshot_revision; SQL recomputes the hash. Account sort key is `[account_code,account_uuid]`, compared as text arrays under
C collation; GL is `[accounting_date,journal_uuid,padded_line_number]`. Cursor is untrusted; validate full
shape and last-key membership in the selected row set. Changed book revision
raises P2114; authorization is always checked first. Cursor follows keyset order,
never offset; next cursor is null at exhaustion. Changing page size is permitted.

Envelope fields: contract_version=`financial-reporting-sql-v1`, report, entity_id,
book_id, snapshot_revision(string), generated_at(UTC timestamp), basis, timezone,
functional_currency/code version/minor units, policy_ids, filters, totals,
comparison(null or `{totals,difference}`), rows, next_cursor. All amounts are
canonical decimal strings, magnitude<10^29, scale<=9. Totals cover full selection,
not current page. Each row has stable `id`, `amounts` object and `selector` with
scope/revision/date/account or category filters. Account rows also carry
account_id/code/name/category/normal_side. GL row includes journal_id,line_number,
accounting_date,posted_at,kind,reverses_journal_id,policy_id,transaction currency
code/version, original amount,functional amount,side,valuation_basis,rate ID and
running_balance. Comparison account rows include `{amounts,difference}` aligned
by stable rowid and zero-filled. No percentages. BS derived unclosed_earnings row
is cumulative residual with revenue/expense selector, not current period profit.

## SQL ownership and policy

Repeatable-read transaction authorizes using existing locked membership/book
function before aggregation; no READ ONLY mode because authorization locks rows.
Only wrapper EXECUTE granted to bookkeeping_api, helpers owner-only. Current
synthetic accrual/UTC/USD-scale2/half-even profile is supported, original foreign
identity/spot amounts retained. Validate contiguous policy coverage through both
comparison/current history and reject currency/version/basis/scale changes.
No new non-USD functional book policy, annual close, translation or automation.

SQL calculates exact debit-positive sums. TB totals use max(net,0)/max(-net,0).
GL opening is all history before start; running totals include rows before page.
P&L revenue=-revenue-net,expense=expense-net,profit=revenue-expense. BS assets=
asset-net,liabilities=-liability-net,directequity=-equity-net,earnings=-(revenue-net+
expense-net),totalequity=directequity+earnings. No balancing plug or absolute-value
statement rendering. Original+reversal count on own dates. Empty valid periods
return zero activity and real opening. Dates are explicit, pointinclusive/rangehalfopen.

## Bounds and Go service

`Service.FinancialReport(ctx,Command)` passes trusted Actor/Entity/Book plus unchanged
Body. Total budget 9 seconds plus bounded rollback cleanup, at most 2 transaction attempts,
statement timeout 5 seconds / lock timeout 1 second. Commit acknowledgement required before returning
Result; cancellation/uncertain commit returns safe failure. SQL P2114 maps to
409 report_snapshot_changed locally without altering old error vocabulary.
Response at most 2 MiB; oversized/aggregate overflow raises result_out_of_range. No
financial arithmetic or cursor trust in Go. SQL has no ledger/receipt/outbox mutation.

## Acceptance and limits

Actual disposable PostgreSQL tests cover golden1300TB/70profit/1145BS, GL openings,
reversal/provenance, exact cents, comparison, deterministic pagination/stale revision,
unauthorized entity/prepare-only/revoked membership, malformed requests/cursors,
restricted helper grants and unchanged state. Unit tests cover adapter error/retry/
commit boundary. Full 100,000-row performance/hosted contention, FX functional transitions,
all future report matrix cases and CSV remain separate #51/#53 acceptance gates.
No new indexes without measured need; full scoped aggregates may timeout explicitly.

## Reviewed field refinements

Coordinator reviewed this foundation on 2026-10-13 before DDL. Coverage starts at
min(requested start/asof, comparison start/asof, earliest posted journal in the scoped book)
and ends at max(selected last date); it does not start at year 0001. Requests before
first policy fail unsupported_policy. All policies spanning that interval must cover
it contiguously and match supported profile/currency. Existing unused policy gaps
outside that interval do not block reports.

Exact `amounts` keys: TB `net,debit_balance,credit_balance`; GL
`debit,credit,running_balance`; P&L account/BS account/derived row `balance`.
Totals: TB `total_debits,total_credits`; GL
`opening,period_debits,period_credits,closing`; P&L `revenue,expense,net_income`;
BS `assets,liabilities,direct_equity,unclosed_earnings,total_equity`.
Comparison amounts/difference use exactly the current row keys; comparison totals/
difference use exactly current totals keys. Selector fields are entity_id,book_id,
snapshot_revision,starts_on(optional),ends_before(optional),through_date(optional),
account_id for account/GL or categories array for derived earnings. Envelope filters
exclude cursor/limit/snapshot_revision and retain the validated report/date/account/
comparison keys. Currency fields: functional_currency, functional_currency_version_id,
minor_units. GL provenance fields use transaction_currency and
transaction_currency_version_id plus transaction_amount and functional_amount.
`line_number` and minor_units remain bounded JSON integers; all money/revisions text.
Acceptance above is required/planned until the runbook names observed outcomes.

## Explicit foundation materialization limit

This implementation uses complete scoped row materialization before keyset page
selection; it is **not** a streaming large-ledger query engine. A preflight LIMIT 4097
count rejects more than 4,096 GL posting lines in the requested range/account, or
more than 4,096 accounts in a book, with result_out_of_range even when page limit 1.
Point reports aggregate the book's full historical journal facts into those bounded
account rows; GL opening history is also fully aggregated, never truncated. Scoped
account names/codes above 1,024 UTF-8 bytes reject account reports before materialization.
The BS derived row adds at most one row. JSON response remains capped at 2 MiB.
Comparison builds at most two bounded sets. Aggregate scans still need the 5-second
deadline; there is no 100,000-row performance claim. Replacing bounded materialization with
measured SQL page/window selection is explicit follow-up before raising these caps.
Cursor hash binds contract_version/entity_id/book_id/filters, not filters alone.
Policy provenance additionally caps 1,024 intersecting policy revisions across the
required history/comparison interval, checked before JSON accumulation; 1,025 fails
result_out_of_range. This is independent of workspace UI limits and cannot be
bypassed by directly provisioned policy rows.

# Transaction detail when categorization is unavailable

## Decision and scope

#293, 2026-10-24. Authorized source detail is independently readable from its
category choices. Preserve the exact already fetched detail when a non-auth
category read fails, show an explicit read-only explanation and retry action,
and clear category/draft/retry state. Retrying reloads current detail and choices;
it never invents accounts, changes dates or executes a financial command.

401/403/404 still erase all scoped snapshots and invoke the existing denial
boundary. Book/session/source changes and obsolete request generations must never
restore old detail or choices. Existing revision/permission checks govern any
later successful draft. No raw API/provider diagnostics displayed for category
failure. No financial request or token enters browser persistence.

## Evidence, alternatives and standards

Reviewed source-review-sql.md and command-recovery.md plus migration11's
banking.review_categories: it selects policy effective at the original booked
date and raises P2109 if none applies. This is a source fact, not confirmation
of the actual older-row rejection observed in the hosted browser; that response
was not captured. Preserve historical observations without changing posting policy.
Existing research/standards/accounting mappings remain authoritative.

Erasing the whole detail loses independently authorized review evidence. Guessing
another date/account would bypass policy. Choose a separate unavailable category
state, and keep genuine authority denials destructive to sensitive UI state.
This is a read-only UI availability change, not a new financial message, API,
SQL schema, accounting rule or ISO20022 mapping. Existing ISO4217/original units
and exact money rendering are unchanged; no new conformance claim.

## Acceptance

Component tests cover delayed lookup, policy/transport failure, explicit retry,
401/403/404, changed scope and obsolete category responses. Browser fixture uses
history before a book's period plus an unavailable category endpoint, on desktop
and mobile: detail/exact amount/date remain visible, no draft or command POST,
and keyboard retry remains available. Existing valid draft flow and required
core/web/full-stack regressions pass. Hosted historical-case response and owner
review remain separate evidence; a source correlation is not a policy diagnosis.

documents.title: First Sandbox book bootstrap
documents.body:
# First Sandbox book bootstrap

## Decision

Issue #136 authorizes two owner-operated SQL stages, never application startup.
The operator selects only `jayburd-bookkeeping-dev` and database `bookkeeping`.
Existing session must have SET authority for safe NOLOGIN `bookkeeping_owner`;
identity stage also requires SET for `bookkeeping_identity_operator`. Missing
capability fails before mutation. Scripts grant no roles and accept no credentials.
API/migrator/worker sessions are not approved operators. Merged migrations remain
unchanged; no persistent helper functions or alternate authentication path exist.

## Reference and identity stage

`sandbox-identity.sql` takes `project`, `subject`, `currency_id`, `source_release`,
`valid_from`, `valid_to`. Issuer is fixed; subject is the invited Identity Platform
UID copied by its owner, never email/token. Exact pinned USD metadata is installed
under owner role, then enrollment runs under the identity-operator role in the
same bounded transaction. Existing currency must match every field; overlapping
or conflicting IDs/versions fail. Existing disabled principals cannot reactivate.
Only currency/principal UUIDs and fixed PASS text are reported; never UID or email.

## Book stage

Superseded for routine creator onboarding by
[self-service connections](self-service-connections.md) in issue #155. The
operator script remains an explicit administrative/recovery path. New creators
use Connect account; runtime prepares the book under the bounded SQL contract.

UI setup may use the custom form or the bounded Sandbox starter preset. The preset
only prepares the ordinary durable setup command with a personal entity, one
monetary checking account, and non-monetary equity/income/expense accounts. The
owner still reviews and explicitly executes it; it adds no alternate SQL or auth
path. After UI setup, `sandbox-book.sql` takes `project`, `actor_id`, `entity_id`,
`book_id`, `worker_login`, `publisher_login`, `scheduler_paused`. Exact fixed dev
IAM login names and a true owner-observed scheduler-paused attestation are required;
SQL cannot query cloud scheduler state. Existing SQL capability predicates must
validate both worker logins. A setup receipt must prove actor created this exact
book/entity, with active read/post authority. Shared read access alone is insufficient.

A distinct per-book service principal uses issuer `urn:jayburd:service:jayburd-bookkeeping-dev`
and subject `acquisition:<book UUID>`; it cannot map a Firebase user. Insert only
missing actor import and service read/import memberships; reject revoked grants or
disabled subjects. Existing owner functions grant connect and enroll connection /
delivery bindings with fixed idempotency keys. No sources, journals, financial
accounts, provider calls, cloud scheduling or database role grants are performed.
Atomic rollback covers new service principal, grants and both binding operations.
Replay never reactivates revoked bindings. Output is IDs/revisions only.

## Standards and source review

USD/840/2 was verified against SIX List One XML, publication `2026-09-17`, retrieved
2026-10-15, SHA256 `33139b438657d1cee116ba737807ea71d19d6de4b90f799a09c56f0cc6a1b0ff`.
[Official maintenance page](https://www.six-group.com/en/products-services/financial-information/market-reference-data/data-standards.html)
and [List One XML](https://www.six-group.com/dam/download/financial-information/data-center/iso-currrency/lists/list-one.xml)
were reviewed for agency ownership, publication and the US Dollar record, not the
full ISO text. The local approved validity is `[2026-09-17,2027-01-01)`; publication
does not establish USD's historical inception. This narrow local window is policy,
not an ISO effective-date claim. Earlier books/import dates need separate reviewed
reference history. [Issue #225](plaid-history-currency.md) adds an owner-only
historical USD interval without changing current-reference replay.
`source_release` retains publication/hash provenance, never a
synthetic-fixture claim. No exchange rates or financial messages are introduced;
ISO 20022 does not apply to these internal provisioning controls.

Alternative runtime auto-enrollment would widen authority. Ad hoc administrator
DML would omit replay/conflict checks. Neither is selected. Synthetic PostgreSQL
acceptance is `scripts/test-sandbox-bootstrap.sh`; hosted execution remains #133.

documents.title: Owner-private Sandbox identity transport — #299
documents.body:
# Owner-private Sandbox identity transport — #299

## Decision and scope

Engineering profile reviewed by the coordinator2026-10-24 before implementation;
human security/owner acceptance is required before actual secret/provider use.
Resolve the missing private producer for the existing tagged identity projector,
not acquisition or financial comparison. One freshly controlled synthetic checking
account, complete posted-only fixture authored before provider data, at most500
rows. The existing projector and financial comparison remain authoritative.

A separate local `sandbox-identity-readback` command defaults offline. Explicit
`-action=readback` requires the absolute independently authored fixture.json,
its exact SHA256, exact synthetic account ID, an absolute expiry no more than60
minutes ahead, and a separate owner-private pipe/socket descriptor3..1024.
The owner supplies exactly client_id, secret and access_token JSON through that
descriptor; token must have the Sandbox prefix. No credentials in flags, env,
files, agent messages or browser storage. No secret/ADC/SQL/vault discovery.
The owner checks Item/account/source consent before injection; this local deadline
does not attest SQL ownership, renew consent or grant access to any existing Item.

Before opening the private descriptor, validate fixture bytes/hash/posted-only
identity profile, account and finite deadline. The total operation has15seconds,
capped by the supplied expiry, including pipe read and response. Credential input
is bounded16KiB, closes on all paths and never appears in diagnostics. One HTTPS
POST to fixed https://sandbox.plaid.com/transactions/sync, API2020-09-14, no proxy,
redirect, retry, refresh, paid operation or cursor. Request count500 with exact
options.account_id and omitted cursor. Expiry is rechecked before request; TLS
verification remains standard. No arbitrary endpoint or Production profile.

Response headers are bounded16KiB with at most one connection. Read at most the
existing2MiB combined fixture/response body bound. In-memory response
goes directly to the existing projector; it must be complete historical readiness,
has_more=false, no modified/removed, exact account, exact preauthored unique tags
and unique IDs. Do not parse financial values to select identities or alter
expectations. Neither raw response nor credentials are written or printed.
Only fixed sibling identity-map.json is written create-only0600 after full
validation. Invalid input/transport leaves no map; an existing map/symlink is never overwritten.
Success emits only readiness Boolean and bounded count. If final stdout delivery
fails after the complete map is committed, preserve that map and treat the
acknowledgement as unknown; do not automatically repeat the provider request.
Inspect the owner's private result before any deliberate next operation.
It is not an equality,
acquisition, current SQL identity or zero-journal receipt.

## Evidence, alternatives and limits

[Reviewed source record](../research/sandbox-identity-transport-sources.md) separates
vendor semantics from this narrow policy. Existing `sandbox-identity-map` remains
an offline alternative when an owner already has an authorized private response
pipe. A hosted bridge was rejected for this slice because it adds deployed
provider/credential/SQL authority before the first controlled proof. General curl,
saved payloads or SQL-derived expectations lack this closed output and independent
oracle boundary. No owner is asked to send a credential or financial record to
the agent. The source helper's availability does not establish how an owner may
retrieve a particular stored Item credential; absent private authorized injection,
leave the actual run blocked rather than export/decrypt through an admin query.

Named acceptance: default/invalid/expired command does zero dependency work;
fixture/hash/tag validation before credential open; exact fixed request/version/
account/omitted cursor with one call; financial-field mutations produce identical
map and unchanged authored bytes; foreign/missing/duplicate/incomplete input fails;
oversize/HTTP/error/redirect/cancel/expiry/pipe failure produces fixed diagnostic
and no map; actual synthetic pipe/file rejection/create-only0600 and cleanup.
Core/race/build plus existing projector/comparator gates remain required.

## Standards and security

Proprietary Plaid API2020-09-14 identity association, not an ISO20022 financial
exchange or ISO21378 audit export. The existing ISO4217 currency/version mapping
and original money lexemes remain unchanged in the independent comparison; no
normalization, FX, accounting policy or conformance claim is introduced.

Threats: supplied wrong Item is constrained by account-filter and exact authored
tags but this does not attest application consent; owner finite scope is required.
Secret/response disclosure is constrained by private bounded input, fixed errors,
no filesystem/raw output and TLS/fixed origin. Stalled input/output is bounded;
owner controls ancestor directory, process and private descriptor. A compromised
owner process or host is outside this helper's guarantees. Expiry stops this
invocation only, not Plaid credentials or existing services. Cleanup closes pipe
and response and removes only a partial newly created map; owner separately
revokes the actual #300 mandate and deletes generation-pinned hosted inputs.

Actual human-reviewed transport/credential injection and #300 comparison/cleanup
remain unproved. Old Sandbox approvals remain expired. No personal-account use.

The shared private descriptor opener validates pipe/socket type, sets nonblocking
mode before os.NewFile and requires read-deadline support. Closing an inherited
blocking descriptor was experimentally insufficient to stop syscall.read on the
local platform. Both producer and existing offline projector use the corrected
opener; invalid descriptors never become ordinary file/standard-stream reads.

After actual human transport/scope acceptance, an owner-side launcher may provide
the private pipe on descriptor3 to this invocation template (placeholders are not
approved values):

```text
bin/sandbox-identity-readback -action=readback
  -fixture=/owner/private/run/fixture.json -fixture-sha256=<reviewed independent hash>
  -account-id=<exact synthetic account> -expires-at=<fresh approved absolute deadline>
  -credential-fd=3
```

The launcher must not echo credentials, use shell tracing, save a credential JSON
file or send values through agent tools. The three envelope fields are exactly
client_id, secret and access_token; only the owner injects their values. This
template supplies no token retrieval/decryption permission. Review private map
readiness/count only, hash the map owner-side for the subsequent finite #300
mandate, and keep all financial comparison/cleanup requirements unchanged.

documents.title: Limited hosted Sandbox release
documents.body:
# Limited hosted Sandbox release

## Decision and scope

For #132, add explicit `sandbox-promote` and `sandbox-rollback` operations to the
existing application and paused-worker release tools. Owner requested the integrated
fictional account journey on2026-10-15. This contract requires owner review/merge
before dispatch; it does not authorize production or complete #11/#26.

Only project `jayburd-bookkeeping-dev`, number `9088794002`, is eligible. Existing
provider composition fixes Plaid to Sandbox; manifests cannot select a provider URL
or environment. Exact image/build, expiry, owner/main, WIF, source ancestry and
Terraform ownership remain unchanged. This is internal release metadata, not an
ISO financial message; existing [standards](standards.md) profiles remain applicable.

## Prerequisites and phases

- App shell: #5/#6/#130 closed on evidence. #130 includes hosted database replay,
  status and actual API IAM denials. Connections may be explicitly null.
- Connection qualification UI and paused workers: additionally #131 implementation
  reviewed/merged. Source writer identity, scoped delivery identity, exact static
  GSM versions and consent expiry are reviewed in the manifest's evidence comments.
- Hosted dynamic credential activation and one manual acquisition remain #133.
  Existing SQL state, exact-version verification and explicit account bindings
  enforce activation; a deployed shell is not successful enrollment.
- Scheduler remains paused; automatic acquisition is outside this release.

The original full promote/rollback gates remain #6/#11/#26 (and #5 for workers).
They cannot be satisfied by closing implementation subtasks. #11 retains hosted
isolation/rotation/revocation/recovery; #26 retains restore/load/cost and operator
disposition. Declaring these complete to unblock deployment is prohibited.

## Execution and recovery

Sandbox app promotion executes read-only schema status using its exact build image
before runtime apply, never `up`. A schema mismatch blocks deployment. Sandbox
rollback without the new explicit repair capability skips SQL and requires a prior
Sandbox receipt with the identical approved connection policy. Repair-enabled
Sandbox rollback instead verifies the selected-image clean schema/hash using the
existing status-only job before runtime; never up/down or automatic repair. It
retains the same prior receipt/configuration digest and fixed source/readiness
gates in [connection release](connection-release.md). Full and Sandbox receipts
cannot cross the rollback boundary.
Worker rollout retains the existing paused checks and fixed binding/version policy.
No API IAM bypass, test identity adapter, secret retrieval, SQL grant or new provider
endpoint is introduced. Runtime receipts explicitly identify Sandbox scope.

## Evidence and alternatives

Sources: existing [Cloud Run rollout](cloud-run-rollout.md),
[status](migration-status.md), [worker release](worker-release.md) and
[connection policy](connection-release.md) contracts and their reviewed GCP sources.
Inference: a separate operation permits qualification without falsely claiming the
broader readiness criteria. Rejected alternatives are silently removing closure
gates, closing incomplete epics, or deploying a local fake-identity demo.

Named `sandbox-release.test.mjs` tests cover profile/project restrictions, unchanged
full gates, missing/expired connection policy, status-before-runtime, scoped rollback
and receipt labels. Existing release/fake-command tests continue to apply. Hosted
UI/MFA/Link/activation/acquisition evidence remains separate; no readiness claim
follows from synthetic tests.

Selected official sections rechecked2026-10-15:
[Cloud Run Execute jobs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/execute/jobs),
“What is job execution?”, required roles and gcloud execution: job configuration
and completed execution are distinct; `--wait` waits for completion. This supports
our execution receipt, not SQL correctness by itself.
[Plaid Sandbox overview](https://plaid.com/docs/sandbox/), “Differences between
Sandbox and Production”: Sandbox has institution/data-consistency limitations.
Therefore this milestone proves a fictional integration, not bank reconciliation
or production compatibility. Review depth: selected sections only; no account data.

documents.title: Scoped Sandbox equality and zero-journal verifier
documents.body:
# Scoped Sandbox equality and zero-journal verifier

## Decision and scope

Coordinator-approved engineering profile for #272/#85/#87/#88, 2026-10-22;
review checkpoint preceded migration30 implementation. Fresh one-source synthetic book only.
No Production, raw-provider export, table SELECT grant, posting, source mutation,
provider request or cloud provisioning. No baseline delta or snapshot nonce.

Existing [synthetic lifecycle proof](../runbooks/plaid-85-verification.md) verifies
exact fixed values through the real adapter/SQL boundary, but hosted UI counts
cannot establish complete equality or absence of automatic journals. This slice
adds a separately enrolled bounded operational capability; deployment and actual
execution remain separately authorized work.

## Physical model and interfaces

New NOLOGIN `bookkeeping_verifier` capability: integration schema USAGE and EXECUTE
only on `integration.verify_sandbox_fixture(uuid,bigint,text,text)`. No external
snapshot or diagnostic capability is granted. Dedicated login is
`jayburd-dev-verifier@jayburd-bookkeeping-dev.iam`. No ADMIN/SET, other bookkeeping,
predefined pg_* or privileged memberships. Bootstrap must precreate the safe
capability before restricted migration; runtime never enrolls itself.

`integration.verification_mandate` grain: one actual verifier login × exact
entity/book/source/namespace/stream/Item × fixture and identity-map digest × pinned
binding/Item/completed generation interval. Columns: mandate_id UUID primary key;
entity_id/book_id/source_account_id/namespace_id/stream_id/sync_item_id composite
FKs; verifier_login name; approving_principal UUID FK; binding_revision,
item_generation,target_generation bigint; fixture_id text; fixture_sha256 and
identity_map_sha256 bytea32; enabled boolean; mandate_revision bigint;
created_by_login name; created_at,expires_at timestamptz. Lifetime at most60minutes
and no later than current source consent. Scope/pins/digests/expiry are immutable.
Only explicit revoke changes enabled true→false and increments revision. Renew
through a new owner mandate; expired history remains immutable.

`integration.verification_operator_receipt` grain `(session_user,operation_key)`:
normalized metadata, result and created_at only. No expected financial rows,
identity-map contents, raw provider bytes, baseline counts or tokens are stored.
Owner-only enrollment checks an explicitly attested approving principal and
current scope; approving principal is not runtime caller identity. Owner-only
revoke takes mandate, expected revision and stable key. Exact known-operation
replay retains its receipt; changed same-key input is rejected.

## Current identity, locks and revocation

Go checks actual session_user=current_user before calling SQL. SECURITY DEFINER
changes current_user, so SQL independently requires safe enrolled session_user and
`current_setting('role')='none'`, never equality against its definer. Reject
privileged attributes, database/schema CREATE, all predefined and other application
roles, direct/effective table/sequence authority, unexpected function capability,
and grant/delegation options. Fixed errors contain no dependency diagnostics.

The Go adapter imposes a four-second context deadline around the entire
SERIALIZABLE transaction, beginning before BeginTx. It configures three-second
statement/one-second lock budgets before the compare call and uses independent
rollback. SQL does not claim that changing statement_timeout within an already
running function bounds a direct caller. No automatic cloud/provider work.
Authority locks precede scope: current approving/consenting/service principals in
UUID order, entity/membership, book, source, Item, stream, mandate. Current read/
source-read authority, active scope, unexpired consent, exact binding/Item pins and
mandate enabled/revision/expiry are rechecked. Runtime source/Item/session/login
cannot be selected by caller parameters. One source belongs to the synthetic book;
other-namespace observations and unexpected review records make equality fail.

The stream must have no active lease and requested_generation=completed_generation=
the mandate's target. New work or scope changes make the snapshot ineligible.
Do not hold database locks across a source-provider request. Revocation serializes
at the existing authority rows and mandate; concurrent changes cause bounded
failure/retry-required evidence, never a false pass. No new financial write occurs.

## Independently authored fixture and identity map

Inputs are proprietary `jayburd-sandbox-verification/1`, at most1000 revisions and
2MiB total. Author expected financial/state fields before provider injection.
Separately bind logical IDs to provider-assigned IDs using bounded injection
response identity metadata where supplied. The documented Sandbox create endpoint
returns no transaction IDs; the proposed first hosted posted-only run uses the
[strict tagged identity readback](hosted-sandbox-verifier.md#identity-readback-correction-engineering-profile-for-review)
instead, subject to that profile's human review and limits. Neither map method may
supply expected amounts/dates/state or regenerate fixture financial fields.
Do not copy raw provider records into the expectation. Complete-source equality
requires a complete controlled fixture, not a selected injected subset.

Fixture rows identify logical entry/revision and assert current pointer, original
numeric lexeme, exact canonical unsigned decimal magnitude, direction, source state,
booked date, ISO currency code and dated currency-version identity, description,
previous revision and current review disposition. Pending links are independent
logical-ID pairs. Identity-map rows contain only logical ID and transaction ID.
Require unique JSON keys, strict required fields, no unknown fields, unique
logical/revision pairs, exactly one current revision per logical ID, unique mapped
provider IDs, complete mapping and valid lineage references. Legitimate equal-value
purchases remain separate identities. Never deduplicate by amount/hash.

Owner enrollment pins SHA256 of exact fixture bytes and exact separate map bytes.
A verifier cannot vary candidate values or IDs to use mismatch counts as a probing
oracle. Changing either requires a new owner-reviewed mandate. Digests are of
independent synthetic expectations, never released hashes of actual observations.
Financial input and map contents stay ephemeral and are not logged or retained.

SQL alone owns exact comparison. Missing/extra revisions, quantity/lexeme/unit/date/
state/direction/description/current-pointer/lineage mismatches and review evidence
mismatches fail equality. Fresh profile requires exactly one review assignment per
observation, one distinct observation per review, and exactly one rendered evidence
entry with the exact observation/namespace/provider identity and expected revision.
Equal-valued purchases cannot share a review assignment. Compare all retained revisions, not only latest state.
No float conversion, rounding, minor-unit truncation or implicit FX translation.
Preserve original currency units; functional-currency accounting is not inferred.

## Output and zero-journal evidence

Only booleans and bounded count strings leave SQL/CLI. Counts saturate at1001
(meaning at least1001); supported actual history/review sets above1000 are rejected. No IDs, names, dates,
amounts, tokens, cursor values, source hashes or raw errors. Only the combined comparison is externally callable. It checks expected values
and counts journals plus `integration.outbox_message` with event_type journal.posted
inside the same authorized snapshot. Equal requires all mismatches zero and both
absolute financial counters zero. A fresh zero book with immutable journals/outbox
establishes no journal additions within that book; this does not attribute effects
in a preexisting nonzero book or qualify unrelated accounts.

## Sources, standards and alternatives

Existing [standards](standards.md), proprietary Plaid/API2020-09-14 mapping in
[provider sync](provider-sync-sql.md), dated ISO4217 semantics in
[history currency](plaid-history-currency.md), and P88-10/11/12 in the
[Plaid source register](../research/plaid-88-test-sources.md) apply. ISO20022 is not
an applicable registered message for this internal redacted operational comparison.
ISO4217 identity/date validity and exact financial mapping remain applicable.
ISO21378:2019 abstract review identifies audit-data relevance but this is not an
audit export or conformance claim; full normative text remains unreviewed.

PostgreSQL17 source basis: existing database foundations S06/S08/S12 and
[bootstrap review](webhook-bootstrap.md#sources-standards-and-alternatives) for
function privileges, serializable locking, role inheritance/delegation and powerful
predefined roles. These establish mechanisms; finite mandates, separate login,
complete independent fixture and absolute-zero gate are project acceptance choices.

Alternative unrestricted owner SQL/raw dumps violate the narrow evidence/privacy
boundary. Reusing sync/API identity couples comparison to acquisition/posting and
widens authority. A caller-selected baseline or unbound nonce can fabricate
causality. The scoped hash-pinned capability adds migration/provisioning work but
allows inspectable exact comparison without general financial reads. Nonzero-book
baseline/attribution remains explicitly deferred rather than weakly asserted.

## Required acceptance

Disposable real-role tests: valid complete lifecycle fixture, every financial/state/
lineage/review mismatch, missing/extra/duplicate identities, duplicate JSON/unknown
fields, hash change, excessive bytes/rows; no identity collapse for equal purchases;
wrong/SET/mixed/predefined/direct-privilege roles, revoked principal/source/mandate,
expired consent/mandate, foreign scope and changed generations. Controlled synthetic
posting must change absolute financial counters and fail zero-journal certification.
No output may contain input source markers. Permission denials require exact
SQLSTATE or closed classification, not connection errors. Migration, ledger, runtime
adapter and CLI inertness gates remain required. No hosted qualification from these.

## Bounded operator command

`cmd/sandbox-verify` without flags prints only `{"offline":true}` and performs no
file, identity, network or database operation. Explicit execution requires
`-action=compare -manifest=/absolute/clean/path/manifest.json`. The <=8KiB strict
metadata manifest has exactly these string fields: `profile` equal to
`jayburd-sandbox-verification-manifest/1`, `instance` for the reviewed development
Cloud SQL instance, `mandate_id`, positive canonical `mandate_revision`, and
lowercase raw-byte `fixture_sha256` / `identity_map_sha256`. It accepts no DSN,
caller actor, secret, provider or sync option. The component derives the verifier
IAM login; its pool has max1/min0.

The command reads only fixed siblings `fixture.json` and `identity-map.json`,
checks each final path is a regular nonsymlink file, enforces the combined2MiB
bound and verifies both digests before creating transport. Ancestor path symlinks
are not a security boundary; the owner supplies the reviewed absolute directory.
No financial values are normalized in Go. The adapter starts its four-second
context **before BeginTx**, applies local3s statement/1s lock limits, checks actual
session identity and runs one SERIALIZABLE comparison/commit attempt. Rollback has
an independent one-second cleanup context. The CLI has an overall15s transport
context; a function-local setting is not claimed to bound an already-running
statement from a direct SQL caller.

Successful committed equal/unequal comparisons print exactly the two booleans and
seven count strings. Unequal results exit nonzero after emitting that bounded
result. Invalid input, denied access, cancellation or uncertain commit emit no
prepared comparison and a fixed diagnostic; no automatic transaction retry occurs.
Owner enrollment/revocation is separate from this read-only command. Unit fakes
prove transport/commit failure handling; the disposable real-login integration
proof also invokes this Go adapter against the real comparison function.

documents.title: Allowlisted secret delivery
documents.body:
# Allowlisted secret delivery

## Decision and scope

Selected for implementation by the coordinator under owner direction, 2026-10-14;
hosted activation remains gated by #11. Replace the assumed native Infisical sync
with an owned delivery adapter. Infisical remains source; GCP remains the runtime
reader. No new database, API route or continuously running service is introduced.
This change implements a callable adapter, not a deployed job.

Source mapping is fixed: root `PLAID_CLIENT_ID` and `PLAID_SECRET` map to
`jayburd-dev-bank-sync-client-id` and `jayburd-dev-bank-sync-client-secret`.
Eight `/bank-sync/slot-00` through `slot-07` keys map to corresponding destinations.
A separate root `JAYBURD_DELIVERY_CANARY` maps only to the precreated canary
destination. The [controlled job](delivery-job.md) initially accepts only this key.
Original root values stay in place; references and whole-folder imports are disabled.
Every invocation selects an exact positive source version and expected source ID.
The configured project/environment and returned identity/version must match.

An immutable GCS intent keyed by destination and source version precedes the sole
Google addVersion attempt. Concurrent calls, conflicting source identity and unknown
intent acknowledgement cannot authorize another write. A lost Google or receipt
acknowledgement returns PARTIAL/unknown: a later call returns a matching immutable
receipt if present, otherwise stops for reviewed recovery. No automatic rotation,
retry or cleanup is implied. Dynamic slots remain never-reused; static rotation
requires another explicit source version. Delivery receipts are transport evidence,
not runtime verification, freshness evidence or permission to use revoked versions.

The adapter has exact-key source read permission, destination versions.add, and
create/read access to its own private registry prefix. It has no destination value
read, project secret listing, source write, container create or delete capability.
Separate runtime verification retains CRC32C/payload matching and numeric pinning.
The new worker identity, registry prefix IAM, owner-injected synthetic canary and
controlled job composition must be reviewed before any hosted execution.

## Sources and alternatives

Reviewed relevant implementation and REST sections on 2026-10-14:

- [Infisical GCP implementation](https://github.com/Infisical/infisical/blob/bd18bfdc374008c79581812529af7672fce71cc2/backend/src/services/secret-sync/gcp/gcp-sync-fns.ts):
  `getGcpSecrets` lists project secrets and reads latest payloads before the sync
  loop filters keys. This establishes upstream behavior, not the hosted version.
- [Google addVersion](https://cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.secrets/addVersion):
  accepts an existing parent and requires versions.add; no idempotency key is
  documented. Our inference is to reserve before attempting and stop on ambiguity.
- [Infisical retrieve](https://infisical.com/docs/api-reference/endpoints/secrets/read):
  exact version, folder, project, environment and disabled expansion/imports allow
  explicit reads. Account permissions still require actual qualification.

Alternative: isolate native sync in a separate GCP project and authorize read-back.
That adds infrastructure and changes runtime project configuration while retaining
broader access inside that project. Direct runtime Infisical reads would change
startup availability. Neither is selected. The owned adapter adds maintenance and
can strand an intent after a crash; recovery is deliberately manual until reviewed.

## Acceptance and applicability

`TestDeliveryCanary` proves fictional root-key delivery, exact source version,
numeric destination receipt and replay without a second write. Failure tests cover
concurrency, lost acknowledgements, mismatched source/receipt, invalid targets,
denied requests and redacted diagnostics. All transports are injected fakes.
Hosted isolation, revocation, rotation and recovery remain required #11 evidence.
This is an internal credential protocol; ISO 20022 does not apply. No accounting
or financial-message contract changes. See the living delivery runbook.

documents.title: Self-service bank onboarding
documents.body:
# Self-service bank onboarding

## Decision

Issue #155 supersedes the per-book operator requirement in the Sandbox bootstrap
contract. A verified creator with current read/post access clicks Connect account.
The existing Begin(new) request prepares missing connection infrastructure and
persists its attempt in one serializable transaction before provider work.

## Authority

Runtime supplies pre-provisioned sync/publisher SQL login identifiers. Requests
cannot choose logins, service principals or grants. SQL verifies worker capability,
the exact setup receipt, active creator/read/post access and book/entity state.
It grants only creator import/connect and per-book service read/import, then uses
the existing audited worker/delivery enrollment functions. API receives execution
on bounded wrappers, never owner membership, direct table writes or role grants.

Existing configuration uses ordinary connection authorization. Revoked grants,
disabled principals/bindings, foreign creators, missing worker capability and
conflicts reject without reactivation. Repeated Begin keys and concurrent requests
retain the existing durable-attempt replay contract. Failed attempt creation rolls
back provisioning; provider failures leave a discoverable durable attempt.

## Discovery and consent

List and attempt discovery may return empty results for an eligible unconfigured
creator after the same checks, without writes or provider calls. Clicking Connect
account is consent to prepare this book for bank setup. Plaid consent and exact
source-account/currency/ledger binding review remain separate and explicit.
No journal, initial balance, scheduler activation or cloud resource is created.

## Sources and standards

Reviewed 2026-10-15: PostgreSQL 17 CREATE FUNCTION, “Writing SECURITY DEFINER
Functions Safely” ([S12](../research/database-sources.md#s12--restricted-posting-functions)),
and Transaction Isolation, “Serializable Isolation Level”
([manual](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/transaction-iso.html)). Relevant
sections reviewed in full. They establish restricted search paths, explicit
execution grants and whole-transaction retry requirements; creator eligibility
and no-reactivation are project policy, demonstrated separately by tests.

Builds on the reviewed [bootstrap](sandbox-book-bootstrap.md),
[connection SQL](connection-sql.md), and [delivery SQL](acquisition-dispatch-sql.md)
contracts. The alternative operator script leaves a product onboarding gap;
granting runtime owner membership would give unrelated authority. Scoped SQL
wrappers retain the existing security-definer and serializable transaction model.
This internal authorization operation has no applicable ISO 20022 message;
existing provider currency and account contracts retain their ISO mappings.

## Acceptance

Named PostgreSQL tests cover discovery without writes, first use, replay,
concurrency, rollback, cross-scope/disabled/revoked denial, and API privilege
boundaries. Service tests prove Begin provisions before provider work. Browser
and real application tests cover a fresh creator-owned book reaching Link.
Shared multi-book publisher dispatch is tracked in
[#156](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/156) and must
be qualified before claiming automatic acquisition across every registered book.

documents.title: API composition and workspace discovery
documents.body:
# API composition and workspace discovery

## Decision

Implementation review for #3/#6. `cmd/api` defaults to a loopback health-only
listener: `/healthz` is 200, `/readyz` is 503 and bookkeeping routes are absent.
No SDK, environment secret or database is consulted in this mode. Managed mode
is explicit; migration and identity enrollment remain separate operator actions.
Sources, alternatives and limits are in [server sources](../research/server-sources.md).

## Managed configuration

Start with `-mode=managed -listen=127.0.0.1:8080 -origin=https://books.example.invalid
-project=OWNER_SELECTED_PROJECT`. The owner injects `JAYBURD_DATABASE_URL` through
the approved secret workflow; never put a DSN on a command line, in logs or Git.
The DSN must be a PostgreSQL URL with explicit user, host and database. Only
`sslmode` may be a query parameter: default `verify-full` uses system roots;
`disable` is permitted only for a loopback database proxy. Certificate, passfile,
service and inherited PG configuration are not supported. File defaults are
explicitly overridden; no user credential file is loaded.

The Admin SDK receives an explicit project and metadata-service token source.
No ADC credential discovery is used. Emulator, metadata-host override, Firebase
config and application credential-file environment presence are rejected before
client construction. Runtime verification also rejects emulator presence.
This requires a separately provisioned GCP workload identity; no cloud resource
or IAM permission is created. Provider verification/revocation and TOTP are the
[identity contract](identity-setup.md), not health-probe assertions.

Legacy URL mode is bounded to eight connections. The [Cloud SQL mode](cloud-sql.md)
uses a five-connection IAM pool and explicit nonsecret instance flags; it rejects
ambient DSN presence. Readiness checks database
reachability, runtime-role membership, unsafe inherited roles, table authority,
