DDL privileges, enrollment exclusion and migration4's discovery entrypoint.
It does not call Identity Platform or prove live-bookkeeping approval. The
container runs as numeric non-root with a static executable and system CA bundle.
TLS termination, network access and abuse rate limits remain deployment gates.

## HTTP lifecycle

The bearer-only frontend uses the [same-origin `/v1/` bridge](private-api-bridge.md). Configure one exact
HTTPS origin; explicit `http://localhost` or `http://127.0.0.1` origins support local
development. Origin changes grant no CORS or cookie authority. No query token,
public signup, actor header or close endpoint exists.

Limits: 32 concurrent handlers, 4KiB request URI, 32KiB headers, 1MiB request body,
5-second header timeout, 15-second read/write timeout, 30-second idle timeout and
12-second handler context. Existing auth/transaction budgets remain shorter.
SIGINT/SIGTERM removes readiness, drains at most 15 seconds, then closes the pool.
API admission, shutdown and URI-limit failures use safe RFC 9457 JSON with a
server-generated request ID. No request or provider access logging.

## Workspace contract

`GET /v1/workspace` takes no query/body and authenticates before SQL. It returns
`entities`, `currencies` and `development_policy: dev-accrual-usd-v1`. Each entity
has `entity_id`, `name`, `kind`, current `permissions` and active `books`. Each book
has `book_id`, `name`, string `book_revision`, `policies`, `periods`, `accounts`.
Policy records contain IDs, ISO 4217 functional currency and effective dates;
periods contain ID/dates/state; accounts contain ID/code/name/category/normal side,
monetary flag and activity dates. Currency versions contain ID/alphabetic code,
minor unit and validity dates. Nullable end dates remain null; collections are
always arrays. Account/reference history is configuration, not journal disclosure.

Actor-first membership indexing bounds discovery to granted scopes.
Principal/entity/membership/book share locks protect a repeatable-read snapshot.
Only active entities with active read permission appear; post alone is insufficient.
Enrolled users with no memberships receive currencies and empty entities to begin
setup. Disabled/unknown principals receive the existing safe 404; bad authentication
receives 401. Responses exceeding 100 entities, 200 total books, 200 accounts/book,
100 policies/book, 240 periods/book, 1000 currency versions or 1MiB fail with 413;
no partial list is returned. Pagination is a future contract before larger scale.

These are internal control/configuration operations, not ISO 20022 exchanges;
existing ISO 4217 version references remain authoritative. No conformance claim.

## Acceptance and limits

`TestServerBoundary`, `TestServerAdmission` and `TestManagedConfiguration` test inert defaults, saturation, safe
configuration, origins, readiness and bounds. `TestWorkspaceAuthorization`,
`TestWorkspaceRevocation` and `TestWorkspaceBounds` exercise actual runtime roles,
read/post separation, both revocation lock orders and oversize failure. Existing
posting/setup suites still apply. `TestRuntimeReadiness` uses isolated roles to
reject table, enrollment, owner/operator and schema authority.
`bash scripts/test-api-container.sh` builds the strict source allowlist and probes
the non-root/read-only health-only image over an internal Docker network; no host
ports or environment secrets are passed. `--local-build` is an explicit fallback
using the host Go compiler and identical pinned CA/scratch runtime; it does not
validate the canonical source-builder stage. Keep that stage required in CI. The [branch runbook](../runbooks/first-app.md)
owns observed execution evidence. Live metadata, IAM, provider and TLS behavior
remain unverified until a separately approved synthetic deployment.

documents.title: Shared acquisition publisher
documents.body:
# Shared acquisition publisher

## Decision record

**Question.** How can every enrolled Sandbox book receive initial and requested
Plaid Transactions sync work without configuring one Cloud Run publisher per book?
Issue #156 extends the existing publisher, not the financial source authority.
The publisher login sees only bindings enrolled for that exact login and each
binding still uses its existing authorization, consent, principal, stream,
lease and generation checks before dispatch. No journal is posted.

**Status and owner.** Accepted for implementation in the development project by
the owner's 2026-10-20 request to make acquisition automatic. Hosted activation
requires migration-first delivery and fresh Sandbox evidence. Live institutions
remain gated by #90.

**Sources and review depth.** The reviewed
[acquisition SQL](acquisition-dispatch-sql.md), [runtime](acquisition-dispatch-runtime.md),
[background work](background-work.md) and [self-service book](self-service-connections.md)
contracts define the existing invariants. The [Plaid Transactions webhook guide](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/webhooks/)
and [Transactions API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/) were
reviewed 2026-10-20 for initial `/transactions/sync`, cursor updates, webhook
wakeup and provider polling cadence; the exact source record is
[shared acquisition sources](../research/shared-acquisition-sources.md).
These are provider facts; shared scheduling, fairness and SQL cursor design are
Jayburd inferences. No tenant webhook configuration or hosted result was observed.

## SQL and runtime contract

`integration.sync_delivery_bindings(maximum)` is a publisher-only,
SECURITY DEFINER, serializable function. It accepts only a limit (1–5), never
book/actor identity. It checks `session_user=current_user` at the login boundary,
the approved publisher role and a durable per-login cursor. An index on enabled
`(publisher_login,binding_id)` supports keyset pagination with wraparound. The
function returns up to five binding IDs for that login and advances its cursor
atomically. A crash after cursor commit delays a binding only until a later
rotation; it does not lose its SQL demand. Missing, disabled and foreign bindings
are not selected. All other binding authority is rechecked inside the existing
`sync_delivery_discover` and subsequent dispatch functions.

`shared-v1` publisher mode visits at most five bindings per tick and at most
five candidate operations per binding, within the existing 60-second request
budget. A revoked binding can fail with the fixed `not_authorized` code and be
skipped; it cannot stop a healthy binding in the same batch. Unexpected database
or transport failures are reported after the remaining bindings have been
attempted. The durable cursor gives eventual round-robin progress beyond one
page, with no in-memory state. Work is still idempotent and at-least-once.

`binding-v1` remains the fixed-binding rollback mode. The runtime and release
manifest explicitly choose `publisher_policy`. `shared-v1` requires an empty
binding ID; `binding-v1` requires the pinned UUID. The consumer remains unchanged.
The Cloud Scheduler tick is enabled only for the Sandbox development deployment,
with OIDC and Cloud Run invoker IAM owned by the existing Terraform stack.
Automatic sync uses the already configured webhook wakeups and periodic SQL
catch-up. It does not call paid `/transactions/refresh` or claim that Plaid has
newer data than the provider makes available.

## Standards, alternatives and acceptance

The scheduler body and Cloud Tasks work-wakeup-v1 are internal control messages,
not ISO 20022 financial messages. Source currency remains ISO 4217 by the
existing decoder contract. ISO 21378/21926 export mappings and accounting
policy do not change. No ISO conformance is claimed.

One publisher per book would make self-service enrollment depend on deployment.
Scanning all bindings every minute would be unbounded; scanning by client
supplied book would cross the scheduler trust boundary. A login-scoped SQL
keyset cursor preserves bounded fairness and existing per-book checks.

Synthetic SQL and Go tests must prove two enrolled books, distinct principals,
five-plus-one pagination, exact-login scope, revoked/disabled skips, concurrent
ticks and bounded work. Release tests must prove `shared-v1` has no binding UUID
and `binding-v1` rollback still works. Hosted acceptance checks scheduler HTTP
200, consumer HTTP204, completed generations and no unauthorized provider effect
for a newly enrolled Sandbox book.

documents.title: Source-first workspace contract proposal
documents.body:
# Source-first workspace contract proposal

Status: proposed under #238, 2026-10-21. [ADR 0006](../decisions/0006-source-first-workspace.md)
owns the decision and evidence. This document defines authority and acceptance
for later scoped SQL/API contracts; it is not an implemented endpoint, migration,
permission grant or posting policy.

## Identity and record grains

| Concept | Grain and authority | Financial effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Verified principal | Exact trusted issuer+subject enrolled by an operator; current owner-private workspace access | Can begin private collection only through an explicit permission; email, caller actor ID and Plaid metadata grant nothing. |
| Plaid Item/consent | One provider/environment/Item identity with one credential reference and lifecycle generation, owned by the private collection workspace | Authorizes provider acquisition only while current principal/consent/service authority holds; one Item may expose accounts of different legal owners. |
| Source account | Stable local identity for one institution account and its provider aliases/reconnect evidence | Holds source transactions and cursor lineage; legal owner is separately asserted, never inferred from name/mask/type. |
| Source observation | One provider transaction identity with immutable acquired revisions, original amount/currency/dates/status and source account | Remains private evidence; pending, modified or removed provider facts do not mutate a posted journal. A new identity after reconnect is held until overlap review. |
| Legal owner assertion | Effective-dated claim for a source account, reviewer, evidence reference and revision | Informs reconciliation proposals; grants no source, entity or book access. Does not post or certify live ownership. Conflicts/overlaps hold review. |
| Topic/strategy label | Versioned owner taxonomy and audited observation label | Analytic only; can span entity views authorized to the principal; changes do not move a book or journal. |
| Suggestion | Provider category or owner rule output with origin/version/confidence or abstention and reviewer decision | Inert until reviewed; no automatic draft, account mapping or posting. Future models have a separate privacy and quality gate. |
| Book disposition | Reviewed link from source observation revision to one or more proposed book treatments with current grants, currency and policy pins | May create a draft only under an approved scoped accounting contract; cross-entity cases hold until #244/#1. |
| Posted journal/source link | Existing balanced, immutable entity/book journal and provenance | Only explicit authorized posting; corrections by linked reversal/new entries. |

No local user account is auto-created from Plaid, no source account is an entity,
and no book is a folder that can change legal entity after posting. A source account
with unknown legal owner remains visible to its authorized collector but cannot be
used to present an entity cash balance.

## Scope and operation matrix

| Operation | Required current authority and behavior | Denial/replay rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Begin/complete Link | Verified enrolled principal with explicit private collection permission; durable attempt, one-shot exchange and secret reference | Expired/revoked identity or consent denies. Unknown remote result remains unresolved; retry cannot exchange twice. |
| Acquire/list source transactions | Current owner collection permission, active Item consent, scoped worker identity and account capability; bounded complete-set publication | Account revocation stops that stream; Item revoke/rotate fences all siblings. Replay rechecks current authority and generation. No book or journal write. |
| All Transactions | Verified principal with current access to each returned source account; server-scoped query and snapshot/cursor pagination | Never use caller-supplied scope as authority. Revocation removes rows on next request; stale cursors fail. No unbounded cross-workspace scan or browser persistence. |
| Assert legal owner | Verified principal authorized for both collection and target entity setup/review; reviewed evidence reference and effective date | Conflicting or overlapping claims hold; no ownership derived from provider fields. Later changes preserve assertion history. |
| Label/accept suggestion | Current source-review permission; exact observation and taxonomy/rule revisions | Immutable decision history; label edit never changes books, posted journals or source revision. |
| Create/select book disposition | Current source read/review plus current target entity/book prepare rights, policy/currency/period checks | Target-denied or stale pins reject. Cross-entity treatment needs independent current rights in each book and #244 policy. |
| Explicit post/correct | Existing book-scoped post/correction authority and reviewed immutable draft/command | No automatic post from acquisition, topic, rule or provider category. Posted journal remains in its original entity/book. |

The new private collection permission is a proposed capability, not a self-grant.
#239 must define restricted SQL functions and grants, exact lock/retry order,
retention and deletion. The browser/API may render only safe projections; credentials,
provider payloads and financial requests never enter browser persistence or logs.

## Source acquisition and migration invariants

- Request up to 90 days on new Transactions initialization, store the requested
  window and expose actual history readiness/coverage separately. An empty early
  sync page is not complete history. Preserve original units with ISO 4217 code
  and applicable dated currency reference; never use floating point for money.
- Use provider/environment/Item/account/transaction plus local identity and
  revision provenance to deduplicate within a provider identity. A changed
  account ID, Item or filter cannot inherit a cursor or silently identify an
  older transaction. New IDs stay distinct and held until explicit overlap
  review. Page mutation restarts the complete filtered pagination loop from its
  original cursor; publication is atomic and replay-safe.
- Current book-scoped Items and posted source anchors remain accessible through
  compatibility reads. Adoption of the same provider/environment/Item identity
  uses one audited authority transition, not a second Item row. The forward
  migration does not reparent, delete or silently copy existing observations,
  journals or source links. Before adoption succeeds, legacy streams keep their
  current behavior; any newly linked Item requires overlap detection and current
  permission checks before combining its history with legacy evidence.
- An account disconnect is a local stream fence; it does not call Plaid Item
  removal or imply provider-side consent revocation. Item removal, rotation and
  consent revocation fence all sibling streams. Credential cleanup and retained
  evidence follow a reviewed retention policy, not a UI assumption.
- A missing dated ISO 4217 reference or unofficial/unsupported currency cannot
  be silently converted or omitted while advancing a cursor. Publish the whole
  acquired change set into private evidence or quarantine with a fixed hold
  reason; mark affected observations visible as held in All Transactions, with
  original units only where validated. They cannot enter book review, draft or
  journal until currency mapping is reviewed. #239 must define atomic cursor/
  hold storage and bounded retention without weakening existing checks.

## Global review and classification boundaries

All Transactions must include unassigned, reviewable, held, draft and posted
observations from every source the principal may currently read. Display source
account, original amount/currency/date, provider pending/modified/removed/held status,
acquisition freshness, legal-owner assertion, topic labels, suggestion provenance,
book disposition and journal status as separate fields. Support bounded server
filters and stable pagination; no empty-state claim of complete history before
provider history readiness is known.

Plaid `personal_finance_category`, merchant and enrichment are untrusted source
metadata. An owner topic can be attached to many observations, and an observation
can have multiple analytic labels. An owner rule may propose a topic or ledger
category, with version/confidence or abstention, but acceptance is a distinct
audited decision. Bookkeeping category is the selected book's ledger account and
policy, not a topic or Plaid category. Any split/allocation or FX treatment needs
its own reviewed accounting contract.

## Standards applicability and planned evidence

Plaid Link/Accounts/Transactions JSON is a proprietary provider exchange. The
proposed ISO 20022 assessment is `not applicable` to this Plaid wire profile;
#240 must record the exact purpose, reviewed registered definitions and final
applicability/mapping before implementation. Do not invent a `camt` designation.
Internal collection commands/events require their own applicability entry,
version and semantic mapping. ISO 4217 currency code and
dated minor-unit reference apply to every monetary observation. ISO 21378 audit
export applicability remains unresolved at field level because only public
abstract/metadata were reviewed. See [standards](standards.md); no conformance
claim follows from a label or XSD.

Planned synthetic evidence, independent of implementation: connection without a
book; one Item/two legal account owners; 90-day request with shorter available
history; empty early response; account and Item revocation; lost exchange and
unknown commit; account-ID churn; pending→posted/modified/removed transaction;
existing bound Item migration; duplicate source suppression; USD/JPY/KWD original
unit preservation; cross-principal denial; global pagination across 3,000 items;
topic/rule override without journal mutation; cross-entity expense held with no
journal before policy; immutable correction after posting. #244 and #1 later own
policy-approved coordinated-entry fixtures. #239–#244 own executable tests and
reviewed results. STD-01–STD-05 in
the standards contract remain required for the applicable implemented slice.

documents.title: Source-derived journals and linked corrections — #332
documents.body:
# Source-derived journals and linked corrections — #332

## Decision, authority and implementation status

Owner2026-10-25 approved bank-read-only access with ledger bookkeeping, retained
source revisions and reconcilable journals. Coordinator engineering design under
#332/#104; no SQL/API implementation, live accounting policy, security review or
activation approval is claimed. #333 implements corrections, #334 opt-in rules,
#335 UI and #336 independent end-to-end proof. Initial personal registration90
does not wait for the complete rule engine; existing manual posting/reversal
can be used only within its actual accepted scope and current permissions.

Bank observations are authoritative evidence of what the provider reports, with
immutable revisions and an explicit current pointer. The ledger is the durable
accounting record, including policy decisions and non-bank entries. Provider
categories/dates alone do not select recognition, accounts, FX or tax treatment.
No real book silently inherits dev-accrual-usd-v1. Reviewed per-book policy and
current prepare/post permissions determine eligible accounting effects.

## Current source inventory and gap

At main1bacecda: migration11 banking.review_posting is immutable and keyed by
entity/book/review; it links one original draft/command/journal and cannot be
updated to a replacement. Migration12 banking.provider_posted_anchor preserves
the original posted observation/journal, and banking.provider_review_exception
records modified/removed source revisions. Subsequent precision/history functions
retain these anchors. Present exception rendering is bounded reference metadata,
not complete before/after financial inspection or correction resolution.

ledger.post_journal/reverse_journal use the existing balanced immutable posting
boundary, canonical receipts, audit/outbox, current authorization and book revision.
Reverse copies original historical money/rates; it does not reprice history.
ledger.interactive_command stores reviewed work before explicit execution and
terminal acknowledgement. These existing functions are reusable mechanisms;
calling two independent HTTP operations is not atomic linked correction.

Acquisition still never writes a journal or receives posting permission. Local
bookkeeping of authorized retained history need not stop merely because new
provider access expires or is paused. Source data access/review and book posting
permissions remain independently current; revoked access is not restored by
having a historical receipt. Provider fetch/retention authority is not bypassed.

## Review snapshot and logical interfaces

The #333 SQL/API review must freeze exact physical signatures/OpenAPI before DDL.
Logical boundaries are owned source-correction inspection, immutable reviewed
preparation, and same-command atomic execution/recovery; no arbitrary SQL selector
or caller actor. Expected SQL names are banking.get_source_correction,
banking.prepare_source_correction and banking.execute_source_correction, not
implemented guarantees. Public actor always comes from verified identity.

Inspection requires current book/source read; preparation adds current prepare
and source-review authority; execution adds current post. Current retained-source
policy must be checked explicitly rather than assuming active provider consent
is a prerequisite for every local ledger read or correction. Operator/superuser
access is outside runtime guarantees. No table DML or new implicit grant.

The persisted reviewed snapshot pins entity/book/source/namespace/observation,
original root journal, currently effective journal, expected correction-chain
version, exact original-posted and target source revisions, binding/source/review/
book revisions, exception identities, policy/rule version, action/reason, accounting
date, eligible category/ledger accounts and full normalized posting/valuation pins.
Currency versions, original amount lexemes and functional assertions remain exact
strings. Current bank state and current accounting state are separate fields.
Return bounded authorized structured facts, not a provider payload or credential.

First actions:

- replace: exact reversal of the effective ordinary journal plus one reviewed
  eligible replacement. No reversal of a reversal; the replacement becomes the
  next effective journal while the original root remains immutable.
- no_financial_effect: explicit reviewed evidence that changed metadata does not
  change accounting under the pinned policy. No journal, book revision or
  journal.posted intent; retain a resolution/audit receipt.
- reverse_only: explicit reviewed cancellation/removal under a permitted policy,
  confirming no replacement should be recorded. Exact historical reversal only;
  never infer this merely from a removed feed record or emit a zero-value journal.

Pending/unmatched replacement, unknown removal meaning, unmapped classification,
unsupported currency, missing FX/policy, zero replacement or closed period remain
actionable holds until a valid reviewed action exists. Missing capabilities stay
visibly unavailable. Old period data is not rewritten; a later correction date
needs the selected policy, not an automatic date/rounding plug.

## Durable operation, locking and atomicity

Register the exact reviewed correction on the existing principal interactive gate
before execution; explicit confirmation and terminal acknowledgement remain.
Registration/discovery/cancellation never post. A versioned deterministic rule
uses its separately reviewed durable operation under an approved current service
principal and scoped post authority; a webhook/acquisition wakeup is not that grant.

Serializable transaction, SQL-owned canonical full-body equality and whole-
transaction retry remain authoritative. First lock all participating current
principals in UUID order, then existing entity/membership/book order, source/
permission and namespace/observation/review, correction chain/command/receipt,
policy/period/accounts and effective journal in the reconciled existing order.
The exact lock table must be reviewed in #333 against current posting/import/
acquisition functions before implementation; never take a weaker lock first and
upgrade through a conflicting path. No provider/network/key work inside locks.

Reauthorize and compare all uncommitted expected pins before financial work. The
same transaction creates the original-value reversal, policy-valued replacement,
their existing journal receipts/audit/outbox, immutable correction resolution,
source-to-effective-journal links and committed command result. Either every
effect commits or none. Preserve each underlying journal's normal book-revision
increment: replace has two increments, not an invented single journal revision.
Do not expose a half-corrected report or acknowledge before COMMIT.

Preserve banking.review_posting, provider_posted_anchor and exception rows.
Append a scoped immutable resolution/correction chain with predecessor/root/
effective-journal/revision references. Unresolved status is derived from exception
plus resolution evidence; a counter or latest100 projection cannot silently drop
older unresolved work. Validate unique correction targets and no cross-book or
namespace chain, cycles, duplicate active effects or repeat reversal. Exact table/
constraint/grant definitions belong to the forward #333 migration review; no
migration version is reserved by this document.

Same committed command/body under current operation permission returns its exact
original result without revalidating old rates/source/current pins or new writes.
A newer bank revision does not invalidate knowledge of an already committed
correction. It creates new unresolved work. Changed body/same key conflicts; a
new key/stale snapshot cannot become another reversal. Lost result means inspect/
reconcile the same command, never invent a new transaction. If source60 arrives
before an uncommitted55 correction executes, stale pins deny; after55 committed,
read its receipt and prepare a new55->60 operation targeting effective journal55.

## Independent worked expectations

Fictional expense scenarios, same open period and explicitly eligible accounts/
policy, no opening-balance invention. These are fixed oracle values, not results
generated by implementation. Dr expense / Cr bank; reversals swap exact sides.

| Stage | New journals | Retained journal count | Net expense/bank credit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Booked source USD50, reviewed original post | original50 |1|USD50|
| Source changes to55, before correction | none |1|USD50, unresolved discrepancy5|
| Confirm replace with reversal50 and replacement55 |2|3|USD55|
| Replay event/command/lost terminal reply |0|3|USD55|
| Later source60, confirmed effective55 reversal and replacement60 |2|5|USD60; original50 and first correction retained|
| Metadata-only later change under unchanged recognition |0|5|USD60, explicit no-effect resolution|

EUR example: original EUR10 at explicitly selected synthetic EUR/USD1.20 ->
functional USD12.00. Changed source EUR11 with the same eligible policy/rate ->
replacement USD13.20. Exact reversal retains EUR10/USD12.00 and its historical
rate identity. Three journals net EUR11/USD13.20; no aggregation of unlike units.
A different replacement FX/date requires a separately reviewed eligible pin;
missing rate holds. Synthetic rates never authorize a live market-rate policy.

## Source/standards evidence, alternatives and threat review

[Posting sources P01–P07](../research/posting-sources.md) record exact source
sections/depth/limits. Plaid settled changes are vendor feed facts; this restricted
correction protocol is our engineering choice. Existing proprietary financial
mapping, ISO4217 dated currencies and original units remain. This internal
operational command is not a registered ISO20022 exchange; ISO21378 audit relevance
retains abstract-only limits and no export/conformance claim. SQL/Go profile
compatibility and versioned normalized correction input must be fixed before DDL.

Alternatives: rewriting original journals destroys audit evidence; reconstructing
all journals as a bank-table view loses manual/policy/non-bank accounting; two HTTP
calls expose partial correction. Delta adjustments can be legitimate but are not
selected without their own reviewed operation. Full linked reversal/replacement
reuses existing historical valuation and balanced posting boundaries.

STRIDE: spoofed source/tenant/rule (high) -> verified/current roles plus all scoped
FK/pins; stale/tampered/replayed work (high) -> immutable review/body equality,
serializable locks and unique targets; partial effects (high) -> one transaction/
same-command recovery; disclosure (high) -> current scoped reads, no-store/memory-
only browser state/fixed errors/no financial logs; abusive automation (high) ->
explicit versioned rule grant, holds and kill switch. Human review before sensitive
code merge and real mandates remain required; this is not independent signoff.

Named proposed evidence: TestSourceJournalCorrection50To55,
TestSuccessiveSourceCorrectionsTargetEffectiveJournal,
TestCorrectionMetadataNoEffectAndRemovalHold,
TestCorrectionOriginalEURAndHistoricalValuation,
TestCorrectionAtomicFailureAndUnknownCommit,
TestCorrectionConcurrentSourceUpdateAndRevocation,
TestCorrectionReplayAfterLaterSourceRevision and
TestCorrectionNoProviderIOForAuthorizedHistoricalWork. Real restricted SQL/API/
browser fixtures and exact reports in #333/#335/#336; no admin impersonation,
mock-only money totals or generator self-oracle. Core/ledger/migration/web/full-
stack gates follow changed boundary. No new feature is implemented by this plan.

documents.title: Synthetic source-account registry
documents.body:
# Synthetic source-account registry

## Decision and scope

Issue #81 implements only the registry portion of [durable import](durable-import.md):
stable source accounts, immutable adapter identities, explicit read grants and
scoped SQL reads. No upload, observation, draft, posting, provider connection,
HTTP endpoint or cloud provisioning. Coordinator review of this precise contract
precedes migration 000009. This resolves synthetic operator enrollment only;
neither a UUID nor operator assertion proves ownership of a real bank account.

## Operator and runtime boundary

Reuse NOLOGIN `bookkeeping_owner`; no new bootstrap role or API self-enrollment.
Operator functions are SECURITY INVOKER, executable only as current_user
bookkeeping_owner in SERIALIZABLE. An authorized provisioning login explicitly
SET LOCAL ROLEs to that owner. Audit records session_user independently from
approved_by, the active enrolled entity reader named in the reviewed manifest.
Runtime cannot assume this role, call provisioning or grant source permissions.
No new ledger membership value is added. The vocabulary reserves bind/import/review/read for the parent design, but only
read has a grant operation or runtime meaning here. No acquisition authority.

Every mutation takes approved principal, entity, read membership and book locks
following the ledger authorization protocol, with explicit canonical UUID order
for all affected principals/memberships before the book lock. This owned helper
retains the locks needed to revoke a disabled reader without weakening approver
authority; it does not call ledger.authorize twice in inconsistent order. The book lock serializes receipt replay; new work then locks the source. State/permission
changes and runtime reads share the same source/grant lock boundary. Dates and
money are not inferred from names. Existing account semantics are immutable;
future acquisition must revalidate account activity for each booked date.

## Exact SQL operations

All IDs are UUID, all raw inputs strict unique-key JSON objects <=8192 bytes,
keys match `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}`. UUID input normalization accepts the existing
hyphenated grammar; date strings use ledger.date_value. Revision strings are
canonical unsigned bigint. All functions use schema-qualified references and
`search_path=pg_catalog,pg_temp`. Error codes P2300 malformed, P2301 unavailable,
P2302 conflict, P2303 unsupported mapping/profile, P2304 limit/overflow;
messages contain no source values. Transaction isolation errors are P2300.

| Function | Arguments / result and authority |
| --- | --- |
| banking.register_source | `(approved_by,e,b,key,raw)` →jsonb. Owner-only. Exact raw keys ledger_account_id,currency_version_id,binding_date,binding_evidence_ref,reader_principal_id,namespace. Namespace keys profile,synthetic_dataset_id,source_account_ref. Atomically create source, first namespace, read grant and receipt/audit. |
| banking.register_source_namespace | `(approved_by,e,b,source_id,key,raw)` →jsonb. Owner-only. Keys expected_binding_revision,namespace. Add immutable namespace, increment binding revision; subsequent namespace permanently carries overlap_review_required=true. |
| banking.set_source_state | `(approved_by,e,b,source_id,key,raw)` →jsonb. Owner-only. Keys expected_binding_revision,state. active↔paused, either→retired; retired never reactivates. Retire all namespaces, keep identities and read access. Same state is a conflict, not another transition. |
| banking.set_source_permission | `(approved_by,e,b,source_id,key,raw)` →jsonb. Owner-only. Keys expected_binding_revision,principal_id,enabled (JSON boolean). Grant/revoke only read; grant requires active current entity reader. No-op requested state conflicts. Increment binding revision; no ledger membership mutation. |
| banking.get_source | `(actor,e,b,source_id)` →jsonb. SECURITY DEFINER, API EXECUTE only. Repeatable-read or serializable; current entity read plus unrevoked source read; principal/entity/book/grant locks serialize revocation. Unknown/wrong-scope/denied returns uniform P2301. Paused/retired records remain readable history, never acquisition authority. |

Owner results are `{source_account_id,namespace_id?,binding_revision}`. Full
normalized request, operator login, approved_by, operation and idempotency key
identify replay. Same request returns the original result without applying grants
or state again; changed request conflicts. Replay still checks current approver authority and active grantee membership
for enrollment/grant. Revocation locks an existing reader even if disabled or
without current membership; otherwise a dormant source grant could survive later
identity reactivation. Returned revision is the operation's committed revision, not current
state. Unknown COMMIT requires replay with the same key and body; no HTTP recovery
operation is introduced. Retired identity cannot be reused with a new key.

Read result profile source-registry-v1 contains entity_id,book_id,source_account_id,
ledger_account_id,currency_version_id,currency,minor_units,binding_date,state,
binding_revision,source_revision and namespaces. Each namespace contains namespace_id,
profile,synthetic_dataset_id,source_account_ref,state,overlap_review_required.
Migration12 adds a tagged provider namespace variant, documented in
[provider sync SQL](provider-sync-sql.md): provider, environment, item_id and
provider_account_id replace CSV dataset/ref fields. Existing CSV output remains
unchanged; the profile selects the identity shape. This is not a new public HTTP
enrollment surface or proof of live account ownership.
Revisions are decimal strings, namespace order UUID ascending, max 25 and <=64 KiB
result. No grant roster, evidence reference, approval identity or database login
is exposed. No list/discovery endpoint in this slice.

## Physical model and invariants

Book-owned rows use composite `(entity_id,book_id,id)` keys/FKs; no cascades.
Objects belong to bookkeeping_owner. All columns NOT NULL except revoked_at.
Timestamps are finite timestamptz. Server mints IDs; source_revision is zero until
a separately reviewed observation migration. Ordinary owner DML cannot rewrite identity or receipts/audit; controlled
provisioning is the supported path. The trusted schema owner can perform privileged
maintenance; this slice does not claim to contain a malicious database owner.

| Table | Fields and invariants |
| --- | --- |
| banking.source_account | source_account_id,ledger_account_id,currency_version_id,binding_date,binding_evidence_ref,created_by,created_at,state,binding_revision,source_revision. Unique entity/source UUID and scoped ledger_account_id. One source per ledger account is a deliberate first-profile restriction and survives retirement; it is not proof of real-world identity. Ledger FK preserves book scope. Binding requires asset/debit/monetary account active on binding_date; currency has nonnull ISO minor-unit metadata and validity covering date. No automatic USD default or FX. State active/paused/retired; binding_revision>=1. |
| banking.source_namespace | namespace_id,source_account_id,profile,synthetic_dataset_id,source_account_ref,state,overlap_review_required,created_by,created_at. Unique entity/profile/dataset/ref across books and source IDs. Profile exactly jayburd-synthetic-statement-csv/1; dataset UUID nonzero, ref `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` case-sensitive. Source FK scoped; max 25; state active/retired. Identity never changes, including after retirement. |
| banking.source_permission | source_account_id,principal_id,capability (read/bind/import/review; only read used here),revoked_at nullable; scoped PK includes principal/capability. FK to principal and source. Grants convey no permission without current ledger membership. |
| integration.source_registry_receipt | scope,operator_login,operation,idempotency_key,approved_by,normalized_request,result,recorded_at. PK scope/operator/operation/key. Immutable, <=16384-byte normalized request (raw input <=8192 bytes) and <=64 KiB result. Records exact manifest and database operator as both replay receipt and provisioning audit; existing audit.action is journal-scoped and unsuitable. |

Registration atomically writes all four rows or none. Additional namespace/state/
grant changes write corresponding rows and receipt together. No journal, outbox,
account mutation or ledger book-revision increment. Separate source identity does
not prove two different ledger accounts represent different real bank accounts;
the operator must review that manifest. Cross-adapter continuity and actual Plaid
namespaces require their accepted profile and explicit overlap decision later.

## Standards, sources and alternatives

Source registry is internal authorization/provenance metadata, not an ISO 20022
financial exchange. The decoder's explicit synthetic CSV exception and SI01–SI06
remain authoritative. ISO 4217 applies through installed immutable currency versions;
full-date follows RFC 3339/ISO 8601 profile. No IBAN/BIC/LEI, camt message or audit
export conformance is claimed. Live metadata releases and provider ownership remain
unresolved gates.

Reviewed sources: [DI01–DI03](durable-import.md#standards-sources-and-alternatives),
[bibliography S07/S08/S12](../research/database-sources.md) and
[schema ADR 0004](../decisions/0004-schema-ownership.md). PostgreSQL 17 constraints, serializable locking and SECURITY DEFINER
sections explain scoped FKs, replay transactions and restricted entrypoints;
they do not establish bank ownership or tax retention. These previously reviewed
sections underpin this implementation; no new financial standard is inferred.
Owner-only enrollment is narrower than adding a global operator role/bootstrap
for one synthetic fixture slice. Read grants avoid circular bind self-provisioning.
Unrestricted JSON identity would admit unreviewed adapters; explicit CSV columns
are chosen now, with later additive reviewed provider identity support.

## Required evidence

TestSourceRegistryEnrollment: exact same-key replay, changed-body conflict,
duplicate ledger account/namespace conflict, concurrent replay and no financial
effects. TestSourceRegistryMapping: inactive/mixed-scope/nondeposit accounts,
unsupported currency/date/null minor units and malformed fields fail atomically;
USD/JPY/KWD retain metadata. TestSourceRegistryAuthority: allowed, missing/revoked,
disabled principal/entity/book, wrong scope and current grant replay checks.
TestSourceRegistryLifecycle: pause/resume/retire, stale revision, namespace reuse,
immutable rows, explicit grant/revoke (including disabled/revoked grantees) and cap. TestSourceRegistryPrivileges:
API/worker/operator-role separation, no direct tables/DDL/helper execution.
TestSourceRegistryAtomicity: late receipt-write failure rolls back all source/grant
rows; same-key retry then succeeds. TestSourceRegistryMixedScope: real cross-book
account/FK/namespace violations fail. TestSourceRegistryRevocationRace: actual competing sessions prove read-first and
revoke-first serializations. These are required tests, not PASS until the runbook
records execution.

documents.title: Source review, category drafts and explicit posting
documents.body:
# Source review, category drafts and explicit posting

## Decision and limits

Migration11 implements #96: a readable source review inbox, immutable two-line
category drafts and recoverable `source_post`. A draft creates **no journal**.
Only explicit execution of its reviewed command creates the journal and immutable
source link in the same transaction. Existing posting SQL remains the authority
for policy, periods, exact money, accounts, balance, receipts and outbox intent.
[Durable import](durable-import.md), [import SQL](import-sql.md),
[posting boundary](posting-boundary.md) and [command recovery](command-recovery.md)
remain the underlying contracts.

Coordinator reviewed signatures before DDL and approved these bounded refinements:
one source observation per review, one selected offset account, original booked
date as accounting date, and same-currency identity valuation only. Source USD,
JPY and KWD units remain visible and exact. A foreign source against the book's
functional currency returns explicit `fx_required`; it never guesses a rate or
converts the source amount. Full split/spot category drafts, overlap matching,
correction intake and source-linked reversal are separate contracts. The existing
synthetic posting policy supports USD functional books; this migration does not
silently broaden that accounting policy.

Journal description is an explicit 1..500-character draft memo, separate from
immutable original source description. Categories come from the selected book's
active chart of accounts, excluding the bound source account. Categories are
account choices, not automatic accounting classifications. Outflow credits the
source asset and debits the chosen offset; inflow debits the source and credits
the chosen offset. A reviewer chooses the economic classification and must review
the complete resulting posting lines before confirming.

## Storage, permissions and revisions

New immutable `banking.review_draft` is keyed by scope/draft UUID, uniquely by
scope/review/review revision and scope/creator/idempotency key. It stores the
review/source/binding/book pins, exact generated posting body, complete normalized
review request, creator and timestamp. New immutable `banking.review_posting` has
one row per scoped review, unique draft/command/journal, scoped draft and journal
FKs and the original result. No history cascade or deletion is allowed.

`review_item` now permits only monotonic needs_review→draft_ready,
draft_ready→draft_ready and draft_ready→posted, with exactly one review revision
increment per transition. Its identity/source/created_at stay immutable.
Overlap_hold cannot draft/post. `review_decision` retains initialization and adds
immutable explicit-category draft decisions. Existing source observations,
revisions, assignments and evidence remain immutable.

Read/list/detail/categories require current entity read and explicit source read.
Draft mutation additionally requires current entity prepare and source review;
source_post registration/discovery/execute/cancel/acknowledge additionally requires
current entity post. No import grant substitutes for review/prepare/post. Current
permissions are checked before replay, including already committed commands.
Revoked unacknowledged work continues to block the principal gate until authority
is restored; this is not bypassed for convenience.

Owner-only `banking.set_source_review_permission(actor,e,b,source,key,raw)` accepts
`{expected_binding_revision,principal_id,enabled}`. It explicitly attests only the
source review grant, requires active current read membership when granting, and
permits dormant-grantee revocation. Existing entity prepare/post grants remain
separate. It records authenticated operator `session_user` and attested approver in
the existing immutable registry receipt, and increments binding revision. No API
self-grant or new runtime owner membership is introduced.

Each draft and source post increments source_revision as well as review_revision:
source revision now snapshots both source evidence and its review projection.
This makes state-filtered pagination consistent across requests. It conservatively
invalidates other previews/drafts on the same source. Drafts return the **new**
source revision they pin; source posting checks it before mutation. Drafting does
not change the book revision; successful posting increments it once through the
existing ledger function. A new draft supersedes but never overwrites an old draft.

Mutations require SERIALIZABLE, reads REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE with READ WRITE
transactions for authorization locks. Lock order starts with principal (strongest
lock for commands), entity/membership/book, source, then command/review as needed.
Source/book locks serialize snapshot changes. Functions own no commit and perform
no object I/O. Owner remains NOLOGIN bookkeeping_owner; API has narrow EXECUTE only,
no table DML or helper/operator EXECUTE. Observer/publisher grants are unchanged.

## Exact SQL and wire boundaries

All IDs are UUIDs; revision and money values are decimal strings, never floating
point. `actor,e,b` are trusted actor and entity/book UUID arguments. All functions
return jsonb. Bodies reject duplicate/unknown keys and malformed types before writes.

| Function | Input and result |
| --- | --- |
| `banking.list_sources(actor,e,b)` | `{profile:"source-list-v1",items:[Source]}`. Only readable sources, including paused/retired history; maximum100. Source: source_account_id, display_name (ledger account name), currency, currency_version_id, ledger_account_id, state, binding_revision, source_revision. Account labels are not ownership proof. |
| `banking.list_review_items(actor,e,b,raw text)` | Exact `{source_account_id,state,limit,cursor}`; state null or needs_review/overlap_hold/draft_ready/posted, limit integer1..100, cursor null or opaque string. Returns `{profile:"source-review-page-v1",source_account_id,source_revision,items:[Summary],next_cursor}`. |
| `banking.get_review_item(actor,e,b,review uuid)` | Existing signature, expanded detail below. Existing P2401 denied/inaccessible behavior is preserved. |
| `banking.review_categories(actor,e,b,review uuid)` | `{profile:"source-review-categories-v1",review_id,source_account_id,book_revision,policy_id,accounting_date,source_currency,functional_currency,fx_required,accounts}`. Accounts have account_id, code, name, category, normal_side, monetary. Maximum100 active accounts excluding source, ordered by code/UUID. |
| `banking.create_review_draft(actor,e,b,review uuid,key text,raw text)` | Exact `{expected_review_revision,source_revision,binding_revision,expected_book_revision,category_account_id,policy_id,accounting_date,description}`; returns Draft below. Body <=8KiB; key ASCII1..128. Accounting date must equal the immutable source booked date. |

Summary fields: review_id, state, review_revision, booked_date, currency,
currency_version_id, direction, amount, description, draft_id and journal_id;
last two nullable. Detail adds profile `source-review-v1`, source_account_id,
source_revision, binding_revision, book_revision, ledger_account_id, created_at,
blockers, evidence and nullable draft. Original evidence fields from import remain:
observation_id/revision, namespace_id, external_entry_id, source_state, booked_date,
currency_version_id, direction, amount and description. Detail flags overlap holds
and stale draft pins. Historical posted detail retains its original draft/journal.

Draft is `{draft_id,review_id,review_revision,source_revision,binding_revision,
book_revision,posting_body}`. Posting body is the complete existing PostingRequest
with two exact source/offset lines. Identity valuation has equal transaction and
functional amounts and no rate ID. The draft key is creator/book scoped and compares
full stored review/body identity; exact retry returns the original immutable draft
under current authorization before mutable state checks.

Cursor is bounded canonical hex-encoded JSON containing entity, book, source,
source_revision, complete state filter and last review UUID. SQL revalidates all
fields and current authority, rejects filter/scope changes, and returns
review_snapshot_changed when the source revision changed. It is an opaque position,
not an authorization token; tampering cannot grant source access. Pages are UUID
ordered, at most100; no unbounded dataset download or application-side filtering.
Source/account selector overflow fails explicitly rather than silently truncating.

Error codes: P2500 invalid_review/400; P2501 review_denied/404; P2502
review_conflict/409; P2503 review_snapshot_changed/409; P2504 fx_required/422;
P2505 review_limit/422. Existing posting P2100-series and source P2401 semantics
remain applicable. Messages contain no financial payloads or raw SQL diagnostics.

## Recoverable source posting

`source_post` shares the existing one-unacknowledged-principal command gate.
Its body is exactly `{review_id,draft_id,review_revision,source_revision,
binding_revision,expected_book_revision,posting_body}`. Including the complete
posting body makes remount/recovery human-reviewable; it is not an alternate
posting authority. SQL compares it and every pin with the immutable referenced
draft before registration or disclosure. Execution always uses the stored draft.

First execution rechecks current permissions, active source, draft_ready state,
review/source/binding/book pins and existing source link. It calls
`ledger.post_journal` inside the same transaction and writes the source snapshot
increment, posted review projection, immutable review_posting and committed command
audit/result. Any link/projection/command failure rolls the journal, lines, audit,
posting receipt, outbox and book revision back as well. There is no HTTP-post-then-link
sequence, worker posting or automatic confirmation.

Result is `{entity_id,book_id,review_id,draft_id,journal_id,book_revision,journal,
review_revision,source_revision}`; journal is the exact existing Journal response.
A committed command replays its exact result after current authorization without
rechecking mutable active/period state. Another command for the same immutable
already-posted draft returns the existing linked result; it cannot create a second
journal. A different historical draft conflicts. Direct manual journal duplication
is not solved by this link; manual-to-source matching remains separate work.
Two feeds representing opposite sides of an inter-account transfer also require a
future transfer-pair workflow; independently categorizing both is not semantic
deduplication. This slice does not automatically identify or match transfer pairs.

Cancel affects only the prepared command, leaving immutable draft history and
review state available for later explicit confirmation. A stale draft requires a
new explicit category draft/current pins, cancellation and acknowledgement of any
old prepared command, then new registration/confirmation. A committed command cannot
be cancelled. Acknowledgement releases the gate without deleting history. Unknown
commit means recover the same command, never generate a replacement key.

## Standards, sources and remaining gates

Applicability follows [standards](standards.md), existing SI01–SI06 import sources
and [posting policy sources](../research/posting-sources.md). This is an internal
workflow, not an ISO20022 financial message. ISO4217 currency-version/minor-unit
references and the existing ISO8601/RFC3339 date profile remain unchanged. Source
units and immutable provenance are retained; no ISO conformance or live accounting
approval is claimed. Financial exchanges, exports and accountant policy selection
remain under their dedicated contracts.

Mechanism review, 2026-10-13: existing DI01 and database source records, PostgreSQL17
[constraints](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/ddl-constraints.html),
[serializable transactions](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/transaction-iso.html)
and [owned function privileges](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-createfunction.html)
selected sections, plus repository migration2's exact posting implementation.
Inference: one database transaction can bind source review and ledger mutation
without a service bus. Separate HTTP posting/link writes were rejected because a
partial failure can orphan a journal or duplicate it. A full arbitrary-line editor
would broaden validation/UI scope; fixed two-line category drafts retain exact
source legs while explicit FX/split support is designed separately.

Actual evidence is in the [runbook](../runbooks/source-review-sql.md). Remaining work:
FX/split drafts, overlap matching, source corrections/reversals, reconciliation,
real acquisition/ownership, hosted retention and live policies. A populated synthetic
demo demonstrates flow, not accounting cutover readiness.

documents.title: Standards applicability contract
documents.body:
# Standards applicability contract

## Decision

Owner requirement: every financial message, data contract and practice must use
applicable ISO standards. This is an accepted design requirement, not evidence
of implemented conformance. It covers imports, exports, APIs, internal events,
currency metadata and audit data. Accounting recognition and measurement still
require a selected accounting framework and applicable jurisdictional rules.

## Reviewed sources and applicability

| Source | Application and review boundary |
| --- | --- |
| [ISO 20022 FAQ](https://www.iso20022.org/faq), sections About and Compliance | Financial messaging methodology and repository. Implementation depends on community requirements; there is no official ISO 20022 certification authority. Public FAQ reviewed, not the purchased standard's eight parts. |
| [Official message catalogue](https://www.iso20022.org/catalogue-messages), documentation and versions | Select registered definitions, schemas, Message Definition Reports and applicable Message Usage Guides. Catalogue overview reviewed; individual integration definitions remain to be selected and read. |
| [ISO 4217 currency codes](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html) | Use maintained currency identifiers and minor-unit metadata, including historical validity. Public overview reviewed. Codes do not determine exchange rates, functional currency or accounting rounding policy. |
| [ISO 21378:2019](https://www.iso.org/standard/70823.html), abstract | Audit-data collection and accounting data elements are relevant to audit exports. Abstract/metadata reviewed; full normative text not reviewed. Field-level conformance remains unverified. |

This list is a starting register, not an exhaustive declaration that other ISO
standards are inapplicable. Each slice must search authoritative sources for
additional applicable standards, including identifiers and audit semantics.
Textbooks and arXiv explain mechanics; they do not override accounting standards.

## Required record before implementation

Each message or practice contract must name:

1. Business purpose, direction, counterparties and responsible component.
2. Applicable standard, edition/effective date, exact message identifier and
   version, namespace, code-list release and bank/community usage profile.
3. Reviewed source sections and access limits. A paywalled abstract cannot
   substantiate detailed normative requirements.
4. A field/meaning mapping to internal contracts, including amounts, currencies,
   debit/credit perspective, dates, identifiers, statuses and reversal semantics.
5. Required fields, validation rules, supported versions, extension handling,
   information-loss policy and migration/compatibility policy.
6. Named synthetic fixtures, expected outcomes and the review evidence needed
   to assert the precisely scoped conformance claim.

Record `applicable`, `not applicable` with justification, or `unresolved` for
each assessed standard. An unresolved required mapping blocks implementation
of that slice. Deviations require a documented reviewed decision; silence is
not an exception. Prefer current definitions where counterparties support them;
pin supported versions instead of silently upgrading to a moving latest version.

## Project design consequences

Financial exchange adapters must validate the selected schema and its business
rules/profile. Schema validity alone cannot establish bookkeeping correctness.
Unsupported versions and unmapped financially material fields must be rejected
or held for explicit review before posting; never silently discard them.

Non-ISO bank feeds need explicit, traceable mappings into the internal financial
contract. Custom JSON does not become a registered ISO message by sharing field
names. Internal notifications may use a local schema when no ISO definition
applies, with that assessment recorded. Transport encoding is selected by the
applicable definition/profile, not a blanket XML requirement for every job.

Preserve original message identity and mapping/version provenance under the
data-access and retention policy. Retries, ordering, duplicates, corrections and
authorization remain governed by the accounting and background-work contracts.
These controls are project requirements, not claims that ISO alone specifies
the implementation.

## Required acceptance evidence

| Evidence identifier | Required result before a supported integration ships |
| --- | --- |
| STD-01 applicability review | Every message/practice in the slice has a sourced assessment and resolved required mappings. |
| STD-02 schema/profile fixtures | Valid examples pass; malformed, wrong-version and profile-invalid examples fail. |
| STD-03 semantic mapping fixtures | Currency, decimal precision, debit/credit perspective, dates, status and correction meaning survive mapping; prohibited loss fails. |
| STD-04 replay/correction fixtures | Duplicate input has one authorized effect; correction retains provenance and cannot rewrite posted books. |
| STD-05 compatibility review | Supported versions, code-list updates and any deviations have explicit evidence and review. |

These are planned evidence items, not existing tests. No runtime financial
messages or ISO conformance have been implemented on this research branch.

documents.title: Synthetic statement decoder
documents.body:
# Synthetic statement decoder

## Decision and boundary

Issue #73 implements only the pure Go decoding portion of
[the statement proposal](statement-import.md). Owner direction permits this
synthetic internal CSV starting point; broader #8 approval gates remain open.
This is not an ISO 20022 message or a bank adapter. Source rationale, syntax and
standards limits remain [SI01–SI06](../research/statement-import-sources.md).

## Exact API

`ingestion.Decode(io.Reader, Expectations) (Statement, error)` consumes at most
1 MiB + one sentinel byte. Expectations supplies an exact source account reference,
statement starts-on/ends-before dates and one currency snapshot: code, immutable
version ID, minor unit (0–9), valid-from and optional valid-to (exclusive).
Source account references match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}`. Currency version ID
is a lowercase hyphenated UUID and cannot be all zero. Both interval boundaries
must be valid, with starts-on strictly before ends-before; currency validity
has the same ordering rule. All dates are four-digit Gregorian full dates,
years 0001–9999. Invalid caller
expectations fail before reading. The caller owns reader deadlines/cancellation;
a byte limit cannot interrupt a blocking reader. The decoder validates equality, not authority;
callers remain responsible for approved metadata and binding permissions.

A successful Statement contains profile version, exact byte SHA-256 and byte count,
plus rows in original order. Each row retains its one-based physical record ordinal
(header is 1), seven decoded fields, original amount lexeme, canonical amount and
currency version ID. Canonical amount removes leading integer zeros and trailing
fractional zeros without rounding. No totals, classifications or functional
currency conversions are computed. No raw file is retained by the result.

Failure returns a zero Statement and `*DecodeError` with bounded Diagnostics
(code, record ordinal, field name), total error count and truncated flag. No raw
values, input reader errors or paths enter error strings. Record 0 means file or
expectation error. Structural failures stop immediately with one structural diagnostic (earlier
semantic diagnostics are discarded); semantic errors collect
at most 100 diagnostics while counting errors across the bounded file. An I/O
failure rejects all rows. No usable partial success is returned.

## Profile clarifications

Exact unquoted header bytes are required. Files contain 1–1000 data records;
header-only input is rejected. CRLF separates physical records; final CRLF is
optional. The 2048-byte physical record cap excludes CRLF and applies to header
and rows. Quoted commas and doubled quotes are accepted; embedded record breaks,
blank rows, BOM, controls and non-ASCII bytes are rejected. No trimming occurs.

Field bounds and account/date/sign/currency rules follow the statement proposal.
Amount limits count lexical digits (29 integer, 9 fractional), including zeros;
insignificant fractional zeros may exceed minor unit within the nine-digit cap.
Duplicate IDs reject even identical rows; different IDs preserve identical
purchases. One supplied currency version must cover each booking date; there is
no default, metadata lookup or cross-file duplicate handling.

## Implementation evidence and alternatives

Coordinator reviewed this API before implementation on 2026-10-13. The Go
[encoding/csv reference](https://pkg.go.dev/encoding/csv), Overview and Reader
fields, reviewed 2026-10-13, documents blank-line skipping, CRLF normalization
and multiline quoted fields. Local implementation uses the repository-pinned
Go 1.26.9 standard library. Our inference: prevalidate bytes and physical records,
then use its strict quoted-field parser per line. Using the reader alone would
accept inputs this profile prohibits; writing a second quoting parser would add
unnecessary ambiguity and maintenance. No external parser dependency is added.

## Acceptance

Named tests cover profile quoting, valid boundaries, 0/2/3-decimal exact money,
invalid caller expectations, invalid fields/dates/account, duplicate identity,
size/record/error bounds and I/O failure redaction. They use independent synthetic
expected values. Current evidence belongs to the
[living runbook](../runbooks/statement-decoder.md). No persistence, draft, API,
provider, SQL or posting behavior is implemented by this package.

documents.title: Synthetic statement-import contract
documents.body:
# Synthetic statement-import contract

## Decision and scope

**Proposed, not approved or implemented**, 2026-10-13; owner: project maintainer.
[Issue #61](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/61)
designs the first bounded slice of [#8](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/8).
Propose `jayburd-synthetic-statement-csv/1`: an internal fixture template for one
synthetic deposit account, producing uncategorized import drafts only. No real
statement uploads, card/liability accounts, balances/reconciliation completion,
pending items, provider calls, OCR, automatic journals, fees/FX splitting or
source corrections in this version. Foreign-currency deposit accounts are allowed;
this is not a USD-only importer. [Sources SI01–SI06](../research/statement-import-sources.md)
record review depth and alternatives.

## Standards applicability and approval gate

| Assessment | Profile/mapping and unresolved evidence |
| --- | --- |
| ISO 20022 applicable to eventual bank statement exchange | No bank, registered message version or usage profile is selected for production. This custom CSV is **not** an ISO financial message. Proposed deviation: allow only an internal synthetic ingestion fixture while camt artifact/profile review remains open in [#17](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/17). Owner approval of this restriction is required before implementation. No implied camt field-level mapping or conformance. |
| ISO 4217 applicable | Currency column maps to installed alphabetic code, valid booking date and immutable currency-version ID; source release must be retained. Fixtures explicitly select reviewed metadata. Currency lists do not authorize rates/rounding. |
| ISO 8601 date semantics applicable through RFC 3339 full-date subset | `booked_on` is a valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD date, not an instant. No locale guessing or UTC shift. Operational timestamps use RFC 3339 UTC. Full ISO normative text not reviewed. |
| ISO 21378/21926 audit semantics unresolved for exports | Retain provenance; no audit-export format or conformity claim. No IBAN/BIC/LEI fields are accepted, so their identifier standards do not govern our opaque synthetic reference. A real identifier adapter needs a separate review. |

STD-01/03/05 review evidence must resolve this proposed internal-template exception,
metadata snapshot and mappings below. STD-02/04 future fixtures cannot substitute
for that review. SI01 supports syntax; SI06 supports separating statements from books.

## Binding and exact field contract

Before upload, an authorized actor explicitly selects entity, book and **monetary
asset deposit** ledger account. A separately reviewed binding records stable
source-account UUID, synthetic source namespace, exact `source_account_ref`, selected
currency/version, target IDs, and binding revision. Never infer ownership from
filename, last four digits, amount, description or upload actor. Binding and current
read/import permissions are checked on preview, import, replay and retrieval.
The import permission and controlled binding operation are proposed extensions,
not existing grants. A source account cannot simultaneously bind to different
books; rebinding needs a future reviewed history/migration procedure, not a new
namespace to evade duplicates. No cross-entity discovery from duplicate errors.

CSV requires this exact header/order and seven fields per record:

```csv
source_account_ref,entry_id,booked_on,currency,direction,amount,description
SYNTH-CASH-01,P001,2026-01-05,USD,outflow,12.50,Paper shop
SYNTH-CASH-01,P002,2026-01-05,USD,outflow,12.50,Paper shop
SYNTH-CASH-01,D001,2026-01-06,USD,inflow,100.00,"Owner funding, synthetic"
```

These are original fictional examples. Actual fixture bytes use CRLF, optional
final CRLF, no BOM, and printable ASCII; quoted comma/escaped double quote allowed,
embedded line breaks/control bytes forbidden. No blanks, comments, extra headers,
columns or silent whitespace trimming. Header counts toward size but not row count.
`text/csv; charset=us-ascii; header=present` describes this narrow profile; `.csv`
and MIME alone are insufficient validation. Reject unsupported encodings rather
than replacing characters. Non-ASCII real descriptions require a new profile review.

| Field | Mapping and rejection boundary |
| --- | --- |
| source_account_ref | Exact binding match; 1–64 ASCII letters/digits/hyphen/underscore. One account per file. |
| entry_id | Stable source transaction ID, 1–64 of same characters. Identity survives overlapping exports. Missing IDs are rejected; do not synthesize IDs from row order or a content hash. Synthetic fixture authors maintain IDs across revisions. |
| booked_on | Actual valid date, within caller-declared statement interval `[starts_on, ends_before)`. Source-booked evidence only; accounting date is later explicit review. |
| currency | Three uppercase ISO letters, matches binding currency, unambiguous valid installed version on date. One currency per file; other bindings can use EUR/JPY/KWD. |
| direction | Exactly `inflow` or `outflow` from the account holder's deposit balance perspective. Suggested deposit-account leg: inflow debit, outflow credit. Neither determines an offset account, expense category or a posted journal. |
| amount | Positive unsigned decimal string matching `[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?`; up to 29 integer/9 fractional digits, significant fractional digits no finer than currency minor unit. No sign, exponent, grouping, zero, NaN or float conversion; excess precision fails without rounding. Preserve original lexeme; canonical equality strips leading/trailing insignificant zeros. |
| description | 1–500 printable ASCII characters; preserve exact decoded text, render escaped inert text. Never execute formulas/HTML or export to a spreadsheet in this slice. Description differences are material to replay equality. |

No functional amount/rate is invented. E.g. EUR `10.00` remains original EUR 10;
a later USD journal requires explicit reviewed valuation. JPY `125` and KWD
`1.005` are valid with 0/3-decimal metadata; JPY `1.1` and USD `12.501` fail.
The suggestion above applies only to asset deposits, not bank-side debit/credit
labels or liability accounts. Closed book periods do not destroy source evidence;
later posting independently applies period/account/FX policy.

## Durable identity and preview/import transitions

Request metadata includes binding revision, profile version, synthetic namespace,
statement reference (1–64 characters), interval, and a server-computed SHA-256 of
exact bytes. A scoped file occurrence records these plus server object ID and
upload actor/time; filename is display-only. Same exact file and metadata returns
its existing authorized occurrence. Same statement identity with changed content
is a visible revision conflict, never a silent replacement. Byte identity is not
row identity: line endings/quoting/reordering may produce different files.

The durable row uniqueness key is `(entity_id, stable_source_account_id, entry_id)`.
Keep decoded immutable fields and canonical exact amount for equality, plus original
file/record ordinals and lexemes. Hashes accelerate lookup; compare full canonical
fields, never accept hash-only equality. A row key with equal content links the new
file occurrence to the existing draft; changed content is a source-correction
conflict. Repeated entry IDs **within one file** reject the file even if equal.
Different IDs with identical date/description/amount remain distinct purchases.
Identity claims from this template are trusted only as synthetic input, not proof
that a bank issued IDs. A live adapter must establish stable ID semantics first.

1. `received → validating → preview_ready | rejected`: parse the entire bounded
   file; preview lists each new/existing row and all bounded errors. Preview writes
   no drafts, accounting facts or posted entries. The durable upload/validation
   record survives retries; repeated validation is deterministic for pinned versions.
2. Preparation itself requires current read/import permission and the same entity/
   book/account binding; caller-supplied actor IDs never grant authority. Explicit
   import confirmation prepares a recoverable operation naming immutable
   preview ID/revision, binding revision, profile and content identity. New operation
   types require review of [command recovery](command-recovery.md); existing setup/
   post endpoints do not already implement import. Discovery never executes it.
   Proposed replay scope is principal + import operation + idempotency key; compare
   the complete validated command identity. Changed identity under the same key
   conflicts, and a different actor cannot replay another actor's receipt.
3. Execution rechecks principal/grants/binding/reference versions and row identities
   in one transaction; create **all** new drafts, file-row links, receipt and audit,
   or none. Changed preview/dedup state returns conflict requiring refreshed preview
   and explicit confirmation. Do not silently skip a newly discovered conflict or
   commit a valid prefix. Receipt replay resolves before mutable preview validation,
   while current authorization still applies.
4. `imported` reports created/existing counts and stable draft IDs. Timeout/unknown
   commit recovers the same operation; acknowledgement never imports again. Cancel
   before import creates no drafts; a commit winning cancellation remains imported.
   Draft classification/splits and later explicit posting are separate operations;
   every split retains source-row linkage. No posted journal is mutated or auto-created.

No background worker is introduced by this contract. Parsing is bounded and must
not retain a database transaction during object access. If asynchronous validation
is selected under #8/#7, its operation/outbox intent, fences and receipt follow
[background work](background-work.md); the existing #7 dependency is not waived.
Concrete SQL, object-storage coordination, HTTP commands and worker ownership need
separate accepted contracts before implementation.

## Security, provenance and retention

Proposed hard limits: 1 MiB exact bytes, 1,000 data records, 2,048 bytes per physical
record, seven fields and limits above; at most 100 displayed errors plus a truncated
flag/total count when determinable. First structural failure may end parsing; never
claim unparsed rows valid. Stable error code, ordinal and field name only: no raw
financial values, filesystem paths, object URLs or another scope's identities in
logs/errors. No archives, remote URL fetching, macros or executable parsing. Exceeding
any bound rejects the file before draft writes; retries cannot expand limits.

Raw bytes use generated private object IDs outside public web assets, encrypted
storage and scoped retrieval; no public links, analytics payloads or browser
persistence. Preserve uploader/time, binding/format/parser/currency versions,
byte digest, record ordinals, original values, canonical values, immutable preview,
import operation/receipt and draft links. Object publication must complete before
preview availability; failure leaves no draft and a discoverable failed upload.
Orphan objects are privately quarantined and swept, never interpreted as imports.

Synthetic-only proposed retention: rejected/orphan bytes at most 24 hours;
unconfirmed previews/raw bytes seven days; imported raw bytes 30 days. Keep
normalized imported evidence, dedup keys and receipts for the synthetic dataset's
lifetime, even after raw deletion; clearly mark raw evidence unavailable. Deletion
cannot free an ID for accidental reimport. Explicit dataset purge retires its
namespace permanently and erases associated synthetic evidence; it is not selective
bookkeeping-history deletion. No tax/statutory retention duration is inferred.
Live retention, backup deletion, legal holds, owner/audience and incident handling
remain approval gates; raw expiry alone cannot authorize live records.

## Independent examples and future acceptance

All names below are **planned**, not implemented/passing tests. Expected outcomes
are hand-authored here, independent of parser/draft code. Each fixture verifies
that ledger journals/lines and `journal.posted` outbox intent do not change merely
from preview/import. Import-specific audit records, receipts, drafts and file-row
links change only as specified; those audit writes must not be mistaken for
accounting postings.

| Named future evidence | Required expected result |
| --- | --- |
| `TestStatementProfile` | Exact three-row example creates preview with three new rows; quoted comma preserved. Invalid header/encoding/date/sign/scale and missing entry ID reject, zero drafts. |
| `TestStatementBinding` | Allowed binding succeeds; mixed accounts, foreign entity, missing/revoked grant, disabled/deleted principal and changed binding fail without revealing source content. |
| `TestStatementMoney` | Example total USD inflow100/outflow25, net increase75; both 12.50 purchases remain separate. EUR10 preserved without USD rate; JPY/KWD cases above exact. Totals never combine currencies. |
| `TestStatementReplay` | First confirmed import creates3 drafts; identical replay creates0 additional; reserialized same IDs in a new statement creates0 and3 links. Overlap P002 plus new P003 creates1 and links1. Same P001 changed12.51 conflicts; no silent edit. |
| `TestStatementAtomicity` | Valid rows1/3 with invalid row2 create0 drafts; injected failure after each draft/link/audit/receipt write rolls all back. Retry creates exactly3. Two concurrent equal imports have at most3 total drafts. |
| `TestStatementPreviewRace` | Membership revocation, changed binding/reference metadata or concurrent dedup change between preview and execution prevents stale new work; authorized known receipt replay has no additional effects. |
| `TestStatementRecovery` | Lost commit response recovers same draft IDs; cancel/import race has one terminal outcome; lost acknowledgement cannot create a second import. |
| `TestStatementBoundsAndRetention` | Each limit+1 rejects; diagnostics redact contents; text is inert; private retrieval denies wrong scope; raw expiry retains dedup identity, preview expiry blocks first execution, dataset purge prevents namespace reuse. |

## Handoff and blockers

Owner must accept/revise the internal CSV exception, binding and stable source-ID
requirements, permission, limits and synthetic retention. #17 remains a real camt
integration blocker, not a prerequisite proof magically supplied by this CSV.
#8 needs reviewed draft/provenance SQL and API/recovery contracts, storage consistency
and cleanup design, applicable #7 behavior, then these fixtures. This contract
neither closes #8 nor authorizes live data. Review evidence and actual checks are
in the [living runbook](../runbooks/statement-import.md).

documents.title: Verifier IAM authentication compatibility
documents.body:
# Verifier IAM authentication compatibility

Issue272, owner-directed implementation2026-10-23; proposed sensitive-source
review before migration/application. Migration30 remains immutable.

## Evidence and decision

Read-only hosted role metadata showed the verifier login and NOLOGIN capability
