have safe attributes and the operator can SET bookkeeping_owner. The login's only
membership is cloudsqliamserviceaccount, ADMIN false, INHERIT true, SET true.
The blanket SET-membership rejection therefore prevents bootstrap before grants.
No financial records were read and no authority persisted from the rejection.

Selected official sections reviewed2026-10-23:

- [Google Cloud SQL users, System users and roles](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/users#cloud_sql_system_users_and_roles):
  cloudsqliamserviceaccount designates IAM service-account authentication;
  system roles cannot be modified/deleted or assigned by customers (except the
  documented cloudsqlsuperuser assignment). Vendor implementation guidance,
  not an accounting standard; actual instance metadata separately establishes
  this membership's options.
- [PostgreSQL17 SET ROLE, Description and Notes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-set-role.html):
  SET membership permits assuming the target role; INHERIT grants its effective
  privileges without switching. Selected sections, not the entire manual.

Decision: allow SET only for the exact login-to-cloudsqliamserviceaccount edge,
ADMIN false and INHERIT true, with a safe NOLOGIN marker having no parent-role
memberships. Every other SET/ADMIN edge remains rejected, including capability
memberships and alternate grantors. The existing effective database/schema/
table/column/sequence/function checks still cover the marker through inheritance.
Marker ownership and unsafe attributes must not open an authority path. Explicit
SET marker execution still cannot invoke verification: existing entrypoints
require the original session identity and role NONE. No marker role is created,
modified or granted by bootstrap; local synthetic tests supply the simulation.

Alternative: alter/remove Google's marker membership. Rejected because it changes
managed authentication and conflicts with the documented system-role boundary.
Alternative: allow all cloudsql roles or all SET edges. Rejected: broadens authority.
Inference: this narrowly inspected marker is compatible with restricted execution;
its name alone is insufficient. Unexpected privileges or role topology still fail.

## Standards and acceptance

This is internal database authorization, with no financial message/data mapping.
ISO20022/4217 and ISO21378 mappings are unchanged by this slice; no applicable
financial message identifier is invented. Existing verifier financial semantics
and multicurrency requirements remain unchanged; no ISO conformance claim.

Forward migration31 replaces only integration.verifier_login; signature,
ownership and existing EXECUTE ACL remain intact. Down restores the previous
predicate; live down-migration is not an approved rollout. Bootstrap mirrors the
narrow preliminary exception and retains the complete final predicate check.

Acceptance: migration-test, ledger-test, sandbox-verification-test and
verifier-bootstrap-test on disposable PostgreSQL17; safe marker bootstrap/replay
and actual login succeed, while marker ADMIN, NOINHERIT, unsafe attributes,
parent roles, effective financial/column/function authority, unrelated SET edges,
and direct capability SET remain denied. SET marker does not authorize comparison.
Core check/test/build plus exact-head CI remain required. Human security review,
trusted rebuilt migration image, approved finite release and hosted retry are
separate gates; no hosted PASS or mandate follows from source tests.

documents.title: Owner-operated Sandbox webhook bootstrap
documents.body:
# Owner-operated Sandbox webhook bootstrap

## Decision and scope

Issue #271 preparation; coordinator approved this operational profile2026-10-22.
Reuse migration14's existing `bookkeeping_webhook` capability and
`integration.set_webhook_ingress`; no product DDL, rewritten migration or startup
migration. SQL role wiring and ingress enrollment are one serializable transaction.
Cloud IAM/user provisioning is a separate reviewed infrastructure operation.
Neither this contract nor the wrapper authorizes cloud execution or source consent.

`db/bootstrap/webhook-login.sql` is executed by an owner-authorized SQL operator
with existing CREATEROLE/ADMIN authority over the target/capability, database grant
rights and SET permission on `bookkeeping_owner`. It checks session=current user
before the explicit owner switch. The runtime never receives those capabilities.
No email/caller actor substitutes for authenticated SQL identity.

## Explicit interface and authority

`scripts/bootstrap-webhook.sh` has no default operation. `--check` validates metadata
only; `--apply` requires a separately owner-created authenticated local Unix socket.
Both require explicit `--project`, `--operator-user`, `--socket-dir`,
`--operation-key`, `--enabled`. Only project `jayburd-bookkeeping-dev` is supported;
SQL derives `jayburd-dev-webhook@jayburd-bookkeeping-dev.iam` and independently
requires database `bookkeeping`. There is no runtime-login override, DSN, password,
secret version, cloud CLI invocation, IAM token lookup or provider call. The operator
login is a connection identity, not an application actor. Socket setup and operator
authentication remain owner operations under the existing Cloud SQL procedure.

The wrapper clears inherited libpq configuration, uses `psql -X -w`, fixed port5432,
explicit database/login/socket, rejects host-list commas, five-second connection timeout and no password or
service file. It suppresses SQL/results/server diagnostics and emits only a fixed
success or failure. Metadata check is not authentication or permission evidence.

Before grants, SQL rejects unsafe LOGIN/capability attributes, owner/API/sync/other
bookkeeping, predefined `pg_*` and privileged transitive memberships, ADMIN or SET options from any
grantor, database CREATE/TEMP, schema CREATE, product table/sequence privileges,
and unintended function EXECUTE. The closed permitted inherited functions are
`integration.accept_verified_webhook(text,text,text)` and, after migration32,
`integration.accept_verified_link_session(text,text,text)`. The latter stores
owned signed session receipts only; no API identity, claim, bank secret or wakeup
authority is added. The API/ledger cross-role guard remains unchanged. Direct product function
ACLs and schema/database delegation options are rejected, even for the intended
function. Existing normal USAGE on the integration schema through the capability
is expected. Unknown extra roles with no elevated/app privilege are not represented
as approved application capabilities; actual Cloud SQL IAM role compatibility
remains a hosted acceptance gate.

Then grant only `bookkeeping_webhook` with INHERIT TRUE, ADMIN FALSE, SET FALSE;
CONNECT; search_path `pg_catalog`; connection cap4. This supports at most one old
and one new revision, each max1 instance × two pooled connections. Cap4 alone
does not enforce Cloud Run instance policy. No privilege is silently revoked to
make an unsafe account appear valid. Unexpected privilege causes atomic failure.
SQL uses statement10s/lock2s/idle-in-transaction15s limits; no automatic retry.

## Ingress enrollment, replay and revocation

After role validation/grants, `SET LOCAL ROLE bookkeeping_owner` invokes only:
`integration.set_webhook_ingress(actual_login,'sandbox',stable_key,enabled)`.
The function's durable key is `(session_user,idempotency_key)` and its normalized
body includes login, environment and enabled. Exact same-key replay returns its
existing receipt without incrementing ingress revision. Changing enabled with the
same key raises P2802 and rolls the entire bootstrap transaction back.

Therefore disable uses a **new stable operation key**, for example `release-271-disable-1`;
retry that exact disable with the same key until known. A later enable uses another
new key. A post-call owner check confirms the current exact login/enabled state; replaying an older enable after a later disable fails without re-enabling. Owner identity changes also change the receipt key, so the same textual
key through another operator is not an exact replay. Operators retain operation
identity and inspect only approved redacted outcomes. An uncertain COMMIT is not a
successful bootstrap; owner may replay identical inputs, never invent a new key to
resolve uncertainty. The wrapper does not retry automatically.

Disabling ingress revokes acceptance through the existing SQL mandate, leaving
role wiring and immutable historical receipts intact. It does not delete provider
Items, revoke source consent or change private API/workers. It requires the login
to remain safe; preexisting unsafe authority blocks bootstrap and needs a separately
reviewed owner repair, rather than executing a mixed-capability operation. For emergency acceptance stop,
an independently authorized operator can use the existing serializable owner
`integration.set_webhook_ingress(actual_login,'sandbox',NEW_STABLE_DISABLE_KEY,false)`
boundary directly: its disabled branch does not require the runtime login to pass
its enabled-role check. This is a separately scoped owner operation, not a wrapper
fallback. It does not repair unsafe grants; quarantine and repair remain separate.
No live emergency operation is authorized or executed by this preparation.

## Sources, standards and alternatives

Reviewed2026-10-22, selected full relevant PostgreSQL17 sections:
[GRANT](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-grant.html), role membership
INHERIT/SET/ADMIN and grantor-specific grants;
[ALTER ROLE](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-alterrole.html), connection
limits, role configuration and CREATEROLE/ADMIN constraints;
[psql](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/app-psql.html), -X/-w, variables and
connection parameters; [Predefined roles](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/predefined-roles.html),
Table21.1 and the following file/program-access paragraph. These predefined roles
can grant powerful file/program/data access without SUPERUSER or BYPASSRLS;
attribute checks alone do not establish safety. The bootstrap rejects their
transitive membership. The synthetic negative fixture grants
`pg_execute_server_program` and checks rejection without executing a server
program, file read or COPY operation. Inspected migration14's actual key/body/revision behavior,
`db/bootstrap/worker-logins.sql`, [Cloud SQL](cloud-sql.md) and
[managed webhook runtime](webhook-managed-runtime.md). Public manuals establish
mechanisms; project choice is fixed development metadata, fail-closed ACL checks,
bounded budgets and atomic enrollment. No hosted administrator compatibility was
established by public documentation or synthetic superuser setup.

This is internal operational provisioning, not an ISO20022 financial message or
an audit-data export. Existing proprietary notification and ISO4217/date mapping
remain unchanged; no amount, currency or accounting semantics are introduced.
No ISO conformance claim. The sources do not approve public exposure or live use.

Alternative: reuse worker bootstrap and borrow sync authority. Rejected because
webhook runtime forbids mixed capabilities. Alternative: startup auto-enrollment
or implicit psql environment. Rejected because it couples runtime to owner grants
or selects an unreviewed database. An explicit standalone owner command adds an
operator step but preserves the existing bootstrap/runtime boundary.

## Acceptance and limits

`bash scripts/test-webhook-bootstrap.sh` uses pinned PostgreSQL17/migrate images,
private disposable network and fictional roles. It proves exact replay/revocation,
actual login inheritance, SET/DDL/table/owner-function denial, unsafe role/direct
ACL/grant-option rejection, unchanged mandate after rejection and inert metadata
validation. Fixed SQLSTATE42501 catches forbidden operations; connection failures
are not accepted as permission proof. Existing migration/ledger permission gates
remain required. Production, actual Cloud SQL owner authority and hosted ingress
qualification remain open; tests do not renew expired source consent.

documents.title: Sandbox webhook enrollment
documents.body:
# Sandbox webhook enrollment

## Decision and scope

Engineering profile for #271, coordinator reviewed 2026-10-22 under the owner's
implementation-only swarm authorization. No provider/cloud execution, deployment,
public exposure, credentials, consent renewal or Production activation.

`connections.HTTPConfig.WebhookURL` is optional and defaults empty. Empty keeps
the existing new-Link request unchanged, including omission of the `webhook`
field. A nonempty value must exactly equal `SandboxTransactionsWebhookURL`:

`https://jayburd-dev-webhook-9088794002.us-central1.run.app/webhooks/plaid`

This public canonical endpoint identifies only the dedicated development
Transactions receiver. Constructor validation rejects every other spelling,
scheme, project, host, port, path, userinfo, query or fragment before constructing
the provider. No request body, user choice, environment discovery or provider
response selects a receiver. Changing the approved endpoint requires source
review and a release-policy update, not a permissive URL parser.

For `Mode=new`, the fixed Sandbox `/link/token/create` request adds the reviewed
`webhook` value only when explicitly configured. It retains Transactions only,
US/English, Hosted Link, exact API version 2020-09-14, bounded no-retry transport
and the existing encrypted handoff/one-shot exchange rules. Reconnect remains
unqualified and disabled. Startup performs no provider call or Item mutation.
The API exposes optional `-plaid-webhook-url` and `connectionruntime.Config`
threads it to the provider. Before I/O, a nonempty value additionally requires
ProjectID `jayburd-bookkeeping-dev` and ProjectNumber `9088794002`. Disabled
composition still requires an entirely zero configuration, so a receiver flag
alone never enables enrollment. The coordinator owns release metadata and
infrastructure propagation; adding these fields changes no running deployment.

## Sources, alternatives and standards

[WE01–WE03](../research/webhook-enrollment-sources.md) records selected current
official sections and access limits. Plaid accepts `webhook` during new Link
creation; update-mode Link creation does not change an existing Item's webhook.
Initial sync activates `SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE` delivery. Therefore opt-in
enrollment metadata is necessary configuration, not signed-chain evidence.

Alternative arbitrary HTTPS configuration is rejected: malformed or substituted
recipients could receive provider account notifications. Alternative enabling
the URL by default is rejected: public receiver/IAM readiness and owner scope
must precede activation. Exact optional configuration preserves old deployments.
Alternative treating an update acknowledgement as success is rejected: the
acknowledgement is a different Item event, without receipt-to-publication proof.

STD-01 applicability: this adds an operational destination to proprietary Plaid
Link JSON, not an ISO 20022 financial exchange. Mapping is internal reviewed URL
→ `/link/token/create.webhook`; there are no amounts, currencies, dates or
journal mutations. Existing ISO 4217/source-accounting mappings are unchanged.
No ISO conformance, privacy-policy or live-use approval is claimed. A registered
ISO financial message does not substitute for this provider-specific bootstrap.

## Existing Items — proposed, not implemented

Plaid requires `/item/webhook/update` with the existing access token; Link update
mode cannot perform this change. Do not add an unguarded method, route, token
CLI argument or provider allowlist entry. Required reviewed design:

1. An authenticated actor/entity/book command names one known Item, its expected
   generation, complete affected approved stream set, exact reviewed target and
   finite owner-authorized Sandbox interval. An Item may back multiple streams;
   account-level permission alone is not Item-wide mutation authority.
2. Current SQL authority and consent must be rechecked before any provider I/O.
   A deterministic durable operation and claim resolve concurrent requests and
   lost replies. The current schema has no approved webhook-update command;
   review a new SQL/API boundary rather than repurposing rotate/remove/reconnect.
3. A scoped credential resolver reads the immutable current vault reference and
   decrypts only in process. Match exact credential version/Item/generation;
   neither agents nor operator flags retrieve access tokens. No extra vault/KMS
   access is granted to the inbound webhook host.
4. The adapter uses the fixed Sandbox endpoint, fixed URL, bounded one-attempt
   transport and redacted errors. Validate the returned Item identity and URL.
   An ambiguous response remains uncertain; inspect authoritative Item webhook
   metadata under the same scope before deciding whether another action is safe.
   Never blindly retry a mutation or broaden a single Item into an enumeration.
5. Provider `ITEM/WEBHOOK_UPDATE_ACKNOWLEDGED` goes to the new receiver. The
   current verifier/handler accepts only Transactions notifications and must
   continue rejecting it. Do not call an HTTP acknowledgement, provider response
   or this Item event W01/W02 success. Supporting Item events needs its own
   reviewed profile; no silent broadening of this receiver.
6. Actual acceptance must traverse first sync/signed
   `SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE` → durable receipt/wakeup → publisher/task/worker →
   correctly scoped source publication. Add duplicate/retry/missed-event cases,
   independent exact/no-journal evidence and cleanup/rollback procedures.

The proposal cannot run with expired consent. Existing Item activation remains
blocked until these authority, migration/API, release and owner-scope decisions
are reviewed separately.

## Validation and remaining evidence

`TestWebhookEnrollmentOptIn`: empty configuration omits the wire field; explicit
configuration emits the exact independently written destination; constructor is
inert, new enrollment retains Transactions-only scope and performs one request.
`TestWebhookEnrollmentRejectsDestinationSubstitution`: hostile/lookalike hosts,
scheme/project/service/path substitutions, userinfo, port, query, fragment,
case/whitespace variants fail before transport and reveal fixed errors only.
`TestWebhookConfigurationScope` rejects disabled, foreign-project and substituted
configuration before SQL, token minting or secret reads. `TestWebhookOptInStartup`
proves valid composition reads only the two existing exact static versions; no
provider/SQL/enrollment operation occurs at startup.

Run existing `internal/connections` race tests and `make check test build`.
No SQL or browser/API contract changes in this slice. Root integration must test
optional configuration/release propagation separately. Hosted W01–W05/W07 remain
open until exact-image deployment and actual signed delivery are observed under
fresh explicit scope. Merely configuring this URL is not qualification.

documents.body:
# Dedicated Sandbox webhook runtime

## Decision and boundary

Engineering composition for #103/#87 under owner-authorized #88 swarm, reviewed
by the coordinator 2026-10-22. Extends the existing
[verified ingress](provider-webhooks.md) and [hosted identity](hosted-workers.md)
profile to a separate executable host. No new financial service, database,
business authority or webhook type. Human security review and exact release
authorization are required before new internet exposure or IAM grants; neither
is supplied by this document. Repository Infisical/GCP instructions govern over
the security skill's generic Azure examples.

The host runs only the existing exact `/webhooks/plaid` handler. It never mounts
bookkeeping, setup, posting, debug or credential routes. It accepts only the
reviewed Sandbox Transactions notification. Item events, Hosted completion
webhooks and Production need their own explicit profiles; this host does not
pretend to implement them. No migration or enrollment runs at startup.

## Composition and capabilities

- Cloud SQL component `webhook` derives only
  `jayburd-dev-webhook@PROJECT.iam`, bookkeeping database, us-central1, existing
  metadata-only IAM connector; pool maximum2/minimum0, no raw TCP/ADC/DSN or
  API/sync/owner identity substitution. This is constructor support, not a grant.
- Operator provisions the dedicated Cloud SQL IAM user and only existing
  `bookkeeping_webhook` inherited capability, without ADMIN/SET or direct table
  privileges. The existing SQLReceiver verifies that restricted authority on
  each call before invoking `integration.accept_verified_webhook`.
- Credentials come from existing runtime-managed exact numeric secret versions,
  fixed `jayburd-dev-bank-sync-client-id` and `jayburd-dev-bank-sync-client-secret`
  resources in the explicit numeric project. No arbitrary secret path, aliases,
  environment plaintext or agent retrieval. Infisical remains the secret owner.
- Reuse existing bounded metadata token source, CRC32C reader, fixed Sandbox
  key endpoint, verifier and SQLReceiver. Key cache misses resolve credentials
  only in memory. Request-controlled key identifiers never select secret paths.
- Configuration validates before database/secret/provider access. Startup checks
  database transport only; per-call SQLReceiver inspection remains authority.
  No bank acquisition or queue call.
  Durable wakeups are consumed by the already separate publisher/worker.
- Cleanup drains requests, closes the SQL pool/connector and idle HTTP connections
  once. Cancellation or ambiguous SQL commit never acknowledges success early.

Future deployment must pin a trusted image, exact SQL/secret-version/identity
metadata and unchanged private API IAM; separately review public invocation of
this one host and enrollment webhook URL. Default local/CI commands stay offline
and use only synthetic keys and disposable databases.

The existing worker image packages `/webhook` alongside its other explicit
executables. Default entrypoint stays `/worker`; a separately reviewed webhook
service must explicitly select `/webhook`. Reuse the trusted worker-image build,
scan/SBOM and immutable candidate receipt without inventing a fifth unreviewed
image promotion channel. Offline exact-image startup proof covers invalid webhook
configuration and proves no network/default enrollment behavior.

## Standards, sources and alternatives

This is an internal operational capability and proprietary Plaid notification,
not an ISO20022 financial message. No amount/currency mapping or accounting rule
changes; existing ISO4217/source decoder profile remains authoritative. No ISO
conformance claim. Source applicability: selected current official sections in
[P88-18–P88-20](../research/plaid-88-test-sources.md); existing P88-14/15 cover
signature, body hash, age and response constraints. Full ISO text not reviewed.

Alternative: mount on the application API or borrow sync credentials. Rejected:
it widens routing/credential authority and cannot pass SQLReceiver role checks.
Alternative: remain injected-only. Safe for synthetic host proof, but cannot
receive real delivery; accepted only as an intermediate stage, not W01 clearance.

## Threat review and acceptance

| Threat / initial risk | Mitigation and required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Spoofing/tampering/replay, high | Existing ES256/raw-body/age/key validation and durable replay receipt; negative signatures never reach SQL; W06/W07. |
| Privilege escalation, high | Dedicated derived login, SQLReceiver role inspection, no direct table authority/private routes; constructor and SQL role tests. |
| Credential/data disclosure, high | Fixed resources, no logging/reflection/persistence; synthetic redaction tests and reviewed runtime identity policy. |
| Resource exhaustion, high | Header/body/socket/context/admission bounds, small pool/key-cache budgets and Cloud Run instance cap; real-socket host tests and hosted retry/load evidence. |
| Lost/duplicate work, high | Receipt+wakeup atomicity before acknowledgement, uncertain commit retry, existing generation fences and catch-up; SQL receipt/dispatch and W02–W05. |

Residual hosted risk remains until dedicated IAM/SQL provisioning, routing,
trusted image, actual signed chain and bounded overload/recovery tests are
reviewed. Loopback or Terraform mocks do not qualify cloud identity/delivery.
Root constructor acceptance: `TestConnectorConfiguration` verifies derived
webhook identity, pool bounds and no raw fallback; invalid role aliases fail.
Host/managed acceptance must additionally prove inert constructors, fixed secret
configuration, route isolation and fixed/redacted errors without real credentials.

documents.title: Isolated webhook infrastructure and release boundary
documents.body:
# Isolated webhook infrastructure and release boundary

## Decision, owner and scope

#271 engineering preparation, coordinator-reviewed2026-10-22 under
`PLAID-271-PREP-20261022T1725Z`; implementation and synthetic tests only. Extends
[managed runtime](webhook-managed-runtime.md) with separate bootstrap/runtime roots.
No cloud apply, provider call, secret access, source consent renewal or public
exposure is authorized by merging this contract. Human/security review remains
required under the applied Citizen Developer security skill. Repository
Infisical/GCP authority governs over generic enterprise Azure examples.

## Ownership and inert defaults

`infra/gcp/webhook-bootstrap` owns only `jayburd-dev-webhook` service account,
Cloud SQL client/login project bindings, a `CLOUD_IAM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` user on
existing instance `jayburd-dev`, two static secret-level reader bindings, and the
optional Invoker binding on the fixed `jayburd-dev-webhook` service. It creates
no secret/value/version, database, bucket, scheduler, queue, KMS, WIF, deployer
capability or private API/worker resource. `enabled=false` creates no resources.
`public_invocation_approved=false` is independent: identity preparation does not
expose ingress. The public binding requires explicit enabled+approval and an
already-existing service. It retains IAM invocation checks and grants allUsers
only on that service. Organization policy failure is a stop, never an automatic
IAM-check bypass or private-API exposure.

`infra/gcp/webhook-runtime` owns exactly one fixed service when `runtime` is
non-null; default null creates no service. Inputs are explicit project ID/number,
reviewed regionus-central1 and runtime `{image,client_id_version,client_secret_version}`.
The image must be that project's `jayburd-dev/worker@sha256:<64 lowercase hex>`;
versions and project number are canonical positive signed64 decimal identifiers,
never aliases. No arbitrary identity, service name, executable, secret path,
provider URL, environment value or volume is configurable. Runtime owns no IAM.

Owner-created backend buckets must be distinct: `PROJECT-jayburd-dev-webhook-bootstrap-state`
(prefix `webhook-bootstrap`) and `PROJECT-jayburd-dev-webhook-runtime-state`
(prefix `webhook-runtime`). Backend examples are not loaded by tests. Existing
application/workers/worker-runtime state and `deploy-workers` manifest remain
unchanged. Existing SQL is immutable; root coordinates separate owner bootstrap
proof, release tooling and shared source/index integration.

## Exact service profile

Service `jayburd-dev-webhook` selects command `/webhook` from the reviewed worker
digest and passes exactly five public arguments: listen0.0.0.0:8080, explicit
Cloud SQL instance, numeric project, and full fixed-name numeric client-ID and
client-secret version resources. It uses only the dedicated webhook identity.
No secret values or bank-token slot reads are injected. Secret IAM grants cover
only `jayburd-dev-bank-sync-client-id` and `jayburd-dev-bank-sync-client-secret`;
version pinning is enforced by configuration, not claimed as version-level IAM.

Targets: request timeout10s, concurrency16, service/revision max1 instance/min0,
1CPU/512Mi, idle CPU enabled, startup boost disabled, bounded TCP startup probe
on8080, deletion protection and single100% latest traffic. TCP startup proves
listener availability, not signature verification or SQL authority. The Go pool
maximum is2; planned old/new revision overlap needs up to4 SQL connections.
Scaling settings are requested capacity policy, not an absolute billing/load
ceiling. Hosted latency/retries/cold starts still need measurement.

Reviewed Sandbox enrollment constant is
`https://jayburd-dev-webhook-9088794002.us-central1.run.app/webhooks/plaid` for
`jayburd-bookkeeping-dev`; the generic Terraform root computes the corresponding
project-number URL for isolated synthetic tests. Exact release orchestration must
bind the approved project/number and confirm observed URL/revision/configuration
before enrollment. No deploy-by-tag, source rebuild between stages or automatic
fallback to old worker command is accepted.

## Operator sequence and revocation

1. Review source, trusted same-source worker build/exact-image tests/SBOM/scans,
   finite Sandbox Item/book scope, current consent, exact secret versions and
   security approval. Expired releases/consent are not renewed implicitly.
2. Owner explicitly bootstraps identity/Cloud SQL IAM user/two secret reads with
   public approvalfalse. Existing SQL IAM authentication/secret containers must
   already exist. No provider tokens are retrieved by an agent.
3. Separately reviewed owner SQL bootstrap grants only `bookkeeping_webhook`
   with INHERIT true, ADMIN/SET false, database CONNECT, search_pathpg_catalog and
   bounded connections; reject privileged/mixed/direct-table authority. Owner
   binds/enables actual login using existing `integration.set_webhook_ingress`
   in a serializable owner transaction with stable idempotency key. IAM login
   creation and successful transport Ping are insufficient authority evidence.
4. Owner-operated guarded runtime release validates exact approved metadata,
   applies only dedicated runtime state, then confirms Ready/generation, image,
   command, exact args, identity, traffic, URL and private IAM unchanged.
5. After independent public-exposure approval, bootstrap public flag grants
   invocation only to this service. Fixed unsigned rejection and private-route
   denial are transport checks, not W01 success.
6. Configure approved enrollment URL / scoped existing-Item webhook update through
   reviewed credential-owning adapters. Actual signed SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE must
   reach SQL receipt/wakeup and existing publisher/task/worker/source review.
   Update acknowledgement and fire_webhook response alone do not qualify it.

Rollback uses a previously qualified worker digest with identical webhook
configuration and identity; it must still contain `/webhook`. Root owns exact
release/readback/rollback tooling; existing worker receipt cannot be reused as
webhook deployment proof. To stop ingress, owner disables the SQL ingress binding
and removes the dedicated public grant with separately reviewed operations; do
not change private-service IAM or delete durable receipts. Current consent and
stream authority remain checked. `prevent_destroy` deliberately blocks toggling
bootstrap off/runtime null after creation as a destructive shortcut. Revocation,
retention and cleanup must preserve evidence; no automatic Item removal or consent
renewal occurs. New root deployment and W01–W05/W07 qualification remain open.

## Evidence, alternatives and threat review

[WR01–WR06](../research/webhook-release-sources.md) record authoritative sections,
review depth and access limits. Standards assessment: internal operational
infrastructure and existing proprietary notification; no financial message,
amount/currency/SQL contract or accounting policy changes. Existing ISO applicability
is unchanged; no ISO20022 designation or conformance claim.

Alternative of adding a third mode to private worker release was rejected because
its strict manifest and Scheduler-paused receipt govern different caller authority.
Two roots cost separate bootstrap/state ownership but avoid coupling public
invocation to private API/workers. Bootstrap public approval remains explicit;
merely attaching an evidence URL is not authorization.

| Threat / initial risk | Mitigation / remaining acceptance |
| --- | --- |
| Spoofing/tampering/replay, high | Existing ES256/body/hash/age and SQL receipt atomicity; real signed provider chain still required. |
| Privilege elevation, high | Fixed dedicated identity, two secret-level readers, no additional service capabilities; SQL actual-session checks and owner bootstrap proof. |
| Disclosure, high | No Terraform secret values, secret creation, env/mount injection or provider payloads; exact pinned paths and redacted evidence. |
| Resource exhaustion, high | Fixed request/compute/concurrency/scaling targets, Go socket/admission/key/pool bounds; real timing/overload and cost monitoring still open. |
| Repudiation/lost work, medium/high | Trusted candidate and exact readback receipt, durable notification/wakeup, separate redacted operational audit; hosted retry/catch-up proof pending. |

Mocked tests name `default_is_inert`, `dedicated_identity_and_two_static_reads`,
`public_approval_is_one_fixed_service`, `isolated_route_identity_and_budget`, and
negative project/region/image/version scenarios. They prove requested configuration,
not effective inherited IAM, a created resource, transport, delivery or posting safety.

documents.title: Existing webhook updater
documents.body:
# Existing webhook updater

## Decision and owner boundary

#271 wave2, coordinator-reviewed2026-10-22 under lease
`PLAID-88-WAVE2-20261022T1930Z`. Implements the missing executable updater after
merged preparation in PR273. No actual federation, deployment, provider operation,
source-consent renewal or new enabled release manifest is authorized here.

First creation remains owner-operated: dedicated bootstrap identity/SQL login,
restricted SQL grants and mandate, first **private** runtime creation in the fixed
isolated backend, separate security/public-Invoker approval and effective identity
review. Only then may owner prepare updater federation and a fresh exact release.
This avoids giving the routine updater create/delete/IAM/bootstrap authority.
Existing deploy-workers, private application IAM, workers and Scheduler are untouched.

## New owner bootstrap capability

`infra/gcp/webhook-delivery` defaults `enabled=false` and creates nothing.
With explicit owner review it creates a separate `jayburd-dev-webhook-deployer`,
custom roles and narrowly bound permissions. Separate `federation_active=false`
disables the pool/provider while preserving protected identity/grants. Activation
requires enabled resources and an exact reviewed40-hex `workflow_sha`. Owner must
review and update the pin for each new main workflow commit; dispatch inputs do
not select cloud trust. Invalid contradictory activation is rejected.

The pool/provider bind the canonical numeric repository/owner/actor IDs,
workflow_dispatch, refs/heads/main, exact deploy-webhook workflow_ref and SHA.
The workflow also checks triggering actor, latest main and tracked manifest bytes.
Short-lived tokens are minted only by the explicit pinned auth step; there are no
credential files or service-account keys. Disabling federation stops future
exchanges, **not already issued tokens**. Those expire separately; emergency
runtime/SQL mandate/public-binding controls remain owner operations.

Capabilities:

- Exact service `jayburd-dev-webhook`: get, update, getIamPolicy only. No service
  creation/deletion, setIamPolicy, public binding change, role administration,
  secret access/write, SQL grant, source fetch or worker/Scheduler capability.
- Project read-only `run.operations.get` for provider polling and `iam.roles.get`
  for actual custom-role definition verification. These are broader metadata reads,
  not project-wide service mutation.
- ActAs only the dedicated webhook runtime service account.
- ObjectAdmin only the existing `PROJECT-jayburd-dev-webhook-runtime-state` bucket;
  no bootstrap/delivery/application/worker state bucket. Backend must be owner-created
  and handed off explicitly. Tooling never reads state or plan contents; Terraform
  privately creates/applies its opaque plan using the existing approved pattern.
- Artifact Registry reader only on existing `jayburd-dev` repository, required for
  image deployment. This is read access to that repository's images, not image-path
  IAM or registry writes.

Owner-only backend for this bootstrap is
`PROJECT-jayburd-dev-webhook-delivery-state`, prefix `webhook-delivery`. The updater
has no access to it. No backend, public service or IAM grant is applied by tests.

## Executable release

The new `deploy-webhook.yml` workflow has only workflow_dispatch. Missing
`deploy/webhook-release.json` or invalid hash fails before authentication. No
fresh authorization dates or scope have been invented in a committed example.

Before explicit WIF authentication, it validates exact manifest SHA256/expiry and
fixed Sandbox project, downloads the exact trusted successful owner/main worker
run/attempt artifact, verifies tracked manifest bytes and current HEAD/main, and
checks immutable PR270/273 ancestry. Binary inputs in Dockerfile.worker, go.mod,
go.sum, internal and the four compiled command directories must match the trusted
build source even when release tooling/docs changed afterward. Tests run before
cloud authentication. Candidate-only receipt is not deployment permission.

`scripts/deploy-webhook.sh` rederives the runtime variables from approved tracked
bytes, requires explicit injected tokens and verifies an existing, reconciled,
correctly configured public webhook service before touching only the fixed runtime
root/backend. It prepares/applies the opaque private plan. Immediately before
apply it rechecks actual latest main, provenance and authorization expiry. It
cannot inspect/import/repair state: owner evidence must attest the first private
creation and isolated state handoff. Missing/wrong state must fail through narrow
IAM/protected resource semantics; there is no broad permission fallback.

The collector calls only fixed v2 Service GET, service getIamPolicy and the fixed
custom-role GET, with explicit WIF token held in process memory. No token is placed
in argv, files or logs; no ADC/token discovery occurs. HTTPS reads have10s timeout,
128KiB maximum and no redirects. Server-side field mask excludes raw environment
values. Raw selected responses remain in memory and are rejected without logging;
only strict validated public receipt is written. Preflight permits an old valid
worker image/version policy but requires current fixed identity, routing and bounds.
Post-apply receipt requires the exact newly approved image/versions/configuration.

Public service policy permits the existing sole allUsers Invoker plus optionally
one **exact** updater binding to the fixed deployer. The optional role must also
be read from actual IAM: fixed name, GA, not deleted, exactly get/update/getIamPolicy.
No role-name-only trust or extra conditional/public/admin binding is accepted.
Direct service policy does not establish absence of inherited broad IAM; owner
identity evidence must independently verify that before enabling federation.

Only the public receipt artifact is retained. Provider diagnostics, raw metadata,
opaque plans and state are never uploaded or inspected. Any failure stops; partial
apply is possible and needs owner review. No automatic rollback, paid refresh,
Item mutation or posting occurs. A successful receipt remains control-plane
configuration evidence, not actual signed receipt→wakeup→worker publication,
financial equality, zero-journal proof or Production approval.

## Cleanup and rollback

Before qualification end, the named owner disables the scoped SQL ingress mandate
with a new stable key and removes the dedicated public binding through its original
bootstrap, preserving receipts. Owner deactivates updater federation while keeping
enabled identity/grants; existing short-lived token expiry is a separate bound.
Do not toggle protected resource enabled flags/runtime null to simulate rollback.
A compatible rollback uses a newly reviewed finite forward manifest selecting a
retained trusted compatible worker digest, exact evidence and readback again.
Authorization dates do not stop Cloud Run or renew source consent automatically.

## Evidence and security review

[WU01–WU07](../research/webhook-rollout-sources.md) distinguish platform facts from
project choices and actual hosted gaps. Alternative of automatically creating a
public host was rejected because it requires broader IAM and mixes first bootstrap
with routine promotion. Alternative of accepting a role name without its definition
was rejected because an administrator could widen that role after initial setup.

| Threat / risk | Control / remaining evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Untrusted dispatch/source, high | Owner/repo/main/event/workflow SHA federation, tracked hash, trusted build provenance and immutable ancestry; actual federation remains untested. |
| Privilege elevation, high | Service-only update, actual exact role readback, one ActAs/state bucket; inherited IAM needs owner verification. |
| Disclosure, high | Explicit in-memory token, no credential files/argv, bounded selected response and receipt-only upload; fake failure/redaction tests. |
| Lost/partial promotion, high | Current-main/expiry rechecks, strict preflight/post-readback and owner cleanup; no blind retry/automatic rollback. |
| Resource abuse, high | Existing finite service profile, short-lived token, separate inactive default; hosted timing/cost/load remains open. |

The Citizen Developer security skill requires human/security review before cloud
exposure or IAM/federation activation. Repository Infisical/GCP authority remains
in force. This operational interface is not an ISO20022 financial exchange; no
money/currency/SQL or accounting semantics change, and no ISO conformance is claimed.

documents.title: Controlled worker release
documents.body:
# Controlled worker release

This contract separates release configuration from infrastructure ownership. It
introduces no financial wire format and makes no new ISO conformance claim; the
existing acquisition message and accounting contracts remain authoritative.

## State and authority

`infra/gcp/foundation` owns the dedicated `jayburd-dev-worker-deployer` identity,
`jayburd-dev-worker-deploy` workload identity pool, `owner-worker-deploy` provider,
and `${project}-jayburd-dev-worker-runtime-state` bucket. Federation is disabled
by default. The only accepted workflow is owner-dispatched
`.github/workflows/deploy-workers.yml@refs/heads/main`, with immutable repository,
owner and actor IDs. Application deployment trust remains separate.

`infra/gcp/workers` remains owner-operated: SQL IAM users, queue, secret containers,
storage, runtime and release IAM, invocation bindings and Scheduler. Scheduler is
always configured paused. `worker_services_exist=false` initially withholds the
two invocation bindings; the owner sets it true only after both services exist and
pause is verified. This flag is not a CI input.

`infra/gcp/worker-runtime` owns only two Cloud Run services. Its isolated backend
uses prefix `worker-runtime`. It never reads bootstrap remote state. Inputs are
`project_id`, positive canonical int64 `project_number`, fixed `region=us-central1`,
and required `runtime={image,binding_id,publisher_policy,client_id_version,client_secret_version}`.
`binding-v1` requires an enrolled binding UUID. `shared-v1` requires an empty
binding ID and uses the publisher login's enrolled bindings through
[shared acquisition](shared-acquisition-publisher.md).
Image must be a worker digest in this project's repository. Secret versions are
positive canonical int64 identifiers, never aliases or values. No activation flag
exists. Runtime capacity remains one instance and one concurrent request per
service, 90-second request timeout, private IAM invocation, fixed service accounts,
exact caller subject lookups, and the existing bounded worker arguments.

Release authority is the custom permission set `run.services.create/get/update`,
`run.operations.get`, and read-only `cloudscheduler.jobs.get`. It also has repository
reader, ObjectAdmin on its own state bucket, serviceAccountUser on publisher/sync
only, and `iam.serviceAccounts.get` on scheduler/task-invoker only. It receives no
IAM policy mutation, secret access/admin, SQL ownership, service deletion, queue
publication, Scheduler creation/update/run/enable or token creation permission.
Create/update permissions are project-scoped: Terraform and reviewed release code
constrain resource names; this is not an IAM guarantee of only two service names.
A deployer can alter code running as its allowed identities, so digest review and
protected workflow trust are material security boundaries.

## Owner migration and first deployment

No agent reads state, plans, secret values or live provider data. The following is
an owner procedure, not an executed migration:

1. Freeze application/worker releases; pause and verify any existing Scheduler
   job. Resolve queued/in-flight work separately: a paused schedule does not cancel
   tasks already queued. Do not claim a provider-free maintenance window from pause
   alone. Apply foundation additions with owner authority.
2. For existing deployments, retain `worker_services_exist=true` so invocation IAM
   stays under the same bootstrap addresses. Remove obsolete `runtime` and
   `scheduler_enabled` owner variables. Review the bootstrap plan: the included
   `removed { destroy=false }` block forgets only the two service instances; it must
   not delete or replace them. Existing Scheduler address `[0]` is unchanged.
   Apply only the reviewed owner migration. Never apply both states as owners of
   the same services.
3. Initialize the new dedicated runtime backend. The owner imports the existing
   service IDs into `google_cloud_run_v2_service.worker["publisher"]` and
   `["sync"]`: `projects/PROJECT/locations/us-central1/services/jayburd-dev-acquisition-publisher`
   and `.../jayburd-dev-acquisition-sync`. Use the currently approved image and
   metadata for initial adoption. Review a no-destroy/no-replacement reconciliation
   before authorizing CI. Preserve private owner backups; do not upload state/plan.
4. For a fresh deployment instead, apply workers with `worker_services_exist=false`
   first. It creates the paused job before service invocation permission exists.
   The owner may create the two runtime services directly with the reviewed
   runtime root, then verify Scheduler remains paused; owner subsequently
   applies workers with `worker_services_exist=true`. The provider creates a job
   before issuing pause, so invocation isolation during initial creation matters.
5. Alternatively, first creation may use CI after the separate worker federation
   is enabled based on pre-deployment evidence (successful runtime creation is not
   a prerequisite). Enable federation only after ownership, SQL role/binding,
   credential-version/mapping and identity evidence is reviewed. CI checks PAUSED
   before and after applying runtime. It does not invoke workers or activate jobs.
   A separate explicit activation review is required for provider traffic.

On partial migration failure, keep releases frozen and finish import using known
resource identifiers. Never recreate services or restore dual state ownership as
an automated retry. The owner reviews any rollback and IAM drift separately.

## Reviewed evidence and limits

Reviewed 2026-10-14, primary documentation sections and pinned provider code:

- [Cloud Run permissions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/iam/permissions),
  Services table: get/update/create are separate from setIamPolicy/delete.
- [Cloud Run image deployment](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/deploying),
  Required roles: service identity actAs and repository read are separate grants.
- [Operation polling](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.operations/get):
  `run.operations.get` authorizes asynchronous deployment polling.
- [Scheduler IAM](https://docs.cloud.google.com/scheduler/docs/access-control),
  role permission table: job configuration and invocation permissions differ;
  job create can also target project Pub/Sub, supporting owner-only ownership.
- [Google provider v8.6.0 Run service implementation](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google/blob/v8.6.0/google/services/cloudrunv2/resource_cloud_run_v2_service.go),
  Create/Read/Update: reads service resource and polls operation; this configuration
  does not require a separate revisions.get grant. No quota billing override is
  configured; additional serviceusage permissions are not assumed necessary.
- [Google provider v8.6.0 Scheduler implementation](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google/blob/v8.6.0/google/services/cloudscheduler/resource_cloud_scheduler_job.go),
  Create/paused handling: pause follows creation, not an atomic create-paused API.
- [HashiCorp state refactor](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/state/refactor),
  cross-state removed/import procedure: `destroy=false` preserves infrastructure.

These facts support the local design; mocked Terraform tests validate shape,
separation, default pause, exact trust and bounds. They do not establish deployed
IAM correctness, workload identity authentication, a completed owner state
migration, credential freshness, or successful provider acquisition. Hosted
permission gaps must fail deployment and be reviewed, never trigger broad grants.

## Limited Sandbox qualification

The separately reviewed [Sandbox release contract](sandbox-release.md) adds explicit
`sandbox-promote`/`sandbox-rollback` operations for the fixed development project.
Full promote/rollback gates above remain unchanged. Sandbox releases require the
bounded database proof (#130), and connection-enabled/worker releases also require
delivery implementation (#131). Hosted activation is separately tracked in #133.
Scheduling remains paused; no production or full-readiness claim follows.
