documents.body:
# Journal observer SQL contract

## Decision, authority and implementation status

**Local SQL foundation implemented by migration 000008**, 2026-10-13;
owner: project maintainer; [#74](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/74),
parent #57, implementation #7. Implement only `journal.observe` version 1:
consume a committed journal fact and durably record observation. No financial
mutation, provider call, generalized scheduler, cursor or arbitrary handler.
[Background work](background-work.md) owns delivery semantics and the internal
`work-wakeup-v1` envelope. Its STD-01 assessment applies unchanged: internal
wakeup/receipt, no ISO 20022 financial exchange or audit-export conformance.

Existing `integration.outbox_message`, journals, posting/setup receipts and
`ledger.interactive_command` remain unchanged. No observer changes book revision,
account balances, outbox rows or the original poster's authority. Migration 000008 adds only observer sidecars and restricted functions. Migrations
000001–000007 remain unchanged. Hosted transport and activation remain pending.

## Concrete authorization and roles

Use NOLOGIN roles `bookkeeping_publisher` and `bookkeeping_observer`, neither
member of API/owner/migrator/identity-operator or each other. Separate actual
workload login roles receive exactly one role. Cloud Tasks invocation identity
is not a database login and receives no SQL grant. HTTP middleware still verifies
configured OIDC issuer/audience/service identity before invoking observer SQL.

`integration.observer_binding` is owner-provisioned, not a self-enrollment API:

| Column | Type and constraint |
| --- | --- |
| binding_id | uuid PRIMARY KEY |
| entity_id, book_id | uuid NOT NULL; composite FK to `ledger.book`, NO ACTION |
| principal_id | uuid NOT NULL FK `ledger.principal`, NO ACTION; dedicated service principal, not original poster |
| publisher_login, consumer_login | name NOT NULL; distinct; exact PostgreSQL `session_user` login names |
| consumer_id, handler_version | text CHECK = `journal.observe`; integer CHECK = 1 |
| binding_revision | bigint NOT NULL CHECK > 0 |
| enabled | boolean NOT NULL |
| created_at, updated_at | finite timestamptz NOT NULL |

UNIQUE `(entity_id,book_id,consumer_id,handler_version)` and UNIQUE
`(entity_id,book_id,binding_id)`. Binding IDs/scope/principal/consumer/version/login
names never mutate; enable/disable increments revision. Changing identity needs a
future explicit handoff contract, not assigning old work to a new login silently.
Only the provisioning owner controls binding rows, creates the ledger principal
and supplies `read` membership for its entity. No invented `observe` permission
is inserted into the existing membership CHECK. Binding additionally narrows that
entity-level membership to one book; database functions never accept actor input.
Do not mint Firebase tokens or interpret end-user email as service identity.
The exact synthetic/hosted enrollment procedure is a prerequisite to DDL rollout.

All callable functions are owned by `bookkeeping_owner`, SECURITY DEFINER,
VOLATILE/PARALLEL UNSAFE, `SET search_path=pg_catalog,pg_temp`, fully qualified
relations/functions. Revoke PUBLIC EXECUTE in the same migration transaction;
only grant named entrypoints below. No direct table SELECT/DML, sequence access,
schema CREATE, role elevation or execution of internal helpers for either role.
Require SERIALIZABLE for every entrypoint. Set transaction-local
statement_timeout=5s and lock_timeout=1s before invocation; tests verify safe
failure when callers omit required transaction mode. Functions set their own
lock timeout defensively; handler's SQL context bounds the entire call.

Resolve immutable operation→binding metadata, then require the function-specific
`session_user` to equal the enrolled publisher/consumer. Do not trust `current_user`
inside SECURITY DEFINER or a caller-supplied worker UUID as principal authority.
Recheck binding and call `ledger.authorize(principal_id,e,b,'read',false)` in the
same SERIALIZABLE transaction, taking the existing principal/entity/membership/book
locks. Map P2101/P2102 to the uniform worker denial below, without scope disclosure.
The service principal must remain enabled with current read membership at discovery,
claim and completion. Posting-user revocation does not cancel independent authorized
observation. Deletion of referenced principals is **not solved** here: current FKs
restrict deletion, and #4's deletion-policy/testing gap remains open.

## Rows, keys and indexes

All columns NOT NULL unless explicitly `nullable`. UUIDs are generated by the
server. All timestamps finite; all counters bigint and nonnegative with guarded
overflow. Repeated scope columns use composite FKs; no cascading deletes. Owner
triggers reject updates/deletes of immutable sidecars, attempts and receipts.
All new tables belong to `integration` and are implemented in migration 000008.

### work_operation

`entity_id uuid, book_id uuid, operation_id uuid, binding_id uuid,
message_id uuid, consumer_id text='journal.observe', handler_version integer=1,
request_digest bytea CHECK octet_length=32, created_at timestamptz,
state text, attempt_count bigint DEFAULT 0, failed_attempt_count bigint DEFAULT 0,
execution_generation bigint DEFAULT 0, fence_token bigint DEFAULT 0,
dispatch_generation bigint DEFAULT 1, next_eligible_at timestamptz,
first_claimed_at timestamptz nullable, deadline_at timestamptz nullable,
lease_holder uuid nullable, lease_until timestamptz nullable,
claim_binding_revision bigint nullable, terminal_code text nullable,
finished_at timestamptz nullable`.

PK `(entity_id,book_id,operation_id)`; UNIQUE `operation_id`; UNIQUE
`(entity_id,book_id,message_id,consumer_id,handler_version)`. Composite FKs to
binding and outbox message. CHECK consumer/version constants; state in
`ready,running,retry_wait,succeeded,blocked,quarantined`.
`failed_attempt_count <= attempt_count`; `execution_generation=attempt_count`.
First claim sets first_claimed_at once and deadline_at=first_claimed_at+24h;
CHECK both null together, otherwise exact interval. Running iff holder, lease and
claim revision all nonnull; lease bounded by its attempt's start+90s. Succeeded/
blocked/quarantined iff terminal_code and finished_at nonnull. Code CHECK uses
closed list `observed,authority_revoked,event_mismatch,retry_exhausted,age_exhausted`.
Success code is `observed` only; blocked code is `authority_revoked`; quarantine
codes are `event_mismatch,retry_exhausted,age_exhausted`. Cross-row/state correspondence is owned-function
plus deferred constraint-trigger authority, not an unsupported CHECK subquery.
No opaque financial JSON body or runtime-selectable handler.

`request_digest` uses SHA-256 over UTF-8 with fixed ASCII delimiter `|` and these
canonical values: `journal.observe|1|entity_uuid|book_uuid|message_uuid|target_uuid|book_revision`.
UUIDs lowercase canonical; revision unsigned decimal. These fields cannot contain
`|`. Compute server-side with pg_catalog SHA-256 support; compare all source fields
as well as digest when resuming. Digest is an accelerator/integrity check, not
business identity. Binding configuration/retry counters are not source identity.

Indexes: partial `(next_eligible_at,operation_id)` for ready/retry_wait;
partial `(lease_until,operation_id)` for running; `(binding_id,state,operation_id)`
for scoped recovery. UNIQUEs above enforce deduplication across dispatch generations.
No assumption of contiguous journal revisions or event order.

### outbox_delivery

`entity_id uuid, book_id uuid, message_id uuid, consumer_id text='journal.observe',
handler_version integer=1, operation_id uuid, created_at timestamptz`.
PK `(entity_id,book_id,message_id,consumer_id,handler_version)`; UNIQUE
`(entity_id,book_id,operation_id)`; scoped FK to existing outbox; composite FK of
scope/message/consumer/version/operation to a matching UNIQUE on work_operation.
Immutable sidecar. Insert operation, sidecar and dispatch 1 atomically. Existing
outbox facts remain unchanged even when no consumer is enrolled.

### work_dispatch

`entity_id uuid, book_id uuid, operation_id uuid, dispatch_generation bigint CHECK >0,
target_version integer CHECK =1, task_name_digest bytea CHECK octet_length=32,
state text, enqueue_attempt_count bigint DEFAULT 0, publisher_fence bigint DEFAULT 0,
lease_holder uuid nullable, lease_until timestamptz nullable, created_at timestamptz,
last_attempt_at timestamptz nullable, last_result_at timestamptz nullable,
result_code text nullable`.
PK scope/operation/dispatch_generation; FK to scoped operation. State in
`pending,publishing,enqueued,uncertain,retired`; publishing iff holder/lease nonnull.
Result nullable or `accepted,already_exists,timeout,transient,rejected`.
Task digest is SHA-256 of `operation_uuid|dispatch_generation|target_version`;
queue task ID uses its hex encoding. Target 1 resolves only through deployment
allowlist, never an arbitrary stored URL. UNIQUE task_name_digest. Partial index
`(created_at,operation_id,dispatch_generation)` for pending/uncertain; partial
`(lease_until,operation_id,dispatch_generation)` for publishing. Old rows are
retained as transport history; they cannot complete or revive work.

### work_attempt and work_receipt

Attempt columns: `entity_id uuid, book_id uuid, operation_id uuid,
execution_generation bigint CHECK >0, attempt_id uuid UNIQUE,
fence_token bigint CHECK >0, holder_id uuid, binding_revision bigint CHECK >0,
started_at timestamptz`. PK scope/operation/execution_generation; scoped operation
FK. Immutable start row. No later UPDATE to fill end-time fields; its matching
receipt supplies termination. UNIQUE `(entity_id,book_id,operation_id,
execution_generation,fence_token)` supports the receipt FK.

Receipt columns: `entity_id uuid, book_id uuid, operation_id uuid,
execution_generation bigint CHECK >0, fence_token bigint CHECK >0,
outcome text, request_digest bytea CHECK octet_length=32,
binding_revision bigint CHECK >0, recorded_at timestamptz`.
PK scope/operation/execution_generation; exact composite FK to attempt including
fence; outcome in `observed,retryable,abandoned,authority_revoked,event_mismatch,
retry_exhausted,age_exhausted`. Immutable. Unique partial index on
`(entity_id,book_id,operation_id) WHERE outcome='observed'` is the successful-effect
guard. Receipt binding_revision equals its attempt binding_revision (the authority
version captured by that execution); outcome distinguishes successful observation
from later revocation, not a claim that old authority remains valid.
Receipt has no journal amounts, tokens, provider bodies or caller-controlled
exception text. Journal provenance is reached through operation→outbox→journal.

An attempt starts once, then receives at most one outcome. Retry/failure closure
inserts outcome and increments failed_attempt_count in the same transaction under
operation lock; a competing scanner cannot count that attempt again. Pre-claim
blocked/quarantined decisions may have attempt_count=0, record terminal code/time
on operation and **do not fabricate an attempt or execution-0 receipt**. Their
fixed terminal acknowledgement is derived from the durable operation state.

## Lock order, clock and restricted functions

Every operation uses this order: immutable lookup without lock → binding FOR SHARE
(or UPDATE for owner disabling) → ledger principal → entity → membership → book
via authorize → work_operation FOR UPDATE → dispatch rows by ascending generation
→ attempt/receipt inserts. For recovery, process one scoped operation per transaction. Discovery may insert
up to 25 new operations for one authorized binding/book in event order; it never
locks an unordered collection of different books in one transaction. Candidate
selection is a nonauthoritative bounded read; acquire authorization locks before
`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` on operation/dispatch. Recheck predicates after lock.
Revocation transactions that touch binding and membership together follow this
same order. Existing membership-only revocation shares the authorize lock boundary.
No network operation runs while a SQL transaction remains open.

After all potentially waiting row locks, set `t=clock_timestamp()`; check lease
and deadline against **this** time. Lease validity requires `t < lease_until`.
Heartbeat cannot resurrect expiry. Increment counters/fences only after range
checks; exhaustion fails safely, never wraps. Dispatch and consumer fences are
independent. Changing a dispatch generation does not increase ledger revision.
Recheck actual time immediately before final state/receipt writes, after any
additional lock wait. Runtime commits immediately; no external await or user work
is allowed between the function return and COMMIT. Login-role transaction/idle
timeouts and handler context must bound open transactions during implementation.
Database wall-clock changes may affect liveness; generation fences plus locked
state still prevent a replaced holder from committing. Clock-based leases are
not a claim of a monotonic system clock.

All signatures below are under `integration`. `uuid` holder parameters identify
attempts, never authority. Functions return only the stated minimal metadata;
private helpers are not executable by runtime roles.

| Entry point / granted role | Exact inputs and returned values; owned transition |
| --- | --- |
| `observe_discover` / publisher | `(binding_id uuid, limit integer)`; require 1..25. Return integer inserted count only. Current scoped authority, bounded ordered outbox scan by created_at/message_id where no sidecar, validate header, atomic operation/sidecar/dispatch insertion. Concurrent inserts conflict harmlessly only if full identity matches. |
| `observe_dispatch_claim` / publisher | `(operation_id uuid, holder uuid)` → `(dispatch_generation bigint,target_version integer,task_name_hex text,publisher_fence bigint,lease_until timestamptz)` or fixed `not_due`. Lock operation before current dispatch; eligible unfinished work only. Claim pending/uncertain/expired publishing with new publisher fence, 30s lease, enqueue attempts+1. |
| `observe_dispatch_result` / publisher | `(operation_id uuid, dispatch_generation bigint, holder uuid, publisher_fence bigint, result text)` → boolean recorded. Result closed enum above; CAS matching unexpired claim, clear publisher lease, persist enqueue result only. accepted→enqueued; others→uncertain. No operation-state mutation; stale acknowledgement returns false. |
| `observe_claim` / observer | `(operation_id uuid, dispatch_generation bigint, holder uuid)` → fixed status plus execution_generation/fence/lease only when claimed. Require dispatch row belongs to operation; absent/future generation rejects; persisted older generation may wake due work. Current auth; successful/terminal operation returns `done` without detail, active lease returns `busy`, not eligible returns `not_due`. Eligible claim creates attempt, increments attempt/execution/fence, sets running with 90s lease and binding revision. |
| `observe_heartbeat` / observer | `(operation_id uuid, holder uuid, execution_generation bigint, fence bigint)` → boolean. Matching holder/execution/fence/binding revision, live lease/deadline and current authority only; lease becomes least(t+90s, attempt.started_at+90s); first slice cannot extend attempt duration. No counters/effects. |
| `observe_finish` / observer | `(operation_id uuid, holder uuid, execution_generation bigint, fence bigint)` → fixed `observed`/`done`. Reauthorize; verify holder/execution/fence, unexpired lease/deadline and unchanged claim binding revision, fixed digest/event/header; atomically insert observed receipt, clear lease and mark succeeded. No input journal, actor, outcome or financial data. |
| `observe_fail` / observer | `(operation_id uuid, holder uuid, execution_generation bigint, fence bigint)` → fixed `retry_wait`/`quarantined`. Current live claim only; trusted handler reports a retryable internal execution failure, never arbitrary text. Close attempt once with retryable outcome, increment failed count; apply retry/age caps before releasing lease. |
| `observe_recover` / publisher | `(operation_id uuid)` → fixed outcome only. Current scoped authority; recover expired attempt/dispatch or missing delivery of due work as detailed below. No network, arbitrary retry budget or terminal-state reset. |

Publisher needs a bounded `observe_candidates(binding_id uuid, limit integer)`
entrypoint returning operation UUIDs only; limit 1..25, current scope authority,
ordered by next eligible time/UUID including expired claims/stale dispatches.
Discovery and candidates require explicitly configured binding IDs; no API to
enumerate every LLC. This read executes within SERIALIZABLE for consistent policy.
Role ACL tests must require SQLSTATE 42501 for every other function/table/DDL.

### Exact return shapes

The function table above is normative for inputs. These SQL return declarations
and closed statuses remove any implied free-form JSON result:

- observe_discover: RETURNS integer (0..25).
- observe_candidates: RETURNS TABLE(operation_id uuid), 0..25 rows.
- observe_dispatch_claim: RETURNS TABLE(status text, dispatch_generation bigint,
  target_version integer, task_name_hex text, publisher_fence bigint,
  lease_until timestamptz), exactly one row. Status is claimed or not_due;
  metadata all nonnull only for claimed, all null otherwise. task_name_hex is
  exactly 64 lowercase hex characters.
- observe_dispatch_result and observe_heartbeat: RETURNS boolean, never null.
- observe_claim: RETURNS TABLE(status text, execution_generation bigint,
  fence_token bigint, lease_until timestamptz), exactly one row. Status in
  claimed,done,busy,not_due; metadata all nonnull only when claimed. done includes
  durable succeeded/blocked/quarantined, exposing no outcome details.
- observe_finish: RETURNS text in observed,done. A newly observed receipt returns
  observed; existing completion or a newly committed block/quarantine returns done.
- observe_fail: RETURNS text in retry_wait,quarantined,done. A new retry/failure
  terminalization returns its state; prior terminal outcome or newly blocked
  authority returns done.
- observe_recover: RETURNS text in no_change,retry_wait,redispatched,blocked,
  quarantined,done. Return the most significant committed transition: terminal
  transition first, abandoned-attempt retry second, dispatch replacement third.
  Already terminal operation returns done; healthy/not-yet-due returns no_change.

These statuses apply only after transaction commit. Statement-level returns cannot
justify a task acknowledgement before COMMIT succeeds. SQL exceptions use the
separate error mapping below; they never masquerade as a returned terminal result.

## Completion, revocation and recovery transitions

The observer verifies outbox scope, target, event_type `journal.posted`, version 1
and revision equal the corresponding immutable journal header. A reversal journal
is eligible; its existing historical amounts are not recalculated or copied.
Mismatch closes an active attempt with event_mismatch and quarantines; it never
throws after writing the quarantine, which would roll back that evidence.

Authorization denial requires special handling: caller-login/binding existence is
checked first. Wrong caller sees uniform P2201 with no writes. A correctly enrolled
login whose previously bound service authority was revoked can only mark the
owned operation `blocked/authority_revoked`, clear its lease/increment fence and,
if running, close its attempt with authority_revoked. This restricted no-data
transition locks the same available principal/entity/membership/book rows even
when disabled/revoked, in the same order; it cannot read journal contents, enqueue,
claim or finish. Repeated denial adds no attempts or receipts. An already succeeded
operation returns only fixed `done` to its enrolled consumer even after revocation.
Only observe_claim, observe_finish, observe_fail and observe_recover own this
no-data blocking transition. Discovery, candidate enumeration and dispatch calls
deny with P2201 instead; heartbeat returns false after binding verification.
This is a receipt-suppression path, not permission to fetch its result.

Normal retry: with fewer than 8 failures and before first-claim+24h, clear lease,
set retry_wait and next_eligible_at=t+jitter. Delay range is
`[max(1s,B/2),B]`, `B=min(900s,5s*2^(failed_attempt_count-1))`; choose server-side,
never sleep in a transaction. This journal observer has no provider Retry-After.
At failure 8 quarantine with retry_exhausted; at deadline quarantine with
age_exhausted, whichever first applies. Successful completion must also occur
before the deadline. Claim, finish and recovery all evaluate deadline before
normal lease-contention handling. Deadline exhaustion closes any outstanding
attempt with age_exhausted (one failed count), fences its holder and atomically
quarantines, even if its lease has not yet expired; an already succeeded operation
stays succeeded. No new attempt is fabricated if none is outstanding.
Non-claim deliveries, denial and healthy lease contention
consume no attempt/failure budget. Event mismatch counts one failed attempt;
authority denial is a blocked outcome and consumes no failure budget.

On expired running recovery: under operation lock insert abandoned receipt if
no receipt exists for that execution, increment failed count once, clear holder,
advance fence, then apply same retry/cap rule. A new claim occurs only when due,
with a new execution generation. Heartbeats/finishes by the abandoned holder fail.
No attempt receipt exists yet for pre-claim age exhaustion; persist the operation's
terminal code instead. `succeeded`, `blocked` and `quarantined` never auto-reopen.

Recovery retires a current dispatch only when work is due, no healthy consumer
claim exists, and the current dispatch creation time is older than 15 minutes, or the
current transport attempt was explicitly rejected. Increment dispatch_generation
and insert pending dispatch atomically with retirement. An expired first publisher lease permits retrying that same generation/task
identity. Once at least two enqueue claims have expired, the same fixed 15-minute
age bound permits replacement. A healthy publisher lease remains protected.
Repeated `ALREADY_EXISTS`, timeout or transient result timestamps do not reset
the creation-age bound; they are transport history, not progress evidence.
This correction was coordinator-reviewed during implementation after identifying
that refreshing the age on every uncertain result could postpone recovery forever. ALREADY_EXISTS is
uncertain delivery evidence, never successful observation; queue deletion/purge
cannot erase SQL intent. Publisher result arriving after consumer completion may
update matching dispatch metadata but never regress succeeded work. Old queued
messages remain bound to the same operation and cannot create a second effect.

No cancellation or administrative retry endpoint is in this first slice. Preserve
terminal evidence for owner investigation; a later scoped audited budget-grant/
cancel contract is required to reopen/cancel work. Do not reset counters, edit
receipts or delete/recreate an operation to bypass exhaustion. Synthetic fixture
teardown drops the disposable database, not selected evidence rows. Hosted retention,
operator audit UI and deletion lifecycle remain deployment gates.

## SQLSTATE and caller behavior

Migration 000008 reserves P2200–P2205 after checking prior migrations:
P2200 malformed arguments/unsupported isolation; P2201 uniform unavailable scope
or caller; P2202 identity/digest conflict; P2203 stale holder/fence/lease;
P2204 counter exhaustion; P2205 unsafe configuration. Fixed messages only, no
SQL details or private scope identifiers. Normal busy/not_due/done are typed
results, not errors. Revocation/mismatch terminal transitions return fixed results
only after their durable transaction commits. A denied helper exception caught by
a wrapper must not accidentally retain unvalidated data in its response.

40001/40P01 roll back and retry the whole bounded transaction with identical IDs,
up to three attempts within the request deadline; 55P03/57014 roll back and return
retryable transport failure without inventing a business receipt. If a claim had
already committed, its eventual lease recovery accounts for abandonment exactly
once. Unknown commit: reconnect and inspect operation through scoped claim/status
semantics before any new effect; never interpret a lost response as noncommit.
HTTP acknowledges only committed success/terminal outcome, otherwise non-2xx.
Workload OIDC rejection does not invoke SQL or acknowledge a durable business result.

## Source review and alternatives

Sources reviewed 2026-10-13, selected sections only; proposed project decisions,
not vendor guarantees. Existing [BW01–BW05](../research/background-work-sources.md)
and bibliography S08/S12 remain canonical pattern/identity/transport references.
This section is the source record for the additional physical choices:

- **WS01**, PostgreSQL Global Development Group, PostgreSQL 17
  [SELECT: Locking Clause](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-select.html#SQL-FOR-UPDATE-SHARE),
  paragraphs on SKIP LOCKED and joined relations. Queue scans can avoid row waits,
  but produce an inconsistent view. Our inference is bounded candidate discovery
  plus fresh authorization and locked predicates; not a fairness or ordering proof.
- **WS02**, same publisher/version,
  [Date/Time §9.9.5](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/functions-datetime.html#FUNCTIONS-DATETIME-CURRENT),
  transaction/statement/clock distinctions reviewed. Actual clock time changes
  within statements; transaction time does not. Our lease check samples actual
  time after locks; application-supplied time is rejected. Clock monotonicity is
  not established by this documentation.
- **WS03**, same publisher/version,
  [CREATE FUNCTION: Writing SECURITY DEFINER Functions Safely](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-createfunction.html#SQL-CREATEFUNCTION-SECURITY),
  search-path and PUBLIC execute paragraphs reviewed. Isolate trusted object
  resolution and revoke default invocation before commit. Our inference uses
  explicit login-bound entrypoints; the source does not verify our grant model.

A simpler single atomic observe call could omit consumer lease/attempt state,
but would not exercise the selected recovery/fencing boundary before provider
work. This fixed handler intentionally proves those mechanisms without financial
side effects. A universal JSON jobs table would add undefined authority and
migration surface; provider-specific records remain in their separate contract.

## Named acceptance and smallest migration handoff

The disposable proof implements the tests below; exact evidence and remaining
boundaries are recorded in the [living runbook](../runbooks/journal-observer.md).
Use disposable PostgreSQL,
separate synthetic publisher/observer logins, explicit service binding/read grants
and hand-created journal fixtures using existing restricted posting operations.
`bash scripts/test-observer.sh` runs the actual restricted-role SQL fault proof;
default Go checks alone do not validate these semantics.

| Test | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `TestObserverSchemaBoundary` | Exact constraints/FKs/indexes, no outbox mutation; role DML/DDL/cross-function denial 42501; spoofed actor/session role fails; fixed SECURITY DEFINER path resists temporary-object substitution. |
| `TestObserverDiscoverAtomicity` | Crash after operation/sidecar/dispatch writes leaves all or none; concurrent discovery produces one operation; no skipped history, revision gaps and reversal journals accepted. |
| `TestObserverReceiptAtomicity` | Event/header mismatch quarantines; failures before receipt/commit roll back; ack loss recovers one observation; journal/outbox/book revisions unchanged. |
| `TestObserverPublisherRace` | Consumer completes before enqueue result; late result cannot regress success; timeout/ALREADY_EXISTS/rejected and stale publisher fence maintain truthful dispatch state. |
| `TestObserverFenceClock` | Real two-session expiry/takeover, lock wait beyond lease, stale heartbeat/finish, request cancellation and overflow all reject stale effect. No production clock-injection API; owner-created expired synthetic rows isolate clock cases. |
| `TestObserverRetryBudget` | Failure8 OR age24h quarantines; duplicate deliveries no extra counts; two sweepers abandon one crashed attempt exactly once; jitter bounded; successful terminal operation cannot reset/reexecute. |
| `TestObserverAuthorizationRace` | Binding/service membership/entity/book disable before claim/finish; commit-first versus revocation-first outcomes; completed-receipt suppression reveals no financial output; original poster revocation does not revoke a separate service mandate. |
| `TestObserverQueueLoss` | Task purge/tombstone/scheduler downtime yields a new dispatch on the same operation; old/new arrivals still produce one observation; healthy lease cannot be stolen. |
| `ReviewObserverProvisioning` | Owner-approved exact service enrollment/login binding, grants, STD-01 mapping, retention and shared connection budget; actual hosted proof remains #26/#11/#7. |

Completed local sequence: coordinator review → migration 000008 → restricted
entrypoints and disposable fault tests. Next: least-privilege Go transport and
Cloud Tasks fake → separately reviewed Terraform and hosted acceptance. Reject or revise the contract if fault tests expose unhandled
lock orders or completion races. #74 does not close #7, #4, #11 or #26.

## Local enrollment and remaining hosted gate

The isolated test runner creates actual LOGIN roles `synthetic_publisher` and
`synthetic_observer`, each inheriting exactly its matching NOLOGIN capability.
Owner fixture setup inserts a dedicated ledger principal, current entity `read`
membership and one book binding with those exact login names. This is synthetic
owner provisioning, never runtime self-enrollment or end-user impersonation.
Hosted migration bootstrap must pre-create both safe NOLOGIN capability roles
because the restricted migrator has no CREATEROLE. No workload LOGIN or service
binding is provisioned by migration 000008. Actual hosted enrollment, role-level
transaction/idle timeouts, OIDC, runtime cancellation/retry and shared pool budget
remain deployment gates. The test client sets statement/lock timeouts, retries
whole serializable transactions at most three times and commits immediately;
there is no production Go worker or network queue adapter in this slice.

documents.title: ADR 0001: transactional Go bookkeeping on GCP
documents.body:
# ADR 0001: transactional Go bookkeeping on GCP

## Decision

Accepted direction, 2026-10-11: Go backend, PostgreSQL authoritative ledger,
Next.js/TypeScript frontend, GCP Cloud Run/Cloud SQL, GitHub Actions and Terraform.
Python is not a runtime requirement. DuckDB is deferred until an analytical
workload justifies it. No full event sourcing or distributed ledger writes.

## Boundaries

Start as a modular application with independently runnable commands. The API,
outbox publisher, bank sync handler and import/export runner reuse the same
accounting rules. Separate executables do not imply separate ledgers or copied
posting logic. Only introduce services for permission, scaling or failure domains.

Proposed future layout (create directories with their first tested behavior):

```text
cmd/api/                  HTTP application composition
cmd/outbox-publisher/     bounded delivery of committed intent
cmd/bank-sync/            private task endpoint
cmd/import-export/        bounded batch job
internal/accounting/      posting and reconciliation rules
internal/ingestion/       provider-independent acquisition operations
internal/platform/        database, identity and transport adapters
db/migrations/            checksummed forward SQL migrations
web/                      Next.js UI
infra/                    Terraform roots with separate state ownership
```

## Consistency

A single database transaction validates authority/open period, posts the full
balanced journal, records audit/idempotency evidence, and writes outbox intent.
No independent debit/credit messages. Closing and posting coordinate locks.
Initially, authoritative reports read posted ledger rows directly.
See [accounting](../contracts/accounting.md) and
[background work](../contracts/background-work.md).

## Tradeoffs

Go favors explicit operations and small executables. PostgreSQL provides durable
transactions but cannot infer correct accounting. Concurrency remains bounded
by database connections, provider limits and per-connection ownership. The
monorepo shares review/build tooling, not an obligation to deploy everything
on every change. Database tooling now follows [ADR 0003](0003-database-first.md); application
library installation remains a JB-003 slice.

documents.title: ADR 0002: repository context and GitHub execution
documents.body:
# ADR 0002: repository context and GitHub execution

## Decision

Adopt Brainblast's linked decisions, bounded work packets, explicit dependencies,
dry-run mutations and evidence-based handoffs. Keep this project's context beside
its code. GitHub owns issue state, discussion and native dependency relationships.
Repository Markdown owns product contracts, decisions, research and runbooks.

The initial backlog is a one-time publication seed. After publication, its
acceptance text is historical input; update active scope in the Issue and link
revised contracts. Never mirror ongoing status into this file. The issue registry
stores stable identity links only. Generated drafts/packets are not authority.

## Why

[Local inspection](../research/brainblast.md) found useful tested query/sync
primitives, but also a fail-open queue rule and project-specific coupling.
GitHub now supports native dependencies and sub-issues. A single-project repo
does not need bidirectional Markdown/Issue synchronization or an agent scheduler.

This intentionally adapts the task-orchestrator workflow: the external vault is
a read-only reference, not the canonical task store for Jayburd. No private vault
notes, organization records, or copied implementation are incorporated.

## Rules

- Unknown, missing, canceled or inaccessible predecessors block scheduling.
- A closed issue is complete only when its closure reason is completed and its
  acceptance/merge evidence is present. Labels and checkboxes are not proof.
- Native dependency relationships own execution order after publication.
- One issue per independently reviewable outcome; one active slice per person.
- An optional GitHub Project is a view, not another database of task truth.
- No automated deployment or agent execution from issue text or labels.

## Sources

[GitHub dependencies](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/creating-issue-dependencies)
and [Project automation](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/using-the-built-in-automations),
checked 2026-10-11. Board auto-close is not an accounting acceptance gate.

documents.title: ADR 0003: SQL-first contracts and golang-migrate
documents.body:
# ADR 0003: SQL-first contracts and golang-migrate

## Decision

Accepted migration tool: `golang-migrate/migrate` v4.20.1. Use reviewed PostgreSQL
SQL files, with paired six-digit sequential `up.sql` and `down.sql` filenames.
The disposable tooling proof uses PostgreSQL 17.11; cloud-version selection stays
in JB-005. Image indexes are pinned by digest for amd64/arm64 reproducibility.

No ORM is needed. Recommend `pgx/v5` for application connections and `sqlc` to
generate typed Go methods from reviewed SQL when queries exist. Those application
dependencies are not installed yet. The migrate CLI's PostgreSQL driver is an
implementation detail, independent of the future application driver.

## Why

An ORM maps tables to objects and can provide relationships, change tracking and
query construction. It does not establish balanced journals, entity isolation,
posting/close locking or idempotency. Explicit SQL makes these boundaries easier
to review. sqlc removes repetitive parameter/scanning code without owning schema
changes. Generated row types are persistence types, not HTTP or domain contracts.

## Contract order

Review a small accounting workflow and invariants, then its logical relationships,
physical columns/constraints, transaction protocol and role matrix. Implement the
corresponding migration and PostgreSQL contract tests before application features.
Iterate per slice; do not predesign every future provider or report.

Use [the database contract](../contracts/database.md) as the design home. SQL is
the executable schema authority. Mermaid is a review aid; do not introduce DBML
or ORM models as competing schema authorities. OpenAPI later owns the HTTP boundary,
not internal table definitions.

## Limits

Migration manifests validate the submitted source bundle; they do not prove a
running database has that bundle. Before cloud deployment, implement a durable
release/checksum receipt and verify prior applied contents. `schema_migrations`
alone stores version/dirty state. No automatic `force`, drop, or production down
operation. Ordinary migration files use explicit transactions; nontransactional
DDL needs a separately reviewed migration and failure-recovery procedure.

## References

- [golang-migrate format](https://github.com/golang-migrate/migrate/blob/v4.20.1/MIGRATIONS.md)
- [Failure and locking](https://github.com/golang-migrate/migrate/blob/v4.20.1/FAQ.md)
- [sqlc](https://docs.sqlc.dev/)

documents.title: ADR 0004: Domain schemas and SQL ownership
documents.body:
# ADR 0004: Domain schemas and SQL ownership

## Decision and status

Accepted by owner for namespace/naming direction, 2026-10-11. Physical grants and
posting implementation below are proposed for JB-002 review. Keep application
objects out of `public`; schemas express responsibility, not individual LLCs.

| Schema | Responsibility | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ledger` | Entities, authorization membership, books, accounts, periods and journals | `ledger.journal_entry` |
| `banking` | Source accounts, observations and reconciliation | `banking.statement` |
| `reference` | Currency definitions and immutable rate observations | `reference.currency` |
| `audit` | Actor/action evidence | `audit.action` |
| `integration` | Idempotency receipts and outbox intent | `integration.operation_receipt` |
| `reporting` | Authorized derived reports | `reporting.trial_balance` |
| `deployment` | Bootstrap/migration metadata, inaccessible to application roles (#26) | `deployment.migration_artifact` |

Create a schema with its first implemented reviewed slice. Use lowercase
`snake_case`, singular table names, `<subject>_id` identifiers, `_date` for business
dates and `_at` for instants. Use schema-qualified references in SQL. Constraints
use `<table>_<purpose>_<pk|fk|uq|ck>`; indexes use `<table>_<purpose>_idx`.
Avoid quoted mixed-case identifiers, reserved `pg_` prefixes and redundant `tbl_`.
These names are project conventions, not ISO-prescribed field names.

## Ownership and evidence

Use shared domain tables with entity/book-scoped references. A schema per LLC
would multiply migrations and complicate cross-book reporting; separate databases
remain an option if future isolation or recovery requirements justify them.
Schemas alone do not enforce tenant security. See [SQL contract](../contracts/ledger-sql.md)
for the proposed role matrix and controlled write/read boundary.

PostgreSQL 17 [§5.10](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/ddl-schemas.html), reviewed
§§5.10.1–6, establishes namespace qualification, separate object/schema grants and
search-path trust. Inference: migration ownership plus restricted runtime roles
fits our single ledger authority. Reject runtime schema ownership and writable
untrusted search paths. Set grants explicitly rather than depending on database
creation/upgrade defaults. Review extension schema requirements separately.

Done when `TestSchemaPrivileges` proves no application objects in `public`, no
runtime DDL, no unchecked ledger DML and no function/search-path privilege escape.
This test is specified, not implemented. Owner/schema reviewer resolves grants
before the first product migration; revisit only for a concrete isolation need.

## Cloud SQL migration namespace — #26

The [Cloud SQL contract](../contracts/cloud-sql.md) adds deployment before product
migrations run. Owner bootstrap owns its schema; the restricted migrator owns its
artifact receipts and golang-migrate version table. This avoids public objects and
leaves merged product migrations unchanged. The tool-owned `schema_migrations`
name is an explicit exception to singular naming. `TestRestrictedMigration` and
`TestRuntimeReadiness` cover runtime denial; this is operational metadata, not an
ISO financial message or an additional ledger.

documents.title: ADR 0005: First development accounting policy
documents.body:
# ADR 0005: First development accounting policy

## Decision, owner and scope

Owner requested the proposed accrual/USD posting sequence on 2026-10-11. Adopt
`dev-accrual-usd-v1` as the concrete **synthetic development profile**, reviewed and
merged in #19. It is not a real LLC's approved reporting policy or tax election.
US GAAP is the intended research target; do not label these books GAAP-compliant.
ASC topic review and real-entity facts remain required before official use.

First workflow: a fictional service LLC receives owner capital, earns service
income, pays expenses, uses a card, transfers cash and records manual accruals and
corrections. Use AC-01–10 and a separate second LLC for isolation. The model and
posting interface retain foreign currency and support reviewed spot conversion;
full foreign receivable settlement/remeasurement follows its own contracts.

## Profile

| Decision | Selected development rule |
| --- | --- |
| Basis | Accrual; transaction recognition is a reviewed manual decision, not inferred from bank-feed dates |
| Functional currency | USD; source currency metadata is versioned, with EUR fixtures for foreign transactions |
| Calendar | UTC, explicit accounting date, Gregorian monthly half-open periods; January `[2026-01-01, 2026-02-01)` in the proof |
| Opening | Original AC-01 synthetic capital journal; no inferred live opening equity or imported personal data |
| Chart | Asset/liability/equity/revenue/expense; explicit normal side and monetary flag; original fixture accounts; no automated subledger controls yet |
| Precision | Storage amounts 38 digits/9 fractional; rates 38/18; USD functional posting scale 2; original amount must be an exact multiple of selected currency minor unit, no silent rounding |
| Rounding | Exact product, round once to functional scale using ties-to-even; SQL is authoritative; client functional amount is an assertion |
| Rate policy | `synthetic-reviewed-spot-v1`: immutable fixture observation, base transaction/quote USD, purpose spot, UTC effective date equals accounting date; source explicitly synthetic; no live provider/fallback/inversion |
| Corrections | Exact linked reversal into an open period; original values/rates preserved; no deletion or reversal-of-reversal |
| Closing | Closed periods reject new work; no user-facing close operation until close-evidence contract exists; test closed state through controlled fixture setup |
| Permissions | Separate read/prepare/post/close memberships; post does not imply read, prepare cannot post; setup belongs to controlled migration/test identity |

Amounts that round to zero, overflow, invalid minor-unit precision and any
functional mismatch fail. A journal must balance exactly after per-line rounding.
No automatic rounding plug or tolerance is enabled. USD 1.005 rounds to 1.00;
1.015 rounds to 1.02; 2.675 rounds to 2.68. These are conversion-result vectors,
not permission to post three-decimal USD original amounts. A genuine rounding
adjustment needs a separately reviewed operation; the generator's one-cent errors
must continue to fail.

## Evidence and alternatives

[P01–P04](../research/posting-sources.md) review accrual mechanics, PostgreSQL
rounding, restricted functions and JSON validation. These sources establish
mechanisms, not this policy's approval. Half-even, the same-day synthetic rate
restriction and the bounds are project choices. C04's IAS-21-derived examples
remain illustrations, not a substitute for ASC 830.

Cash basis is simpler for some workflows but would not exercise AC-10's accrual
and settlement separation. Integer minor units are viable but add currency-scale
handling to every conversion; bounded exact numeric keeps the selected model
explicit. Half-up is viable, but half-even makes tie behavior explicit and avoids
always rounding positive ties upward. Broader rate-provider rules are deferred
until provider coverage, timestamps and exception policies can be reviewed.

## Done when and follow-up

The [posting boundary and acceptance matrix](../contracts/posting-boundary.md)
define the next implementation gate. Tests must prove rounding, balance, replay,
isolation and authorization; a document does not implement them.

Keep #1 open for a named real entity, accounting timezone, complete opening
trial balance, accountant export/review and cutover acceptance. Tax basis,
revenue-recognition automation, annual closing, currency transitions and foreign
position accounting are not selected by this development profile. Profile changes
require a new policy revision; never reinterpret posted history.

documents.title: ADR 0006: Source-first account workspace
documents.body:
# ADR 0006: Source-first account workspace

## Status and question

Proposed for #238 review, 2026-10-21. The owner accepted the product direction:
connect accounts before creating books, import each provider transaction once under
its source account, review all authorized transactions, and organize accounting
into entity books. This ADR proposes the authority boundary. It does not approve
physical SQL, live-account ownership, intercompany policy or automatic posting.
Reviewers: owner for product/consent, identity and database owners for authority,
accounting owner/accountant for any future cross-entity posting treatment.

Question: how can a verified creator connect a Plaid Item containing accounts for
different entities, acquire available history before any book exists, and later
review/label/account for the observations without changing posted history?

## Decision proposed

1. A **private collection workspace** is scoped to a verified, explicitly enrolled
   principal. A Plaid Item, its credential reference, consent state, verified
   account inventory, filtered cursors and acquired observations belong to that
   workspace. Current identity is issuer+subject, never email, browser actor ID or
   Plaid account metadata. Sharing this collection with another principal is
   deferred until an explicit grant and revocation contract is reviewed.
2. Each institution account has a stable local source identity. Plaid account IDs
   and transaction IDs are external identifiers with recorded Item/environment and
   revision provenance; reconnect or ID churn cannot silently reuse an old cursor
   or duplicate posted evidence. Each provider identity is recorded once under
   its local source account, including before entity/book setup. New IDs after
   reconnect remain distinct held evidence until an explicit overlap/link
   review; no universal cross-Item transaction identity is assumed.
3. The source account's **legal owner** is a separate, explicit, effective-dated
   assertion with reviewer and evidence reference. Plaid type, mask, name and
   `holder_category` do not prove LLC ownership. Unknown ownership is an allowed
   review state, not a reason to invent a holding book. Owner assertion grants
   no source or book access and is not independent verification for a live account.
4. Each book belongs to one entity. A book's ledger account, period, journal,
   posting authority and reports retain that entity/book scope. Reviewed
   dispositions may link one source observation to accounting work in one or more
   books without moving or copying the observation. Once an owning book is
   created and approved, its account must remain reconcilable. Cross-entity
   entries require #244 and #1 policy, separate current permissions and balanced
   entries in each book; until then,
   mixed-entity items stay in an explicit review hold.
5. The workspace has **All Transactions** across its authorized source accounts,
   including unassigned history and provider pending/modified/removed states.
   Provider categories are inert source suggestions. Owner topics and strategies
   are versioned analytic labels. Owner-authored rules may propose topics and
   bookkeeping categories, but neither a provider category, rule nor model can
   draft or post automatically. A reviewer chooses book-specific accounting
   treatment; explicit posting remains the only journal mutation path.
6. Existing book-scoped Items, sources, observations, cursors and posted links
   remain valid and immutable. An existing Item is adopted through one audited
   transition of its current credential/consent authority, never by creating a
   second row with the same global provider/environment/Item identity. Until
   adoption succeeds, its legacy book-scoped path continues; a newly linked Item
   has distinct identity and requires overlap review before shared history is
   treated as one account. #239 must specify the additive physical migration and
   compatibility reads without journal or source-anchor rewrite. Credentials
   remain opaque references under the existing secret authority.

The detailed proposed authority matrix and acceptance cases are in
[source-first workspace](../contracts/source-first-workspace.md). This ADR does
not replace the currently implemented [connection SQL](../contracts/connection-sql.md)
or [provider sync SQL](../contracts/provider-sync-sql.md) until the new contract and
forward migration have been reviewed, implemented and proved.

## Evidence, interpretation and alternatives

| Source reviewed | Fact from source | Project inference / limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plaid [Transactions API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/), `/transactions/sync` request, pagination, response and readiness sections; public documentation reviewed 2026-10-21 | Sync returns Item changes through a cursor, supports depository/credit/loan accounts, requires pagination restart from the original cursor on a mutation, and can return empty arrays before history is ready. | Preserve complete-set, account-filtered cursor/revision evidence before book mapping; an empty first response cannot mean zero history. Provider documentation does not authorize posting or prove coverage. |
| Plaid [Accounts API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/), `/accounts/get` and `account_id` description; reviewed 2026-10-21 | One Item lists accounts; `account_id` can change after provider reconciliation failure or token recreation. | Use local source identity and explicit reconnect matching; name/mask/holder metadata cannot establish legal owner. |
| Plaid [Link API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/), `/link/token/create` `transactions.days_requested`; reviewed 2026-10-21 | Initial Transactions history request can specify days, default 90 and maximum 730; it cannot be changed after initialization. | Request up to 90 days by default for new Items, retain the configured value, and report actual coverage separately. Existing Items are not silently reset. |
| [PI01–PI13 source record](../research/plaid-ingestion-sources.md) | Records exact selected sections, prior source review, versions and access limits. | Reuse existing provider decoder/version decisions; no private payload or institution was inspected for this ADR. |
| [Database foundations](../research/database-foundations.md), S02/S03/S07–S12 | Imported bank facts and book adjustments are distinct; normalized design and current SQL authority require reviewed keys, constraints and isolation. | Keep a collection layer within the existing PostgreSQL database; #239 owns physical columns, grants and lock order. |
| [Current connection](../contracts/connection-sql.md) and [sync](../contracts/provider-sync-sql.md) contracts | The implemented Item/source/stream scope is one entity/book and current grants are checked on replay. | This is a material compatibility change. A frontend reorder cannot deliver it. |

Alternatives considered:

| Alternative | Why it is insufficient for the accepted journey |
| --- | --- |
| Create an automatic holding book before Link | Invents an accounting entity and produces misleading balances/permissions; later moves conflict with immutable posted history. |
| Bind each Item to one book and ask the user to reconnect for every LLC | Preserves current code but cannot organize multiple legal owners from one Item, and duplicates consent/reconnect work. |
| Keep only account metadata before book setup | Enables connect-first screens but does not deliver the accepted automatic history and All Transactions review before assignment. |
| Copy transactions into each target book | Loses one source identity and invites duplicate review/posting; cross-entity treatment must be linked, not copied. |

## Open policy and implementation boundaries

- #239 decides physical schema, restricted functions, retention/deletion and
  migration proof. No schema-per-LLC, extra database or event store is implied.
- #240 decides Link/reconnect and acquisition operation details under the reviewed
  contract. Initial 90-day request is a target, not guaranteed coverage.
- #241 decides legal owner attestation/review and book setup; assertion evidence
  required for live use remains unresolved.
- #242/#243 decide global query, taxonomy, private rule evaluation and model
  quality/privacy gates. A future model needs a separate reviewed data-use decision.
- #244 and #1 decide intercompany/owner accounting treatment. No posting route is
  authorized by this ADR. Reversal/correction remains explicit and posted journals
  remain immutable.

## Acceptance before promotion

Review the matrix and synthetic fixtures in the linked contract. Require
`TestConnectWithoutBook`, `TestOneItemTwoLegalOwners`,
`TestUnassignedHistoryNoJournal`, `TestCrossPrincipalDeny`,
`TestItemRevokeFencesAllAccounts`, `TestAccountRevokeKeepsSibling`,
`TestReconnectCursorIdentity`, `TestProviderRevisionPreservesPostedAnchor`,
`TestExistingBoundMigrationNoRewrite`, `TestTopicNeverPosts`, and
`TestCrossEntityHeldWithoutPolicy`. These are **planned names**, not passing tests.
Owner/identity/database review of this decision is the gate for #239; the existing
synthetic posting proof does not establish live bookkeeping approval.

documents.title: Delivery workflow
documents.body:
# Delivery workflow

## Ownership

GitHub Issue = executable task and discussion. PR = implementation and review.
Markdown = decisions/contracts/evidence. GitHub Actions run = build evidence.
Issue registry = stable links. No local task-status mirror.

## Start a slice

1. Use `make backlog` before publication, or GitHub Issues afterwards.
2. Inspect native blockers and their completion evidence. Missing or canceled
   blockers remain unresolved; do not infer readiness from a closed checkbox.
3. Run `make packet ID=JB-001` and read the linked current docs. The output is
   marked as a seed packet, never proof of live readiness.
4. Assign the issue and create `issue/<number>-short-description` in an isolated
   worktree. Add a brief claim comment; GitHub assignments are not distributed locks.
5. Define named tests and keep the issue bounded. Update its scope before coding
   if understanding changes.

## Review and completion

Each PR links its issue, relevant decision, stage runbook, exact verification and
migration/rollback implications. Run `make check test build` plus issue-specific
tests. A Go tooling build does not prove a ledger, migration or deployment.
Before committing, stage the branch's updated runbook and run
`bash scripts/check-stage-runbook.sh --staged`.
Review the `Seed / validate` workflow result initially (job context `validate`).
GitHub returned HTTP 403 for private branch protection on 2026-10-11: this
account needs Pro to enforce it. Until upgraded, the owner must review passing
checks before merge; this is a manual convention, not an enforced gate. Replace/extend it with product
unit, PostgreSQL integration, UI, migration and infrastructure checks as those
components appear. Validate branch protection capability before relying on it.

Complete only when acceptance evidence and review/merge are recorded. Closure
as not planned never satisfies a dependency. End sessions with outcome, branch,
commit/PR, checks, blockers and one next action in the issue and runbook.

## Publish the initial issues

`make issue-drafts` validates the graph and writes ignored `.local/issues/*.md`.
Review those bodies. Publication needs an explicit destination and authorization.
Search all open and closed issues for each `jayburd-seed:JB-...` marker before
creating; adopt the matching identity, never overwrite its body or reopen it.
Use `gh issue create --body-file` and native `--blocked-by` relationships.
Record only stable ID, number and URL in `planning/issues.json`.

The seed is an initial proposal, not an issue-sync engine. New work is authored
directly in GitHub using the issue form. Project boards are optional views.

documents.title: GCP build and deployment contract
documents.body:
# GCP build and deployment contract

## Status

The [foundation](gcp-foundation.md) was applied on 2026-10-12 to
`jayburd-bookkeeping-dev` (project number `9088794002`), with billing linked,
remote Terraform state and build federation configured. Live OIDC exchange and
application/database deployment remain unverified.
The [Cloud SQL slice](contracts/cloud-sql.md) adds unapplied database Terraform,
IAM connector configuration and restricted migration proofs. CI now checks the Go server, synthetic PostgreSQL
ledger and Next.js application. An API Dockerfile is available for local proof;
it has not been published or deployed. See [application evidence](runbooks/first-app.md).
The [image-delivery slice](contracts/image-delivery.md) adds owner-triggered candidate
publication; runtime identity configuration is implemented. The [rollout slice](contracts/cloud-run-rollout.md) adds reviewed digest promotion and separate runtime/migration state, without provisioning approval.
Delivery work is tracked by [epic #25](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/25).
The owner authorized foundation provisioning. Application auth configuration and
application/database apply scope remain separate provisioning gates. Do not report placeholder deployment success.

## Accepted synthetic deployment — 2026-10-11

Owner direction: retain transactional Go/PostgreSQL bookkeeping, use managed GCP
services and target **under $50/month** at low development usage. This target is
not a guaranteed cap. `us-central1` is the provisional region, not a deployed choice.

| Component | Selected development default |
| --- | --- |
| API and Next.js frontend | Cloud Run, request billing, min 0/max 2 instances each |
| Ledger | Cloud SQL PostgreSQL 17 Enterprise, `db-g1-small`, single zone, initial 10 GiB SSD |
| Directed background work | Cloud Tasks to one private Go HTTP consumer, OIDC service identity |
| Outbox publisher | Private bounded Cloud Run HTTP handler, Cloud Scheduler every minute |
| Publisher and consumer capacity | Min 0/max 1 instance each; queue limits and DB pools budgeted together |
| Secrets | Infisical scoped sync to Secret Manager; values never enter Terraform/Git |

Use the Cloud SQL Go connector with automatic IAM database authentication and
lazy refresh. Initial connectivity uses encrypted public-IP connector access
without authorized networks, a dedicated VPC connector or NAT; validate project
policy first. Separate IAM login identities from SQL privileges and prove managed
role compatibility. Include overlapping revisions and administrative reserve in
the connection budget. Test IAM login latency/recovery under shared-core CPU pressure
before accepting this tier. Require daily backups, PITR, bounded storage growth,
deletion protection and an isolated restore drill. This tier is not an HA promise.

Posting commits the whole journal and outbox intent atomically. The first consumer
checks a `journal.posted` fact against its immutable journal and records a durable
receipt; it never creates another posting. Define the versioned envelope, directed
command wrapper and ISO applicability before implementing #7. Public APIs remain
compatible. Preserve durable failures independently of queue retention.

No Kubernetes/self-hosted broker or Pub/Sub in this milestone. Reconsider Pub/Sub
when independent subscribers need the same event; reconsider Kubernetes only with
measured sustained usage or shared-capacity economics. Managed queues and request
billing fit intermittent development traffic; this is our inference, not a priced
benchmark. See the reviewed [GCP sources](research/gcp-sources.md).

Before provisioning, estimate all services, including identity, scheduler, storage,
backups, logging, images, network and the temporary restore instance. Configure
alerts/resource bounds and review actual spend after seven days. Owner-supplied
project, billing and auth configuration cannot be inferred from another project.

## Delivery slices and evidence

GitHub owns current status and native dependencies; this table is a navigation map.
The [delivery runbook](runbooks/gcp-delivery.md) records review and release evidence.

| Issue | Owned outcome |
| --- | --- |
| [#5](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/5) | Terraform foundation, IAM, cost and promotion boundary |
| [#26](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/26) | Cloud SQL, migrations, pool limits and restore |
| [#27](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/27) | Authenticated application deployment and compatible rollback |
| [#7](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/7) | Outbox lifecycle and directed consumer proof |
| [#11](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/11) | Infisical isolation, rotation and sync recovery |
| [#12](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/12) | 1,000 synthetic postings, delivery faults, restore and seven-day spend |

Infrastructure preparation and local outbox work can proceed independently after
their existing prerequisites are evidenced. Database follows foundation;
application acceptance requires database, identity and secrets evidence. Final
cloud acceptance requires merged PR #23 recovery and PR #24 synthetic capabilities,
without deploying their test identity adapters. Inspect current PR state first.

The early infrastructure proof no longer depends on a full accounting month #10.
Live-pilot #13 still requires #10 and #12. Older open issues are not automatically
completed by this planning change. No bank integration, accountant approval or
live-bookkeeping readiness follows from synthetic cloud success.

## Build once, promote by digest

PR: credential-free tests, real disposable PostgreSQL integration tests, UI
checks, migration tests and Terraform validation as components become available.
Main: build tested component images once, scan, publish to Artifact Registry,
record commit and image digests, provenance and dependency inventory.
Deployment: promote exact digests, migrate through a dedicated identity, verify
health/authorization, then record the revision and reviewed evidence.

## Infrastructure boundary

Terraform owns infrastructure and configured service/job revisions; workflows
invoke it rather than independently changing the same fields with gcloud.
Separate bootstrap/foundation and application state. Bootstrap must establish
the restricted remote state bucket and GitHub federation before workflows can
use them: there is an explicit owner-operated first step, not circular automation.
Infrastructure plans/state may contain sensitive data; never publish them in
Issues or agent context. Owner review and approved apply happen in the deployment
boundary. Use minimal metadata receipts for project context.

## Application secrets

Follow [Infisical delivery](infisical.md): scoped sync to GCP Secret Manager,
runtime service-account access, no values in Terraform or build workflows.
JB-013 must pass before the synthetic deployment milestone.

## Access and operations

- Restrict OIDC trust to repository identity and approved branch/environment;
  fork PRs receive no cloud credentials. No `pull_request_target` code execution.
- Separate deployer, migrator, API, publisher and worker identities. Runtime
  database roles cannot perform migrations or bypass entity authorization.
- Cloud Run API/workers remain private until an explicit user-authenticated
  ingress contract exists. No public demo shares real ledger data or credentials.
- Cloud SQL backups/PITR, restore drills, deletion protection and bounded
  connection pools; workload max instances respect the total connection budget.
- Redacted structured logs, task/operation IDs, freshness/backlog alerts, budget
  alerts, failure quarantine and separate development/production targets.
- Serialize deployments per environment. Use expand/contract migrations;
  application rollback does not mean automatically reversing database changes.

## GitHub protection caveat

Private branch protection returned HTTP 403 on 2026-10-11 (Pro upgrade required).
Verify environment/reviewer capabilities separately before cloud releases.

documents.title: GCP foundation ownership and operations
documents.body:
# GCP foundation ownership and operations

## Decision

The development foundation was applied with owner authorization on 2026-10-12.
Terraform state was migrated to its private GCS backend. Build federation is
enabled for the merged owner-triggered, main-only image workflow; GitHub still has
no Terraform apply permission. Application/database deployment and live OIDC
exchange remain unverified. See the [evidence ledger](runbooks/gcp-delivery.md).

[Bootstrap instructions](../infra/gcp/foundation/README.md) own the exact commands.
The [delivery contract](gcp-delivery.md) owns the selected architecture.

## Applied bootstrap identity and state boundary

| Identity | Granted in this slice | Later owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Owner bootstrap | Existing separately supplied administrative authority; not minted here | Owner applies foundation and privately reviews state/plans |
| Builder | Writer on only the development image repository; narrowly scoped WIF impersonation, enabled for development | #27 builds/scans/promotes digests; no state, runtime impersonation or secrets |
| Deployer | Object admin on only application-state bucket; no WIF or cloud deployment rights | #27 adds minimum resource roles and a reviewed promotion gate |
| Migrator | Account only | #26 owns DDL role and bounded migration invocation |
| API, frontend | Separate accounts only | #26/#27 own database/connectivity and ingress privileges |
| Publisher, consumer | Separate accounts only | #7 owns task enqueue/handling and SQL receipt rights |
| Scheduler, task-invoker | Separate accounts only | #7 scopes invoke/token permissions to the specific handlers |

The table records the initial applied bootstrap. New, unapplied #27 source moves
deployer state access to a third runtime bucket and adds separately disabled
deployment federation; the [rollout contract](contracts/cloud-run-rollout.md) owns
its permissions and promotion gate. Foundation state has no application-deployer grant. Both buckets enforce uniform
access, public-access prevention, versioning and Terraform deletion guards. These grants
do not erase inherited owner/org permissions; verify effective IAM before apply.
Infisical impersonation/secret containers and values stay in #11; this foundation
creates no unused secret or machine credential.

## Promotion and recovery

Private main protection returned HTTP 403 on 2026-10-11; environments list was empty.
Neither a workflow label nor a manual convention is an enforced approval. Before
#27 enables publishing, owner reviews passing checks and initiates the exact main
workflow. Provider checks actor, immutable repository/owner IDs, event, ref and
workflow path. This limits build authority; repository administrators remain trusted.
No automatic apply or deployment follows a push, merge or issue label.

Only Terraform may own configured runtime revisions. #27 must serialize each dev
migration/deployment, accept an already scanned digest, stop on migration/readiness/
auth failure and roll back only to a schema-compatible digest. Runtime DDL is denied;
failed migrations never trigger force/automatic down. Retain last known good tagged
images; cleanup deletes only untagged images older than seven days.

On federation incident, owner disables pool/provider before reviewing trust;
already-issued access tokens can remain valid until expiry. Revoke scoped grants
where immediate containment is required. For state loss, owner restores a version
privately and verifies it against resources; never delete buckets or force-unlock
without identifying the lock owner. Default tests cannot exercise these cloud paths.

## Capacity, costs and acceptance inputs

Initial proposed DB pool budget for #26: API 5 per instance, publisher 2, consumer 2;
maxima 2/1/1 give 14 connections. Allow a second revision of each (28), two migrator
and 5 administrative connections: 35 total (migration lock plus execution). Verify the actual server connection limit
and load behavior; frontend has no SQL pool. This is a proposal for #26, not an
implemented pool setting or permission to exhaust the server.

Development recovery objectives proposed for owner acceptance: restore within four
hours and lose at most 24 hours of synthetic work through the backup path; PITR is
additionally tested. One-minute publisher activation is a schedule, not a delivery
SLA; measure enqueue/completion latency and investigate oldest pending work above
five minutes. No live-bookkeeping recovery objective is inferred from these defaults.

Budget alerts at 50%, 80% and 100% of USD 50 exclude credits and apply to the selected
project. They notify default billing recipients; owner must verify those recipients
and delivery in the cloud proof. Alerts never enforce a spend cap.

Reviewed Iowa SQL rates give an illustrative 730-hour baseline: db-g1-small at
$0.035/hour = $25.55; 10 GiB SSD at $0.000232877/GiB-hour = about $1.70;
10 GiB of used backup storage at $0.000109589/GiB-hour = about $0.80.
That subtotal is $28.05 before PITR growth, restore resources and other services.
Shared-core instances have no Cloud SQL SLA. See G10 in the
[source register](research/gcp-sources.md).

Planning envelope (not a quote): reserve $30 for database compute/initial storage,
$5 for backups/PITR and restore testing, $5 for application/publisher/consumer compute,
$1 for scheduler/tasks, $3 for state/artifacts/logging and $3 for authentication/secrets/
networking, leaving $3 contingency. These are allocation limits, not verified SKU
estimates. Require a regional calculator estimate before apply; do not assume free
allowances are unused across this billing account. Bank subscriptions are excluded.
Observed seven-day spend, synthetic restore timing, backlog latency and the 1,000-post
proof belong to #12. Project and billing metadata are now established and #5 is closed in GitHub.
Application auth, actual trust-denial tests, cost measurements and recovery
acceptance remain separate cloud evidence gates.

## Acquisition bootstrap state

The hosted acquisition slice adds a fourth private versioned state bucket,
`PROJECT-jayburd-dev-workers-state`, for the owner-operated workers root. The
application deployer's existing runtime-state grant does not cover it. Apply the
reviewed foundation addition before installing that backend; a prefix in the shared
runtime bucket is not a substitute for IAM separation. Mocked tests verify the
configuration; this change has not provisioned the bucket. See the
[hosted platform boundary](contracts/hosted-platform.md).

documents.title: Infisical setup and delivery
documents.body:
# Infisical setup and delivery

## Decision

Infisical owns application secrets. Target delivery is a scoped, one-way sync to
GCP Secret Manager; Cloud Run reads selected versions through its service account.
GitHub deploys through GCP workload identity and need not read application secrets.
This keeps Infisical availability out of each application startup. Sync freshness,
rotation and rollback must be proved before live use (JB-013).

## Seed now

Create an empty Secret Management project named `jayburd-bookkeeping` in the
owner's Infisical organization. Record its actual ID, generated slug and cloud
region after creation. GitHub-linked login authenticates the human, not workflows.

Create environments `dev`, `staging`, `prod`, with component folders `/api`,
`/bank-sync`, `/import-export`. Owner override (2026-10-14): existing Plaid keys remain at root.
The [allowlisted delivery contract](contracts/scoped-delivery.md) maps only the
two selected root keys; do not enable a root-wide native sync.
Use owner-only access initially. Runtime access is read-only per component and
environment. If the account cannot enforce this scope, split projects; do not
compensate with broad access. Confirm plan capabilities before enabling identities.

Current setup and resource-adoption evidence is in the
[delivery runbook](runbooks/scoped-delivery.md). The GCP connection worked per owner
report; secret propagation is not yet qualified. Repository is now public.
Native sync is blocked by its upstream destination-read requirements.

## Cloud integration: JB-005 and JB-013

Historical native-sync candidate: Infisical Cloud's GCP service-account impersonation connection, with a dedicated
sync service account per environment. Resolve the region-specific Infisical
principal from official setup instructions; grant impersonation only on that
account. Respect the documented organization-ID suffix for its name. Review exact
sync permissions against pre-created destination secrets; never grant project
Owner or distribute service-account keys. Terraform owns containers/IAM, while
Infisical owns values and versions. No secret values in Terraform inputs/state.

Native sync remains disabled. The following are historical qualification requirements,
not instructions to enable the incompatible native adapter. Scope each sync to one
component folder and environment. Use a unique destination
prefix such as `jayburd-dev-api-`; configure manual initial sync and disable
destination deletion. Review the initial-sync behavior before enabling it: the
overwrite option can delete unrelated destination secrets. Never import existing
unrelated GCP secrets. After a synthetic canary proof, define freshness alerts and
controlled rotation, version selection, revocation and recovery procedures.

Cloud Run gets access only to its required destination secrets. A compromised
bank-sync worker must not read another component or production environment.
Direct Infisical GCP ID Token Auth is an alternative only through a reviewed
decision; do not implement both delivery paths by default.

## Optional future GitHub access

Seed CI has no Infisical access or OIDC permission. If a later job truly needs
Infisical, use a separate read-only machine identity and OIDC, remove default
Universal Auth, set TTL/max TTL to 900 seconds and grant only that job access.
Verified repository trust metadata (2026-10-11):

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Issuer/discovery | `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com` |
| Repository ID | `1414515318` |
| Owner ID | `55423093` |
| Subject prefix | `repo:justin-napolitano@55423093/jayburd-bookkeeping@1414515318` |
| Main-only subject suffix | `:ref:refs/heads/main` |
| Environment subject suffix | `:environment:dev` (only for a job using that environment) |
| Audience | `https://github.com/justin-napolitano` (request and validate exactly) |

Require exact repository/owner IDs and `ref=refs/heads/main` claims alongside the
selected subject. No wildcard trust or fork/PR access. Environment protection
must actually be available before relying on it. Never print JWTs to debug claims.

## Verification and sources

JB-013 requires synthetic allow/deny, cross-environment denial, rotation/revocation,
sync-failure recovery and redacted receipts. Owner enters values separately; agents
receive names and PASS/FAIL evidence only. Default local and PR checks stay offline.

- [GCP impersonation connection](https://infisical.com/docs/integrations/app-connections/gcp)
- [GCP sync options](https://infisical.com/docs/integrations/secret-syncs/gcp-secret-manager)
- [GitHub OIDC and immutable subjects](https://infisical.com/docs/documentation/platform/identities/oidc-auth/github)

## Per-account bank tokens

Owner selected [encrypted PostgreSQL persistence](contracts/bank-token-vault.md)
under #162–#164. New API/worker binaries use Cloud KMS envelopes in the database,
not dynamic Infisical keys or delivery slots. Infisical still owns static Plaid
client credentials; their existing controlled delivery remains separate.

The [legacy provider vault](contracts/provider-vault.md) and its eight-slot pool
are retained only for history and explicit legacy recovery, with no automatic
fallback, import or resource deletion. Existing legacy release identifier fields
remain validated for schemaVersion2 compatibility but do not select a dynamic
writer in the new binaries. Retiring these fields requires a versioned release
contract change. Do not paste tokens into SQL or create slot placeholders.
