documents.body:
# Multi-account connection plan

## Goal

Allow the owner to repeat the Plaid Sandbox enrollment and bind all three selected
depository accounts in one reviewed action. Each provider account gets a distinct
ledger and source account. No automatic journal or opening balance is created.

## Delivery sequence

1. **Freeze the contract.** Merge the request shape, account classification,
   Plaid type/subtype support profile, atomicity, retry and standards decision in
   `docs/contracts/automatic-account-binding.md`. The initial allowlist is
   depository `checking`, `savings`, `money market` and `cash management`.
2. **Add migration 22.** Extend the restricted binding function so optional
   reviewed ledger-account definitions are validated and inserted before source
   bindings in the same serializable transaction. Add forward, replay, rollback,
   role, conflict and failure-atomicity evidence.
3. **Extend service and HTTP models.** Add the optional account definition and
   bounded provider subtype. Validate the allowlist on the server and regenerate
   OpenAPI types. Preserve token redaction, current permission checks and the
   existing endpoint.
4. **Make review usable.** Default every eligible depository account to a distinct
   new account proposal, show editable code/name/date/currency, and retain choices
   for existing account or do-not-bind. Explain unsupported credit/loan accounts
   with a link to #210's policy boundary.
5. **Prove the boundary.** Add focused Go/SQL/UI tests and a browser→API→PostgreSQL
   journey for three accounts, lost acknowledgement, no duplicates, no partial
   setup and zero automatic journals.
6. **Review and release.** Run repository gates, merge through a linked PR, stage
   migration before runtime, deploy reviewed images, then repeat the owner-driven
   Sandbox enrollment. Hosted success updates #88 but does not approve live use.

## Scope controls

- #209 owns depository auto-creation only.
- #210 owns credit and loan liability mapping after policy review.
- `cd`, `ebt`, `hsa`, `limited purpose checking`, `paypal` and `prepaid` remain
  unbound pending explicit policy; investment, other and payroll are out of scope.
- Existing bindings and one-account enrollment remain compatible.
- No source-provider call or cloud mutation occurs during implementation/testing.
- No credential, provider payload, balance or personal financial record enters
  commits, issues, test fixtures or logs.

## Done

The feature is done when all #209 acceptance tests pass, the migration and runtime
are deployed in order, and a fresh Sandbox attempt binds all selected supported
accounts as distinct active streams. Transaction acquisition/review is separate
evidence; provider success alone is not complete-history or bookkeeping approval.

# Bookkeeping delivery and qualification plan

Planning snapshot 2026-10-24; parent [#50](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/50),
agent registry [#65][i65].
GitHub owns current status, blockers and leases. This document owns delivery
sequence and acceptance boundaries; it does not dispatch agents or authorize releases.

Owner clarification2026-10-25: read-only refers to bank access, not a blanket
ledger posting ban. The [source-driven bookkeeping plan](source-driven-bookkeeping.md)
tracks initial registration separately from reviewed rules/immutable corrections
under #332–#336. #337 retains the unresolved actual Production deployment/pilot
decision. No old source-consent or release approval is renewed by this change.

## Starting evidence

Owner activated the one-account goal on2026-10-24. Immediate source fixes merged:
[PR307](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/pull/307)
expiry availability (main74dd4b1),
[PR309](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/pull/309)
auth loading/retry (a702fa0), and
[PR310](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/pull/310)
read-only detail preservation (5f803c8). Each cleared five exact-head CI checks.
These source fixes have not been deployed/accepted in the managed browser; their
issues retain that hosted boundary. Later rows describe their outcomes, not a
request to reimplement the merged patches.

The [actual Tartan run](../runbooks/tartan-browser-qualification.md) registered
nine supported sources, opened nine inboxes with 46 visible rows and completed
one savings repeat at demand 2/2 with six rows unchanged. Cards, student,
mortgage and auto transaction bindings were included. Five other discovered
types remained explicitly unbound. These observations do not qualify every
account type, the Liabilities product, a complete ninety-day interval, exact
financial equality or zero automatic journals. Do not fabricate bindings for
unsupported types; adding each type requires a reviewed accounting/data contract,
currency/permission/replay fixtures and a bounded child of [#104][i104]/#70.

Migration31 and verifier SQL bootstrap are accepted; the app recovery release
works with finite configuration. [#281][i281] still owns durable availability after
optional consent expires. The observed source-consent end is 2026-10-24T23:00Z;
recheck authority before any later provider action. There is no renewal in this plan.

Current-period transaction details and category forms load. Existing test books
lack expense/revenue accounts, so no legitimate expense draft or posting was
submitted. Earlier-period detail can disappear after category lookup failure.
No successful hosted category/post/report loop or independent four-row verifier
result is claimed. Dashboard metadata reported **Production approved**; [#274][i274]
still owns app-specific applicability, and runtime remains Sandbox. Do not submit
another Production request merely because internal qualification remains open.

Some foundations already exist: `TestGoldenMonth`,
`TestFinancialReportsGoldenMonth`, `TestSpotReversalHistoricalProvenance`,
`TestReversalOfReversalDenied` and browser `TestSyncReviewPostJourney`.
Open issues require clause-by-clause evidence reconciliation before deciding
which tests/features are actually missing. A test name, closed predecessor or
successful deployment cannot substitute for the exact acceptance case.

## Outcomes and order

1. Make the current book-based workflow usable and resilient; add legitimate
   accounts and prove an explicit synthetic category-to-report loop.
2. Deliver the already agreed connect-first architecture: private account/history
   registration before books, All Transactions, topics/strategies and reviewed
   organization into entity books. Source identity stays stable.
3. Complete applicable Plaid, privacy, security and recovery qualification with
   independent expectations and truthful evidence. Run independent lanes alongside
   product work where paths and authority do not overlap.
4. After the live gate and a concrete owner grant, qualify one bank-read-only account
   with legitimate scoped bookkeeping and source-to-statement reconciliation.
   Official books require additional reconciliation, accounting and cutover gates.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C296[296 Chart contract] --> C297[297 SQL and Go]
  C297 --> C298[298 Chart UI]
  C298 --> C301[301 Hosted bookkeeping loop]
  C293[293 Detail repair] --> C301
  S238[238 Source authority] --> S239[239 Private registry]
  S239 --> S240[240 Bookless acquisition]
  S240 --> S241[241 Entity organization]
  S239 --> S304[304 Query and topics API]
  S304 --> S305[305 All Transactions UI]
  S305 --> S243[243 Private suggestions]
  V299[299 Private verifier input] --> V300[300 Independent hosted proof]
  W302[302 Webhook deployment] --> W303[303 Signed hosted delivery]
```

This diagram shows selected critical chains; the tables and native GitHub
relationships include additional review and integration gates.

### A. Immediate product repairs and a complete fictional workflow

Relative estimates below are Fibonacci sizes, not time promises. H/M/L denote
confidence in scope. READY means eligible for a bounded claim after a fresh
GitHub/path check; it does not mean a lease exists.

| Issue | Bounded delivery and acceptance | Dependency / readiness | Size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [#281][i281] | Expired optional enrollment authority disables only unauthorized capabilities; baseline identity, ledger and recoverable commands remain available. Injected-clock before/at/after/restart, malformed-config fail-closed and real synthetic full-stack recovery. Never extend consent implicitly. | READY; review capability contract before code | 5 M |
| [#289][i289] | Distinct auth-config loading, retryable failure and invalid configuration; delayed success/retry/abort/logout tests, verified MFA and memory-only session preserved. | READY; separate auth files | 3 H |
| [#291][i291] | GET failure means read unavailable; POST unknown result retains same-command reconciliation. Test unavailable pending discovery never enables new mutations. | READY; owns API error mapping, coordinate UI consumers | 3 M |
| [#293][i293] | Preserve authorized detail when non-auth category lookup fails; lock draft with reason. Clear sensitive state on denial/book/session change, reject stale responses; investigate earlier-period cause. | READY; ReviewInbox exclusive | 3 M |
| [#290](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/290) | Recognizable institution/account labels, distinguish duplicate cards, missing labels and discovered/unbound types. Minimize metadata under reviewed privacy/API rules. | Design READY; no implicit metadata/DDL expansion | 3 M |
| [#226][i226] | History coverage versus book period versus posting date; historical review remains readable, posting obeys policy. Bound larger-window capacity, no truncation/cursor loss. | Audit [#225][i225] evidence first; serialize ReviewInbox work with [#293][i293] | 5 M |
| [#294](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/294) / [#296][i296] | Reviewed account-add authority, account classes/normal sides, currencies, concurrency, command recovery and independent examples. | Contract READY; real chart policy stays [#1][i1] | 3 M |
| [#297][i297] | Restricted SQL/Go reviewed account addition, stable replay, audit and zero journals from chart changes. | Hard blocked [#296][i296]; sole SQL writer | 5 M |
| [#298][i298] | Accounts and review entry points; review/register/execute/acknowledge account addition; refresh categories, keyboard/mobile and lost-response recovery. | Mocks after [#296][i296]; integration after [#297][i297]; serialize [#293][i293] | 5 M |
| [#301](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/301) / [#104][i104] | Source -> legitimate category -> balanced reviewed draft -> explicit post -> acknowledgement -> source/journal/GL/trial/P&L/balance sheet. Independent expectations, dropped committed reply yields exactly one effect. | After [#298][i298] and [#293][i293]; audit [#84][i84] / existing journey first | 5 M |
| [#84][i84] | Statement-to-ledger golden month, independent expected money/counts, two entities, fees/refunds/transfers/duplicates/timing and mutation probes. | Existing corpus/report tests are inputs; identify missing import/reconciliation proof | 5 M |
| [#10][i10] / [#51][i51] / [#53](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/53) | Reconcile full fictional interval; adjustment/close/correction contract and reviewed exports tied to immutable journals. | Audit shipped reports; design close before implementation; [#1][i1]/#2 policy for official use | 8 L |

The hosted loop explicitly posts only fictional reviewed work. Keep it separate
from [#300][i300], whose oracle requires zero journals. [#1][i1] does not prevent
synthetic UI repairs under the existing development policy; it does prevent
assuming that development policy approves real entity books.

### B. Connect first, review everything, organize later

Retain [#237](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/237)
as this epic. Its proposed [decision](../decisions/0006-source-first-workspace.md)
and [authority contract](../contracts/source-first-workspace.md) remain subject
to [#238][i238] review; this plan does not silently accept their material policy choices.

| Issue | Delivery / named evidence | Hard integration gates | Size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [#238][i238] | Principal-private Item/account/observation ownership; legal-owner effective dates, disposition/grants/revocation/retention and existing-bound-Item migration. API/SQL authority matrix and fixed two-LLC/mixed-use/denied/reconnect/correction fixtures. | Contract review before implementation; accounting policy only where applicable | 5 M |
| [#239][i239] | Private pre-book registry; duplicate/revision/revoke/reconnect/migration and no-journal tests. No fake holding book. | [#238][i238]; sole SQL writer | 8 L |
| [#240](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/240) | Verified bookless Link, one exchange, recoverable completion, automatic available history and incremental acquisition; truthful loading/coverage. No book required and no journal from acquisition. | [#238][i238] then [#239][i239] integration; existing [#187](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/187)/#156/#164/#225 evidence reused | 8 L |
| [#241][i241] | Legal ownership and versioned source-to-book dispositions; create/select books during organization, immutable source identity and explicit correction after posting. | [#238][i238]/#239/#240; SQL writer serialized. Cross-entity posting additionally [#244][i244]/#1; explicit review hold may ship earlier | 8 L |
| [#242](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/242) / [#304][i304] | Scoped All Transactions queries, bounded filters/pagination and versioned topic hierarchy/atomic bulk labels; 3,000 rows, principal denial, stale revision and posted-retag immutability. | [#238][i238]/#239, reviewed API/SQL; sole SQL writer | 8 L |
| [#305](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/305) | Pre-book and assigned history, topic/strategy filters, bulk-label review and source/disposition/journal provenance; keyboard/mobile, denied/empty/error/loading and 3,000-row pagination. | Wire mocks after reviewed contract; integration [#304][i304] | 8 L |
| [#243](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/243) | Attributed provider labels plus owner-private versioned rules and suggestions, override/abstention/provenance. No suggestion posts; private scope/stale-version/override tests. | [#238][i238]/#242; future learned model requires separate reviewed privacy/evaluation decision and independently labeled synthetic corpus | 5 L |
| [#244][i244] | Cross-entity allocation/intercompany policy alternatives, both-book authority, exact original/functional-currency examples, correction/replay and separate balanced books. | [#238][i238] then explicit owner/accountant [#1][i1] acceptance before adopting posting treatment | 5 L |
| [#246][i246] | Fixture-only connect-first prototype with source inventory, topics/strategies/suggestion provenance and book handoff; desktop/mobile/keyboard. | Independent of production SQL; design input only | 3 M |

Provider category, topic/strategy, suggestion, reviewed ledger category and posted
journal are distinct states. Organizing into entities must never move a posted
journal or duplicate a source observation. Same-entity progress need not wait for
cross-entity accounting policy; unsupported dispositions stay explicitly held.

Keep [#247][i247] as the focused Position/Ledger parent. Audit [#248](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/248)/#249 delivered
contracts/screens against their remaining acceptance before changing code. [#250](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/250)
direct Ledger and [#255](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/255) Investigate consume authoritative read models/statuses;
they must not invent attention metrics or add unposted transactions to balances.
Scope these as separate 3–5 point claims after their contracts, with coordinator
ownership of navigation. [#251](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/251) available-to-use remains proposed planning work,
not required to fix bookkeeping or prove the bank-read-only pilot. [#59](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/59) consolidation
and advanced FX are deferred; ordinary multicurrency accounting remains required.

### C. Plaid qualification and security

The [#88 matrix](plaid-88-test-matrix.md) remains the canonical test inventory.
For every row record PASS/PARTIAL/OPEN/BLOCKED/N/A with rationale, exact source,
fixture and independent expected outcome, command/action, runtime when relevant,
redacted result and defect issue. Nothing becomes PASS merely by being planned.

| Owner issue | Remaining bounded stages | Blocking evidence / size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#272](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/272) / [#299][i299] | Review private identity-only pipe/bridge; immutable authored expected financial fields, strict tags/scopes, no verifier raw-evidence/bank-secret access. Synthetic transport/cleanup proof first. | READY design; migration31 not reapplied; 5 L |
| [#300][i300] | Separate controlled four-row single-checking case; <=60-minute hash/scope-pinned mandate, one task/retries0, exact equality and zero journals/outbox, revoke/delete exact inputs/remove idle job. | [#299][i299] plus fresh finite owner/cloud/provider scope; 3 L |
| [#271][i271] / [#302][i302] | Exact-image isolated HTTPS receiver, actual restricted SQL/workload identity and caller/ingress/least-privilege verification; release/rollback receipt. | Preparation READY; actual release needs concrete reviewed scope; 5 L |
| [#303](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/303) | Real signed delivery -> durable demand -> task/worker -> publication, duplicates/reordering/missed-event cases and no journals. | [#302][i302]; exact W01–W07 dispositions, [#89](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/89) for broad faults; 5 L |
| [#275][i275] | First bounded claim: modern session-proof contract and negative fixtures. Next separate implementation claim: owned SQL/Go association, retained token hash/attempt/Item generation, dedup and fenced repair. Then UI integration and actual reset_login/revoked/reduced-scope/lost-tab cases. Never use a second public-token exchange as reconnect proof. | Relevant [#271][i271] signed path before hosted repair. No current migration reservation; contract 3 M, implementation 8 L, hosted proof 3 L |
| [#276](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/276) | Desktop OAuth then real iOS/Android mobile web installed/absent cases where applicable; return/cancel/expired/revoked/wrong-target/update-mode recovery, exact device/browser evidence. | Owned reconnect [#275][i275] for repair; owner device/login handoff. Viewport emulation is not physical-device proof; 5 L |
| [#274][i274] | Map actual Launch Center app/products/country/platform/registration requirements to every [#88][i88] row; explicit NEW_ACCOUNTS_AVAILABLE applicability. Record exclusions and owner attestations, not settings changes. | Read-only authenticated review; no new Production request implied; 3 M |
| [#85][i85]/#86/#87/#94 | Clause-level audit of sync lifecycle/fuzz/exact-money/isolation/signature/replay proofs; add only named missing cases with independent expectations. | Synthetic gaps READY after inventory; hosted cases stay distinct; 3–5 M per bounded gap |
| [#88][i88]/#104/#187 | Duplicate Item/account detection versus same-attempt replay; hosted exit/expiry/lost response, actual supported types, pending->posted/removal/pagination mutation/oversize/partial history, consent/revoke/retention evidence. | Each matrix row owns its fixture and scoped follow-up; L06 pass is narrow, R02/R03 remain open |

Before closing [#88][i88], coordinator audits **every** matrix row against linked
evidence, including supplemental persona fixtures and explicit N/A rationale.
If an acceptance row has no bounded existing owner, create a child under [#88][i88]
before dispatch; do not hide an unowned test in a checklist. Refresh cited
official sections before source-dependent design. Existing source records
[P88-01–17](../research/plaid-88-test-sources.md),
[Link recovery](../research/plaid-link-recovery-sources.md) and
[webhook release](../research/webhook-release-sources.md) record reviewed depth
and access limits; they are not a claim of current exhaustive documentation review.

### D. Operations, controlled personal accounts and official books

The source audit confirmed a previously implicit hard prerequisite: enrollment,
sync contexts, credential AAD/SQL and signed webhook validation are Sandbox-only.
Dashboard approval does not implement Production. The
[profile proposal PR317](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/pull/317)
records fresh source review, deployment alternatives and pending owner/security
decisions. [#308](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/308)
and native #90 children/blockers
[#311](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/311)
(SQL), [#312](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/312)
(transport), [#313](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/313)
(credential/runtime), [#314](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/314)
(webhook), [#315](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/315)
(independent synthetic integration) and
[#316](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/316)
(finite release preparation) own this work. All remain subject to accepted
contracts and exact leases; no new migration number or cloud target is reserved.
Never switch credentials/URL or relabel Sandbox/synthetic records to evade these
fences. Actual account/platform/interval/cost/retention scope remains pending.

| Issue group | Plan and exit evidence | Gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#64](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/64)/#89 | Owner accepts workload/cost/SLO/RTO/RPO targets. Synthetic 1k/10k/100k events, 1/10/100 books, 1/2/4/8 workers; measure latency/throughput/resources, independent effects and noisy-neighbor bounds. Isolated restore, queue/cursor replay and fault recovery; exact cleanup. | Harness/audit READY; hosted soak needs budget/duration/scope. Proposed efficiency/latency numbers are not accepted SLOs. 5–8 L per bounded run |
| [#62](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/62)/#56/#11/#164/#174/#154 | Audit actual MFA/current permission/revocation, secrets/KMS/federation/canonical-origin and retention/deletion/audit evidence. Reconcile shipped implementation with remaining operator setup; no secret/env/state reads. | Separate exact-path defects/receipts, human review of sensitive authority changes; 3–5 M per gap |
| [#58][i58]/#13 | Support incident contact, pause/revoke/rollback/restore playbooks, costs, retention, reconciliation and official-bookkeeping go/no-go. | Accepted targets and isolated recovery evidence; never overwrite a real ledger to test restore |
| [#90][i90] | One explicitly authorized bank-read-only personal account: no money movement; internal journals/corrections under scoped permission/policy. Exact owner/entity/source/purpose/duration/audience/retention/budget/kill switch. Complete opening/closing statement reconciliation and explained discrepancies; disconnect/revoke/reconnect/delay recovery. | Existing [#90][i90] prerequisites remain: correctness/security/Sandbox/scale, [#1][i1], [#10][i10], [#27](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/27) and privacy approval; actual deployment decision337. Owner privately supplies records/credentials; agent evidence only redacted outcomes. Full rule engine is not a registration prerequisite. 5 L |
| [#1][i1]/#2/#54/#60/#67/#17 | Owner/accountant basis/jurisdiction, entities, functional currencies, dates, opening balances, chart/loan principal-interest/card-payment/FX/rounding/correction policy. Audit existing invariant/reversal/corpus proofs; add independently expected gaps only. | Development policy supports synthetic work; real books/cross-entity treatment need explicit accepted policy |
| [#10][i10]/#51/#53/#13 | Full fictional month reconciliation/adjustment/close/correction plus reviewed traceable export, then limited real cutover plan. | Never mount deferred close route or call reports/accountant approval complete from builds |

## Foundation issue reconciliation

The roadmap covers remaining outcome work, not a rewrite of every open legacy
issue. No issue is closed by this planning change. At the next relevant claim,
compare each criterion to merged SHA, source contract and named evidence; split
a newly discovered gap and link it back. Keep canceled/missing predecessors
unresolved until explicitly dispositioned. These ownership groups prevent older
open issues disappearing from the plan:

Under #50/#132, review outstanding release/dependency PRs against current main
and their original authority before any merge. In particular, PR283's finite
renewal is not current release authority after the later app recovery; never
merge an expired approval just to clear the queue. PR181's dependency update
needs its own compatibility/CI review. This planning change neither merges nor
closes those PRs.

| Existing issues | Reconciliation owner and action |
| --- | --- |
| [#3](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/3)/#12/#25/#26/#27/#39 | [#58][i58]/#62 audit build, synthetic-cloud, restricted SQL and real managed-identity evidence; exact new-head tests remain required for changes |
| [#7](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/7)/#57/#100/#103/#156 | [#85][i85]/#87/#271 audit worker publication, fencing, outbox, signed ingress and multi-book dispatch; already published nine-source evidence is bounded |
| [#8](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/8)/#55/#61/#70/#81/#82/#92/#93 | [#84][i84]/#237 audit source/import/staging contracts and implementation; preserve CSV and server-source authority during account-first migration |
| [#9](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/9)/#50/#52/#80/#104/#132 | Product lanes A/B and [#88][i88] reconcile UI/enrollment/review/release acceptance; [#132](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/132) release scope never implies all qualification complete |
| [#160](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/160)/#186/#187 | [#104][i104] audit original completion/inspection defects against merged fixes and current actual recovery; don't close obsolete symptoms without exact original criteria |
| [#225][i225] | [#226][i226] verify dated-currency repair and original units; still-open issue is not evidence repair is absent |
| [#51][i51]/#53/#60/#67/#84/#86/#94 | Exact report/corpus/reversal/money evidence audit, independent expected results and missing probes; no redundant accounting engine |
| [#247][i247]/#248/#249/#250/#251/#255 | Focused workspace parent, accepted/proposed contract distinction, direct evidence navigation; planning metric remains separate |

## Parallel execution and leases

Maximum current team capacity is four active agents including coordinator: three
bounded implementation/design workers plus coordinator/reviewer. This is a
capacity ceiling, not four safely writable copies of the same app. No agents
are started or preassigned by this plan.

Suggested first wave: [#281][i281] startup/capability slice, [#289][i289] auth configuration
slice and [#296][i296] contract author, with coordinator reviewing contracts,
issue graph and shared files. [#238][i238] or [#246][i246] can replace a lane if immediate code
is blocked. Other ready tasks are queued rather than assigned overlapping paths.

Later waves: [#297][i297] is the sole SQL writer while [#293][i293] owns ReviewInbox
and [#238][i238] owns the source-first contract. Run [#291][i291] on API mapping only if exact
consumer edits are handed to the UI owner. [#226][i226]/#293/#298 and connection
labels/reconnect UI must serialize overlapping component writes. Run verifier
and webhook preparation alongside product work only with disjoint paths and
separate concrete execution mandates. Never run competing cloud mutations.

After [#238][i238], serialize SQL claims [#297][i297] -> [#239][i239] -> [#241][i241] or
[#304][i304] or [#275][i275] according to reviewed priority/dependency readiness;
this is writer scheduling, not an invented architectural dependency. Go/UI work
can proceed against reviewed contracts in separate paths. Migration numbers are
allocated only after a fresh main/lease check; earlier planned migration30/31
reservations are obsolete. All merged SQL stays immutable.

Each dispatch must record in [#65][i65] and the bounded issue:

```text
token / issue / owner / UTC start / heartbeat / expiry / status
base SHA / branch / worktree
exclusive exact paths (including shared-file handoffs)
reviewed dependency SHAs and unresolved acceptance gates
bounded outcome / non-goals / named tests / stage runbook
handoff SHA / results / limitations / successor authority
```

Use a proposed 60-minute renewable lease and heartbeat at meaningful stages,
at least every 15 minutes; future dispatcher must set actual UTC values.
Expired writers stop before edits and reconcile with coordinator. Expiry does
not authorize overwriting another worktree. Release ownership before another
writer starts; record review/integration separately from acceptance/completion.
Coordinator exclusively owns OpenAPI, generated types, navigation/global styles,
index/bibliography, CI/Makefile and schema fixtures unless exact files are
delegated. Shared-file ownership can be transferred explicitly, never inferred.

## Required delivery evidence

Every implementation PR links a bounded issue, exact parent/dependencies,
contract and stage runbook; states migration impact and unresolved risks; names
tests versus proposed cases. Before commit run staged runbook validation.
Run `make check`, `make test`, `make build`; add `migration-test` for SQL/tooling,
`ledger-test` for accounting, web check/test/build/browser for browser/API and
`app-integration` for browser/API/SQL changes. Use disposable synthetic databases.
Do not run the long foundation suite merely to replace these relevant gates.

Hosted evidence additionally pins source SHA, exact images/config/revisions,
finite authority, independent fixture expectation, actual action/result and
cleanup. Owner performs credentials/MFA privately. No raw payload, financial
record, statement, secret or browser token is published. For financial exchanges
record applicable ISO edition/message/profile/mapping/validation, and rationale
where no ISO financial message applies; exact money and multicurrency remain
required. Standards names, XSD validation and generator self-checks are not
ledger conformance or accounting approval.

Planning acceptance is a deduplicated issue graph and reviewable document.
Implementation completion, hosted qualification, live-account enrollment and
official-books approval each remain distinct recorded outcomes.

documents.body:
# Financial workspace design

## Decision

Issue #80 implements a book-first workspace under #52/#50 using the existing
Next.js identity, durable-command and ledger-read boundaries. The static
[prototype](../prototypes/financial-workspace.html) remains design history, not
an application route or runtime data source. No combined balances across LLCs.

## Implemented work

Select an authorized entity/book, then use **Overview, Accounts, Account activity,
Reports or New journal**. The compact header retains functional currency and
explicit dates. Workspace metadata revision is labelled separately from freshly
read report snapshots. Overview and Accounts read the existing trial-balance API;
amounts remain exact strings. Account activity uses the existing scoped general
ledger, followed by revision-pinned journal detail. There is no book-wide
transaction endpoint or connected bank feed.

Account balance → account ledger → journal → Overview preserves date context.
Changing book remounts scope-owned state; dates invalidate superseded responses.
Hidden report views cannot repopulate from late requests. Denied reads clear the
book selection. Loading/error/denied is never rendered as zero. Report comparison,
CSV review download and source-provenance behavior retain their owned contracts.

Recovery stays mounted. Idle status and discovery action remain visible in a
compact row; registration uncertainty, pending work, errors and unacknowledged
results retain the full recovery panel. Scope/navigation/editing remain locked
until authoritative recovery permits new work. New journal moves behind explicit
navigation without bypassing review or terminal acknowledgement.

## Evidence and remaining gates

[Living workspace evidence](../runbooks/book-workspace.md) owns named tests and
review captures. Native controls, visible focus, semantic tables and mobile layout
reuse [FW01–FW02](../research/financial-workspace-sources.md). Amount/read correctness
still comes from SQL contracts, not screenshots or synthetic browser mocks.

Owner visual approval, full accessibility audit and hosted evidence remain separate.
Review inbox, reconciliation, bank-provider ingestion and live policy approval are
future work; #80 does not close #52/#50. No arbitrary functional FX or audit-export
conformance is introduced by this interface.

documents.body:
# Plaid #88 qualification test matrix

## Scope and clearance rule

Owner requested this coverage audit on 2026-10-22. GitHub [#88](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/88)
owns execution state; this document defines cases and evidence. Sources and
review limits: [P88-01–P88-17](../research/plaid-88-test-sources.md).

Current scope: US Transactions, web frontend, one Item per Link attempt,
account-filtered streams, checking/savings/card/loan transaction feeds. Current
historical dynamic acceptance covers seven types (B). Fresh Tartan initial
acquisition metadata adds savings/money-market/cash-management (F), plus bounded
savings first/repeat UI proof. Exact financial equality remains unqualified. Loan binding does
not qualify a Liabilities API integration. No money movement or automatic posting.
The ninety-day request is an intended lookback, not a guarantee of supplied history.

Statuses: **PASS** = the exact named observation was verified; **PARTIAL** =
some evidence exists but the row is not cleared; **OPEN** = no qualifying result;
**BLOCKED** = named prerequisite missing; **N/A** = exclusion with rationale.
Historical synthetic PASS does not clear a required hosted case. Proposed IDs
below are acceptance cases, not assertions that corresponding automated tests exist.

Every executed row must record date, exact source SHA, deployed revisions/image
digests when applicable, named case, fictional fixture and independent expectation,
command/action, result, redacted receipt link, limitations and defect issue.
No raw responses, tokens, cursors, transaction identifiers or financial records
belong in public evidence. A missing result is never PASS. Aggregate UI counts
are weaker than exact fixture/SQL assertions.

## Evidence already available

- **A:** [2026-10-21/22 qualification](../runbooks/plaid-sandbox-20261021.md),
  initial smoke and synthetic suites; preserves the failed browser volume gate.
- **B:** [migration29 rollout and final comparisons](../runbooks/plaid-258-rollout.md),
  runtime source `f334d062e2ee4c572af52b823969c299cd37bf93`, trusted build
  `39715438972` attempt2, API/web revision19 and worker revision7. Final
  read-only comparison recorded at documentation commit `04bebc3` / PR268.
- **C:** [this audit runbook](../runbooks/plaid-88-test-matrix.md), current
  source inventory and fresh synthetic unit/core validation. Integration
  evidence in A/B remains historical; it is not rerun or relabeled by this audit.
- **D:** [swarm integration](../runbooks/plaid-88-swarm.md), new independent
  adapter/SQL lifecycle oracle, signed socket/SQL acquisition composition,
  bounded managed webhook executable and explicit exit recovery. These are
  synthetic implementation proofs; no new hosted row is cleared by them.
- **E:** [wave two](../runbooks/plaid-88-wave2.md): bounded Hosted completion
  correction, finite hash-pinned independent SQL comparison and inert existing-host
  updater. These are synthetic proofs; actual hosted R02/R03/W01 remain open.
  [LC01](../research/plaid-launch-center-review.md) records personalized Dashboard
  signals and scope limits. #274 owns mapping, #275 reconnect, #276 OAuth clients.
- **F:** [2026-10-24 actual Tartan browser run](../runbooks/tartan-browser-qualification.md):
  managed setup/acknowledgement, original-attempt recovery,9 supported bindings,
  natural scheduled delivery and exact-book read-only acquisition counts all
  historical-ready/published. After browser recovery,9 inboxes loaded46 rows;
  savings generation2 completed with6 All-status rows/source revision1 unchanged.
  Standard provider case, not the pre-authored oracle; R02/R03 remain open.

## Link and supported clients

| ID / source | Test and exact clearance evidence | Current status / next action | Owner issue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L01 / 02 | Interactive non-OAuth dynamic Link → verified session → one exchange → reviewed binding → application publication. | PASS for seven dynamic types (B). API-created smoke cannot replace interactive proof. | #88 / #104 |
| L02 / 04 | Successful, exited, failed and incomplete Hosted Link sessions correlate to the verified owner; reject missing/ambiguous/foreign completion. | PARTIAL. Success observed; strict modern exit now yields explicit conflict/recovery before claim (D); `TestHostedLinkCompletion`, `TestPlaidHTTPSessionAssociation` cover synthetic rejection. Hosted negative cases OPEN. | #187 / #104 |
| L03 / 04 | Completion is recoverable after lost tab, reload, expired app session or lost exchange response; inspect persisted attempt before safe restart. Test completion delivery mechanism and expiry. | PARTIAL. Inspection recovery observed (A/B); `TestHostedReloadCompletion`, `TestConnectionUncertainEffects` are synthetic. Signed SESSION_FINISHED absent; polling alternative needs reviewed disposition. | #187 |
| L04 / 07 | Exit/cancel and expired/invalid Link token recover without duplicate exchange; replacement begins only after inspecting prior attempt. | PARTIAL. Existing cancellation/claim tests; actual token expiry and user-exit recovery OPEN. Hosted lifetime differs from SDK lifetime. | #187 / #104 |
| L05 / 06 | Same institution/login/account connected again is detected safely; distinguish legitimate distinct logins and partial account selections. No duplicate import or needless token exchange. | OPEN. Same-attempt replay and stable counts do not establish duplicate-Item prevention. | #104 / #88 |
| L06 / 02 | Simple-user depository/savings enrollment, binding, first acquisition and repeat. | PASS for bounded standard-Tartan UI/metadata (F): active binding, initial1/1 and explicit repeat2/2 historical-ready,6 All-status rows/source revision1 unchanged. Exact financial equality/no-journal proof remains R02/R03. | #104 / #88 |
| O01 / 03 | Desktop OAuth happy path, return to correct attempt, no unsupported-browser loop. | OPEN. Non-OAuth success does not clear OAuth. | #104 / #88 |
| O02 / 03 | iOS mobile web OAuth, institution app installed and absent. Record real device/browser versions. | OPEN; required before mobile web is advertised. | #104 / #88 |
| O03 / 03 | Android mobile web OAuth, institution app installed and absent. | OPEN; same support boundary as O02. | #104 / #88 |
| O04 / 03 | OAuth update-mode repair after Sandbox reset_login. | BLOCKED on I01; run on each supported web client. | #104 / #88 |
| O05 / 03 | Reduced/revoked account consent and OAuth errors preserve scope; no acquisition of unselected accounts. | PARTIAL synthetic authority denials; actual consent cases OPEN. | #87 / #104 |
| O06 / 03 | Native iOS/Android SDK, universal/app links, app webview redirect. | N/A to current web-only release. Reopen before shipping native/webview clients. | #88 |

## Transactions and exact publication

| ID / source | Test and exact clearance evidence | Current status / next action | Owner issue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T01 / 09,10,16 | First empty pull remains loading; initial/history readiness advances correctly; request policy and available coverage are visible. | PARTIAL. Seven historical-complete UI statuses (B); `TestPlaidEmptyInitialization`, `TestSyncEmptyAccountItemReadiness` synthetic. Fixture-known ninety-day coverage OPEN; do not infer it from readiness. | #226 / #88 |
| T02 / 10 | Each selected account has its own cursor stream; foreign account/Item and switched filter with reused cursor are rejected. | PARTIAL. `TestPlaidLiabilityAccountPin`, `TestSyncSourceProjectionAndBinding`; hosted persisted-cursor assertions OPEN. | #85 / #87 |
| T03 / 09 | Initial publication followed by unchanged repeat has no duplicate effects. | PASS for bounded UI counts (B): checking69 (33 review/36 held), card55, mortgage47, student6, auto/consumer/LOC47 each, all source revision1. Exact DB replay/no-journal proof still R02/R03. | #88 |
| T04 / 11 | Induce dynamic pending removal + posted replacement across pages; retain lineage when matched, tolerate null match/changed amount/name, and disappearing authorization hold. | OPEN hosted. `TestAcquisitionLifecycleOracle` now covers real adapter/SQL with independent literal expectations (D); earlier SQL/decoder tests remain separate. Provider Refresh required; another app sync alone does not induce the transition. Student schedule is a separate expectation. | #85 / #88 |
| T05 / 11 | Apply added/modified/removed data, including corrections to already-posted provider transactions, without rewriting ledger journals. | PARTIAL. `TestSyncPostedEvidenceRemainsOriginal` synthetic; actual induced source correction/held disposition OPEN. | #85 / #88 |
| T06 / 11 | Exact quantity/currency retained; precision/pending/zero held when ineligible; no rounding or draft bypass. | PARTIAL. Matrix/fuzz and `TestSourcePrecisionHold`, `TestPrecisionEligibilityForgery` pass in B; actual held warning/no-draft observed. Independent full provider-to-review equality OPEN (R02). | #86 / #88 |
| T07 / 10,12 | Multi-page update plus mutation/error restarts at original cursor; publish only complete set and final cursor. | PARTIAL. `TestAcquisitionMutationRestart`, `TestSyncPublicationAtomicity` synthetic. Hosted multi-page/failure evidence OPEN; if not inducible, record limitation and reviewed fault-injection substitute. | #85 |
| T08 / 10 | Durable filtered cursor survives worker/process restart; empty initial tail cannot erase data; terminal receipt replay does not refetch. | PARTIAL synthetic acquisition/sync tests; hosted restart/SQL proof OPEN. | #85 |
| T09 / 09 | Custom known transaction injection reaches only named account; fixed exact expected values match review. | OPEN; never use default first-account selection. Fixture metadata only, no raw payload evidence. | #88 |
| T10 / 09 | Persona fixtures: earned-wage, young-professional and small-business histories; refresh may return no new data. | OPEN as supplemental coverage; one representative small-business fixture is required for bookkeeping acceptance. Others need a recorded disposition. | #88 |

## Webhook delivery and failure recovery

| ID / source | Test and exact clearance evidence | Current status / next action | Owner issue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| W01 / 13 | Set actual webhook URL during enrollment (or explicit update); first sync activates notifications; signed SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE reaches receiver. | BLOCKED hosted. Dedicated isolated host/managed command implemented and synthetically tested (D); API remains private. Actual IAM/SQL principal, HTTPS deployment and enrollment URL still required. fire_webhook success alone is insufficient. | #103 / #87 / #88 |
| W02 / 13 | Follow signed delivery → durable receipt/demand → task/worker → correct source publication; initial/history flags never themselves publish readiness. | OPEN hosted. D now composes signed socket→restricted SQL receipt/wakeup→acquisition/review, duplicates/tamper/disconnected denial and zero journals/outbox; real cloud task transport remains unproved by this test. | #87 / #88 |
| W03 / 14 | Duplicate/reordered delivery, webhook during running sync and durable-commit failure are safe; only durable receipt acknowledged, response under ten seconds. | PARTIAL. Receipt/fence/concurrency tests synthetic; hosted transport timing and retry OPEN. | #85 / #87 |
| W04 / 14 | Retryable delivery failures recover, permanent denials remain denied, overload/429 bounded; no acceptance before durable commit. | PARTIAL synthetic handler/admission tests; actual safe non-production retry experiment OPEN. Do not assume every4xx retries. | #87 / #89 |
| W05 / 14 | Missed webhook/outage recovers through scheduled catch-up without duplicate effects or cross-source access. | PARTIAL synthetic catch-up/dispatch; Scheduler ENABLED is configuration evidence only. Hosted missed-event recovery OPEN. | #85 / #89 |
| W06 / 15 | ES256/kid/key rotation/expiry, exact raw-body digest, old/future JWT, malformed/oversize and invalid signature fail closed. | PASS synthetic unit behavior only: `TestPlaidWebhook`, `TestWebhookRejectedInputs`, `TestWebhookKeyLifecycle`, `TestEquivalentECDSADelivery`. Real signed delivery remains W01. | #87 |
| W07 / 15 | Key service outage/timeout/cache budget; wrong environment, unknown/revoked Item, account/tenant isolation; no SQL work for unauthenticated input. | PARTIAL synthetic `TestKeyTransportFailures`, `TestWebhookPersistenceFailure`, SQL scope tests. Hosted identity/scope path OPEN. | #87 |
| R01 / 12 + project | API rate limits, timeouts, unavailable institution, malformed page, bound overflow and worker lease expiry preserve last completed publication. | PARTIAL `TestProviderFailures`, acquisition/dispatch fault suites; exact coverage gaps require case inventory, not suite-name inference. | #85 / #89 |
| R02 / project | Independent fixture oracle compares source identity/quantity/unit/date/state to persisted observations and review; explain every discrepancy. | PASS synthetic E for full history/current review/lineage and negative mismatches under a finite mandate; OPEN hosted #272. UI row-count equality is not this proof. No raw payload retention. | #272 / #88 / #84 |
| R03 / project | Before/after DB assertions: acquisition/replay produces zero journal and journal-posting outbox additions. Lost COMMIT, stale writer and permission revocation cannot duplicate effects. | PASS synthetic (`TestAcquisitionCommittedReplyLoss`, sync/providerflow suites); OPEN for current hosted application DB. UI zero balances/Posted filter insufficient. | #85 / #88 |

## Item lifecycle and Link errors

| ID / source | Test and exact clearance evidence | Current status / next action | Owner issue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| I01 / 05 | reset_login → ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED → actionable repair → update-mode success → same Item continuity and sync resumes. | BLOCKED. HTTP adapter's reconnect path lacks qualified Hosted Link completion; VerifySession rejects nonempty expectedItem. Synthetic SQL reconnect is not concrete provider proof. | #104 / #88 |
| I02 / 05 | PENDING_DISCONNECT; consent expiry; renewal; LOGIN_REPAIRED clears stale messaging without unauthorized collection. | OPEN. Current ingress accepts only Transactions notifications; Item lifecycle event support requires implementation/review. | #103 / #104 |
| I03 / 05 | NEW_ACCOUNTS_AVAILABLE → explicit account selection; revoked access cannot be reacquired silently. | OPEN; same Item-event gap. | #103 / #104 / #87 |
| I04 / 05 + project | Disconnect/removal acknowledgement and ambiguous result; disable future acquisition, preserve approved immutable history, no stale-worker publication. | PARTIAL synthetic `TestConnectionRotationAndDisconnect`, `TestConnectionRemovalUncertainty`; diagnostic Item cleanup passed(A), app disconnect/reconnect not exercised. | #104 / #87 |
| I05 / 05 | PENDING_EXPIRATION / UK-EU renewal variant. | N/A for current US profile; reopen with country scope. US consent cases remain I02. | #88 |
| E01 / 08 | MFA device OTP, questions, selections and multiple rounds: success, wrong answer, user cancellation. | OPEN actual Link cases; public Sandbox fixtures only. | #104 / #88 |
| E02 / 08 | reCAPTCHA success/failure and recovery. | OPEN, owner-operated challenge; no unattended solving. | #104 / #88 |
| E03 / 08 | Non-OAuth Link errors: ACCESS_NOT_GRANTED, COUNTRY_NOT_SUPPORTED, INSTITUTION_NOT_RESPONDING, INSTITUTION_NO_LONGER_SUPPORTED, INSTITUTION_REGISTRATION_REQUIRED, INSUFFICIENT_CREDENTIALS, INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, INVALID_CREDENTIALS, INVALID_MFA, INVALID_SEND_METHOD. | Each OPEN; record individual outcome and safe retry/exit behavior. | #104 / #88 |
| E04 / 08 | ITEM_LOCKED, ITEM_NOT_SUPPORTED, MFA_NOT_SUPPORTED, NO_ACCOUNTS, UNAUTHORIZED_INSTITUTION, USER_INPUT_TIMEOUT, USER_SETUP_REQUIRED. | Each OPEN. Payment and deposit-allocation errors excluded below. | #104 / #88 |
| E05 / 08,17 | OAuth error selector: INSUFFICIENT_CREDENTIALS, ACCESS_NOT_GRANTED; missing institution/account and cancel return safe UI state. | OPEN. NO_AUTH_ACCOUNTS is N/A Transactions-only. | #104 / #88 |

## Production request and exclusions

| ID | Requirement / disposition | Current status / owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G01 | Review account-specific Launch Center; record product/country/platform checklist, app/company/use-case profile and OAuth prerequisites without copying private fields. Compare each item to this matrix. | PARTIAL, #274 under #88. [LC01](../research/plaid-launch-center-review.md): Production-approved header; individual account setup signals complete despite0/4 group counters; all12 task panels inspected for selected details. Exact scope/registration and full applicable mapping remain open. |
| G02 | Review Hosted Link vs official web SDK recommendation for owned frontend. Retain current boundary until explicit decision, then qualify chosen completion/recovery flow. | OPEN, #187/#104; P88-04 conflicts with assuming Hosted Link is the final UX. |
| G03 | Production environment/credential/SQL isolation, required products only, consent/privacy, retention and budget; no Sandbox fixture endpoints in live path. | BLOCKED under #90; current runtime intentionally Sandbox-only. |
| G04 | Secure token/identifier handling, redacted support evidence and Item removal/retention review. | PARTIAL synthetic vault/redaction; hosted security and owner policy review remain #164/#62/#90. Raw identifiers seen in Sandbox UI require Production exposure review (P88-01). |
| G05 | Institution-specific history, OAuth and statement reconciliation with one explicitly authorized read-only real account. | BLOCKED #90; impossible to establish from Sandbox alone (P88-02). |
| D01 | Auth, micro-deposits, Identity, Liabilities API, Investments, Assets, Statements, Income, Transfer/Payment Initiation, verification/Monitor and other unrequested products. | N/A to this integration. Also excludes their payment/deposit error fixtures. Reopen if products enabled; loan transaction support does not clear Liabilities tests. |
| D02 | Recurring Transactions, provider Refresh in the customer UX, Multi-Item Link, Link Recovery beta, returning-user Profiles and Link Delivery SMS/email. | N/A as shipped product features, not permanently waived. Refresh remains required as the Sandbox stimulus in T04. SDK onExit/onEvent applies if SDK chosen; Hosted session outcomes remain L02. |

## Execution order and issue boundaries

1. #88: finish G01 applicability and exact remaining-case inventory. Do not close
   #85/#87 from historic suite names; compare their original criteria to cases.
2. #103/#87: W01–W07 narrow ingress and actual signed chain. #104/#187:
   L02–L05, O01–O05, I01–I04 and E01–E05. These are separate reservations in
   #65 before editing shared connection/webhook/API/SQL paths.
3. #85/#88: T04–T09 and R01–R03 with an independent oracle and bounded runtime
   evidence capability. Synthetic-only substitutes require explicit reviewed
   rationale for cases the provider cannot reliably induce.
   Current UI cannot establish R02/R03: design a reviewed redacted comparator/
   count capability before execution; do not obtain general live SQL or raw pages.
4. Close #88 only when required applicable rows have evidence, every supplemental
   row has a reviewed disposition, and Launch Center adds no unmapped cases.
   Failed cases need fixes and reruns on named source, never timeout inflation.
   #89's known 1,000-command failure remains separate and unresolved.
5. #90 owns real-account pilot/statement reconciliation and explicit privacy,
   retention and interval approval. Sandbox completion does not authorize it.

Original #88 obligations remain: actual Link/exchange, initial/incremental and
dynamic lifecycle, signed delivery, provider-to-review/cursor/replay/no-journal
proof, owner-injected credentials, redacted evidence and institution/history/
balance limits. This matrix expands clarity without lowering those requirements.

documents.title: Focused financial tools — #249
documents.body:
# Focused financial tools — #249

Owner-approved visual/scope, 2026-10-22. The [approved reference](../prototypes/position-approved.png)
and [Position contract](../contracts/position-read-model.md) drive this slice.
Read the [source record](../research/position-sources.md) and
[delivery evidence](../runbooks/position-workspace.md) before extending it.

## Screen and navigation

Position opens with all currently authorized books, grouped by entity. A scope
selector narrows it to an entity or book. Each row shows functional currency,
assets, liabilities, book equity and signed equity change from an explicit earlier
date. The SQL report supplies every amount and difference; the browser only
formats exact strings. There is no cross-book total, consolidation or FX conversion.
Every book has its own report revision and generation timestamp. A failure in one
row is unavailable, not zero, while other authorized rows remain usable.

Position, Ledger and Reports are always visible in the top navigation. Ledger
uses the existing account-scoped report and journal reader. Reports retains the
existing statement/comparison/export tools. Those tools require a book; opening
them from All books presents explicit book choices rather than silently selecting
one. A Position book link selects that book and hands its revision to Ledger's
first read. A changed revision yields the existing conflict and explicit refresh.
Dates remain in memory across tools. Review, journal, accounts, connections,
refresh and sign-out remain available through Tools. Setup is a separate disclosure.
An unacknowledged command stays visible and blocks unsafe new work and reads.

## Visual language

One clean system sans-serif family, readable dark text, modest headings, aligned
tabular numerals and white background. No typewriter effect or decorative hero.
Book rows alternate faint neutral gray (`#f3f4f4`) and unshaded white; entity
headings remain white. No colored column backgrounds. Positive equity changes
use restrained green (`#286044`), negative changes muted red (`#9b3e38`), and exact
zero stays neutral. Signs remain visible independently of color. These are signed
movements, not claims of profitability or funds available to spend. Other asset,
liability and credit values remain neutral; an increase is not universally favorable.

At narrow widths, each book becomes a labeled two-column reading inside the same
semantic table, preserving every amount and its label without page overflow or
sideways scrolling. Desktop remains the approved six-column statement. Native
date/select controls, focus outlines, heading focus and accessible snapshot
descriptions support keyboard and assistive use.

## Boundary and acceptance

No API/OpenAPI, SQL, migration, accounting policy, authorization or durable
command storage changes. Standards applicability and versioned currency mapping
are inherited from the reviewed Position/reporting contracts; no new financial
message or ISO designation is introduced. The current server's synthetic
functional-policy limits remain explicit; original multicurrency units remain
available in Ledger/journal evidence. Cash classification, available-to-use
planning, investigation status ownership and group consolidation retain their
own reviewed contracts/issues.

Acceptance evidence: Position unit cases for exact large decimals, versioned
currencies, old-response invalidation, zero/unavailable, denial and bounded reads;
browser cases for all-book/entity/book scope, dates, partial failure, keyboard
tool navigation, recovery lock and desktop/mobile layout; existing saved-command
journeys and real browser/Next/Go/PostgreSQL integration. Visual QA compares the
approved reference with actual screenshots. Test-only fixtures never enter app routes.

documents.title: Product and data-collection delivery
documents.body:
# Product and data-collection delivery

## Decision

Make Jayburd useful for daily multi-LLC bookkeeping: visible balances, traceable
transactions and explicit review. Competing with established financial products
is an ambition, not a benchmark result. Go/PostgreSQL/Next.js and reviewed
accounting contracts remain authoritative. GitHub owns current task/lease state.

## Work

| Milestone | Delivery and acceptance |
| --- | --- |
| Usable books | #80 under #52/#50: compact book context; Overview, Accounts, Account activity, Reports and New journal. Owner can find a balance, inspect its postings and return with context. Keyboard/mobile and recovery locking must pass. |
| Durable source foundations | #81 stable account/namespace identity and scoped grants; #82 immutable local synthetic staging. Contracts precede code. Neither alone is a working importer. |
| Complete CSV workflow | #8: register batch, publish validated preview, explicitly confirm recoverable import, persist observations/provenance, review/classify, then atomically post and link a journal. Upload/preview/import/draft each create zero journals. |
| Connected acquisition | #7 private HTTP/OIDC/Cloud Tasks service composition; #70 Plaid enrollment, sync pagination, verified webhook triggers and scheduled catch-up. All feed the same source/review core. Provider acquisition does not imply bookkeeping completion. |
| Reconcile and operate | #10 statement reconciliation and close; #58 recovery/retention/load/cost evidence. #27 hosted application and #13/#1 source qualification/official-books cutover remain separate gates. |

Parallel work has separate worktrees and bounded leases in #65. One SQL writer
owns each new migration; coordinator owns shared API/CI/version integration. Reuse stopped
threads; no duplicate agents or shared-file writes. Keep merged migrations immutable.

This bounded build (#92/#93) implements the SQL/Go import foundation;
#94 adds independent decoder money properties. The [delivery runbook](../runbooks/durable-import-delivery.md)
distinguishes this backend foundation from a complete upload/review/post UI.

## Done when

The [sync quality gates](sync-quality.md) connect #84–#90 to these milestones:
independent reconciliation, provider recovery, fuzz/isolation, webhook security,
Sandbox, measured scaling and a separately authorized live pilot.

Named tests prove each journey with independent synthetic results, exact currency
units, replay/conflict/failure and current scope checks. Distinguish source evidence,
drafts and posted journals. Every balance links to ledger evidence; unavailable
or stale data is never displayed as zero. Record measured fixture sizes and
actual latency before making scale claims. Owner reviews the completed journey.

## Blockers

No active provider or hosted frontend is implied. Private cloud storage, raw
retention/deletion, connection identity/secrets and hosted queue acceptance remain
required. Initial staging/enrollment are synthetic only. Advanced FX and group
consolidation remain explicitly deferred under #59.

## Generated acquisition and review slice

PR #99, #105 and #106 are merged. #101 connection state/service and #102 acquisition
have synthetic backend evidence. The current #104 slice adds connection management
and source-review navigation against those contracts; see
[connection and acquisition](../runbooks/provider-acquisition.md). #103 verified
webhooks/catch-up and the remaining #104 discovery/status/wakeup contracts stay open.
The [connections workspace](../runbooks/connection-workspace.md) records UI evidence
and the full browser qualification boundary. #7 retains
hosted worker composition, and #88 separately qualifies provider/secret delivery.
Native GitHub dependencies determine dispatch; local proof does not activate Plaid.

Owner direction: no user-prepared CSV is required. #97 loads 3,000 generated
transactions across fictional LLCs through private staging and the real import
authority. #96 supplies scoped review/category drafts and atomic source-linked
posting; #98 presents the inbox and explicit confirmation. Exact source units

documents.title: Register real accounts and derive reconcilable bookkeeping
documents.body:
# Register real accounts and derive reconcilable bookkeeping

Owner direction2026-10-25 supersedes the agent-proposed blanket ledger posting
ban. Read-only means bank access: no moving money. Current-authorized manual
bookkeeping and reviewed deterministic rules may create balanced journals;
source changes produce traceable corrections, preserving immutable originals.
Source bank evidence does not itself select recognition/classification/FX policy.
GitHub owns task state/leases; source docs own decisions/evidence. No live scope,
security review, deployment/spend or secret access is approved by this plan.

## Fast path to the first personal account

1. Merge/review the #308 closed source profile baseline. Implement #312 transport
   in isolation, then #311 SQL/source-origin and #313 credential/runtime composition;
   #314 signed matched-environment notifications and #315 synthetic profile proof.
   Retain current Sandbox compatibility. No new DB/provisioning in transport work.
2. Complete applicable actual #88/#299/#300/#302/#303/#275/#320 Sandbox/equality/
   recovery evidence with fresh finite reviewed scope. Green source CI is not it.
3. #337 records actual isolation/resources/retention/identity/cost/account/policy
   choice, separately from source-only profile construction. #316 prepares exact
   source/images/schema/bootstrap/receiver compatibility, finite release/rollback
   and cleanup for owner approval. Do not reuse expired approvals or swap secrets
   into the dev profile. Human security review remains before sensitive release.
4. Owner privately signs into one named supported account and approves consent.
   Automatically register/bind only the scoped account, import available90-day
   history, show truthful initial/history/coverage status and incremental sync.
   Review and reconcile the complete agreed statement interval privately; retain
   allowed redacted counts/outcomes. Current manual journal/reversal workflow can
   be used under reviewed policy/post permission once its acceptance passes.

The entire rule engine, connect-first reorganization237/238, topic modelling243,
consolidation59 and every new correction UI are not prerequisites to initial
registration. They remain real deliverables, not cancelled scope. Unsupported or
uncertain actions stay visibly held until implemented/qualified. Official books,
closing and cutover remain1/10/13/58/90 policy/evidence gates.

## Bookkeeping lane

| Issue | Bounded outcome / independently named evidence | Hard delivery predecessor |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #332 | Accepted source->policy/rule->journal/correction contract; inspect implemented anchors/holds and independent50->55 and EUR examples before DDL | Existing posting/source contracts; design can start independently |
| #333 | Actual restricted SQL/Go correction inspection and atomic linked reversal/replacement/resolution; stale/revoked/closed-period/unknown-commit/replay tests | Merged #332 contract, exact SQL/API review; one SQL writer |
| #334 | Opt-in versioned deterministic rules using existing scoped posting boundary; post once under current permission, hold uncertain mappings | Merged #332; legitimate account creation297 where required, separate SQL lease |
| #335 | Current/original evidence and journal chain, reviewed correction preview/register/execute/acknowledge/reload/reports in browser | Merged #333 API, shared generated types coordinated |
| #336 | Real fictional SQL/browser source50/original50/change55/reverse50/replace55/net55 and exact reports, duplicate/reorder/lost reply, original EUR/FX, independent oracle | #333/#335; #334 for automated cases; reuse301/84 reporting proof |

Existing #294/#296/#297/#298 supply legitimate category-account creation;
#301 keeps its explicit category->journal->reports acceptance. No fake equity/
expense mapping is used to claim a posted pilot. Rule implementation is incremental
and cannot inherit dev-accrual-usd-v1 as a real book's policy without review.

## Invariants and initial worked expectations

Bank revisions are retained; current pointer changes without overwriting history.
One operation identifies exact book/source/revision, policy/rule/permissions and
currency/valuation pins. Bank pending is not a final accounting instruction;
unmapped/ambiguous/unsupported/closed-period changes require actionable review.
The acquisition transaction and receiver do not acquire posting privileges.

For a reviewed same-currency expense case: source50 -> original journal50;
source revision55 -> exact historical reversal50 + reviewed replacement55;
expected three immutable journals and net expense55. Repeated feed/command/reply
recovery adds no fourth journal. Metadata-only change has no monetary correction.
Other legitimate adjustment operations require their own reviewed accounting
contract; do not silently invent a delta/plug or subtract unlike currencies.
Transfers/card payments/loan principal-interest need reviewed mappings and may
combine evidence; one feed row is not automatically one expense. Separate original
and functional units; preserve original historical rates on reversal.

Every correction/rule effect rechecks current authority and stale revisions,
commits balanced immutable journal/audit/receipt/outbox together and recovers
unknown outcomes via the same durable operation. Never edit/delete a posted entry,
erase a receipt or generate a replacement from observed test results.

#300 remains a separate deliberately unposted Sandbox fixture with absolute-zero
journal/journal.posted assertions. Posting qualification has exact nonzero expected
effects; these two cases cannot share a book or relax each other's assertions.

## Leases and evidence

Conventional estimates are in the native issues, not dates. Each implementation
claims one bounded issue with fresh main/dependencies, exact exclusive paths/base/
branch/worktree/token/expiry and heartbeat in65. One SQL writer; no version now.
API/OpenAPI/generated types/navigation are coordinator paths unless reserved.
Do not count an unmerged/missing/cancelled predecessor complete or bypass owner
resource/security decisions to start live work. Follow annotated sources, standards,
decision evidence, independent corpus, stage runbook and applicable core/ledger/
migration/web/full-stack checks. Plans/test names are obligations, not passed tests.

documents.title: Sync correctness and scaling gates
documents.body:
# Sync correctness and scaling gates

## Decision

Prove complete source-to-book correctness before live use. Existing ledger,
observer and staging tests are component evidence, not a qualified bank sync.
GitHub owns scheduling and acceptance state; [#65](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/65)
owns bounded agent leases. [Sources](../research/sync-quality-sources.md) explain
provider behavior and the limits of horizontal scaling.

## Work

| Issue | Required proof | Prerequisites |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#84](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/84) | Independent golden statement through import, review, posting and reconciled reports | #8, #10 |
| [#85](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/85) | Provider pagination, revisions, atomic cursor publication, replay and crash recovery | #7, #8, #70 |
| [#86](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/86) | Exact money, independent property oracles and cross-LLC denial | Existing boundary tests now; new adapter properties after implementation |
| [#87](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/87) | Webhook verification and revoked/wrong-source isolation | #7, #70 |
| [#88](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/88) | Opt-in real Plaid Sandbox qualification | #8, #85, #87; owner-injected secrets |
| [#89](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/89) | Scaling, overload, noisy tenants and recovery | #64 design; #7/#8 runtime; #26/#27 hosted gates |
| [#90](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/90) | One authorized read-only account reconciled to a complete statement | Prior quality gates, #1/#10/#27 and explicit live scope |

Extend the existing golden corpus; do not regenerate expectations from production
code. Imports create no journals until explicit posting. A balanced duplicate
journal is still wrong. Reconciliation explains pending/timing differences and
compares compatible dates, currencies and balance meanings.

## Scaling acceptance proposal

Measure 1k/10k/100k events, 1/10/100 books and 1/2/4/8 workers. Hold fixture shape
and database resources fixed within each comparison. Record throughput of unique
committed effects, p50/p95/p99 lag, backlog age, retries, resource pressure and
cost per 1k events; separate warmup and repeated measurements.

Proposed review target: at least 70% efficiency `T(n)/(n*T(1))` for independent
books before measured saturation, with p95 at most twice baseline at matched
per-worker offered load and zero lost/duplicate effects. This is a project target,
not an observed result or unlimited scaling guarantee. Measure hot-book contention
separately. Preserve serializable correctness; do not weaken isolation to pass.
[#64](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/64) retains
budget, RTO/RPO, cleanup and hosted-run acceptance ownership.

## Done when

Each issue records named tests, immutable code SHA, inputs, independent expected
results and failures/limits. Default CI stays synthetic and credential-free.
Sandbox and live qualification are separate gates. The
[runbook](../runbooks/sync-quality.md) records what actually ran.

documents.title: Product scope
documents.body:
# Product scope

## Decision

Build separate books for multiple LLCs and personal finances. First prove one
complete month for one LLC; enforce entity isolation with two fictional entities
from the first database test. Account aggregation is an input, not the ledger.

## First usable bookkeeping release

Chart of accounts; reviewed opening balances; bank/card statement import;
drafts and splits; balanced posting and reversals; transfer matching;
statement reconciliation; trial balance, general ledger, P&L and balance sheet;
period closing; evidence attachments; accountant-readable exports.

Default workflow: import -> review -> post -> reconcile -> close -> export.
Bank feed corrections cannot silently rewrite posted or closed books.
Account ownership is per legal entity, not per provider login or account mask.

## Scope decisions still open for real use

[ADR 0005](decisions/0005-development-accounting-policy.md) selects the synthetic
accrual/USD development profile; it does not select real-entity policy.

- Cash versus accrual basis and required adjusting-entry workflow.
- Functional and transaction currencies, FX policy, reporting period/timezone,
  rounding policy and precision.
- LLC/account counts, providers and accountant export format.
- Whether initial invoicing and bills are manual entries or dedicated workflows.
- Retention/deletion policy, access roles, initial opening balances and cutover.
- Recovery objectives, monthly cloud budget, and acceptable dispatch latency.

Multicurrency is required from the ledger design onward, including conversion,
settlement and period-end measurement contracts. Use ADR 0005 for the bounded development proof and resolve real-use policy
in JB-001 before connecting live accounts. An accounting basis choice does not remove
double-entry requirements. Apply the [standards contract](contracts/standards.md)
to financial messages and practices.

## Deferred

Payroll calculation, tax filing, inventory costing, brokerage tax lots,
public SaaS signup, payments/money movement and
complex consolidated financial statements. Basic intercompany transfers still
need explicit entity-specific entries and reconciliation; dashboard aggregation
must not present itself as statutory consolidation.

## Done when

A reviewed representative month reconciles to statements, trial balance and
reports agree, every figure traces to journal/source evidence, corrections and
period locks work, and an accountant reviews the export and cutover evidence.
Passing software tests alone does not approve official-bookkeeping use.
