documents.body:
# Bank connection recovery — 2026-10-15

Owner reached hosted Plaid success, but token persistence failed before a dynamic
Infisical secret appeared (#160). PR #165 replaces per-account slots/delivery with
KMS-encrypted PostgreSQL records and incorporates #161 recovery UI. See the
[contract](contracts/bank-token-vault.md) and [living evidence](runbooks/bank-token-vault.md).
The implementation passed synthetic encrypted enrollment/acquisition/posting and
lost-acknowledgement recovery. It is not deployed yet. #164 owns KMS provisioning,
migration 18, matching API/consumer images and hosted owner acceptance. Static
Plaid client secrets retain their managed-secret path. No old token was recovered.

# Current delivery — 2026-10-14

Managed Plaid Link loading and controlled paused-worker promotion are implemented
for review; see [current evidence](runbooks/link-worker-delivery.md) and
[worker operator steps](../deploy/WORKERS.md). The browser adapter loads only after
explicit setup, and tokens remain in memory. Worker release uses a separate
identity/state with no bootstrap IAM or secret administration.

Synthetic frontend, release and browser/API/PostgreSQL checks passed. Owner
infrastructure setup, Infisical propagation, actual Link Events association and
hosted OIDC/queue evidence remain acceptance gates in #7/#11/#88. Reconnect and
OAuth return are not implemented by this slice. #90 gates live accounts and #89
measured scaling. Sync alone never posts journals.

The snapshots below are historical; use the linked living evidence for current
implementation and remaining work.

# Acquisition delivery build

This branch is stacked on open PR #108 (`8f64a78`); #107 is merged. It adds
SQL-owned acquisition dispatch, a bounded Go publisher/consumer adapter, isolated
HTTP/queue profile and an injected worker server lifecycle. Current evidence and
remaining checks: [dispatch delivery](runbooks/acquisition-dispatch.md).

Hosted composition is still required: worker executables and dependency wiring,
queue/Scheduler/IAM Terraform, scoped Infisical credential writes/propagation,
Link/reconnect hosting and real OIDC/queue qualification. Then run explicitly
authorized #88 Plaid Sandbox qualification; #90 separately gates live accounts.
Sync alone never posts journals. #89 owns measured scaling evidence.

The following snapshot describes the predecessor delivery.

# Current connection operations build

PR #107 is merged. #103/#104 now add unfinished-attempt discovery after reload,
per-account pause/resume/manual sync controls, safe publication status and signed
webhook/catch-up intent. Synthetic integration and regression gates passed; see the
[operations runbook](runbooks/connection-operations.md) for current evidence.

Before real bank data: complete #7 hosted worker/dispatch wiring, scoped Infisical
writer and credential-version propagation, hosted Link/reconnect composition,
#88 end-to-end Plaid Sandbox qualification and #90 explicit live-pilot approval.
Acquisition never posts journals. Sync request, complete publication and reviewed
posting remain separate operations; provider-update time is unknown unless backed
by provider evidence. Scale is a measured #89 gate, not an assumed guarantee.

The following historical snapshot describes the preceding delivery.

# Project status — 2026-10-13

## Decision

Continue small Go/PostgreSQL delivery slices. PR #106 is merged (`6c6b546`) with synthetic enrollment/acquisition evidence.
This delivery adds the supported #104 connections workspace. Implemented local behavior is distinct
from hosted proof and approval to keep official books.

| Area | Evidence and remaining boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Ledger | Atomic double-entry posting, immutable journals, explicit reversals and exact valuation: [posting proof](runbooks/posting-proof.md). Advanced FX and accounting-policy cutover remain separate work. |
| Interactive bookkeeping | Book-first navigation adds visible balances, account activity, reports and manual entry: [workspace evidence](runbooks/book-workspace.md). Recoverable commands: [recovery evidence](runbooks/command-recovery.md). |
| Financial review | Trial balance, account general ledger, balance sheet, P&L, comparisons, journal detail and internal CSV: [review tools](runbooks/report-review-tools.md). |
| Synthetic demonstrations | Real browser/Go/PostgreSQL posting; 1,000-posting proof passed. Full 5,000/10,000 runs remain unproved: [demo evidence](runbooks/synthetic-demo.md). |
| Background work | Restricted observer SQL and recovery tests are merged: [foundation evidence](runbooks/ingestion-foundations.md). Merged #105 adds private HTTP and injected Cloud Tasks transport with real PostgreSQL replay tests: [transport evidence](runbooks/observer-transport.md). Hosted executable, queue and OIDC qualification remain pending. |
| Ingestion | Generated acquisition and category review/source-linked posting are merged: [populated demo](runbooks/populated-demo.md). Merged #105 adds fenced provider publication and exact Plaid decoding. Merged #106 adds scoped enrollment and a restartable acquisition runner: [delivery evidence](runbooks/provider-acquisition.md). Hosted composition, connection UI, webhook ingress and real provider qualification remain open. |
| Hosted application | Read-only Cloud Run service listing across regions returned no services in `jayburd-bookkeeping-dev` on 2026-10-13. No hosted frontend URL is available from that check. |

## Review the frontend

Start with `make demo` using the [demo prerequisites](runbooks/synthetic-demo.md).
Open the printed loopback URL. Data is fictional, disposable and backed by real
ledger validation.

1. Click **Load demo books** to import 3,000 generated transactions across three
   fictional LLCs. Select an LLC using **Entity and book**. Loading does not post.
2. **Overview** loads account balances for the visible through date; **Accounts**
   keeps the same ledger-backed balance view.
3. Select an account to open **Account activity**, then **Review journal line**
   to inspect its journal. The activity date range is explicit and revision-pinned.
4. **Reports** provides trial balance, balance sheet, P&L, comparisons and internal
   CSV. **New journal** contains manual entry; recovery remains visible and blocks
   new work until required acknowledgement.
5. **Review transactions** opens source evidence. Choose a category, create a
   draft, review its posting command and explicitly post. Acknowledge the result,
   then inspect the updated balance or the posted item's linked journal.

The merged workspace supplies runtime navigation. Data remains synthetic; connected-bank
feeds and consolidated multi-entity reports are not implied. Review the [workspace
evidence](runbooks/book-workspace.md) for named tests and current limitations.

## Connections workspace

The **Connections** tab lists scoped accounts, opens their transaction review and
confirms account-only disconnect. An injected Link adapter enables enrollment and
explicit verified account binding. Default startup has no adapter and shows setup
unavailable. [Evidence and remaining contracts](runbooks/connection-workspace.md)
distinguish this UI from working real bank connectivity.

## Next delivery

Follow the [product and collection milestones](plans/product-and-ingestion.md).
The merged #96–#98 slice supplies generated acquisition and explicit source-linked
posting without owner-prepared files. #100–#104 plan connected collection. The [enrollment and acquisition delivery](runbooks/provider-acquisition.md) builds
on the merged [sync foundations](runbooks/sync-foundations.md). Next: connection
UI (#104), verified webhook ingress (#103), hosted credential/provider composition
and separately authorized Sandbox qualification (#88). [Quality gates](plans/sync-quality.md)
remain open for reconciliation, provider qualification and measured scaling.

documents.title: Application integration sources
documents.body:
# Application integration sources

Reviewed 2026-10-11. These are engineering sources, not accounting or ISO
conformance evidence. Component-specific source reviews remain with their owners.

## A01 — openapi-typescript 7.x

[Official introduction](https://openapi-ts.dev/introduction), Setup and Basic
usage sections reviewed. The generator supports OpenAPI 3.1 and local schemas,
producing TypeScript declarations without a running API. Inference: generate UI
types from the repository contract and check for drift in CI. Types do not
validate runtime payloads or prove SQL invariants. The competing hand-maintained
interface approach is simpler initially but adds a second contract authority.
Acceptance: generated-file check, frontend typecheck and API fixture tests.
The installed 7.13.0 package's peer metadata requires TypeScript 5.x; pin 5.9.3
instead of forcing an incompatible major. The lockfile and typecheck validate
this compatibility choice, not merely a latest-version preference.

## A02 — Node.js release policy

[Official releases](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases), release policy
and supported version table reviewed. Node 24 is LTS; production should use an
LTS release. Inference: pin an available patched Node 24 version for web CI/builds
rather than the current non-LTS major. Actual package pins and dependency-audit
evidence belong in the lockfile and application runbook.

## A03 — Playwright CI setup

[Official CI guide](https://playwright.dev/docs/ci-intro), installation and test
workflow sections reviewed. Browser binaries/dependencies are explicitly installed
before tests. Inference: a distinct frontend CI job uses the lockfile, runs unit
and type checks, then synthetic Chromium journeys. No production provider or data
is required; mocked browser journeys prove UI behavior, not a live identity flow.

## A04 — GitHub setup-node

[Official setup-node repository](https://github.com/actions/setup-node), v6
reference resolved through GitHub to immutable commit
`249970729cb0ef3589644e2896645e5dc5ba9c38`. The action selects the CI Node toolchain;
pin it consistently with the existing immutable checkout/setup-go action policy.
No npm registry credential or cloud identity is needed for public dependencies.

documents.title: Automatic account binding source review
documents.body:
# Automatic account binding source review

Reviewed 2026-10-19 for issue #209. This record covers only the source sections
named below. It is not a claim that every Plaid account type is supported by
Jayburd or that provider metadata determines accounting treatment.

## AB01 — Plaid Accounts API account type schema

**Publisher and source:** Plaid,
[Accounts API — account type schema](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/#account-type-schema).

**Selected sections reviewed:** the `type`, `subtype`, `account_id`, balances
currency fields, account type schema, and account type/product support matrix.
The page was accessed 2026-10-19.

**Observed provider facts:** Plaid's current schema recognizes top-level account
types `depository`, `credit`, `loan`, `investment`, `other` and `payroll`. The
documented depository subtypes are `cash management`, `cd`, `checking`, `ebt`,
`hsa`, `limited purpose checking`, `money market`, `paypal`, `prepaid` and
`savings`. Plaid publishes a separate product matrix because product availability
varies by account type.

**Project interpretation:** Provider types and subtypes are external descriptive
metadata. They may gate a reviewed Jayburd policy, but they do not establish a
ledger category, normal side, ownership restriction, opening balance or financial
statement presentation. Issue #209 therefore allows only `depository` accounts
with subtype `checking`, `savings`, `money market` or `cash management` to seed a
new monetary asset/debit ledger account. All other combinations fail closed and
remain visible for explicit follow-up.

**Access and freshness limits:** This was a public web-document review. No Plaid
tenant configuration, institution behavior or real account payload was inspected.
Plaid can revise its schema and product matrix; a future change requires a new
review and an explicit Jayburd policy change rather than automatic acceptance.

## AB02 — Plaid Sandbox

**Publisher and source:** Plaid, [Sandbox](https://plaid.com/docs/sandbox/).

**Selected sections reviewed:** Sandbox institution, credential and multi-account
test behavior. The page was accessed 2026-10-19.

**Project interpretation:** Sandbox supports fictional multi-account acceptance
evidence. It does not prove production institution coverage, live credential
handling, complete transaction history or accounting correctness.

## Acceptance use

The fixed synthetic manifest for #209 must include three distinct supported
depository accounts and at least one unsupported account. Tests must prove that
the supported accounts receive distinct ledger/source accounts in one atomic
command while the unsupported account remains visible and unbound. A provider
success screen alone is not acceptance evidence.

documents.title: Available-to-use source record
documents.body:
# Available-to-use source record

Reviewed 2026-10-21 for proposed #251. This record uses the existing annotated
[bibliography](bibliography.md), [decision-evidence requirements](decision-evidence.md)
and linked canonical records. It records selected-section review, not a new
normative conformance review. Project rules and proposals are labeled inference.

| ID | Source and reviewed portion | Fact supported; limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ATU-01 | OpenStax *Financial Accounting*, accounting equation/journals and cash/accrual discussion, as recorded at [S01](database-sources.md#s01--accounting-foundations); selected sections in existing register | Ledger balances and accrued obligations are different concepts; does not define discretionary cash or this Plan formula. |
| ATU-02 | OpenStax *Financial Accounting*, bank reconciliation section, [S02](database-sources.md#s02--reconciliation); selected teaching section | Bank observations and book balances require explicit reconciliation; no claim that a provider balance equals spendable cash. |
| ATU-03 | [Financial reporting contract](../contracts/financial-reporting.md), scope/dates/snapshot and amount semantics; repository design, not external authority | Existing proposal supplies book revision, date, exact decimal and authorization boundaries. #248 may refine Position; reporting design does not approve this Plan metric. |
| ATU-04 | [ISO 20022 FAQ](https://www.iso20022.org/faq), About and Compliance, and [message catalogue](https://www.iso20022.org/catalogue-messages), overview/version navigation; [R01](bibliography.md#r01--iso-20022-faq)–[R02](bibliography.md#r02--iso-20022-message-catalogue) | Registered financial-message use needs a selected definition and profile. No Plan message was selected; normative eight-part text and payment profile not reviewed. |
| ATU-05 | [ISO 4217 overview](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), public overview, [R03](bibliography.md#r03--iso-4217-currency-codes); [multicurrency contract](../contracts/multicurrency.md) representation | Currency codes and minor units are reference metadata, not future FX rates or a cash policy. Release-specific production mapping still requires verification. |
| ATU-06 | [ISO 21378:2019](https://www.iso.org/standard/70823.html), abstract/edition, [R04](bibliography.md#r04--iso-213782019-audit-data-collection); [ISO 21926:2026 preview](https://www.iso.org/obp/ui?_escaped_fragment_=iso%3Astd%3Aiso%3A21926%3Aed-1%3Av1%3Aen), contents/introduction/§1, [R05](bibliography.md#r05--iso-219262026-semantic-data-model-for-audit-data-services) | Audit data and semantic mapping are relevant to future exports. No field-level clauses or full text reviewed, so no Plan export mapping or conformance claim. |
| ATU-07 | [Identity/setup contract](../contracts/identity-setup.md), authentication and authorization sections; repository design | Verified issuer/subject maps to a principal; email and caller IDs cannot confer authority. Future service identity/execution is a separate decision under #56. |

## Interpretation and alternatives

Accounting and reconciliation sources support keeping posted balances separate
from source observations and projections. They do **not** endorse a universal
“available to use” figure. The dated minimum-curve model, overlap rule, reserve
floor and uncertainty behavior are project design proposals. The simpler
cash-minus-reserve model hides due-date shortfalls; the dated model costs more
input review. This tradeoff is for owner/accountant decision, not source fact.

## Gaps and acceptance

No real-entity accounting, legal restriction, debt/tax schedule, forecast
accuracy, data-freshness SLA, service authority, or payment usage profile was
reviewed. Do not infer these from the synthetic development policy. Acceptance
requires owner/accountant review of the contract's questions, fixed independent
worked cases, #248 Position, #1 policy, #56 permissions, and the named tests in
the contract before implementation. A future export or payment workflow must
refresh the applicable standards source review and pin versions/profiles.

documents.title: Background work source review
documents.body:
# Background work source review

## Scope

Selected public sections reviewed 2026-10-13 for #63, starting with bibliography
S13–S15 and G03. Supports the [proposed worker contract](../contracts/background-work.md).
No live provider calls, deployment verification or normative certification.

## BW01 — Transactional outbox

Chris Richardson, [Transactional outbox pattern](https://microservices.io/patterns/data/transactional-outbox.html),
Problem/Solution/Result context reviewed. Durable business changes and message
intent share a transaction; a relay can send twice after a crash, so consumers
need idempotency. This is engineering pattern guidance, not accounting authority.
Our separate sidecars are an inference from this repository's immutable outbox;
the pattern does not approve a particular DDL, fence or retry budget. Alternative:
database-only polling; revisit when measured transport overhead exceeds benefit.

## BW02 — Actual Cloud Tasks behavior

Google Cloud, [Issues and limitations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/common-pitfalls),
Execution order, Duplicate execution, Backoff errors, Resource limitations and
long-running task ramp-up reviewed (page updated 2026-10-09). Delivery order and
absence of duplicate execution cannot be relied upon; overload changes throughput.
**Inference:** operation identity lives in SQL and completion is not queue depth.
No provider statistical percentage establishes our correctness or latency SLO.

Google Cloud REST **v2**, [RetryConfig](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/reference/rest/v2/RetryConfig),
`maxAttempts`, `maxRetryDuration`, backoff fields reviewed. Attempt/duration retry
stopping conditions are documented jointly; queue configuration is not our OR
business limit. **Inference:** enforce attempt/age cutoff durably in the database.
Defaults and mutable service docs must be rechecked when Terraform is implemented.

Google Cloud REST **v2**, [Task resource](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.queues.tasks),
`dispatchDeadline`, schedule/attempt fields reviewed. HTTP deadlines have bounded
supported values; request timeout does not guarantee worker processing stops.
**Inference:** resource fence and commit predicate must survive duplicate handlers;
our handler/lease budgets are project policies, not recommended universal settings.

## BW03 — Enqueue identity and authenticated delivery

Google Cloud REST **v2**, [tasks.create](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.queues.tasks/create),
Request body/task deduplication and response view reviewed. Explicit names can
reject duplicates including recently deleted/executed tasks; hashed IDs are advised.
**Inference:** `ALREADY_EXISTS` is not durable work completion or proof of a live
pending task. Persist generation and recover independently of name retention.
No fixed deduplication window is used as a correctness premise.

Google Cloud, [Create HTTP target tasks](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/creating-http-target-tasks),
Set up service account and Use HTTP target tasks with authentication tokens reviewed.
OIDC service identity supports authenticated Cloud Run invocation; queue overrides
may affect task authentication configuration. **Inference:** pin handler audience
and allowed invocation identity, then separately check current business authority.
No IAM resources or credentials created/read; exact Terraform grants remain a
reviewed deployment deliverable, not a copied sample's assumed suitability.

## BW04 — Database claim semantics

PostgreSQL Global Development Group, PostgreSQL **17**,
[SELECT, Locking Clause](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-select.html#SQL-FOR-UPDATE-SHARE),
reviewed `FOR UPDATE`, `SKIP LOCKED`, queue-like use and inconsistent-view warning.
Short queue claims can skip contended rows; this does not provide fairness,
business ordering or a fence across external calls. **Inference:** deterministic
scan key, durable deadlines, compare-and-set ownership and recovery scans are
separate application requirements. Existing bookkeeping transaction isolation and
authorization locks remain authority for financial operations. Expiring a lease
does not terminate the holder process; verify stale commits with actual SQL tests.

## BW05 — Financial message applicability

ISO 20022 Registration Authority, [FAQ](https://www.iso20022.org/faq), About and
Compliance sections, reviewed 2026-10-13 in the adjacent reporting research.
The methodology/registered messages and community usage requirements must not be
confused with arbitrary JSON field naming. **Inference:** the internal
journal-fact/wakeup pair has no selected external financial-message profile;
owner reviews this bounded applicability assessment before implementation.
Individual ISO message definitions were not exhaustively reviewed. Bibliography
R03–R05 remain currency/audit research authority; no normative audit fields or
new currency recognition policy derived here. Financial provider adapters must
resolve their own required profile/mapping gates under the standards contract.

## BW06 — Acquisition delivery and host review

Refreshed BW02–BW04 on 2026-10-13 for acquisition dispatch: at-least-once
transport, task-name tombstones and cancellation cannot establish SQL completion.
The [acquisition transport profile](../contracts/acquisition-transport.md) selects
separate immutable routes and deadlines. The 80-second HTTP / 85-second task /
90-second server bounds are local policy, leaving room for a 60-second provider
attempt and committed settlement. They are not provider service guarantees.

Google Cloud, [Cloud Run request timeout](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/request-timeout),
request timeout behavior reviewed: a timed-out request does not terminate its
container. Inference: SQL fences and cooperative cancellation remain necessary.

Go, [net/http Server](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http#Server), Serve, Shutdown and Close
reviewed with pinned Go 1.26.9 source for the [host proof](../runbooks/worker-host.md).
Shutdown waits for active connections; Close does not forcibly stop arbitrary Go
handler code. Inference: injected handlers, request-context cancellation, bounded
drain and fixed errors form a reusable lifecycle boundary. This is local synthetic
proof, not Cloud Run termination or deployed IAM evidence.

# Research index

[Position](position-sources.md): P01–05, fixed USD/EUR.
[Available-to-use](available-to-use-sources.md): ATU01–07, proposed.

[Expiry](../contracts/enrollment-availability.md): Go/Cloud Run selections2026-10-24.

[Production](production-pilot-sources.md): PP01–09,2026-10-26.

## Reading order

[Verifier IAM](../contracts/verifier-iam-compatibility.md): Google/PG17,2026-10-23.

[Link recovery](plaid-link-recovery-sources.md): LR01–07, Plaid/React,
2026-10-24; reconnect/OAuth unqualified.

[Plaid #88](plaid-88-test-sources.md): selected official,2026-10-22; hosted gaps.
[Launch Center](plaid-launch-center-review.md): panels,2026-10-22; partial.
[Verifier](../contracts/sandbox-verification.md#sources-standards-and-alternatives):
selected Plaid/PG,2026-10-22; synthetic.
[Identity](sandbox-identity-transport-sources.md): sync/date2026-10-24; hosted unproved.

[PL04](plaid-liability-sources.md): selected loan/product review, 2026-10-22.
[Webhook release](webhook-release-sources.md), [enrollment](webhook-enrollment-sources.md):
[updater](webhook-rollout-sources.md), WU01–07: official selections2026-10-22;
synthetic only.

[History](../contracts/plaid-history-currency.md).
[PI13](plaid-ingestion-sources.md#pi13--source-first-accounthistory-refresh-2026-10-21): Item/account/history; ownership is project policy.

[Plaid types](automatic-account-binding-sources.md), [loans](plaid-liability-sources.md).
[Shared sync](shared-acquisition-sources.md): Plaid cursor/webhooks.
[Removal](binding-review-recovery-sources.md): Item removal and `ITEM_NOT_FOUND` #215.
[Credentials](../contracts/bank-token-vault.md): Plaid/KMS/CRC32C (2026-10-15).

[Sandbox bootstrap](../contracts/sandbox-book-bootstrap.md#standards-and-source-review):
SIX ISO4217 List One (2026-09-17), retrieved2026-10-15 with SHA256 and USD/840/2
review. Bounded local reference evidence; paid ISO text was not reviewed.

[Plaid browser](../contracts/plaid-link-browser.md): Web SDK lifecycle (2026-10-14),
pinned Go source (2026-10-19); synthetic policy, not institution qualification.
[Worker release](../contracts/worker-release.md): bootstrap/runtime federation.
[Operator guide](../../deploy/WORKERS.md): exact-byte promotion/rollback limits.

Worker review (2026-10-14); [#258 rollout/CI sources](plaid-rollout-sources.md)
(selected sections, 2026-10-22):
[Cloud Run ServiceStatus](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rest/v1/namespaces.services#ServiceStatus)
covers generation/Ready/revisions;
[TrafficTarget](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rest/v1/TrafficTarget)
covers revision allocation/tagged routes;
[Scheduler Job/State](https://docs.cloud.google.com/scheduler/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.jobs#State)
covers paused/disabled/error states and HTTP OIDC. Receipt policy requires
reconciled generations, one exact-image 100% target and paused exact Scheduler.
It does not prove queue drain, IAM or provider qualification.

[Connection release](../contracts/connection-release.md): selected HashiCorp
variable precedence/Cloud Run revision sections,2026-10-14. Omitted inputs reset;
version/digest policy is our inference, not hosted/provider proof.

Hosted/Sandbox (2026-10-14):

[PI12 Hosted Link](plaid-ingestion-sources.md#pi12--hosted-link-completion-and-recovery-refresh-2026-10-18):
official guide/API review and snapshot hashes, 2026-10-18. User-associated token
and completion webhook are recommended; browser-only recovery is project policy.

- [Hosted workers](../contracts/hosted-workers.md): selected Cloud Run metadata
  identity, Cloud SQL IAM login and container lifecycle references; understand
  private caller binding and bounded pools. Synthetic checks do not prove hosted IAM.
- [Provider vault](../contracts/provider-vault.md): Infisical v4 create/read,
  GCP ID-token login and GCP sync options, plus Secret Manager numeric addressing
  and CRC32C. Explains why source/logical/destination versions are independent.
- [Hosted evidence](../contracts/hosted-evidence.md): GCS JSON v1 generation
  preconditions, object reads and integrity metadata; selected sections support
  create-only storage and generation-pinned reads, not application authorization.
- [Sandbox qualification](../contracts/plaid-sandbox-qualification.md): official
  Link, Transactions and Sandbox references SQ01–SQ05; distinguishes adapter
  diagnostics, Link event association and complete hosted acceptance.

Sections/inferences/limits recorded; no normative ISO, cloud config or credentials reviewed.

- [Connection lifecycle](../contracts/connection-sql.md), [service](../contracts/connection-service.md)
  and [HTTP boundary](../contracts/connection-http.md): PI05–PI10 distinguish verified
  Link/account evidence, one-shot remote mutations and local credential recovery.
  Dynamic writes/update association remain unqualified.
- [Acquisition runner](../contracts/acquisition-runner.md): PI01/PI02/PI08 guide
  account-filtered pagination, whole-loop restart and explicit API versioning.
  Durable local evidence and current SQL authority are project decisions with
  synthetic fault tests, not provider or cloud guarantees.

The [sync implementation boundary](../contracts/provider-runtime-boundaries.md)
records refreshed Plaid pagination/account-filter sections and PostgreSQL17
isolation/function-privilege sections. It distinguishes vendor mechanisms from
our bounded publication and role decisions. No live-provider or measured scalability proof.

- [Plaid decoder contract](../contracts/plaid-decoder.md): selected official
  transaction/version fields, exact numeric interpretation, inert metadata allowlist
  and limitations. Its [runbook](../runbooks/plaid-decoder.md) separates independent
  fixed/fuzz evidence from provider qualification.
- [Private observer transport](../contracts/observer-transport.md): OT01–OT06 cover
  Cloud Run caller identity, Cloud Tasks request/deduplication semantics and the
  pinned Google verifier. Local synthetic tests do not prove hosted IAM behavior.
- [Provider sync SQL](../contracts/provider-sync-sql.md): forward extensions to
  scoped source history, complete-set publication and current permission checks;
  [runtime boundaries](../contracts/provider-runtime-boundaries.md) explain the
  selected first-slice limits and deferred enrollment.

The [source review contract](../contracts/source-review-sql.md) applies existing
PostgreSQL and accounting source records to category drafts and atomic source-linked
posting. The [generated acquisition contract](../contracts/demo-acquisition.md)
documents fixture design and the absence of live-provider evidence.


The [independent decoder property evidence](../runbooks/import-properties.md)
records reviewed Go1.26.9 `math/big` integer/rational source sections and the
separate exact-money oracle. It supplements parser fuzzing; it does not establish
provider behavior or database isolation.

For bank sync qualification and measurable scaling, read the
[sync quality source review](sync-quality-sources.md): selected official Plaid
lifecycle/Sandbox and Google Cloud concurrency/queue sections, reviewed
2026-10-13. These constrain test design; they do not certify live readiness.

Shared index, updated 2026-10-22; listings do not approve designs or compliance.

Start with these six reading steps:

1. **Learn the books:** OpenStax accounting foundations and reconciliation (S01–S02).
2. **Understand financial interchange:** ISO 20022 FAQ and catalogue (R01–R02).
3. **Separate currency codes from FX accounting:** ISO 4217, then the applicable
   accounting framework's currency rules (R03, R06–R07).
4. **Design the data:** BCcampus relational design (S03), then audit-data
   definitions and semantic modelling (R04–R05).
5. **Protect posting and closing:** PostgreSQL constraints/isolation and the SSI
   paper (S06–S12).
6. **Handle asynchronous work:** transactional outbox and actual Cloud Tasks
   semantics (S13–S15), then migration/access tooling (S18–S20).

## How to read the review labels

- **Selected sections reviewed:** only the sections identified in the detailed
  source record were read; never infer a cover-to-cover review.
- **Overview / abstract / preview only:** useful for discovery and scope;
  insufficient evidence for unseen detailed requirements.
- **Pending:** a reading destination, not supporting evidence for a design claim.

The [database source register](database-sources.md) is the authoritative home for
S01–S22 citation metadata, exact sections, findings and limitations. The table
below is a navigation guide, not a second copy of those evidence records.

## Accounting, database and engineering resources

| ID and resource | What it is and why read it | Review status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [S01 — OpenStax financial accounting](database-sources.md#s01--accounting-foundations) | Free textbook introduction to the accounting equation, journals and double-entry. Start here for the business vocabulary. | Selected sections reviewed |
| [S02 — OpenStax bank reconciliation](database-sources.md#s02--reconciliation) | Worked teaching material for comparing bank statements with book balances and identifying adjustments. | Selected sections reviewed |
| [S03 — Watt & Eng, Database Design, 2nd ed.](database-sources.md#s03--relational-design-textbook) | Open textbook on ER models, normalization and the design process; useful before drawing our schema. | Selected chapters reviewed |
| [S04 — Codd, relational model (1970)](database-sources.md#s04--relational-independence) | Foundational research explaining logical data independence; background for separating business models from storage choices. | Opening sections reviewed |
| [S05 — Ellerman, double-entry mathematics (2014)](database-sources.md#s05--double-entry-mathematics) | Mathematical account of debit/credit pairs and signed representations; helps reason about signs and reversals. | Pages 1–7 reviewed; not accounting-policy authority |
| [S06 — Ports & Grittner, PostgreSQL SSI (2012)](database-sources.md#s06--serializable-snapshot-isolation) | Research paper on serializable isolation, including a close/report anomaly relevant to period locking. | Overview and §§2–3 reviewed; older PostgreSQL implementation |
| [S07 — PostgreSQL constraints](database-sources.md#s07--database-constraints) | Official reference for CHECK, keys and references; identifies limits of row-local enforcement. | Selected PostgreSQL 17 sections reviewed |
| [S08 — PostgreSQL isolation](database-sources.md#s08--isolation-semantics) | Official behavior of snapshots, isolation levels and transaction retries. | Selected PostgreSQL 17 sections reviewed |
| [S09 — PostgreSQL row security](database-sources.md#s09--row-level-security) | Official RLS rules and bypass caveats; relevant to separate LLC books. | Selected PostgreSQL 17 sections reviewed |
| [S10 — PostgreSQL numeric types](database-sources.md#s10--exact-amounts) | Exact numeric storage, precision and special values; useful when specifying money validation. | Selected PostgreSQL 17 sections reviewed |
| [S11 — PostgreSQL triggers](database-sources.md#s11--deferred-enforcement) | Mechanism reference for a candidate deferred balance check. | Selected PostgreSQL 17 sections reviewed |
| [S12 — PostgreSQL function security](database-sources.md#s12--restricted-posting-functions) | Privilege and search-path rules for a candidate restricted posting function. | Selected PostgreSQL 17 sections reviewed |
| [S13 — Helland, Data on the Outside versus Data on the Inside (2005)](database-sources.md#s13--internal-state-versus-messages) | Paper about service data and transaction boundaries; useful before splitting services. | Introduction/§1 reviewed |
| [S14 — Richardson, transactional outbox](database-sources.md#s14--transactional-outbox) | Pattern description for committing business changes and message intent together. | Pattern sections reviewed |
| [S15 — Google Cloud Tasks pitfalls](database-sources.md#s15--actual-queue-semantics) | Provider documentation about duplicates and ordering; grounds retry assumptions in the planned transport. | Relevant sections reviewed; recheck at implementation |
| [S16 — Square Books (2019)](database-sources.md#s16--production-ledger-case-study) | Engineering case study of an immutable double-entry ledger; example rather than a universal blueprint. | Accounting/model sections reviewed |
| [S17 — Fowler, Event Sourcing (2005)](database-sources.md#s17--event-sourcing-distinction) | Pattern explanation of state reconstruction and replay costs; helps distinguish ledger history from full event sourcing. | Selected sections reviewed |
| [S18 — Sadalage & Fowler, Evolutionary Database Design](database-sources.md#s18--evolving-schemas) | Design article about incremental schema changes and coordination with application releases. | Selected sections reviewed |
| [S19 — sqlc documentation](database-sources.md#s19--sql-generated-access) | Tool reference for generating Go access from SQL and binding queries to transactions. | Overview and versioned transaction guide reviewed |
| [S20 — golang-migrate documentation](database-sources.md#s20--migration-tool-guarantees) | Owner-selected migration tool's format and failure-handling reference. | v4.20.1 format/FAQ sections reviewed |
| [S21 — Kleppmann & Riccomini, Designing Data-Intensive Applications, 2nd ed.](database-sources.md#s21--additional-book-preview-only) | Broader systems textbook for further study of distributed-data tradeoffs. | Publisher introduction/contents preview only |
| [S22 — GORM documentation](database-sources.md#s22--orm-counterexample) | Alternative-tool reference separating explicit transactions from automatic schema migration. | Transaction/migration pages reviewed |

## Standards and multicurrency resources

These R entries are the canonical bibliographic records for this additional
reading set. Access/review date: 2026-10-11. Full normative texts and applicable
amendments must be reviewed before claiming detailed conformance.

### R01 — ISO 20022 FAQ

**Publisher/link:** ISO 20022 Registration Authority,
[Frequently asked questions](https://www.iso20022.org/faq).
**What it is:** official orientation to the financial-message methodology,
repository and implementation context. **Use:** understand what an ISO 20022
claim means before designing integrations. **Reviewed:** About and Compliance
sections of the public FAQ. **Limit:** not a review of the eight normative parts
or a particular bank's usage requirements.

### R02 — ISO 20022 message catalogue

**Publisher/link:** ISO 20022 Registration Authority,
[Catalogue of messages](https://www.iso20022.org/catalogue-messages).
**What it is:** entry point to registered definitions, schemas, Message Definition
Reports and available usage guides. **Use:** select exact versions and obtain
the artifacts required by an integration contract. **Reviewed:** catalogue
documentation/version overview. **Pending:** individual messages and bank profiles;
no implementation version has been selected.

### R03 — ISO 4217 currency codes

**Publisher/link:** ISO, [Currency codes](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html).
**What it is:** official overview of currency identifiers, minor units and their
maintenance. **Use:** currency reference-data design and a route to the designated
maintenance agency. **Reviewed:** public overview. **Limit:** neither an exchange-rate
feed nor a source of recognition, remeasurement or rounding policy; the actual
data release used by software must be recorded separately.

### R04 — ISO 21378:2019, Audit data collection

**Publisher/link:** ISO, [standard page](https://www.iso.org/standard/70823.html).
**What it is:** common accounting data definitions for audit extraction across
ledger and related business areas. **Use:** assess accountant/auditor export
mappings. **Reviewed:** public abstract and edition metadata; the page records
confirmation in 2025. **Limit:** full standard not reviewed; field-level requirements
and mappings remain pending.

### R05 — ISO 21926:2026, Semantic data model for audit data services

**Publisher/link:** ISO, [official browsing preview](https://www.iso.org/obp/ui?_escaped_fragment_=iso%3Astd%3Aiso%3A21926%3Aed-1%3Av1%3Aen).
**What it is:** a framework for modelling accounting/audit semantics and binding
them to exchange formats, building on audit-data definitions. **Use:** evaluate
our shared glossary, semantic contracts and export mappings. **Reviewed:** contents,
introduction and §1 Scope. **Limit:** detailed modelling clauses and annexes remain
unreviewed; it does not supply a complete physical ledger schema or implementation.

### R06 — FASB Accounting Standards Codification, including Topic 830

**Publisher/link:** Financial Accounting Standards Board,
[Accounting Standards Codification](https://asc.fasb.org/).
**What it is:** the US GAAP codification; Topic 830 is the foreign-currency research
target. **Use:** resolve US GAAP policy and exact paragraph-level requirements if
that reporting basis is selected. **Status: pending normative review.** The site
returned no readable body in this research tool. Do not cite unseen paragraphs
or substitute an accounting firm's interpretation for the authoritative text.
Applicable version, amendments and effective dates still need recording.

### R07 — IAS 21, The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates

**Publisher/link:** IFRS Foundation,
[IAS 21 official overview](https://www.ifrs.org/issued-standards/list-of-standards/ias-21-the-effects-of-changes-in-foreign-exchange-rates/).
**What it is:** IFRS guidance concerning foreign-currency transactions, functional
currency and financial-statement translation. **Use:** research the IFRS currency
model and distinguish transaction, functional and presentation currencies.
**Reviewed:** About and standard-history overview only. **Limit:** full operative
paragraphs and effective amendments remain pending; IFRS must not silently become
the policy for a US GAAP book.

## Testing resources

The [synthetic accounting resource register](testing-sources.md) describes T01
Beancount, T02 hledger, T03 ISO 20022 artifacts and T04 the MIT synthetic
accounting generator, with pins, review depth, rights and observed limitations.

The [posting policy source notes](posting-sources.md) add P01 accrual mechanics
and the US GAAP authority gap, P02 numeric rounding, P03 restricted functions and
P04 strict JSON/replay handling, P05 pinned pgx transactions, P06 reference
serialization and P07 provider corrections (2026-10-25 selections).

The [identity source notes](identity-sources.md) add I01–I06: managed ID-token
verification, revocation, TOTP MFA the pinned Firebase Admin Go API and dependency maintenance evidence. These
support the identity/setup contract and isolated provider configuration/state;
live deployment evidence remains separate.

## Cloud delivery resources

The [GCP source register](gcp-sources.md) describes managed request billing,
Cloud Tasks pricing and duplicate delivery, Cloud SQL connectivity and IAM
authentication, Terraform mock tests, state bootstrap, GitHub federation, the pinned Cloud SQL connector and restricted
migration role design, standalone packaging, image provenance limits and private
service invocation, runtime identity configuration, and explicit quota-project settings for user ADC bootstrap. Read its section-level review limits before implementing cloud
delivery; provider documentation and budget assumptions are not deployment proof.
G24 reviews Cloud SQL IAM database-role assignment and pinned provider behavior
for a possible administrator bootstrap path; it does not establish role compatibility
or authorize elevated application logins.
G25 covers the pinned owner-operated IAM proxy, private socket boundary and
outbound connector requirement; read it before diagnosing bootstrap connectivity.
G26 records Cloud Shell command access and its owner-administration boundary,
including observed CLI behavior and the distinction from runtime authentication.
G27 describes immutable job execution metadata and completion counts used to bind
migration evidence to the approved image and workload identity.

## Agent maintenance rules

The first application adds three source registers: [server composition](server-sources.md)
for bounded HTTP, workload identity and PostgreSQL pooling;
[browser authentication](browser-auth-sources.md) for memory-only sign-in and
TOTP enrollment/challenge and explicit email verification through hosted action links and the isolated local rehearsal (BA04); and [frontend behavior](frontend-sources.md) for
Next.js patch advisories/React/browser tests. The [integration source notes](app-integration-sources.md)
record generated OpenAPI types, Node LTS and CI choices. Read their stated review
depth and limits; offline tests do not verify live provider configuration.

[Recovery and application integration](recovery-sources.md) reviews PostgreSQL
transaction/lock behavior, OWASP browser-storage guidance and Playwright real
response interception. It supports durable reviewed commands and synthetic
browser/API/database proofs; it does not establish live identity or accounting approval.

The [contract-design source notes](contract-sources.md) add C01 (PostgreSQL
schemas/locking), C02 (OpenAPI 3.1.1), C03 (RFC 9457 HTTP problems) and C04
(public AASB 121 currency guidance). Read them alongside the SQL/API contracts.
C04 is a limited paragraph review of an Australian source incorporating IAS 21,
not a substitute for pending US GAAP research.

Use stable S/R identifiers when linking a source to an ADR or contract. Read the
underlying section before relying on it, and update its canonical record with
title, publisher, version, section/pages, access date, relevance and limitations.
Keep discovery separate from reviewed evidence. Cite direct authoritative links
in decisions; this index is a navigation aid, not a substitute for the source.
Do not mirror copyrighted texts or infer approval from a bibliography entry.

Apply the [decision evidence standard](decision-evidence.md) and
[standards applicability contract](../contracts/standards.md). Maintain these
records in the same change as a source-dependent decision. Unresolved FX policy,
message-profile selection and export mappings remain research work; this guide
does not declare them complete.

Runtime rollout, job ordering, IAM ingress and revocation permission references are annotated as G19–G23 in the [GCP source register](gcp-sources.md).

G28 in the [GCP source register](gcp-sources.md#g28--node-runtime-image-contents--2026-10-12)
reviews Node maintainers' guidance on excluding build package managers from runtime.

G29 in the [GCP source register](gcp-sources.md#g29--execution-field-serialization--2026-10-12)
records Cloud Run timeout encoding and CLI array projections, checked against the
first completed migration execution.

G30 in the [GCP source register](gcp-sources.md#g30--read-only-migration-metadata-snapshot--2026-10-12)
reviews PostgreSQL 17 read-only restrictions and snapshot limits for workload-owned
migration verification.

## Financial review and import design — 2026-10-13

- [Financial reporting sources](financial-reporting-sources.md), FR01–FR05:
  OpenStax statement relationships, PostgreSQL snapshot/row-lock semantics,
  OWASP CSV hazards, ISO applicability/access limits and IETF transport formats.
  Selected sections support the proposed report contract; normative audit mappings,
  real accounting policy and performance acceptance remain open.
- [Workspace source notes](financial-workspace-sources.md), FW01–FW02:
  W3C focus and table guidance used for the isolated synthetic prototype.
  DOM checks are not visual, keyboard, screen-reader or accessibility-conformance
  evidence; actual browser and owner review remain pending.
- Reporting cursor encoding: [RFC 4648 sections 3.2–3.5 and 5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4648)
  defines padding, alphabet and canonical base64url behavior;
  [Go encoding/base64](https://pkg.go.dev/encoding/base64) documents the raw URL
  encoding and strict decoder. Reviewed these sections on 2026-10-13 for the
  reporting HTTP profile: unpadded encoding, exact re-encoding check and bounded
  input. This is transport syntax, not accounting standard conformance or an
  authorization token; scope/revision validation remains in SQL. The
  [HTTP contract source register](../contracts/reporting-http.md#sources-and-applicability)
  records RH01/RH02 and the selected profile.
- [Statement-import sources](statement-import-sources.md), SI01–SI06:
  RFC CSV/date syntax, ISO message catalogue, SIX currency maintenance, OWASP
  upload boundaries and OpenStax reconciliation. The custom synthetic CSV is a
  proposed internal template, not a verified bank adapter or ISO message;
  its standards exception and later camt profile still require review.

## Provider ingestion and worker delivery — 2026-10-13

Reporting follow-up source records:
[CSV review profile](../contracts/report-export.md#sources-and-alternatives) rechecks
RFC 4180 quoting/CRLF and OWASP formula hazards for a fixed, generated-field
download; [pinned journal review](../contracts/report-drill.md#sources-and-alternatives)
uses PostgreSQL 17 snapshot and restricted-function guidance. These support
internal transport and authorization choices, not normative accountant-export
mapping or an ISO-conformance claim.

- [Plaid ingestion sources](plaid-ingestion-sources.md): official API, connection,
  lifecycle, webhook and source-precision reviews. Notes distinguish provider
  behavior from Jayburd policy; no
  provider Sandbox, live account or ISO message-conformance evidence is implied.
- [Background-work sources](background-work-sources.md): primary references for
  queue delivery limitations, authentication and database claim/receipt semantics.
  These support the proposed lifecycle and fault matrix, not an implemented
  publisher, deployed worker or measured operational guarantee.

- [Worker SQL source review](../contracts/worker-sql.md#source-review-and-alternatives),
  WS01–WS03: PostgreSQL 17 locking, actual-clock timestamps and SECURITY DEFINER
  guidance for the journal-observer schema/functions. These primary sections
  explain mechanisms; migration8 and the named role, race and receipt tests
  are recorded in [foundation evidence](../runbooks/ingestion-foundations.md).
  Hosted queue delivery remains unproved.
- [Decoder implementation source review](../contracts/statement-decoder.md#implementation-evidence-and-alternatives):
  Go's standard `encoding/csv` behavior explains why this restricted synthetic
  profile validates ASCII and physical CRLF records before quoted-field parsing.
  This supports parser design only; it does not establish bank-format support,
  source ownership, durable import or ledger correctness.

Durable source import design: [DI01–DI03](../contracts/durable-import.md#standards-sources-and-alternatives)
records selected PostgreSQL constraint/isolation, OWASP upload and Plaid transaction
identity sections, their interpretation and access limits. These support proposed
persistence and overlap decisions; they do not establish implemented ingestion or
ISO exchange conformance.

- [Local observer runtime source application](../contracts/observer-runtime.md#evidence-and-sources): existing queue/SQL/pgx sources support short committed claims, injected transport and uncertain-commit handling. Read its named fault evidence separately from future hosted delivery proof.

## Source collection foundations — 2026-10-13

- [Source registry applicability and sources](../contracts/source-registry.md#standards-sources-and-alternatives): applies the existing PostgreSQL key/locking/function and ISO currency source records to narrow synthetic enrollment. Operator attestation is not evidence of live account ownership.

Documented limits include cancellation, cooperative locking, power-loss evidence and separately required hosted encryption/retention.

- [Connections workspace contract](../contracts/connection-workspace.md): application

- [Connection operations source application](plaid-ingestion-sources.md#connection-operations-review--2026-10-13): refreshed official webhook signature/key and sync-notification sections; distinguishes provider requirements from local replay, cache and transaction policies. Signed synthetic proofs do not qualify hosted delivery or actual institution behavior.

- [Acquisition delivery and HTTP host review](background-work-sources.md#bw06--acquisition-delivery-and-host-review): refreshed official Cloud Tasks/Cloud Run timing and Go server lifecycle sections; distinguishes local fencing policy and loopback evidence from hosted qualification.

- [Controlled canary job sources](../contracts/delivery-job.md#sources-alternatives-and-evidence):
  Google provider v8.6.0 job schema and Infisical GCP ID Token Auth guide, reviewed

- [Canary metadata lookup](../contracts/delivery-job.md): reviewed Infisical Retrieve
  query parameters for value-disabled exact-version discovery. Synthetic tests

### Hosted Sandbox smoke test (2026-10-14)

This supports issue #118's synthetic regression, not full Sandbox qualification.

documents.title: Binding review recovery sources
documents.body:
# Binding review recovery sources

Reviewed 2026-10-19 for issue #215.

## Plaid Items API

- Source: <https://plaid.com/docs/api/items/#itemremove>
- Review depth: endpoint purpose, request/response, token invalidation, and
  offboarding guidance.
- Fact: Plaid documents `/item/remove` as the endpoint for removing an Item and
  says the Item access token and associated processor/bank-account tokens become
  invalid. Plaid recommends it when a user disconnects and requires it to end
  billing for subscription products unless the user already revoked access.
- Project decision: a Jayburd binding-review cancellation is not complete until
  provider removal is confirmed. Local state alone cannot represent revoked
  provider access.

## Plaid Item errors

- Source: <https://plaid.com/docs/errors/item/#item-not-found>
- Review depth: `ITEM_NOT_FOUND` definition, causes, and recovery guidance.
- Fact: Plaid says `ITEM_NOT_FOUND` can mean the Item was previously removed by
  `/item/remove`, removed by the user, or removed by Plaid.
- Project decision: only on the exact already-fenced Item-removal retry,
  `ITEM_NOT_FOUND` is accepted as the terminal already-removed result. It is not
  treated as success for account reads, exchange, or any other operation.

## Access limits and standards

The public documentation was reviewed; no provider payload, dashboard record,
credential, or bank data was collected. Item removal is a proprietary lifecycle
operation rather than an ISO 20022 business message. Existing ISO 4217 currency
and accounting contracts remain applicable to binding completion.
