documents.body:
# Brainblast tooling assessment

## Scope and evidence

Read-only inspection on 2026-10-11 of the local Brainblast checkout at base
commit `3440feb`. The worktree is dirty; inspected behavior includes local
uncommitted changes. No external-vault content or implementation was copied.
Only focused synthetic tests were run; this is not a whole-vault audit or a
live GitHub synchronization proof.

| Check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| `ruby scripts/brainblast/test_query_layer.rb` | PASS: 4 tests, 12 assertions |
| `ruby .codex/skills/sync-project-tasks/scripts/test_sync_tasks.rb` | PASS: 6 tests, 27 assertions |
| Temporary synthetic task referencing an absent predecessor, run through `work_queue.rb --format json` | REPRODUCED: `dependencies_ready=true`, expected false |
| Installed GitHub CLI 2.96.0 | Native dependency and sub-issue flags available |

## Keep

Bounded context packets; one authoritative note per decision; links between
contracts/tasks/evidence; explicit predecessor graphs; dry-run mutation plans;
stable identities; focused validation; compact next-action handoffs.

## Adapt or defer

The queue scans root task notes, treats unknown dependencies as satisfied and
accepts canceled tasks as predecessors completed. Its priority map also omits
critical, and epic ordering has a project-specific path. Do not use it unchanged
as an execution gate. Focused sync tests cover formatting and identity helpers;
they do not demonstrate full remote conflict/race correctness.

GitHub's native issue dependencies/sub-issues reduce the need for custom task
graph synchronization. Keep project context in this repo; omit a separate vault
status system, custom leases for AI agents, semantic/vector search and complex
catalog governance until demonstrated scale requires them.

## Sources

Local paths inspected: `scripts/brainblast/work_queue.rb`,
`scripts/brainblast/query_layer.rb`, `test_query_layer.rb`, and the
`sync-project-tasks` skill/scripts. Current platform capabilities:
[dependencies](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/creating-issue-dependencies),
[sub-issues](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues),
[Project automation](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/using-the-built-in-automations).

documents.title: Browser authentication sources
documents.body:
# Browser authentication sources

Reviewed 2026-10-11, relevant official documentation sections; no live provider
requests or credential inspection. Contract: [browser authentication](../contracts/browser-auth.md).

## BA01 — Firebase TOTP for the Web

[Google TOTP guide](https://firebase.google.com/docs/auth/web/totp-mfa),
“Before you begin”, “Enroll users in TOTP MFA” and “Sign in users with a second
factor”. Identity Platform and verified email are prerequisites. Enrollment uses
a fresh first-factor session; sign-in completion uses a managed resolver and TOTP
assertion. Documentation treats enrollment and sign-in separately and does not
establish that enrollment alone produces the backend-required second-factor claim.
Our inference: after enrollment, sign out and require a new password/TOTP challenge.
Manual setup-key entry is supported; no remote QR service is used. Recovery remains
operator-owned. Multiple pre-existing TOTP factors are rejected in this first UI;
operator recovery or a future explicit factor picker is required.

## BA02 — Firebase authentication persistence

[Google persistence guide](https://firebase.google.com/docs/auth/web/auth-state-persistence),
“Supported types of Auth state persistence” and persistence modification. Memory
persistence clears state on refresh; browser default local persistence would survive
window closure. Decision: initialize Auth directly with `inMemoryPersistence`;
no cookie session or local/session storage is used. This sacrifices persistent login
for a smaller session surface. Clearing JavaScript references is not secure memory
erasure and does not protect a compromised browser.

## Acceptance and limits

`AuthController` and `FirebaseAdapter boundary` Vitest suites exercise managed-SDK
boundaries with synthetic responses: memory configuration, verified invitation,
TOTP-only tokens, enrollment isolation, cancellation, failure redaction and stale
session suppression. They do not prove project configuration, recovery controls,
provider availability or end-to-end MFA. Those require an approved synthetic
provider release test before deployment. Google Go verification remains authoritative.

## BA03 — Firebase email verification and hosted actions

Reviewed 2026-10-12: [Manage users](https://firebase.google.com/docs/auth/web/manage-users),
“Send a user a verification email”; [JavaScript Auth reference](https://firebase.google.com/docs/reference/js/auth),
`sendEmailVerification` and `reload`; [email action handlers](https://firebase.google.com/docs/auth/custom-email-handler),
default-handler introduction. SDK methods send to the authenticated user and
reload provider account data; Firebase supplies a default hosted action handler.
The TOTP guide's prerequisites require verified email. Review covers these sections,
not the whole reference. Implementation remains pinned to Firebase 13.0.0.
Our inference: explicit send, provider-hosted links, and a fresh login after
verification avoid custom mail/URL handling. The 60-second UI resend interval is
our choice, not a documented provider quota. Live sender, inbox delivery and
expired-link behavior are unproven and require owner review.

## BA04 — Separate static rehearsal build

Reviewed 2026-10-12: [Vite build options](https://vite.dev/config/build-options)
(output directory, source maps) and [shared options](https://vite.dev/config/shared-options)
(root, public directory, environment directory and Oxc JSX configuration).
These configure a separate browser bundle; they do not provide authentication or
network isolation. The implementation pins the existing Vite 8.3.4 toolchain as
a direct dev dependency and disables public-file copying, environment-file loading
and source maps. Our Node server restricts serving independently. BA01–BA03 remain
the provider authority. Synthetic browser interception cannot prove real mail,
revocation or API-key restrictions; the owner performs that separate rehearsal.

BA04 operator setup also reviewed Google's [Identity Platform REST guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/identity-platform/docs/use-rest-api),
“Before you begin”: Providers → Application setup details exposes the application's
`apiKey`. Only the owner copies that browser identifier into the rehearsal; no
Admin token/credential retrieval commands or REST login examples are executed.

documents.title: Contract design source notes
documents.body:
# Contract design source notes

Accessed 2026-10-11. These records extend the [bibliography](bibliography.md).
Proposals and test requirements are project inferences, not source requirements.

## C01 — PostgreSQL namespaces and privileges

PostgreSQL 17, [§5.10 Schemas](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/ddl-schemas.html).
Reviewed §§5.10.1–6: qualification, privileges and search-path trust. Supports
separate names/grants; does not prescribe our six schemas or tenant layout.
[ADR 0004](../decisions/0004-schema-ownership.md) records the chosen convention.
Also reviewed [SELECT locking clause](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-select.html)
and retained S08/S12 isolation/function-security evidence. Row-locking reads need
careful privilege/transaction design; names alone provide no security proof.

## C02 — OpenAPI Specification 3.1.1

OpenAPI Initiative, [specification](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.1.html).
Reviewed Schema Object §4.8.24 and Reference Object §4.8.23; consulted operation,
response and security object definitions for the draft interface. Describes HTTP
contracts with JSON Schema-compatible shapes. Our operation names, decimal-string
encoding, revision checks and endpoint scope are application choices. OpenAPI is
not an ISO financial-message schema or an authorization implementation.

## C03 — RFC 9457, Problem Details for HTTP APIs

IETF, [RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457.html), 2023.
Reviewed §3 and §3.1 fields and §5 security considerations. Supports structured
HTTP errors with safe detail and extension fields. Our code vocabulary, request
IDs and HTTP status mapping are explicit project choices; avoid leaking internals.

## C04 — Public AASB 121 compilation incorporating IAS 21

Australian Accounting Standards Board,
[AASB 121 October 2023 compilation](https://standards.aasb.gov.au/aasb-121-oct-2023).
Reviewed comparison with IAS 21, operative-period metadata and paragraphs
21–23, 27–29. This compilation applies to periods beginning in 2025–2026.
An attempted older PDF URL was inaccessible; the official HTML was readable.

Evidence: initial transaction-date valuation; different subsequent treatment for
monetary, historical-cost and fair-value items; ordinary monetary exchange
differences in earnings with exceptions. These motivate the conditional FX
examples and separation of foreign quantity from functional carrying amount.
Limit: Australian normative source incorporating IAS 21, not US GAAP authority;
Australian-specific clauses and unreviewed exceptions are not adopted. Full
ASC 830 review is still needed for a US GAAP policy. No claim that reading this
subset establishes general IFRS/AASB compliance or covers consolidation/hedging.

## Review decisions and gaps

Numeric limits, rounding, function boundary and book-lock protocol are proposals
with named tests, not decisions dictated by literature. The owner accepted domain
schemas. Reporting basis, functional-currency policy and automated FX exceptions
remain unapproved. See [policy register](../contracts/accounting-scenarios.md).

documents.title: Bookkeeping database research: first decision review
documents.body:
# Bookkeeping database research: first decision review

## Recommendation

Keep a normalized PostgreSQL ledger with atomic, immutable posted journals.
Separate source observations, editable drafts and posted accounting. Keep one
ledger authority with Go entrypoints; use asynchronous work outside the posting
transaction. Retain golang-migrate and prefer explicit SQL with later pgx/sqlc.
These are project recommendations, not a universally agreed software stack.

Research-only review, 2026-10-11. No schema or application implementation is
authorized by these findings. [Source register](database-sources.md) records
22 source entries, including one publisher-preview-only book. Findings distinguish
documented behavior from our proposed application of it.

## Findings that affect our design

| Question | Source-backed finding | Project recommendation or unresolved choice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What is the accounting core? | Equal debit/credit totals and traceable journals underpin double-entry [S01](database-sources.md#s01--accounting-foundations), [S05](database-sources.md#s05--double-entry-mathematics). | One journal with multiple lines, never a fixed two-row model. Determine normal balances and sign presentation explicitly. |
| Are bank transactions the books? | Reconciliation distinguishes timing differences, errors and book adjustments [S02](database-sources.md#s02--reconciliation). | Import observations and matches separately; classification creates drafts before posting. |
| How should we model data? | ER modelling and dependency analysis precede physical details [S03](database-sources.md#s03--relational-design-textbook), [S04](database-sources.md#s04--relational-independence). | Review a normalized operational model, initially targeting 3NF; retain justified immutable snapshots and derive reporting views. No early warehouse schema. |
| Does a transaction guarantee correctness? | Isolation levels have materially different behaviors [S06](database-sources.md#s06--serializable-snapshot-isolation), [S08](database-sources.md#s08--isolation-semantics). | Prototype SERIALIZABLE for ledger mutations; compare explicit locking only after defining the same invariants. Retry the whole transaction without external side effects. |
| Can CHECK enforce balance? | Cross-row CHECK guarantees are unsupported [S07](database-sources.md#s07--database-constraints). | Review an owned posting function and/or deferred constraint triggers; include empty journals and alternate mutation paths. |
| Does entity_id secure multiple LLCs? | Foreign keys and RLS enforce different boundaries [S07](database-sources.md#s07--database-constraints), [S09](database-sources.md#s09--row-level-security). | Entity-scoped references plus trusted authorization; test RLS with actual runtime roles if adopted. Shared tables versus separate databases remains a deployment choice. |
| Which money type? | Exact numeric still has scale coercion and special values [S10](database-sources.md#s10--exact-amounts). | Choose bounded numeric or integer minor units after currency/precision policy. Reject nonfinite values; define rounding at the boundary. |
| Does ledger history require event sourcing? | Full event sourcing adds reconstruction/replay obligations [S17](database-sources.md#s17--event-sourcing-distinction); immutable ledgers also exist as ordinary SQL services [S16](database-sources.md#s16--production-ledger-case-study). | Append-only posted facts and linked correction entries; do not source every application state transition as an event. |
| Are small services inherently better? | Messages cross trust/transaction boundaries [S13](database-sources.md#s13--internal-state-versus-messages). | Separate executables where useful, while keeping accounting writes under one contract. Source evidence does not justify a database per job. |
| What does an outbox buy? | Durable intent and repeatable delivery; queues may duplicate/reorder [S14](database-sources.md#s14--transactional-outbox), [S15](database-sources.md#s15--actual-queue-semantics). | Durable idempotency and stale-work checks; define per-source sequencing if needed. No exactly-once or FIFO claim. |
| Is an ORM wrong? | Both sqlc and GORM can participate in explicit transactions [S19](database-sources.md#s19--sql-generated-access), [S22](database-sources.md#s22--orm-counterexample). | Prefer SQL-first for this ledger's reviewability. No claim of inherent ORM unsafety or demonstrated performance superiority. |
| Must we finish all database design first? | Reviewed migrations support incremental evolution [S18](database-sources.md#s18--evolving-schemas), [S20](database-sources.md#s20--migration-tool-guarantees). | Complete the contract for one slice, then implement/test it; avoid freezing hypothetical future providers and features. |

## Unresolved enforcement alternatives

This table is a proposal for JB-002, not approval to build either option.

| Alternative | Benefit | Obligation before acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Narrow PostgreSQL posting function; revoke application direct ledger DML | One database entrypoint can validate the complete journal | Prove caller authority, secure function ownership/search_path/EXECUTE grants, and correct audit/outbox/idempotency participation [S12](database-sources.md#s12--restricted-posting-functions) |
| Go transaction plus database constraint triggers | Explicit Go orchestration with final database validation | Cover header and lines, empty journals, correction paths, concurrent edits and role bypasses; deferred triggers alone do not establish the protocol [S11](database-sources.md#s11--deferred-enforcement) |

Current preference: evaluate a small database posting boundary for structural
ledger invariants, with Go handling workflows and user-facing policy. Assign each
rule one owner; do not maintain competing copies in Go and SQL. Decide after the
role matrix and transaction schedules are reviewed.

## Concrete counterexample to review

The SSI paper's batch example includes a writer reading an old batch, a closer
advancing the batch, and a report missing the late write (section 2.1.2, pp. 2–3).
Our analogous risk is a report that claims a closed month while a previously
started posting can still affect it. This is an application of the paper, not
a discovered bug in our unimplemented software. [S06](database-sources.md#s06--serializable-snapshot-isolation)

Require a documented serialization point for close, post and report publication.
Review whole-transaction retries, close-time policy checks and report snapshot
semantics together. Serializable execution alone does not define business rules
for when a month may close. The desired test asserts no successfully closed report
can silently change through a later accepted posting.

## Research-to-design path

| Step | Deliverable before implementation | Owner / issue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Accounting scenarios | Fictional month; basis, currency, opening balances, corrections, bank/card/owner/intercompany examples | Owner, JB-001 / #1 |
| 2. Logical design | Glossary, row grain, candidate keys, relationships, functional dependencies and provenance | Schema review, JB-002 / #2 |
| 3. Physical/transaction contract | Column dictionary, constraints, role matrix, write entrypoints, isolation/lock order, idempotency and report semantics | Schema review, JB-002 / #2 |
| 4. Adversarial test specification | Named failure, race, privilege, replay, reconciliation and restoration cases | JB-002 with JB-003 / #3 |
| 5. Review decision | Accepted ADR with exact source sections, assumptions, alternatives, rejection reasons and owner approval | Owner + implementer |
| 6. First implementation slice | Reviewed migration and PostgreSQL contract tests, then typed queries and application code | After steps 1–5 |

## Boundaries and deferred claims

No source establishes our tax treatment, accountant approval, latency target,
tenant volume or GCP cost. No benchmark or schema experiment ran in this session.
Go/Cloud Run and sqlc remain engineering choices; these readings are not proof
that alternatives cannot work. Spanner, Kafka, sharding, a full event store and
DuckDB require a concrete workload before reconsideration. Full currency conversion,
consolidation/eliminations, legal retention and multi-book accounting need their own
policy/source review rather than being inferred from this foundational pass.

The existing [migration tooling PR #14](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/pull/14)
was verified merged on 2026-10-11 during this research session. That delivers
tooling, not an approved ledger schema. Read this review before advancing product
schema decisions.

documents.title: Database and bookkeeping source register
documents.body:
# Database and bookkeeping source register

For reading order, topic descriptions and the standards/multicurrency resources,
see the [annotated bibliography](bibliography.md). This register retains the
detailed S01–S22 evidence records.

## Scope and method

Targeted public-web research, accessed 2026-10-11. Queries covered relational
design, accounting, PostgreSQL isolation, ledger case studies, outbox delivery,
ORM alternatives and migrations. Followed publisher/author links and read the
sections identified below. This is a focused review, not an exhaustive literature
review or a claim to have read every book/paper cover to cover. No books or papers
are mirrored here; notes are short original paraphrases.

Prefer accounting texts for accounting concepts; versioned PostgreSQL manuals
for PostgreSQL behavior; original papers for mechanisms; vendor cases for examples.
An arXiv listing is not itself peer-review evidence. Search-result timestamps were
not treated as publication dates. Recommendations live in the [decision brief](database-foundations.md).

## S01 — Accounting foundations

OpenStax, *Principles of Accounting, Volume 1: Financial Accounting*,
[section 3.1](https://openstax.org/books/principles-financial-accounting/pages/3-1-describe-principles-assumptions-and-concepts-of-accounting-and-their-relationship-to-financial-statements).
Read: accounting equation, double-entry, journals and account balances.
Evidence: transactions affect accounts through equal debit/credit totals.
Use: journal/header/line model and balance invariants. Limit: educational accounting
text, not a database schema or a decision about this owner's accounting basis.

## S02 — Reconciliation

OpenStax, same book,
[section 8.6](https://openstax.org/books/principles-financial-accounting/pages/8-6-define-the-purpose-of-a-bank-reconciliation-and-prepare-a-bank-reconciliation-and-its-associated-journal-entries).
Read: bank-versus-book adjustments and worked reconciliation.
Evidence: timing differences, bank errors and unrecorded book items are different
causes of disagreement. Use: keep imported observations separate from posted books.
Limit: importing bank rows is not a complete bookkeeping method.

## S03 — Relational design textbook

Adrienne Watt and Nelson Eng (2014), *Database Design, 2nd Edition*, BCcampus.
Read selected material in [ER modelling, chapter 8](https://opentextbc.ca/dbdesign01/chapter/chapter-8-entity-relationship-model/),
[normalization, chapter 12](https://opentextbc.ca/dbdesign01/chapter/chapter-12-normalization/),
and [development process, chapter 13](https://opentextbc.ca/dbdesign01/chapter/chapter-13-database-development-process/).
Evidence: requirements, entities/relationships, dependencies and physical design
are distinct work. Use: a data dictionary and dependency review before DDL.
Limit: introductory simplifications and a waterfall presentation; a surrogate
primary key alone does not establish normalization across all candidate keys.
Use the stages iteratively, not as a requirement to freeze the entire future schema.

## S04 — Relational independence

E. F. Codd (1970), *A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks*,
Communications of the ACM 13(6), 377–387, DOI 10.1145/362384.362685.
[Paper, university-hosted copy](https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~david/cs848s14/codd-relational.pdf).
Read: opening sections on ordering, indexing and access-path dependence.
Evidence: logical representation should not depend on physical access paths.
Use: separate business identity/relationships from indexing and deployment choices.
Limit: foundational model, not a modern PostgreSQL implementation recipe.

## S05 — Double-entry mathematics

David Ellerman (2014), *On Double-Entry Bookkeeping: The Mathematical Treatment*,
[arXiv:1407.1898](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.1898),
[paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.1898).
Read: pp. 1–7, T-account algebra and signed representations.
Evidence: debit/credit pairs admit precise algebra; signed storage requires an
explicit interpretation. Use: test sign conventions and reversals, not an assumption
that double-entry means exactly two SQL rows. Limit: mathematical exposition;
not authority for tax policy, concurrency, or a mandatory storage encoding.
The PDF's extracted metadata title differed; its title page matches the citation.

## S06 — Serializable snapshot isolation

Dan R. K. Ports and Kevin Grittner (2012), *Serializable Snapshot Isolation in
PostgreSQL*, PVLDB 5(12), 1850–1861,
[arXiv:1208.4179](https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.4179),
[paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1208.4179).
Read: overview and sections 2–3, especially the receipt/close/report anomaly.
Evidence: snapshot isolation permits write skew and some read-only anomalies;
SSI detects dangerous dependencies and aborts transactions.
Use: adversarial posting/close/report schedules and whole-transaction retry design.
Limit: implementation/benchmarks concern PostgreSQL 9.1; use S08 for version 17
semantics. The paper's performance results are not our capacity estimate.

## S07 — Database constraints

PostgreSQL 17 manual, [5.5 Constraints](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/ddl-constraints.html).
Read: CHECK limitations, null handling, unique keys and composite foreign keys.
Evidence: row CHECKs cannot reliably maintain conditions over other rows.
Use: explicit NOT NULL, entity-scoped references and a separate balance-enforcement
mechanism. Limit: naming an invariant does not implement its enforcement.

## S08 — Isolation semantics

PostgreSQL 17 manual, [13.2 Transaction Isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/transaction-iso.html).
Read: Read Committed, Repeatable Read and Serializable sections.
Refreshed2026-10-24: full13.2.3 Serializable section, including whole-transaction
retry, committed-read validity and overlapping unique-key caveats.318's closed
receipt writer checks the key before insert; an actual two-snapshot lock-barrier
test verifies duplicate resolution. The manual alone is not that runtime proof.
Evidence: statement snapshots differ under Read Committed; serializable failures
require retrying the transaction. Use: specify isolation per operation and retry
from original inputs. Limit: serializability preserves correctly written operations;
it does not invent accounting rules or automatically order external side effects.

## S09 — Row-level security

PostgreSQL 17 manual, [5.9 Row Security Policies](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/ddl-rowsecurity.html).
Read: defaults, owner/BYPASSRLS behavior, whole-table operations and policy caveats.
Evidence: enabled RLS defaults to denial without policies, but privileged roles
and some operations bypass it. Use: nonowner runtime roles and role-specific tests.
Limit: RLS does not authenticate caller-supplied entity IDs or replace write grants.

## S10 — Exact amounts

PostgreSQL 17 manual, [8.1 Numeric Types](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/datatype-numeric.html).
Read: numeric precision/scale, rounding, special values and floating-point behavior.
Evidence: numeric is exact but can round to declared scale; NaN exists and compares
above finite values. Use: finite-value checks and explicit input/rounding policy.
Limit: documentation does not choose the correct scale, currency rules or minor-unit
encoding for our product. A positive-value check alone is insufficient for NaN.

## S11 — Deferred enforcement

PostgreSQL 17 manual, [CREATE TRIGGER](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-createtrigger.html).
Read: constraint-trigger timing and limitations.
Evidence: constraint triggers are AFTER ROW and can defer to transaction end.
Use: candidate final-journal validation. Limit: a trigger on lines alone cannot
notice an empty journal; concurrency, header transitions and all mutation paths
still need an explicit design and tests.

## S12 — Restricted posting functions

PostgreSQL 17 manual,
[CREATE FUNCTION: security-definer safety](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-createfunction.html#SQL-CREATEFUNCTION-SECURITY).
Read: ownership, trusted search_path and PUBLIC execute privileges.
Refreshed2026-10-24: full PG17 “Writing SECURITY DEFINER Functions Safely” section,
including temp-schema masking and same-transaction revocation of default PUBLIC
EXECUTE, for318's narrow receipt/claim wrappers. Source establishes mechanisms;
actual restricted login/role denial and race tests remain separate evidence.
Evidence: functions can execute with owner privileges and require careful grants.
Use: evaluate a narrow posting function with revoked direct DML. Limit: this is
an elevated trust boundary, not a shortcut around authorization.

## S13 — Internal state versus messages

Pat Helland (2005), *Data on the Outside versus Data on the Inside*, CIDR,
[paper](https://www.cidrdb.org/cidr2005/papers/P12.pdf).
Read: introduction, encapsulation and transaction-boundary discussion (§1).
Evidence: autonomous services exchange data across different trust/transaction
boundaries. Use: keep ledger changes in one authority and treat messages as external
contracts. Limit: the paper assumes a particular service boundary; it does not
prove that each Go executable should be a microservice or own a database.

## S14 — Transactional outbox

Chris Richardson, [Transactional Outbox](https://microservices.io/patterns/data/transactional-outbox.html).
Read: problem, forces, solution and result context.
Evidence: durable message intent shares the business transaction; the relay can
publish again after a crash. Use: transactional intent plus idempotent consumers.
Limit: delivery progress requires a functioning relay; ordering depends on actual
relay/transport design, not merely the presence of an outbox table.

## S15 — Actual queue semantics

Google Cloud, [Cloud Tasks issues and limitations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/common-pitfalls).
Read: execution order, delay and duplicate execution.
Evidence: duplicate execution occurs and tasks have no general execution-order
guarantee. Use: operation identities, durable outcomes and stale/version checks.
Limit: the generic outbox ordering goal in S14 is not automatically provided by
this transport. We must design any required per-account sequencing ourselves.

## S16 — Production ledger case study

Square Engineering (2019),
[Books, an immutable double-entry accounting database service](https://developer.squareup.com/blog/books-an-immutable-double-entry-accounting-database-service/).
Read: accounting model, SQL representation and immutable entries.
Evidence: an operational ledger uses journals and entries with derived/cached balances.
Use: corroborates an append-only posting model. Limit: Square chose Spanner for its
workload and simplified sign conventions. Neither its database choice nor its
payment-ledger model establishes the right general-ledger/accountant model for us.

## S17 — Event sourcing distinction

Martin Fowler (2005), [Event Sourcing](https://martinfowler.com/eaaDev/EventSourcing.html).
Read: definition, rebuild/replay facilities and external-query complications.
Evidence: event sourcing rebuilds application state from events; external historical
inputs require special treatment. Use: distinguish immutable financial postings
from sourcing every application state transition. Limit: replay facilities have
costs; the article does not require them for every bookkeeping application.

## S18 — Evolving schemas

Pramod Sadalage and Martin Fowler,
[Evolutionary Database Design](https://martinfowler.com/articles/evodb.html).
Read: versioned migrations, application/data coordination, CI and sequence collisions.
Evidence: ordered, tracked schema/data changes can evolve alongside code and tests.
Use: small reviewed migrations after each contract slice. Limit: examples use other
tools/databases; specific locking, transactional DDL and recovery require our driver.

## S19 — SQL-generated access

sqlc, [overview](https://docs.sqlc.dev/) and
[using transactions, v1.31.1](https://docs.sqlc.dev/en/v1.31.1/howto/transactions.html).
Read: SQL-to-Go generation and WithTx transaction binding.
Evidence: generated query methods can run within an explicitly supplied transaction.
Use: typed access without schema generation from application models. Limit: it
does not establish authorization, isolation, retries or accounting correctness.

## S20 — Migration-tool guarantees

golang-migrate v4.20.1,
[migration format](https://github.com/golang-migrate/migrate/blob/v4.20.1/MIGRATIONS.md) and
[FAQ](https://github.com/golang-migrate/migrate/blob/v4.20.1/FAQ.md).
Read: version ordering, paired files, failure/dirty handling and PostgreSQL locking.
Evidence: migrations are ordered SQL with explicit failed-state handling.
Use: retain the owner-selected tool. Limit: a successful migration run does not
prove ledger invariants or data recovery. Project manifest/history checks and
deployed-release receipts are separate controls.

## S21 — Additional book, preview only

Martin Kleppmann and Chris Riccomini, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications*,
2nd edition, [publisher chapter 8 preview](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/designing-data-intensive-applications/9781098119058/ch08.html).
Read: visible introduction and table of contents only; full chapter requires access.
Use: further reading on faults and transaction tradeoffs. No detailed design claim
in this review relies on unseen book content. No unofficial book download used.

## S22 — ORM counterexample

GORM, [transactions](https://gorm.io/docs/transactions.html) and
[migration](https://gorm.io/docs/migration.html).
Read: explicit transaction callback/manual control and AutoMigrate behavior.
Evidence: an ORM can support multi-operation transactions; automatic schema changes
are a distinct feature. Use: correct any claim that ORM usage inherently prevents
correct bookkeeping. Limit: convenience features still require our contracts.
SQL-first is a scoped maintainability choice, not a theorem or universal standard.

documents.title: Financial reporting sources
documents.body:
# Financial reporting sources

## Scope and review

Reviewed 2026-10-13 for #51, beginning with the shared
[bibliography](bibliography.md) and existing policy/standards contracts. These
selected sections support the [proposed contract](../contracts/financial-reporting.md),
not live accounting approval. No textbook reproduction or normative certification.

## FR01 — Introductory statement relationships

OpenStax / Rice University, *Principles of Accounting, Volume 1: Financial
Accounting*, §2.3 [Prepare an Income Statement, Statement of Owner's Equity,
and Balance Sheet](https://openstax.org/books/principles-financial-accounting/pages/2-3-prepare-an-income-statement-statement-of-owners-equity-and-balance-sheet).
Reviewed the income statement, owner's equity, balance sheet and connecting
statements subsections. The worked example distinguishes a period's performance
from a dated financial position and connects earnings/distributions to equity.
**Inference:** our review application should expose these relationships and
separate owner movements from expenses. Five-category unclassified statements
and `unclosed_earnings` are project choices, not prescribed classifications.
**Limit:** introductory sole-proprietor illustration; not US GAAP paragraph-level
research or a complete LLC reporting framework. Existing corpus constants are
original fixtures, not copied textbook amounts. Follow-up: #1/#10 real policy.

## FR02 — Snapshot, locking and query mode

PostgreSQL Global Development Group, PostgreSQL **17**,
[§13.2.2 Repeatable Read Isolation Level](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/transaction-iso.html#XACT-REPEATABLE-READ)
and [SET TRANSACTION, Description](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-set-transaction.html).
Also reviewed the PostgreSQL 17 maintenance branch's
[`execMain.c`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/postgres/postgres/REL_17_STABLE/src/backend/executor/execMain.c),
`standard_ExecutorStart` row-mark handling and `ExecCheckXactReadOnly` permission
check, for the row-lock/read-only incompatibility (moving branch, not a deployed
server binary attestation).
Reviewed repeatable-read visibility, lock conflict/retry and read-only command
restrictions. A transaction snapshot persists within that transaction; a later
HTTP request does not inherit it. Read-only mode prohibits row-locking SELECT.
**Inference:** preserve existing authorization `FOR SHARE` locks in bounded
repeatable-read transactions, and reject changed revision on later requests.
That rejection protocol is our design, not a PostgreSQL feature. Alternative:
long-lived snapshots/materialized reports, deferred pending measurements.
**Limit:** documentation does not prove our role grants, cursor protocol or
performance; named synthetic authorization/concurrency tests remain required.

## FR03 — CSV formula hazards

OWASP Foundation community, [CSV Injection](https://community.owasp.org/attacks/CSV_Injection),
current page, reviewed hazard characters, escaping, Excel save/reopen caveats and
cross-application limitations. Formula execution depends on spreadsheet behavior;
quoting alone is insufficient and transformations can alter exported data.
**Inference:** initial review CSV omits arbitrary text and validates generated
field grammars; signed amounts become magnitude plus explicit sign. Exact JSON retains
rich text and lossless decimal meaning. **Alternative:** descriptive CSV with
spreadsheet-specific escaping, deferred until target compatibility is tested.
**Limit:** no universal safety guarantee for downstream edits or spreadsheet
numeric precision; OWASP is security guidance, not an accounting export standard.

## FR04 — Standards scope and limitations

ISO 20022 Registration Authority, [FAQ](https://www.iso20022.org/faq), About and
Compliance sections, and [Catalogue of messages](https://www.iso20022.org/catalogue-messages),
introductory catalogue/version description reviewed. Community usage requirements
matter; a custom report API is not a registered message by naming its fields.
**Inference:** application-owned query responses have no selected bank exchange
profile; reassess when an actual exchange/counterparty exists. Individual report
message definitions were not exhaustively reviewed; no universal non-applicability
claim. No purchased eight-part text reviewed.

ISO, [ISO 4217 currency codes overview](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html),
public code/minor-unit overview reviewed; reuse the existing pinned currency
reference model. This overview supplies no FX valuation policy or new code-list
release approval. See bibliography R03 for canonical currency source context.

ISO, [ISO 21378:2019, Audit data collection](https://www.iso.org/standard/70823.html),
first edition metadata and abstract reviewed; confirmed in 2025. Accounting data
extraction is relevant to future accountant/audit exports. **Limit:** normative
field definitions not accessed, so field-level mapping remains unresolved.
Bibliography R05's ISO 21926:2026 preview remains the semantic-model research
entry; no additional normative clauses reviewed here. Promotion to audit export
requires those mappings and scoped validation, not just a CSV header.

## FR05 — Transport dates and CSV structure

IETF, [RFC 3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339.html), §5.6 Internet
Date/Time Format and §5.7 Restrictions; [RFC 4180](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4180.html),
§2 Definition of CSV Format. Selected sections reviewed. Use valid full dates,
UTC timestamps, fixed field counts and escaped quoted CSV fields. Project choices
further restrict date range, timestamp generation and allowed field grammar.
**Limit:** IETF transport specifications do not define accounting dates, recognition,
authorization or spreadsheet formula safety. No ISO financial message designation
follows from RFC-compatible strings.

documents.body:
# Financial workspace source notes

## Decision and review boundary

Support the proposed [workspace design](../plans/financial-workspace.md), issue
#52. Reviewed 2026-10-13; selected public sections only. These sources constrain
presentation, not accounting policy, authorization implementation or accessibility
conformance. Existing accounting and ISO sources remain authoritative in the
[bibliography](bibliography.md); no new financial interchange is introduced.

## FW01 — Keyboard focus

Publisher: W3C Web Accessibility Initiative. Resource:
[Understanding WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.7: Focus Visible](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible.html).
Version: WCAG 2.2 explanatory guidance; page updated September 6, 2026.
Reviewed: Success Criterion, Intent and Benefits. The source explains the need
for a visible keyboard focus indicator. Interpretation: use native buttons and
selects, persistent focus outlines, a skip link and explicit focus after changing
detail views. This is informative guidance, not a full normative WCAG review;
keyboard/screen-reader/contrast audits remain required before acceptance.

## FW02 — Financial tables

Publisher: W3C Web Accessibility Initiative. Resource:
[Tables with One Header](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/tables/one-header/).
Version: living tutorial, accessed October 13, 2026. Reviewed: Overview and
Table with header cells in the top row only. The source distinguishes header
cells and warns about ambiguous relationships. Interpretation: the prototype
uses table captions and explicit column header scope. A card-only financial
layout was considered but obscures account comparisons and journal sides;
summary cards accompany semantic tables instead. No screen-reader acceptance
is inferred from markup alone.

## Data evidence

The embedded fixture is an exact decoded copy of
[`golden-month.json`](../../tests/corpus/golden-month.json)'s books array.
Fixed report expectations come from that file and the corpus guide: checking
1,045 USD, savings 100, assets 1,145, capital 1,100, distributions 25, revenue
200, expenses 130 and net income 70. Book B remains separate at 70 USD assets.
Money formatting operates on strings; there is no browser FX conversion.
These figures support a synthetic design review, not a runtime reporting claim.

documents.body:
# Frontend source review

## Decision

Use the repository-selected Next.js/TypeScript stack for manual bookkeeping. Browser
code renders exact decimal strings and sends reviewed requests; SQL remains the
accounting authority. This is an implementation decision for #9, reviewed 2026-10-11.

| Source and reviewed section | Evidence and interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| [Next.js 16.4 installation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/installation), manual installation and scripts | Reviewed relevant sections. Next separates build from lint/type checks; this package runs explicit TypeScript, unit, browser and build gates. |
| [Next.js rewrites](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/rewrites), external URLs | Reviewed external rewrite section. A fixed operator-selected backend allows same-origin bearer requests. Browser-controlled upstream destinations are prohibited. |
| [Playwright component tests](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-components), React setup and limitations | Reviewed setup and browser/Node boundary. A separate synthetic test bundle exercises rendered controls without adding an application authentication bypass. This does not prove live Firebase or deployed proxy behavior. |
| [Playwright network mocking](https://playwright.dev/docs/mock), API mocking | Reviewed API interception example. Fixed synthetic responses test pending, denied and replay UX; database correctness uses the independent Go/PostgreSQL suite. |
| [gRPC JavaScript advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-m9gg-hp2v-232j), affected and patched versions | npm audit identified Firebase's unused Firestore dependency retaining vulnerable gRPC. Pin a patched override and validate the resulting graph; no Firestore APIs are used. |

## Alternatives and limits

### Next.js patch review — 2026-10-22, #271/#273

CI39832934816 reported the pinned16.4.0 version in the affected ranges for
maintainer advisories [GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw),
[GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr)
and [GHSA-p3m5-59mp-jv5r](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-p3m5-59mp-jv5r).
Reviewed selected affected/patched version, impact and workaround sections in
the maintainer/GitHub-reviewed records, not exploit reproduction. All identify
16.4.1 as patched; the image advisory also requires patched sharp dependency
resolution. [16.4.2 release notes](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases/tag/v16.4.2)
were reviewed for the subsequent stable patch changes; the npm audit resolver
selected16.4.2. Choose an exact16.4.2 pin and regenerated locked graph over a
scanner exemption or broad forced update. No application feature, financial
message, accounting or ISO applicability changes. No deployed exploitability or
security-conformance claim follows from version/audit results alone.

Acceptance: locked clean install, unchanged high-severity audit gate, web
type/unit/build/browser gates, both actual API/SQL browser journeys and standalone
frontend image proof. Current evidence belongs in the #271 integration runbook.

### Application boundary

A separate browser API origin would add CORS and more deployment configuration;
server-side cookie sessions would require a distinct CSRF/session contract.
The existing bearer boundary and fixed rewrite minimize this slice. We do not
infer standards conformance, deployed identity proof or accounting correctness
from the UI framework. See [UI contract](../contracts/first-ui.md) for acceptance
and recovery limits; revisit request recovery before live use.

documents.title: GCP delivery source register
documents.body:
# GCP delivery source register

## Decision and review boundary

Owner accepted managed Cloud Run, Cloud SQL and Cloud Tasks for the synthetic
milestone. Google Cloud publishes all sources below; accessed 2026-10-11.
These are mutable provider manuals/pricing pages, not accounting standards.
Selected sections were reviewed, not entire documentation sets. Recheck at
implementation; acceptance belongs to the linked issues in [GCP delivery](../gcp-delivery.md).

| ID / source | Reviewed sections and established facts | Application and limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| G01 — [Cloud Run pricing](https://cloud.google.com/run/pricing) | Request-based pricing and billable instance time; request work/startup/shutdown are billed, configured minimum instances incur idle charges; Jobs have a one-minute minimum per instance. | Choose zero minimums and bounded HTTP publisher calls. Actual cold-start/scheduler/load costs require measurement. |
| G02 — [Cloud Tasks pricing](https://cloud.google.com/tasks/pricing) | Billable operations and billing notes: first million operations/month/account free, then $0.40/million at the displayed tier; API calls and delivery attempts count in 32 KB chunks. | Transaction count is not operation count. Retries, payload size, shared allowance and network costs affect spend. |
| G03 — [Cloud Tasks issues and limitations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/common-pitfalls) | Execution order, duplicate execution, backoff and target resource limits. Ordering is not guaranteed; duplicates occur; overloaded targets cause backlog and throttling. | Require durable deduplication, fault tests and bounded queue/pool concurrency in #7. Provider delivery does not prove business completion. |
| G04 — [Connect from Cloud Run](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/connect-run) | Go connector example and connection-pooling guidance. Connector integrates with pgx; public/private connectivity and pool management are explicit choices. | #26 validates encrypted connector access and connection budget. Examples using passwords do not authorize secret retrieval or supersede IAM direction. |
| G05 — [Cloud SQL IAM authentication](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/iam-authentication) | IAM authentication concepts, automatic authentication and performance on shared-core instances. Connector-managed authentication handles short-lived access tokens; database permissions remain separately managed. | Choose automatic IAM authentication; test SQL role grants and managed-service compatibility. Shared-core IAM login can slow or time out under CPU pressure; test bounded connection recovery. No production access has been exercised. |

## Alternatives and uncertainty

Self-hosted Kubernetes/broker adds operational responsibilities; managed request
billing is our preferred fit for intermittent development, not a demonstrated
universal cost win. Pub/Sub fan-out is deferred until independently owned consumers
exist. Neither choice replaces the atomic PostgreSQL ledger.

The under-$50 target excludes bank-provider subscriptions and is not a guaranteed
ceiling. A complete regional estimate remains required by #5, including Cloud SQL
compute/storage/backups, identity, network, scheduler, logs, artifacts and restore
resources. The initial browser extraction of SQL pricing failed; the foundation follow-up
review below retrieved official HTML and records the bounded rate check. Measure
seven-day spend in #12.

## Foundation implementation review — 2026-10-11

- **G06 — HashiCorp, [Terraform provider mocking](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/tests/mocking)**: reviewed Mock Providers and Generated Data. Mocks use provider schemas without resource API calls; passing mocks do not prove real IAM or provider behavior. Implemented six named foundation tests with Terraform 1.15.7/provider 8.6.0. Selected sections only.
- **G07 — Google, [WIF for deployment pipelines](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation-with-deployment-pipelines)**: reviewed GitHub attribute mapping/conditions and default audience. Numeric repository/owner IDs avoid name-reuse trust; mapped claims constrain federation. Our additional owner actor/event/workflow restrictions are a project decision. Actual token denial tests remain cloud evidence.
- **G08 — HashiCorp, [GCS backend](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/backend/gcs)**: reviewed bucket prerequisite, locking, versioning and authentication guidance. Bootstrap must create its bucket first; owner then migrates local state privately. Separate application bucket narrows deployer access. No remote state was read or initialized.
- **G09 — Google, [Cloud Scheduler pricing](https://cloud.google.com/scheduler/pricing)**: reviewed Pricing overview/Free usage. Billing is per configured job, not per execution; first three jobs/account are free, then $0.10/job/31 days. Invocation compute is separate; account-wide usage remains unknown.

The checked-in lock file records signed provider package hashes for macOS ARM64
and Linux AMD64. Release identity was checked against the upstream Google provider
v8.6.0 release. Private branch-protection API still returned HTTP 403; the repository
environments API returned an empty list. The [foundation contract](../gcp-foundation.md)
therefore does not grant GitHub apply access or assume an enforced reviewer gate.

- **G10 — Google, [Cloud SQL pricing](https://cloud.google.com/sql/pricing?hl=en)**: reviewed Shared-core CPU/RAM and Iowa storage/backup tables in official HTML after the browser tool rejected its size. db-g1-small $0.035/hour; SSD $0.000232877/GiB-hour; used backups $0.000109589/GiB-hour. Shared-core types are excluded from the Cloud SQL SLA. The 730-hour example in the foundation contract is our calculation, not a full-stack quote or a billing-account-specific offer. No authenticated billing data was retrieved.

## Cloud SQL implementation review — 2026-10-11

- **G11 — Google, [Cloud SQL Go connector v1.25.3](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-sql-go-connector/tree/v1.25.3)**: reviewed README pgx/IAM sections and installed options.go token-source, lazy-refresh and public-IP options. Connector provides authenticated TLS; pgx's inner TLS can be disabled for the tunnel. Explicit API/login metadata token sources avoid the library's default ADC discovery. Library requires Go 1.26; the repository pins 1.26.9. Unit checks prove configured behavior, not live TLS/IAM acceptance.
- **G12 — Google, [PostgreSQL users and roles](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/users)**: reviewed superuser restrictions, default users, secure search path and IAM users/database roles. Cloud SQL does not expose PostgreSQL superuser; IAM users do not automatically receive database roles. Our precreated NOLOGIN roles and restricted migrator are a project design. Disposable PostgreSQL proves ordinary role semantics; actual administrator ADMIN-option compatibility remains cloud evidence.
- **G13 — golang-migrate, [pgx v5 driver at v4.20.1](https://github.com/golang-migrate/migrate/blob/v4.20.1/database/pgx/v5/pgx.go)**: reviewed installed Config/WithInstance, advisory locking, version/dirty handling and Close. The library closes its supplied SQL handle and owns a reserved connection. We use a second connection for artifact-registration locking, register hashes before migration and reject altered registered files. Source io/fs embeds reviewed SQL; no arbitrary remote SQL or down/force operation is exposed.

Required future evidence: real project API enablement, connector-only transport,
IAM login and SQL privilege separation, shared-core reconnection latency, backup/PITR
restore and observed costs. Terraform mocks and local non-superuser tests are not
substitutes for these checks. No live credential/state/plan was retrieved.

## G14 — Next.js standalone output

Vercel, [output](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/output), documentation identifies 16.4.0; accessed 2026-10-11. Reviewed “Automatically Copying Traced Files” and caveats: standalone emits a minimal server and traced dependencies; static assets require separate copying, PORT/HOSTNAME configure listening. Inference: a read-only non-root image can package the existing app without development dependencies. Container proof remains required; this source does not solve runtime browser identity configuration.

## G15 — Build metadata, scanning and publication

Docker, [buildx build metadata](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/buildx/build/#metadata-file) and [attestations](https://docs.docker.com/build/ci/github-actions/attestations/), accessed 2026-10-11. Reviewed metadata-file, BUILDX_METADATA_PROVENANCE and exporter limitations. Local load can retain a separate provenance record but not attached attestations. Aqua, [Trivy action](https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy-action/tree/ed142fd0673e97e23eac54620cfb913e5ce36c25), v0.36.0, reviewed setup/version, image inputs, severity/exit-code and CycloneDX output; scanner pinned v0.75.0. Inference: test/scan a local image before pushing unchanged, retain unsigned metadata/SBOM and explicitly defer attested promotion. Scan findings depend on the fetched vulnerability database; a clean scan is not a security certification.

## G16 — Build identity and private service invocation

Google, [auth action](https://github.com/google-github-actions/auth/tree/7c6bc770dae815cd3e89ee6cdf493a5fab2cc093), v3, reviewed WIF, token lifetime and create_credentials_file/export_environment_variables inputs; and [Cloud Run service authentication](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/authenticating/service-to-service), reviewed audience and X-Serverless-Authorization sections, accessed 2026-10-11. Auth can deliver a token without generating an ADC file; Cloud Run can validate a service token separately from application Authorization. Inference: authenticate the builder after image checks; a future frontend bridge must supply its own service identity without replacing the user token. No real federation/token exchange was executed. Proposed ingress still needs implementation and denial tests.

## G17 — User ADC quota project during foundation bootstrap

HashiCorp/Google provider [v8.6.0 configuration reference](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google/blob/v8.6.0/website/docs/guides/provider_reference.html.markdown), “Quota Management Configuration”; Google [Set the quota project](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/quotas/set-quota-project), request/environment precedence and permissions, accessed 2026-10-12. Reviewed those sections. The provider documents `USER_PROJECT_OVERRIDE=true` with `GOOGLE_BILLING_PROJECT`; the caller needs Service Usage Consumer authority. Applied these non-secret command settings after the budget API rejected user ADC without an explicit quota project; the subsequent foundation apply succeeded. No credential contents were inspected or changed.

## G18 — Runtime configuration and service-token forwarding

Vercel, [Environment Variables](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/environment-variables), “Bundling Environment Variables for the Browser” and “Runtime Environment Variables”; [Route Handlers](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), HTTP methods and request/response handling; Next.js 16.4.0, accessed 2026-10-12. Reviewed those sections. NEXT_PUBLIC values freeze at build time; request-time server code can expose an explicitly selected public configuration. Google, [Cloud Run service authentication](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/authenticating/service-to-service), “Use the metadata server” and separate authorization-header sections, reviewed again 2026-10-12. A fixed metadata identity request accepts the service URL as audience; X-Serverless-Authorization allows separate application Authorization. Inference: use a dynamic public allowlist endpoint and bounded frontend bridge, rather than a static rewrite or public API. No new dependency is needed for the documented metadata HTTP request. No token caching in this first slice; load impact and actual IAM/MFA remain cloud acceptance gates. Custom auth/API domains and public API ingress are deferred alternatives, not implied supported configurations.

## Runtime rollout sources — 2026-10-12

- **G19 — Google Cloud, Execute jobs**, [gcloud execution](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/execute/jobs#execute_jobs). Reviewed execution and roles sections: configured jobs can execute with `--wait`; job configuration is separate from execution. We infer separate migration state plus wait is a clear deployment gate. No live execution tested.
- **G20 — Google Cloud, Rollbacks and traffic migration**, [Terraform traffic](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/rollouts-rollbacks-traffic-migration). Reviewed Terraform revision/traffic examples; Terraform can own traffic and image rollback. It does not guarantee atomic changes across services or SQL compatibility. [Pinned provider 8.6.0 service source](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google/blob/v8.6.0/google/services/cloudrunv2/resource_cloud_run_v2_service.go), reviewed scaling/audience schema; local schema validation is required.
- **G21 — Google Cloud, Ingress and URLs**, [internal-service access](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/securing/ingress#access_internal_services), [custom/default URLs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/custom-urls). Reviewed ingress routing and default URL sections: Cloud Run calls to internal-only services require suitable VPC routing; deterministic URLs use service/project number/region. We select IAM-restricted network-reachable API plus explicit deterministic token audience, without VPC/NAT. Live reachability/audience acceptance remains unproved.
- **G22 — Google Cloud IAM, Firebase Authentication permissions**, [roles and permissions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/roles-permissions/firebaseauth). Reviewed user-get and viewer/admin lists. Custom API role selects only `firebaseauth.users.get` for revocation lookup instead of broad user administration; actual SDK acceptance is a cloud gate.

- **G23 — Deployment token lifetime and transport**, [pinned auth action access-token inputs](https://github.com/google-github-actions/auth/blob/7c6bc770dae815cd3e89ee6cdf493a5fab2cc093/README.md), [Terraform 1.15.7 GCS backend source](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/v1.15.7/internal/backend/remote-state/gcs/backend.go), [gcloud access-token authentication](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/authenticate#use_an_access_token). Reviewed token lifetime/outputs, backend environment defaults and CLI environment transport. A one-hour masked service-account access token covers the bounded job without relying on a short-lived GitHub subject token to refresh credentials after migrations. No credential file or token command is used. Actual exchange remains a live gate.

## G24 — IAM administrator bootstrap research — 2026-10-12

Google, [Add and manage IAM users](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/add-manage-iam-users),
“Assign database roles while adding an IAM account” and role assignment/revocation;
[PostgreSQL users](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/users), default
users and superuser restrictions; HashiCorp/Google,
[sql_user at provider 8.6.0](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google/blob/v8.6.0/website/docs/r/sql_user.html.markdown),
`database_roles` and IAM type arguments. Reviewed selected sections only.

Google documents assigning `cloudsqlsuperuser` to a separate IAM user, including
a Terraform example. IAM users otherwise receive no application privileges by
default. The pinned provider documents `database_roles` as write-only and replacing
existing memberships. Default `postgres` has explicit CREATEROLE/CREATEDB attributes;
membership alone does not establish every authority our bootstrap needs.

Proposal: evaluate a separate owner IAM operator instead of introducing a database
password. Do not apply that role to API or migrator. Alternative: owner-injected
administrator credentials, with additional secret-handling work. Neither approach
is implemented by this provisioning slice. Acceptance requires installed provider
schema checks, administrator ownership/role-authority probes and actual bootstrap
success followed by restricted-login denial checks. #26 owns the decision and
live compatibility evidence; source examples alone do not close that gate.

G10 pricing was rechecked on 2026-10-12 through indexed official regional tables;
the full page exceeded the browser response limit. This is a bounded price check,
not a new full-page review. The [provisioning estimate](../runbooks/cloud-sql-bootstrap.md#provisioning-estimate)
records assumptions separately from actual spend.

## G25 — Owner-operated IAM proxy — 2026-10-12

Google, [Cloud SQL Auth Proxy v2.26.0 README](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-sql-proxy/blob/v2.26.0/README.md),
installation, credentials, Unix sockets and automatic IAM authentication;
[proxy connection guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/connect-auth-proxy),
Unix socket length and troubleshooting outbound port 3307. Reviewed those sections
and installed proxy help. The proxy consumes ADC internally and supports automatic
IAM login; it does not establish network connectivity or SQL authorization.
Selected source version matches the official connection guide; GitHub's latest
release endpoint returned a v1 tag and was not used as v2 version authority.

Inference: a private 0700 Unix directory confines local access during the operator
check without exposing a TCP listener. Keep this exception outside runtime's
metadata-only connector. A failed TCP 3307 check is evidence of local reachability
failure, not proof of a particular firewall rule. Resume on a permitted network or
review a GCP runner; do not weaken Cloud SQL transport policy. Provider example
commands that print access tokens are not adopted.

## G26 — Cloud Shell command access — 2026-10-12

Google, [Launch Cloud Shell](https://docs.cloud.google.com/shell/docs/launching-cloud-shell),
console launch and local CLI connection sections; installed `gcloud cloud-shell ssh`
help and SDK `command_lib/cloud_shell/util.py`, SSH argument/setup code. Reviewed
these sections, not the entire SDK. Google documents remote command/file access;
the CLI's `--authorize-session` explicitly transfers authorization and was omitted.
The installed custom key-path flag was incorrectly declared boolean; default SDK
SSH handling worked without reading or overwriting keys. Existing Cloud Shell
authorization sufficed for the pinned proxy's IAM login. This is observed owner
administration, not a new runtime authentication path or migration identity.

## G27 — Immutable job execution receipt — 2026-10-12

Google, [Cloud Run v1 Execution](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rest/v1/namespaces.executions),
resource and ExecutionStatus; [ExecutionSpec](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rest/v1/ExecutionSpec),
task count and template; installed `gcloud run jobs execute` help, `--wait`.
Reviewed selected schema/flag sections. Execution captures immutable configuration;
Completed True and succeeded/failed/cancelled/running/retried counts describe its
result. Waiting without exact configuration readback would not bind evidence to
our approved image and identity. We therefore validate selected execution fields
before emitting a bounded receipt or changing services. Actual provider field
serialization remains a live gate; synthetic fixtures prove rejection logic only.

## G28 — Node runtime image contents — 2026-10-12

Node Docker maintainers, [Best Practices](https://github.com/nodejs/docker-node/blob/main/docs/BestPractices.md),
“CMD” and “Smaller images without npm/yarn” sections. Reviewed these sections,
not the whole repository. They describe direct Node execution and retaining build
tools only in the builder. Our standalone runtime starts `node server.js`;
removing npm/Yarn avoids unnecessary runtime dependencies. Alternative: upgrade
bundled npm, retaining unused code and an unfixed scan finding.
Private Trivy 0.75.0 evidence located all Node findings under npm; no application
package was waived. OpenSSL fixed-version bounds come from the scan's Alpine
package findings. Repaired-image scan and isolated runtime proof passed. Alpine's
package-manager web documentation was unavailable; actual build/scan evidence
verifies the update, not a claim of full advisory review. The base stays
digest-pinned; APK resolution can advance patched packages, so only the final
tested/scanned image digest is eligible for release.

## G29 — Execution field serialization — 2026-10-12

Google, [TaskSpec](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rest/v1/TaskSpec),
JSON representation and timeoutSeconds (string/int64), maxRetries (integer);
[resource keys](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/topic/resource-keys),
array paths; [projections](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/topic/projections),
subset selection. Reviewed these sections and installed SDK execution describe/
wrapper code, not the whole CLI. Actual allowlisted readback proves explicit `[]`
preserves containers and conditions whereas the original nested paths omitted them.
Accept only the exact bounded timeout string or number. Alternative broad numeric
coercion or whole-resource export would weaken validation/data minimization.
Synthetic regression checks cover the selected command paths and representation;
corrected validator also passed against the already completed real execution.
No migration replay was needed to repair evidence; the hosted run remains failed.

## G30 — Read-only migration metadata snapshot — 2026-10-12

PostgreSQL 17, [SET TRANSACTION](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-set-transaction.html),
read-only restrictions; [Transaction Isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/transaction-iso.html),
repeatable-read snapshot semantics. Reviewed those sections. Read-only mode rejects
persistent DML/DDL/grants; it does not mean PostgreSQL performs no physical writes.
Repeatable read gives both metadata queries a consistent committed snapshot, not
a guarantee that the database cannot change after verification. Apply with the
existing Cloud SQL identity/job sources G27/G29: no added operator grant or new
provider authentication path. A forced-RLS synthetic fixture checks the actual
transaction mode; wrong/dirty versions and artifact set/hash mismatches fail.

documents.title: Identity sources
documents.body:
# Identity sources

Reviewed 2026-10-11; relevant documentation sections only, not a compliance review.

## I01 — Google, Verify ID Tokens

[Firebase Admin verification guide](https://firebase.google.com/docs/auth/admin/verify-id-tokens),
sections “Verify ID tokens using the Firebase Admin SDK” and claim validation.
Evidence: ID-token verification checks signed identity; ordinary verification does
not check revocation. Project-specific audience/issuer and token times matter.
Inference: use the Go SDK, with explicit project binding; do not build JWT crypto.

## I02 — Google, Manage User Sessions

[Session guide](https://firebase.google.com/docs/auth/admin/manage-sessions),
“Detect ID token revocation”, including SDK examples.
Evidence: revocation checking adds a backend request; refresh tokens expire after
deletion/disabling and certain account changes. Inference: check every request,
fail closed on provider failure; do not promise revocation atomic with SQL commit.

## I03 — Google, Identity Platform TOTP MFA

[TOTP guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/identity-platform/docs/admin/enabling-totp-mfa),
enablement and enrollment/sign-in sections. Managed TOTP requires Identity Platform
configuration and user enrollment. Inference: require TOTP-completed tokens for
bookkeeping; enrollment/recovery must be proven before a remote release.

## I04 — Firebase Admin Go API and source

[Auth API](https://pkg.go.dev/firebase.google.com/go/v4/auth), `Token`,
`VerifyIDTokenAndCheckRevoked`; implementation pinned to v4.22.0 for this slice.
Reviewed downloaded v4.22.0 `auth/auth.go` Token/verification methods and
`auth/token_verifier.go` verifyHeaderAndBody: the reserved firebase claim remains
in Claims, while emulator mode bypasses signature verification. SDK owns signature/key rotation; our tests prove the adapter boundary,
not Google's service behavior. Default commands must not initialize provider
credentials or make provider requests.

Acceptance and alternatives: [identity/setup contract](../contracts/identity-setup.md).

## I05 — Go release and vulnerability evidence

[Official Go downloads](https://go.dev/dl/?mode=json) lists supported Go 1.26.9.
[Firebase releases](https://github.com/firebase/firebase-admin-go/releases/tag/v4.22.0)
records the selected SDK release and dependency maintenance. Reviewed release
metadata and local govulncheck v1.1.4 results. The initial scan found reachable
Go 1.26.5 and x/net v0.55.0 vulnerabilities; select patched 1.26.9/x/net v0.60.0
and refresh affected transitive pins. These are software maintenance decisions,
not an accounting-standard change. Final scan outcome belongs in the runbook.

## I06 — HashiCorp Google provider Identity Platform config

[Provider 8.6.0 resource reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google/v8.6.0/website/docs/r/identity_platform_config.html.markdown).
Reviewed 2026-10-12: lifecycle, sign-in, client permissions, MFA, monitoring,
computed fields and import sections. The resource includes computed password-hash
signing material and client configuration in state. Our inference: isolate state
from application delivery identities, expose no outputs and keep plans/logs private.
Mocked configuration tests establish intended settings; they do not prove login.
Observed discrepancy: the pinned reference lists `deletion_policy`, but validation
with the locked provider rejects it. The implementation uses Terraform lifecycle
`prevent_destroy`; installed-schema validation takes precedence over that example.

I03 rechecked 2026-10-12: project enablement, enrollment patterns and web sign-in
sections. Google documents TOTP configuration and first-factor sessions used for
enrollment. Our choice is ENABLED with one adjacent interval, while Jayburd denies
bookkeeping without a completed TOTP claim. No claim that provider enablement alone
makes MFA mandatory for every project API. See the
[implementation decision](../../infra/gcp/identity/README.md) and live evidence
in the identity runbook. No credential examples from the guide were executed.

# Investigate status source review

Reviewed 2026-10-21 for issue #255. This is a source and authority inventory,
not evidence of live provider health or an implemented Investigate screen.

| Source and section | Depth and established fact | Project interpretation and limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Source review SQL](../contracts/source-review-sql.md), Storage, Exact SQL, Recoverable posting; [HTTP handler](../../internal/ledger/http.go) review routes; [bridge](../../web/src/server/bridge.ts) allowlist | Full named contract sections and relevant route definitions read. Review listing is source-scoped, revision-pinned and paginated; posting is explicit. | Show an authorized source's items; do not infer a book total or assemble an action from a row alone. SQL behavior is backed by its separate synthetic runbook, not live source quality. |
| [Command recovery](../contracts/command-recovery.md), State, HTTP, Browser; [recovery runbook](../runbooks/command-recovery.md) | Full named sections read. One principal-wide unacknowledged command is durable; current authorization gates detail and explicit terminal acknowledgement. | Check target before including it in a selected-book view. A null pending response establishes only the principal gate, not absence of import/connection issues. |
| [Connection status UI](../contracts/connection-status-ui.md), Frozen wire and Fresh link-ready gap; [connection HTTP](../contracts/connection-http.md), Routes; [operations SQL](../contracts/connection-operations-sql.md), Interactive recovery and status | Full named sections read. Attempt discovery owns an unfinished-attempt count. Stream status is a separate single-stream read with generation/readiness and nullable provider update. | Keep attempt and stream statuses separate. Optional runtime, provider history and a complete book-wide health index remain unproved. Hosted Link error observations are not a general failure frequency estimate. |
| [Plaid acquisition recovery](../contracts/plaid-acquisition-recovery.md), Evidence and decision, Standards; [issue #104](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/104) | Full local contract and live issue status read. Fixed decoder/delivery classifications are designed; HTTP acknowledgement does not prove publication. Issue remains open. | Use only fixed safe error codes returned by the owner. No raw provider data or inference that request/retry completed sync. |
| [Reporting HTTP](../contracts/reporting-http.md), Wire and errors; [pinned journal](../contracts/report-drill.md), SQL and wire; [issue #242](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/242) | Full selected sections and live issue status read. Report failure is tied to a scoped read and revision. #242's broader cross-book taxonomy is open and blocked. | Pass transient report context only; do not make a durable item or cross-book transaction index. |
| [OWASP HTML5 Security Cheat Sheet, Local Storage](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/HTML5_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html#local-storage), cited in [recovery research](recovery-sources.md); [W3C focus visible](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible.html) and [table tutorial](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/tables/one-header/), cited in [workspace research](financial-workspace-sources.md) | Existing canonical records reviewed for their selected subsection/criteria; underlying external pages were not re-fetched on this branch. They constrain storage and focus/table presentation, not source completeness. | Keep handoff memory-only, use visible keyboard focus and semantic rows in a future UI. Browser tests and human review are still required. |
| [ISO 20022 FAQ](https://www.iso20022.org/faq), [ISO 4217 overview](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), [ISO 21378:2019 abstract](https://www.iso.org/standard/70823.html), [ISO 21926:2026 preview](https://www.iso.org/obp/ui?_escaped_fragment_=iso%3Astd%3Aiso%3A21926%3Aed-1%3Av1%3Aen), recorded in [bibliography](bibliography.md) and [standards](../contracts/standards.md) | Existing public FAQ/overview/abstract/preview records reviewed; no full normative ISO text or exchange profile read for this status composition. | Internal task status has no selected ISO 20022 message designation. Reuse existing ISO 4217 currency identity; audit export mapping and conformance are unresolved and outside this issue. |

The choice of one source/task at a time is a product inference from the owner's
stated preference for focused Unix-like tools. The implementation contracts
establish data ownership; they do not dictate the navigation label or color/font.
The competing aggregated dashboard would require new server-owned completeness,
permission and freshness semantics. Evidence to revisit: a reviewed API contract,
fixed multi-source fixture, denial/staleness proofs and owner acceptance of the
resulting workflow.
