documents.body:
# Plaid qualification source register — 2026-10-22

## Scope and review depth

Official public documentation, selected sections below read on 2026-10-22.
These are mutable web pages, not a versioned certification checklist. Current
adapter API version is `2020-09-14`; that does not version these guides.
The personalized Dashboard Launch Center was not inspected. Its review is a
separate outstanding acceptance row. No credentials or provider payloads were read.

| ID / authoritative source | Sections reviewed / established facts | Matrix use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P88-01 [Launch checklist](https://plaid.com/docs/launch-checklist/) | Opening replacement notice; Production, Link, storage/logging, Item management and Transactions recommendations. Launch Center supersedes this unmaintained checklist. | G01–G04, D01–D02 |
| P88-02 [Sandbox overview](https://plaid.com/docs/sandbox/) | Bypassing Link; simulating events; live testing; differences. Automated build gates should bypass provider UI; Sandbox cannot establish institution-specific live behavior. | L01, applicability, G05 |
| P88-03 [OAuth guide](https://plaid.com/docs/link/oauth/) | Support, prerequisites, Testing OAuth, consent revocation. Test every supported client, app installed/absent and update mode; simulated consent is not institution-specific evidence. | O01–O06 |
| P88-04 [Hosted Link](https://plaid.com/docs/link/hosted-link/) | Overview/Who should use it; creation; obtaining public token. SDK is recommended for owned frontends. Session results have a six-hour retrieval window; completion webhook is recommended. | L02–L04, integration choice |
| P88-05 [Update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode/) | When to use; login repair; new permissions/accounts; expiration; Testing update mode. Existing Items need a repair/consent flow. | I01–I05 |
| P88-06 [Duplicate Items](https://plaid.com/docs/link/duplicate-items/) | How duplicates arise; callback or Hosted Link metadata; pre-exchange comparison. Institution alone is not a sufficient universal duplicate rule. | L05 |
| P88-07 [Invalid Link token](https://plaid.com/docs/link/handle-invalid-link-token/) | Invalid/expired token handling and fresh initialization; SDK iframe cleanup. | L04 |
| P88-08 [Sandbox test credentials](https://plaid.com/docs/sandbox/test-credentials/) | Transactions, MFA, reCAPTCHA and error lists; special users need non-OAuth institutions. Product-specific unrelated test users excluded explicitly. | E01–E05 |
| P88-09 [Transactions overview](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/) | Integration overview; Sandbox testing; Refresh/Recurring add-ons. Custom additions and persona users support distinct tests; an application sync request is not a provider Refresh call. | T01–T03, T09–T10 |
| P88-10 [Transactions API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/) | `/transactions/sync`: initialization, `account_id`, cursor, update status, history request fields. Separate filtered streams require separate cursors; an empty result need not mean history complete. | T01–T03, T07–T08 |
| P88-11 [Transaction states](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/transactions-data/) | Pending/posted and testing sections. Removal and replacement can span pages; posted source data can later change. Dynamic student-loan refresh does not advance its repayment schedule. | T04–T06 |
| P88-12 [Transactions errors](https://plaid.com/docs/errors/transactions/) | Pagination mutation and Item limit sections. Mutation recovery restarts the whole update from its original cursor. | T07, R01 |
| P88-13 [Transactions webhooks](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/webhooks/) | Configuration, activation, update notifications and Refresh. First sync activates sync notifications; readiness flags distinguish initial/history availability. | W01–W02 |
| P88-14 [Webhooks API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/webhooks/) | Retries, best practices and Sandbox testing. Duplicate/out-of-order delivery and missed-webhook recovery must be handled; receiver must respond within ten seconds. | W03–W05 |
| P88-15 [Webhook verification](https://plaid.com/docs/api/webhooks/webhook-verification/) | ES256/kid, key metadata, signature, issued-at age and exact-body SHA256. Plaid describes verification as optional; Jayburd requires it under its existing contract. | W06–W07 |
| P88-16 [Transactions setup](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/add-to-app/) | Item creation, access-token exchange and fetch/update workflow. Initial history request is bounded by provider availability. | T01, G03 |
| P88-17 [Link troubleshooting](https://plaid.com/docs/link/troubleshooting/) | Link errors, missing institutions/accounts, OAuth configuration and consent/use-case configuration. | E03–E05, G01 |
| P88-18 [Cloud SQL IAM login](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/iam-logins) | Selected automatic IAM authentication and service-account login sections, refreshed2026-10-22. Connector authentication does not substitute for provisioned SQL authority. | Dedicated webhook connector |
| P88-19 [Cloud Run service identity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/securing/service-identity) | Selected service-account and metadata token sections, refreshed2026-10-22. Service identity is distinct from caller authentication. | Managed credential composition |
| P88-20 [Public Cloud Run access](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/authenticating/public) | Selected public invocation/IAM check sections, refreshed2026-10-22. Public invocation is explicit configuration, not granted by application handler code. | Separate release/security review |

## Interpretation and limits

The [matrix](../plans/plaid-88-test-matrix.md) is our acceptance mapping for
Transactions-only US web bookkeeping, including loan/card transaction feeds.
Binding a loan does not implement Plaid's separate Liabilities product. Public
examples are possible scenarios, not evidence that Jayburd passed them.

We choose named rows with separate synthetic and hosted results over a single
"Sandbox passed" checkbox: the latter hides missing lifecycle and security
evidence. New matrix identifiers are planned acceptance IDs, not invented Go
test names. Existing tests are cited only where their source was inspected.
Missing evidence remains open even where implementation exists.

The claimed scope is the reviewed sections, not every Plaid product/platform,
unseen Dashboard requirement, full API schema or paid ISO text. Recheck sources
before execution and add newly applicable scenarios. Launch Center changes must
be mapped, not silently ignored. No financial message, SQL, API or accounting
policy changes here: existing proprietary-Plaid/ISO applicability in
[qualification](../contracts/plaid-sandbox-qualification.md) remains authoritative.

Unavailable guessed paths `/transactions/testing/` and
`/sandbox/test-institutions/` were not used as evidence. Official navigation led
to Transactions overview and `/sandbox/institutions/`; the latter was inspected
only for navigation, not used to qualify any institution.

documents.title: Plaid ingestion sources
documents.body:
# Plaid ingestion sources

## PI13 — Source-first account/history refresh, 2026-10-21

Reviewed official Plaid [Transactions API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/)
sections `/transactions/sync` request, pagination, account filtering, early empty
results and readiness; [Accounts API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/)
`/accounts/get` and `account_id`; and [Link API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/)
`/link/token/create` `transactions.days_requested`. Relevant public sections were
read on 2026-10-21; no private Item, credential, payload or institution was used.
The docs state that sync is Item-cursor based, supports credit/depository/loan
accounts, and requires whole-loop restart on mutation during pagination. A new
Item can return empty arrays before history is ready. One Item exposes multiple
accounts; account IDs can change when Plaid cannot reconcile an account or after
token recreation. Link's Transactions initialization accepts a history request,
default 90 and maximum 730 days; an initialized Item's window cannot simply be
changed. These statements are provider behavior, not local correctness proof.

Project inference for [ADR 0006](../decisions/0006-source-first-workspace.md):
maintain owner-private Item/account/transaction provenance before book setup;
request up to 90 days for new Items and show actual received/readiness separately;
use a stable local source identity, explicit reconnect/overlap decisions and
replay-safe complete-set publication. Plaid account metadata does not attest
legal LLC ownership; Plaid categories do not determine ledger treatment. The
source-first privacy, grants, schema, retention and multi-book disposition rules
are our proposed decisions, not guarantees in Plaid documentation. Existing
PI01–PI12 and the pinned public OpenAPI remain relevant for exact decoder fields.

2026-10-20 history refresh: [history/currency decision evidence](../contracts/plaid-history-currency.md#decision-and-source-evidence)
records selected official sync cursor, account_id, days_requested, has_more and
history-availability sections; also ISO 4217 MA amendment 115 page 1 and the prior
SIX bootstrap publication. It distinguishes provider lookback, local currency
coverage and bookkeeping dates. No private response or full normative ISO text read.

Reviewed 2026-10-13 for [#70](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/70).
Only public documentation was read; no provider endpoint, credentials, Sandbox or
bank account was accessed. The [contract](../contracts/provider-ingestion.md)
labels project proposals separately from provider facts.

| ID / official source / reviewed sections | Evidence and relevance | Review limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PI01 — Plaid [Transactions API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/), `/transactions/sync` request, pagination, response amount/currency/date fields | Cursor streams return added/modified/removed changes; options.account_id defines an independent account-filtered cursor. Amount is described as a JSON number/double, positive for money leaving an account, negative for money entering. ISO and unofficial currency identifiers differ; authorization and posted dates differ. | Relevant sections reviewed, not every product field. Exact-number decoding is our requirement; generated SDK numeric behavior must be inspected before choosing it. API version alone does not freeze every additive response field. |
| PI02 — Plaid [Sync migration guide](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/sync-migration/), pagination, initial trigger, webhook and Item-data sections | Apply complete updates; restart pagination from its original cursor on mutation. Initial sync enables sync notifications; empty initial results need not mean history is ready. | Relevant sections reviewed. Guide examples are not atomic local persistence or permission proofs. Our staging/fencing design is an inference. |
| PI03 — Plaid [Transaction states](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/transactions-data/), pending/posted section | Posting can remove a pending ID and add a different posted ID across pages; pending linkage may be absent. Amount/details may change; even provider-posted items can be modified/removed. | Full relevant section reviewed. Provider “posted” is not our journal state. No source-to-ledger correction authority follows from it. |
| PI04 — Plaid [Webhook verification](https://plaid.com/docs/api/webhooks/webhook-verification/), algorithm/key retrieval, validation and body hashing | Verify ES256 signature, obtain key by kid, enforce five-minute age and compare authenticated SHA-256 against exact body bytes. Key metadata includes expiry. | Relevant procedure reviewed, not a security endorsement of copied sample code. Our future-skew, caching, size and ingress policies require tests. |
| PI05 — Plaid [Link overview](https://plaid.com/docs/link/), flow overview, initialization and errors | Link token initializes consent flow; temporary public token is exchanged server-side for Item/access token. Duplicate Items need handling. | Relevant sections reviewed. Our account ownership, session-binding, secret storage and uncertain-exchange handling remain project responsibilities. |
| PI06 — Plaid [Link update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode/), overview and login/consent recovery | ITEM_LOGIN_REQUIRED and expiration/disconnection notifications can require user reauthentication/update mode. | Relevant lifecycle sections reviewed; no live consent configuration validated. Product/country/account coverage remains qualification work. |
| PI07 — Plaid [Items API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/items/), public-token exchange, access-token invalidation, item removal | Rotation returns a replacement access token and invalidates the previous one. Item removal is a provider lifecycle operation. | Selected endpoint descriptions reviewed; do not infer idempotency or recoverability of a lost rotation response. No token value copied. |
| PI08 — Plaid [API versioning](https://plaid.com/docs/api/versioning/), version header and 2020-09-14 section | Requests can explicitly select Plaid-Version; 2020-09-14 is documented. | Relevant sections reviewed. Proposed pin must be revalidated with contract fixtures and the selected provider environment before implementation. |
| PI09 — Plaid [Link API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/), token creation, token/get and session results | Session results can associate a public token with its Link session. Hosted Link and ordinary Link availability differ; callback metadata alone cannot authorize our connection. | Selected sections refreshed 2026-10-13. Concrete new-session verification requires supported results; ordinary update-mode association is not guessed. Hosted qualification must verify the configured flow. |
| PI10 — Plaid [Accounts API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/), accounts/get and Item metadata | Server-returned account IDs and types drive explicit source selection, not browser-provided names or masks. | Selected fields reviewed by enrollment lane; no institution coverage or ownership certification. Local authorization expiry is a configured policy bound when provider consent expiry is absent, not a fabricated provider fact. |

## Standards and alternatives

Reuse ISO 4217/date source limits in [SI02–SI04](statement-import-sources.md) and
[the standards contract](../contracts/standards.md). Plaid JSON is a proprietary
exchange; explicit semantic mapping is necessary, not an invented camt designation.
Official ISO message/profile verification in #17 stays unresolved.

Compare: date-window `/transactions/get` requires additional change reconciliation;
`/transactions/sync` gives a clearer change/cursor boundary. Item-wide sync keeps
one checkpoint but couples account authorization; account-filtered streams could
isolate subsets, at the cost of separate checkpoints and a reviewed migration.
Our selected profile uses account-filtered connections; account revocation stops
that stream while Item-level consent revocation stops all. Filter/mode changes
require null-cursor new generations and overlap review.
CSV remains an independent adapter into the same proposed source-observation core.
No benchmark or bank coverage was measured. Revisit limits and stream selection
when #13 qualifies an actual institution and #8 implements ingestion.

## Connection operations review — 2026-10-13

#103/#104 refreshed PI04 verification/key metadata and PI01 sync notification
sections before implementation. Source requirements remain signature verification,
five-minute freshness and exact-body digest. Our selected limits (64 KiB body,
8 KiB token, 60-second future skew, bounded key cache and lookup admission),
receipt identity and transaction/outbox design are local policies, not provider
guarantees. Readiness notifications do not establish the time of the provider's
last data update; public provider_updated_at remains null. Database publication
time is separate. Signed fixtures verify protocol behavior without contacting Plaid.

The chosen alternative to direct acquisition in a webhook request is durable
generation intent with separate acquisition. It bounds the public request and
retains a wakeup arriving during an in-flight fetch. Stream revision is separate
from source binding revision so pausing acquisition does not change accounting
mapping authority. SQL and full-stack acceptance are recorded in the
[operations runbook](../runbooks/connection-operations.md); hosted routing and
measured capacity remain qualification work.

## PI01 compatibility refresh — 2026-10-14

Reviewed the official Transactions API transaction_code response description:
nullable classification, populated for European and some US institutions and
null where unavailable. No provider payload was inspected. Accepting this as
bounded inert metadata is a project interpretation; it cannot assign accounting
meaning. See the [decoder contract](../contracts/plaid-decoder.md) and
[regression evidence](../runbooks/sandbox-decoder.md). This selected-field review
is not a complete response-schema audit or proof of the hosted failure cause.

PI01 follow-up: reviewed request cursor, response next_cursor and Item update
status after the hosted cursor rejection. The request documents 256 base64
characters; an empty response cursor signals unavailable transactions. The old
combined error does not identify which local predicate failed. Preserve validation
and separate fixed error classifications before choosing a compatibility change.

The subsequent progress-only failure prompted the narrow account-readiness
interpretation in the [decoder contract](../contracts/plaid-decoder.md): Item
completion is not filtered-account cursor availability. No raw response was
inspected; whether that specific predicate caused the failure remains unproven.

## PI11 — public OpenAPI response review, 2026-10-14

[Plaid public schema, pinned commit](https://github.com/plaid/plaid-openapi/blob/325e2e192bcb422df708029bafe9d950c94df2fd/2020-09-14.yml),
API 2020-09-14. Reviewed all direct fields of TransactionsSyncResponse, AccountBase,
RemovedTransaction, Transaction and inherited TransactionBase; also the referenced
BusinessFinanceCategory and ClientCustomization definitions. This is a public
specification, not a provider response. Those enrichment fields and running_balance
appear in the schema even where hidden from rendered docs. The balance description
warns that provider balances may not reconcile across endpoints.

Owner-approved mapping: null/object enrichment and null/numeric running balance
remain private inert evidence. Preserve exact balance lexemes without floating
point or accounting interpretation; reject malformed types. Blanket unknown-field
acceptance would conceal new financial meaning. See the
[decoder contract](../contracts/plaid-decoder.md) for validation evidence.
Limits: no complete nested-schema validation, no private payload inspection, no
claim that this is the specific field seen in the hosted rejection.

## PI12 — Hosted Link completion and recovery refresh, 2026-10-18

Official Plaid [Hosted Link integration guide](https://plaid.com/docs/link/hosted-link/),
sections **Integration process** and **Obtaining a public token**; [Link API
reference](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/), `/link/token/create`,
`/link/token/get` and `SESSION_FINISHED`; and [Link overview](https://plaid.com/docs/link/),
flow overview. Relevant sections were read, not the entire API catalogue. Public
HTML snapshots were downloaded on 2026-10-18 to a local temporary review folder,
outside the repository; SHA-256 for Hosted Link `3ad60a510218e210f3f3bc9e6d2a1bebf548e3c19c5780e0f40fd1c58afc6792`,
Link API `9c044adeebd88dd4403d489a4025033081ef572bc05beae827c0c5ca1e1e8e63`,
and Link overview `0ad26b1ed8304efe8810c573d2da20f2cdd9301a9d5bf9f6702eb94074a07633`.
The linked official pages remain the canonical source; snapshots are local
review artifacts, not vendored or redistributed documentation.

Plaid recommends storing a Hosted Link `link_token` associated with the
application's user and strongly recommends a completion webhook. Hosted Link
returns `hosted_link_url` at token creation. `/link/token/get` can supply
completed-session results without a frontend callback; Plaid says detailed
session data remain available for up to six hours after completion, and prefers
`results.item_add_results` to deprecated `on_success`. A completion redirect can
occur after success or exit and is not proof of success. The Link API documents
that Hosted Link token expiry tracks its URL and that the lifetime can be
configured. These are provider-documented mechanisms, not evidence that the
owner's specific attempt completed or that Jayburd stored a credential.

Our current memory-only token and explicit completion are project choices, not
Plaid requirements. A scoped encrypted server-side token, verified webhook,
retention policy, local authority check and one-shot exchange are design
inferences needing review and synthetic tests. A fast restart cannot assume
that `link_ready` or local expiry proves absence of a completed provider result.
No Plaid account, token, private response or bank data was accessed in this
review. See [Hosted Link contract](../contracts/hosted-link-enrollment.md) and
[#187](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/187).

## Source precision review (#258, 2026-10-22)

PI01 refreshed: selected `/transactions/sync` amount and ISO currency sections
describe numeric settled quantities and currency identifiers. Public sections
only; no normative ISO text or bank payload inspected. A `double` format does not
justify rounding evidence. Hosted fixed diagnostic confirms currency precision
failure, not its source cause. [Decision](../contracts/plaid-source-precision.md):
preserve bounded exact source quantities, hold sub-minor-unit rows from drafting,
and publish unrelated rows atomically. No ledger precision or posting change.

## Application cancellation decision (#200, 2026-10-19)

The existing PI12 Hosted Link review informed the local cancellation contract.
A refresh of https://plaid.com/docs/api/tokens/ failed through the web tool;
no new provider guarantees were inferred. Cancellation relies on the reviewed
local atomic exchange-claim boundary, retains provider-session uncertainty,
and does not claim remote revocation. See [the decision and tests](../contracts/hosted-link-enrollment.md#explicit-cancellation-and-retry-200).

# Plaid liability source review

Reviewed 2026-10-20 for #210. Access was limited to public documentation;
no tenant setting, institution response or provider payload was inspected.

## PL01 — Accounts API

Plaid, [Accounts API account type schema and product support matrix](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/).
Reviewed `type`, `subtype`, account identity, currency fields and product
matrix. Plaid describes `credit` and `loan` account types, but that description
does not determine Jayburd ledger presentation or posting direction. The
Transactions product matrix supports credit cards and only a subset of loans,
including student and mortgage. Coverage varies by institution. Jayburd's
`credit card`, `student` and `mortgage` allowlist is a local policy inference.

## PL02 — Transactions API

Plaid, [Transactions API `/transactions/sync`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/).
Reviewed account-filtered cursor sync, supported account types and update
status. The API provides transaction observations, not a balanced journal,
opening liability, principal/interest allocation or audited history. The
account-filtered response must still be matched to the trusted stream account.

## PL03 — Liabilities API

Plaid, [Liabilities API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/liabilities/).
Reviewed product scope only. It may expose additional liability details and
loan types but is a separate product and does not expand Transactions coverage.
It is not enabled by #210.

## PL04 — Additional fictional loan registration, 2026-10-22

Refreshed the official [Accounts API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/accounts/)
loan subtype definitions for auto, consumer and line of credit, plus the
account/product matrix caveat that only some loans support Transactions.
Refreshed [Transactions sync](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/)
account type/subtype and amount fields. Public selected sections reviewed; no
institution payload or tenant settings accessed. Fact: subtype vocabulary does
not guarantee product availability. Inference approved by the owner's requested
scope: permit these three verified Sandbox loans to register with the existing
liability mapping and attempt scoped acquisition; retain explicit failure state.
No principal/interest allocation or opening balance follows from registration.

## Limits (continued)

Documentation can change. Fresh Sandbox verification is required for the
selected types and newly bound streams. Live-bank approval remains #90.

# Link recovery source register — 2026-10-22

Selected official sections read in browser; mutable guides, not certification.
Pinned API version remains 2020-09-14, Go SDK v49.0.0. No credentials or provider
payloads were accessed; Dashboard capability/Launch Center was not reviewed.

| ID | Source / reviewed section | Established fact and limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LR01 | [Hosted Link](https://plaid.com/docs/link/hosted-link/), Overview/Who should use it, obtaining token and testing | SDK recommended for owned frontend; Hosted supports update mode. This does not prove Jayburd's update-session association. |
| LR02 | [Update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode/), Using update mode, requesting accounts, refreshing expiration | Existing access token initializes repair and remains unchanged; account-selection widening is explicit. It does not authorize local consent extension. |

Ordinary update success association remains unresolved; CRA update is a different product. |
| LR04 | [Web SDK](https://plaid.com/docs/link/web/), create/onSuccess/onExit/destroy/OAuth navigation | SDK callbacks and lifecycle are browser mechanisms. They do not replace server authority/session proof. Redirect details must be reviewed again before implementation. |
| LR05 | [Hosted Link](https://plaid.com/docs/link/hosted-link/), storing associated token/obtaining public token; [Link API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/), token-get session results; [invalid Link token](https://plaid.com/docs/link/handle-invalid-link-token/), opening recovery sections; refreshed 2026-10-22 | Retain the user-associated Link token and retrieve bounded completed-session results; modern results preferred. URL expiration does not prove no completed session. Explicit restart must preserve Jayburd's one-shot claim and cancellation policy. |
| LR06 | [React19.3 useLayoutEffect](https://react.dev/reference/react/useLayoutEffect), reference/caveats and before-paint state updates, 2026-10-22 | Client layout effects finish state updates before repaint. Apply only to the existing small synchronous review initializer; keep the reviewed date/edit semantics and scope reset. No server effect or accounting rule is introduced. |

Also inspected pinned generated `link.go`: `LinkSessionResults` has Item-add and
CRA update fields; `LinkTokenGetSessionsResponse` contains modern exit and legacy
success fields. Model availability alone does not establish actual provider
semantics or account enablement. No fallback to deprecated fields is approved.

Design alternatives, inferences, uncertainty and required acceptance are in
[the recovery contract](../contracts/plaid-link-recovery-qualification.md).

## LR07 — owned Hosted repair review, 2026-10-24

Read full relevant official sections: [Link API](https://plaid.com/docs/api/link/),
SESSION_FINISHED properties/default enablement; [Hosted Link](https://plaid.com/docs/link/hosted-link/),
supported flows, obtaining session results, testing; and [update mode](https://plaid.com/docs/link/update-mode/),
Using update mode with access token, requesting accounts and consent revocation.
Mutable documentation; pinned API2020-09-14/SDK49.0.0 unchanged.

The modern event supplies outcome, Link token/session and environment, without
Item or completion time; Hosted gets this event by default. Update uses the old
credential without exchange; deselection can remove previously shared accounts.
Sandbox Hosted update can expire after30minutes; our shorter local deadline must
remain authoritative. Model fields alone do not qualify actual provider behavior.

The retained server-created hash→owned attempt→preselected Item/streams join and
proof-gated owner claim are Jayburd's inference, not a provider guarantee. No
ordinary update response, Dashboard setting, actual event, credentials or financial
payload was accessed. Existing verifier checks in `internal/webhook/verifier.go`,
new-only handoff19, connection fencing13 and exact bootstrap ACL were inspected.
The [proposed protocol](../contracts/hosted-reconnect.md) defines alternatives,
ambiguity/expiry/lock boundaries and named future evidence. No runtime acceptance
is claimed, and no deprecated callback or CRA result is substituted.

Wave 2 additionally inspected `HTTPProvider.CompletedPublicToken`, `VerifySession`,
service completion and merged migrations 13/19/23: the new-mode verifier repeats
the same provider association check after a claim. Reusing private verified
hash evidence is our engineering inference, not a Plaid recommendation or a
relaxation of current SQL authority. Physical ciphertext deletion is not
implemented. Read depth is the named sections/model functions only; no Dashboard,
provider payload, credentials or full API review.

documents.body:
# Plaid Sandbox rollout source review — #258

Reviewed 2026-10-22; public selected sections only. No provider payload,
credential, state or plan inspected.

## RQ01 — Cloud Scheduler v1 Job/RetryConfig/State

Google, [REST Job](https://docs.cloud.google.com/scheduler/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.jobs),
`schedule`, `attemptDeadline`, State and RetryConfig fields. PAUSED prevents new
scheduled execution. A deadline cancels an overdue request; this does not prove
the application stopped all work. Default retryCount is zero; zero count with
zero maxRetryDuration does not retry a failed attempt. Existing readback has a
90-second deadline, omitted/default-zero retryCount and maxRetryDuration `0s`;
source Terraform explicitly sets retry_count=0. This is a bounded metadata
interpretation, not inspection of every historic execution.

## Local application boundary and interpretation

Cloud Tasks [v2 tasks.list](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.queues.tasks/list),
responseView and pagination sections, reviewed on the same date: BASIC is the
default view and excludes sensitive payload details; FULL is separate authority.
List order is unspecified and fewer results may arrive than pageSize. The CLI
listing used here follows its normal BASIC mode, paginates and projects only
names into a count with an upper bound. Any nonzero count blocks the empty-queue
observation; no FULL view, task body or arbitrary request header is requested.

`internal/observer/http.go` bounds acquisition publisher/consumer handler context
at 80 seconds after separately bounded five-second caller verification;
`internal/acquisition/runner.go` bounds acquisition at 60 seconds. Context expiry
requires cooperative completion and is not a distributed-drain guarantee.

Rollout procedure: pause the existing Scheduler, verify PAUSED, wait beyond its
90-second request deadline with two observations separated by useful rollout
work, inspect only queue-name counts and fixed known-account lease/status fields,
and keep scheduling paused through worker readback. No task payload is retrieved.
An empty list and inactive known leases are point-in-time evidence, not an
universal absence-of-work proof. If work remains, wait/reinspect rather than purge
tasks or force SQL state. Migration28 also retains the old generic diagnostic,
exact amount rules and existing binding semantics, so residual authorized old
work remains compatible; new loan binding/checking retry wait until matching
services are ready. Restore only the previously enabled schedule afterward.

Alternative: replace workers while normal publication continues. Rejected for
this bounded qualification because it obscures version/diagnostic attribution.
Acceptance: retained migration/status/runtime receipts, PAUSED readbacks, selected
queue/status observations, matching immutable revisions, then actual per-account
completion. No live banking, automatic journals or ISO exchange is introduced.

## CI availability check — 2026-10-22

[npm's public status page](https://status.npmjs.org/), selected current component
and incident sections, reported Security Audit and package installation
operational with no incident for October 22. Public status text only was read;
this does not prove availability from a particular runner. PR #263's actual
audit request returned HTTP 503 from the bulk-advisory endpoint after five
minutes. Preserve that failed-gate evidence and rerun without dropping or
weakening the audit. No dependency or security-policy change follows from a
status page. Current source/SQL tests and actual hosted qualification remain
separate acceptance evidence.

documents.body:
# Position source review and fixed synthetic example

## Review record

Reviewed 2026-10-21 and updated 2026-10-22 for proposed [Position contract](../contracts/position-read-model.md),
starting at the [bibliography](bibliography.md), [decision evidence](decision-evidence.md),
[database foundations](database-foundations.md), and existing [financial reporting
sources](financial-reporting-sources.md). No new normative accounting approval.

| ID | Reviewed source and depth | Fact established | Project inference / limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P01 | OpenStax / Rice University, *Principles of Accounting, Volume 1*, [§2.3 statement relationships](https://openstax.org/books/principles-financial-accounting/pages/2-3-prepare-an-income-statement-statement-of-owners-equity-and-balance-sheet), income statement, owner's equity and balance sheet subsections, reviewed through FR01 | Balance sheet is dated; performance covers a period; earnings/distributions affect equity | Show dated Position and separately labeled change. Introductory example does not decide LLC cash classification, GAAP or spendability. |
| P02 | PostgreSQL Global Development Group, [PostgreSQL 17 §13.2.2 Repeatable Read](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/transaction-iso.html#XACT-REPEATABLE-READ), relevant section reviewed through FR02; local reporting contracts and runbooks reviewed in full for API facts | One transaction has stable snapshot; later request does not inherit it. Existing reporting uses current membership and revision validation. | One response carries current/prior points per book; separate book requests have independent snapshots, not one portfolio snapshot. Documentation alone does not prove our grants or performance. |
| P03 | ISO 20022 Registration Authority [FAQ](https://www.iso20022.org/faq), About/Compliance, and [message catalogue](https://www.iso20022.org/catalogue-messages), catalogue/version overview, reviewed through FR04/R01–R02 | Registered messages have versioned definitions and usage context | Internal Position query has no selected external exchange profile. No individual message or eight-part normative text reviewed; reassess for an actual exchange. |
| P04 | ISO [4217 public overview](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), currency identifier/minor-unit overview, reviewed through FR04/R03 | Maintained codes and minor-unit metadata identify currencies | Preserve existing pinned code/version; no FX method or cash policy follows. No new code-list release assessed. |
| P05 | ISO [21378:2019 standard page](https://www.iso.org/standard/70823.html), abstract/edition metadata, and [21926:2026 official preview](https://www.iso.org/obp/ui?_escaped_fragment_=iso%3Astd%3Aiso%3A21926%3Aed-1%3Av1%3Aen), contents/introduction/§1 through R04–R05 | Audit-data extraction and semantic modelling are relevant future topics | Position is an internal view, not an audit export. Normative field mappings remain unavailable and unresolved. |

Repository facts checked: [financial reporting](../contracts/financial-reporting.md)
defines debit-positive account net and unclassified balance sheet;
[reporting SQL](../contracts/reporting-sql.md) and [HTTP](../contracts/reporting-http.md)
define exact strings, single-book scope, comparison, revision and errors;
[pinned journal](../contracts/report-drill.md) proves a selected GL line. These
are project implementation/contract sources, not accounting standards. Current
[reporting foundation](../runbooks/reporting-foundation.md) and
[HTTP delivery](../runbooks/reporting-http.md) document synthetic tests and
limitations; they do not prove the proposed cash or attention extension.

## Fixed fictional example — independently specified expected values

All IDs below are fixture labels, not database IDs. One synthetic book A uses
functional USD, synthetic accrual/UTC policy and two asset accounts: `A-CASH-USD`
and `A-CASH-EUR`; `A-PREPAID` is noncash. The *fixture's* reviewed cash membership
is `{A-CASH-USD,A-CASH-EUR}` solely for acceptance math; it does not approve a
production policy. Original units are retained per line. All journals balance
in functional USD. `Dr` and `Cr` are sides, never signed input amounts.

| Journal/date | Debit line, original / functional | Credit line, original / functional | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| J1 / 2026-01-02 | A-CASH-USD USD 1000 / USD 1000 | Equity-capital USD 1000 / USD 1000 | Opening capital actually posted |
| J2 / 2026-01-10 | Expense USD 120 / USD 120 | A-CASH-USD USD 120 / USD 120 | Period expense |
| J3 / 2026-01-11 | A-CASH-USD USD 300 / USD 300 | Loan-liability USD 300 / USD 300 | Borrowing, not income |
| J4 / 2026-01-12 | A-PREPAID USD 40 / USD 40 | A-CASH-USD USD 40 / USD 40 | Asset transfer, not expense |
| J5 / 2026-01-13 | A-CASH-EUR EUR 10 / USD 11 | Revenue USD 11 / USD 11 | Immutable EUR-to-USD spot valuation; rate/reference pinned to J5 |
| J6 / 2026-02-02 | Revenue USD 11 / USD 11 | A-CASH-EUR EUR 10 / USD 11 | Linked reversal of J5; original EUR quantity/rate retained |

No retranslation is performed at either date. Jan 13's EUR 10 has a booked USD
11 functional value; a later market quote cannot change J5. J6 offsets the
original in February, not retroactively in January. Raw original EUR 10 and
USD amounts remain separate; no cross-currency original total exists.

| As of | Cash USD functional | Other assets USD | Total assets USD | Liabilities USD | Direct equity USD | Unclosed earnings USD | Total equity USD |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2026-01-02 | 1000 | 0 | 1000 | 0 | 1000 | 0 | 1000 |
| 2026-01-31 | 1151 | 40 | 1191 | 300 | 1000 | −109 | 891 |
| 2026-02-02 | 1140 | 40 | 1180 | 300 | 1000 | −120 | 880 |

At Jan 31, cash is A-CASH-USD `1140` plus A-CASH-EUR functional `11`.
Expense net `+120` and revenue net `−11` yield unclosed earnings `−109`.
Assets `1191 = 300 + 891`. Jan 2→Jan 31 **point changes** are cash `+151`,
other assets `+40`, assets `+191`, liabilities `+300`, direct equity `0`,
unclosed earnings `−109`, total equity `−109`; these are not cash-flow categories.
Feb 2 reverses revenue and EUR bank value: assets `1180 = 300 + 880`.

Each account subtotal traces to exactly its listed J lines; the derived
unclosed-earnings line traces through revenue/expense accounts to J2/J5/J6.
For Jan 31, J6 is excluded because its accounting date is February. Selecting
J5's A-CASH-EUR GL line with Jan `[2026-01-01,2026-02-01)` and the report
revision must retrieve full J5, including both currencies and rate provenance.
The current pinned journal operation proves this one selected GL line, not
an unbounded subtotal-to-journal shortcut.

## Negative and boundary fixtures

| Fixture | Fixed expectation |
| --- | --- |
| Authorized empty book with supported policy | Assets/liabilities/equity all exact string `"0"`; fixture setup proves emptiness, but UI makes no no-entry claim from totals. Cash remains deferred; no journal links are invented. |
| Book A has only source observation for USD 500, unposted draft or pending command | Jan 31 Position stays `1191` assets and `1151` classified cash; separate attention state may mention observation/command, never add USD 500. |
| Book B has J1-like USD 70 capital/cash | Book A remains unchanged; no A+B sum or selector crossing entity/book. |
| Missing credentials, revoked read or foreign book | 401/403/404 respectively; no financial totals, cursor or existence hint. |
| J7 posts after Position revision R was read | Later pinned GL/journal at R returns 409 and no rows; refresh obtains new revision. J7's amount is deliberately unspecified, so no stale result is asserted as current. |
| Source status older than reviewed threshold while book revision is unchanged | Posted Position remains labelled by its own cutoff/revision; separate source warning only. Threshold and feed are not yet approved. |
| Cash membership absent or ambiguous | Show `Not configured`, not total assets, guessed cash or zero; existing BS totals remain available. |

These numbers are hand-fixed expectations independent of a generator or posting
algorithm. Implementers must copy them into a synthetic fixture and test exact
strings plus original-unit detail. If the chosen development posting policy does
not support a fixture operation, split the fixture into an explicitly supported
policy test and a pending policy case; do not weaken the expected accounting math.

## Fixed all-books orchestration cases — 2026-10-22

Owner approved the visual/scope proposal in conversation: all books grouped by
entity, explicit currency, assets/liabilities/book equity/equity change, direct
top navigation and gray zebra rows. This is design evidence, not an accounting
standard, approval of real-book policy, or evidence of runtime test coverage.
The implemented [reporting HTTP contract](../contracts/reporting-http.md) was
reread for per-request authorization, comparison envelope, exact strings, policy
errors and response limits. No external source or new normative edition is added.

The following are fixed synthetic response expectations. Book A uses J1–J6 above;
book B has one USD 70 capital journal on 2026-01-03. Revisions and generation
times are independent fictional metadata; they are never compared numerically
between books or used as one portfolio watermark.

| Row | Entity, book and requested dates | Exact assets / liabilities / book equity / equity change | Independent metadata |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | Entity Alpha / A; current 2026-01-31, prior 2026-01-02 | `1191` / `300` / `891` / `-109` | USD functional; revision `12`; generated 2026-02-03T10:00:00Z |
| B | Entity Beta / B; current 2026-01-31, prior 2026-01-02 | `70` / `0` / `70` / `70` | USD functional; revision `3`; generated 2026-02-03T10:00:02Z |
| A refreshed after correction | Entity Alpha / A; current 2026-02-02, prior 2026-01-31 | `1180` / `300` / `880` / `-11` | USD functional; revision `13`; generated 2026-02-03T10:01:00Z |
| Empty | Entity Alpha / Empty; current 2026-01-31, prior 2026-01-02 | `0` / `0` / `0` / `0`; no UI entry-count inference | Own USD policy/revision/date envelope |
| C | Entity Gamma / C, EUR functional policy unsupported today | No amounts; `unsupported_policy` | Currency remains EUR, never relabeled USD; no conversion |

The empty fixture is known empty from its setup, not from its report totals. The
existing balance-sheet envelope has no journal-count flag; offsetting posted
journals can also produce zero. No first-slice UI no-entry status is inferred.

Each accepted row must display its response's dates and revision details, even
when the shared requested dates match. A response that does not match the active
request must be rejected. The refreshed A row above belongs to a new date/scope
generation and cannot coexist as a late replacement in the old January request.
There is no A+B total, Entity Alpha subtotal, multi-currency total or FX result.
Original EUR 10 in A remains journal evidence, not a EUR-functional book total.

| Orchestration case | Fixed required outcome |
| --- | --- |
| A succeeds; B times out | A stays `1191` / `300` / `891` / `-109`; B shows unavailable with no zero or old values. |
| B access revoked after membership discovery | Per-book read returns denied/inaccessible; B's old financial values are discarded; A remains independently authorized. |
| Global identity expires during queue | Clear financial rows and stop scheduling queued requests; no stored response acts as a grant. |
| A stale revision returns 409 | A has explicit stale/refresh state with no reused amounts; no silent unpinned retry spliced into evidence. |
| Five authorized books selected | At most four requests in flight; fifth is visibly pending then requested when a slot frees; no truncation. |
| User selects Beta while Alpha request completes late | Render only Beta generation; discard late Alpha result. |
| Membership scope has no readable books | Empty workspace state; no fabricated zero portfolio. |
| Book has USD 70 capital journal and exact linked reversal | Assets/liabilities/equity and change can all be `0` despite two posted journals; render zero without a `No posted entries` status. |

## Alternatives, uncertainty and acceptance

A single new batch endpoint could establish a coherent transaction boundary, but
would require reviewed SQL/API work, resource limits and multi-book authorization
evidence. The chosen first slice reuses bounded authorized per-book responses
and explicitly exposes independent snapshots. Unbounded browser fan-out would
increase resource pressure; the initial maximum of four is a conservative project
choice requiring scheduling tests, not a benchmark or a capacity guarantee.
Same-currency summation can still double-count overlapping books and omit
eliminations; consolidation remains #59. Browser arithmetic also duplicates
server sign/currency rules and is excluded. Cash classification remains a future
server-owned policy decision; no cash field ships with this first overview.

Acceptance: the first-slice cases named in the Position contract, fixed multi-book
responses above and owner-reviewed desktop/mobile screenshots. Deferred
`TestPositionCashPolicy`, `TestPositionSourceExclusion` and `TestPositionBounds`
remain proposed extension coverage. #1 owns accountant-approved real-book policy;
#249 owns browser behavior and #59 owns consolidation/translation. Revisit
normative ISO mapping if Position becomes an exchange or audit export. Public
ISO access limits in P03–P05 remain unchanged; the all-books wrapper introduces
no new financial message or currency arithmetic.

documents.body:
# Posting policy and boundary sources

Reviewed 2026-10-11. These extend the [bibliography](bibliography.md),
[database sources](database-sources.md) and [contract sources](contract-sources.md).
The normative project choices are in [ADR 0005](../decisions/0005-development-accounting-policy.md)
and the [posting boundary](../contracts/posting-boundary.md).

## P01 — Accrual mechanics and authority boundary

OpenStax, *Principles of Accounting, Volume 1: Financial Accounting*,
[§4.1, Accrual Accounting](https://openstax.org/books/principles-financial-accounting/pages/4-1-explain-the-concepts-and-guidelines-affecting-adjusting-entries).
Reviewed the accrual-versus-cash discussion: recognition timing differs from cash
movement. This supports using a separately recorded accrual and settlement in
AC-10. It is introductory textbook guidance, not a complete revenue-recognition,
LLC tax or foreign-currency policy. Our service-LLC development workflow is an
engineering scope choice.

FASB [standards portal](https://fasb.org/standards?locale=en-US) identifies the
Codification as the authoritative nongovernmental US GAAP source in public search
metadata; direct browser extraction was effectively empty. **Discovery only**:
no ASC operative paragraphs were reviewed in this session. US GAAP remains a
research target; do not upgrade C04's AASB/IAS examples into US GAAP authority.

## P02 — Exact amounts and rounding

PostgreSQL 17 [§8.1.2 Arbitrary Precision Numbers](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/datatype-numeric.html#DATATYPE-NUMERIC-DECIMAL).
Reviewed exact numeric behavior, scale coercion, special values and tie rounding.
Numeric typmod casts can round before constraints inspect the original input;
built-in numeric rounding breaks ties away from zero. Hence our inference: validate
original text first and implement the selected half-even rule explicitly in the
owned database operation. The precision bounds and half-even choice are ours,
not prescribed by PostgreSQL, ISO 4217 or this accounting textbook.

## P03 — Restricted functions and transactions

PostgreSQL 17 [CREATE FUNCTION, Writing SECURITY DEFINER Functions Safely](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-createfunction.html#SQL-CREATEFUNCTION-SECURITY),
and [§13.2.3 Serializable Isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/transaction-iso.html#XACT-SERIALIZABLE).
Reviewed secure search path, public execution defaults, atomic privilege setup
and whole-transaction retry requirements. These support the restricted operation
boundary and retries; they do not prove our particular lock order, identity trust
or concurrency schedules. Go-with-triggers remains an alternative but would need
a separately demonstrated complete mutation protocol. Our choice favors one
reviewable database authority for the initial journal invariant.

## P04 — JSON input and replay equality

PostgreSQL 17 [§9.16.1, Table 9.48](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/functions-json.html)
(`IS JSON ... WITH UNIQUE KEYS`) and jsonb comparison operators; reviewed the
predicate's nested-key behavior and object/array facilities. Validate unique keys
on text before jsonb, then reject unsupported fields and normalize only defined
values. Our canonical request version is a local contract, not RFC 8785 or an ISO
financial message. Persisting normalized input and comparing it exactly is our
choice; no claim that arbitrary jsonb serialization is an interchange standard.

Also reviewed PostgreSQL 17 [§9.5 `sha256(bytea)`](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/functions-binarystring.html):
core digest computation needs no extension. The digest is diagnostic; stored
normalized-request equality owns replay. Upgrade tests must preserve historical
receipt interpretation even when serializer output changes.

## Applicability and limitations

Manual posting/reversal/read APIs and identifier-only commit notifications retain
the [existing ISO assessment](../contracts/api.md#operations-and-permissions).
Currency versions use ISO 4217 identifiers. No new bank message or external audit
export is introduced here. ISO schema provenance work in #17 neither approves nor
blocks this internal synthetic operation. Real financial exchange requires its
own completed mapping/profile gate. No source above certifies accounting software.

## P05 — pgx transaction adapter

[pgx v5.11.0 API documentation](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/jackc/pgx/v5@v5.11.0#Conn.BeginTx),
MIT licensed, reviewed BeginTx, Tx Commit/Rollback and PostgreSQL error handling.
The caller must explicitly manage transaction completion; cancellation does not
replace rollback cleanup. We pin the driver and module checksums, use explicit
isolation and parameter binding, and retain SQL as accounting authority. Bounded
whole-transaction retry and receipt resolution after uncertain commit are our
protocol; the driver alone does not establish exactly-once business effects.
The service accepts an owned connection/pool interface and never fetches secrets.

## P06 — Reference version serialization

PostgreSQL 17 [§13.3.5 Advisory Locks](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/explicit-locking.html#ADVISORY-LOCKS),
reviewed transaction-scoped lock lifetime. Our controlled currency setup uses a
per-code transaction advisory lock plus overlap checks; repeatable-read setup is
rejected because its old snapshot can miss a committed version after waiting.
Read-committed setup sees the subsequent statement snapshot; serializable setup
must retry a serialization failure. Hash collisions only serialize extra codes.
This is a setup concurrency choice, not a financial standard or a runtime grant.

## P07 — Provider revisions and linked journal corrections (2026-10-25)

[Plaid Transaction states](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/transactions-data/),
Pending and posted transactions: full selected section reviewed. Pending may be
removed/replaced with a distinct settled identity; settled records can also change.
API2020-09-14 sync added/modified/removed facts must preserve provider consistency.
These are feed mechanics, not authorization for accounting recognition or policy.
The existing proprietary mapping and ISO4217 units remain unchanged.

Refreshed PostgreSQL17 P03 selected full Serializable Isolation and Writing
SECURITY DEFINER Functions Safely sections2026-10-25: retries cover the complete
transaction, trusted search path/privilege setup protects restricted functions.
These mechanisms support one atomic correction but do not establish our lock
order, current actor/source permissions or exactly-once effects by themselves.

[Correction decision](../contracts/source-journal-corrections.md) compares linked
reversal/replacement with in-place edits, bank-table regeneration and delta
adjustments. SQL retains exact money/current authority and original historical
valuation; no new live policy is selected. USD50->55->60 and EUR examples are
independently fixed proposed acceptance, not generated implementation results.
Full Plaid manuals/paid accounting or ISO normative text were not reviewed here.

documents.title: Recovery and integration sources
documents.body:
# Recovery and integration sources

Reviewed 2026-10-11 before implementation. Relevant sections only; these are
engineering constraints, not accounting-policy or ISO conformance evidence.

| Source / review depth | Established fact | Project inference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [PostgreSQL17 isolation §13.2.2–3](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/transaction-iso.html), relevant sections reviewed | Serializable transactions can fail and must be retried in full; committed effects have serial semantics. | Commit command completion and financial mutation together; reuse existing full-transaction retry boundary. |
| [PostgreSQL17 locking §13.3.2–4](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/explicit-locking.html), row locks/deadlocks reviewed | Conflicting row locks wait; ordering matters and deadlocks can abort transactions. | Serialize the principal/command workflow and reuse accounting lock order; prove execute/cancel and revocation races independently. |
| [OWASP HTML5 Security, Local Storage](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/HTML5_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html#local-storage), full subsection reviewed | Browser storage is script-accessible and cannot stand in for authorization; sensitive data/session IDs should not be stored there. | Keep tokens and financial payloads out of persistent browser storage; discover server-owned recovery only after authentication. |
| [Playwright network, modify responses](https://playwright.dev/docs/network#modify-responses), relevant section reviewed | Routing can fetch the actual response before altering delivery. | Drop an acknowledged real API response to prove recovery against committed SQL state rather than a fabricated success. This does not test live identity providers. |

Alternatives: storing request bodies in localStorage survives refresh but leaves
financial data on shared browsers and cannot recover on another device. Receipt
lookup alone needs a retained key and cannot safely distinguish an in-flight write
from one never received. Server-owned prepare/execute/acknowledge adds round trips
and a narrow persistent command record, but makes unresolved work discoverable.
One unacknowledged command per principal is an intentional initial concurrency
limit. Revisit for multiple concurrent operators/devices with an explicit workflow
contract; do not silently auto-acknowledge outcomes. Revoked scope recovery remains
operator-mediated. Contract and named proof: [command recovery](../contracts/command-recovery.md).

documents.title: Server composition sources
documents.body:
# Server composition sources

## Decision record

Question: expose the reviewed SQL/identity adapters through one bounded server and
return enough authorized configuration for the first browser workflow. Status:
implementation review, owner project maintainer, reviewed 2026-10-11. This is an
application/security decision, not a change to accounting policy. The precise
contract and acceptance names are in [server contract](../contracts/server.md).

| Source and reviewed section | Established fact | Project interpretation and limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Go net/http: Server, Shutdown, MaxBytesReader](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http#Server), Go 1.26.9 source/API, relevant field and lifecycle sections | Header, read/write and idle deadlines are independent; Shutdown drains active HTTP connections. | Apply all bounds, concurrency cap and bounded drain; handler cancellation alone is not a connection timeout. Health probes do not prove financial readiness. |
| [Firebase Admin Go: NewApp](https://pkg.go.dev/firebase.google.com/go/v4#NewApp), v4.22.0 source `firebase.go` NewApp/getProjectID and Auth composition | Explicit config avoids Firebase config-file defaults; explicit token source bypasses default credential discovery. | Supply both project and token source. Reject emulator and credential-file environment presence; never execute live auth during default tests. |
| [Google OAuth2: ComputeTokenSource](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/oauth2/google#ComputeTokenSource), v0.36.0 source `google.go` computeSource | Obtains service-account tokens from the metadata service rather than a JSON key. | Choose metadata-only GCP workload identity. Local ADC or external file-based federation is deliberately unsupported; actual target metadata/IAM remains a deployment gate. |
| [pgx pool Config](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool#Config), v5.11.0, and local `pgconn/config.go` ParseConfig security notes | Pool limits are explicit; connection parsing can consult service, password and TLS files and environment defaults. | Narrow DSN URL input, reject inherited PG settings and overwrite file paths/defaults; bound pool and statements. Never expose parse errors. |
| [PostgreSQL 17 §13.3.2 and §13.3.4](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/explicit-locking.html) | Row share locks conflict with updates; consistent acquisition order reduces deadlock risk. | Lock principal/entity/membership/book before returning discovery; retain full-transaction retry and independent race proof. This is not proof of provider revocation atomicity. |

Review depth: full relevant linked API/locking sections plus the named locally
pinned SDK/driver source functions; no unseen text or normative ISO claim. Mutable
API pages were checked on the review date; local module versions above govern code.

## Alternatives and follow-up

ADC simplifies local development but can silently discover private files; rejected
for this service boundary. Stateless discovery without locks can race membership
revocation; rejected. An unbounded whole-account export scales poorly; bounded
configuration is the initial scope, with fail-closed limits rather than truncation.
Paginated discovery, distributed admission control and detailed provider readiness
need separate contracts when production size and deployment topology are known.
Issues #3/#6 retain those deployment dependencies; no source citation closes them.

documents.title: Shared acquisition source review
documents.body:
# Shared acquisition source review

Reviewed 2026-10-20 for issue #156. Only the named public sections and
repository contracts were reviewed; no live institution, provider payload or
tenant webhook setting was inspected.

## SA01 — Plaid Transactions webhooks

Plaid, [Transactions webhooks](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/webhooks/),
sections "Configuring Link for transactions webhooks" and "Integrating the
update notification webhook". Plaid says Transactions should be initialized
with Link to start acquisition, and `SYNC_UPDATES_AVAILABLE` follows the first
`/transactions/sync` call. The webhook announces available changes; it does not
replace the cursor pull. Inference: the publisher must dispatch initial demand
without waiting for a webhook, then process durable webhook/manual demand.

## SA02 — Plaid Transactions API

Plaid, [Transactions API `/transactions/sync`](https://plaid.com/docs/api/products/transactions/),
endpoint overview and availability notes. Cursor sync retrieves incremental
updates; empty first results are possible while Item data readies. Plaid
typically checks for new data one to four times daily, varying by institution.
Inference: a one-minute SQL publisher tick reduces application queue delay but
does not force a new bank pull or prove complete provider history.

## SA03 — existing Jayburd dispatch contracts

[Acquisition dispatch SQL](../contracts/acquisition-dispatch-sql.md) and
[runtime](../contracts/acquisition-dispatch-runtime.md), reviewed for function
authority, 25-candidate bound, replay and lease behavior. The fixed binding
is a deployment choice, not a SQL requirement for financial correctness.
Changing selection must preserve per-binding SQL authorization.

## SA04 — Go patch release and container provenance

The [official Go downloads](https://go.dev/dl/) list 1.26.10 for supported
platforms. The PR #230 `govulncheck` run identified GO-2026-6809 in the pinned
1.26.9 standard library and named 1.26.10 as fixed. Reviewed 2026-10-20 at
release listing and CI symbol-result depth; the vulnerability page was not
accessible through the source browser. `docker buildx imagetools inspect`
resolved the official `golang:1.26.10-alpine` multi-platform index to
`sha256:9ce231b28998b32e116927c61aa5c406183061d4f3f2d61b292c88e7f6bdf7ca`.
Inference: update all build/test toolchain pins together, then require the
repository security and container gates to prove the new pin.

| SI04 — SIX / ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency, [Global Financial Data Standards](https://www.six-group.com/en/products-services/financial-information/market-reference-data/data-standards.html), “We Maintain and Update the ISO Currency Codes” and “Current and Historical Lists” | The maintenance agency supplies current/historical currency lists and amendments. | Bind imported code/date to installed versioned metadata. No new list snapshot was downloaded or licensed/pinned here; reuse reviewed synthetic reference records and require source-release evidence for a real adapter. Minor units do not establish FX valuation or recognition policy. |
| SI05 — OWASP, [File Upload Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html), Introduction, Content-Type Validation, File Storage Location, User Permissions, Upload and Download Limits | Uploads require layered type/content checks, authorization, protected storage and bounded resources; client MIME is insufficient proof. | Restrict plaintext synthetic input, disallow archives/network fetch, store private provenance and redact diagnostics. Our numerical limits and retention durations are engineering proposals, not OWASP requirements. No external scanning service receives financial content. |
| SI06 — OpenStax, [Principles of Accounting, Volume 1, §8.6](https://openstax.org/books/principles-financial-accounting/pages/8-6-define-the-purpose-of-a-bank-reconciliation-and-prepare-a-bank-reconciliation-and-its-associated-journal-entries), textbook section reviewed | Bank and company records can differ; reconciliation identifies timing differences and items requiring book adjustments. | A booked statement item is evidence, not authorization to create a journal or recognize an expense. No reconciliation-complete claim without balances/outstanding-item rules. Educational source, not entity-specific GAAP/tax policy. |

## Alternatives and revisit conditions

A bank-specific CSV can be convenient but needs that bank's sign, identity,
correction and date documentation. OFX likewise needs a selected version/profile;
neither was reviewed as a supported adapter. camt carries richer standardized
semantics, but official artifact and usage-profile review remain unresolved.
Propose one internal synthetic CSV to test ingestion boundaries first; require an
explicit standards-deviation decision before implementation, not implied approval
from this source register. Revisit when #8 selects an actual bank/interface.

# Sync quality source review

## Decision and scope

Review date: 2026-10-13. Coordinator review supports the
[quality plan](../plans/sync-quality.md); no accounting-policy, cloud-capacity or
live-data approval follows from vendor documentation. Sources below were read
at the named sections of mutable official documentation; recheck during adapter
implementation. Existing [accounting sources](database-sources.md) and
[test corpus sources](testing-sources.md) remain authoritative for those topics.

## Reviewed sources

| Resource and reviewed sections | Established behavior | Project consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Plaid transaction states](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/transactions-data/), Pending and posted transactions; Testing pending and posted transactions | A pending replacement has a new posted identity; removal/addition can span pages. Details can change and matching links can be absent. Dynamic Sandbox users support lifecycle testing. | #85 must test the complete update; #88 exercises the actual adapter. Local posted journals stay immutable despite source revisions. |
| [Plaid transaction errors](https://plaid.com/docs/errors/transactions/), TRANSACTIONS_SYNC_MUTATION_DURING_PAGINATION | Restart the pagination loop at the original cursor when its underlying data changes. | Inject failure after intermediate pages; no partial cursor publication. |
| [Plaid Sandbox](https://plaid.com/docs/sandbox/), Webhooks; Differences between Sandbox and Production | Test webhooks can be triggered, but institution history and pending behavior are not fully representative. | Sandbox acceptance precedes a separately authorized statement-reconciled pilot; it cannot certify production behavior. |
| [Cloud Run concurrency](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/about-concurrency), Maximum concurrent requests per instance; Cost considerations | Concurrency limits and instance allocation affect resource consumption, scaling and cost. Application parallelism matters. | Measure concurrency, throughput, latency and resources together; replica count alone proves no capacity. |
| [Cloud Tasks pitfalls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/common-pitfalls), Execution order; Duplicate execution; Resource limitations | Delivery can duplicate or reorder; target capacity, throttling and concurrency affect backlog and delay. | Test duplicate effects, fairness, backpressure and recovery with exact final invariants. |

## Interpretation, alternatives and uncertainty

The 70% efficiency and latency targets in #89 are proposed engineering thresholds,
not vendor guarantees. Real results depend on contention, database capacity,
provider limits and workload distribution. Independent books and one hot book
need separate measurements. Finite local workloads establish no hosted cost SLA.

Alternative: only increase Cloud Run instances and watch request success. That
is cheaper to instrument but misses duplicate financial effects, stalled queues
and database saturation. Keep the existing transaction/outbox architecture and
measure it before considering partitioning or another database. #64 owns the
operational target review; #89 owns the executable evidence.

No financial wire format changes in this planning slice. Existing
[standards applicability](../contracts/standards.md) and
[provider mappings](../contracts/provider-ingestion.md) remain required. Plaid
JSON is proprietary; ISO identifiers or schema checks alone do not establish
bank reconciliation or ISO conformance.

# Synthetic accounting test resources

## Decision

Use all four resources below in different roles. None is a universal accounting
certification suite. Original fixtures and fixed expected balances belong to this
repository; downloaded tools, schemas and generated datasets stay in ignored
`.local/`. Reviewed 2026-10-11. See [execution and coverage](../../tests/corpus/README.md)
and [evidence](../runbooks/synthetic-corpus.md).

## T01 — Beancount

[Project and examples](https://github.com/beancount/beancount/tree/v3/examples),
[release metadata](https://pypi.org/pypi/beancount/3.2.3/json),
[license](https://github.com/beancount/beancount/blob/v3/COPYING).
A mature text-based double-entry engine, useful for independent balance assertions
and example vocabulary. Selected 3.2.3; GPL-2.0-only. Reviewed example inventory,
license and CLI behavior; executed `bean-check` on our five functional-currency
projections and an intentionally wrong balance. We do not copy upstream examples
or embed its implementation. Python is an optional external test tool, not a
backend dependency. These checks do not establish equivalent FX recognition,
rounding, tax treatment or valuation policy.

## T02 — hledger

[Testing guide](https://hledger.org/TESTS.html),
[release](https://github.com/hledgerorg/hledger/releases/tag/1.52.4),
[license](https://github.com/hledgerorg/hledger/blob/main/LICENSE).
A separate accounting engine with built-in unit tests and a source-level functional
test collection. Selected 1.52.4; GPL v3 license text reviewed (consult package
notices before redistribution). Reviewed test mechanisms and ran 246 built-in
tests plus our five balance comparisons and a negative assertion. We did not run
its entire source functional suite or vendor its tests. Agreement with Beancount
is useful arithmetic evidence, not proof of our future database transactions.

## T03 — ISO 20022 catalogue and camt.053

[Official catalogue](https://www.iso20022.org/iso-20022-message-definitions),
[official XSD endpoint](https://www.iso20022.org/message/23480/download),
[IPR policy](https://www.iso20022.org/intellectual-property-rights).
Selected `camt.053.001.14` (BankToCustomerStatementV14) for a schema smoke test,
not as an assumed bank-supported version. Reviewed catalogue metadata and IPR;
the official download returned HTTP 403. Contributors retain rights under the
published IPR terms; do not label ISO artifacts as MIT-licensed.

Provisional test artifact: [pinned third-party mirror](https://github.com/sebastienrousseau/camt053/blob/f4ff150917231c71f734abfcc2c25bed486cc184/camt053/xsd/camt.053.001.14.xsd).
Reviewed required statement/entry elements and validated original fictional XML.
Its digest is recorded below; comparison with an official download remains
BLOCKED. Schema acceptance covers structure only: our deliberately wrong closing
balance also validates. Official provenance, message rules, external code lists,
bank usage profiles and reconciliation semantics remain separate gates.

## T04 — Synthetic accounting data generator

[Project at reviewed commit](https://github.com/R3n0va/synthetic-accounting-data-generator/tree/b0f0e34ade2b18995252837e3011f3a89eb1ca52),
[MIT license](https://github.com/R3n0va/synthetic-accounting-data-generator/blob/b0f0e34ade2b18995252837e3011f3a89eb1ca52/LICENSE).
Version 2.3.0 supplies related fictional accounting CSV tables. Reviewed CLI,
smoke/baseline configuration, seeded randomness, money helper and output writer;
this was not a full security audit. The writer can delete its output directory:
use a new ignored directory only. Its two-decimal half-up rounding and German
VAT context do not define our accounting policy.

Two seed-42 smoke runs produced 35 byte-identical CSVs: 8 clients, 115 journals,
293 lines. Although its own validation passed, our exact-decimal audit found
15 journals with ±0.01 EUR residuals. Adopt it for import, volume and rejection
tests; do not bless those journals or auto-plug differences. The bounded sample
is not a scale benchmark. A four-journal balanced review subset is now embedded
in the integration-only demo seeder; its [provenance and MIT notice](../../internal/server/testdata/demo/README.md)
record unchanged EUR amounts, synthetic date/rate mappings and fixed cent oracles.
The remaining dataset is not bundled. The 15 invalid journals remain rejected.

## Local review transport

[Vite shared options, envDir](https://vite.dev/config/shared-options.html#envdir)
was reviewed for the separate loopback demo. `envDir: false` disables environment
file loading; an allowlisted process environment and fixed proxy target keep this
review bundle independent of managed identity configuration. This uses the locked
Vite dependency already supplied by the browser test toolchain, not a Next route.

## Pins and integrity

| Artifact | Pin / SHA-256 | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Beancount | 3.2.3 | Executed version verified; dependencies not fully locked |
| Beancount source archive metadata | `f52c4d237bcb092cbf02a29373d3e59d95349c2828a91491818ae437ee220f74` | PyPI advertised digest, not installed-wheel verification |
| hledger mac-arm64 archive | `c90a0fe4537439e958ce530f7175d937749f5f126759c94c1212774abe9eb971` | Download digest matched release metadata |
| Provisional camt XSD | `fdad51c5748d8b05056bb6dc140952e6c87ec749e63368df6834e4f36f9e6a9f` | Download digest computed; official comparison pending |
| Generator | `b0f0e34ade2b18995252837e3011f3a89eb1ca52` | Checkout HEAD verified; Python 3.12 / PyYAML 6.0.3 |

`JB-AC` in fixtures refers to our [accounting scenarios](../contracts/accounting-scenarios.md).
Source IDs identify influence/reference checks, not copied upstream data or
approval of the accounting policy. Changes to any pin require renewed evidence.
