# Dedicated webhook release sources — 2026-10-22

Selected official sections were reviewed for #271 before infrastructure changes.
These sources establish platform mechanisms, not approval to deploy or proof of
hosted receipt/publication. No provider payload, credentials, private state or
personalized Dashboard requirement was read. Public provider docs are mutable;
Terraform provider reference below is pinned to repository Google8.6.0.

| ID / authoritative reference | Reviewed sections / fact | Project inference and acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WR01 [Cloud Run container configuration](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/containers) | Configure entrypoint and arguments, including Terraform command/args. Overrides select the executable independently of image default. Relevant section read in full. | Same trusted worker digest explicitly selects `/webhook`, never worker default. `isolated_route_identity_and_budget` mocked test; actual revision readback remains required. |
| WR02 [Cloud Run public invocation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/authenticating/public) | Assign Invoker to allUsers, Terraform example and organization policy caveat. Relevant section read in full. | Explicit separate approval grants invocation on one fixed webhook service; retain IAM checks, preserve private services. `public_approval_is_one_fixed_service`; human/security review before exposure. No automatic fallback if organization policy rejects it. |
| WR03 [Cloud SQL IAM authentication](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/iam-authentication) | Automatic versus manual authentication; user/service-account administration and required instance flag. Relevant sections read in full. | Existing metadata-only connector and IAM SQL user plus separately reviewed PostgreSQL grants. Terraform user creation does not provide ledger authority. `dedicated_identity_and_two_static_reads` and owner SQL bootstrap proof. |
| WR04 [Secret Manager access control](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/access-control) | Secret Accessor permission table and principle of least privilege. Relevant sections read in full. | Exactly two existing secret-level bindings. These cover versions within each secret; exact numeric-version selection is runtime/release validation, not a version-level IAM claim. Bootstrap mocked grant assertions. |
| WR05 [Google provider8.6.0 Cloud Run service reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google/v8.6.0/website/docs/r/cloud_run_v2_service.html.markdown) | command/args, invoker_iam_disabled, scaling, request concurrency, timeout, resources, startup probe and traffic descriptions; selected relevant fields read. Registry HTML was unavailable; official tagged source used. | Dedicated service root, fixed bounds and TCP probe; mock tests verify requested configuration only. Actual traffic/Ready/image identity and effective IAM remain separate qualification. |
| WR06 [Google provider8.6.0 SQL user reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-google/v8.6.0/website/docs/r/sql_user.html.markdown) | IAM service-account example, username suffix, password/type argument descriptions. Relevant sections read in full. | Derive `.iam` SQL username from dedicated service identity; no password field. Bootstrap mock test verifies type/name/no password. |
| WR07 [Terraform provider mocking](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/tests/mocking) | Mock provider data and override timing sections read in full. Computed mock values default to unknown during plan; `override_during=plan` provides synthetic values without real provider operations. Mutable documentation; verified with pinned Terraform1.15.7. | Both suites keep `command=plan` and explicit mock provider. Mock SA email is synthetic; no real apply is needed to assert derived IAM identities. |
| WR08 [Cloud Run v2 Service](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.services) | Selected Service reconciliation, RevisionTemplate, ServiceScaling and TrafficTargetStatus JSON/field sections reviewed. Generation strings, readiness and serving traffic must agree after reconciliation; manual scaling ignores the maximum. | Offline receipt checks complete fixed runtime settings, serving canonical URL, automatic capacity and isolated public IAM. Synthetic drift tests; actual selected v2 readback remains unqualified. |
| WR09 [ContainerPort](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rest/v2/Container#ContainerPort) and [ProtoJSON](https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/json/#presence-and-default-values) | Selected HTTP protocol and omitted implicit-default descriptions, independently reviewed by the enrollment peer. No full API specification review. | Accept absent false/zero defaults only; reject null/wrong types, h2c, manual scaling and disabled URL/IAP. Fixed mutation fixtures cover these readback decisions. |

Existing P88-14/15 in [Plaid source register](plaid-88-test-sources.md) govern
webhook receipt/verification; [managed runtime](../contracts/webhook-managed-runtime.md)
records the existing proprietary-notification/ISO applicability. No financial
message, currency semantics, SQL schema or accounting policy changes here. Full
ISO text was not reviewed and no conformance is claimed.

The [SQL bootstrap source assessment](../contracts/webhook-bootstrap.md#sources-standards-and-alternatives)
records selected PostgreSQL17 grant, role, libpq and existing owner-function
sections and named synthetic acceptance; source review does not authorize grants.

WR10 [PostgreSQL17 predefined roles](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/predefined-roles.html):
reviewed Table21.1 and file/program privilege discussion. Such memberships can
carry authority without superuser attributes. Bootstrap and per-request receiver
therefore reject inherited `pg_` roles. Tests grant/revoke fixed roles only; no
server file access or program execution is attempted.

Alternative of widening worker/API roots was rejected because it couples private
IAM, caller policy and scheduler authority to a public notification boundary.
Two new roots require separate owner-created backend buckets and explicit release
orchestration, but make ownership reviewable. Mutable platform behavior, cold
start/latency, inherited IAM and eventual consistency remain hosted evidence gaps.
A source citation does not grant cloud mutation or approve residual security risk.

# Accounting proof hardening

<!-- stage-runbook: true -->

## Status and boundary

Issue [#67](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/67),
following merged audit #66 at `92044b0`. Strengthen synthetic evidence for the
existing [posting contract](../contracts/posting-boundary.md), exact historical
reversal and restricted writes. No accounting-policy, SQL migration, runtime,
API or cloud changes. General FX lifecycle and non-USD functional books remain
outside this proof.

## Stage ledger

| Stage | Result | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claim | #65 ACCT lease; isolated branch `issue/67-accounting-proof-hardening` | Preserve exact file scope |
| Implement tests | Historical spot reversal, reversal-of-reversal denial, exact SQLSTATE and complete-row comparisons | Review expected values |
| Validate | Default gates and full isolated PostgreSQL ledger suite passed | PR review and hosted checks |

## Current evidence

- `TestSpotReversalHistoricalProvenance`: independently specified EUR 100 / USD
  110 original, later eligible 1.25 rate proved by a separate USD 125 posting;
  reversal must retain USD 110 and original currency/rate IDs, account order,
  opposite sides, policy, scope and linkage. Original header/lines stay unchanged;
  replay leaves all captured durable rows unchanged.
- `TestReversalOfReversalDenied`: expected `already_reversed` semantic error,
  unchanged journal/line/audit/receipt/outbox/book/reference rows and subsequent
  authorized read. This does not test a provider or physical principal deletion.
- `TestSchemaPrivileges`: seed real history before mutation probes, require
  SQLSTATE 42501 and unchanged rows, then prove an authorized posting/read still
  works despite the temporary-table/search-path probe.
- `TestJournalCorrectionHistory`: immutable-row trigger must return P2108;
  compare complete durable rows after each denied update/delete, then read the
  trial balance successfully.

PASS on 2026-10-13 with Go 1.26.9: `make check test build` (vet, race tests,
context/doc links, migration integrity and binaries) and `make ledger-test`
(pinned PostgreSQL 17.11, all integration tests including the four above,
forward-upgrade sentinel, restore/replay and runtime-readiness denials).
The initial Docker credential-helper failure inside the sandbox was resolved by
an approved outside-sandbox rerun; no credential values were inspected. The
integration executable uses the existing static internal-network harness;
the ordinary Go tests use `-race`. No hosted identity or scale claim follows.

Source authority is the existing [SQL dictionary](../contracts/ledger-sql.md),
[development policy](../decisions/0005-development-accounting-policy.md) and
[audit findings](core-acceptance-audit.md). No new normative interpretation or
claim of accounting/ISO conformance.

## Remaining work

Hosted PR checks and owner review remain pending. Cloud acceptance stays #26/#27/#12; real policy,
import provenance and close/reconciliation remain their existing issue gates.

## PR handoff

Only integration tests and this runbook change. No migration or application
rollback is needed. Review expected values and row comparisons independently of
the posting implementation. Keep #1–4/#17 open; #67 acceptance is this bounded
test improvement, not broad bookkeeping readiness.

# Acquisition dispatch runtime delivery

## Status and boundary

Issue #7, DISPATCH-GO-7: local Go publisher/consumer foundation implemented and tested with provisional SQL15.
No live provider, cloud deployment, scheduler or financial posting is enabled.
Root owns HTTP/transport composition and proof harness; the SQL lane owns migration15.

## Stage ledger

- Read merged observer/acquisition contracts, implementation and source index.
- Coordinator approved target2, strict existing wakeup, separate authority and bounded
  request/settlement budgets. SQL author froze seven JSON function signatures.
- Implemented transaction adapter, bounded publisher and stable-claim consumer.
- Eight focused unit groups pass: ambiguous commit, confirmed rollback retries,
  queue/runner outside transactions, retry delay/error redaction, boundaries and
  cancellation, unknown settle/conflicting transport outcomes, returned metadata/profile isolation,
  and preserving a full retry delay through durable handoff.

## Current evidence

`go test -race ./internal/syncdispatch` and `make check test build` pass using pinned
Go1.26.9. The default suite required loopback-listener sandbox escalation; no
external provider was called. Logs: `/private/tmp/jayburd-dispatch-default.log`. Actual SQL15/Runner composition now passes: eleven groups, nine subtests including
three real PostgreSQL groups. Real acquisition uses restricted logins, pinned HTTP
with injected synthetic responses and private durable staging. Evidence covers:

- Exact `9007199254740993.01`, cursor C1, one source observation, no journals/outbox.
- Actual completion and settlement commits with lost replies; duplicate delivery
  makes no second provider request. Current revoked authority denies receipt replay.
- Actual unknown delivery claim performs zero provider calls and creates no sync set.
- HTTP429 Retry-After3600 creates retry_wait and generation2 atomically before ack;
  old delivery cannot bypass the delay. Fixture-controlled eligibility advance lets
  generation2 complete with exactly one source observation and no journal.

Proof log: `/private/tmp/jayburd-sync-dispatch-go-proof.log`. Root owns the final
SQL15 integration rerun and private HTTP/Cloud Tasks composition proof. No hosted
acceptance is claimed.

## Remaining work

Final SQL15 and private HTTP/task composition passed in the
[coordinator delivery proof](acquisition-dispatch.md). Actual cloud delivery/OIDC and provider qualification remain separate gates.

## PR handoff

Initial implementation handoff: unit/race/default gates passed; actual PostgreSQL
proof passed against provisional and final integrated migration15. Owned paths are internal/syncdispatch (excluding SQL author's
SQL integration file), this runbook and the corresponding contract.

- Follow-up stage: real delayed retry and redispatch proof passed without changing
  production Go; initial core handoff was `6985353`.

matching API and web images. The new worker image needs its own paused release
and binding review before acquisition. Hosted Sandbox enrollment remains the
acceptance gate.

## Matching application promotion

This second, dependent release restores the reviewed Sandbox connection policy
and public browser identity metadata while pinning API, migrator and web to the
same successful build 38843645129. Dispatch only after migration-only release
reports `migration-execution-passed` at schema 18. The runtime workflow checks
the current schema before changing Cloud Run services. The separate paused
worker image, account binding and actual hosted Sandbox completion remain to
be verified after application promotion.

## First paused worker candidate

The owner reported binding `b095afc3-d9e4-4273-9c2f-bc7c766adce3` from the
scoped read-only lookup. The same successful build 38843645129 contains an
encrypted-reader worker candidate, pinned by digest in
`deploy/worker-release.json`. A [metadata-only preflight](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/164#issuecomment-6219312071)
read back paused Scheduler, an existing queue, enabled static credential version
metadata, narrow KMS key IAM, and an absent worker service pair. The dedicated
worker deployment identity provider was disabled at preflight. This established
the initial release boundary; it is superseded by the paused deployment below.
No provider credential, Terraform state/plan, or financial row was read.

## Paused worker deployment

PR #172 merged the pinned candidate to main after all five checks passed. On
2026-10-16 the owner authorized enabling the isolated worker WIF pool and OIDC
provider directly in GCP. Readback confirmed the provider still restricts the
numeric owner, actor and repository IDs, `workflow_dispatch`, main and the exact
`deploy-workers.yml` workflow; its service-account impersonation binding is
scoped to that repository ID. The private worker runtime state bucket exists
with versioning. The direct enablement creates Terraform drift: preserve the
already-enabled build and application deployment flags, and set
`enable_github_worker_deploy_identity=true` in the owner-operated foundation
inputs before the next foundation apply. No foundation state or plan was read.
The checked-in `deployed-dev-identities.tfvars` overlay keeps all three GitHub
identity flags true when passed after private `owner.tfvars`. Foundation input
validation rejects a plan for this deployed project if any is false, including
when the overlay is omitted. Owner review and apply against private state remain
required to reconcile the direct GCP enablement.

[Worker release run 38946843411](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/actions/runs/38946843411)
passed exact manifest/build evidence, infrastructure tests, workload identity
authentication, isolated runtime apply and receipt validation. The public
receipt reports `paused-workers-observed`, publisher revision
`jayburd-dev-acquisition-publisher-00001-rs4`, sync revision
`jayburd-dev-acquisition-sync-00001-ktn`, and Scheduler `PAUSED`; independent
Cloud Run and Scheduler metadata readback agrees. This is control-plane evidence
only. It does not prove hosted ciphertext persistence, authorized worker read,
provider acquisition or ledger acceptance. Do not activate Scheduler from this
release alone.

The old Hosted Link attempt remains a one-shot recovery case. Its binding ID
does not demonstrate encrypted credential persistence or a completed Item.
Issue #160 remains open until the owner uses the updated UI to classify the
attempt and demonstrates a fresh Sandbox completion through binding review.
Issue #164 remains open through hosted API ciphertext and worker read acceptance.

# Cloud Shell SQL bootstrap
<!-- stage-runbook: true -->

## Status and boundary

Issue #26 continues from merged #43 (`dc77d9a`), owner-authorized development
bootstrap. Cloud Shell network reachability was reported by the owner; remote
command access was independently verified. Neither proves SQL authorization.

## Stage ledger

| Stage | Evidence | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connectivity | Owner reports TCP 3307 PASS; remote command probe PASS | Test IAM and SQL authority |
| Operator | Existing reviewed Terraform optional operator apply exited 0; IAM login/capability query passed | Execute the reviewed SQL transaction |
| Bootstrap | Hash-verified merged SQL committed, then replayed successfully | Verify grants and ownership |
| Privilege readback | API has no schema creation or owner/operator membership; migrator has explicit owner SET, no ADMIN or inheritance | Execute the dedicated migration artifact in a later controlled stage |

## Current evidence

- PASS: Cloud Shell command access through `gcloud cloud-shell ssh`; existing
  session authorization used internally. No `--authorize-session`, token printing,
  credential-file inspection or credential transfer was used. SDK-created SSH
  keys remain outside Git and were not inspected.
- PASS: proxy v2.26.0 IAM authentication as the separate operator. Readback confirmed
  CREATEROLE, cloud administrator membership, database ownership authority and
  schema creation permission.
- PASS: `db/bootstrap/cloud-sql.sql` SHA256
  `44e7e971be93ba5a17cc9f0660b9797fa806422fc97298f2a617017b8c5b635d`
  verified after copying to Cloud Shell. Initial transaction and replay both
  completed with ON_ERROR_STOP. This proves the managed administrator can execute
  the existing login alterations and role grants; merged SQL is unchanged.
- PASS: SQL privilege metadata confirms API safe attributes, bookkeeping_api
  membership, no owner/identity-operator/cloud-admin membership, no database,
  deployment or public schema CREATE, and connection limit 20. Migrator has safe
  attributes, owner membership with SET true / INHERIT false / ADMIN false,
  database/deployment CREATE, no public CREATE or cloud administrator membership,
  and connection limit 2.
- PARTIAL: these are actual catalog/privilege readbacks through the administrator,
  not separate API/migrator IAM logins or attempted DDL denial under those sessions.
  The `ledger` schema is absent; no product migration or enrollment ran.
- Each proxy stopped through an exit trap. Only reviewed SQL and the official
  proxy binary were transferred/downloaded; operational logs stayed private.
- PASS: post-bootstrap private Terraform drift check exited 0 with the operator
  input preserved. This covers infrastructure, not write-only SQL memberships.
- PASS: `make check test build` with Go 1.26.9, including vet/race tests, migration
  artifact checks and binaries. No product code or merged migration was changed.

## Remaining work

Run the dedicated migrator artifact under its own workload identity, prove
forward migration/replay and API denial with actual runtime sessions, then perform
restore and pool/load acceptance. Do not use the administrator to run migrations
or relax metadata-only application authentication to run it under Cloud Shell's
human identity. Image/job provenance and reviewed deployment gates still apply.

## Operator retention and resume

The successful bootstrap created an ownership dependency: `deployment` is owned
by the operator, which also executed role grants. The operator is intentionally
retained for the next administration stage; cleanup is not claimed. Review schema
ownership and grantor dependencies before revoking its membership or deleting it.
Do not force-drop or ABANDON it. Complete this ownership review before runtime
release; it is part of #26's remaining work.

Preserve the explicit `bootstrap_operator_email` input on subsequent application
applies while this dependency exists. The selected human IAM login can be verified
by names/types through `gcloud sql users list`; never retrieve credentials or state.
Private Terraform directory remains
`/private/tmp/jayburd-iam-bootstrap/.local/iam-bootstrap/application`, using the
existing application GCS backend. Its source matches merged #43. Resume inputs
and quota settings are in [provisioning](cloud-sql-bootstrap.md#operational-resume).

Cloud Shell working directory: `/tmp/jb-bootstrap.lhcrBG`; reviewed SQL and proxy
are there with private logs. Treat the directory as ephemeral. Recopy/reverify
the exact SQL hash if it disappears. The [IAM bootstrap instructions](iam-bootstrap.md)
describe the pinned proxy and private socket boundary. `gcloud cloud-shell ssh`
with `--command` worked; the installed CLI's custom `--ssh-key-file` flag was
incorrectly boolean, so SDK default SSH handling was used without overwrites.

## PR handoff

Keep #26 open until named cloud acceptance passes. Source and implementation
authority remain [G24/G25](../research/gcp-sources.md) and the
[Cloud SQL contract](../contracts/cloud-sql.md).

Follow-up: [IAM operator implementation and connectivity evidence](iam-bootstrap.md)
records the next attempt and its local transport blocker.
The subsequent [Cloud Shell bootstrap](cloud-shell-bootstrap.md) succeeded;
follow that record for current role state and operator retention.

1. Establish the administrative SQL bootstrap path. The current Terraform root
   provisions only API/migrator logins; neither is an administrator. G24 in the
   [source register](../research/gcp-sources.md) documents a possible separate IAM
   operator path. It is a proposal, not an applied grant or proven compatibility.

   identity mapping and hosted finance acceptance under #26/#6/#27.

Use secret-free configuration and redacted outcomes. Never retrieve a password or
print an access token. If the IAM operator cannot satisfy the administrator gate,
the owner must inject any required credential privately; this is not permission
to give the API or migrator cloud administrator membership.

Private operational copies: `.local/cloud-sql/foundation` and
`.local/cloud-sql/application` in this worktree. Logs, plans and state remain
protected and excluded from Git. GCS backends use
`jayburd-bookkeeping-dev-jayburd-dev-foundation-state` / prefix `foundation` and
`jayburd-bookkeeping-dev-jayburd-dev-application-state` / prefix `application`.
Initialize from the merged source if the temporary worktree is unavailable.

Both roots require `project_id=jayburd-bookkeeping-dev`. Foundation also uses
`project_number=9088794002`, `billing_account_id=012EA6-AB37B6-77BD42`,
`enable_github_build_identity=true`, `enable_github_deploy_identity=false`.
With existing user ADC, supply `USER_PROJECT_OVERRIDE=true` and
`GOOGLE_BILLING_PROJECT=jayburd-bookkeeping-dev` (source G17).
Keep command output private; a `plan -detailed-exitcode` result of 0 means no drift,
1 failure, 2 changes. Do not inspect or publish its contents.

## PR handoff

Keep #26 open until its named cloud acceptance checks pass. This runbook records
actual results, not readiness inferred from a Terraform apply.

## Provisioning estimate

Rechecked [Google's Iowa list prices](https://cloud.google.com/sql/pricing) on
2026-10-12; the full page exceeds the research tool's response limit, but indexed
regional compute/storage tables were available. This arithmetic estimate replaces
an interactive calculator export for this authorized development apply:

| Assumption | Monthly USD at 730 hours |
| --- | ---: |
| db-g1-small × 0.035/hour | 25.55 |
| Initial 10 GiB SSD × 0.000232877/GiB-hour | 1.70 |
| Assumed 10 GiB used backups × 0.000109589/GiB-hour | 0.80 |
| Baseline subtotal | 28.05 |

At the 20 GiB disk cap and assumed 20 GiB used backups, the subtotal is USD30.55.
Backup usage is not capped by that assumption. Retain the existing USD5
backup/PITR/restore allocation; a four-hour same-tier restore adds roughly USD0.15
compute/storage before backup/log/egress charges. Other services, log/PITR growth,
network egress, taxes and actual restore duration are additional; the USD50
project alert is not a hard limit. Observed spend remains #12 evidence.

# Connection browser proof

## Status and boundary

routes, credentials, provider calls, secret discovery or migration changes. Explicit

## Stage ledger

## Current evidence

The fixture injects memory-only Link/exchange/manifest/secret dependencies and the

serializes reads/writes, independently of sequential browser behavior. It accepts
no caller-selected entity, source, credentials or provider payload. Repeated trigger
calls reuse the claim and must not refetch. The separate explicit fixture-owner
source review grant precedes acquisition; product binding does not self-grant review.

000000000002/000000000003; bank 000000000011, expense 000000000012. Existing
synthetic browser principal and USD currency remain unchanged. UI adapter receives
`synthetic-link` and returns `synthetic-public`. This proves owned boundaries only,
not provider identity, live Link or Infisical qualification.

## Remaining work

Coordinator must exercise browser enrollment, explicit binding, acquisition, reviewed
category draft and explicit source-linked posting, with lost committed reply/reload
recovery. Database assertions require two source observations, one journal/link/outbox,
exact 0.10 posting and no automatic posting before approval. Fixture alone does not
claim that journey passed. Live connection deployment and provider qualification stay
separate.

## PR handoff

Only new test fixture, minimal integration-server injection and this runbook belong
to this lane. Root owns script, browser harness and acceptance assertions. Existing
non-connection app and demo paths remain selected by their existing flags.

# Connection operations SQL delivery

## Status and boundary

SQL foundation for #103/#104, lease OPS-SQL-103-104. Migration 14 only; prior migrations
remain unchanged. Public recovery discovery, stream operations and dedicated verified
notification intake share existing acquisition generations. No real provider, cloud,
secret retrieval, scheduler deployment or financial mutation.

## Stage ledger

| Stage | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Source review | Selected official Plaid verification/Transactions and PostgreSQL 17 isolation sections reviewed; contract labels project inferences. |
| Contract approval | Coordinator approved interfaces, individual stream pause, authoritative unfinished count, separate stream pin and scoped signal outbox before implementation. |
| Initial PostgreSQL proof | Migrations 1–14 and first four test groups passed using disposable actual API/sync/webhook/operator logins. |
| Defaults | `make check test build` PASS; `/private/tmp/jayburd-connection-ops-default.log`. |
| Final regression | All eight actual PostgreSQL groups PASS, including completion/signal race, nulls/revoked replay, expired binding vs unknown claim and concurrent fresh enrollment. |

## Current evidence

`internal/connectionops/operations_integration_test.go` runs only with explicit
`-connection-ops-proof` against synthetic connection_ops_template databases. Tests
use immutable exact literals; no credentials or provider payloads are loaded.

- Discovery/guard: same-actor scoped pagination, global unfinished count, expiry,
  exact-key recovery, fresh attempt rejection and revoked access.
- Pause/resume: held-set fencing, independent stream revision, unchanged binding
  approval, unaffected sibling, stale operation denial and atomic resume intent.
- Webhook receipt: same-JWT replay once, later same-body notification preserved,
  conflicting replay rejected, paused siblings excluded and current revocation.
- Catch-up/roles: bounded pagination, stable tick, restricted function ACL and mixed
  role denial. Actual acquisition remains owned by the existing runner.
- Completion race: simultaneous real database completion and notification preserve
  a later generation, with complete timestamp and unknown provider update time.
- Malformed/revoked replay: required nulls, old issue time, unknown Item, revoked
  source bind and wrong scope leave no partial receipt or wakeup.

Proof log: `/private/tmp/jayburd-connection-ops-proof.log`. Test names here do not
claim independent provider verification; the Go verifier lane owns that evidence.

## Remaining work

Coordinator integrates webhook Go, HTTP/API, UI, schema-version and role bootstrap
changes and runs combined regressions. Deployment, real ingress/secret policy,
message transport, scheduler/backoff and live qualification remain separate. The
new wakeup outbox is a durable intent, not a claim of delivered or completed work.

## PR handoff

Owned files: migration14 pair/checksum, new connectionops SQL tests, contract and
this runbook. Copied scripts/test-connection-ops.sh remains untracked; root owns it.
No push or external mutation. Defaults, stage guard and diff check required before
commit; final named evidence recorded here.

Expiry boundary proof preserves old paused Item/reference history while allowing a new
attempt only for known expired binding_review; expired unknown claims remain blocked.
Concurrent fresh Begin proves exactly one attempt wins and one receives P2804.

## Follow-up: existing lifecycle fixture ordering

The combined regression exposed an older test that created a fresh new enrollment
after deliberately leaving a rotation claim unresolved. Migration 14 correctly
rejects that sequence. The fixture now prepares and expires the unrelated unclaimed
attempt before starting the competing lifecycle claims. All private-context expiry,
public-history readability and exclusive-claim assertions remain unchanged; no
production guard is relaxed. Existing connection-state PostgreSQL proof PASS: 12 top-level groups and 5 named
subtests against migrations 1–14. Log: `/private/tmp/jayburd-connection-ops-legacy-proof.log`.
This fixture-only adjustment does not change the final migration checksum.

`c50044383052eba4b2bd89cc32d6b723000745c6`. Build 39276797882 attempt 1

using a separate runtime manifest. The worker candidate hash is
`10889eb58d46aed7bfc6fdf365cf81a0dd1561c720ee39ef320a5a6d12f98027`;

PR #192 passed all five required checks and merged as
`42167d86d0c335ee9c701cc187b09878f736c6f4`. Owner-dispatched image build
[39208669344](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/actions/runs/39208669344)

The first fresh production-like Sandbox acceptance attempt after the migration
and runtime rollout (`f9b70761-90b4-4988-9ecf-7d13c6f6fe95`) remained
`link_ready`. Cloud Run request metadata recorded POST `/complete` returning
503 in 0.13 seconds on 2026-10-19; the attempt GET returned 200. A connected
Item, encrypted credential write, and binding review have **not** been observed.
The 503 alone does not distinguish encrypted handoff read, Plaid session status,
credential preflight, or a later execute step. A retry of the same attempt is
safe only after checking it is still `link_ready`; never repeat an exchange after
the claim state changes.

This branch adds bounded, static server-side failure-stage logging for Hosted
completion. Logs identify the attempt and fixed stage but never include Link or
public tokens, provider responses, credentials, or error strings. The browser
contract and provider call behavior remain unchanged. Acceptance requires a
fresh Sandbox completion reaching `binding_review` with a stored credential and
then a connected Item; diagnostics alone do not close #187.

[39199242284](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/actions/runs/39199242284)

metadata. Only after that runtime release should the owner start a fresh Plaid

recoverable token, and a successful release alone does not establish a
completed Plaid exchange or connected Item.

schema before the API/web rollout proceeds.

passed locally. Migration deployment 39201782204 produced a successful

[39201782204](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/actions/runs/39201782204)
completed with `migration-execution-passed` using the pinned migrator image.

`transport-smoke-passed` receipt records ready API revision
`jayburd-dev-api-00010-fj8` and web revision `jayburd-dev-web-00010-l28` from
the approved build. The canonical public web origin returned HTTP 200 on
2026-10-19. This release did not activate the acquisition Scheduler.

A fresh user-driven Plaid Sandbox enrollment is now the outstanding acceptance
test: create a new connection attempt, complete Hosted Link, use **Check bank
setup completion**, and confirm binding review and a connected Item. Old
attempts predate encrypted handoff storage and cannot validate reload recovery.
Neither transport smoke nor a Plaid success screen proves exchange or a stored
credential; #160/#164 remain open until those observations are recorded.

## Status and boundary

Build on merged PR110 (60c0e3e). Fix explicit connection configuration through the
existing reviewed release pipeline; no deployment or provider call.

## Stage ledger

Reviewed release/hosted contracts and official variable/revision sections. Selected
runtime manifest v2 with mandatory explicit connection state and unchanged migration
v1. Preserve existing gate authority; record approved configuration separately from
provider/runtime acceptance.

## Current evidence

`make release-test`:23 Node tests and fake-executable deployment orchestration PASS.

policy expiry, exact CLI input generation, migration isolation and rollback digest.

v1 stays compatible. Legacy rollback receipts lack configuration evidence and fail
closed. No product SQL/API/browser changes, cloud mutation or credential retrieval.

## Historical attempt review release candidate (#160)

PR #176 merged with all five checks passing. Its browser change keeps an authorized
book selected after an attempt-only denial and redirects Cloud Run's alternate
service URL to the configured public origin. Successful image build
[39067510528](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/actions/runs/39067510528)

`d1913796ad51699c361413b7915d4eb0e81ddc4d`. The next

the reviewed Sandbox connection policy, public identity configuration, and
schema-status-only `sandbox-promote` operation. It does not migrate SQL or alter
the paused acquisition worker.

Release checks and owner review precede dispatch. After promotion, verify the
canonical web URL, inspect the historical attempt without losing the book, and
only then begin a fresh Sandbox Hosted Link session if the old credential is
confirmed unavailable and explicitly abandoned. Binding review, encrypted
credential persistence and authorized worker read remain hosted acceptance
evidence, not claims of this image build.

`05803d7210c8fa40cade63cd196dad65f407b922ff31fbbc36683e23cd99512e`,

PR #177 merged as `700fdbca45e1e51559612cf7a9f0f45d6ba47ced`.
[Deployment 39072895377](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/actions/runs/39072895377)

Scheduler readback remains PAUSED. Issue comments
[#160](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/160#issuecomment-6241885269)
and [#164](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/164#issuecomment-6241889935)
retain the hosted acceptance limits. No fresh Hosted Link completion, ciphertext
persistence or authorized worker read has been observed from this release.

## Failed-connection retry release candidate (#160)

PR #184 merged as `c0cb29efe0d71c26293a1b9b9c4ccdc7ce73cbbc` after all
five checks passed. Owner-dispatched [image build 39152439769](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/actions/runs/39152439769)

The browser offers **Try connecting again** for a failed new connection. It
reconciles the exact old attempt and asks the server to close it only after a
confirmed missing-credential result. A stored credential, another unfinished
attempt, or uncertain response stops the restart. A fresh Link session begins
only after the server confirms the old attempt is safely closed. This release
does not claim a successful fresh enrollment, encrypted credential write,
binding review, transaction acquisition or posted journal. Those require the
owner's next hosted Sandbox test and separate review.

Release metadata validation passed against the successful build run and all
three retained candidate receipts. The exact manifest SHA-256 is
`767ce3e126bbaf0f35b86c05baab2da8533ad50c5de52a044905bea7c53eca98`.

The deployed Begin request returned 503 before returning a Hosted Link URL.

and accepted the project-ID resource for the same development key. This does not
qualify the runtime service account. The bank-token-vault contract records the

accepts canonical key-version metadata while retaining numeric historical rows;

A canonical-key synthetic encrypt/decrypt roundtrip also passed under the
operator account. Runtime identity qualification remains outstanding.
Deploy migration 20 before promoting API and worker
images. Keep Scheduler paused until the separate acquisition acceptance.

Official Plaid SDK adoption is tracked separately in #195. Fresh hosted enrollment
and credential persistence remain unproved; passing unit tests or rollout alone
does not close #187.

## Official connection SDK (#195)

Pinned Plaid Go v49 source review is recorded in plaid-link-browser. Replace
connection wire models with generated clients, preserving bounded Sandbox-only
transport, redacted errors, no retries and decimal ingestion. Validation passed: `make check test build connection-service-test provider-flow-test`,
`make app-integration connection-browser-test`, and explicit SDK no-retry, ambient
configuration, and monetary-field projection regressions. Local tests use Go 1.26.5
via an external modfile; repository toolchain remains 1.26.9. No SQL changes beyond
the #194 dependency. CI, image promotion and fresh hosted acceptance remain pending.

The browser fixture now composes the actual official SDK-backed HTTPProvider
against an in-memory synthetic HTTP transport. The strengthened
`make connection-browser-test` passed: Hosted Link pending/completed checks,
one public-token exchange, encrypted storage, acquisition, review, posting and
lost-response recovery. The earlier direct provider-interface fixture remains
in the separate provider-flow test; it does not qualify SDK wire behavior.

| Implement | Migration 13 adds actor/scope/expiry/nonce attempts, one-shot claim and manifest-before-secret publication, immutable credential receipts, explicit binding, scoped management and current acquisition context/resume. |
| Review refinements | Same-Item/account verification, precise affected-stream pins, per-account vs Item fences, exact UTC expiry and malformed-container diagnostics; worker configuration disable explicitly distinguished from revoking enrolled acquisition. |
| SQL proof | Disposable PostgreSQL migrations 1–13 plus **12 top-level groups and 5 named subtests PASS**. Actual operator/API/sync logins; no role impersonation at runtime boundaries. |
| Default checks | `make check`, `make test`, `make build` PASS with Go 1.26.9 and isolated caches. |
| Integration | Coordinator owns runner/Make/CI/schema-version and prior privilege-fixture extensions; shared combined regression runs after this commit is integrated. |

## Current evidence

Executed on 2026-10-13:

```sh
PATH=/private/tmp/jayburd-toolchain-1.26.9/go/bin:$PATH \
GOCACHE=/private/tmp/jayburd-go-cache GOMODCACHE=/private/tmp/jayburd-go-modcache \
bash scripts/test-connection-state.sh
```

The host Docker credential helper required normal sandbox escalation. Tests used
only private disposable synthetic PostgreSQL databases and fixed fictional logins;
no inherited DSNs or credential files. Proof log:
`/private/tmp/jayburd-connection-sql-proof.log`.

- `TestConnectionOneShotAndRecovery`: first-only Link/exchange execution grants,
  uncertain exchange not retried, manifest-before-secret confirmation, resolved
  reference acknowledgement and explicit binding without journal creation.
- `TestConnectionProviderFirstAndOverlap`: two new provider sources, bounded explicit
  source grants, safe public status/listing and overlap hold for an existing source.
- `TestConnectionRotationAndDisconnect`: one account disconnect leaves sibling
  acquisition valid; rotation fences shared Item before remote work, publishes a new
  reference/version, preserves disconnected state and rejects old worker claims.
- `TestConnectionRemovalUncertainty`: unknown provider reply remains pending; exact
  confirmation/replay disconnects every approved sibling without blind removal retry.
- `TestConnectionReconnectIdentity`: different Item or missing bound account rejected;
  same Item update preserves source identities/reference/version.
- `TestConnectionClaimCommitRecovery`: deliberately discard an application-visible
  committed claim reply, then contend two real replay sessions. Both return no
  execution permission; exactly one reservation event. This models reply loss, not
  an injected network partition inside PostgreSQL COMMIT.
- `TestConnectionRevocationAndScope`: current read/import/connect/source-bind,
  wrong entity and disabled service gates apply to successful attempt reads/replay.
- `TestConnectionManifestAndBindingGates`: unknown token field and duplicate provider
  metadata rejected; five unverified/account-class/currency/grant/duplicate selection
  subtests leave no partial binding.
- `TestConnectionWorkerContextAndPrivileges`: current fenced opaque-reference lookup,
  explicit absent resume, role/table/helper denials and immutable claim identity.
- `TestConnectionExpiryAndAtomicBinding`: strict UTC/expired handoff; one invalid
  account rolls back all selected source/grant publication.
- `TestConnectionMalformedContainers`: null/object/scalar account and binding
  containers return fixed diagnostics, including malformed nested entries.

Default logs: `/private/tmp/jayburd-connection-check.log`,
`/private/tmp/jayburd-connection-test.log`, `/private/tmp/jayburd-connection-build.log`.
Connection-service and acquisition integration evidence belongs to their lanes and
the coordinator's combined runbook; this lane does not claim their results.

## Remaining work

Live Link/session-association qualification, provider/Infisical permissions and
verified secret-store adapters, approved retention/cleanup, hosted execution and
Sandbox/production acceptance remain explicit external gates. Existing runtime
Infisical read-only policy is not expanded by SQL reference publication. New accounts
are not silently added to existing Items; a separately reviewed binding expansion
must approve their scope. Overlap release and posted correction resolution remain
separate; source and journal evidence is retained across disconnect/removal.

An exchange_claimed attempt after a crash is unresolved recovery, never retry
permission. No lease-based claim takeover or automatic remote retries exist. A lost
secret acknowledgement resolves only its preallocated reference/verified manifest.
A configuration change affects connection management enrollment authority; stopping
existing acquisition requires its current grant revocation or Item/account lifecycle.

## PR handoff

Owned files: migration 13 pair/checksum, `internal/connectionstate` SQL tests,
contract and this runbook. Migrations 1–12 untouched. Coordinator's copied
`scripts/test-connection-state.sh` stays untracked and is not committed here.
Stage guard and diff check required before every implementation commit. No push,
provider access or deployment from this lane.

## Follow-up: credential context and exclusive remote operations

Independent service review found that current actor authorization alone did not
revalidate Item generation before credential reads. Private context now rejects
stale nonterminal Item/sibling pins and expired unclaimed attempts while public
status stays readable. Begin and first claim reject Items with unresolved remote
operations, preventing overlapping rotation/removal/reconnect calls.

`TestConnectionPrivateContextFenceAndExclusiveClaim` PASS in the disposable
PostgreSQL proof: two attempts prepared before a claim, rejection of the second
claim/context, rejection of all new lifecycle modes after the claim, generation
change rejection before credential access, and retained public status reads.
The focused proof now passes 12 top-level groups and 5 named subtests. Unknown
operations without a persisted manifest still require separately reviewed recovery;
there is no automatic retry or fresh-attempt escape.

# Connections workspace delivery

<!-- stage-runbook: true -->

## Status and boundary

Build the supported frontend slice of #104 from merged #106 `6c6b546`.
Existing connection HTTP/service contracts are authoritative. Default startup has
no provider composition; no real credentials, Link script or provider calls.

## Stage ledger

- Verified merge and reviewed #104 against merged API, SQL and workspace behavior.
- UI agent owns new connection component/tests and its contract; bridge agent owns
  exact route forwarding/tests. Root owns navigation, source handoff and validation.
- Supported slice: list, injected enrollment, explicit verified binding, known-attempt
  inspect/reconcile and confirmed account disconnect. Unknown provider effects never
  invite blind re-execution. Tokens remain transient memory only.

## Current evidence

- `make check test build`: PASS, including Go race tests and unchanged migration checksums.
- `make web-test`: 221 tests PASS; generated API check and TypeScript PASS.
- `make web-browser`: 13 existing journeys PASS; production Next build PASS.
- Actionlint PASS. `make connection-browser-test` PASS against the integrated
  implementation: one exchange/fetch across replay, zero journals before approval,
  exact 0.10 posting, lost-response recovery, one journal/link/outbox and two source
  observations. `make app-integration` PASS for existing setup/posting recovery.
- Temporary alternate ports preserved the owner preview; committed defaults restored.

`TestConnectionsScopeAndRecovery` and related component cases cover stale scope,
revocation, single-flight handoff, cancellation, memory-only tokens and same-key
binding/disconnect recovery. The new `TestSyncReviewPostJourney` composes browser,
production Next bridge, Go enrollment/acquisition and actual PostgreSQL. Its explicit
fixture-owner review grant is separate from product connection binding. Backend-only
#106 evidence is not substituted for browser acceptance.

## Remaining work

Full #104 needs safe unfinished-attempt discovery after reload, public sync status
and timestamps, pause/manual wakeup APIs, qualified reconnect and hosted Link/secret
composition. Current workspace permissions do not advertise connect; server authority
remains decisive. No synthetic callback or UI state claims provider qualification.

## PR handoff

Refs #104; original acceptance remains open. No SQL migrations or hosted deployment.

## Review findings

Independent review confirmed the source preference is checked against current
`/sources` authority, and synthetic Link/acquisition are absent from production
composition. Mobile screenshot inspected at 390px: controls and long references
wrap within the viewport. First browser attempts corrected a label selector and
an expected presentation string: draft amounts are canonical exact `0.1`, while
trial-balance display pads USD to `0.10`; neither uses floating-point arithmetic.

The real browser proof exposed an initial source-discovery race: changing the filter
advanced the shared request generation before `/sources` completed, leaving no
source options. Discovery now holds the busy boundary until it finishes or hands
off to the selected-source read; selectors remain disabled while the source list
is unavailable and an empty selection cannot supersede discovery. `locks filters until connection source discovery
finishes` proves this regression; source authority remains checked before handoff.

## Mobile CI follow-up

PR #107's Linux frontend gate exposed horizontal overflow in book navigation.
Three `1fr` tracks inherited min-content widths from non-wrapping labels. A wider
monospace test font reproduces the same 390px overflow locally before the fix.
Mobile tracks now use `minmax(0, 1fr)` and labels wrap; no document clipping or
weakened overflow assertion. The existing workspace browser journey retains the
wide-font regression. Before fix: named browser case FAIL; after fix: all 13
browser journeys PASS and mobile screenshot inspected. Default Go checks/race tests/
build, generated API/types, 221 web unit tests and production web build PASS.
GitHub Linux validation must pass on the corrected head before merge.

# Accounting-core acceptance audit

<!-- stage-runbook: true -->

## Status and boundary

Decision: preserve the implemented synthetic posting core; fill specific evidence
gaps rather than rebuild it. Issues #1–4 and #17 remain open. This audit does not
approve real-LLC policy, broaden supported currencies, or accept hosted deployment.

Issue [#60](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/60),
parent [#54](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/54).
Reviewed main `0376b8793c882311f2d9cf0fbb2e99ecfc0bf540` on 2026-10-13.
Branch `issue/60-core-acceptance-audit`; sole changed path is this runbook.
[Lease #65](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/65)
and the claim on #60 own session status, not this document.

**Main gaps:** exact foreign-currency reversal assertions; explicit deletion
semantics; stale contract/tooling status; non-USD functional-book policy and the
full FX lifecycle; close/reconciliation/export contracts; official XSD provenance.
These are coverage or delivery gaps, not reproduced accounting defects.

## Follow-up evidence

The observations below remain the original audit of `0376b87`. Subsequent
`TestSpotReversalHistoricalProvenance` and `TestReversalOfReversalDenied` add
exact historical FX and second-order reversal assertions. The
[posting gate follow-up](posting-gate.md) records physical unused-principal
removal, historical-reference retention and disabled-principal denial separately.
It does not define an erasure lifecycle or close #4; consult that runbook for
current execution evidence and the remaining acceptance decision.

## Stage ledger

| Stage | Evidence / result | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claim | #60 open, no native blockers or competing claims; no open PRs at claim | Isolated worktree from main |
| Review | All 24 original criteria across #1–4/#17 mapped below; inspected actual assertions and SQL | Review bounded follow-ups |
| Validation | Default checks and all three isolated database suites passed | Review documentation PR |

## Current evidence

**Evidence vocabulary:** PROVEN means this audit ran the relevant synthetic test;
RECORDED means a prior runbook reports an observation, not rerun here; PARTIAL
means only a bounded subset is supported; OPEN means required evidence is absent
from the reviewed scope. Documented policy is not an automated test result.

Merged delivery anchors verified through GitHub: #14 migration tooling, #16
contracts, #18 corpus, #20 posting (`76f64c3`), #21 identity/setup, #30 restricted
migrator, #48 exact permission denials and #49 read-only migration status. Earlier
runbooks describe their historical slice; their “not implemented yet” wording
must not override later source or evidence.

Inspected executable evidence: [ledger integration tests](../../internal/ledger/integration_test.go),
[restricted migration tests](../../internal/migration/integration_test.go),
[corpus tests](../../cmd/corpus/main_test.go),
[generator rejection](../../cmd/corpus/generator_test.go),
[posting SQL](../../db/migrations/000002_posting.up.sql),
[Seed workflow](../../.github/workflows/seed.yml) and
[image workflow](../../.github/workflows/build-images.yml).

Observed on 2026-10-13 with Go 1.26.9 and the scripts' pinned synthetic images:

```sh
PATH=/private/tmp/jayburd-toolchain-1.26.9/go/bin:$PATH \
GOCACHE=/private/tmp/jayburd-go-cache \
GOMODCACHE=/private/tmp/jayburd-go-modcache make check test build

PATH=/private/tmp/jayburd-toolchain-1.26.9/go/bin:$PATH \
GOCACHE=/private/tmp/jayburd-go-cache \
GOMODCACHE=/private/tmp/jayburd-go-modcache make migration-test ledger-test cloud-sql-test
```

PASS: default vet/race/build/context/integrity checks; fresh/replay and expected
dirty-migration rejection; ledger integration, forward-upgrade sentinel and
restored receipt replay; runtime readiness denials; restricted migration,
read-only status, contention and dirty-failure tests. Initial Docker credential
helper failure inside the sandbox was resolved by an approved outside-sandbox
rerun; no credential values were inspected. Expected division-by-zero/dirty
errors are fault-test outcomes, not a recommendation to force a migration.

### Criterion map

Numbers within each issue follow its original acceptance list, not later planning
paragraphs. Links below identify inspected sources; test names refer to their
actual assertions, not a promise of complete coverage.

| Issue / criterion | Evidence and disposition |
| --- | --- |
| #1.1 Workflow, currency, basis, timezone, opening source | PARTIAL: [ADR 0005](../decisions/0005-development-accounting-policy.md) selects fictional accrual/USD/UTC and capital opening. Real entity, complete opening balances and owner/accountant approval remain OPEN. |
| #1.2 Fictional transaction scenarios | [AC-01–10](../contracts/accounting-scenarios.md) cover every listed scenario. `TestCorpusFixtures` checks fixed expectations; `TestGoldenMonth` posts the first book through SQL. This does not implement statement deduplication or reconciliation. |
| #1.3 Chart, precision, permissions, exports, cutover | PARTIAL: ADR 0005 and [posting boundary](../contracts/posting-boundary.md) specify the synthetic chart, exact amounts and permissions. Report/export contracts #51 and accountant/cutover review #10/#13 remain OPEN. |
| #1.4 Unsupported cases and decision owners | Documented: scenario policy register identifies owner/accountant/schema decisions and excluded automation. Full FX and tax treatment are not selected by an agent. |
| #2.1 Ownership, principals, journals, source references, opening, reversals, periods | PARTIAL: [SQL dictionary](../contracts/ledger-sql.md) and migrations define the first slice; `TestControlledSetup`, `TestSecondBookIsolation`, `TestJournalCorrectionHistory` exercise parts. Source-observation/import links and close evidence remain future contracts; rate provenance is not statement provenance. |
| #2.2 Restricted writes, composite keys, finite exact money | `TestSchemaPrivileges`, `TestSecondBookIsolation`, `TestMoneyInputBounds`, `TestManualSpotPosting`, `TestCurrencyScalesAndRounding`; restricted bootstrap also has exact SQLSTATE checks in `TestRestrictedMigration`. These are local roles, not actual API IAM login proof. |
| #2.3 Close locking and replay conflicts | Posting contract plus `TestPostingCloseRace`, `TestPostingReplayConcurrency`, `TestReceiptActorAndArchive`. The closer is privileged fixture code; no production close endpoint/evidence workflow is established. |
| #2.4 Every invariant mapped; migration/restore approach | PARTIAL: posting matrix and tests below; `TestLedgerRestoreReplay` restores synthetic data with roles already present. Coverage qualifications below and actual restore/PITR #26 remain OPEN. |
| #3.1 Pinned stack and query-generation decision | PARTIAL: CI pins Go 1.26.9; scripts pin PostgreSQL 17.11 and migrate 4.20.1 image digests; go.mod pins pgx/v5 5.11.0. ADR 0003 still says application dependencies are absent and recommends sqlc; current service uses explicit pgx calls. Record the actual query-access decision before closure. |
| #3.2 Isolated local/CI PostgreSQL and cleanup | `make migration-test ledger-test cloud-sql-test`; inspected scripts use dedicated synthetic containers/networks and invocation-owned cleanup, not an inherited live DSN. No database port is published. |
| #3.3 Lock/checksum/fresh/replay/failure/compatibility | `TestArtifactIntegrity`, `TestRestrictedMigration`, `TestMigrationContention`, `TestMigrationDirtyFailure`, `TestMigrationStatus`, shell fresh/replay/failure checks, `TestSchemaCompatibility`, forward-upgrade sentinel. Current-schema checks do not establish arbitrary old/new application compatibility. |
| #3.4 Non-root health-only image | RECORDED: [GCP evidence](gcp-delivery.md) and `scripts/test-api-container.sh`; not rerun in this audit. Current server also has managed accounting mode. Review the historical health-only criterion against inert/default mode rather than removing working routes. |
| #3.5 Integration CI, dependency review, image scans, required checks | PARTIAL: `seed.yml` runs database suites, govulncheck and npm audit; `build-images.yml` scans candidate images. Required-check enforcement was unavailable in the recorded private-repo plan; [delivery workflow](../delivery.md) requires owner review. No fresh scan or branch-protection capability probe here. |
| #4.1 Atomic journal/audit/receipt/outbox | `TestPostingInvariants` injects failures after book/header/line/audit/receipt/outbox writes and at COMMIT; `TestGoldenMonth` checks committed counts and fixed balances. This proves outbox intent, not worker delivery. |
| #4.2 Invalid/scope/revoked/deleted/closed/money rejection | PARTIAL: `TestPostingInvariants`, `TestEntityReferencesAndPrivileges`, `TestSecondBookIsolation`, both revocation-order tests, `TestPostingCloseRace`, money/scale tests. Disabled/missing principals are tested; a distinct physical-deletion lifecycle is not established. Resolve what “deleted” means before marking the entire criterion complete. |
| #4.3 Replay/conflicts/concurrency | `TestPostingReplayConcurrency`, `TestReceiptActorAndArchive`, `TestCommitAcknowledgementLoss`, `TestHTTPPostCommitBoundary` prove one effect, actor/payload conflict, historical replay and uncertain-COMMIT recovery. |
| #4.4 Immutable history and exact correction provenance | PARTIAL: `TestJournalCorrectionHistory` rejects mutation and repeat reversal and checks net trial balance; `TestReceiptActorAndArchive` rejects reversal into an archived account. No dedicated assertion compares every foreign original/reversal line and historical rate/policy identity; add that proof. Source-document provenance belongs to future import contracts. |
| #4.5 Write-stage failures and close races | `TestPostingInvariants` and `TestPostingCloseRace` execute against PostgreSQL with observed lock barriers. This is transaction ordering, not full month-close acceptance. |
| #17.1 Source versions/hashes/rights/review depth | RECORDED in [testing source register](../research/testing-sources.md); official schema provenance is explicitly incomplete, not silently promoted. |
| #17.2 Independent month/FX exact fixtures | `TestCorpusFixtures`, `TestCorpusRejectsMutations`, `TestFXExposureMutation`, `TestDecodeBoundary` check independent fixture expectations. FX lifecycle fixture arithmetic is not SQL lifecycle implementation. |
| #17.3 Beancount/hledger comparison | RECORDED: five functional projections and deliberately wrong balances tested in [corpus runbook](synthetic-corpus.md); `TestFunctionalExports` only checks emitted fixture assertions locally. External engines not rerun here. |
| #17.4 Official camt.053 schema and negatives | OPEN: prior official download failed; pinned mirror checks are RECORDED only. Obtain authoritative artifact/version/profile evidence, then rerun schema and semantic cases. |
| #17.5 Bounded generator evaluation | RECORDED: 15/115 journals rejected for cent residuals. `TestGeneratorAudit` independently rejects a one-cent difference, cross-journal netting and malformed amounts. Do not “fix” the oracle to match generated output. |
| #17.6 Offline defaults and optional checks | Inspected [corpus guide](../../tests/corpus/README.md), Makefile and scripts: external accounting engines/generator/XSD acquisition are explicit optional steps. Stale corpus-only “no database in default CI” wording does not describe today's full Seed workflow. |

### Assertion-level qualifications

1. **Multicurrency scope:** `ledger.mutate` currently accepts the selected
   accrual/USD/UTC/scale-2 profile and rejects other functional-book policies.
   JPY/EUR/KWD transaction-unit conversions are tested. Arbitrary functional
   currencies, position settlement/remeasurement and consolidation are not thereby
   implemented. See [multicurrency contract](../contracts/multicurrency.md) and #59.
2. **Reversal evidence:** migration 000002 constructs reversed lines from stored
   amounts, currency-version IDs and rate IDs. That is inspected implementation,
   not proof all those fields survive correctly: existing correction tests use
   identity-valued examples and aggregate assertions. Add exact field comparisons,
   later-period reversal with a different eligible rate, and reversal-of-reversal
   denial. Do not edit immutable migration history to add tests.
3. **Named matrix drift:** `TestMoneyInputBounds` does not alone exercise every
   case assigned to it in the posting matrix; spot-rate tests and scale tests
   supply other cases. `TestGoldenMonth` checks the first fixture book;
   `TestSecondBookIsolation` separately checks isolation. Avoid attributing a
   full product workflow to either name.
4. **Denial quality:** older `TestSchemaPrivileges` and immutability probes accept
   any SQL error. #48's `TestRestrictedMigration` checks 42501, but only for its
   enumerated subset. Harden remaining probes to expected errors and independent
   unchanged-state assertions; a failed query alone is weaker evidence.

### Source-review boundary

This is repository evidence review, not a new accounting policy or standards
interpretation. Read the [bibliography](../research/bibliography.md),
[decision evidence rules](../research/decision-evidence.md), ADR 0005,
[standards contract](../contracts/standards.md), and their recorded review limits.
No external normative text or external accounting engine was newly reviewed/run.
ASC 830 review, real policy approval and full ISO mappings remain unresolved
where their source registers say so. Do not label the system GAAP/ISO compliant.

## Remaining work

| Priority / owner | Bounded next delivery and acceptance |
| --- | --- |
| Next / ACCT, #4 | Add proposed `TestSpotReversalHistoricalProvenance` and `TestReversalOfReversalDenied`; compare original/reversal values, sides, reference IDs, links and original unchanged state. Extend denied-mutation checks with exact SQLSTATE and unchanged-state evidence. Run `make ledger-test`; no schema change expected. |
| Next / ACCT, #3/#2 | Review ADR 0003 query-access choice against explicit pgx implementation; reconcile historical “no schema/runtime” statements in database/corpus docs. Map current evidence accurately without rewriting historical stage results or inventing sqlc adoption. Shared-doc reservation required. |
| Next / ACCESS, #62 | Resolve disabled/absent/deleted-principal semantics against retention and provider revocation boundaries, then specify the missing named tests. No deletion or IAM expansion during review. |
| Policy / #1, #2, #59 | Owner/accountant resolves real functional currencies, basis, timezone, rates and openings; contract and independently worked non-USD/FX cases precede broader implementation. Keep this required scope visible. |
| Product / #51, #61, #10 | Report, source-import and close/reconciliation contracts and independent expected results. Trial-balance success does not replace these workflows. |
| Reference / #17 | Authoritative XSD acquisition/provenance and profile/semantic evidence; preserve generator rejection cases. |
| Cloud / #26, #27, #12 | Actual workload migration verification/replay, API role denials, restore/load and hosted synthetic proof remain their existing gates. Local reruns do not satisfy them. |

Prefer these scoped follow-ups over rebuilding the ledger or closing all old
issues because a suite passes. Only #60's audit deliverable is proposed for review;
the parent criteria and policy decisions retain their owners.

## PR handoff

Documentation-only change in the leased path. No SQL/API/runtime changes, no cloud
execution, no financial data or credentials. Review the criterion map and proposed
test gaps against the linked source before assigning implementation. Required
checks and synthetic database suites passed as recorded above. Hosted PR checks
remain separate evidence; this audit does not close #1–4/#17.

<!-- stage-runbook: true -->
# Hosted database verification

## Status and boundary

Forward migration execution passed after #128. The current candidate selects
`operation=verify` with the same immutable build38654097056 images to establish
clean version15 and exact registered migration hashes. Verification has not run.
It updates the existing job action to status; no SQL mutation or API/frontend
rollout. Contracts: [read-only status](../contracts/migration-status.md) and
[migration-only release](../contracts/migration-release.md).

## Stage ledger

- Baseline verification38663999729, execution jayburd-dev-migrate-sp7xd, passed
  at clean version5 with exact hashes using build38327676280.
- Owner restored Cloud Shell authorization. Merged role bootstrap, replay and
  catalog-only privilege readback passed through the retained operator. All seven
  capability roles are safe NOLOGIN roles; API has no DDL or privileged/worker
  membership; migrator has explicit owner SET without inheritance, ADMIN or
  CREATEROLE. Connection limits remain20/2. Pinned proxy2.26.0 stopped on exit.
- Bootstrap SHA256:
  `c19921224c635ad7105f5a46d1a6d6e66012a0699a1d3f3077280ea273cf15dd`.
- Forward run38743082827, execution jayburd-dev-migrate-g4pj4, completed successfully
  at 2026-10-15T13:31:59.567105Z. Retained receipt and independently validated
  allowlisted metadata match the exact image, identity, up arguments, one task,
  zero retries and 660-second timeout. This proves execution, not status or replay.
- Prepared verification candidate retaining build38654097056 attempt1 at
  `5c10e944678e15caf5f832fc87b5c95aa6f86456`, all three image digests, and bootstrap
  evidence. Updated only operation, compatibility evidence and expiry.

## Current evidence

Prior local `make migration-test` and `make cloud-sql-test check test build` passed,

<!-- stage-runbook: true -->
# Hosted API database permission proof

## Status and boundary

Implements the bounded runner for #130, child of #26. No hosted execution or
migration replay is claimed. The API image contains a separate explicit probe;
the normal API command and health default are unchanged. No source SQL changes,
new grants, public endpoint, business-data reads or credentials are involved.

## Decision and evidence

Follow the existing [Cloud SQL contract](../contracts/cloud-sql.md), particularly
exact SQLSTATE denial and metadata-only authentication. Its linked
[GCP source register](../research/gcp-sources.md) and
[database source register](../research/database-sources.md) remain authoritative:
PostgreSQL transaction rollback provides cleanup; IAM login proves the real
runtime identity. Reusing an operator's SET ROLE would only simulate that identity.
This operational probe is not an ISO financial message; no accounting contract changes.

`databaseprobe.Run` checks exact session/current user and safe role capabilities,
then requires 42501 for DDL, zero-row direct-table reads and forbidden owner/worker
roles. Workspace unknown-principal rejection must be P2101 at repeatable-read.
Each statement has its own transaction, always rolled back, including unexpected
success. Read-only mode is deliberately not substituted: 25006 is not an ACL proof.
The reserved synthetic unknown-principal UUID must not be enrolled in hosted data.

## Operator procedure

After review/merge and a successful Build images run containing this binary,
validate its API build receipt and immutable digest against that exact commit.
Record run, commit and digest in #130 before execution. Do not reuse the pre-probe
API image. The commands below use that reviewed public digest as `probe_image`.

Initialize `infra/gcp/database-probe` with the existing approved GCS backend bucket
and independent prefix `database-probe` (see its README). Using the existing
authorized deployer/operator, apply only this root with `project_id` set to
`jayburd-bookkeeping-dev` and `image` set to that digest. Keep state, plan and
provider output private. No environment or secrets are mounted. This operation
does not require closing #26 and cannot grant itself additional permissions.

Execute once, record the returned execution name as `probe_execution`, and read
only the allowlisted metadata:

```sh
gcloud run jobs execute jayburd-dev-database-probe --project=jayburd-bookkeeping-dev --region=us-central1 --format='value(metadata.name)'
gcloud run jobs executions describe "$probe_execution" --project=jayburd-bookkeeping-dev --region=us-central1 --format='json(metadata.name,spec.taskCount,spec.template.spec.containers[].image,spec.template.spec.containers[].command,spec.template.spec.containers[].args,spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName,spec.template.spec.maxRetries,spec.template.spec.timeoutSeconds,status.conditions[].type,status.conditions[].status,status.succeededCount,status.failedCount,status.cancelledCount,status.runningCount,status.retriedCount,status.completionTime)' > /tmp/jayburd-api-probe-metadata.json
node scripts/database-probe-receipt.mjs "$probe_image" /tmp/jayburd-api-probe-metadata.json /tmp/jayburd-api-probe-receipt.json "$probe_execution"
```

Poll selected metadata until terminal; do not treat acceptance of the execution
request as success. Retain only the validated receipt. On failure stop; do not
inspect raw logs, widen permissions or substitute another identity. No automatic
retry or destructive cleanup is configured. A successful receipt proves the
actual API IAM SQL boundary, not end-user enrollment or restore/load acceptance.

Replay remains a separate reviewed `operation=migrate` release with the same v15
image, followed by `operation=verify`; retain both receipts. Keep #26 open.

## Current evidence

PASS: `TestProbeOutcomes`, `TestConnectionFailure`,
`TestOfflineAndRejectedArguments`, `TestRestrictedMigration` through
`make cloud-sql-test`, and `make check test build release-test`.
All three mocked Terraform tests passed, including `bounded_api_permission_probe`.
`scripts/test-api-container.sh --local-build` passed offline probe/default rejection
and normal API health behavior. This proves the runtime image only; canonical
source-builder verification remains CI evidence, not a local claim.

## Stage ledger

- Issue #130 published before implementation. Added rollback-only probe and mock
  receipt/Terraform tests. Disposable PostgreSQL exact-probe acceptance passed.
- Initial documentation validation identified missing required runbook headings;
  added them before rerunning repository checks.
- Root review added identity-operator and Cloud SQL superuser membership denial.
  Full checks and exact disposable probe passed afterward. Sandbox blocked initial
  localhost/Docker/provider access; approved reruns passed without source changes.

- Integrated main after PRs #134/#135 merged; resolved the Makefile conflict by
  retaining both Sandbox release-policy and database-probe receipt test suites.
  `make check test build release-test` passed again on the merged branch.

## Remaining work

Review and build immutable API image, then run the separate
hosted proof and migration replay/status releases. No hosted PASS is inferred.

## PR handoff

No cloud resources changed in this branch. Hosted acceptance remains outstanding.
Record exact tested outcomes here before handoff; never close #130 based on local tests.

Issue #52 stays open. Files are confined to design, prototype, source notes and
this runbook. Root coordinator links the source record and merges independent
agent work. Lease is ready for REVIEW after passing required checks and commit.

### Reproduce FW-DOM

After installing the locked web dependencies, run from the repository root:

```sh
node <<'NODE'
const fs = require('node:fs');
const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
const { JSDOM } = require('./web/node_modules/jsdom');
const html = fs.readFileSync('docs/prototypes/financial-workspace.html', 'utf8');
const dom = new JSDOM(html, { runScripts: 'dangerously' });
const d = dom.window.document;
// Use only the trusted checked-in synthetic HTML; never execute supplied documents.
function click(selector) { assert(d.querySelector(selector)); d.querySelector(selector).click(); }
// Model selector changes without claiming native keyboard or browser coverage.
function select(id, value) { d.getElementById(id).value = value; d.getElementById(id).dispatchEvent(new dom.window.Event('change')); }
// Inspect the current financial surface, excluding embedded fixture source.
function surface() { return d.getElementById('surface').textContent; }
assert.deepEqual(JSON.parse(d.getElementById('fixture').textContent), JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('tests/corpus/golden-month.json')).books);
assert(surface().includes('1,145.00'));
click('[data-view="Reports"]'); assert(surface().includes('130.00'));
select('currency', 'original'); click('[data-account="Assets:Checking"]');
click('[data-journal="AC-02"]'); assert(surface().includes('200.00'));
assert.equal(d.activeElement.id, 'heading');
click('[data-back="journals"]'); click('[data-back="report"]');
assert.equal(d.getElementById('currency').value, 'original');
assert.equal(d.getElementById('period').value, '2026-01');
click('[data-account="Assets:Checking"]'); click('[data-journal="AC-02"]');
select('entity', 'b-usd'); assert(!surface().includes('AC-02')); assert(!surface().includes('1,145.00'));
select('entity', 'all'); assert(surface().includes('not a consolidated')); assert.equal(d.querySelectorAll('[data-book]').length, 2);
click('[data-book="a-usd"]'); select('period', '2026-02'); assert(surface().includes('not a verified zero'));
select('period', '2026-01');
for (const state of ['loading', 'error', 'denied', 'stale']) { select('state', state); assert(!surface().includes('1,145.00')); assert(!surface().includes('AC-02')); }
click('[data-retry]'); assert(surface().includes('1,145.00'));
click('[data-view="Review inbox"]'); assert(surface().includes('not pending ledger commands'));
click('[data-view="Reconciliation"]'); assert(surface().includes('planned'));
assert(!/fetch\(|localStorage|sessionStorage|XMLHttpRequest/.test(html));
console.log('PASS FW-DOM');
NODE
```

replace only the module path if reusing that cache. Browser validation remains
