- PASS: `make check test build`, browser type checks/33 unit tests/production build and three Chromium journeys; actionlint; canonical standalone frontend container with static asset and unavailable-route checks. API/migrator host-build runtime checks pass; their canonical builders remain hosted CI gates.
- Fixed the merged #30 CI readiness race: socket readiness saw PostgreSQL’s temporary initialization server. Cloud SQL and ledger proofs now wait for TCP, matching the migration harness. `make cloud-sql-test migration-test ledger-test` passes after the fix.
- The first frontend proof caught a self-proxy loop (default API port matched frontend port); the unconfigured image now targets unused loopback port 1. Node SIGTERM exit 143 is accepted; forced-kill exit 137 remains failure.
- No workflow dispatched, identity enabled, registry push or cloud mutation. Trivy publication scans and real federation remain unexecuted until explicit owner setup/dispatch.
- PR #31 merged at `cda91ff`; its hosted foundation/frontend/validate checks all passed, including canonical Go images and the PostgreSQL readiness fix. The receipt compatibility fix follows in a separate PR. A local Trivy 0.75.0 image scan could not download its vulnerability database because the Docker VM lacked the outbound proxy CA; no scan result is claimed and TLS verification remains enabled.
- Local Buildx metadata proof exposed a Docker store difference: containerd reports the manifest/index ID and omits the configuration digest. Receipt validation now accepts either recorded content ID, rejects unrelated IDs, and never labels an index as a configuration digest. Named receipt tests cover both stores.
- Next: private service-token bridge/runtime browser configuration, then Terraform rollout. Current frontend is deliberately unconfigured; all receipts are candidate-only.

## Stage ledger

| Stage | Evidence / outcome | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reconcile existing work | Reviewed #5/#7/#11/#12 and open PRs #23/#24; preserved existing evidence and identity | Use native dependencies before claiming a slice |
| Publish bounded work | Created epic #25, database #26 and app #27; updated existing issues with named acceptance and recovery requirements | Native relationships verified |
| Record architecture | Updated GCP contract, index and annotated sources; scoped early proof separately from full month-close | Review documentation PR |
| Implement foundation | Two state buckets, nine identities, image repository, disabled build WIF and budget alerts; no runtime resources | Review IAM and owner bootstrap |
| Mocked provider proof | Terraform validate and six tests pass; invalid project/number/billing/region denied | Review PR and hosted CI |
| Cloud SQL configuration | Three new mocked tests pass for PostgreSQL settings, transport, recovery and inputs | Live provider verification remains open |
| Restricted migration | Non-superuser administrator/bootstrap and restricted migrator/replay pass; API DDL/table denial, durable checksum drift, contention and dirty failure pass | Review PR; execute named cloud gates after owner setup |

## Current evidence

Current bootstrap results are recorded above; the following items preserve prior
planning evidence. Local `make check test build` also passed for this documentation update.

- PASS: issue creation/edit commands returned expected URLs; native sub-issue and dependency mutations succeeded.
- PASS: GitHub API read-back confirmed epic children 5/7/11/12/26/27; #26 blocked by #5; #27 blocked by #5/#6/#11/#26; #12 blocked by #5/#6/#7/#11/#26/#27. #13 retains #10/#12.
- PASS: `PATH=/private/tmp/jayburd-toolchain-1.26.9/go/bin:$PATH GOCACHE=/private/tmp/jayburd-go-cache make check test build` (Go vet/race tests, documentation links, migration-file checks and binaries). Initial sandbox cache-write denial resolved by an approved rerun; no cloud credentials used.
- PASS: `git diff --check` and `bash scripts/check-stage-runbook.sh --staged`.
- PASS: native dependency read-back via `gh api repos/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/12/dependencies/blocked_by --jq '.[].number'`; equivalent checks covered #26/#27/#13 and epic #25 sub-issues.
- Source review: [GCP register](../research/gcp-sources.md), selected sections only.

## Remaining work

No GitHub token exchange or image publication has been executed.

Next: Terraform runtime settings/Invoker grants and serialized migration/rollout.
Runtime browser configuration and private service-token forwarding are implemented
with synthetic evidence on this branch. Identity and Infisical acceptance remain
open. PRs #23/#24 were open at the last feature review; recheck before final cloud
acceptance. Final #12 proof still requires recovery, 1,000 postings and measured
spend. Default CI remains credential-free. No live-bookkeeping approval follows
from foundation provisioning.

## PR handoff

Review Terraform runtime/migration roots, deployment trust/state isolation and the
owner-dispatch manifest workflow. #27 stays open: this is implementation evidence,
not deployment or real identity acceptance. No SQL migration or accounting/API
contract changes. No provisioning or workflow dispatch performed. Hosted checks
pending PR creation; see current slice above for local evidence.

## Foundation evidence — prior slice

- PASS: Terraform 1.15.7 `validate` and `test -filter=tests/foundation.tftest.hcl`, six mocked runs; Google provider 8.6.0 schema validation caught and resolved an unsupported budget notification block before handoff.
- PASS: provider lock records signed darwin_arm64/linux_amd64 packages.

- PARTIAL: `gcp-identity-boundary` proves configured trust and grants offline; live token allow/deny tests remain unexecuted. `gcp-cost-review` has an allocation envelope, not a verified regional quote. `gcp-promotion-review` confirms no branch protection/environments; build/app promotion implementation belongs to #27.

## Cloud SQL evidence — prior slice

- PASS: `make cloud-sql-test` uses an internal Docker network, non-superuser administrator with ADMIN on test login roles, unchanged product migrations and a runtime with no table/DDL authority. `TestRestrictedMigration`, `TestMigrationContention`, `TestMigrationDirtyFailure` and checksum cases pass.

# Optional hosted Sandbox connections

## Status and boundary

Coordinator approved managed API composition, same verified API pool, explicit Link
events acknowledgement, canonical numeric secret versions and absolute local consent
expiry at most30days. Owned cmd/api/main.go, internal/connectionruntime and these
contract/runbook documents. No frontend, SQL, shared server, IAM or deployment edit.

## Stage ledger

Reviewed actual server.Dependencies/Managed, ledger.Service.DB, connection Service,
providersecrets reader/registry/writer and managed metadata interfaces before code.
Identified Infisical identity UUID audience mismatch; worker author corrected its
metadata adapter using reviewed official source. Numeric GCP project response names
are pinned explicitly; no project ID alias inference. Implemented complete opt-in
validation and cleanup, static credential reads, HTTPProvider and SecretStore/service
composition. Disabled startup is inert. Fixed errors suppress underlying diagnostics.

## Current evidence

Focused connectionruntime race tests and API command build PASS. Tests prove disabled
and invalid settings never touch dependencies; enabled startup reads exactly two
numeric versions with CRC32C and no DB transaction, Infisical identity login, writer
mutation or Plaid request. Failure tests cover canceled startup, wrong version,
transport diagnostics and invalid secret payload. `make check test build` PASS
after recopying the worker author's corrected dependency; no borrowed changes staged.
Dependencies providersecrets/workerruntime and clouddb changes were copied locally
for compilation and remain outside this commit; coordinator owns their integration.

## Operator configuration

Keep optional settings absent until the full hosted/secret/Link readiness review.
The [contract](../contracts/hosted-connections.md) lists exact identifier flags.
The local consent expiry is a fixed RFC3339 instant, never a rolling thirty-day
extension. This is an owner policy ceiling, not provider-reported consent lifetime.
Provider manifest applies the earlier actual expiry where present. Static credentials
must already exist at their exact numeric Google versions; no startup alias lookup,
Infisical fallback, rotation, Link creation or credential publication occurs.

Cold restart after that absolute expiry intentionally fails; obtain explicit new
local consent approval instead of a rolling extension. The registry bucket/prefix
and two static containers are fixed to the Terraform namespace in the contract;
foreign or swapped containers fail before I/O.

The API command shares its existing restricted pool and closes the injected direct
HTTP transport with normal server cleanup. Metadata supplies managed tokens. Runtime
writer permissions and the one-way Infisical propagation into the eight precreated
slots require separate deployed qualification. Existing API12s request budget stays;
uncertain work must use the existing durable reconciliation routes.

## Remaining work

Frontend real Link remains unavailable and Link-events acknowledgement is an operator
assertion, not proof. Verify actual Plaid enablement or implement/review Hosted Link,
then perform full Sandbox qualification. Hosted identity, static secret delivery,
Infisical token TTL, writer access and asynchronous propagation are not exercised by
these synthetic tests. DB readiness is not provider or propagation readiness.

## PR handoff

No migration or financial contract changes. Integrate after providersecrets and
workerruntime, including UUID audience support. Add canonical project number and the
explicit identifier flags through the coordinator's reviewed deployment workflow;
do not enable from defaults. Primary source selection is recorded in the contract.

## Optional runtime metadata stage

Added null-default `connections` metadata to the runtime Terraform module without
changing release manifests/workflows. Exact static resource names, UUIDs, approved
origins and explicit Link qualification are validated; derived flags use only the
fixed dev environment/registry namespace. Plan-time expiry must be future within
30 days; runtime repeats the check. Mocked cases cover disabled and complete enabled
arguments, unqualified Link, foreign/alias versions, zero identity, expired and
unbounded consent. No cloud apply, provider traffic or secret retrieval occurred.

Final metadata evidence: clean temporary module copy, pinned Google8.6.0 filesystem
mirror and empty environment; `terraform test` PASS10 cases, 0 failed. No backend,
state or owner variable files copied. Initial full infrastructure script stopped on
registry DNS after foundation8 passed; the owned runtime module was then tested
successfully with the cached provider. Terraform fmt and git diff checks PASS.
Logs: `/private/tmp/jayburd-connection-runtime-proof.log` and
`/private/tmp/jayburd-hosted-connections-default.log`.

## Numeric validation follow-up

Aligned Terraform project numbers with canonical positive signed-int64 identifiers
and bounded both static secret versions to int64 maximum. Added independent overflow,
zero, leading-zero and exact-maximum test cases. README now explicitly warns that
current promotion omits the object and therefore resets an owner opt-in to disabled.
Reviewed integrated cmd/api composition read-only: startup failures close allocated
transport/pool, server construction failure closes dependencies, and Server.Run closes
its dependency wrapper after shutdown/listen failure. No bypass or cleanup blocker
identified; no additional production changes made.
Follow-up validation: clean-temp mocked runtime Terraform suite PASS16/0, including
both int64 overflows and exact maximum acceptance. Terraform fmt and diff checks PASS.
Go sources unchanged since the passing default gates above.

# Canonical KMS repair handoff — #326

## Status and boundary

Sole SQL writer `SQL326-HANDOFF-KMS`, branch `fix/326-owned-handoff-kms`,
base `fb414a4` (32/323 and signed receiver324 merged). Forward33; merged1–32
remain unchanged. Child/prerequisite326 of319; service work is held in its
dedicated worktree. No managed apply, deploy, provider/KMS call or live account.

## Stage ledger

| Stage | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Resume | Current65/319/326 and main32 rechecked; sole-writer33 reservation; bibliography/database foundations/decision/standards and original20/32 reviewed |
| Failure evidence | Concrete319 actual SQL/production AEAD/SDK fixture fails at Begin handoff:32 rejects canonical project-ID wrapping resource; do not replace it with an easier numeric fixture |
| Design | Restore exactly20 grammar in32 reconnect function; preserve every other gate/ACL/winner; down refuses incompatible retained history |
| Implementation | One forward function replacement and guarded disposable down; no schema/data/AAD/key rewrite or privilege change |
| SQL proof | All connection-ops cases PASS, including four new canonical/profile/upgrade/rollback cases and prior32 authority/race/expiry cases |
| Required gates | `make check test build migration-test ledger-test connection-service-test webhook-test webhook-bootstrap-test` PASS on disposable synthetic databases |
| Composite diagnostic | Held319 concrete signed SQL/AEAD/SDK service fixture PASS with the exact sealed33 pair/checksum; no Go edits or managed action during this proof |

## Current evidence

Authoritative original selected source: bank-token-vault canonical-project
review2026-10-19 (#194), official Cloud KMS resource hierarchy/encrypt-decrypt
resource-name sections/examples. Those support the canonical mechanism, not
authorization to deploy or successful hosted key use. Current20 accepts numeric
nonzero project numbers or6–30character lowercase project IDs with the fixed
location/keyring/key and positive numeric version.32 accidentally copied19.
33 applies exactly20's grammar, not arbitrary KMS URLs or a fallback key policy.
Full crypto key/AAD equality still belongs to the existing Go/KMS adapter.

Alternative numeric-only synthetic key was rejected: it would hide a real runtime
compatibility failure. Editing merged32 was rejected: delivered SQL is immutable.
Widening runtime key matching or rewriting ciphertext was rejected: neither is
needed. Apply a forward correction before matching repair runtime qualification.
This is an operational nonfinancial credential-storage profile under the existing
STD-01 assessment; financial messages, ISO identifiers/currency and accounting
rules are unchanged. No ISO or cryptographic certification claim.

Named independent SQL expectations:

- `TestHostedRepairSQLCanonicalHandoff`: canonical and numeric accepted through
  actual API login; replay/different encrypted candidate returns the same winner;
  foreign actor and dedicated receiver denied; no claim/wakeup/journal effects.
- `TestHostedRepairSQLHandoffProfile`: independently fixed invalid project length/
  case/leading-zero number, location/key/version/path and malformed/extra envelope
  fields reject without a retained handoff.
- `TestHostedRepairSQLHandoffMigration`: disposable33 down→32 rejects canonical;
 33 up accepts; down with canonical repair history fails55000 before function or
  ciphertext changes, and the same bytes remain readable/replayable.
- `TestHostedRepairSQLHandoffNewMode`: canonical new enrollment keeps20 fallback
  support across33 down/up, without confusing nonrepair history with the guard.

Fixtures cover SQL syntax/authority, not real cryptography. The held319 suite uses
production AEAD and a fictional in-memory wrapping key with the real canonical
resource profile, signed HTTP and concrete SDK transport; it must pass after33
before service acceptance. Existing32 proof/claim/scope/race/expiry cases remain.

Executed composite diagnostic: publication, lost claim/manifest/confirmation
replies, pending/exit/ambiguous/current revoked/expired/reduced account/currency/
type scope and paused-stream cases pass with33 using the production encrypted
handoff/store and pinned concrete SDK with injected synthetic transport. The same
held Go source failed before33 and passed after only the sealed migration inputs
changed. This supporting evidence does not publish/accept the unfinished319
service branch or qualify actual provider/managed behavior.

Source comparison also confirms33 up's function body differs from32 only by the
reviewed20 resource grammar; down restores32's body exactly (whitespace-normalized
comparison of CREATE function definitions). SHA256 manifest adds only the33 pair;
existing1–32 hashes and SQL remain unchanged. Local cached Go1.26.5 override and
pinned synthetic PG17/migrate images; tracked Go1.26.10/dependencies unchanged.

## Remaining work

Finish required synthetic gates and exact-head CI. Then rebase/resume319 under a
fresh Go path lease, use33 and prove the actual canonical service path. Runtime
capability is a separate explicit opt-in, with existing configuration disabled.
Human security review, schema/binary/bootstrap compatibility and exact finite
owner release approval are required before managed activation. No hosted gate,
real account or reconciliation is cleared here.

Down is for a quiesced disposable fixture, not live recovery or a claim of safe
concurrent function downgrade. It fails on retained canonical repair envelopes,
including abandoned attempts; never delete them to force a down migration.
No service/operator may use this guard as permission to enumerate real ciphertext.
Forward33 must follow32; prior expired31-only Sandbox manifest cannot apply it.

## PR handoff

Fixes326 only after all acceptance evidence passes;319/275/88/90 remain open.
Migration impact: additive forward function correction, no DDL/data rewrite.
CREATE OR REPLACE retains owner/SECURITY DEFINER/fixed search_path and current

documents.body:
<!-- stage-runbook: true -->
# Hosted Link enrollment delivery

## Status and boundary

Implementation and synthetic validation complete for #125. Synthetic validation only; no deployment,
credential retrieval or live-bank connection. Contract: ../contracts/hosted-link-enrollment.md.

## Issue #187 recovery delivery (2026-10-18)

The new migration 19 retains each Hosted Link token as immutable AEAD ciphertext
wrapped by the existing bank-credentials KMS key, bound to authenticated actor,
entity, book and attempt. The public attempt and discovery responses still omit
tokens and ciphertext. `POST /connection-attempts/{attempt}/complete` rechecks
current SQL authority, decrypts the original token server-side, checks the hash,
and queries Plaid's completed session result before using the existing one-shot
exchange claim. The UI offers completion from a discovered `link_ready` attempt
after remount. Same-tab checks use the same route. The Next bridge and OpenAPI
allowlists include only this new empty-body operation.

Synthetic evidence: migration 19 fresh install/replay passes. Unit tests prove
per-actor/attempt envelope separation, pending completion without claim, reload
completion, one exchange, and public route behavior. The full synthetic
Connections browser/API/PostgreSQL proof passes with a remount between the
pending and completed checks, then covers account binding, acquisition and
explicit posting. `make app-integration` also passes. These tests use a fake
Plaid provider and synthetic KMS wrapper; deployed Sandbox acceptance remains.
CI's restricted Cloud SQL migration-status proof was updated to expect migration
19 as current, with 18 and 20 as invalid metadata; the old hard-coded current
version made CI reject the new migration even though the product migration passed.
The ledger schema-compatibility fixture likewise expects the current version 19;
its posting and accounting invariants remain unchanged.

The completed-session recovery window follows Plaid's six-hour result window.
The Hosted URL still expires at Plaid's reported time. A finished exit or lost
provider result does not yet have an immediate safe **Start over** path;
`link_ready` abandonment requires a separate provider-absence and concurrency
contract. Immutable ciphertext retention needs a reviewed cleanup policy.
Verified webhook delivery is still tracked under #103/#87. This change does not
deploy, connect a live bank, or activate a worker.

## Stage ledger

- Reviewed official Link creation/session/completion documentation and current service/SQL boundaries.
- Selected explicit Sandbox Hosted Link completion; retained one-shot exchange and review boundaries.
- For #160, reviewed the owner-observed attempt-review reset against current Connections
  and SQL discovery/inspection paths. Attempt discovery is a separate authorized read;
  a denied historical detail must be rechecked before clearing the selected book.

## Attempt-review recovery patch

The Connections UI now rechecks the current connection list and attempt discovery
when a historical attempt detail returns 403/404. If those scoped reads succeed,
it keeps the book and reports that the attempt is unavailable; new enrollment
remains blocked while an unresolved attempt exists. If current scope revalidation
also fails, it clears financial state as before. This is a presentation and
authorization-recheck fix, not a credential reset, provider exchange or proof
that the old attempt is recoverable.

The development web service also has a second Cloud Run URL. Its bridge accepts
the configured public origin (`jayburd-dev-web-9088794002.us-central1.run.app`),
while the service-reported `*.a.run.app` alias can lead to rejected requests.
The application landing page now redirects that alias to the configured origin
before sign-in. The owner should use the configured URL for the next test.

`Connections.test.tsx` covers both the attempt-only denial and actual scope
revocation; `page.test.tsx` covers canonical-host routing. Fresh Sandbox acceptance still requires an owner-authorized Hosted
Link session to reach verified binding review, followed by ciphertext/worker-read
evidence under #164. Keep Scheduler paused until those checks pass.

Validation for this patch: `make web-check web-test web-build web-browser`
passed on the final patch (273 unit and 17 browser tests).
`make check test build` could not start:
the pinned Go 1.26.9 toolchain download returned HTTP 403 even after a permitted
network retry; local Go 1.26.5 is below the module requirement. The existing
synthetic browser/API/PostgreSQL Hosted Link journey is unchanged but must pass
in PR CI before merge. Hosted owner acceptance remains unproven.

## Current evidence

PASS: `make check test build release-test`; `make web-check web-test web-build
web-browser` (258 unit tests, 15 browser tests). Final focused Go/type/unit and generated-contract checks also pass.
`bash scripts/test-infra.sh` passes 68 mocked Terraform tests across eight roots.

PASS: `make app-integration connection-browser-test` in an isolated copy with
only test ports changed from 39081–39083 to 41881–41883, preserving the running
demo. `TestSyncReviewPostJourney` covers a pending completion, lost committed
exchange reply, reload discovery, explicit account binding, acquisition and
reviewed exact 0.10 posting. SQL assertions confirm no automatic journals and
one final journal/source-link/outbox. Synthetic provider and identity only.

`TestHostedLinkCompletion`, `TestHostedLinkNavigation` and
`TestHostedCompletionClaimBoundary` cover ambiguous/stale results, navigation,
pre-claim authority, pending checks and replay. UI tests cover unsafe URL,
uncertain reply, cancel and scope change. Release/Go configuration tests accept
explicit false SDK enablement while retaining other gates.

## Remaining work

After merge, build the pinned API/web images
and promote reviewed connection metadata with link_events_qualified=false.
Actual hosted interactive qualification remains separate under #88.

## Operator steps after deployment

1. Sign in, select the intended development entity/book, then open Connections.
2. Choose Connect account, then Open Plaid Sandbox. Keep the original tab open;
   complete only a fictional Sandbox bank session in the new tab.
3. Return and choose Check bank setup completion. Pending means check later;
   unknown outcome means inspect the durable attempt, never repeat exchange.
4. Review account-to-ledger mappings, matching currency and binding date, then
   confirm selected bindings. View sync status and request a sync once the worker
   deployment is verified; a queued request is not evidence of completed import.
5. Review transactions after publication. Posting remains a separate explicit
   action. Record a redacted hosted receipt before closing any #88 acceptance gate.

## PR handoff

Targets main; no migration. Owner merge precedes image build and hosted acceptance.

## Hosted recovery investigation (#160)

Owner observed Hosted Link success followed by completion HTTP 409. The new
attempt's public status is `credential_recovery_required` with a recorded account
manifest. That establishes that the service got through provider verification and
manifest recording; it does not prove source storage or destination delivery.
GSM slot-00 version metadata currently lists no versions. API source creation
and separate allowlisted delivery still need to be distinguished. No credential
values or provider payloads were accessed. Storage object-name lookup was blocked
by local TLS trust; certificate verification was not bypassed.

Fixed UI recovery: independently successful durable-attempt discovery survives an
Item-list transport failure. Hosted completion 409 inspects the exact attempt by
GET, exposes credential recovery and clears the one-shot handoff without another
execute or provider exchange. `Connections.test.tsx` names both regressions.
These changes do not deliver a credential, reset attempts or activate acquisition.
The owner is checking existence only of /bank-sync/slot-00 in the isolated writer
project; no secret values are requested. Hosted acceptance remains incomplete.

Validation for #160 recovery UI: PASS `make check test build`; PASS
`make web-check web-test web-build web-browser` (265 unit, 17 browser tests);
PASS `make app-integration` against the real local API/disposable PostgreSQL.
The initial sandbox cache-access denial was rerun with approved cache access.
These tests verify recovery presentation and retained discovery, not hosted
credential creation/delivery. No migration or deployment in this patch.


PR #165 incorporates this #160/#161 recovery presentation fix together with the
owner-selected encrypted database token path. The historical source/delivery
investigation above is superseded for new runtime credentials by
[bank-token-vault](../contracts/bank-token-vault.md); no old token was retrieved
or reconstructed. Hosted acceptance remains pending coordinated deployment.

## Historical reconciliation feedback retest (#160)

After deployment 39072895377, the owner inspected attempt `e8e959ae-…` and
clicked **Reconcile recorded credential**. The attempt remained in
`credential_recovery_required`; the browser showed only its generic unconfirmed
operation message. The screenshot did not include the HTTP status, so it does not
prove whether the service returned its expected 409 or a separate failure.
The browser now offers **Try connecting again** on a failed new setup. It
reconciles the exact attempt and, after a confirmed 409, reads it again. If it
is still unresolved, the same click requests server-guarded abandonment. Only
a confirmed abandoned state plus zero unfinished attempts opens a fresh Link
session. Stored-credential conflicts and uncertain replies stop the retry.
The old provider exchange is never repeated; its audit history remains.
Synthetic UI coverage checks the successful restart and uncertainty path.
Fresh Hosted Link completion, encrypted persistence,
binding review, and worker read remain separate hosted acceptance gates.

## Fresh retry still blocked at attempt review (2026-10-18)

After release #185, the owner used **Try connecting again**. Discovery showed
new attempt `4d72d362-beae-47a9-a901-994137ba172b` as `link_ready`, one
unfinished attempt, two older attempts (one expired unclaimed, one abandoned),
and no connected Item. Clicking **Review attempt** for the new attempt showed
“This operation could not be confirmed.” The screenshot did not contain the
exact GET HTTP status, fixed problem code or response shape, so the cause is
still unconfirmed. A `link_ready` row proves Begin persisted an attempt; it
does not prove Plaid completion, exchange, ciphertext or account binding.

Current source behavior: Review attempt calls an exact read. It does not reopen
Plaid or call `/execute`. A hosted URL/nonce/token is held only in the browser
component; reload, scope change or cancel can discard it. If the original tab
still displays **Open Plaid Sandbox**, the owner can use it and then **Check bank
setup completion**. Otherwise, the implemented fallback is to wait for the
unclaimed attempt to expire, refresh discovery and start a fresh attempt. Do
not repeat an old provider exchange or infer that an unresolved attempt is safe
to abandon.

[#186](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/186)
owns the exact-read diagnosis and regression. Record only method, scoped route,
HTTP status, fixed problem code and redacted trace metadata; never capture or
post Authorization headers, Link/public tokens, provider payloads or financial
data. [#187](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/187)
owns the proposed guarded lost-handoff restart and user-facing flow. The
[Hosted Link contract](../contracts/hosted-link-enrollment.md) and
[connection status UI contract](../contracts/connection-status-ui.md) define
acceptance. Keep [#160](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/160)
and [#164](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/164)
open until a fresh Sandbox session reaches binding review and the separate
credential/worker evidence passes. No production account or automatic journal
posting is implied by this plan.

Official Plaid Hosted Link and Link API documentation was refreshed and saved as
public-page snapshots for review; see PI12 in the
[Plaid source register](../research/plaid-ingestion-sources.md). It changes the
priority of #187: Plaid recommends retaining a user-associated Link token and
a completion webhook, while Jayburd's token currently disappears with the
browser component. The proposed primary recovery is a scoped encrypted
server-side token and verified completion/status path. A fast **Start over**
remains a fallback only when absence of a completed provider result and local
claim/credential can actually be proven. No provider account or token was read.

Documentation-only validation: `git diff --check` passed. `make check test
build` stopped before project checks because the pinned Go 1.26.9 toolchain
download failed (connection reset in the sandbox; HTTP 403 on approved retry).
No application code, database migration, cloud resource or hosted connection
was changed by this documentation update.

## In-app retry/cancel (#200)

Owner requested application recovery instead of manual database operations.

# Owned Hosted repair SQL
<!-- stage-runbook: true -->

## Status and boundary

Base27062957592bef2128c85969eafa5b302968d39b; branch
`feat/318-hosted-repair-sql`. Forward32 reserved after current31/#65 check.
The [reviewed protocol](../contracts/hosted-reconnect.md), merged321 after all5 CI
checks, owns the design. No actual provider event, production, cloud mutation or
managed apply32. Source319/UI320 and dedicated signed delivery remain separate.

## Stage ledger

| Stage | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Resume | Read current318/275, merged protocol/source register, database foundations/standards and current13/14/19/23/28 functions |
| SQL review | Two immutable grains, exact restricted interfaces, full principal/source/Item/attempt lock order and compatibility reviewed below |
| Implementation | Forward32, two immutable receipt grains, scope pin, private credential read, ten compatibility wrappers and closed bootstrap allowlist |
| Independent SQL tests | All16 Hosted repair cases PASS on actual restricted-login disposable PostgreSQL, including forced duplicate snapshots and receipt/claim/cancel races |
| Required gates | Core/race/build, migration, ledger, connection state/service/ops, webhook/bootstrap,342 web units/26 browser cases and real synthetic browser/API/SQL command recovery PASS |
| Handoff | Pending PR; no hosted gate or issue closure |

## Current evidence

Existing source has no concrete HTTP reconnect, so SQL guards must land before
enabling it. Merged19 changes the default and record extension for both modes;
32 must cap only reconnect. Attempts have no created_at; the unique immutable
begin event provides the age origin. Current confirmation otherwise copies a
manifest expiry, requiring an explicit reconnect no-extension check.

SQL design: one immutable `link_session_receipt` row per verified delivery
(environment/receipt SHA key; exact attempt FK, hashed Link/session/body, closed
outcome and signed issuance time). One immutable `link_repair_claim` per claimed
attempt pins a successful receipt, claim UUID, existing credential identity and
old consent ceiling. API can read only owned proof projection and execute its
existing commands; dedicated webhook can only accept normalized signed receipts.
Neither runtime role gets table access or old-helper EXECUTE. No raw provider
body/JWT/token or financial amounts enter these tables.

The attempt's immutable-once scope digest pins source binding/stream revisions
and states only at fresh begin, excluding changing cursors/demands and labels.
Legacy missing snapshot denies; never infer it from current rows. This bounded
profile requires the original consent principal, with no delegated-owner switch.
The receiver has its own narrow SQL-selected-actor locker: global API/ledger
cross-role denial is unchanged, no SET ROLE or event-supplied actor. Refreshed S12
PG17 full SECURITY DEFINER safety section; qualified names, pg_temp last, exact
EXECUTE grants/revocations occur within the migration transaction.

All principal identities (actor, configured worker, existing consent principal,
stream service principals) lock in UUID order before current authority/book,
source accounts in order, Item, attempt, then receipt/claim. Source/Item generation
and complete stream set recheck after locks. Receipt pins no claim or wakeup;
confirmation uses stable repair:attempt signal per active approved stream and
preserves paused streams. Exact same effect key cannot advance again.

Compatibility: retain new/rotate/remove semantics and public API shape; add private
`item_consent_expires_at` only for reconnect service use. Old concrete provider
still rejects reconnect. Legacy unclaimed reconnect's mutable expiry is capped
once with an immutable policy-change event; immutable history is never rewritten.
Missing/ambiguous begin provenance expires eligibility rather than guessing.
Legacy claimed reconnect without signed proof cannot resume. Existing terminal
receipts remain scoped readable; no item/credential/journal alteration from this
backfill. Fresh attempts get the same explicit cap before returning a Link.

## Remaining work

Exact-head canonical CI and source review remain before merge; human security
review precedes managed release. The closed bootstrap allowlist has only the
two intended receipt functions; no broader role or IAM exception. #319 must cap
manifest consent at the SQL-projected live ceiling,
check signed proof before bank-token work and recover exact unknown claims.
The purpose-specific `get_repair_bank_credential` read derives the existing tuple
from this repair;319 must wire it into the scoped vault instead of18's generic
expiry-ordered attempt lookup. Reconnect never writes another encrypted version.
This SQL change alone cannot enable concrete reconnect or clear service recovery.

Review distinction:15minutes limits unclaimed Link/proof/claim. A committed

directory and `sql_operator` to the same IAM email. Query only capability metadata:

```sh
PGPASSFILE=/dev/null psql -X -w -h "$sql_socket_dir/jayburd-bookkeeping-dev:us-central1:jayburd-dev" \
  -U "$sql_operator" -d bookkeeping -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 \
  -c 'SELECT rolcreaterole FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname=current_user;'
```

This is only the first capability check, not permission to run migrations. Follow
the [bootstrap contract](../contracts/cloud-sql.md#bootstrap-and-migration) for
the remaining authority checks and `db/bootstrap/cloud-sql.sql` invocation.
Stop the proxy after use. Remove the optional operator and connector/login bindings
through Terraform if no SQL objects were created. After a successful bootstrap,
review ownership dependencies before deleting or downgrading it. Never use
ABANDON or leave an unnecessary privileged login to hide a failed cleanup.

## PR handoff

Keep #26 open for managed-service acceptance, pool recovery and restore proof.
Include this runbook in every commit. Private operational logs/state stay ignored.

## Status and boundary

payloads or authenticator setup material will be inspected by agents.

| Synthetic validation | 105 unit/component tests, two rehearsal browser tests, six existing browser journeys, static-server denials | Owner rehearsal |

## Current evidence

PASS: `make web-check web-test web-build`, `make identity-rehearsal-test web-browser`,
`make check test build`, pinned actionlint and document-link checks. The rehearsal tests intercept every external request;
no actual mail/provider acceptance is claimed. Server tests verify strict routing,
Host/origin/method denial and CSP. Initial validation caught test imports/React
prop typings, corrected before final checks. Registry sandbox stall resolved
through approved install; no credentials were inspected. Vite reports an expected
Next.js `use client` directive warning in the entirely client-side static bundle.
Identity Platform configuration is applied. On 2026-10-12 the owner reported
successful authenticator setup after correcting the setup-key entry. This is
owner-reported evidence; no credentials, provider payloads or authenticator screen
were inspected. Separate fresh password/TOTP sign-in, logout, expired/reused link
and revoked/deleted identity checks have not been individually confirmed.
PR #41's foundation, validate, frontend, application-integration and secret checks
all passed on commit `bd5ccde`; this documentation update records the new evidence.
Owner review server started at `http://127.0.0.1:39091`; root returned 200 and
`/v1/entities` returned 404. This is transport evidence, not a user login.

## Remaining work

PARTIAL: owner reports authenticator setup succeeded. Record separate redacted
outcomes for mail delivery, verified email, fresh challenge and logout; do not
infer the entire acceptance matrix from the successful setup report.
Cloud database/Go revocation and hosted access remain separate gates.

## PR handoff

Contract: [identity rehearsal](../contracts/identity-rehearsal.md). No SQL,
financial API or cloud changes. Keep #39 open until owner evidence exists.

## Owner instructions

From this branch/worktree, run `npm --prefix web ci` once, then
`make identity-rehearsal`. Open **http://127.0.0.1:39091** (not localhost).

1. Open [Identity Platform providers](https://console.cloud.google.com/customer-identity/providers?project=jayburd-bookkeeping-dev)
   → **Application setup details**. Copy only `apiKey` into the local form.
2. Sign in with your invited account. Click **Send verification email**, open
   Google's link privately, then return and click **I have verified my email**.
3. Sign in again, select **Set up authenticator**, enter the private setup key
   in your authenticator, and verify its code. Enrollment signs you out.
4. Sign in once more with password and authenticator code. The completion screen
   confirms browser sign-in only. Sign out when finished; Ctrl-C stops the server.

If configuration/login fails, check the selected project and API-key restrictions
privately; report only the visible generic message and step. Do not send credentials,
links or setup-key screenshots. No automatic email is sent by starting this tool.
Missing mail: request once, check spam, wait at least 60 seconds before retrying;
provider quotas may require longer. Expired links need a new request.

# Import money properties

## Status and boundary

Issue #94 implements the decoder property slice of #86. Test-only external
`ingestion_test` package uses exported Decode/types; no production, SQL, provider
or cloud changes. Lease IMPORT-PROPERTIES-2100. No new dependency or migration.

## Stage ledger

| Stage | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Contract review | Coordinator approved independent integer oracle, 0/2/3-decimal representation and purchase identity properties before implementation. Reused statement-decoder and SI01–SI06. |
| Implementation | Independent ASCII byte scanner and base-ten integer accumulation; exact scale divisibility, canonical rendering by integer division and rational quantity comparison. No production predicate or float reused. |
| Oracle checks | Fifteen manually specified oracle expectations plus actual-decoder boundary examples; CSV fixture preserves candidate bytes without CR normalization. |
| Validation | PASS focused decoder/staging race tests, both 60-second fuzz targets and make check test build on Go 1.26.9. No failure corpus or production defect found. |

## Current evidence

`TestDecoderMoneyOracle` independently checks USD cents, JPY integral units, KWD
thousandths, above-JavaScript-safe-integer magnitude, 29 integer/9 fractional lexical
limits and invalid signs/exponents/control bytes. Numeric equivalence cannot waive
the lexical digit limits, including insignificant zeros.

`FuzzDecoderMoney` compares real decoder acceptance to the independent oracle,
then checks original text, canonical quantity, currency/version, row identity and
ordinal. Invalid input must return a zero Statement. Candidate amounts over 4,096
bytes are excluded; existing file/record-size tests own those bounds.

`FuzzDecoderRepresentationIdentity` starts from positive integer minor units,
adds equivalent leading/trailing zeros, and checks canonical quantity against the
original generated integer. Distinct identical purchases retain both identities
and order; duplicate IDs reject atomically. Equivalent lexemes preserve their
separate original representations. Both targets have 54 committed deterministic
seed cases, also executed by ordinary `go test` without fuzz discovery.

Observed 2026-10-13, base `91891f0`, two workers per target:

| Target | Budget | Executions | New interesting / total | Package duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FuzzDecoderMoney | 60 s | 5,041,389 | 40 / 94 | 61.452 s |
| FuzzDecoderRepresentationIdentity | 60 s | 2,685,604 | 80 / 134 | 60.283 s |

Counts include all harness executions, including excluded oversize candidates;
these are bounded coverage observations, not throughput or exhaustive proof.
Interesting inputs live in the local fuzz cache; no failing input needed a committed
regression fixture. No scheduler/CI discovery budget is added in this slice.

Exact commands, from repository root with Go 1.26.9:

```sh
go test -race -count=1 ./internal/ingestion/...
go test ./internal/ingestion -run '^$' -fuzz '^FuzzDecoderMoney$' -fuzztime=60s -parallel=2
go test ./internal/ingestion -run '^$' -fuzz '^FuzzDecoderRepresentationIdentity$' -fuzztime=60s -parallel=2
make check test build
```

Execution used `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/jayburd-quality-fuzz-cache` and existing
`GOMODCACHE=/private/tmp/jayburd-go-modcache`. New target baselines each contained
only their 54 source seeds. Focused race packages passed: decoder 1.521 s, staging
5.111 s. Logs: `/private/tmp/jayburd-import-properties-{race,money,identity,default}.log`.

Source review: reused [statement contract](../contracts/statement-decoder.md) and
[SI source register](../research/statement-import-sources.md). Read Go 1.26.9 local
`src/math/big/int.go` Int.QuoRem and `ratconv.go` Rat.SetString API comments;
[public math/big navigation](https://pkg.go.dev/math/big). Integer quotient/remainder
supports exact minor-unit representability. Rat.SetString accepts broader syntax,
so the independent byte grammar is checked first. These API sections support the
test mechanism, not accounting policy or ISO conformance; the online default
version is newer than the locally pinned source reviewed.

## Remaining work

No durable effects, SQL authorization/isolation, FX valuation or posting arithmetic
is exercised. Generated retry/restart/reorder state sequences, cross-adapter matching,
provider profiles and scheduled fuzz automation remain #86 or dependent issue gates.
Pure decoder rejection proves only no returned rows, not database rollback.

## PR handoff

Only `internal/ingestion/money_property_test.go` and this runbook changed. Default
and focused gates passed; staged runbook guard and diff check required before commit.
Coordinator owns integration, shared indexes and issue handoff.

# Inaccessible saved-command recovery
<!-- stage-runbook: true -->

## Status and boundary

Issue #133 hosted acceptance found an authenticated owner blocked before first-book
setup by an older unacknowledged command whose current scope authorization fails.
Add one explicit recovery action for the owning principal. It returns only whether
work was cleared, never the command, scope, request, result, or financial data.

## Stage ledger

- PostgreSQL locks the active principal and pending command in a serializable
  transaction, reuses current command authorization, and permits clearing only
  the existing not-found/permission-denied cases.
- Prepared work is cancelled and then acknowledged; committed or cancelled work
  is acknowledged. Accounting functions are never called and immutable history
  plus cancel/acknowledge audit records remain.
- The API and same-origin bridge expose `POST /v1/commands/pending/clear` with an
  exact empty object. The UI requires an explicit click and reloads recovery and
  workspace state only after confirmed success.
- PR #145 merged as `cacc5a0`. Owner-dispatched build 38809806298 passed all
  validation and published matching API, migrator, web, and worker candidates.
- Migration-only release PR #146 merged and run 38813529384 completed
  successfully, applying migration 16 without changing application services.
- Matching application release PR #147 and run 38815405193 completed, but hosted
  acceptance exposed a stale-shell defect: the root response retained the prior
  release's asset map under `Cache-Control: s-maxage=31536000` even though the
  current content-hashed bundle contained the recovery control.
- The root route now renders dynamically and the candidate-container gate
  requires `no-store`; content-hashed static assets retain their normal cache
  policy. This prevents an authenticated browser from pinning obsolete UI code
  across releases.

## Current evidence

- `make migration-test` passed fresh, replay, down/up, and dirty-state proofs.
- `make ledger-test` passed the full PostgreSQL suite after advancing the schema
  compatibility sentinel to clean migration 16. Recovery tests also reject
  empty, malformed, and nonempty bodies through the owned error contract.
- `make check test build` passed. All 261 web unit tests, the production build,
  and all 17 browser tests passed, including explicit denied recovery and
  restored starter-book setup.
- The cache correction repeated all 261 web unit tests and all 17 browser tests.
  The production route manifest marks `/` dynamic, and a loopback production
  response returned `Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0,
  must-revalidate` while referencing content-hashed static assets.
- PR #149 merged as `bc3f932`. Owner-dispatched build 38818907429 passed the
  complete validation matrix, exact candidate runtime checks, vulnerability
  gates, and published matching digest-pinned application images.
- Deployment PR #150 and run 38821143876 completed. Live verification returned
  `no-store` and the current recovery bundle. Owner acceptance then exposed a
  ambiguous state: discovery can succeed while a rejected action's denial remains
  visible. Successful discovery now clears stale discovery and uncertain-transport
  errors while preserving definitive action failures. Idle copy is hidden whenever
  an action error exists. The screenshot alone does not establish which request
  was denied; hosted setup authorization remains unverified.
- `make app-integration` passed the synthetic PostgreSQL, API, and web
  composition gate.
- Build 38809806298 passed its complete reusable validation plus per-image
  runtime, vulnerability, and publication gates.

## Remaining work

Issue #151 correction: `make web-check web-test web-build web-browser` passed
with 263 unit tests and 17 browser journeys. New hook regressions cover denied
discovery followed by successful retry and definitive setup rejection followed
by empty pending discovery. No database or API contract changes are required.
PR #152 merged as `262b54e` with every check green. Owner build 38823429691
passed validation, integration, all candidate runtimes and vulnerability gates.
The promotion manifest pins its API, migrator and web receipts; database work
is read-only migration status verification. Hosted action authorization remains
unverified until the owner completes the starter-book flow.

Hosted scope denial remains fail-closed; no private payload or log was inspected.
The stale-error correction and owner starter-book acceptance remain.
The earlier local candidate-container rerun was blocked before application
startup by an Alpine mirror certificate/index refresh failure; build 38818907429
subsequently passed that independent candidate-image gate in CI.

## PR handoff

Migration execution is complete. The next handoff is the exact
`operation: sandbox-promote` manifest for build 38818907429. Hosted acceptance is
the root returning `no-store`, followed by the owner explicitly clearing
inaccessible work and preparing the starter book without exposing the old command.

| Handoff | Owner/coordinator reviews task vocabulary and whether a future server-owned index is desired. Implementation requires its own scoped issue/evidence and current dependency check. |

## Current evidence

The proposed source and handoff contract is written and has no implementation
effect. The following fixed examples define expected later evidence.

### Fixed synthetic examples

All IDs, dates and amounts below are fictional. The selected book is B1, the
selected source S1, and no example performs an action automatically.

| Case | Inputs / evidence | Expected presentation and action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Actionable review | Authorized S1 read returns one `needs_review` row R1 at source revision `7`, `USD 12.34`; detail and categories confirm current pins. | `Review source: 1 visible item` for S1 only. Open R1's existing review flow; draft creation makes no journal. Explicit command confirmation remains separate. |
| Empty selected source | Authorized S1 source list and complete `needs_review` page return `items:[]`, `next_cursor:null`, revision `7`. | `No known items for S1` under that filter. No book-wide All clear or zero across unseen sources. |
| Incomplete page | S1 first page returns a cursor and the next page fails or returns `review_snapshot_changed`. | `Status unavailable` or `Changed since you opened it`; do not call S1 empty or keep stale action pins. |
| Optional runtime absent | Connection reads are unavailable because the connection service is not composed. | `Connection status unavailable`; no zero attempts, no Begin/retry inferred, no global All clear. |
| Denied book | Current read grant for B1 is revoked between handoff and fetch. | `Permission denied`; clear B1 financial/status detail and discard late prior responses. |
| Stale status | Stream action was shown with generation `10` and revision `3`; fresh status is generation `11`/revision `4`. | Explain changed status and require review of the fresh pins before any confirmation. A queued request is not completed acquisition. |
| Other-book command | Principal pending command targets B2 while B1 is selected. | Do not disclose B2 body in B1. State only a generic principal gate blocker if authorized by the recovery contract; navigate to B2 only through verified current scope. |
| Handoff/back | Ledger passes B1, date `2026-10-20`, account A1 and revision `42` in memory. Investigate has no account-wide status index. | Retain B1/date context, ignore unsupported A1 for queue filtering, read a selected owned source; return to Ledger with B1/date/A1 and let Ledger refresh revision `42`. |

# Migration metadata and replay
<!-- stage-runbook: true -->

## Status and boundary

Continue #26/#27 after merged #47 (`10a50b1`). Owner authorized continuing cloud
acceptance. Read migration-control metadata only; replay the approved migrator
only after a clean version/hash check. No new SQL, privileges or service deployment.

## Stage ledger

| Stage | Evidence | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prerequisite | #47 merged, hosted checks passed | Verify database metadata |
| Metadata query | Read-only transaction and pinned proxy transferred with hash checks; proxy could not start, no SQL ran | Owner restores Cloud Shell authorization |
| Replay | Not dispatched | Requires clean baseline |
| Denial tests | `make cloud-sql-test` passes with SQLSTATE 42501 and repeatable-read P2101 checks | Use these exact outcomes for the future cloud API proof |

## Current evidence

The first migration succeeded; its original hosted receipt failed and was recovered
read-only as recorded in [execution evidence](migration-execution.md). This stage
does not reinterpret that failed workflow as successful.

Metadata-query SHA256:
`0dfb84cc83db9cede248a3295a039da321b3def08fa8bed4a11cab0dbe0fdcac`.
Query compares `deployment.schema_migrations` and `migration_artifact` only and
returns a fixed PASS/BLOCKED result; it reads no journals or identity rows.
Expected hashes come from the approved source's `db/migrations/SHA256SUMS`.
Cloud Shell temporary directory: `/tmp/jb-replay.m8xFAg`; private query/proxy logs
remain excluded from Git. Existing operator retained; no new grants are authorized.

Cloud Shell restarted and lost the earlier temporary files. Direct proxy download
timed out; local official v2.26.0 download and transfer succeeded, SHA256
`a38fe97690a27490e60a7945a8a178186ff9464abb81fe2bc652a3f773443387`.
The verified binary reports v2.26.0. Its private socket did not start; fixed-category
diagnostics found a connection-refresh failure. A separate existing-CLI project
number lookup also failed. No raw error, token, credential or financial data was
printed. Owner was asked to reauthorize Cloud Shell; no authorization transfer or
new privilege grant was attempted. Proxy cleanup ran, and replay was not dispatched.

The local permission tests previously accepted any error. They now require
PostgreSQL `42501` for DDL/direct-table/SET ROLE denial; zero-row reads prevent
payload retrieval. The workspace unknown-principal test now uses repeatable read
and requires `P2101`, avoiding a false pass on its `P2100` isolation precondition.
These are synthetic checks, not proof of Cloud SQL API identity authorization.
`make cloud-sql-test` passed restricted migration/replay, permission denial,
contention, artifact integrity and dirty-failure checks in disposable PostgreSQL.
`make check test build` also passed (vet/race, source integrity, docs and binaries).

## Remaining work

Verify clean version and all artifact hashes before and after replay. Retain the
successful hosted execution receipt if emitted. Actual API IAM login and forbidden
DDL/direct-table access tests, operator ownership cleanup, restore and connection
load/recovery remain separate #26 gates.

Owner recovery: open Cloud Shell for `jayburd-bookkeeping-dev`, run
`gcloud projects describe jayburd-bookkeeping-dev --format='value(projectNumber)'`,
and approve its authorization prompt. Expected public output: `9088794002`.
Do not send credentials. Then rerun only the bounded read-only check first;
successful CLI authentication alone does not prove the proxy or SQL session works.

## PR handoff

Do not dispatch or repeat a job after a failed metadata check. Investigate without
force, down migration or privilege expansion. Keep #26/#27 open until their named
acceptance criteria pass; metadata and replay alone do not approve live bookkeeping.

# Workload-owned migration status
<!-- stage-runbook: true -->

## Status and boundary

Continue #26/#27 from merged #48 (`5cb958b`). Owner restored Cloud Shell access.
The IAM proxy now starts; the human operator's metadata read is denied with 42501,
and its existing migrator SET ROLE capability is false. No grants were added and
no replay ran. Proxies stopped through cleanup traps.

## Stage ledger

| Stage | Evidence | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cloud retry | Authentication restored; metadata SELECT denied; existing role-switch unavailable | Keep operator separation |
| Decision | [Status contract](../contracts/migration-status.md): same job/identity, read-only SQL snapshot | Implement without widening grants |
| Implementation | `status` command and `verify` release operation; exact completion/argument receipt | Review PR |
| Validation | Go/race/build, 18 release tests, isolated SQL status/migration suites, 24 mocked Terraform runs, actionlint and shell syntax pass | Build fresh images after merge |

## Current evidence

No cloud version/hash acceptance is claimed. The first execution remains successful
as documented in [execution evidence](migration-execution.md); its metadata is not
accessible through the human operator. Cloud query/binary hashes and temporary
directory remain in [replay evidence](migration-replay.md).

Local status checks require one clean current version and exact registered file
hashes in repeatable-read/read-only mode. A forced RLS test fixture exposes metadata
only when `transaction_read_only=on`; malformed/missing/dirty/drifted metadata and
elevated/API identities must fail. The initial fixture exceeded the migrator's
two-connection limit; its preliminary reader now closes before migration setup.
No production connection limit was changed.

PASS: `make check test build release-test cloud-sql-test migration-test infra-test`;
actionlint for the changed workflow, shell syntax and diff checks. Named
`TestMigrationStatus` proves missing/dirty/behind/ahead version, missing/extra/changed
artifact, elevated/API identity rejection and forced read-only visibility.
Release CLI tests prove `verify` emits `action=status` with no service variables;
orchestration rejects an `up` execution and never reaches runtime roots.

## Remaining work

Merge, build fresh images, then prepare a separate exact-digest `verify` manifest
for owner review. The currently committed manifest still requests `migrate` with
the old image: do not dispatch it for inspection. A successful status snapshot
permits a separately reviewed replay, followed by another status check.
Actual API IAM denial, operator ownership cleanup, restore and load remain open.

## PR handoff

No new SQL, data access grants, identity or cloud resources are applied here.
Verification updates only the existing job's reviewed action, never service roots.
Current old manifest bytes are unchanged. Keep #26/#27 open; implementation and
local evidence do not substitute for the new image's hosted acceptance.

# Migration 30 development rollout

Existing dedicated job uses migration29 image with status-only action. Selected
metadata confirms fixed migrator workload identity. No migration30 execution yet.
Bootstrap prerequisite follows merged db/bootstrap/cloud-sql.sql. SQL operator
must only create/validate the safe NOLOGIN capability, not run product migration.

The paragraph above records the initial state. Actual migration-only

Thirty release/receipt tests and migration-only isolation script passed. Local core checks, race

Go1.26.10 unchanged; canonical pinned CI remains authoritative. The initial
default local toolchain download failed with a connection reset.

and validated receipt are complete. This follow-up copies deploy/migration30-verify.json
byte-for-byte to deploy/dev-release.json; merge and dispatch its already approved
hash for independent clean-latest30/checksum evidence. Core check/test/build passed
again with the same documented local toolchain limits. Do not blindly retry failed
receipts, force migration state or run administrator product SQL. Issue272/88 hosted
acceptance remains open after this schema-only work.

`279a35ca1a05836cc3f439544db1345402e41ec4989f735396c85ff3d0a6afdb`.
Exact following status manifest SHA256:
`d11f04988dde3ecd7c72cfc23d9b7689f26c1cabab003a0d36ca2f1f4b59def4`.
Both expire2026-10-24T13:00:00Z. Trusted build39898191502 attempt1;
migrator digest `da41aa09a13e8652228697ff90180eb20cc69ad913b0d35e2fbc2058c843258e`.

Release metadata only; merged migrations remain immutable. Follow deploy/README.md
and docs/contracts/migration-release.md. Record exact execution receipts, validation
and any remaining risk before handoff.

# Observer runtime delivery

<!-- stage-runbook: true -->

## Status and boundary

Build the bounded local Go publisher/consumer adapter for #7/#57 on merged #78.
No SQL migration, hosted transport, cloud mutation or financial effect.

## Stage ledger

- Assigned one implementation agent a bounded adapter/test scope; coordinator
  reviewed the API before implementation and requested independent review.
- Documented project status and exact frontend navigation after owner review.
- Integrated agent commit `78c09b5` as `fa470e8`; independent review verified
  ambiguous COMMIT SQLSTATE classification and regression tests after correction.
- Recorded owner navigation feedback and proposed next UI slice in issue #52.

  preserving the existing demo. Port overrides remain in the review worktree.

Local review frontend returned HTTP 200 at localhost:39283 and was opened in the
system browser. Owner supplied a screenshot of the running synthetic page.

provider connection. Keep #7/#57 open for remaining hosted acceptance. The local
demo is a separate review worktree; its temporary port overrides are not in this PR.

# Local observer adapter
<!-- stage-runbook: true -->

## Status and boundary

Implemented the [reviewed adapter contract](../contracts/observer-runtime.md):
role-separated Go calls, a bounded publisher tick and receipt-only consumer.
Transport is injected; no HTTP/OIDC, Cloud Tasks SDK or hosted activation exists.

## Stage ledger

- Reviewed SQL/background-work contracts and proposed the API before code.
- Root approved role separation, deadlines, committed-result gates and fake queue.
- Implemented all nine SQL primitives, strict wakeup parsing and task-name checks.
- Independent review found ambiguous COMMIT SQLSTATEs were classified too broadly.
  Corrected 08007/40003 and other unclassified outcomes to `commit_unknown`;
  explicit rollback/constraint outcomes remain known. No unknown outcome retries.

## Current evidence

2026-10-13:

- `make check test build`: PASS.
- `make observer-test`: PASS against disposable PostgreSQL 17.11, including the
  existing 19 SQL fault tests, seven adapter unit groups and six adapter integration
  groups. All nine production adapter primitives execute under actual role-bound
  sessions; no inherited DSN, credential or provider is used.
- `TestAdapterTransactionFaults` and `TestPublisherUnknownSQLStateNeverEnqueues`:
  full SERIALIZABLE retries, stable holder, safe errors, bounded cleanup and no
  replay/enqueue/metadata on ambiguous commit.
- `TestWakeupBoundary`, `TestAdapterRoleAndMetadata`,
  `TestPublisherCommitBeforeTransport`, `TestTransportContradiction`:
  strict input/output, digest and deadline checks; queue calls outside transactions.
- `TestObserverAdapterFastConsumer`, `TestObserverAdapterQueueLoss`:
  fast completion, late acknowledgement, stable uncertain task identity and
  duplicate/reordered old/new dispatches preserve one observed receipt.
- `TestObserverAdapterUnknownCommit`: actual successful PostgreSQL COMMIT with an
  injected lost application reply at discovery, dispatch claim/result and consumer
  claim/finish. Scoped retries recover committed state. This is not TCP fault injection.
- `TestObserverAdapterAuthority`, `TestObserverAdapterExpiryAndDeadline`,
  `TestObserverAdapterFailure`: wrong-role rejection, current revocation, expiry,
  real query cancellation and retryable failure retain durable SQL authority.

## Remaining work

No command/service composes this adapter yet. Add separately reviewed authenticated
HTTP/Cloud Tasks transport, caller identity, configured endpoint allowlist, bounded
pool composition and hosted deployment evidence. Runtime objects never retrieve
secrets. The fake transport cannot establish provider delivery or OIDC guarantees.

## PR handoff

Issue #7, additive Go implementation and docs; no migration or cloud mutation.
Root owns integration/CI/status documentation. Tick counts report partial relay
progress, never total backlog completion or financial effects.

# Observer service transport
<!-- stage-runbook: true -->

## Status and boundary

Implemented the [transport foundation](../contracts/observer-transport.md) for
#7 under lease WORKER-HTTP-7. Separate authenticated HTTP handlers wrap the
existing publisher/consumer. Cloud Tasks REST creation and Google signature
verification receive injected transports/credentials. No cloud/provider calls,
deployment, credential discovery, SQL migration or accounting mutation. No
worker executable or hosted authentication acceptance is claimed.

## Stage ledger

- Read current worker/runtime contracts, issue #7 and background-work sources.
- Reviewed Google service authentication, token types and REST v2 task creation;
  OT01–OT06 record reviewed sections and alternatives in the contract.
- Coordinator approved exact routes/caller policy, run.app-only destinations,
  60s handler/65s dispatch budget, injected credentials and no runtime activation.
- Implemented strict auth-before-body, one request admission, fixed response
  vocabulary, exact envelope/digest validation and no application create retry.
- Added bookkeeping_sync to the existing adapter's mixed-capability rejection
  under coordinator's explicit scope extension; no SQL grant changed.
- Independent review found a valid-JWKS-plus-padding response could accept a
  truncated prefix. Replaced truncation with strict max-plus-one rejection and
  an exact65536/65537-byte regression; reviewer verified the fix with no blockers.
- Added synthetic cryptographic, HTTP, queue/credential fault and cancellation
  tests, followed by actual PostgreSQL HTTP-to-HTTP composition proof.

## Current evidence

2026-10-13:

- `make check test build`: PASS, including default synthetic checks.
- `go test -race ./internal/observer -count=1`: PASS after transport fault cases.
- `make observer-test`: PASS against disposable PostgreSQL 17.11 (first transport
  run:42 groups; final expanded suite:44 top-level groups). The Docker
  sandbox credential-helper failure was rerun through approved escalation.
- `TestObserverHTTPComposition`: real restricted-login publisher and consumer
  run through their HTTP handlers and fake Cloud Tasks REST. Actual receipt
  COMMIT reply is dropped: first consumer response503, two duplicates204.
  Queue create reply is also dropped. Result remains one observed receipt and
  one attempt, original one journal/outbox, unchanged book revision; second
  publisher tick makes no additional queue call.
- `TestObserverHTTPMixedSyncRole`: mixed sync capability returns503 before
  discovery and creates no operation. Fixture-only role creation supports both
  pre-sync and integrated migration sets.
- Unit tests use generated synthetic RSA keys and fake JWKS/REST responses;
  they do not fetch public keys or call Google. No token/body/error text escapes.

## Remaining work

A separate executable/composition must inject scoped workload credentials,
restricted independent pools, exact caller subject/email/audience and required
HTTP server deadlines. The existing public API is unchanged. Hosted Cloud Run
IAM/OIDC/header behavior, queue overrides/limits, scheduled activation, actual
service role enrollment, key rotation and cost/latency proof remain separate
acceptance gates. Identity tokens do not replace current SQL scope authority.
No user/provider ingestion or automatic posting is introduced.

## PR handoff

Coordinator owns shared composition, bibliography/index and CI. New tests are
picked up by existing observer-test; no script/Makefile/go.mod changes. No
migration. Independent review resolved the key-response limit finding and reported no
remaining blockers. `git diff --check` and staged runbook guard passed.
