documents.body:
# Plaid lifecycle and failure verification

<!-- stage-runbook: true -->

## Status and boundary

Issue #85, parent #88; lease `PLAID-88-SWARM-20261022T1540Z`, lane VERIFY85.
Base `52ef702`. Tests and this proposal only; no runtime, SQL, HTTP, dependency,
cloud, provider credential or financial contract change. No provider calls.
Synthetic evidence cannot qualify the hosted application or close #85/#88.

## Stage ledger

1. Read repository index, bibliography, #85/#86 acceptance, matrix T04–T09 and
   R01–R03, runner/runtime contracts, corpus independence rules and existing
   acquisition/sync/providerflow source. Inspected actual assertions rather than
   treating suite names as proof.
2. Re-read official Plaid [transaction states](https://plaid.com/docs/transactions/transactions-data/)
   pending/posted and testing sections, and [Transactions errors](https://plaid.com/docs/errors/transactions/)
   pagination mutation and Item-limit sections, 2026-10-22. These are P88-11/12 in
   the [canonical source register](../research/plaid-88-test-sources.md).
   Relevant sections were read; no unseen Dashboard or institution behavior claimed.
3. Added one fixed lifecycle oracle through original loopback HTTP, the actual
   Plaid adapter/decoder, restricted SQL worker and disposable PostgreSQL29.
   Separate literal expected facts are not generated by the decoder or fixtures.
4. Added second-page rate-limit, unavailable-institution HTTP503, malformed-body
   raw-byte-overflow and network-timeout faults after a known completed publication.

## Current evidence

`make acquisition-test` PASS with cached pinned Docker images, local Go1.26.5
and external modfile (tracked Go1.26.10 unchanged). Log:
`/private/tmp/jayburd-85-acquisition.log`. Initial sandbox Docker access denial
was environmental; approved rerun reached the actual synthetic database.

| Test | Exact assertions | Matrix coverage and limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TestAcquisitionLifecycleOracle` | Pending removal and posted replacement across two pages; changed amount/date/name; explicit lineage; null-linked new posted transaction; disappearing authorization hold; added/modified/removed; exact magnitude, original numeric lexeme, currency, date, direction, state and revision; corrected API review projection; C1 remains visible until whole update completes; receipt replay performs no fetch; zero journals and outbox messages. | New synthetic T04/T05/T07/R02/R03 evidence. API projection uses the actual restricted API SQL login and fictional actor; no trusted browser identity or hosted API authentication proof. Unmatched transaction is deliberately not inferred to be a replacement. Existing namespace overlap policy remains visible in expected states. |
| `TestAcquisitionPageFaultPreservesPublication` | Five independent second-page faults leave C0, original observation/revision and zero journal/outbox counts unchanged; exactly three total provider calls, no automatic refetch. | New synthetic R01/T07 evidence. HTTP503 is a simulated unavailable institution, not a real institution test. Network timeout uses a shortened 250ms test-only HTTP client deadline against a stalled loopback response; production ten-second configuration is unchanged. It does not test a real institution or worker restart. |

Existing tests separately exercise committed response loss at claim/stage/complete,
whole-loop mutation restart, permission revocation, expired leases, SQL bounds,
posted evidence immutability and wakeup concurrency. Their source was inspected;
this branch does not rename them as the original issue's broader acceptance names.
These deterministic scenarios are not #86 seeded sequence/fuzz proof.

## Remaining work

Hosted T04–T09/R01–R03 remain open. Run provider Refresh to induce dynamic lifecycle;
another local sync is not the stimulus. Compare named-account custom fixtures, not
only UI counts. Independent hosted equality and zero-journal proof need the scoped
capability below before execution. Reconstruction of
an entire runner/evidence adapter after process loss, and original #85 trigger
matrix need final assertion-level inventory; no claim that all are closed here.

### Proposed runtime comparator — review required, not implemented

Question: obtain R02/R03 evidence without exposing source records or granting a
worker general ledger access. Proposed owner: #88/#85, coordinator review pending.
This is an operational verification protocol, not an ISO20022 financial message;
existing proprietary Plaid API2020-09-14, ISO4217 currency and date assessment apply.
No new accounting or conformance claim.

Prefer a separate, explicit, Sandbox-only one-shot verifier identity over an API
route or widening sync worker privileges. New forward migration required before
implementation; immutable merged migrations stay untouched. It gets EXECUTE only
on two new fixed security-definer functions, no table SELECT or posting grants,
no role membership in owner/API/sync/publisher. Validate session/current identity,
NOINHERIT and forbidden mixed memberships exactly as existing runtime probes.
No bypass through caller-supplied actor IDs. Current authorization uses a separately
owner-installed finite mandate binding verified service login, exact
entity/book/source/Item/account/namespace, expected completed generation and
expiry; recheck at every call. Revocation/expiry/foreign scope fail closed. Never
accept arbitrary SQL, DSN, object path, raw payload or unrestricted account list.

1. `verification_snapshot(mandate_id)` executes a single read-only snapshot and
   returns only bounded counters/revisions: source revision, current generation,
   completion state, all-book journal count and journal-posting outbox count,
   plus a random verification nonce. It does not return transaction fields.
   Before/after measurements must pin the same mandate and book. Counts alone
   cannot establish causation under concurrent manual posting: require an explicit
   isolated test window and record that limitation. It must neither persist the
   receipt nor enqueue an event; output is collected as a redacted run artifact.
2. `verification_compare(mandate_id, expected_fixture)` accepts at most the existing
   1,000-change/2MiB bound, rejects duplicate fixture identities, and compares the
   complete authorized source projection, revisions and exact provider lexemes,
   currency IDs/codes, dates, state, direction and pending lineage against an
   independently authored fixed fixture. Include retained history when expected,
   not only the latest pointer. Check review evidence through its authorized
   projection as well. Return total and per-field mismatch *counts*, complete-set
   equality and fixed error codes only; never values, IDs, names or hashes that
   could disclose small amounts. The fixture is ephemeral input, never logged,
   persisted, retained in a command, or echoed. Secret/raw-provider payloads are
   not an allowed fixture source. For hosted use start with named custom synthetic
   transactions, independently specified before provider injection.

The CLI must be inert by default and require explicit operation, manifest and
mandate; finite timeout, one attempt, no automatic provider sync, no credential
file/environment scanning and no default cloud operation. Bind redacted results
to reviewed image/build, schema version, manifest digest and observation time.
Snapshot race/expired mandate and unknown outcome fail evidence, never silently
retry as a pass. No mechanism may authorize a posting or mutate source data.

Acceptance before hosted execution: restricted-role disposable PG tests deny
wrong/revoked/expired mandate, foreign entity/book/source, mixed roles, oversized
fixtures and unknown fields; demonstrate unit/date/state/lineage mismatch detection
and missing/extra/duplicate identities; demonstrate no sensitive outputs; unchanged
journal/outbox zero for acquisition and replay. Trigger a controlled synthetic
journal addition in the disposable DB to prove counters detect it. Production
mandates must be rejected. Retain failed comparator evidence as fixed reasons.

Alternative: owner-run arbitrary SQL/dumps are quicker but violate the narrow
runtime/privacy boundary. Reusing worker authority for ledger reads couples
acquisition to posting evidence and unnecessarily expands its privilege. A public
comparison endpoint expands sensitive input and authorization surfaces. Deferred
one-shot scoped functions add migration/review work but give inspectable least
privilege and exact reproducible proof. Neither this proposal nor source review
approves that migration or authorizes hosted execution.

## PR handoff

Tests only; migration impact none. Links #85/#88; does not close #86 or hosted
acceptance. Core and additional integration gates are recorded below after running.

Final local gates PASS: `make check test build`; `make acquisition-test` (including
all five second-page faults); `make sync-state-test provider-flow-test ledger-test`
(including restore replay). No skips/failures in the disposable integration logs.
Core synthetic listeners required approved execution after the initial sandbox
bind denial. Logs: `/private/tmp/jayburd-85-core.log`,
`/private/tmp/jayburd-85-acquisition.log`, `/private/tmp/jayburd-85-integrations.log`.
Staged runbook guard and `git diff --check` run before commit. No browser/API wire
contract changed, so browser build/recovery gates are not added for these tests.

### Follow-up: signed socket to actual restricted SQL

Coordinator requested the missing composition proof after independent review.
Dependency commits `f79e3ea` (bounded host) and `2422e68` (runtime identity contract)
were applied before this test-only follow-up; they are not implemented again here.
Extended `TestProviderEnrollmentAcquisitionFlow` rather than adding another harness:
real ephemeral loopback listener → maintained-library synthetic ES256 signature →
actual verifier → `Host.NewSQL` → `synthetic_webhook` login → PostgreSQL29 receipt
and wakeup → existing acquisition runner → review evidence. The script adds only a
fictional webhook login to its disposable database. No live DSN or provider access.

`make provider-flow-test` PASS, log `/private/tmp/jayburd-85-webhook-flow.log`:
invalid signature and altered bytes each return401 with no receipt/generation
change; exact signed delivery and duplicate each return204 but persist one receipt,
one webhook wakeup and one generation increment (1→2). Existing acquisition then
publishes two exact cents observations and replays without another fetch, with
zero journal entries and journal outbox rows. Disconnect makes the same valid
signed replay return403 and leaves receipt/generation counts unchanged. Synthetic
HTTP identity remains the existing test adapter; this proves listener/signature/
SQL composition, not provider enrollment, hosted IAM, proxy timing or delivery.
Core checks and staged guard recorded before the follow-up commit.

Follow-up core `make check test build` PASS, including race tests for the bounded
host, log `/private/tmp/jayburd-85-webhook-core.log`; provider-flow proof above PASS
without skips. This follow-up adds no production implementation or migration.

   checks after the source-backed repair; preserve the broader #88 gates.

student, mortgage, auto, consumer and line of credit. Each uses six independently
fixed ordinary examples, three precision-held examples across three currencies
and two fixed storage rejections. It asserts exact lexical retention, rational quantity equality,
fixed diagnostic codes and zero partial page on rejection. This does not prove
hosted completeness or ledger approval.

# Plaid qualification pass — 2026-10-21

## Status and boundary

with Plaid and running the recommended tests. This pass uses fictional Sandbox
accounts and disposable synthetic databases. It does not authorize production
accounts, deployment, IAM changes, Scheduler activation, or automatic posting.

4. **Hosted API smoke — partial, expected boundary.** The existing diagnostic
   authenticated to Plaid, exchanged a disposable fictional Item, decoded initial
   and repeat sync, and removed that Item. Details below.
5. **Hosted application journey — partial with checking failure.** Interactive
   fictional Link and four reviewed bindings committed. Card, mortgage and
   student acquisition completed; checking failed exact decoding and published
   nothing. Card repeat acquisition completed. Read-only review evidence below;
   no draft creation or posting was attempted.

## Current evidence

The 1,000-command volume test exceeded its 270-second completion assertion while still cycling through command lifecycle states. No completed total was verified. |

`sandbox-probe` job via the fixed manual workflow on main, with no overrides.

it cannot attest the latest application revision. It creates/exchanges/removes

agent context. Workflow submission success is not execution success.

Execution completed successfully at `2026-10-22T00:14:21.309624Z`, with one
succeeded task and no configured task retry. The profile
`plaid-sandbox-diagnostic-v1` receipt at `2026-10-22T00:14:10.481702Z` reported
overall `partial` with these allowlisted outcomes:

checks/reasons/counts were read. No general logs, raw responses, financial
fields, Item/account identifiers, cursors, credential values or process
environments were inspected. Probe success does not complete #88.

### Current runtime metadata readback

On 2026-10-22, selected Cloud Run metadata confirmed API revision
`jayburd-dev-api-00017-znq` and web revision `jayburd-dev-web-00017-b42`, each
serving 100% traffic. The acquisition publisher Scheduler is **ENABLED**, on

request-status records from 00:12–00:16 UTC returned HTTP 200 on publisher
revision `jayburd-dev-acquisition-publisher-00005-w97`. No Scheduler or runtime
configuration was changed. This current readback supersedes the release
runbook's historical PAUSED state; endpoint acceptance does not prove a
selected account's source publication, queue completion or SQL/no-journal
invariants.

### Browser volume finding

`web/tests/demo/volume.spec.ts:15` waited 270 seconds for `Volume run verified`
or `Stopped for review`, but received `Saving immutable request`. The call log
continued alternating save, SQL execute and receipt acknowledgement; it does
not establish a deadlock, wrong amount or duplicate posting. The error snapshot
did not capture a committed count, and the disposable database was cleaned up;
no completed count or USD 495.55 oracle pass is claimed. The other three demo
tests passed, and the independent SQL report test committed 1,024 cent journals
and checked nine GL pages in 17.68 seconds.

`TestAppIntegrationBridge` launches a `docker exec ... busybox nc` process for
each HTTP connection. That is a plausible contributor to this local volume
latency, not a measured root cause or a production-capacity conclusion. #89
owns a controlled timing/progress breakdown across browser command lifecycle,
bridge, SQL and resources. The test timeout was not raised and no retry was
used to relabel the failed gate. The synthetic error artifact is retained
locally as `/private/tmp/jayburd-88-volume-error-context.md`.

### Interactive hosted application — 2026-10-22 UTC

Resumed under lease `PLAID-88-INTERACTIVE-20261022T0028Z`, after owner sign-in

Used First Platypus Bank, non-OAuth `ins_109508`, with its public dynamic

financial record, raw provider response or credential store was inspected.

Plaid displayed seven fictional account types and reached its success screen.
The application then reached verified binding review and committed four selected
bindings: checking, credit card, mortgage and student loan. Auto, consumer and
line-of-credit accounts explicitly could not bind. The selected pre-existing
Sandbox book and its dated currency policy were retained; enrollment did not
create a new entity or book. The attempt became active with no unfinished attempt.
One completion/status read initially showed the generic unconfirmed outcome;
subsequent explicit inspection recovered the completed state. No duplicate
enrollment or exchange was initiated to work around uncertainty.

| Account | Observed acquisition and review outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Credit card | Initial generation 1/1, HISTORICAL UPDATE COMPLETE, publication `00:38:27.856894Z`. Explicit scoped repeat request completed generation 2/2 at `00:42:06.619626Z`, no queued request or active lease. Source revision remained 1. After repeat, needs-review pagination contained 50 + 5 rows; posted filter contained zero rows. The full pre-repeat count was not measured, so no count-equality assertion is claimed. |

All-status review showed source revision 0 and no transactions. Left held; no retry or rounding workaround. |

The checking result is a qualification failure with an undiagnosed cause, not
proof that the provider value was invalid or that the configured money limit is
correct. A bounded follow-up must distinguish provider decimal representation,
approved range and decoder behavior using synthetic reproductions and redacted
runtime evidence. Preserve exact money and atomic publication requirements.

Read-only review demonstrated imported unposted observations, including card
dates before the book's current policy start. It did not prove a full 90-day
window, exact provider-to-review equality, cursor state or absence of all

# Plaid Sandbox qualification diagnostic

## Status and boundary

Issue #88; coordinator-approved bounded read-only harness. No provider, secret,
cloud or real application database has been accessed by this lane. Overall Sandbox
qualification remains unperformed. The diagnostic deliberately cannot emit an
overall pass, even when exact-decoding and repeat-delta checks pass.

## Stage ledger

Reviewed AGENTS, issue #88, decoder/acquisition/connections and webhook boundaries,
current official Sandbox/Link/Transactions docs. Reported real Link prerequisite:
ordinary Link session event enablement or reviewed Hosted Link implementation is
needed before current VerifySession can qualify association. Coordinator approved
an offline-default pipe-fed sync diagnostic and explicitly deferred webhook firing.
Implemented strict bounded input, production HTTP/decoder reuse, aggregate page/
change/byte budgets, cancellation, fixed redacted receipt and executable offline
proof. Inherited pipes become nonblocking before Go wrapping so five-second input
read deadlines actually apply. Invalid flags are never echoed as diagnostics.

## Current evidence

`make check test build` PASS, including all-package race tests.
`bash scripts/test-sandbox-qualification.sh` PASS (focused race tests, executable
build and default blocked/offline receipt with exit2). Logs:
`/private/tmp/jayburd-sandbox-default.log` and
`/private/tmp/jayburd-sandbox-offline.log`. Synthetic tests exercise exact cents above float precision,
pagination and repeat cursor, scope mismatch, parser rejection, missing/null currency
precision, credential redaction, opt-in denial, ordinary-file descriptor rejection,
actual pipe read deadline, cancellation and aggregate budgets. Tests perform no
provider calls; an injected fake RoundTripper receives fictional credentials only.

## Operator sequence

1. Run `bash scripts/test-sandbox-qualification.sh` for offline proof, or build
   `go build -o /your/private/output/sandbox-qualify ./cmd/sandbox-qualify`.
   Default executable exits 2 with a blocked/offline JSON receipt. This is expected.
2. Complete coordinator readiness review: Sandbox account only, real Link proof
   path, owner-approved secret injection, deployed app/SQL evidence and hosted IAM.
3. Only after explicit provider execution authorization, the operator's private
   secret injector supplies the [contract input](../contracts/plaid-sandbox-qualification.md)
   on inherited pipe FD >=3. Invoke the binary with
   `-mode sandbox-sync -allow-sandbox -input-fd 3`. Never put values in arguments,
   process environment, repository files, shell history, screenshots or agent output.
   The injector must finish/close its write end within five seconds. Regular files,
   stdin/stdout/stderr and TTY input are rejected. No agent reads that pipe.
4. Save only the redacted receipt if desired. Exit 3 means partial diagnostic
   evidence, never completed qualification; exit 2 means blocked. Investigate fixed
   blocked checks using owner-controlled provider/app tooling, without copying raw
   errors or payloads to this repository. Provider-not-ready is not an empty book.

This mode does not modify source SQL, generate transactions, refresh an Item,
exchange/rotate tokens, fire webhooks or post journals. A read-only provider probe
cannot prove application no-journal effects. Repeat delta can legitimately change;
no automatic retry is attempted. Cursors are not retained for later runs.

## Remaining work

Full #88 real Link/exchange, dynamic pending-to-posted, signed webhook delivery,
provider-to-review exact consistency, persisted cursor/idempotency and no-journals
proof remain explicit blocked receipt checks. Infisical/runtime evidence design and
hosted deployment qualification belong to the coordinator's other lanes. Sandbox
simulation is not production institution history/balance/consent correctness.

## PR handoff

Owned new qualification package, executable, offline script, contract and this
runbook only. No SQL migration, shared API, CI, dependency or production adapter
change. Primary source annotations SQ01–SQ05 are in the contract; coordinator owns
shared bibliography/index links. Do not close #88 from this partial harness.

# Posting acceptance follow-up

<!-- stage-runbook: true -->

## Status and boundary

Decision: prove the existing principal-deletion and retention boundaries for
[#4](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/4), without
inventing an erasure policy or changing SQL/runtime behavior. This follows the
[original acceptance audit](core-acceptance-audit.md). #4 remains open pending
review of the acceptance wording and unresolved lifecycle scope.

## Stage ledger

| Stage | Evidence / result | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Review | Read live #4, posting/identity contracts, migrations and existing invariant tests | Add only missing deletion proofs |
| Implementation | Two disposable PostgreSQL tests distinguish physical deletion, historical retention and disable | Run default and ledger gates |
| Validation | Default checks and full disposable ledger suite passed on 2026-10-13 | Review deletion interpretation; keep #4 open |

## Current evidence

New tests in [posting gate integration](../../internal/ledger/posting_gate_integration_test.go):

- `TestDeletedUnusedPrincipalDenied`: create then physically delete an unused
  principal; posting returns `not_found` and all durable posting state is unchanged.
- `TestHistoricalPrincipalRetentionAndDisable`: a separate poster with no policy
  approval reference posts, then membership removal leaves only historical
  references. Administrative deletion fails with exact SQLSTATE `23503`; principal
  and full ledger snapshots remain unchanged. With memberships restored, disabling
  denies fresh posting, historical receipt replay and journal read. An active,
  authorized actor still reads that history.

Observed PASS on 2026-10-13: `make check test build`, then `make ledger-test`,
using Go 1.26.9 and the script-pinned PostgreSQL/migrate images. Both new tests
passed, as did the existing invariant, replay, close-race, historical reversal,
forward-upgrade, restore-replay and runtime-readiness tests. The initial ledger
invocation hit the sandbox Docker image-helper error; the approved outside-sandbox
rerun passed without inspecting credentials. Logs: local
`/private/tmp/jayburd-posting-gate-tests.log` and
`/private/tmp/jayburd-posting-gate-ledger.log` (not required repository inputs).

Source authority is the existing
[posting boundary](../contracts/posting-boundary.md),
[identity contract](../contracts/identity-setup.md), immutable migrations 000001/2
and [P03–P06 source review](../research/posting-sources.md). No new accounting
policy, financial message, external-source interpretation or ISO claim is added.

Existing tests already cover the remaining narrow posting criteria:
`TestPostingInvariants` injects every write-stage/deferred-COMMIT failure;
`TestPostingReplayConcurrency`, `TestCommitAcknowledgementLoss` and
`TestPostingCloseRace` cover replay/uncertain commit/lock ordering;
`TestSpotReversalHistoricalProvenance` compares exact original/reversal lines,
rate/currency/policy identities with an independently posted newer rate;
`TestReversalOfReversalDenied` rejects second-order correction unchanged.
These are retained, not duplicated.

## Remaining work

The phrase “deleted” in #4 does not define a user-facing deletion/erasure,
retention, identity-provider deletion propagation or anonymization lifecycle.
The tests establish only existing database authorization and foreign-key behavior.
Owner review must settle that scope before claiming the complete criterion or
using issue closure to unblock #7. Live policy, full FX, imports, close evidence,
worker delivery and hosted reliability remain separate gates.

## PR handoff

Review the named assertions and deletion qualification. No migrations, runtime
code, provider calls or live data are changed. Default and ledger gates passed; reviewers can rerun `make check test build
ledger-test` with the pinned Go toolchain. No browser/API/migration behavior changed.

## Current evidence

Observed locally with Go 1.26 and pinned PostgreSQL 17.11/migrate 4.20.1 images:

```sh
make check test build
make migration-test
make ledger-test
```

PASS default checks: doc/context links, vet, Go race tests, migration-file integrity,
and tooling builds. PASS pinned actionlint 1.7.7 on the modified workflow. PASS migration fresh install/replay, transactional failure and
dirty-state rejection. PASS integration suite and restore replay. CI runs the same
three targets. The Go adapter reserves one second of its five-second budget for rollback cleanup.

and executes on an internal Docker network; ordinary Go tests run with `-race`.

only resources created by each invocation are removed. Both database and test
containers mount only the required migrations, test executable and synthetic corpus.

receipt and outbox, plus a deferred COMMIT failure; all state rolls back.
`TestCommitAcknowledgementLoss` / `TestHTTPPostCommitBoundary` drop a real commit
acknowledgement: response is 503, then original receipt replays without duplication.
`TestSchemaPrivileges`, `TestTransactionIsolation`, `TestEntityReferencesAndPrivileges`,
`TestReceiptActorAndArchive` and `TestSchemaCompatibility` cover grants, scope,
revocation, archival and setup bounds. Remaining tests map to the

`GOCACHE=/private/tmp/jayburd-go-cache GOMODCACHE=/private/tmp/jayburd-go-modcache`.
Before commit run `bash scripts/check-stage-runbook.sh --staged`.

Real-LLC policy, ASC review, opening balances, accountant exports/cutover, close
review evidence, live rate selection, settlement/remeasurement positions and outbox
delivery remain open. Test-only close races do not implement the close workflow.
Restore proves this synthetic database with roles already provisioned, not a live
recovery SLA or complete disaster-recovery procedure. No scale benchmark is claimed.

Down migrations intentionally fail; repair financial history forward. Runtime
cannot perform setup or table DML. Owner/superuser remains trusted administrative
authority. Keep broader #1/#2/#3 gates open; this is the bounded development proof,
not official-bookkeeping approval. Source review is recorded as P05/P06.

defaults; listener defaults only to127.0.0.1:8080. No DSN, role, plaintext-secret,
provider environment or caller-supplied URL override is accepted.

numeric project, fixed client ID/secret names and numeric versions, bounded
literal listen host/port. Managed construction does no credential/key read; it
opens only the dedicated webhook Cloud SQL connector/pool and a20s startup Ping.
Ping proves transport only. Existing SQLReceiver still checks actual session
capability per delivery before atomic SQL work. Runtime and Host reject reuse
and post-close execution. Failures unwind partial dependencies; successful
shutdown closes pool/connector and idle HTTP connections once. CLI emits one fixed
failure message, never arguments, infrastructure diagnostics, payloads or tokens.

Named synthetic tests: `TestManagedInvalidConfigurationHasNoIO`,
`TestManagedOwnershipAndDedicatedPool`, `TestManagedFailureCleanup`,
`TestPinnedCredentialResolution`, and `cmd/webhook` `TestParse`/`TestExecute`.
They cover inert configuration, exact secret resources, no construction-time
SQL/key lookup, dedicated component, startup cancellation, partial construction
cleanup, command failure cleanup and redacted outcomes using generated keys and
injected capabilities. Targeted managed/CLI race tests PASS. Final
`make check test build` PASS; explicit `go build -trimpath -o bin/webhook
./cmd/webhook` PASS (root coordinates addition to the shared build target).
Local log `/private/tmp/jayburd-103-managed-core.log`; Go1.26.5/external modfile,
tracked pinned toolchain unchanged. Staged runbook guard and diff check PASS.
No new dependency or migration.

Remaining hosted prerequisites from the prior stage still apply. The component
constructor now exists, but no dedicated IAM user/grants, secret permissions,
public routing, image release, enrollment update or actual provider delivery has
been provisioned. Root coordinates separate real-socket→restricted-SQL integration
proof and exact trusted-image delivery review. No source-provider/cloud call,
financial command, environment/credential inspection or account activation was
performed by this implementation/testing lane. W01–W05 and hosted W07 remain open.

  bounded USD metadata; explicit review and execution remain required.
- Reviewed existing enrollment/setup/connection/delivery SQL and operator bootstrap.
- Verified SIX List One's publication/hash and USD record; recorded a bounded local
  validity window, distinct from ISO historical dates.
- Added transactional identity/reference and creator-owned book bootstrap scripts.
- Added isolated PostgreSQL tests and the application-integration CI step.

## Current evidence

PASS: the focused browser test proves the starter registers the exact bounded
setup request without executing it. `make web-check web-test web-build
web-browser` passes: 258 unit tests and 16 Chromium component tests. No provider
call, source account or journal is part of this UI change.
PASS: `make check test build` passes with the pinned Go 1.26.9 toolchain. After
stopping an obsolete three-day-old local demo that held the proof ports,
`make app-integration` passes through the production Next bridge, Go HTTP, and
disposable PostgreSQL. The integration identity and database remain synthetic.
PASS: eight named PostgreSQL test groups, including initial/replay/conflict,
rollback after a deliberately failed delivery insert, disabled actor/service,
revoked grant, cross-entity, wrong/missing worker capability and API denial.
PASS: `make check test build` and pinned actionlint on `seed.yml`. Initial
sandbox execution lacked Docker/loopback permission; authorized isolated reruns
passed. Independent review strengthened expected-error assertions and disabled
binding cases; those use existing operator functions with fresh idempotency keys. Tests use fictional subjects,
no network, and disposable PostgreSQL; source provenance assertions use the reviewed
public source identifier, not fictional accounting data as ISO authority.

## Remaining work

Owner provides their Identity Platform UID privately (Users console), never email,
password, token or TOTP code. The local rehearsal does not expose UID. Confirm the
existing operator has SET on both owner and identity-operator roles. Scripts do
not self-escalate. Missing owner SET is a separate administration-review blocker.
If enrollment authority alone is missing, the administrator may explicitly review
`GRANT bookkeeping_identity_operator TO "<operator IAM login>" WITH ADMIN FALSE,
INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE`; do not grant this to API/migrator/workers.

Use the retained [Cloud Shell proxy procedure](cloud-shell-bootstrap.md), verify
its dev instance, private socket and selected `bookkeeping` database first. Run
psql with `-X -qAt -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1`, no password prompt, and redirect stderr to
an owner-private file; never upload diagnostics. Do not use shell tracing/SQL echo.
Before each stage review the merged script hash and exact metadata inputs.

Identity stage: `-v project=jayburd-bookkeeping-dev -v subject=<owner UID>` plus a
new reviewed `currency_id` UUID, `valid_from=2026-09-17`, `valid_to=2027-01-01`, and
`source_release=SIX-list-one:2026-09-17:sha256:33139b438657d1cee116ba737807ea71d19d6de4b90f799a09c56f0cc6a1b0ff`,
then `-f db/bootstrap/sandbox-identity.sql`. Save returned principal/currency IDs.
Use this currency in the UI to create a fictional book entirely within that window.
A changed UID deliberately identifies a different invited principal; review it as

   standards, existing proposal and runtime/permission contracts. Coordinator
   approved exact schema, TTL60min, combined-compare-only grant and actual-role
   semantics before implementation. [Contract](../contracts/sandbox-verification.md)
   records decisions, source applicability, alternatives and acceptance limits.

   finite immutable scope/digest mandate, owner metadata receipt/enroll/revoke and
   private current-authorization checks. Only the combined comparison is externally
   granted. No general snapshot, table SELECT or posting privilege.

   actual HTTP adapter/decoder/restricted SQL publishes provider inputs. Two equal
   inflows remain distinct identities. Raw expectations are not derived from
   generated/provider/decoder output and only their SHA256 pins persist.

   lexeme/review/lineage mismatch, complete-set omissions/extras, unknown/duplicate
   fields/map identities, size bounds, current role/permission/expiry/generation
   failures, revoke replay and explicit controlled posting invalidating zero counts.
5. Coordinator review identified review-collapse risk: enforce one observation per
   review, one evidence entry and exact observation/namespace/provider identity.
   A disposable owner bad-merge fixture retains FKs but disables only the immutable
   assignment trigger to represent corrupted/future merge behavior. Runtime has no
   such authority. Counter output is bounded/saturated1001; fresh enrollment checks
   journal.posted outbox only. SQL catches paused streams and expiry at result time.

## Current evidence

Validation results recorded after final execution below. Local Go1.26.5 uses the
external reviewed modfile/cache; tracked Go1.26.10 unchanged. All data is synthetic.
Initial proof iterations corrected unmerged PL/pgSQL syntax, alias collision and
explicit nullable-history fields; no merged migration was changed. An attempted
fixture-only consent timestamp update correctly hit the existing Item generation
guard and was removed; expiry uses actual finite mandate time and generation pins.

and add bounded Go adapter/CLI. Its four-second deadline must begin before BeginTx;
SQL does not claim that function-local statement_timeout bounds a direct caller's
already-running statement. Root owns connector/component, shared CI/Makefile/index
and final integration. Hosted identity/bootstrap/image/manifest/fixture/interval
execution remain separate explicit authorization. #272/#88 remain open until actual
hosted proof; Production access status does not authorize any real account.

Links #272/#85/#87/#88. Migration30 is new; empty-only down/up is supported, retained mandates/receipts block downgrade; merged SQL immutable.

hash metadata. This slice cannot establish nonzero-book before/after causality or
institution behavior. Required core/migration/ledger and focused proofs precede

   authorization, fairness, fixed-v1 rollback and hosted evidence are defined.
3. **Implementation — complete.** Migration 27 adds login-scoped durable
   selection; shared-v1 runs a bounded rotation through the existing SQL relay.
   The worker release policy selects shared-v1 or the binding-v1 rollback mode.
4. **Synthetic validation and candidate build — complete.** Migration
   fresh/replay/roundtrip, restricted SQL dispatch, repository check/test/build,
   release and Terraform infrastructure suites passed. Candidate build
   [39530293602](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/actions/runs/39530293602)

   emitted a matching `migration-execution-passed` receipt for execution
   `jayburd-dev-migrate-5kmwk`. The later application promotion passed the
   status-only migration gate before replacing services.
6. **Worker release — paused and observed.** The reviewed worker manifest pins the
   same build's worker image, selects `shared-v1` with empty binding ID, and links
   fresh compatibility
   [evidence](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/issues/156#issuecomment-6306325433).

   applied the worker runtime but its final readback rejected because the

   `jayburd-dev-acquisition-publisher-00005-w97` and consumer revision

   [Promotion 39537836698](https://github.com/justin-napolitano/jayburd-bookkeeping/actions/runs/39537836698)

   `jayburd-dev-api-00017-znq` and web revision `jayburd-dev-web-00017-b42`.
   Loan and credit enrollment is deployed; liability posting remains blocked.

   then owner-activate the Sandbox job and prove a newly enrolled second book
   progresses through publisher HTTP 200, consumer HTTP 204, and completed
   generations. No live bank or automatic journal follows from these receipts.

`make migration-test` passed, including migration 27 fresh/replay/roundtrip.
`scripts/test-sync-dispatch.sh` passed in a disposable PostgreSQL container,
including five-plus-one rotation across distinct service principals, login
scope and disabled exclusion. Worker
release/receipt Node tests, `make check`, `make test`, `make build`,
`make release-test` and `make infra-test` passed. Local Go 1.26.5 uses a temporary modfile
because pinned Go 1.26.9 download returned HTTP 403; CI remains authoritative.

publisher policies, including the shared empty-binding requirement.
PR #230 CI found two Go files missed the separate `gofmt -l cmd internal`
gate; they were formatted and that gate was rerun before merge.

function allowlist omitted the new selector. The allowlist now names only
`sync_delivery_bindings`; observer permissions remain unchanged.

so this security result cannot be claimed from the local Go 1.26.5 suite.

<!-- stage-runbook: true -->
# Source-first workspace prototype

## Status and boundary

Issue #246, lease `UX-246-20261021T2315Z`. This branch adds one standalone,
fixture-only HTML design preview. It makes no production route, API, SQL, provider,
or accounting change. The prototype is not evidence that the connect-first epic
has been implemented or that any account is ready for live bookkeeping.

## Reviewed basis and design choice

- Read `docs/research/bibliography.md` first, then the selected internal contracts:
  `docs/contracts/source-review-sql.md` (source review and explicit posting),
  `docs/contracts/plaid-history-currency.md` (requested history versus observed
  availability), `docs/contracts/plaid-liability-bindings.md` (credit/loan review
  limits), and `docs/contracts/plaid-decoder.md` (provider categories are inert
  source metadata). Existing product expectations are in issues #104, #52 and #9.
- Current review reads are book and source scoped. This preview explores a global
  owner workspace before those contracts are changed; it does not imply an
  authorized global API already exists.
- Chosen layout: connection inventory followed by All Transactions, then a
  detail view with distinct owner topics, suggestion provenance, and book-specific
  accounting state. A book-first layout was considered, but it cannot show
  unassigned source history as the owner requested. A single merged financial
  total was rejected because separate entities and currencies cannot be pooled.
- First-release suggestions in this fixture come from owner rules or inert
  provider metadata. Model suggestions remain future work until a separate
  evaluation and authority contract is reviewed; no model result is simulated.
- The initial history request can be up to 90 days; the interface reports only
  observed coverage. A simulated Item includes checking, credit card and student
  loan accounts. Liability entries stay held for later accounting policy. Source
  amounts remain decimal strings in USD or EUR.
- The prototype adds no new financial message or data contract. Existing
  proprietary Plaid adapter and ISO 4217 currency applicability assessments
  remain in the cited contracts. No ISO or accounting conformance is claimed.

## Stage ledger

| Stage | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Source and issue review | Read issue #246 and current docs/index, bibliography, source-review, history and liability contracts before implementation. |
| Prototype | `docs/prototypes/source-first-workspace.html` shows first-run simulated Connect, three account statuses, two entity books, six fictional transactions, global search/filter, detail, topic toggle and distinct classification authority. No network or browser persistence. |
| Display states | Loading, empty, unavailable and denied replace prior transaction content. Native controls, skip link, focus transfer, semantic tables, labels and mobile layout are built in. |
| Rule-first review correction | TX-101 now shows an owner rule suggestion. No active model result appears; later model proposals require evaluation and a reviewed contract. Focused static assertion and `make check` pass. |
| Browser review | Owner explicitly requested an HTTP-hosted walkthrough. Localhost Edge rendered the fixture at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/source-first-workspace.html`. Desktop and 390×844 mobile views, keyboard activation, search/filter, detail, topic edit, ownership notice, and replacement loading/empty/error/denied states were inspected. |
| Browser corrections | The sidebar now reports three fictional accounts after simulated Connect; the topic notice clears when returning to the list; mobile book cards stack instead of squeezing into two columns. The mobile document width stayed at the viewport width while its transaction table scrolled inside its wrapper. |
| Repository gates | `make check`, `make test`, and `make build` PASS with local Go 1.26.5 and a temporary modfile outside the repository. `make test` required approved unsandboxed execution for synthetic localhost listeners. Locked `npm ci` and `make web-check web-test web-build web-browser` PASS (286 unit and 17 browser tests). Script syntax and fixture interaction smoke PASS. Staged runbook guard recorded at commit. |

## Current evidence

Static script syntax and required control IDs passed with Node's `vm.Script`.
A DOM stub exercised first-run Connect → All Transactions → card detail → Books
→ denied-state clearing; all assertions passed. `git diff --check` passed.
The original `file://` preview was rejected by CUA: “The requested URL protocol
is not allowed. Allowed protocols: `http:`, `https:`.” On the owner's subsequent
explicit request to host and use the fixture, a local HTTP listener and Edge
browser opened it successfully. The desktop screenshot showed the source-first
overview and cross-account table. A mobile viewport showed the transaction
detail, scrollable table, and corrected single-column entity cards. Browser
DOM measurements showed no document-level horizontal overflow at the mobile
viewport; the transaction table itself had an internal horizontal scroll area.
The browser images were inspected in-session and a separate Playwright capture
saved `/private/tmp/jayburd-246-{desktop,mobile}-{transactions,books}.png` for
local owner review; no image artifact is committed. That script checked six
rows, document width, connection-status text and mobile book grid columns.

Keyboard Enter activated All Transactions and a filtered Review button. Search
for `TX-099` selected one cross-entity posted example; loan + Held selected
one EUR fixture; loan + Posted produced the explicit no-match state. The card
topic toggle changed only its topic while its held accounting state stayed
unchanged. A posted cross-entity example likewise kept its journal evidence
after a topic toggle. The ownership action reported that no assignment was made.
Loading, empty, unavailable, and denied previews replaced prior transaction
content rather than leaving stale rows visible.

The pinned Go 1.26.10 download failed due unavailable network access. A copy
of `go.mod`/`go.sum` under `/private/tmp` changed only the Go directive to the
installed 1.26.5 for these gates; tracked module files are unchanged. Initial
sandboxed `make test` failed solely where `httptest` and worker tests could not
bind localhost; the approved unsandboxed rerun passed.

### Explicit review scenarios

1. Open the file: first-run Connect explanation says the button is simulated.
   Activate it with Enter; three fictional accounts appear with distinct history
   coverage and legal-owner review status.
2. Open All Transactions; search and filter across accounts, including unassigned,
   held and posted examples. Original USD and EUR labels stay on each row, with no
   pooled total. An empty search result is not presented as complete bank history.
3. Open a card transaction: Plaid category is a suggestion with provenance,
   owner topic is an analytic label, and the bookkeeping section has no draft or
   journal. Toggle a topic; no book or posting status changes.
4. Open posted checking activity: posted journal evidence is separate from the
   topic. Inspect the cross-entity example: source ownership and book treatment
   are separately explained, with no automated allocation asserted.
5. Preview loading, error and denied; prior transaction rows disappear. On a
   narrow screen, navigation and table remain reachable by keyboard and the
   document itself should not overflow. These behaviors were observed in Edge
   on the local HTTP fixture; no production accessibility certification follows.

## Remaining work

`web/src/bookkeeping/BookWorkspace.tsx` and `ReviewInbox.tsx` currently select a
book/source before review. `docs/contracts/source-review-sql.md` has no global
transaction query. The synthetic topic toggle and suggestion presentation have
no authority, audit or persistence implementation. Book assignment, transaction
allocation, liabilities, model evaluation, search pagination and 3,000-item
performance require their own reviewed contracts and tests. A visual prototype
does not prove accessibility, permissions, sync completeness or posted balances.

## PR handoff

This bounded branch changes only the prototype and this stage runbook. The
coordinator owns shared index updates, issue discussion, PR creation and any
production implementation. The browser walkthrough is complete; product and
accounting acceptance remain separate.

# Local generated-data review

<!-- stage-runbook: true -->

## Status and boundary

Implemented for #9, based on PR23. Owner requested a usable local synthetic demo
and cent checks. This is an isolated review harness, never a production auth mode.

## Integration into main — 2026-10-12

PR #23 merged to main at `42ee7a8`; #24 merged to the old recovery branch at
`5e03aed`, not main. This branch merges that ancestry without duplicating SQL.
Updated the current API bridge to carry the already-reviewed recovery routes and
respect registration versus transition idempotency. The test-only identity uses
an unsigned three-segment synthetic marker to exercise normal transport syntax;
production authentication remains unchanged. The harness selects explicit loopback
mode and waits for PostgreSQL TCP readiness. Deployment now checks predecessor
merge commits are ancestors of the release, not merely marked merged in GitHub.
PASS: Go check/race tests/build, 94 frontend units, six browser journeys,
production build and workflow lint. The existing demo occupies ports 39081/39083;
left it running. Real integration uses a disposable tracked-source copy with only
fixed port substitutions to 39181–39183. Recovery through the production bridge
and all three guided/cents/volume demos passed. The 1,000-posting browser test
completed in 3.1 minutes, verified USD 495.55, and the shell independently confirmed
exactly 1,000 PostgreSQL journals. No cloud or real financial data access.

## Stage ledger

| Owner | Work | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Coordinator | Loopback demo lifecycle and browser review | Real demo cent posting, reload, guided flow and SQL count PASS |
| Data agent | Generated fixtures, exact cent audit and SQL seeding | Four reviewed generator journals + three original cents journals; stored balances verified |
| UI agent | Decimal-string currency formatting | Currency display and six mocked browser journeys PASS |
| Flow agent | Watched prepare/execute/acknowledge, rejection and replay | Guided real browser proof PASS |
| Volume agent | Bounded sequential 1,000/5,000/10,000 runs | Real 1,000 run PASS in approximately 3.2 minutes |

## Current evidence

Reviewed [generator source audit](../research/testing-sources.md#t04--synthetic-accounting-data-generator):
15 upstream journals have one-cent residuals. Invalid journals must not enter
posted books or receive fabricated balancing lines. Existing accounting policy,
ISO4217 references and SQL authority remain unchanged. Demo data is disposable.

PASS: `TestDemoCentsOracle` rejects a one-cent imbalance, fractional cents and a
wrong expected balance. Startup checks original EUR and functional USD balances
against independent fixed oracles. The [source mapping and license](../../internal/server/testdata/demo/README.md)
record the four-journal subset and explicit fictional parity rate.

PASS: Go `make check test build`, generated-type drift and TypeScript checks.
PASS: `make web-test web-browser` (53 units including volume checks, six Chromium journeys).
PASS: standalone demo Chromium test: generator bank5432.29 and totals5749.26;
cents bank0.29 and totals0.30; posting0.01 then reload gives bank0.30/totals0.31.
PASS: `make app-integration demo-test web-build` for the seeded demo.
After adding watched flows, `make demo-test` passed all three real browser tests:
guided flow 21.9s, manual review 1.4s, bulk 1,000 approximately 3.2 minutes. The bulk
test verified bank debit 495.55/capital credit 495.55 and 1,000 unique response IDs;
the shell independently confirmed exactly 1,000 PostgreSQL journal rows.
The 5,000/10,000 options have fixed-oracle unit checks; those full browser runs
have not been executed. Final `make check test build web-check web-test web-build
web-browser` passed against the complete implementation (53 units, six mocked
journeys, production build and Go race/vet checks).

Startup initially rejected duplicate synthetic rate references; fixed with
date-specific references and reran successfully. Type checks caught a Vite option
and Playwright import mismatch; corrected and TypeScript passed.

## Review commands

Requires Docker, Go1.26.9, Node24.18.0, locked `npm --prefix web ci` dependencies,
and free loopback ports39081–39083. Browser test additionally needs Chromium.

```sh
make demo
# Open http://localhost:39083; Ctrl+C stops and cleans the owned database.
# Run make demo again for a clean reset.
make demo-test
```

The review page uses the production bookkeeping components against real Go/SQL;
its synthetic identity and Vite entrypoint live outside Next application routes.
No environment files are loaded. Production mode still requires managed sign-in.
Currency display uses exact strings and versioned minor units; no float
conversion or rounding hides nonzero extra digits.

**Watch a few transactions** offers manual stepping or a 19-step continuous suite:
setup, deposits 0.10/0.20, fee 0.01, same-command replay, rejected imbalance and
trial balance. The timeline records observed API boundaries, not invented SQL
tracing. **Run thousands** creates a separate Volume Lab and posts 1,000/5,000/
10,000 real deposits sequentially. Each request is prepared, executed, receipt-
checked and acknowledged; recent receipts are bounded to 20 rows. Pause finishes
the current transaction. Retry retains the same request/key/command identity.
No execution occurs merely by opening the page. Start explicitly authorizes this
fixed synthetic sequence and its acknowledgements.

Each volume receipt must have a unique journal ID, expected revision and exact
cents. A separate closed-form oracle checks the final API trial balance;
the 1,000 case expects bank 495.55 and capital credit 495.55. The test runner also
queries PostgreSQL for exactly 1,000 journal rows in the created Volume Lab.
Count and elapsed time describe actual confirmed responses. They include this
local HTTP bridge and sequential browser overhead; no production capacity claim.

## Remaining work

Local checks complete; PR review and hosted CI remain pending.
This is local workflow evidence, not production capacity. Larger browser runs
and multi-user concurrency/load benchmarks remain separate evidence.

## PR handoff

No migrations, production authentication bypass or live provider connections.
Reset stops and recreates only the demo's owned disposable database.

# Tartan browser registration and initial acquisition
<!-- stage-runbook: true -->

Trusted build40004622277 attempt1/sourcefb4ac0411f8f5673ab0659825bcafbdb4e64253e:

permissions; a real permission mismatch must stop, never widen to RunAdmin.

infra target and test entrypoints. Retain only validated public receipt; no raw
metadata/provider diagnostics/state/plan/token upload. Failures may follow partial
apply and require owner-controlled mandate/public-binding revocation and review.

# Worker binding lookup

## Status and boundary

Issue #170: the creator's first **Connect account** action now prepares the
per-book delivery binding automatically under [self-service onboarding](../contracts/self-service-connections.md).
`sandbox-book.sql` remains an administrative recovery path, not the routine way
to obtain the binding ID. This helper reads one active binding ID only; it does
not modify SQL, contact Plaid, deploy workers, or enable scheduling.

## Stage ledger

- Reviewed the current self-service connection contract, migration 17, the
  delivery-binding table in migration 15, and the worker release inputs.
- Added a bounded `psql` lookup through `bookkeeping_owner` and a shell wrapper
  that validates two UUIDs, suppresses connection diagnostics and prints only
  one binding UUID.
- Tested the SQL on a disposable synthetic database: active scoped lookup,
  wrong-entity and wrong-book queries passed. Wrapper tests cover successful,
  missing, failed-connection and malformed-ID outcomes without network access.
- Added a Cloud Shell launcher that checks the selected IAM operator, opens a
  short-lived local proxy, invokes the same lookup, and stops the proxy on exit.
- Copied the three lookup files to `~/jayburd-binding` in the owner's Cloud Shell
  and verified matching SHA256 hashes. Remote `gcloud config get-value account`
  currently returns `(unset)` because the Cloud Shell session still requires
  owner authorization. No hosted database connection was attempted.

## Current evidence

`make sandbox-bootstrap-test` passed against disposable PostgreSQL and the
wrapper passed its no-network outcome checks. `bash -n` and `git diff --check`
passed. The repository-wide `make check test build` attempt was blocked before
checks because this machine has Go 1.26.5 while `go.mod` pins 1.26.9; the
official toolchain download returned HTTP 403 even after an unrestricted retry.

## Remaining work

The owner still needs to run this metadata lookup through their existing
development Cloud SQL connection and review the returned UUID. Worker federation
and paused runtime release remain separately gated.

## PR handoff

The branch adds a read-only SQL file, a small validated wrapper, synthetic SQL
and wrapper checks, and this operator instruction. It changes no migration,
application API, cloud resource or credential handling.

## Operator use

In an **authorized** Google Cloud Shell as `personal.jnapolitano@gmail.com`, run
the launcher copied to `~/jayburd-binding`. It starts and stops the development
proxy automatically and uses the fixed IAM operator login:

```sh
~/jayburd-binding/scripts/run-worker-binding-cloud-shell.sh 9781d120-b826-4f77-949e-51ceda2c5e0f 8b09e985-e348-4497-9bca-2b10eaf61417
```

For an existing development Cloud SQL proxy and operator IAM `psql` setup,
as documented in [Cloud Shell bootstrap](cloud-shell-bootstrap.md), the lower
level script also works. Verify that the proxy targets
`jayburd-bookkeeping-dev:us-central1:jayburd-dev`; it cannot infer the proxy's
target from a PostgreSQL session. From the repository:

```sh
scripts/show-worker-binding.sh ENTITY_UUID BOOK_UUID
```

For the book previously shown in the owner's Sandbox UI, those arguments are:

```sh
scripts/show-worker-binding.sh 9781d120-b826-4f77-949e-51ceda2c5e0f 8b09e985-e348-4497-9bca-2b10eaf61417
```

The script prints only the active binding UUID. A missing row means the chosen
book has no active delivery binding with the expected dev worker logins; do not
invent an ID or dispatch the worker release. The operator must have `SET` on
`bookkeeping_owner`. No token, password, DSN or provider value is an input.

## Evidence and limits

The lookup proves only the selected row's metadata at query time. It does not
prove current consent, successful token persistence, hosted worker IAM, or Plaid
transactions. The owner reviews the returned ID before pinning a paused worker
release. Scheduler activation and controlled Sandbox acquisition stay separate.

<!-- stage-runbook: true -->
# Bounded worker HTTP host

## Status and boundary

Issue #7, lease HOST-7. Coordinator authorized the fixed host profile before code.
Implemented only `internal/workerhost`: injected handler and listener; no routing,
readiness, environment, files, credentials, ADC, cloud calls or deployment wiring.
## Stage ledger

`New` is inert. `Host.Serve` takes listener ownership after validation, runs once,
and returns only fixed errors. The coordinator owns acquisition transport composition.

## Lifecycle contract

Read-header timeout 5s; total read timeout 10s; write timeout 90s; idle timeout 30s;
maximum configured headers 16KiB. Go's parser has its documented implementation
allowance above MaxHeaderBytes; this is not an exact serialized-request byte cap.
Cancellation propagates through BaseContext before graceful shutdown. Shutdown has
an independent 10s context; failure triggers Close. Serve's goroutine is joined.
Unexpected listener failure follows the same cancellation and draining path.
Default HTTP panic/error logging is discarded to prevent request diagnostics from
entering logs. Handlers still own fixed responses, authentication and durable receipts.

This host cannot terminate arbitrary Go code or external I/O that ignores context.
Hijacking/WebSockets are outside the approved worker handler profile; net/http does
not drain or close hijacked connections. An injected listener must obey net.Listener's
Close contract and unblock Accept. The bounded guarantee concerns ordinary HTTP
connections and cooperative handlers, not arbitrary malicious implementations.
Host shutdown never implies that an acquisition committed or rolled back.

## Reviewed sources and decision

Reviewed official Go [Server](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http#Server) fields BaseContext,
ReadTimeout, ReadHeaderTimeout, WriteTimeout, IdleTimeout, MaxHeaderBytes and ErrorLog;
[Shutdown](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http#Server.Shutdown),
[Close](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http#Server.Close), and
[Serve](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http#Server.Serve). Also inspected the pinned Go1.26.9
`src/net/http/server.go` definitions and shutdown implementation locally.
These selected sections establish cancellation injection and graceful-drain mechanics;
the fixed timeout values and fail-closed error vocabulary are project policy.
Chosen over default http.Serve (unbounded server defaults) or TimeoutHandler (does
not supply lifecycle draining). No financial message is introduced, so ISO 20022
mapping is not applicable; existing acquisition contracts retain that responsibility.
The annotated source record is linked from the shared bibliography.

## Current evidence

`make check test build` passed, including all-package race tests. Worker host
race tests passed (five named tests; actual loopback and ten-second forced drain).
Log: `/private/tmp/jayburd-worker-host-checks.log`. Sandbox initially denied local
socket bind; the approved rerun used loopback outside the sandbox. Named tests: TestFixedProfile,
TestCancellationDrains, TestForcedClose, TestValidationAndListenerFailure,
TestCancelledBeforeServe. Tests use synthetic local loopback requests, including
an actual 10s forced shutdown and explicit release/join of the uncooperative test
handler. No provider, database, cloud, credential or business-transaction proof is
claimed by these transport tests.

## Remaining work

Coordinator wires reviewed worker handler and deployment lifecycle separately.
No hosted availability or production qualification claim.

## PR handoff

Issue #7; no schema or financial API changes. Integrate this bounded host with the
coordinator acquisition transport tests; do not mount an arbitrary public handler.

## Independent dispatch regression followup

Coordinator additionally assigned the isolated
`internal/syncdispatch/fairness_sql_integration_test.go` after peer review found
candidate starvation. `TestDeliveryCandidateFairness` creates 30 earlier UUID
operations under one binding: 15 future retries and 15 healthy running leases,
plus a later ready operation. It requires the real publisher SQL candidate call
(limit 25) to return only the ready operation. Fixtures retain constraints and
triggers; no provider calls or trigger bypasses. Separate SQL-author tests own
the exact first-claim deadline and derived-lease takeover regressions.

Reviewed SQL fix uses one timestamp for first claim/deadline and excludes future
retry waits, healthy outer/inner leases and recently accepted task deliveries from
candidate slots. Root owns the migration, harness and merged proof. Borrowed
migration15/checksum/harness are uncommitted local validation inputs only.

Followup evidence: actual PostgreSQL dispatch proof PASS including the new fairness
case (`/private/tmp/jayburd-dispatch-fairness.log`); `make check test build` PASS
again including all-package race tests. The first fixture attempt failed on an
ambiguous UUID/text SQL parameter; explicit UUID casting fixed the fixture before
the successful full proof. These results qualify synthetic SQL behavior only.

documents.title: Jaysearch
documents.body:
# Jaysearch

Jaysearch is a governed research, planning, and ERA-inspired execution toolkit.

It is currently a modular toolkit repo: contracts, docs, CLIs, artifacts, tests, and Python tools live together until the boundaries are stable enough to split into separate repos.

## What This Is

Jaysearch turns project work into explicit graph nodes and packet handoffs.

The core idea:

```text
research and planning define the work
governance validates legal state transitions
execution generates candidate artifacts
evaluation scores evidence
selection chooses a winner
apply happens only through a governed boundary
```

The current execution spine is:

```text
candidate_dag_manifest
  -> candidate_dag_selection
  -> dag_execution_unit_manifest
execution_unit
  -> candidate_patch_manifest
  -> implementation_attempt[]
  -> attempt_evaluation[]
  -> attempt_selection
  -> solution_artifact
  -> applied_solution
```

See the full node graph:

- [docs/toolchain-node-graph.mmd](docs/toolchain-node-graph.mmd)

Public site:

- <https://justin-napolitano.github.io/jaysearch/>

## Fast Demo

Run the fixture-backed demo:

```bash
bin/run-jaysearch-demo --root .
```

The demo proves the current graph-to-execution bridge:

```text
fixture candidate DAGs
  -> selected DAG
  -> execution units
  -> ERA smoke report
```

Outputs are written to:

```text
artifacts/demo/runs/<run_id>/
  demo-report.json
  demo-summary.md
```

This is a technical demo, not a production autonomy claim. It does not synthesize code, apply patches to the source worktree, or complete arbitrary repo tasks.

## Question To DAG Demo

Run the interview-oriented question-to-DAG flow:

```bash
bin/run-jaysearch-question-dag-demo \
  --root . \
  --question "How should we build the candidate generation boundary?"
```

This emits:

```text
artifacts/demo/question-dag-runs/<run_id>/
  question.packet.json
  evidence.packet.json
  candidate-dags/
  selection/
  execution-units/
  question-dag-demo.report.json
  question-dag-demo-summary.md
  demo.html
```

The demo claim is intentionally bounded: Jaysearch can turn a problem/question into a traceable, evidence-backed DAG and execution-unit handoff. Autonomous development execution is the next production boundary.

## Repository Map

- `src/platform_tools/`: Python tools and materializers.
- `bin/`: CLI wrappers for the tools.
- `spec/contracts/`: packet contracts and registry.
- `docs/`: research notes, policies, and design docs.
- `artifacts/`: DAGs, validation packets, generated run artifacts.
- `.agent/execplans/`: execution plans for build slices.
- `tests/`: contract, tool, and flow tests.

## Main Toolchain Nodes

- `problem_node`: a manageable project problem. Not executable.
- `node_option`: a candidate approach for a problem. Not executable.
- `execution_unit`: the first buildable work contract.
- `candidate_patch_manifest`: artifact-backed candidate patches for an execution unit.
- `implementation_attempt`: one candidate implementation attempt, usually with a patch ref.
- `attempt_evaluation`: evidence-backed evaluation of one attempt.
- `attempt_selection`: deterministic selection among evaluated attempts.
- `solution_artifact`: selected implementation result and completion evidence.
- `applied_solution`: isolated applied result after post-apply validation.

## Full Smoke Path

Given an execution unit and a candidate patch manifest:

```bash
bin/run-execution-era-loop-smoke \
  --root . \
  --execution-unit-path artifacts/execution-unit.packet.json \
  --candidate-patch-manifest-path artifacts/candidate-patch-manifest.packet.json \
  --validate-patch \
  --validate-patch-ref \
  --apply-solution
```

Given one patch file:

```bash
bin/run-execution-era-loop-smoke \
  --root . \
  --execution-unit-path artifacts/execution-unit.packet.json \
  --patch-source-path artifacts/change.patch \
  --validate-patch \
  --validate-patch-ref \
  --max-attempts 2 \
  --apply-solution
```

## Candidate Patch Manifest

Use this when you want multiple distinct candidate patches:

```bash
bin/materialize-candidate-patch-manifest \
  --root . \
  --execution-unit-path artifacts/execution-unit.packet.json \
  --patch-source-path artifacts/candidate-a.patch \
  --patch-source-path artifacts/candidate-b.patch \
  --validate-patches
```

The manifest preserves valid and invalid candidates. Invalid candidates remain visible with blockers instead of disappearing from the trace.

## Validation

Run the Jaysearch readiness gate:

```bash
bin/run-jaysearch-ci
```

Run the design review:

```bash
bin/design-iteration --root .
```

`bin/run-local-ci` remains available for legacy platform-template compatibility checks, but it is not the default Jaysearch readiness gate.

## Current Boundary

Jaysearch can now rank and apply supplied patch candidates in an isolated target.

The next major boundary is autonomous candidate generation: tools that synthesize candidate patches while emitting the same `candidate_patch_manifest` contract.

documents.title: ADR 0001 graph canonical execplan projection
documents.body:
id: ADR-0001
title: Graph Is Canonical and ExecPlan Is a Contract Projection
status: proposed
date: 2026-03-10
deciders:
  - justin-napolitano
  - agent/codex-01

## Context

The repository already uses ExecPlans, governed prompts, and workflow validators. That is sufficient for contract enforcement, but it is not sufficient for canonical planning state. A planner control plane needs durable local planning artifacts, dependency-aware task structure, and downstream sync capability without allowing external systems or markdown contracts to become workflow authorities.

Without an explicit architectural decision, the platform risks collapsing back into prose-first planning, hidden conversational state, or external-tool-driven workflow semantics.

## Decision

The planner control plane will treat local canonical graph state as the source of truth for planning and execution readiness.

Planner session artifacts will be durable local records used to derive and refresh graph state.

ExecPlans will be treated as governed contract projections rendered from canonical planner state when readiness criteria are met. ExecPlans are not the planner system itself.

External project-management systems such as GitHub Projects, Jira, and Microsoft Lists will be treated as downstream projections. They may receive selected task data and may support selective pullback later, but unresolved conflicts default to local canonical state.

## Consequences

Positive:

- planning state becomes explicit, local, and auditable
- provider integrations become adapters rather than architectural dependencies
- ExecPlans remain useful as human-reviewable execution contracts
- hidden chat-state authority is reduced

Negative:

- the platform must maintain both canonical machine-readable artifacts and rendered markdown contracts
- projection and sync logic must preserve provenance carefully
- implementation work must define graph validation and projection boundaries precisely

documents.title: ADR 0002 cross repo integration is contract first
documents.body:
id: ADR-0002
title: Cross-Repo Integration Is Contract-First
status: proposed
date: 2026-05-07
deciders:
  - justin-napolitano
  - agent/codex-01

## Context

The platform is evolving from a single governed repo template into a system that will orchestrate specialized external capabilities. Without an explicit architectural rule, capability repos could begin to depend on the platform repo's private internals or on target repos' private layouts. That would turn orchestration into cross-repo entanglement and make replacement, testing, and governance harder.

## Decision

Cross-repo integration will be contract-first.

Repos may interact only through explicit public surfaces such as:

- versioned schemas
- CLI or API contracts
- plugin contracts
- declared output destination roots

Private source-tree imports and undocumented folder-layout assumptions are not valid integration mechanisms.

## Consequences

Positive:

- repos stay independently testable and replaceable
- orchestration remains reviewable and auditable
- target repos can remain mostly self-contained

Negative:

- more contract definition work is required up front
- integration must be validated explicitly rather than improvised

documents.title: ADR 0003 researcher capability is external and self critical
documents.body:
id: ADR-0003
title: Researcher Capability Is External and Self-Critical
status: proposed
date: 2026-05-07
deciders:
  - justin-napolitano
  - agent/codex-01

## Context

The platform now needs a governed research capability. That capability should be reusable across multiple repos and projects, which argues for a separate researcher repo rather than embedding the full engine in the platform repo. At the same time, the researcher should be able to identify weaknesses in its own harness and suggest improvements.

Without an explicit architectural decision, the platform risks either over-centralizing the researcher implementation or allowing uncontrolled self-modification of governance and runtime contracts.

## Decision

The researcher capability will be implemented outside the platform repo and orchestrated through platform-defined contracts.

The researcher capability may critique its own harness and emit self-improvement proposals, but those proposals must be surfaced as governed review artifacts. The capability may not silently modify platform governance or self-authorize contract changes.

## Consequences

Positive:

- the researcher engine becomes reusable and independently evolvable
- the platform repo stays focused on governance and orchestration
- self-improvement becomes explicit and auditable

Negative:

- an additional repo and integration layer must be maintained
- self-improvement proposals add review overhead instead of applying immediately

documents.title: Agent Capability Boundaries
documents.body:
# Agent Capability Boundaries

## Purpose

This slice defines anti-cheat boundaries for governed work. The goal is not to freeze governance forever; it is to stop an active implementation branch from redefining the rules or exception path that would let it pass itself.

## Capability Model

Capability is evaluated from local repository state:

- actor class
- branch class
- active slice goal area
- changed files since the branch base
- active ExecPlan `changes` field
- active exception registry state

The default governed actor is the active implementation agent on an `impl-execplan/*` branch.

Every new Codex session and every worker session must bootstrap from
repository-local governance state before mutating governed artifacts.
That bootstrap is fail-closed when branch role, active ExecPlan, or
required authority artifacts are ambiguous.

## Protected Surface Categories

- `rule_surface`
  - global rules and governance law
- `referee_surface`
  - local validator and legality commands
- `capability_policy_surface`
  - anti-cheat policy and protected-surface definitions
- `exception_registry`
  - authority-granting exception records
- `canonical_state_surface`
  - graph, ExecPlan, and other canonical in-repo state
- `projection_surface`
  - queue mirrors and provider-board projections

Worker-runtime governance additions:

- worker launchers and worker-runtime modules are treated as governed
  runtime surfaces, not as free-form helper scripts
- worker sessions must execute in isolated checkouts or ephemeral
  container-local clones
- worker sessions must hand off authority through Git-backed artifacts,
  not through durable process memory

## Default Anti-Cheat Rules

- non-governance implementation branches may not change:
  - `rule_surface`
  - `referee_surface`
  - `capability_policy_surface`
  - `exception_registry`
- governance implementation branches may change:
  - `capability_policy_surface`
  - a bounded allow-list of `referee_surface` files needed to enforce governance
- governed agents may never write:
  - `.agent/governance/exceptions.yaml`

## Self-Authorization Denials

The anti-cheat referee blocks these cases explicitly:

- an agent modifies exception records that could authorize itself
- a non-governance branch modifies rule or referee surfaces
- a governance branch modifies referee surfaces outside the bounded anti-cheat allow-list
- a protected-surface path is edited without being declared in the active ExecPlan
- GitHub authority is promoted above projection/evidence roles

## Human Authority

Humans still retain final authority. The anti-cheat model preserves:

- explicit human-authorized exceptions
- separate governance work on dedicated branches
- bounded checker repairs when the active governance slice is legitimately implementing policy

What it removes is silent self-authorization by the governed agent on the branch being judged.

documents.title: Agent Framework Comparison
documents.body:
# Agent Framework Comparison

## Purpose

This document compares the most relevant current agent/runtime frameworks against the needs of this repository. It is not a generic leaderboard. The point is to evaluate which frameworks fit a governed kernel with explicit local state, merge-gated execution, and human authority boundaries.

## Scope

Frameworks compared here:

- Microsoft Agent Framework
- LangGraph
- OpenAI Agents SDK
- CrewAI
- DeerFlow as a product-pattern reference rather than a pure framework

Primary source links:

- Microsoft Agent Framework overview: `https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/overview/`
- Microsoft Agent Framework FAQ: `https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/support/faq`
- Microsoft Agent Framework GitHub: `https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework`
- LangGraph docs: `https://docs.langchain.com/oss/javascript/langgraph`
- OpenAI Agents SDK docs: `https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/agents-sdk/`
- OpenAI Agents SDK Python docs: `https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/`
- CrewAI docs: `https://docs.crewai.com/`
- DeerFlow GitHub: `https://github.com/bytedance/deer-flow`

## Repo Lens

This repository already has a strong kernel:

- canonical local artifacts
- graph-backed work state
- deterministic validation
- explicit human finalization
- explicit prohibition on hidden authority

What it does not yet have is a strong runtime harness:

- skill and tool loading
- session runtime and handoffs
- memory model
- sandbox abstraction
- service ingress and UI surfaces

Any framework choice should therefore be judged as a possible harness layer, not as a replacement for the kernel.

## Short Verdict

### Microsoft Agent Framework

Best fit if the organization wants Microsoft alignment, enterprise workflow primitives, .NET and Python support, middleware, telemetry, and a forward path from AutoGen and Semantic Kernel.

### LangGraph

Best fit if low-level orchestration control and explicit workflow/state graphs matter more than enterprise ecosystem alignment.

### OpenAI Agents SDK

Best fit if the team wants the smallest useful primitive set and is willing to build more of the runtime shape itself.

### CrewAI

Best fit if the team wants a more packaged multi-agent workflow product quickly, but it is less attractive as the substrate for this repo’s explicit-governance model.

### DeerFlow

Best thought of as a runtime product reference and feature benchmark, not as the most obvious underlying framework choice for this repository.

## Compare by Dimension

### 1. Kernel Compatibility

Microsoft Agent Framework:

- compatible as a harness layer
- does not inherently replace the repo’s graph or ExecPlan authority
- heavy enough that governance boundaries would need to be defended explicitly

LangGraph:

- highly compatible with the repo’s explicit state-machine mindset
- feels natural beside graph-backed canonical state
- does not force a product-shaped runtime model too early

OpenAI Agents SDK:

- compatible because it is minimal
- easier to keep subordinate to the repo’s kernel
- would require more custom runtime assembly for sessions, memory, and service layers

CrewAI:

- more likely to push the repo toward its own team/task abstractions
- workable, but less naturally aligned with the local graph and governed artifact model

DeerFlow:

- inspirationally compatible at the harness level
- not itself the kernel answer for this repository

### 2. Enterprise and Microsoft Fit

Microsoft Agent Framework is strongest here.

Good:

- Microsoft-backed
- open source
- Python and .NET
